#### `almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek` — The left adjoint B ↦ B_!! of almostification on algebras

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Algebra`.

**Statement.** For a basic setup S = (V, m) and an almost V-algebra B, B_! = m̃ ⊗_V B_* is a non-unital V-algebra; B_!! := (V ⊕ B_!)/I, where I is the V-submodule spanned by the elements (xy, −x ⊗ y ⊗ 1) for x, y ∈ m, is a unital commutative V-algebra with B ≅ (B_!!)^a, and B ↦ B_!! is left adjoint to R ↦ R^a from A_!!-algebras to A-algebras (for any almost algebra A with B an A-algebra). B is exact if 0 → m̃ → V ⊕ B_! → B_!! → 0 is exact; every almost algebra is exact when m̃ → m is an isomorphism (e.g. m flat), and V^a × B is always exact. B ↦ B_!! commutes with all colimits, in particular with tensor products; the natural map B_!! → B_* is an almost isomorphism. B ↦ B_!! preserves faithful flatness of morphisms but not flatness (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Ring structure on V ⊕ B_!: (v, b)(v', b') = (vv', vb' + v'b + bb'); I is an ideal (GR 2.2.23).
2. Adjunction: an A-algebra map φ : B → C^a gives B_! → C (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints) and with V → C a ring map V ⊕ B_! → C killing I; conversely localize (GR Proposition 2.2.27).
3. B ≅ (B_!!)^a: the kernel of V ⊕ B_! → B_!! is the image of m̃, which is almost isomorphic to m ⊂ V (GR Remark 2.2.26).
4. Colimits: left adjoint; tensor products are pushouts (GR Remark 2.2.28(i)); B_!! → B_* almost isomorphism (Bhatt Remark 4.2.8).

**Acceptance.**

- (V^a)_!! ≅ V: (V^a)_! = m̃ and (V ⊕ m̃)/I ≅ V via (v, x ⊗ y) ↦ v + xy.
- For m flat (valuation or root setups with ϖ a nonzerodivisor), every almost algebra is exact.

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| --- | --- | --- |

| `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekAdj` | universal-property | Over an almost algebra A: B ↦ B_!! is left adjoint to R ↦ R^a from A_!!-algebras to A-algebras. |
| `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekUnitIso` | equivalence | B ≅ (B.shriekShriek)^a. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsExact` | data | B is exact: 0 → S.tilde → V ⊕ B_! → B_!! → 0 is exact. |
| `Almost.Algebra.isExact_of_bijective` | relation | If S.tilde → S.ideal is bijective (e.g. m flat), every almost algebra is exact. |
| `Almost.Algebra.isExact_prod` | example | V^a × B is exact for every B. |
| `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_preservesColimits` | instance | shriekShriek preserves colimits; shriekShriekTensorIso : (B ⊗_A C)_!! ≅ B_!! ⊗_{A_!!} C_!!. |
| `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriekToElements` | data | The natural map B_!! → B_*, an almost isomorphism. |
| `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_faithfullyFlat_iff` | characterisation | φ faithfully flat ↔ φ_!! faithfully flat (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness). |

- `Almost.Algebra.shriekShriek_test_not_flat` (non-example): For S = ofValuationRing V with residue field k: the projection V × V → V is flat but its image under (−)^a then (−)_!! is V ×_k V → V, which is not flat (GR Remark 3.1.3(ii)); so flatness of almost algebra maps cannot be defined through (−)_!!.

#### `almost-finitely-generated-and-presented` — Almost finitely generated, uniformly almost finitely generated and almost finitely presented modules

*definition* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Finiteness`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module, M = N^a over A = R^a. N^a is almost finitely generated if for every finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m there are n and an R-linear φ : Rⁿ → N with m₀·coker φ = 0; uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n if one n works for all m₀; almost finitely presented if for every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m there is a complex R^k →ψ Rⁿ →φ N with m₀·coker φ = 0 and m₀·ker φ ⊆ im ψ. These conditions depend only on N^a (not on the representative N), and agree with GR's definitions through the uniform structure on isomorphism classes (GR Definition 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.10); under condition (A) (e.g. root and valuation setups) they are equivalent to Sch12's ε-formulation: for every ε ∈ m there is a finitely generated (presented) R-module N_ε and N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion). For an arbitrary almost algebra A they are applied to M_* over A_* (P0/almost-algebras). Pinned: our uniform notion (maps from Rⁿ with small cokernel) implies GR's U_n(A) in general and is equivalent to it under (A) (GR Remark 2.3.9).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; R a V-algebra; N an R-module.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Definitions as stated, with finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m (Mathlib `Submodule.FG`).
2. Independence of the representative: if N → N' is an almost isomorphism, replace m₀ by m₁ with m₀ ⊆ m₁² ... using m = m²: generators of N' multiplied by elements of m lift to N (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); the kernel condition for presentations is handled as in GR Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12.
3. Comparison with GR 2.3.8: GR Proposition 2.3.10(i) and (ii)(c) are exactly our conditions for almost finitely generated and presented modules.

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Example 4.9 / Bhatt Example 4.2.7: for K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): L°a is almost finitely presented and uniformly almost finitely generated with bound 2 over K°a.
- In the classical setup the notions are finite generation and finite presentation.

| `Almost.Module.UniformlyAlmostFG` | data | ∃ n, the same with n independent of m₀. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostFP` | data | ∀ m₀ f.g., ∃ complex R^k → Rⁿ → N with m₀ • coker = 0 and m₀ • ker ≤ range. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostFG.of_almostIso` | extensionality | The predicates depend only on N^a: they are invariant under almost isomorphisms. |
| `Almost.Module.almostFG_of_finite` | compatibility | Module.Finite R N → AlmostFG; Module.FinitePresentation R N → AlmostFP. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostFG.extension` | relation | Extensions of almost f.g. (f.p.) modules are almost f.g. (f.p.); for M almost f.p., a quotient is almost f.p. iff the kernel is almost f.g. (GR Lemma 2.3.17). |

| `Almost.Module.almostFG_iff_epsilon` | characterisation | Under condition (A): AlmostFG ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃ f.g. N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion). |

#### `almost-flat-projective-finiteness` — Flat, faithfully flat, almost projective and almost finite projective almost modules

*definition* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Flat`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. M is flat if M ⊗_A − : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact, faithfully flat if moreover M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 implies N ≅ 0, almost projective if alHom_A(M, −) : A-Mod → A-Mod is exact (GR Definition 2.4.4), and almost finite projective if it is almost projective and almost finitely generated (P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented); 'uniformly almost finite projective' adds a uniform bound. Pinned convention: categorical projectivity (Hom(M, −) exact) is never used — Almost.Module S has no nonzero projective objects when V is local and m ≠ V (GR Example 2.4.5). For a V-algebra R and an R-module N: N flat (faithfully flat, projective) implies N^a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) over R^a (GR 2.4.8). Characterisations: Tor and Ext criteria (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion), ε-factorisation (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation), finite projective = flat + almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost V-algebra; A-Mod as in P0/almost-algebras.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Define the three predicates on objects of A-Mod through the functors M ⊗_A − and alHom_A(M, −) (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom for A-Mod).
2. Compatibility with honest modules: if N is R-flat then N ⊗_R − preserves almost zero modules and exact sequences, so it induces an exact functor on the Serre quotient (GR 2.4.8); faithfulness from m ⊗ (N ⊗ X) = 0 ⇔ m ⊗ X = 0 for N faithfully flat; projective N is a summand of a free module and alHom(R^{(I)}, −) = ∏ is exact.
3. Almost projective ⇒ flat: multiplication by ε factors through a free module (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)).
4. Stability: tensor products and base change preserve flatness and almost projectivity (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii)); transitivity along almost algebra maps (GR Lemma 2.4.7).

**Acceptance.**

- Over S = (K°, K°°): M is flat over K°a iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)); K°a is flat, (K°/ϖ)^a is not.
- V^a is almost projective and flat but not a projective object when V is local and m ≠ V.

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| `Almost.Module.Flat` | data | M ⊗_A − preserves finite limits (it is exact). |
| `Almost.Module.FaithfullyFlat` | data | Flat and M ⊗_A N ≅ 0 → N ≅ 0. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective` | data | alHom_A(M, −) preserves epimorphisms. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostFiniteProjective` | data | AlmostProjective ∧ AlmostFG; uniformly with bound n. |
| `Almost.Module.flat_toAlmost` | compatibility | Module.Flat R N → Flat ((toAlmost _).obj N); likewise FaithfullyFlat and Projective → AlmostProjective. |
| `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective.flat` | relation | AlmostProjective M → Flat M. |
| `Almost.Module.Flat.tensor` | structure | Flat and AlmostProjective are stable under ⊗_A and under base change B ⊗_A −. |
| `Almost.Module.Flat.trans` | functoriality | If B is a flat (almost projective, almost f.g., almost f.p.) A-algebra and M such a B-module, M is such an A-module (GR Lemma 2.4.7). |
| `Almost.Module.flat_iff_tor` | characterisation | Flat (N^a) ↔ ∀ X i, 0 < i → IsAlmostZero (Tor_i^R(N, X)) (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion). |
| `Almost.Module.almostProjective_iff_factor` | characterisation | For M almost f.g.: AlmostProjective M ↔ ∀ ε ∈ m, ∃ n u v, v ∘ u = ε • 𝟙 through A^n (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation). |
| `Almost.Module.almostFiniteProjective_iff` | characterisation | AlmostFiniteProjective M ↔ Flat M ∧ AlmostFP M (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff). |

- `Almost.Module.AlmostProjective_test_not_projective` (non-example): For V local with S.ideal ≠ ⊤: (toAlmost S).obj V is AlmostProjective but not Projective in Almost.Module S; a definition using categorical projectivity would exclude the unit object.
- `Almost.Module.Flat_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V and a V-module N: Flat (N^a) ↔ Module.Flat V N, FaithfullyFlat (N^a) ↔ Module.FaithfullyFlat V N, and AlmostProjective (N^a) ↔ Module.Projective V N.

**Uses.**

- Sch12 Proposition 4.10, Definition 4.13; GR 3.1.1: finite projective modules and flat/étale morphisms of almost algebras
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected, D2/v-descent-of-functions: (S⁺/ϖ)^a is faithfully flat over (R⁺/ϖ)^a (automatic flatness)

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Definition 2.4.4, p. 23.

  > Definition 2.4.4. Let M be an A-module. (i) We say that M is flat (resp. faithfully flat) if the functor N 7→ M ⊗A N, from the category of A-modules to itself is exact (resp. exact and faithful). (ii) We say that M is almost projective if the functor N 7→ alHomA (M, N) is exact.

  The definitions.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Example 2.4.5, p. 23.

  > As an example, suppose that V is local; then every projective V -module is free, so if m 6= V the condition P = mP implies P = 0, ergo, there are no non-trivial projective V a -modules.

  Why categorical projectivity is not used.

#### `almost-flatness-tor-criterion` — Tor and Ext criteria for almost flatness and almost projectivity

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Flat`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, R a V-algebra and N an R-module. (i) For R-modules M, N and i ≥ 0 there are natural isomorphisms Tor_i^{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Tor_i^R(M, N)^a and alExt^i_{R^a}(M^a, N^a) ≅ Ext^i_R(M, N)^a, where Tor^{R^a} and alExt are the derived functors of ⊗ and alHom on R^a-Mod (computed by flat resp. injective resolutions). (ii) N^a is flat over R^a iff Tor_i^R(N, X) is almost zero for all R-modules X and all i > 0; (iii) N^a is almost projective iff Ext^i_R(N, X) is almost zero for all X and i > 0; (iv) N^a is faithfully flat iff it is flat and, for every R-module X, N ⊗_R X almost zero implies X almost zero. (v) An almost projective module is flat.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; R a V-algebra.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Derived functors on R^a-Mod exist: enough injectives and enough flat and almost projective objects (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints; GR 2.4.8, 2.4.10); bounded above exact complexes of flat (almost projective) objects are acyclic for ⊗ (alHom(−, M)).
2. (i): the exact functor (−)^a takes a flat resolution of M to a flat resolution of M^a (GR 2.4.8), whence (2.4.11); for Ext use the adjunction between (−)_! and (−)^a on derived categories (GR 2.4.9, Lemma 2.4.14(i)).
3. (ii)-(iii): M is flat (almost projective) iff all higher Tor (alExt) vanish (GR Remark 2.4.12(i)); combine with (i) and P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (vanishing of M^a iff M almost zero).
4. (iv): faithfulness of N^a ⊗ − means N^a ⊗ X^a ≅ 0 ⇒ X^a ≅ 0.
5. (v): multiplication by ε ∈ m on an almost projective M factors through a free module (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).

**Acceptance.**

- Over S = (K°, K°°): M^a flat iff Tor_1(M, K°/ϖ) = M[ϖ] is almost zero, iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.9.11: A°/ϖ → B°/ϖ almost faithfully flat means Tor_i^{A°/ϖ}(M, B°/ϖ) almost zero for i > 0; by (ii) this is flatness of (B°/ϖ)^a over (A°/ϖ)^a.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, (2.4.10), p. 24.

  > We denote by TorA i (M, −) (resp. alExtiA (M, −), resp. alExtiA (−, M)) the corresponding derived functors.

  The derived functors.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Remark 2.4.12(i), p. 24.

  > Remark 2.4.12. (i) Clearly, an A-module M is flat (resp. almost projective) if and only if

  Tor/Ext vanishing criterion.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(i), p. 19.

  > (i) The module M is flat over K ◦a if and only if M∗ is flat over K ◦ if and only if M∗ has no $-torsion.

  The field case in Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i), deduced from the Tor criterion.

- Kedlaya, *Sheaves, stacks, and shtukas* (AWS 2017), §2.9, Lemma 2.9.11, p. 74.

  > and A◦ /($) → B ◦ /($) is almost faithfully flat; that is, for any A◦ /($)-module M , the

  Tor formulation of almost (faithful) flatness used by consumers.


#### `almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation` — Almost projectivity via ε-factorisations through free modules

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Flat`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and M an A-module. (i) M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there is a set I and A-linear maps M →u A^{(I)} →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M. (ii) If M is almost finitely generated, M is almost projective iff for every ε ∈ m there are n(ε) ∈ ℕ and M →u Aⁿ →v M with v ∘ u = ε·1_M; M is uniformly almost finite projective with bound n iff n can be taken independent of ε (Kedlaya–Liu's definition of (uniformly) almost finite projective).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; M an A-module.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. ⇐: applying alExt^i(−, N) to M → A^{(I)} → M shows that ε kills alExt^i(M, N) for i > 0; as ε ∈ m is arbitrary these are almost zero, hence zero in A-Mod (P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion).
2. ⇒ (finitely generated case, GR proof of Lemma 2.4.15): choose φ_ε : Aⁿ → M with ε·coker φ_ε = 0, factor through its image M_ε; almost projectivity makes alHom(M, Aⁿ) → alHom(M, M_ε) an epimorphism, so for δ ∈ m the map δ·γ_ε (with ε·1_M = j_ε ∘ γ_ε) lifts to u_{εδ} : M → Aⁿ; then φ_ε ∘ u_{εδ} = εδ·1_M; products εδ span m.
3. ⇒ (general case): the same argument with a free module A^{(I)} surjecting onto M.

**Acceptance.**

- For P = L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): the maps L° → (K°)² → L° with composite p^{1/p^{n−1}} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7) exhibit P as uniformly almost finite projective with bound 2.
- KL Definition 5.5.8 takes (ii) as the definition of almost finite projective.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.15, p. 25.

  > Lemma 2.4.15. Let M be an almost finitely generated A-module. Then M is almost projective if and only if, for arbitrary ε ∈ m, there exist n(ε) ∈ N and A-linear morphisms

  Statement (ii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.15, p. 25.

  > such that vε ◦ uε = ε · 1M .

  The factorisation condition.

- Kedlaya–Liu, *Relative p-adic Hodge theory: foundations* (arXiv:1301.0792v5), arXiv v5, §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132.

  > An A-module B is almost finite projective if for each t ∈ mA , there exist a finite free A-module F and some morphisms B → F → B of A-modules whose composition is multiplication by t.

  The same condition as a definition.


#### `almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion` — The ε-criterion for almost finite generation and presentation under condition (A)

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Finiteness`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup satisfying condition (A) (m is a filtered union of principal ideals; e.g. root setups and valuation setups), R a V-algebra and N an R-module. Then N^a is almost finitely generated (resp. almost finitely presented) iff for every ε ∈ m there are a finitely generated (resp. finitely presented) R-module N_ε and an R-linear map N_ε → N whose kernel and cokernel are killed by ε; and N^a is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound n iff for every ε ∈ m there is Rⁿ → N with cokernel killed by ε. In a general basic setup the same equivalences hold with ε replaced by finitely generated subideals m₀ ⊆ m, which is the definition of P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup with condition (A).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Under (A) every finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m lies in a principal ideal εV ⊆ m, and every ε ∈ m generates a finitely generated subideal; so the m₀-conditions and the ε-conditions are equivalent for generation (take N_ε := image, kernel 0).
2. Presentation: GR Proposition 2.3.10(ii), equivalence of (a), (b), (c), with (b) the ε, δ-formulation; from a complex R^k → Rⁿ → N with ε-small cokernel and δ-small homology one builds N_ε := Rⁿ/im ψ and conversely (Claims 2.3.11–2.3.12).
3. Uniform bound: GR Remark 2.3.9.

**Acceptance.**

- For S = ofValuationRing K°, Sch12 Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii) is this ε-formulation.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.3, Remark 2.3.9, p. 18.

  > Remark 2.3.9. Under condition (A), an A-module M lies in Un (A) if and only if, for every ε ∈ m there exists an A-linear morphism An → M whose cokernel is killed by ε.

  The uniform ε-criterion under (A).

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Definition/Proposition 4.7(iii), p. 19.

  > (iii) If R is a K ◦ -algebra and N is an R-module, then M = N a is said to be an almost finitely generated (resp. almost finitely presented) Ra -module if and only if for all

  Sch12's ε-formulation (citing GR book Definition 2.3.8, Remark 2.3.9(i), Corollary 2.3.13).


#### `almost-finite-projective-iff` — Flat + almost finitely presented ⟺ almost projective + almost finitely generated

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Flat`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and M an A-module. (i) If M is almost projective and almost finitely generated, M is almost finitely presented (and flat). (ii) If M is flat and almost finitely presented, M is almost projective. Hence 'finite projective' in Sch12's sense (flat and almost finitely presented) coincides with almost finite projective (almost projective and almost finitely generated). (iii) If A → B is a monomorphism of almost algebras and M is an almost finitely generated flat A-module with B ⊗_A M almost finitely presented over B, then M is almost finitely presented.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (ii) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(ii): for ε, δ ∈ m pick A^m →ψ Aⁿ →φ M with ε·coker φ = 0 = δ·(ker φ/im ψ); P := coker ψ_* is a finitely presented A_*-module; flatness and Lemma 2.4.17 (Tor_1 of the transposed presentation) give γ·φ = w ∘ v through a free module for every γ ∈ m; assemble α, β with β ∘ α = εδγ·1_M and conclude by P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation.
2. (i) GR proof of Proposition 2.4.18(i): for a finitely generated m₀ ⊆ m pick φ : A^r → P with m₀·coker φ = 0; ε_i·1_P lifts to P → A^r/ker φ and, P being almost projective, ε_jψ_i lifts to A^r; Claim 2.3.11 gives finitely generated submodules of ker φ containing ε_iε_j ker φ, so m₀²·ker φ lies in a finitely generated submodule.
3. (iii) GR Proposition 2.4.19.

**Acceptance.**

- For the classical setup this is the statement that finitely presented flat modules are projective and finitely generated projective modules are finitely presented.
- Sch12 Proposition 4.10 is the case S = (K°, K°°).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.18, p. 26.

  > Proposition 2.4.18. Let A be a V a -algebra. (i) Every almost finitely generated projective A-module is almost finitely presented. (ii) Every almost finitely presented flat A-module is almost projective.

  Statement (i)-(ii).

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Proposition 4.10, p. 20.

  > module M is flat and almost finitely presented if and only if it is almost projective and almost finitely generated.

  Sch12's formulation (citing GR Proposition 2.4.18, same number in the book).

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, after Proposition 4.10, p. 20.

  > By abuse of notation, we call such A-modules M finite projective in the following, a terminology not used in [14].

  Sch12's name 'finite projective'.


#### `tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective` — E ⊗ alHom(F, N) → alHom(F, E ⊗ N) is an isomorphism for almost finite projective E or F

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Trace`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and E, F, N A-modules. The natural map E ⊗_A alHom_A(F, N) → alHom_A(F, E ⊗_A N) is (i) an isomorphism if E or F is almost finite projective, if E is flat and F almost finitely presented, if F is almost projective and E almost finitely presented, or if E is almost projective and F almost finitely generated; (ii) a monomorphism if E is flat and F almost finitely generated, or if E is almost projective; (iii) an epimorphism if F is almost projective and E almost finitely generated. Consequences: for P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism, P is reflexive (P ≅ P**), and B ⊗_A alHom_A(P, N) ≅ alHom_B(B ⊗_A P, B ⊗_A N) for every A-algebra B.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Free finite case: alHom(Aⁿ, N) ≅ Nⁿ and the map is an isomorphism.
2. Almost finite projective F: for ε ∈ m apply the natural transformation to F →u_ε A^{I(ε)} →v_ε F (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation) with I(ε) finite; a diagram chase shows that kernel and cokernel are killed by ε, hence almost zero, hence zero (GR proof of Lemma 2.4.29).
3. The remaining cases reduce, via almost elements and ε-approximations, to classical statements for finitely generated (presented) modules and free modules (Bourbaki Algèbre commutative I §2 Prop. 10), as in GR.
4. ω_{P/A} is the case E = P, N = A; reflexivity and base change: GR Lemma 2.4.31.

**Acceptance.**

- For P = (Rⁿ)^a free: ω_{P/A} is the usual identification Rⁿ ⊗ (Rⁿ)^∨ ≅ End(Rⁿ) after almostification.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.29, p. 27.

  > Lemma 2.4.29. Let E, F , N be three A-modules. (i) The morphism (2.4.27) is an isomorphism in the following cases :

  Statement.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.29(i)(b), p. 27.

  > (b) when either E or F is almost finitely generated projective;

  The case used for traces.

#### `almost-dual-and-trace` — Duals, traces of endomorphisms and the trace form of an almost finite projective algebra

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Trace`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. For an A-module M, the dual is M* := alHom_A(M, A) with evaluation ev_{M/A} : M ⊗_A M* → A. For P almost finite projective, ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* → End_A(P)^a is an isomorphism (P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective) and the trace is tr_{P/A} := ev_{P/A} ∘ ω_{P/A}⁻¹ : End_A(P)^a → A. For an A-algebra B which is almost finite projective as an A-module, μ : B → End_A(B)^a (b ↦ multiplication by b, defined on almost elements) gives the almost trace Tr_{B/A} := tr_{B/A} ∘ μ : B → A, the trace form t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A, and τ_{B/A} : B → B*; t_{B/A} is a perfect pairing if τ_{B/A} is an isomorphism. Properties: tr(ψ∘φ) = tr(φ∘ψ); tr(φ ⊗ ψ) = tr(φ)·tr(ψ); additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules; Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}; Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}; τ is B-linear and compatible with base change. Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` (zero on non-free modules) is not used for almost finite projective modules; it agrees with tr on free modules.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; P almost finite projective; B an A-algebra, almost finite projective as A-module.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Define P*, ev and ω on almost elements (GR Definition 2.4.23, 2.4.26); ω iso by P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective; tr := ev ∘ ω⁻¹ and ζ_P := ω⁻¹(1_P) (GR Definition 4.1.1).
2. Cyclicity: reduce by A-linearity to rank-one maps x ↦ n·α(x), then compute (GR Lemma 4.1.2); multiplicativity (Lemma 4.1.3); additivity via the ε-split pullback trick (Proposition 4.1.4).
3. Algebra traces: μ is a B-linear monomorphism (GR 4.1.7); base change and transitivity (Proposition 4.1.8); τ_{B/A} and base change (Lemma 4.1.13).
4. Compatibility with free modules: for P = (Rⁿ)^a, ω and ev are almostifications of Mathlib's `dualTensorHom` and evaluation, so tr = (LinearMap.trace)^a.

**Acceptance.**

- For B = (Rⁿ)^a with R-algebra structure free of rank n: Tr_{B/A} = (Algebra.trace R Rⁿ)^a.
- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)): Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2 and t_{L°a/K°a} is perfect, while the honest trace form on R_n = K° ⊕ p^{1/2p^n}K° has discriminant 4p^{1/p^n} (Bhatt Example 4.2.7).

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Almost.Module.dual` | constructor | M* := alHom_A(M, A), with evaluation M ⊗_A M* ⟶ A. |
| `Almost.Module.dualTensorHomIso` | equivalence | For P almost finite projective: ω_{P/A} : P ⊗_A P* ≅ End_A(P)^a. |
| `Almost.Module.trace` | constructor | tr_{P/A} : End_A(P)^a ⟶ A := ev ∘ ω⁻¹. |
| `Almost.Module.trace_comp_comm` | relation | tr_{M/A}(ψ ∘ φ) = tr_{N/A}(φ ∘ ψ). |
| `Almost.Module.trace_tensor` | relation | tr_{M⊗N/A}(φ ⊗ ψ) = tr_{M/A}(φ) · tr_{N/A}(ψ). |
| `Almost.Module.trace_additive` | relation | Additivity on short exact sequences of almost finite projective modules with compatible endomorphisms. |
| `Almost.Module.isReflexive` | characterisation | P ≅ P** for P almost finite projective. |
| `Almost.Algebra.trace` | constructor | Tr_{B/A} : B ⟶ A for B almost finite projective over A. |
| `Almost.Algebra.trace_baseChange` | compatibility | Tr_{C⊗_A B/C} = 1_C ⊗ Tr_{B/A}. |
| `Almost.Algebra.trace_trans` | functoriality | Tr_{C/A} = Tr_{B/A} ∘ Tr_{C/B}. |
| `Almost.Algebra.trace_of_iso` | simp | If A → B is an isomorphism, Tr_{B/A} is its inverse. |
| `Almost.Algebra.traceForm` | constructor | t_{B/A} := Tr_{B/A} ∘ μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B ⟶ A and τ_{B/A} : B ⟶ B*. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsPerfectTraceForm` | data | τ_{B/A} is an isomorphism. |
| `Almost.Algebra.traceFormDual_baseChange` | compatibility | η ∘ (1_C ⊗ τ_{B/A}) = τ_{C⊗B/C} (GR Lemma 4.1.13). |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `Almost.Module.trace_test_free` (compatibility): For P = (toAlmost _).obj (Fin n → R): Almost.Module.trace P ((toAlmost _).map f) = (toAlmost _).map (LinearMap.trace R _ f) (Mathlib's trace), and for a free finite R-algebra R', Almost.Algebra.trace = (Algebra.trace R R')^a.
- `Almost.Algebra.trace_test_quadratic` (computation): For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): Tr_{L°a/K°a}(1) = 2 and IsPerfectTraceForm (L°a/K°a).
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_zero` (degenerate): For P = 0, tr_{P/A} = 0; for B = 0, Tr_{B/A} = 0 and t_{B/A} is perfect.
- `Almost.Module.trace_test_not_linearMap_trace` (non-example): For P = L°a over K°a (L° is not a free K°-module), (LinearMap.trace K° L°)^a = 0 ≠ tr_{P/A}(1) = 2: the almost trace cannot be defined through Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` of a representative.

**Uses.**

- Sch12 Definition 4.14 and Theorem 4.16 (P0/trace-form-criterion): finite étale iff the trace form is perfect
- KL Definition 5.5.8 and Theorem 5.5.9: almost finite étale defined by an almost perfect trace pairing
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p: S₀^⊥ via the perfect trace pairing, and the ε-splittings built from the diagonal idempotent and the trace
- GR 4.3 (P0/rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective): χ_P(X) = Σ tr(Λ^i 1_P) X^i determines the rank
- GR Corollary 4.1.11: the trace of a faithfully flat finite étale map is an epimorphism

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tensor-hom-comparison-almost-projective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`, `mathlib:LinearMap.trace`, `mathlib:Algebra.trace`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, Definition 4.1.1, p. 72.

  > Definition 4.1.1. Let P be an almost finitely generated projective A-module. Then ωP/A is an isomorphism by lemma 2.4.29(b).

  ω_{P/A} is an isomorphism.

  tr_{P/A} := ev ∘ ω⁻¹.

  > Lemma 4.1.2. Let M, N be almost finitely generated projective A-modules, and φ : M → N, ψ : N → M two A-linear morphisms. Then : (i) trM/A (ψ ◦ φ) = trN/A (φ ◦ ψ).

  Cyclicity.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, (4.1.7), p. 74.

  > will also be called the almost trace morphism of the A-algebra B.

  Tr_{B/A} := tr_{B/A} ∘ μ.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, Proposition 4.1.8(ii)-(iii), p. 74.

  > (ii) If C any other A-algebra, then TrC⊗A B/C = 1C ⊗A TrB/A . (iii) If C is an almost finite projective B-algebra, then TrC/A = TrB/A ◦ TrC/B .

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, (4.1.12), p. 75.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Remark 4.15, p. 20.

#### `rank-decomposition-of-finite-projective` — Rank decomposition of uniformly almost finite projective modules

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Trace`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup satisfying condition (B) (k-th powers generate m; implied by (A)), A an almost V-algebra and P a uniformly almost finite projective A-module. Then P has finite rank: Λ^r_A P = 0 for some r. For P almost projective with Λ^r_A P = 0 there is a unique decomposition A ≅ A_0 × A_1 × ⋯ × A_{r−1} such that P_i := P ⊗_A A_i has constant rank i over A_i: Λ^{i+1}_{A_i} P_i = 0 and Λ^i_{A_i} P_i is an invertible A_i-module (P_i ⊗ P_i* ≅ A_i). The decomposition is compatible with base change A → A'.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup with condition (B) (used for uniform continuity of Λ^r, GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi), and for Proposition 4.3.4); root and valuation setups satisfy (A) hence (B).
- Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 4.11 cites GR Proposition 4.3.27 and Remark 4.3.10(i) in book numbering; the arXiv v3 statements with these numbers are the ones quoted here.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Finite rank: a uniformly almost finitely generated module with bound n lies in the closure U_n(A) of the modules generated by n almost elements; under (B) the operation Λ^{n+1} is uniformly continuous (GR Lemma 2.3.7(vi)) and vanishes on modules generated by n elements, so Λ^{n+1}P = 0 (GR Remark 4.3.10(i)).
2. Formal rank: χ_P(X) = Σ_i tr(Λ^i 1_P) X^i defines an endomorphism of Ĝ_m (GR Corollary 4.3.8, from Proposition 4.3.4 whose proof uses (B)); for finite rank it is (1 + X)^α for a locally constant α (Remark 4.3.10(ii)).
3. Decomposition: induction on r, the case r = 2 being GR Lemma 4.3.12, the inductive step using Lemma 4.3.26 (Λ²(Λ^{r−1} P) = 0) (GR Proposition 4.3.27).
4. Uniqueness and base change: the idempotents are determined by χ_P, which is compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.3.2(i)).

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a over K°a (L = K(√p)): r = 3, A = A_2 (constant rank 2).
- For A = K°a × K°a and P = K°a × 0: A_1 = first factor, A_0 = second factor.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `mathlib:Module.Invertible`, `mathlib:ExteriorAlgebra.exteriorPower`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.3, Proposition 4.3.27, p. 88.

  > Proposition 4.3.27. Let P be an almost projective A-module of finite rank; say that ΛrA P = 0. There exists a natural decomposition A ≃ A0 × A1 × ... × Ar−1 such that Pi := P ⊗A Ai is an Ai -module of constant rank equal to i for every i = 0, ..., r − 1.

  The decomposition.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.3, Remark 4.3.10(i), p. 85.

  > Remark 4.3.10. (i): It follows easily from lemma 2.3.7(vi) that every uniformly almost finitely generated projective A-module is of finite rank.

  Finite rank of uniformly almost finite projective modules.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.3, Definition 4.3.9(iv), p. 85.

  > (iv) Let r ∈ N; we say that P has constant rank equal to r if Λr+1

  Constant rank.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.11, p. 20.

  > Theorem 4.11 ([14, Proposition 4.3.27, Remark 4.3.10 (i)]). Let A be a K ◦a -algebra, and let M be a uniformly finite projective A-module.

  Sch12's statement over (K°, K°°).


#### `almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras` — Flat, unramified, étale and finite étale morphisms of almost algebras

*definition* **Planet:** *Almost finite étale algebras*. Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Etale`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost V-algebras; view B as a B ⊗_A B-algebra through the multiplication μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B, with kernel I_{B/A}. Following GR Definition 3.1.1: φ is flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) if B is a flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) A-module; (uniformly) almost finite if B is a (uniformly) almost finitely generated A-module; weakly unramified (unramified) if B is a flat (almost projective) B ⊗_A B-module; weakly étale (étale) if flat and weakly unramified (unramified). φ is finite étale if it is étale and B is an almost finitely presented A-module (Sch12 Definition 4.13; GR's A-Ét_afp; Kedlaya–Liu's and Bhatt's 'almost finite étale'); then B is almost finite projective over A (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff). A_fet denotes the full subcategory of A-algebras that are finite étale over A. Equivalent descriptions: unramified iff there is a diagonal idempotent e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with μ(e) = 1 and I_{B/A,*}·e = 0 (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation, Sch12's definition); for B almost finite projective over A, étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} is perfect (P0/trace-form-criterion). Pinned: 'finite étale' always means étale and almost finitely presented; in the classical setup it is Mathlib's finite étale (P0/finite-etale-localizes), while GR's 'étale' without finiteness is more general than EGA étale (GR Remark 3.1.3(i)).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras; module notions as in P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness and P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented, applied to B as an A-module and as a B ⊗_A B-module.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Define the predicates on morphisms of Almost.Algebra S through the module structures of B over A and over B ⊗_A B (μ_{B/A} a morphism of almost algebras).
2. A_fet := full subcategory of Under A on the finite étale morphisms.
3. The characterisations are P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation (GR Proposition 3.1.4), P0/trace-form-criterion (GR Theorem 4.1.14) and P0/etale-morphisms-stability (GR Lemma 3.1.2).

**Acceptance.**

- Bhatt Example 4.3.2: for K = completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), L = K(√p), p ≠ 2: L°a is finite étale over K°a; the diagonal idempotent e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1) satisfies p^{1/p^n} e ∈ L° ⊗ L° for all n, so e ∈ (L°a ⊗ L°a)_*, although e ∉ L° ⊗_{K°} L°.
- Sch12 Theorem 4.17 and GR Theorem 5.3.27 are statements about A_fet (P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras).

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsFlat` | data | φ : A ⟶ B is flat (faithfully flat, almost projective) if B is so as an A-module. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsUnramified` | data | B is almost projective over B ⊗_A B via μ_{B/A}; IsWeaklyUnramified: flat instead of almost projective. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale` | data | IsFlat ∧ IsUnramified; IsWeaklyEtale: IsFlat ∧ IsWeaklyUnramified. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale` | data | IsEtale ∧ AlmostFP B over A. |
| `Almost.Algebra.FiniteEtale` | data | A_fet: the full subcategory of Under A on finite étale morphisms. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.baseChange` | compatibility | Flat, unramified, étale, weakly étale and finite étale morphisms are stable under base change A → A'. |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsEtale.comp` | functoriality | and under composition (P0/etale-morphisms-stability). |
| `Almost.Algebra.isUnramified_iff_exists_idempotent` | characterisation | IsUnramified φ ↔ ∃ e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* idempotent, μ(e) = 1, I_{B/A,*} e = 0 (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation). |
| `Almost.Algebra.isEtale_iff_isPerfectTraceForm` | characterisation | For B almost finite projective over A: IsEtale φ ↔ IsPerfectTraceForm φ (P0/trace-form-criterion). |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale.almostFiniteProjective` | relation | B is almost finite projective over A. |
| `Almost.Algebra.isFiniteEtale_toAlmost` | compatibility | Mathlib finite étale R → R' gives a finite étale R^a → R'^a (P0/finite-etale-localizes). |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_quadratic` (computation): For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, L = K(√p): IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost _).map (algebraMap K° L°)) over S = ofValuationRing K°.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_idempotent_not_honest` (non-example): In the same example the diagonal idempotent is an almost element of L°a ⊗ L°a but does not lie in L° ⊗_{K°} L° (only p^{1/p^n}e does, for every n): a definition requiring an honest idempotent of B_* ⊗_{A_*} B_* would reject L°a/K°a.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V and a V-algebra map R → R': IsFiniteEtale ((toAlmost S).map f) ↔ Algebra.Etale R R' ∧ Module.Finite R R' (Mathlib).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsFiniteEtale_test_trivial` (degenerate): 𝟙 A, A → 0 and the diagonal A → A × A are finite étale.

**Uses.**

- P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras (Sch12 Theorem 4.17, GR Theorem 5.3.27): the lifting equivalence A_fet ≅ (A/ϖ)_fet
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem (ECD Theorem 6.1(iii), KL Theorem 5.5.9): S° is almost finite étale over R°
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (Sch12 Propositions 5.22-5.23): finite étale algebras over perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras and S°a/R°a in characteristic p
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the chain R_fet ← A_fet ≅ Ā_fet ≅ A♭_fet → R♭_fet
- P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (GR Theorem 3.2.18): weakly étale and étale algebras lift along nilpotent ideals
- P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent: étale and weakly étale algebras descend along faithfully flat maps

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Algebra.FormallyUnramified`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Definition 3.1.1(iii)-(iv), p. 39.

  > (iii) We say that φ is weakly unramified (resp. unramified) if B is a flat (resp. almost projective) B ⊗A B-module (via the morphism µB/A defined above).

  Weakly unramified and unramified.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Definition 3.1.1(iv), p. 39.

  > (iv) φ is weakly étale (resp. étale) if it is flat and weakly unramified (resp. unramified).

  Weakly étale and étale.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Definition 4.13, p. 20.

  > Definition 4.13. A morphism A → B of K ◦a -algebras is said to be finite étale if it is étale and B is an almost finitely presented A-module.

  Finite étale = étale and almost finitely presented.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, (3.2.27), p. 46.

  > 3.2.27. We denote by A-Étafp the full subcategory of A-Ét consisting of all étale A-algebras B such that B is almost finitely presented as an A-module.

  GR's name A-Ét_afp for A_fet.

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.3, Definition 4.3.1, p. 25.

  > Definition 4.3.1. A map A → B of Ra -algebras is almost finite etale if

  Bhatt's 'almost finite étale', the same notion.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39.

  > Then we caution the reader that our notion of “étale morphism” is more general than the usual one, as defined in [40].

  GR-étale is more general than EGA-étale in the classical limit.


#### `unramified-idempotent-characterisation` — Unramified ⟺ existence of the diagonal idempotent

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Etale`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. φ is unramified (B almost projective over B ⊗_A B) iff there is an almost element e_{B/A} ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with e² = e, μ_{B/A}(e) = 1 and x·e = 0 for every x ∈ (I_{B/A})_*. The element e is unique, and B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B as B ⊗_A B-algebras (I_{B/A} with unit 1 − e). More generally, for an ideal I of an almost algebra A, A/I is almost projective over A iff I is generated by an idempotent of A_*, which is then unique.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. ⇒: for ε ∈ m almost projectivity gives an ε-splitting u_ε : B → B ⊗_A B of μ with μ ∘ u_ε = ε·1_B (P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation); e_ε := u_ε(1) satisfies e_ε² = ε e_ε, μ(e_ε) = ε and I_*·e_ε = 0 by B ⊗_A B-linearity.
2. δ e_ε = ε e_δ for ε, δ ∈ m, so ε ⊗ δ ↦ δ·e_ε is a well defined map m ⊗_V m → (B ⊗_A B)_*, i.e. an almost element e (GR (3.1.7)), with the required properties.
3. ⇐: u(b) := e·(1 ⊗ b) is B ⊗_A B-linear by the annihilation property and splits μ, so B is a direct summand, hence almost projective (GR Lemma 2.4.15).
4. Uniqueness and the product decomposition: GR Corollary 3.1.9 and Remark 3.1.8.

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the idempotent is Bhatt's e = (1/(2√p ⊗ 1))(1 ⊗ √p + √p ⊗ 1).
- In the classical setup with B finite étale over A, ker μ is a finitely generated idempotent ideal, generated by the idempotent 1 − e (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`, `mathlib:IsIdempotentElem`, `mathlib:Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Proposition 3.1.4, p. 40.

  > Proposition 3.1.4. A morphism φ : A → B is unramified if and only if there exists an almost element eB/A ∈ B ⊗A B∗ such that (i) e2B/A = eB/A ; (ii) µB/A (eB/A ) = 1; (iii) x · eB/A = 0 for all x ∈ IB/A∗ .

  The characterisation.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.8, p. 40.

  > Remark 3.1.8. The proof of proposition 3.1.4 shows that if I is an ideal in an almost V -algebra A, then A/I is almost projective over A if and only if I is generated by an idempotent of A∗ . This idempotent is uniquely determined.

  Idempotent ideals.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Definition 4.12(i), p. 20.

  > (i) The morphism A → B is said to be unramified if there is some element e ∈ (B ⊗A B)∗ such that e2 = e, µ(e) = 1 and xe = 0 for all x ∈ ker(µ)∗ .

  Sch12 takes the idempotent description as the definition.

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.3, Definition 4.3.1(2), p. 26.

  > 2. (Unramifiedness) There exists a diagonal idempotent in (B ⊗A B)∗ , i.e., an element e ∈ (B ⊗A B)∗ such that e2 = e, µ∗ (e) = 1, and ker(µ)∗ · e = 0, where µ : B ⊗A B → B is the multiplication map.

  Bhatt's formulation.


#### `etale-morphisms-stability` — Stability of flat, unramified and étale morphisms of almost algebras

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Etale`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B, ψ : B → C morphisms of almost algebras. (i) Flatness, almost projectivity, faithful flatness, almost finiteness, weak unramifiedness, unramifiedness, weak étaleness and étaleness are stable under base change A → A' and (ii) under composition. (iii) If φ is flat and ψ ∘ φ faithfully flat then φ is faithfully flat. (iv) If φ is weakly unramified and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly étale) then ψ is flat (weakly étale). (v) If φ is unramified and ψ ∘ φ étale then ψ is étale. (vi) φ is faithfully flat iff it is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (vii) If φ is almost finite and weakly unramified then φ is unramified. (viii) If ψ is faithfully flat and ψ ∘ φ flat (weakly unramified) then φ is flat (weakly unramified). Finite étale morphisms are stable under base change and composition.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i), (ii), (iii), (viii): the module-theoretic stability of P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness (GR Remark 2.4.12(ii), Lemma 2.4.7) applied to B over A and over B ⊗_A B.
2. (vi): Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0.
3. (vii): B is an almost finitely presented B ⊗_A B-module (I_{B/A} is a quotient of (B ⊗_A B) ⊗_A B), so flat implies almost projective (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff).
4. (iv), (v): μ_{B/A} is étale when φ is unramified; Γ_ψ := 1_C ⊗_B μ_{B/A} is étale by (i), p := (ψ∘φ) ⊗_A 1_B is flat (étale), and ψ = Γ_ψ ∘ p; apply (ii).
5. Finite étale: base change and transitivity of almost finite presentation (GR Lemma 2.4.7, 2.3.7(v)).

**Acceptance.**

- In the classical setup (vi) is the usual criterion 'faithfully flat iff injective with flat cokernel'.
- Base change of L°a/K°a along K°a → (K°/ϖ)^a gives a finite étale (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(i), p. 39.

  > (i) Let A → A′ be any morphism of V a -algebras; if φ is flat (resp. almost projective, resp. faithfully flat, resp. almost finite, resp. weakly unramified, resp. unramified, resp. weakly étale, resp. étale) then the same holds for φ ⊗A 1A′ .

  Base change.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(v)-(vii), p. 39.

  > (vi) φ is faithfully flat if and only if it is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module.

  Faithful flatness criterion.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(v), p. 39.

  > (v) If φ is unramified and ψ ◦ φ is étale, then ψ is étale.

  Cancellation.


#### `trace-form-criterion` — Almost finite projective algebras are étale iff the trace form is perfect

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Trace`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras with B almost finite projective as an A-module. Then φ is étale iff the trace form t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A is a perfect pairing, i.e. τ_{B/A} : B → B* = alHom_A(B, A) is an isomorphism. In that case (1_B ⊗ τ_{B/A})(e_{B/A}) = ζ_B, where e_{B/A} is the diagonal idempotent and ζ_B = ω_{B/A}⁻¹(1_B). In particular, for B almost finitely presented, φ is finite étale iff B is flat over A and t_{B/A} is perfect.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; B almost finite projective over A.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. τ_{B/A} is B-linear and compatible with base change (GR Lemma 4.1.13), giving the B ⊗_A B-linear diagram (4.1.15).
2. ⇒: for φ étale, B ⊗_A B ≅ I_{B/A} × B (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation), so τ_{B⊗B/B} = τ_{B/B} ⊕ τ_{I/B} and after B ⊗_{B⊗_A B} − all arrows of (4.1.15) are isomorphisms, in particular τ_{B/A}.
3. ⇐: put e := (1_B ⊗ τ⁻¹)(ζ_B); Claim 4.1.16 (I_{B/A}·ζ_B = 0 and σ(ζ_B) = Tr_{B/A}) gives I_{B/A}·e = 0 and μ(e) = 1, hence e is the diagonal idempotent (GR Proposition 3.1.4).

**Acceptance.**

- For L°a/K°a (L = K(√p)) the trace form is perfect on the almost level (the discriminants 4p^{1/p^n} of the approximations R_n tend to a unit up to m).
- In the classical setup with B finite free: the classical criterion 'finite free étale iff discriminant is a unit'.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, Theorem 4.1.14, p. 75.

  > Theorem 4.1.14. An almost finite projective morphism φ : A → B of almost V -algebras is étale if and only if the trace form tB/A is a perfect pairing.

  The trace-form criterion for étaleness.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §4.1, Remark 4.1.17, p. 76.

  > Remark 4.1.17. By inspection of the proof of theorem 4.1.14, we see that the following has been shown.

  The formula (1 ⊗ τ)(e) = ζ_B.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.16, p. 21.

  > Theorem 4.16 ([14, Theorem 4.1.14]). In the situation of the definition, the morphism A → B is finite étale if and only if the trace map is a perfect pairing

  Sch12's statement (book and arXiv numbers agree).

- Kedlaya–Liu, *Relative p-adic Hodge theory: foundations* (arXiv:1301.0792v5), arXiv v5, §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132.

  > we say that B is almost finite étale if the trace pairing induces an almost isomorphism B → HomA (B, A). This is not the definition used in [52], but is equivalent to it via [52, Theorem 4.1.14].

  Kedlaya–Liu use the criterion as definition.


#### `almost-inversion-and-completion` — Inverting an element of m: almost modules become honest modules over V[1/ϖ]

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Completion`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and ϖ ∈ m. The localisation M ↦ M[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ] ⊗_V M is exact and kills almost zero modules (ϖM = 0), so it factors, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, through an exact functor Almost.invert ϖ : Almost.Module S → ModuleCat V[1/ϖ] with invert(M^a) ≅ M[1/ϖ] and invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ] ≅ M_![1/ϖ]. Consequences: almost isomorphisms become isomorphisms and almost exact complexes become exact after inverting ϖ; the setup S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical (m·V[1/ϖ] = V[1/ϖ]), so Almost.Module over it is ModuleCat V[1/ϖ]; invert is symmetric monoidal and sends almost algebras to V[1/ϖ]-algebras. The ϖ-adic completion side of this passage — completeness of M versus M_*, and exactness of complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ, with the lim¹ term kept — is P0/almost-completeness-via-almost-elements and P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m (so ϖ kills almost zero modules; ϖ need not be a nonzerodivisor).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. M ↦ M[1/ϖ] is exact (Mathlib localisation is exact) and kills almost zero modules; by Mathlib `SerreClassLocalization.essImage_whiskeringLeft` it factors through toAlmost as an exact functor.
2. invert(M) ≅ M_*[1/ϖ]: apply the factorisation to M ≅ (M_*)^a (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).
3. S.baseChange V[1/ϖ] is classical because ϖ ∈ m becomes a unit (P0/basic-setup-base-change); invert is then the composite of change of setup (P0/change-of-basic-setup) and Almost.Module.classicalEquiv (GR 5.2.17: 'A[ε^{-1}] is a usual V-algebra').
4. Monoidality: localisation commutes with tensor products, so invert is symmetric monoidal and carries commutative monoids to commutative V[1/ϖ]-algebras.

**Acceptance.**

- S = (K°, K°°): invert((K°/ϖ)^a) = 0, invert(K°a) = K, invert(R°a) = R for a perfectoid K-algebra R.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D2: H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for i > 0 gives H^i(X, O) = H^i(X, O⁺)[1/ϖ] = 0 (cohomology on quasicompact sites commutes with the filtered colimit defining O = O⁺[1/ϖ]).

#### `finite-etale-localizes` — Comparison of finite étale almost algebras with Mathlib's finite étale algebras

*comparison* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Etale`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and R → R' a map of commutative V-algebras. (i) If R' is finite étale over R in Mathlib's sense (`Algebra.Etale R R'` and `Module.Finite R R'`), then R^a → R'^a is finite étale in the almost sense. (ii) In the classical setup (m = V) the converse holds, so A_fet for A = R^a is equivalent to Mathlib's category of finite étale R-algebras. (iii) For ϖ ∈ m, if R'^a is finite étale over R^a then R'[1/ϖ] is finite étale over R[1/ϖ] in Mathlib's sense (inverting ϖ turns almost statements into honest ones, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion). (iv) GR-étale morphisms in the classical setup are exactly the absolutely flat (weakly étale) maps whose diagonal is almost projective; they need not be of finite presentation, and a classical étale map in EGA's sense is étale in GR's sense.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; R → R' a map of V-algebras.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i) R' is a finitely presented projective R-module (finite étale ⇒ finite, flat, finitely presented), so R'^a is almost finite projective (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness); the kernel J of R' ⊗_R R' → R' is finitely generated with J = J² (Ω_{R'/R} = 0), hence generated by an idempotent (Mathlib `Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`), whose image is the diagonal idempotent (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation).
2. (ii) In the classical setup almost notions are honest: almost finitely presented = finitely presented, the diagonal idempotent gives Ω_{R'/R} = 0 (formally unramified), and a flat, finitely presented, formally unramified algebra is étale (GR 3.4.44: étale = absolutely flat and finitely presented).
3. (iii) Apply the exact monoidal inversion functor (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and (ii) for the classical setup (V[1/ϖ], V[1/ϖ]).
4. (iv) GR Remark 3.1.3(i) and digression 3.4.44.

**Acceptance.**

- For K a perfectoid field and L/K finite separable: L°a is finite étale over K°a (ECD/Sch12), while L° need not be finite étale over K° in Mathlib's sense (it is not finitely presented in general); (i) is strictly weaker than the almost statement.
- For R → R' = R × R the diagonal idempotent is (1,0) ⊗ (1,0) + (0,1) ⊗ (0,1).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`, `mathlib:Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg`, `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.44), p. 64.

  > A ring homomorphism A → B is étale in the usual sense of [40] if and only if it is absolutely flat and of finite presentation.

  The classical-limit comparison.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(i), p. 39.

  > Then we caution the reader that our notion of “étale morphism” is more general than the usual one, as defined in [40].

  GR-étale versus EGA-étale.

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.3, Construction 4.3.3, p. 26.

  > Construction 4.3.3 (Finite étale algebras seen explicitly as finite projective modules).

#### `almost-differentials` — Almost Kähler differentials Ω_{B/A} and almost derivations

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras, I_{B/A} = ker(μ_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → B). The module of almost differentials is the B-module Ω_{B/A} := I_{B/A}/I_{B/A}², with the A-derivation δ : B → Ω_{B/A}, b ↦ 1 ⊗ b − b ⊗ 1 on almost elements. For a B-module M, an A-derivation B → M is an A-linear ∂ with ∂(b₁b₂) = b₁∂(b₂) + b₂∂(b₁) on almost elements; they form a V-module Der_A(B, M), and f ↦ f ∘ δ is an isomorphism Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) ≅ Der_A(B, M). Properties: Ω_{C⊗_A B/C} ≅ C ⊗_A Ω_{B/A}; for A → B → C an exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0; for C = B/I an exact sequence I/I² → C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → 0; Ω commutes with colimits; (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}; for V-algebras R → R', Ω_{R'^a/R^a} ≅ (Ω_{R'/R})^a (Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A → B a morphism of almost algebras.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Define I_{B/A}, Ω_{B/A} and δ in B ⊗_A B-Mod (P0/almost-algebras).
2. Universal property (2.5.24) and Proposition 2.5.25 as for rings, working on almost elements (GR 2.5.23 leaves them as exercises).
3. (Ω_{B/A})_! ≅ Ω_{B!!/A!!}: compare derivations B_!! → M with almost derivations B → M^a (GR Lemma 2.5.28).
4. Comparison with Mathlib: (−)^a is exact and monoidal, so it carries the kernel of R' ⊗_R R' → R' and its square to I_{B/A} and I_{B/A}².

**Acceptance.**

- Ω_{A[X]/A} ≅ A[X] (free on δX) for the polynomial almost algebra A[X] := (A_*[X])^a.
- Ω_{B/A} = 0 for φ unramified (the idempotent kills I_{B/A}, so I = I²).

#### `almost-cotangent-complex` — The almost cotangent complex L_{B/A}

*construction* **Planet:** *Almost cotangent complex*. Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and A → B a morphism of almost algebras. Put Ã := V^a × A and B̃ := V^a × B (exact almost algebras). The almost cotangent complex is L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗_{B̃_!!} L_{B̃_!!/Ã_!!}, an object of the derived category of B_!!-modules, where L_{−/−} is the classical cotangent complex of the ring map Ã_!! → B̃_!! (simplicial polynomial resolution; supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0); its almostification L^a_{B/A} ∈ D(B-Mod) is the object used in deformation theory. Properties: H_0(L^a_{B/A}) ≅ Ω_{B/A}; Ext^i_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext^i_B(L^a_{B/A}, M) (GR (3.2.8)), Ext⁰ ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Ext¹ ≅ Exal_A(B, M) (P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison); transitivity triangle (P0/cotangent-transitivity); Tor-independent base change (P0/cotangent-flat-base-change); L_{colim B_λ/colim A_λ} ≅ colim L_{B_λ/A_λ} for filtered systems; vanishing for weakly étale maps (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale); for V-algebras R → S, L^a_{S^a/R^a} ≅ (L_{S/R})^a (P0/almost-cotangent-comparison-classical), so 'the almost cotangent complex depends only on R^a → S^a' (Sch12 §5).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, used in Proposition 2.5.34 and Theorem 2.5.35).
- The classical cotangent complex of a ring map, with transitivity, base change for Tor-independent squares, filtered colimits, H_0 = Ω and Ext¹ = Exal, is imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 (request); the pinned Mathlib has only the naive cotangent complex (`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `Algebra.H1Cotangent`).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Replace A → B by Ã → B̃: these are exact almost algebras, and (−)_!! commutes with finite products and tensor products (P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek).
2. Define L_{B/A} by the base change formula of GR Definition 2.5.20 from DD.0's L_{B̃!!/Ã!!}.
3. Derived category: B_!!-modules form an abelian category with enough injectives; the almostification functor to B-Mod is exact and induces D(B_!!-Mod) → D(B-Mod) (GR 2.4.9).
4. The listed properties are the lemmas cited with them; H_0 ≅ Ω is P0/almost-differentials and filtered colimits commute with the construction because (−)_!!, B_!! ⊗ − and DD.0's complex do.

**Acceptance.**

- For A → A (identity) L_{A/A} ≃ 0; for A → A[X] := (A_*[X])^a, L^a ≃ Ω_{A[X]/A}[0], free of rank one.
- For K perfectoid and A a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra, L^a_{A/(K°a/ϖ)} ≃ 0 (Sch12 Corollary 5.16; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi).

#### `cotangent-transitivity` — Transitivity triangle for almost cotangent complexes

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and A → B → C morphisms of almost algebras. There is a natural distinguished triangle C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A} → L_{C/A} → L_{C/B} → C_!! ⊗_{B_!!} L_{B/A}[1] in D(C_!!-Mod), and hence C ⊗_B L^a_{B/A} → L^a_{C/A} → L^a_{C/B} → in D(C-Mod); on H_0 it extends the exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_{B/A} → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Apply the classical transitivity triangle (Illusie II.2.1.2, from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) to Ã_!! → B̃_!! → C̃_!! and base change to C_!! (GR Theorem 2.5.32).
2. Almostify (exact functor) for the L^a version; H_0 by P0/almost-differentials.

**Acceptance.**

- For A → A[X] → A (X ↦ 0): the triangle A ⊗ L_{A[X]/A} → L_{A/A} ≃ 0 → L_{A/A[X]} → gives L^a_{A/A[X]} ≃ (X)/(X²)[1] ≅ A[1], the conormal module in homological degree 1.
- Used in Sch12's proof of Theorem 5.10 for A → A_n → A_{n−1} (with base change).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.32, p. 35.

  > Theorem 2.5.32. Let A → B → C be a sequence of morphisms of almost V -algebras. There exists a natural distinguished triangle of D(s.C!! -Mod)

  The triangle.


#### `almost-cotangent-comparison-classical` — The almost cotangent complex of R^a → S^a is the almostified classical one

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and f : R → S a map of V-algebras. (i) If f^a : R^a → S^a is an isomorphism, then (L_{S/R})^a ≃ 0 in D(S^a-Mod). (ii) The natural map L^a_{S^a/R^a} → (L_{S/R})^a is an isomorphism in D(S^a-Mod). Hence the almost cotangent complex of a morphism of almost algebras coming from V-algebras is computed by the classical cotangent complex, and it depends only on R^a → S^a.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; L_{S/R} the classical cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (ii) from (i) by transitivity applied to (R^a)_!! → R and (S^a)_!! → S, whose almostifications are isomorphisms.
2. (i) by induction on q of H_q(L^a_{S/R}) = 0: transitivity for R → f(R) → S reduces to f injective or surjective; replace S by its standard free simplicial resolution S_• and R by R_• := S_• ×_S R (levelwise almost isomorphisms) and use the spectral sequence H_j(L_{S[i]/R[i]}) ⇒ H_{i+j}(L^Δ_{S_•/R_•}); for S = V[T] free: if f surjective use a section; if f injective, compare with Sym(m̃ ⊗ F) ⊆ R ⊆ Sym(F) using flatness of m̃ and F (GR proof of Proposition 8.1.7).

**Acceptance.**

- For R = V and S = V × k (k = V/m): f^a is an isomorphism (cokernel k almost zero), and L_{S/V} ≅ 0 × L_{k/V} has homology consisting of k-modules, hence almost zero, as (i) predicts.
- Sch12 §5 uses (ii) implicitly when stating that L^a_{S/R} depends only on R^a → S^a.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7, p. 219.

  > Proposition 8.1.7. Let f : R → S be a map of V -algebras. We have:

  The comparison, located in GR §8.1 (simplicial almost algebras).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §8.1, Proposition 8.1.7(i)-(ii), p. 220.

  > (ii) The natural map LaS a /Ra → LaS/R is an isomorphism in D(s.S a -Mod).

  Part (ii).

#### `cotangent-flat-base-change` — Tor-independent base change for almost cotangent complexes

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A → B and A → A' morphisms of almost algebras, B' := B ⊗_A A', and suppose the natural map B ⊗^L_A A' → B' is an isomorphism (Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0 for i > 0; e.g. B or A' flat over A). Then B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'} and (B'_!! ⊗_{B!!} L_{B/A}) ⊕ (B'_!! ⊗_{A'!!} L_{A'/A}) → L_{B'/A} are quasi-isomorphisms. This is the result Sch12 cites as 'Theorem 2.5.36 of [14]' (LNM 1800 book numbering) in the proof of Theorem 5.10; in arXiv v3 it is Theorem 2.5.35 (arXiv Theorem 2.5.36 is the vanishing statement of P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, used in Proposition 2.5.34).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Proposition 2.5.34: if A, B, C, B ⊗_A C are exact, m̃ ⊗ Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) → Tor_i is an isomorphism for i > 0, and Tor^A_i(B, C) = 0 implies Tor^{A!!}_i(B!!, C!!) = 0 (uses m̃ flat).
2. Replace algebras by V^a × (−) (commutes with tensor products) so that everything is exact, then apply the classical Tor-independent base change (Illusie II.2.2.1, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0) (GR proof of Theorem 2.5.35).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 proof of Theorem 5.10: for A_n flat over (K°/ϖ^n)^a the square (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, A_n → A_{n−1} is Tor-independent, so L_{A_{n−1}/(K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ≅ A_{n−1} ⊗ L_{A_n/(K°/ϖ^n)^a}; with transitivity this gives the triangle used there.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.35, p. 35.

  > Theorem 2.5.35. Let B, A′ be two A-algebras. Suppose that the natural morphism B ⊗A A′ →

  The theorem (arXiv numbering).

  The Tor comparison used in the proof.

#### `cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale` — Vanishing of the almost cotangent complex when the diagonal is Tor-trivial

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and R → S' a morphism of almost algebras with Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 and Tor^{S'⊗_R S'}_i(S', S') = 0 for all i > 0 (S' ⊗_R S'-module structure via μ). Then L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 in D(S'_!!-Mod). In particular L_{S'/R} ≃ 0 for every weakly étale (hence every étale, every finite étale) morphism R → S'.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Tor^R_i(S', S') = 0 gives, by P0/cotangent-flat-base-change, (S'⊗S')_!! ⊗ L_{S'/R} ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/S'} and (…⊗L) ⊕ (…⊗L) ≅ L_{S'⊗S'/R}.
2. Tor^{S'⊗S'}_i(S', S') = 0 gives L_{S'/S'⊗_R S'} ≅ L_{S'/S'} ≃ 0.
3. Transitivity for R → S' ⊗_R S' → S' (P0/cotangent-transitivity): S'_!! ⊗ L_{S'⊗S'/R} ≅ L_{S'/R}; combined, L ⊕ L → L is an isomorphism that is the sum map, so L ≃ 0 (GR Theorem 2.5.36).
4. Weakly étale: S' is flat over R and over S' ⊗_R S', so both Tor conditions hold.

**Acceptance.**

- Every idempotent quotient A → A/eA is weakly étale, so L_{(A/eA)/A} ≃ 0.
- For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra the vanishing L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0 is of a different nature (Frobenius; Sch12 Proposition 5.13, PerfectoidSpaces:P1).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-flat-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36.

  > Theorem 2.5.36. Let R → S be a morphism of almost algebras such that

  The vanishing theorem (arXiv numbering).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.36, p. 36.

  > Then LS/R ≃ 0 in D(S!! -Mod).

  Conclusion.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, proof of Theorem 3.2.18, p. 43.

  > By induction we can assume I 2 = 0. Then (i) follows directly from proposition 3.2.16 and theorem 2.5.36.

  Use for weakly étale lifting.


#### `almost-exal-ext-comparison` — Square-zero extensions of almost algebras are classified by Ext¹ of the almost cotangent complex

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Cotangent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A → B a morphism of almost algebras and M a B-module. (i) Almostification Exal_{A!!}(B_!!, M_*) → Exal_A(B, M) is an equivalence of categories of square-zero extensions, inducing a group isomorphism on isomorphism classes, functorial in all arguments. (ii) There are natural isomorphisms Ext⁰_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Der_A(B, M) and Exal_A(B, M) ≅ Ext¹_{B!!}(L_{B/A}, M_!) ≅ Ext¹_B(L^a_{B/A}, M). (iii) For an epimorphism A → B with kernel I, Hom_B(I/I², M) ≅ Exal_A(B, M) via pullback of 0 → I/I² → A/I² → B → 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A-extensions of B by M are short exact sequences 0 → M → E → B → 0 in A-Mod with E an A-algebra, M a square-zero ideal with its given B-module structure (GR 2.5.2–2.5.7).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): send X = (0 → I → E → B → 0) to X_! = (0 → I_! → E_!! → B_!! → 0), right exact, and push out along I_! → I_* (GR Lemma 2.5.17, Remark 2.5.19); the category is additive by the Baer-sum construction on ExalC (GR 2.5.5–2.5.6) and (2.5.15).
2. (ii): Ext⁰ via Illusie II.1.2.4.2 and Lemma 2.5.28 (GR Proposition 2.5.29); Ext¹ via Illusie III.1.2.3 applied to Ã_!! → B̃_!! and (i) (GR Theorem 2.5.30); the almost form via (3.2.8), which uses GR Proposition 2.5.42 and Lemma 2.4.14(i).
3. (iii): GR Lemma 3.2.1 (factor the structure map through A/I²).

**Acceptance.**

- For the trivial extension B ⊕ M, the class is 0; for A → B = A/I with I² = 0 the extension A itself corresponds to 1_{I}.
- In Sch12 Theorem 5.11 these groups classify deformations of perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Lemma 2.5.17(i), p. 32.

  > (2.5.18) ExalA!! (B!! , I∗ ) → ExalA (B, I) X 7→ X a

  Part (i).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.30, p. 34.

  > Theorem 2.5.30. There is a natural isomorphism

  Exal ≅ Ext¹.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §2.5, Proposition 2.5.29, p. 34.

  > Proposition 2.5.29. Let M be a B-module. There exists a natural isomorphism of B!! -modules

  Ext⁰ ≅ Der.
