#### `almost-local-flatness-criterion` — Local flatness criterion for square-zero thickenings, honest and almost

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Deformation`.

**Statement.** (i) (classical) Let R be a ring, J ⊆ R an ideal with J² = 0, R' = R/J, and M an R-module; put M' = M/JM. Then M is R-flat iff M' is R'-flat and the natural map u(M) : J ⊗_{R'} M' → JM (x ⊗ m' ↦ xm) is an isomorphism. (ii) (almost) Let S be a basic setup and f̃ : B̃ → C̃ a morphism of A-extensions 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0 and 0 → J → C → C₀ → 0 (I² = J² = 0) whose square is cofibred (C₀ ≅ C ⊗_B B₀). Then B → C is flat iff B₀ → C₀ is flat and C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I → J is an isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- J² = 0 (nilpotent of order two; the general nilpotent case follows by induction).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i) Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 22.3 ((1)⇔(3) for a nilpotent ideal), as recalled by GR (3.2.19): ⇒ tensor 0 → J → R → R' → 0 with M; ⇐ show Tor_1^R(N, M) = 0 for all N by dévissage 0 → JN → N → N/JN → 0 to R'-modules N', where Tor_1^R(N', M) is controlled by u(M) and flatness of M'.
2. (ii) Apply (i) to the ring map B_!! → C_!! and almost elements, using exactness of (−)^a, (−)_! and the Tor comparison of P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion (GR Lemma 3.2.6: 'the almost version of the local flatness criterion').

**Acceptance.**

- For R = k[ε]/(ε²), M = R: M' = k flat and u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → εR bijective; for M = k: u(M) : (ε) ⊗ k → 0 not injective, and k is not flat over R.
- Used in P0/almost-deformation-theory to identify flat deformations with extensions by C₀ ⊗ I.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `mathlib:TensorProduct`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, (3.2.19), p. 44.

  > By the local flatness criterion ([54, Th. 22.3]) M is flat over R if and only if M ′ is flat over R′ and u(M) is an isomorphism.

  Part (i) as recalled by GR.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Lemma 3.2.6, p. 41.

  > Lemma 3.2.6. Let fe : B e→C e be a morphism of A-extensions as above, such that the corresponding square diagram of almost algebras is cofibred. Then the morphism f : B → C is flat if and only if f0 : B0 → C0 is flat and (3.2.5) is an isomorphism.

  Part (ii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, proof of Lemma 3.2.6, p. 41.

  > It follows directly from the (almost version of the) local flatness criterion (see [54, Th. 22.3]).

  The proof route.


#### `almost-deformation-theory` — Flat square-zero deformations of almost algebras: obstruction, torsor, automorphisms

*theorem* **Planet:** *Nilpotent deformations of almost algebras*. Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Deformation`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ = (0 → I → B → B₀ → 0) an A-extension (I² = 0) and f₀ : B₀ → C₀ a flat morphism of almost algebras. Let ω(B̃, f₀) := ∂(I → C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ∈ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I), ∂ the boundary of the transitivity sequence for B → B₀ → C₀. Then (i) ω(B̃, f₀) = 0 iff there is a flat deformation of C₀ over B, i.e. a B-extension C̃ = (0 → C₀ ⊗ I → C → C₀ → 0) with C flat over B and C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀; (ii) if ω = 0, the isomorphism classes of flat deformations form a torsor under Exal_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext¹_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I); (iii) the automorphism group of a flat deformation (acting trivially on C₀ and on C₀ ⊗ I) is Der_{B₀}(C₀, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I). More generally (GR Proposition 3.2.9) for any B₀-linear u : I → J the obstruction ω(B̃, f₀, u) = v_! ∘ ω(B̃, f₀) governs extensions C̃ with kernel J.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat); I² = 0; f₀ flat.
- Book/arXiv numbering: Sch12 Theorem 5.11 cites GR Proposition 3.2.9 (same number in arXiv v3).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀ gives Exal_{B₀}(C₀, J) → Exal_B(C₀, J) → Hom_{B₀}(I, J) →∂ Ext²_{C₀}(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, J) (P0/cotangent-transitivity, P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison, GR Lemma 3.2.1).
2. Obstruction, torsor and automorphisms as in Illusie III.2.1.2.3, applied through the almost Exal/Ext dictionary (GR Proposition 3.2.9).
3. Flatness of the deformation: by P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion, C is flat over B with C ⊗_B B₀ ≅ C₀ iff its kernel is C₀ ⊗_{B₀} I via (3.2.5), which is the choice u = (I → C₀ ⊗ I) (GR 3.2.10, Corollary 3.2.11).

**Acceptance.**

- If L^a_{C₀/B₀} ≃ 0 (e.g. C₀ étale over B₀, or a perfectoid (K°/ϖ)^a-algebra over (K°/ϖ)^a) then a flat deformation exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; Sch12 Theorem 5.10 applies this over (K°/ϖ^n)^a → (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a.
- For A = B = B₀ ⊕ I trivial and C₀ = B₀[X] (almost polynomial), the trivial deformation C₀ ⊕ C₀ ⊗ I exists and deformations form a torsor under Ext¹(L^a, −) = 0.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-local-flatness-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Proposition 3.2.9, p. 41.

  > Proposition 3.2.9. Let the A-extension e B, the B0 -linear morphism u : I → J and the morphism of A-algebras f0 : B0 → C0 be given as above.

  General statement.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Corollary 3.2.11, p. 42.

  > Corollary 3.2.11. Suppose that B0 → C0 is flat. Then

  Flat deformations.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Corollary 3.2.11(ii), p. 42.

  > then the set of isomorphism classes of flat deformations of C0 over B forms a torsor under the group ExalB0 (C0 , C0 ⊗B0 I).

  Torsor.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Corollary 3.2.11(iii), p. 42.

  > (iii) The group of automorphisms of a given flat deformation of C0 over B is naturally isomorphic to DerB0 (C0 , C0 ⊗B0 I).

  Automorphisms.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §5, Theorem 5.11, p. 24.

  > Theorem 5.11 ([22, III.2.1.2.3], [14, Proposition 3.2.9]).

  Sch12's use of the almost version.


#### `almost-morphism-lifting` — Lifting morphisms along square-zero extensions of almost algebras

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Deformation`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, B̃ an A-extension 0 → I → B → B₀ → 0, and C̃ⁱ = (0 → Jⁱ → Cⁱ → C₀ⁱ → 0), i = 1, 2, A-extensions with morphisms f̃ⁱ : B̃ → C̃ⁱ, together with v : J¹ → J² and g₀ : C₀¹ → C₀² such that u² = v ∘ u¹ and f₀² = g₀ ∘ f₀¹. The class v_* e(C̃¹) − e(C̃²) ∗ g₀ ∈ Ext¹_{C₀¹}(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) is the obstruction to a morphism of A-extensions g̃ : C̃¹ → C̃² over v and g₀ with f̃² = g̃ ∘ f̃¹; when it vanishes, such g̃ form a torsor under Der_{B₀}(C₀¹, J²) ≅ Ext⁰_{C₀²}(C₀² ⊗ L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²). In particular, if C and C' are flat over B with reductions C₀, C₀' and f₀ : C₀ → C₀', the obstruction to lifting f₀ lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I) and lifts form a torsor under Hom(L^a_{C₀/B₀}, C₀' ⊗ I).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; I² = 0.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. The classes e(C̃ⁱ) ∈ Ext¹(L^a_{C₀ⁱ/B}, Jⁱ) come from P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison; the problem is solvable iff v_*C̃¹ and C̃² ∗ g₀ coincide.
2. Transitivity for B → B₀ → C₀¹ shows the difference lies in Ext¹(L^a_{C₀¹/B₀}, J²) (GR (3.2.15)); conclude as in Illusie III.2.2.2 (GR Proposition 3.2.16).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Theorem 5.12 (almost version) is the flat case; with L^a ≃ 0 it gives unique lifting of morphisms, the full faithfulness in Sch12 Theorem 5.10.
- For C₀ étale over B₀: morphisms lift uniquely (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (i)).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exal-ext-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-transitivity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Proposition 3.2.16, p. 43.

  > Proposition 3.2.16. With the above notations, the class (3.2.15) is the obstruction to the existence of a morphism of A-extensions

  Obstruction.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Proposition 3.2.16, p. 43.

  > When the obstruction vanishes, the set of such morphisms forms a torsor under the group DerB0 (C01 , J 2 )

  Torsor.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §5, Theorem 5.12, p. 25.

  > Theorem 5.12 ([22, III.2.2.2], [14, Proposition 3.2.16]).

  Sch12's use (same number in the book).


#### `nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras` — Étale almost algebras lift uniquely along nilpotent ideals

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Deformation`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a nilpotent ideal, A' := A/I. (i) For B weakly étale over A, C any A-algebra and J ⊆ C nilpotent, Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C) → Hom_{A-Alg}(B, C/J) is bijective. (ii) B ↦ A' ⊗_A B is an equivalence from weakly étale A-algebras to weakly étale A'-algebras; (iii) it restricts to an equivalence of étale algebras A-Ét ≃ A'-Ét and (iv) to an equivalence of finite étale algebras A_fet ≃ A'_fet (étale and almost finitely presented).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; I nilpotent (induction reduces to I² = 0).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): I² = 0 by induction; lifts of morphisms are governed by Ext^{1,0}(L^a_{B/A}, −) (P0/almost-morphism-lifting), and L_{B/A} ≃ 0 for B weakly étale (P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale).
2. (ii): a weakly étale B' over A' has a unique flat lift B (P0/almost-deformation-theory with L ≃ 0); B is weakly étale: μ_{B'/A'} is weakly étale, lifts to a flat μ̃ : B ⊗_A B → C, and by (i) C ≅ B compatibly, so B is B ⊗_A B-flat (GR proof of Theorem 3.2.18(ii)).
3. (iii): if B' is étale, I_{B'/A'} is an étale B' ⊗ B'-algebra (Corollary 3.1.9), lifts, and B ⊗_A B ≅ C ⊕ B, so B is almost projective over B ⊗_A B.
4. (iv): an étale B with A' ⊗_A B almost finitely presented is almost finitely presented (GR Lemma 3.2.25(iii), Tor^A_1(A', B) = 0 by flatness) (GR Theorem 3.2.28(ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- A = (K°/ϖ^n)^a, I = ϖ^{n−1}A: finite étale (K°/ϖ^{n−1})^a-algebras lift uniquely to (K°/ϖ^n)^a; this is the finite-level step of GR Theorem 5.3.27.
- In the classical setup (iii) is SGA 1 I.8.3 in GR's generality of étale (not necessarily finitely presented) algebras.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-deformation-theory`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-morphism-lifting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/cotangent-vanishing-weakly-etale`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`

  Part (i).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Theorem 3.2.18(iii), p. 43.

  > (iii) The equivalence of (ii) restricts to an equivalence A-Ét → A′ -Ét.

  Part (iii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Theorem 3.2.28(ii), p. 46.

  > (ii) The equivalence of theorem 3.2.18(ii) restricts to an equivalence A-Étafp → A′ -Étafp .

  Part (iv).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Lemma 3.2.25(iii), p. 45.

#### `lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness` — B ↦ B_!! preserves and reflects faithful flatness, but not flatness

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Descent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is faithfully flat iff φ is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module. (ii) φ is a monomorphism iff φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is injective, and B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! is flat over A_!! iff B/A is flat over A. (iii) Hence φ is faithfully flat iff φ_!! is a faithfully flat ring map. (iv) Flatness is not preserved: for S = ofValuationRing V with residue field k, the flat projection V^a × V^a → V^a becomes V ×_k V → V under (−)_!!, which is not flat.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; m̃ flat is used in (ii) through GR Proposition 2.4.35.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): GR Lemma 3.1.2(vi), Tor sequences for 0 → A → B → B/A → 0 in A-Mod.
2. (ii): the kernel of φ_!! is (ker φ)_! and (−)_! reflects zero; B_!!/Im A_!! ≅ B_!/A_! (both are cokernels of V ⊕ (−)_! modulo the same ideal); (−)_! takes flat modules to flat modules and back (GR Proposition 2.4.35, Remark 3.1.3(ii)).
3. (iii): apply (i) to φ and the classical criterion to φ_!!.
4. (iv): (V^a × V^a)_!! = V ×_k V (fibre product of rings over the residue field) and V ×_k V → V is not flat (GR Remark 3.1.3(ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- For φ = identity, φ_!! is the identity.
- Bhatt Remark 4.2.8(2): (−)_!! preserves faithful flatness but may not preserve flatness.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 39.

  > The naive hope that the functor A 7→ A!! might preserve flatness is crushed by the following counterexample.

  Part (iv).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Remark 3.1.3(ii), p. 40.

  > On the other hand, faithful flatness is preserved.

  Part (iii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.1, Lemma 3.1.2(vi), p. 39.

  > (vi) φ is faithfully flat if and only if it is a monomorphism and B/A is a flat A-module.

  Part (i).

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.2, Remark 4.2.8, p. 25.

  > (Exercise) (−)!! preserves faithful flatness. However, it may not preserve flatness; see [GR, Remark 3.1.3].

  Bhatt's summary.


#### `almost-faithfully-flat-descent` — Faithfully flat descent for almost modules and almost algebras

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Descent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras. (i) φ is of effective descent for modules: M ↦ (B ⊗_A M, can) is an equivalence from A-Mod to the category Desc(B/A) of B-modules N with a B ⊗_A B-linear isomorphism β : p₂*N ≅ p₁*N satisfying the cocycle condition p₁₂*(β) ∘ p₂₃*(β) = p₁₃*(β); (ii) the same holds for A-algebras; (iii) both statements are stable under base change A → A' (universal effective descent); (iv) under (i) the full subcategories of flat, almost finitely generated, almost finitely presented and almost finite projective modules correspond, and under (ii) those of weakly étale, étale and finite étale algebras correspond; (v) almost projectivity descends when B is almost finitely presented over A (for general faithfully flat φ this is not asserted: GR Remark 3.2.26(iii) leaves it open).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat (P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. φ_!! : A_!! → B_!! is a faithfully flat ring map (P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness).
2. Classical descent: extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`); the identification of comonad coalgebras with descent data (cocycle and uniqueness), and descent for algebras, is Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 0E (request).
3. Transport: a descent datum (N, β) over B/A gives (N_!, β_!) over B_!!/A_!! because (−)_! commutes with tensor products (P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom) and (B ⊗_A B)_!! ≅ B_!! ⊗_{A_!!} B_!!; descend to an A_!!-module and almostify; A-Mod ≃ Almost.Module (S.baseChange A_!!) via A ≅ (A_!!)^a (P0/change-of-basic-setup).
4. (iv): descent of flatness, almost finite generation and presentation (GR Remark 3.2.26(ii)), of almost finite projectivity (Remark 3.2.26(iii) with P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), of (weakly) étale algebras (GR 3.4.1, P0/etale-morphisms-stability (viii)).
5. (v): GR Remark 3.2.26(iv) via Lemma 2.4.31(i) and Proposition 2.4.18(ii).

**Acceptance.**

- For V-algebras R → R' with R' faithfully flat, the almostification of Grothendieck's descent is (i) for R^a → R'^a.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3: with (S⁺/ϖ)^a faithfully flat over (R⁺/ϖ)^a (automatic flatness), the descent datum on (S̃⁺/ϖ)^a descends to an almost (R⁺/ϖ)^a-algebra.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-tensor-and-internal-hom`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/change-of-basic-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/etale-morphisms-stability`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `mathlib:comonadicExtendScalars`, `mathlib:ModuleCat.extendScalars`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0e-effective-descent-and-spreading-out`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, introduction, p. 55.

  > 3.4. Descent. Faithfully flat descent in the almost setting presents no particular surprises: since the functor A 7→ A!! preserves faithful flatness of morphisms (see remark 3.1.3)

  Proof strategy.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 55.

  > 3.4.1. So for instance, faithfully flat morphisms are of universal effective descent for the fibred categories

  Parts (i)-(iii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 55.

  > Then, using remark 3.2.26, we deduce also universal effective descent for the fibred subcategories of flat (resp. almost finitely generated, resp. almost finitely presented, resp. almost finitely generated projective) modules.

  Part (iv), modules.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 56.

  > Likewise, a faithfully flat morphism is of universal effective descent for the fibred subcategories Éto → V a -Algo of étale (resp. w.Éto → V a -Algo of weakly étale) algebras.

  Part (iv), algebras.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.2, Remark 3.2.26(iii), p. 45.

#### `almost-amitsur-complex-exact` — The Amitsur complex of an almost faithfully flat map is exact

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Descent`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, φ : A → B a faithfully flat morphism of almost algebras and M an A-module. The augmented Amitsur complex 0 → M → M ⊗_A B → M ⊗_A B ⊗_A B → ⋯ (differentials the alternating sums of the coface maps) is exact in A-Mod. In honest terms: for V-algebras R → R' such that R'^a is faithfully flat over R^a (e.g. Tor_i^R(X, R') almost zero for i > 0 and X ⊗_R R' almost zero only if X is), and any R-module N, the cohomology of 0 → N → N ⊗_R R' → N ⊗_R R' ⊗_R R' → ⋯ is almost zero; in particular N^a is the equalizer of (N ⊗ R')^a ⇉ (N ⊗ R' ⊗ R')^a.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; φ faithfully flat.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. After base change along φ the complex acquires a contracting homotopy (the extra degeneracy from the multiplication B ⊗_A B → B).
2. B ⊗_A − is exact and faithful on A-Mod, hence reflects exactness of complexes.
3. Honest form: (−)^a is exact, so cohomology of the honest complex almostifies to the cohomology of the almost complex; P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion translates the Tor hypotheses into faithful flatness of R'^a.

**Acceptance.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions: R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ ⇉ S⁺/ϖ ⊗ S⁺/ϖ is almost exact (ECD Proposition 8.8 uses the honest faithfully flat version for totally disconnected X).
- For A → A × A (faithfully flat, split) the Amitsur complex is split exact.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flatness-tor-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `mathlib:CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §3.4, (3.4.1), p. 55.

  > 3.4.1. So for instance, faithfully flat morphisms are of universal effective descent for the fibred categories

  Descent of morphisms, of which exactness of the Amitsur complex in degrees 0 and 1 is the module form.

- Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds* (arXiv:1709.07343v4), arXiv v4, §8, proof of Proposition 8.8, p. 42.

  > is almost exact. As everything is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsionfree, where ϖ ∈ R+ is a

  Consumer use: almost exactness of Čech/Amitsur complexes of O⁺ along v-covers.


#### `tight-ideal` — Tight ideals, the Jacobson radical and henselian pairs of almost algebras

*definition* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Henselian`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup and A an almost V-algebra. An ideal I ⊆ A is tight if there are a finitely generated ideal m₀ ⊆ m and n ∈ ℕ with Iⁿ ⊆ m₀·A (GR Definition 5.1.5); for ϖ ∈ m the ideal ϖA is tight. The Jacobson radical of A is rad(A) := rad(A_*)^a (GR 5.1.1); for a V-algebra R and an ideal J ⊆ R, J^a ⊆ rad(R^a) iff mJ ⊆ rad(R) (GR Lemma 5.1.2). A pair (A, I) with I ⊆ rad(A) is henselian if (A_*, m·I_*) is a henselian pair (Mathlib `HenselianRing A_* (m·I_*)`), and tight henselian if moreover I is tight (GR Definition 5.1.8); (R^a, J^a) is henselian iff (R, mJ) is (GR Lemma 5.1.10). If A is I-adically complete (A → lim A/Iⁿ an isomorphism), (A, I) is henselian (GR Remark 5.3.7).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; A an almost algebra; ideals of A are subobjects I ↪ A stable under multiplication, with powers Iⁿ the images of I^{⊗n}.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Define IsTight via Submodule.FG subideals of m and the ideal m₀·A.
2. Define rad(A) and henselian pairs through almost elements, using Mathlib's `Ideal.jacobson` and `HenselianRing`.
3. Lemma 5.1.2 and Lemma 5.1.10: compare R with (R^a)_* through the map R → (R^a)_*, whose kernel is square-zero (killed by m) and whose image differs from (R^a)_* by an almost zero module; henselianity is insensitive to nilpotent ideals (GR Remark 5.1.9).
4. Complete ⇒ henselian: lift factorisations of monic polynomials through A_*/I_*^{n+1} (GR Remark 5.3.7; Mathlib `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing` for the honest step).

**Acceptance.**

- For ϖ ∈ m and A = R^a with R ϖ-adically complete: (A, ϖA) is tight henselian.
- In the classical setup, every ideal is tight and henselian pairs are Mathlib's henselian pairs.

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight` | data | ∃ m₀ ≤ S.ideal, m₀.FG ∧ ∃ n, Iⁿ ≤ m₀ • A. |
| `Almost.Algebra.isTight_span` | example | For ϖ ∈ S.ideal, (ϖ • A) is tight. |
| `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.mono` | relation | A subideal of a tight ideal is tight; powers of tight ideals are tight. |
| `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.map` | functoriality | Tightness is preserved by base change along A → A'. |
| `Almost.Algebra.jacobson` | constructor | rad(A) := (Ideal.jacobson ⊥ of A_*)^a. |
| `Almost.Algebra.le_jacobson_toAlmost_iff` | characterisation | J^a ≤ rad(R^a) ↔ S.ideal • J ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥ (GR 5.1.2). |
| `Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair` | data | I ≤ rad A ∧ HenselianRing A_* (S.ideal • I_*). |
| `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_toAlmost_iff` | characterisation | IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R (S.ideal • J) (GR 5.1.10). |
| `Almost.Algebra.isHenselianPair_of_isAdicComplete` | compatibility | If A ≅ lim A/Iⁿ then (A, I) is henselian (GR Remark 5.3.7). |
| `Almost.Algebra.Ideal.IsTight.elements_le_jacobson` | relation | For I tight in rad(A): I_* ≤ rad(A_*), and (A_*, I_*) is henselian if (A, I) is (GR Corollary 5.1.16). |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_varpi` (computation): For ϖ ∈ S.ideal, the ideal ϖA is tight (m₀ = ϖV, n = 1).
- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_unit` (non-example): For S = ofValuationRing K° and A = V^a, the unit ideal A is not tight: A ⊆ m₀A would force m ⊆ m₀ for a finitely generated (hence principal) m₀ = εK° ⊊ m.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsTight_test_zero` (degenerate): The zero ideal of any almost algebra is tight.
- `Almost.Algebra.IsHenselianPair_test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V: every ideal is tight and IsHenselianPair (R^a) (J^a) ↔ HenselianRing R J (Mathlib), since then m·J = J and (R^a)_* = R.

**Uses.**

- GR Theorems 5.3.24 and 5.3.27 (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras): the lifting equivalences hold for tight ideals
- GR Lemma 5.1.6 (P0/almost-nakayama): Nakayama for almost finitely generated modules needs I tight and in rad(A)
- GR Proposition 5.1.17 (P0/tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting): idempotents lift along tight henselian pairs
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (GR 5.4, Sch12 Proposition 7.4): henselian pairs along (ϖ) and their almost versions
- P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi: Nakayama along the tight ideal generated by a root of ϖ

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Submodule.FG`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Definition 5.1.5, p. 103.

  > Definition 5.1.5. Let I be an ideal of a V a -algebra A. We say that I is tight if there exists a finitely generated subideal m0 ⊂ m and an integer n ∈ N such that I n ⊂ m0 A.

  Tight ideals.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Definition 5.1.1, p. 103.

  > Definition 5.1.1. Let A be a V a -algebra. The Jacobson radical of A is the ideal rad(A) := rad(A∗ )a

  Jacobson radical.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Lemma 5.1.2, p. 103.

  > Lemma 5.1.2. Let R be a V -algebra, I ⊂ R an ideal. Then I a ⊂ rad(Ra ) if and only if mI ⊂ rad(R).

  Comparison of radicals.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Definition 5.1.8, p. 104.

  Henselian pairs.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, Remark 5.3.7, p. 112.

  > Remark 5.3.7. Notice that, in the situation of lemma 5.3.5, the pair (A∞ , I) is henselian.

  Complete pairs are henselian.


#### `almost-nakayama` — Almost Nakayama lemma for tight ideals

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Henselian`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ rad(A) a tight ideal. (i) If M is an almost finitely generated A-module with IM = M, then M = 0. (ii) If φ : N → M is a morphism of almost finite projective A-modules such that φ ⊗_A A/I is an isomorphism, then φ is an isomorphism. (iii) If M is almost finitely generated and M ⊗_A A/I = 0 then M = 0.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; I tight (Iⁿ ⊆ m₀A) and I ⊆ rad(A).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): pick a finitely generated Q with m₀M ⊆ Q ⊆ M; then M = IⁿM ⊆ m₀M ⊆ Q, so M = Q is finitely generated; for a finitely generated A_*-submodule M₀ with M₀^a = M one gets m₀M₀ ⊆ mI_*·m₀M₀, and mI_* ⊆ rad(A_*) (GR Lemma 5.1.2), so m₀M₀ = 0 by Nakayama, whence mM₀ = 0 and M = 0 (GR proof of Lemma 5.1.6).
2. (ii): Coker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 and Coker φ almost finitely generated (GR Lemma 2.3.17(i)) give Coker φ = 0; then Ker φ is almost finitely generated (Lemma 2.3.17(ii), M almost finitely presented) and Ker φ ⊗ A/I = 0 by flatness of M, so Ker φ = 0 (GR Corollary 5.1.7).
3. (iii) is (i) since M ⊗ A/I = M/IM.

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a (K perfectoid), I = ϖA: an almost finitely generated M with M = ϖM is zero; the hypothesis 'almost finitely generated' is needed, since K = K°[1/ϖ] satisfies K = ϖK.
- Used in P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi with I generated by a root of ϖ.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`, `mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103.

  > Lemma 5.1.6. Let A be a V a -algebra, I ⊂ rad(A) a tight ideal. If M is an almost finitely generated A-module with IM = M, we have M = 0.

  Part (i).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Corollary 5.1.7, p. 104.

  > Corollary 5.1.7. Let A, I be as in lemma 5.1.6; suppose that φ : N → M is an A-linear morphism of almost finitely generated projective A-modules such that φ ⊗A 1A/I is an isomorphism. Then φ is an isomorphism.

  Part (ii).


#### `tight-henselian-idempotent-lifting` — Idempotents lift uniquely along tight henselian pairs

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Henselian`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup and (A, I) a tight henselian pair of almost algebras (e.g. A I-adically complete with I tight). Then A → A/I induces a bijection from the idempotents of A_* to the idempotents of (A/I)_*.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; (A, I) tight henselian.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. If m̃ has homological dimension ≤ 1: (A_*, I_*) is henselian (GR Corollary 5.1.16), so idempotents of A_* and A_*/I_* correspond; an idempotent almost element of A/I lifts to an almost element of A because the obstruction in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, I) dies in Ext¹(V^a, I) coming from Ext¹(V^a, Iⁿ) for n large (Claim 5.1.19, using Ext²(V^a, −) = 0 from Lemma 2.4.14), and liftings of idempotents along nilpotent thickenings are unique (GR Proposition 2.5.13(i)).
2. General m: write m as a filtered union of subideals m_λ with m_λ² = m_λ and m̃_λ flat of homological dimension ≤ 1 (GR Theorem 2.1.12), apply the first case to each (V, m_λ) and glue the unique lifts (GR proof of Proposition 5.1.17).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = (V⟦X⟧)^a and I = XA: idempotents of A_* and of (A/I)_* = (V^a)_* = V_*-idempotents agree.
- Used with the rank decomposition to lift the decomposition A/ϖ = ∏ Ā_i to A (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).

#### `unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction` — Unramifiedness lifts from the reduction modulo a tight ideal

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra, I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A I-adically complete (A ≅ lim_n A/I^{n+1}). (i) For ideals I, J and φ : A → B: if φ ⊗ A/I and φ ⊗ A/J are unramified then so is φ ⊗ A/IJ. (ii) If B is an almost finite projective A-algebra such that B/IB is unramified over A/I, then B is unramified over A. (iii) More generally, for I ⊆ rad(A) tight and B almost finite over A with B/IB unramified over A/I, B is unramified over A.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete for (ii).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): reduce to IJ = 0; B is B ⊗_A B-flat by the Tor base change (Claim 5.2.13), and almost projective by the 2-cartesian square of almost projective modules over B ⊗ B/(I' ∩ J') (GR Proposition 3.4.21) and Lemma 3.2.25(i) (GR proof of Theorem 5.2.12(ii)).
2. (ii): by (i) with J = Iⁿ, each B_n := B/I^{n+1}B is unramified over A_n; the diagonal idempotents e_n (P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation) are compatible by uniqueness and define an idempotent of lim (B_n ⊗ B_n)_* = (B ⊗_A B)_* (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, Claim 5.3.25); μ = lim μ_n and I_{B/A} = lim I_{B_n/A_n} give conditions (ii), (iii) of the characterisation (GR Claim 5.3.29).
3. (iii): Ω_{B/A} is almost finitely generated with Ω ⊗ A/I = 0, so Ω = 0 (P0/almost-nakayama); then I_{B/A} is idempotent and locally generated by idempotents after inverting generators of m₀ and modulo m₀ (GR Corollary 5.2.15 via Theorem 5.2.12(iv) and Theorem 5.2.4).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a and B = L°a (L/K finite étale), unramifiedness of L°a/K°a follows from that of (L°/ϖ)^a over (K°/ϖ)^a.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-idempotent-characterisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-nakayama`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-differentials`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/etale-morphisms-stability`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.2, Theorem 5.2.12(ii), p. 109.

  > (ii) If φ ⊗A 1A/I and φ ⊗A 1A/J are unramified, then the same holds for φ ⊗A 1A/IJ .

  Part (i).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, Claim 5.3.29, p. 116.

  > Claim 5.3.29. Let B be an almost finitely generated projective A∞ -algebra such that B0 := B ⊗A∞ A0 is unramified. Then B is unramified.

  Part (ii).

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.2, Corollary 5.2.15, p. 110.

  > Corollary 5.2.15. Let I ⊂ rad(A) be a tight ideal. If B is an almost finite A-algebra and B/IB is unramified over A/I, then B is unramified over A.

  Part (iii).


#### `adic-almost-projective-modules` — Almost finite projective modules over I-adically complete almost algebras

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, A an almost algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal with A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism, A_n := A/I^{n+1}. Then M ↦ (M ⊗_A A_n)_n is an equivalence from almost finite projective A-modules to compatible systems (M_n) of almost finite projective A_n-modules (M_{n+1} ⊗ A_n ≅ M_n), with quasi-inverse (M_n) ↦ lim_n M_n; in particular P ≅ lim_n P ⊗_A A_n for every almost finite projective P. Moreover an I-c-adic A-module whose reduction M_0 is almost finitely generated is almost finitely generated with M ⊗_A A_n ≅ M_n.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; I tight; A I-adically complete (GR's conditions (a), (b) of Lemma 5.3.5 for A_n = A/I^{n+1}).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Topological modules over A∞ with I-c-adic topology correspond to compatible systems (GR Lemma 5.3.16).
2. Almost finite generation of lim M_n from M_0 almost finitely generated and I tight: find almost elements whose images generate modulo m₀ at level n+1, then I^{n+1}M ⊆ N and N is closed (GR Lemmas 5.3.17, 5.3.18).
3. Almost projectivity of lim M_n: a topologically almost split surjection from the completed free module and ε-factorisations (GR Lemma 5.3.20).
4. Full faithfulness: P → lim P ⊗ A_n is an isomorphism, first for P = A^r, then for P almost finite projective via ε-factorisations P → Aⁿ → P (GR Claim 5.3.25, P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation).

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a, I = ϖA: almost finite projective K°a-modules are the limits of compatible almost finite projective (K°/ϖ^n)^a-modules.
- P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras uses this for the underlying modules of finite étale algebras.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-projective-epsilon-factorisation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finitely-generated-and-presented`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, Theorem 5.3.24, p. 115.

  > Theorem 5.3.24. In the situation of (5.3.21), suppose that I is tight. Then (5.3.22) is an equivalence of categories.

  The equivalence.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, (5.3.21), p. 115.

  > 5.3.21. For a V a -algebra A, let us denote by A-Modafpr the full subcategory of A-Mod consisting of all almost finitely generated projective A-modules.

  The categories involved.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, Claim 5.3.25, p. 115.

  > Claim 5.3.25. Let P be an almost finitely generated projective A∞ -module. Then the natural morphism

  P ≅ lim P ⊗ A_n.

#### `finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras` — Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely modulo a tight ideal of a complete almost algebra

*theorem* **Planet:** *Finite étale lifting*. Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic`.

**Statement.** Let S = (V, m) be a basic setup, A an almost V-algebra and I ⊆ A a tight ideal such that A is I-adically complete (A → lim_n A/I^{n+1} an isomorphism). Then B ↦ B ⊗_A A/I is an equivalence of categories A_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet, with quasi-inverse B₀ ↦ lim_n B_n, where B_n is the unique finite étale A/I^{n+1}-algebra lifting B₀. In particular, for ϖ ∈ m and A ϖ-adically complete, A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet; this is Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over an arbitrary basic setup (Sch12 states it for S = (K°, K°°) and A flat over K°a). Complements: if A is flat over V^a then every B ∈ A_fet is flat over V^a and ϖ-adically complete (P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete); for root setups B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B/ϖB is over A/ϖ (P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup (m̃ flat, needed for the cotangent complex behind the nilpotent lifting).
- I tight (e.g. I = ϖA with ϖ ∈ m) and A I-adically complete; flatness of A over V^a is not needed for the equivalence itself.
- Sch12 cites GR Theorem 5.3.27 (same number in the book and in arXiv v3).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Finite levels: A_{n+1} → A_n has nilpotent kernel, so A_{n+1,fet} ≃ A_{n,fet} (P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras (iv)); hence 2-lim_n (A_n)_fet ≃ (A/I)_fet (GR proof of Theorem 5.3.27).
2. Passage to the limit: for a compatible system (B_n), B := lim B_n is almost finite projective over A with B ⊗ A_n ≅ B_n (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules), unramified (P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction (ii)), hence étale (almost projective ⇒ flat) and almost finitely presented (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), i.e. B ∈ A_fet.
3. Full faithfulness: Hom_A(B, C) = lim_n Hom_{A_n}(B_n, C_n) because C ≅ lim C_n (Claim 5.3.25) and morphisms of finite étale algebras lift uniquely at each finite level.

**Acceptance.**

- S = (K°, K°°), A = K°a, ϖ ∈ K°°: K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet, the middle link in K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet (Sch12 §4).
- A finite étale (A/ϖ)-algebra has exactly one finite étale lift to A, up to unique isomorphism.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/unramified-lifts-from-complete-reduction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`

**Sources.**

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, Theorem 5.3.27, p. 116.

  > Theorem 5.3.27. In the situation of (5.3.21), suppose that I is tight. Then (5.3.23) is an equivalence of categories.

  The equivalence A∞-Ét_afp → A₀-Ét_afp for a tight ideal I.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.3.27, p. 116.

  > It follows easily from theorem 3.2.28(ii) that the natural functor 2-lim An -Étafp →

  Finite-level step.

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.17, p. 21.

  > Then the functor B 7→ B ⊗A A/$ induces an equivalence of categories Afét ∼

  Sch12's statement for flat, ϖ-adically complete K°a-algebras A: the special case S = (K°, K°°), I = ϖA.

#### `finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete` — Finite étale algebras over complete flat almost algebras are flat and complete

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is ϖ-adically complete (B ≅ lim_n B/ϖⁿB), and if A is flat over V^a then so is B.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; A ϖ-adically complete; for the flatness clause, A flat over V^a.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. B is almost finite projective over A (P0/almost-finite-projective-iff), so B ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A A/ϖ^n (P0/adic-almost-projective-modules, Claim 5.3.25) and B ⊗_A A/ϖⁿ = B/ϖⁿB.
2. B almost projective over A ⇒ flat over A; flatness is transitive along A → B (GR Lemma 2.4.7), so B is flat over V^a.

**Acceptance.**

- For A = K°a and B = L°a (L/K finite, K perfectoid): L°a is flat and ϖ-adically complete, as L° is.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/adic-almost-projective-modules`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-iff`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`

**Sources.**

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.17, p. 21.

  > Any B ∈ Afét is again flat over K

  Sch12's complement to Theorem 4.17, proved there only by 'The rest is easy'.


#### `uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi` — Uniform finite projectivity of a finite étale algebra can be checked modulo ϖ (root setups)

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Adic`.

**Statement.** Let S be the root setup of (ϖ_n) (P0/root-ideal-basic-setup), ϖ = ϖ_0, A an almost algebra which is ϖ-adically complete, and B ∈ A_fet. Then B is uniformly almost finitely generated over A with bound r iff B/ϖB is uniformly almost finitely generated over A/ϖ with bound r; hence B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B ⊗_A A/ϖ is uniformly finite projective over A/ϖ. (Sch12 Theorem 4.17, last sentence, over (K°, K°°); in a general basic setup no source proves the reverse implication.)

**Hypotheses.**

- S a root setup (used to find, for each k, elements ϖ_{k+1} and t = ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} with ϖ = ϖ_{k+1}²·t); A ϖ-adically complete; B finite étale over A.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. ⇒: base change preserves uniform bounds (GR Lemma 2.3.7(v)).
2. ⇐: fix k ≥ 1 and δ := ϖ_{k+1}. Choose φ̄ : (A/ϖ)^r → B/ϖB with cokernel killed by δ, and lift δ·φ̄ to φ : A^r → B (almost elements lift up to multiplication by δ, P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints (v)); then δ²B ⊆ φ(A^r) + ϖB.
3. Let C := coker φ, an almost finitely generated A-module; δ²C ⊆ ϖC = t·δ²C with t := ϖ_{k+1}^{p^{k+1}−2} ∈ m (p^{k+1} ≥ 3 for k ≥ 1), so M := δ²C satisfies M = tM.
4. tA is tight (t ∈ m) and contained in rad(A) because t^{p^{k+1}} ∈ ϖA and A is ϖ-adically complete; M is almost finitely generated, so M = 0 by P0/almost-nakayama; hence δ² = ϖ_{k+1}² kills coker φ, and so does ϖ_k (a multiple of ϖ_{k+1}²).
5. Every ε ∈ m is a multiple of some ϖ_k, so for every ε there is A^r → B with cokernel killed by ε: B is uniformly almost finitely generated with bound r (P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion, condition (A)).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Theorem 4.17 over (K°, K°°) with ϖ having compatible p-power roots; used by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for 'S°a is uniformly finite projective over R°a'.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-nakayama`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/tight-ideal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-generation-epsilon-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §4, Theorem 4.17, p. 21.

  > Moreover, B is a uniformly finite projective A-module if and only if B ⊗A A/$ is a uniformly finite projective A/$-module.

  The statement, whose proof Sch12 calls easy.

- Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), arXiv v3, §5.1, Lemma 5.1.6, p. 103.

  > Lemma 5.1.6. Let A be a V a -algebra, I ⊂ rad(A) a tight ideal. If M is an almost finitely generated A-module with IM = M, we have M = 0.

  The Nakayama step of the proof.


#### `almost-completeness-via-almost-elements` — ϖ-adic completeness of an almost module and of its almost elements

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Completion`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m, and M an almost V-module whose almost elements M_* have no ϖ-torsion. Then: (i) (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿM_* for all n; (ii) M_*/ϖⁿM_* → (M/ϖⁿM)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel; (iii) M is ϖ-adically complete (M → lim_n M/ϖⁿM an isomorphism in Almost.Module S) iff M_* is ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) M_*`); the comparison lim M_*/ϖⁿ → lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* = (lim M/ϖⁿ)_* is injective with almost zero cokernel, the lim¹ of the almost zero cokernels being almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; M_* ϖ-torsion-free (for S = (K°, K°°) this is flatness of M, Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i)).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): ϖ is injective on M_* hence a monomorphism on M, so ϖⁿM ≅ M and (ϖⁿM)_* = ϖⁿ M_*.
2. (ii): left exactness of (−)_* gives injectivity; the cokernel embeds in Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M)[ϖⁿ], and Ext¹_{V^a}(V^a, M) is almost zero because V^a is almost projective (Bhatt proof of Lemma 4.4.1(3)).
3. (iii) ⇒: (−)_* commutes with limits, so M_* ≅ lim (M/ϖⁿ)_* ⊇ lim M_*/ϖⁿ with almost zero cokernel Q (lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero), and Q is killed by ϖ ∈ m; since M_* is ϖ-torsion-free, Bhatt Lemma 4.4.2 (for α injective between ϖ-torsion-free modules with ϖ-torsion cokernel, the source is complete iff the target is) shows M_* is complete.
4. (iii) ⇐: (−)^a preserves limits (it has a left adjoint (−)_! and a right adjoint), and M ≅ (M_*)^a.

**Acceptance.**

- For S = (K°, K°°) this is Sch12 Lemma 5.3(iii)-(iv); for Bhatt's setup (R, I) and a finitely generated J, Bhatt Proposition 4.4.3 proves the analogue without torsion-freeness using derived completeness.
- M = (K°/ϖ)^a is ϖ-adically complete but M_* = Hom(K°°, K°/ϖ) has ϖ-torsion: the torsion-freeness hypothesis is not decorative for (i).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`

**Sources.**

- Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces* (arXiv:1111.4914v1), arXiv v1, §5, Lemma 5.3(iv), p. 22.

  > (iv) If M is flat over K ◦a , then M is $-adically complete if and only if M∗ is $-adically complete.

  Statement (iii) over (K°, K°°).

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.4, Lemma 4.4.1(3), p. 30.

  > 3. Assume M is almost flat. Then for each t ∈ K ◦ , we have tM∗ ≃ (tM )∗ , and M∗ /tM∗ ⊂ (M/tM )∗ by the canonical map.

  Statements (i)-(ii).

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.4, proof of Lemma 4.4.1(3), p. 31.

  > Now note that Ext1Ra (Ra , M ) is almost zero (as it vanishes once we pass back to the almost world)

  The almost zero cokernel.

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.4, Lemma 4.4.2, p. 31.

  > Assume that α is injective with t-torsion cokernel Q. Then M is t-adically complete if and only if N is so.

  The completeness transfer.

- Bhatt, *Lecture notes for a class on perfectoid spaces* (2017), Lecture notes (April 23, 2017), §4.4, Proposition 4.4.3, p. 32.

  > Proposition 4.4.3. Fix (R, I) as in the rest of this section. Fix J = (f1 , ..., fr ) ⊂ R a finitely generated ideal. Then an Ra -module M is J-adically complete if and only if M∗ is so.

#### `almost-exactness-passes-to-completion` — Complete torsion-free complexes that are almost exact modulo ϖ are almost exact, with the lim¹ term controlled

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Completion`.

**Statement.** Let S be a basic setup, ϖ ∈ m and C^• a cochain complex of V-modules (C^i = 0 for i < 0) such that every C^i is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete. If the cohomology of C^•/ϖC^• is almost zero in every degree, then: (i) H^i(C^•/ϖⁿC^•) is almost zero for all n ≥ 1 and all i; (ii) for every i there is an exact sequence 0 → lim¹_n H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) → H^i(C^•) → lim_n H^i(C^•/ϖⁿ) → 0 (Milnor sequence of the tower C^• = lim_n C^•/ϖⁿ, whose transition maps are termwise surjective), and both outer terms are almost zero, so H^i(C^•) is almost zero; (iii) C^•[1/ϖ] is exact. Neither the torsion-freeness nor the completeness can be dropped, and the lim¹ term is not discarded: it is almost zero because every H^{i−1}(C^•/ϖⁿ) is.

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; ϖ ∈ m; C^i ϖ-torsion-free (for exactness of 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} → C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0) and ϖ-adically complete (C^i = lim C^i/ϖⁿ).

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. (i): torsion-freeness makes 0 → C/ϖ^{n−1} →·ϖ C/ϖⁿ → C/ϖ → 0 exact; the long exact cohomology sequence (Mathlib `ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`) and closure of almost zero modules under extensions (P0/almost-zero-serre-class) give induction on n.
2. (ii): completeness and surjectivity of transitions give the short exact sequence of complexes 0 → C^• → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → ∏_n C^•/ϖⁿ → 0 (second map (x_n) ↦ (x_n − x̄_{n+1})); its long exact cohomology sequence, with H^i(∏_n −) = ∏_n H^i(−) for modules, is the Milnor sequence.
3. Products, lim and lim¹ of almost zero modules are almost zero (P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits), so H^i(C^•) is an extension of almost zero modules.
4. (iii): localisation at ϖ is exact and kills almost zero modules (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

**Acceptance.**

- Non-example for completeness: C^0 = V[1/ϖ] (torsion-free, not ϖ-adically separated), C^i = 0 otherwise: C/ϖ = 0 is exact, but H^0(C) = V[1/ϖ] is not almost zero.
- ECD Proposition 8.8: the complex 0 → R⁺ → S⁺ → O⁺(Y ×_X Y) → ⋯ for a v-cover of a totally disconnected X is almost exact because it is so modulo ϖ; Berkeley proof of Proposition 8.2.8 for affinoid pro-étale covers.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:HomologicalComplex.homology`

**Sources.**

- Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds* (arXiv:1709.07343v4), arXiv v4, §8, proof of Proposition 8.8, p. 42.

#### `almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology` — Almost sheaves, almost sheaf cohomology and almost Čech complexes on a site

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Sheaf`.

**Statement.** Let (C, J) be a site and S = (V, m) a basic setup. For a sheaf F of V-modules on (C, J) (Mathlib `Sheaf J (ModuleCat V)`): F is almost zero if m·F(U) = 0 for all U; almost zero sheaves form a Serre class of the abelian category of sheaves, and the Serre localization Almost.Sheaf J S is the category of sheaves of almost V-modules (GR 3.3.1–3.3.2: a basic setup relative to the topos of (C, J)), with exact localization F ↦ F^a. For X ∈ C and n ≥ 0 the cohomology H^n(X, F) of the underlying abelian sheaf (Mathlib `Sheaf.H'`) is a V-module through the action of V on F, and its almostification H^n(X, F)^a ∈ Almost.Module S depends only on F^a (almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology); F is almost acyclic on X if H^n(X, F)^a = 0 for n > 0. For a family 𝔘 = (U_i → X) the Čech complex Č(𝔘, F) (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` on the underlying presheaf) is a complex of V-modules with almostification Č(𝔘, F)^a, and the augmented complex F(X) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact if its cohomology is almost zero. The Čech-to-derived comparison for almost acyclic bases is P0/almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion.

**Hypotheses.**

- (C, J) a site whose category of sheaves of V-modules is abelian with enough injectives (Mathlib `sheafIsAbelian`, `HasSheafify`); S a basic setup.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Almost zero sheaves: m·F = 0 is closed under subsheaves, quotient sheaves (sheafification preserves m-torsion: m kills the presheaf quotient, hence its sheafification) and extensions (m² = m), so it is a Serre class.
2. V-action on cohomology: each v ∈ V acts on F by an endomorphism of sheaves, hence on H^n(X, F) by functoriality (`Sheaf.H.map`), making H^n(X, F) a V-module; if m·F = 0 then ε acts by zero on H^n.
3. Almost Čech complex: apply cechComplexFunctor to the presheaf of V-modules and then toAlmost S termwise.
4. Relative basic setup: Almost.Sheaf J S is equivalent to sheaves on (C, J) with values in almost modules computed through (−)_* (GR 3.3.2: M_* is a sheaf).

**Acceptance.**

- On the one-point site, Almost.Sheaf J S ≃ Almost.Module S and almost cohomology vanishes in positive degrees.
- For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and F = O⁺_X (a sheaf of R⁺-modules for the setup (R⁺, root ideal)), PerfectoidSpaces:P2 proves H^n(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for n > 0.

**API.** What a user needs in order to work with the object without unfolding its definition.

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostZero` | data | For F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat V): ∀ U, S.IsAlmostZero (F.val.obj U). |
| `Almost.Sheaf.almostZero_isSerreClass` | instance | The almost zero sheaves form a Serre class of Sheaf J (ModuleCat V). |
| `Almost.Sheaf` | data | Almost.Sheaf J S: the Serre localization of Sheaf J (ModuleCat V) at almost isomorphisms of sheaves. |
| `Almost.Sheaf.toAlmost` | constructor | The exact localization functor F ↦ F^a. |
| `Almost.Sheaf.cohomologyModule` | structure | The V-module structure on H^n(X, F) (Sheaf.H') from the V-action on F. |
| `Almost.Sheaf.almostH` | constructor | H^n(X, F)^a := (toAlmost S).obj (H^n(X, F) as V-module). |
| `Almost.Sheaf.IsAlmostAcyclic` | data | ∀ n > 0, IsZero (almostH F n X). |
| `Almost.Sheaf.almostCech` | constructor | The almost Čech complex (toAlmost S).mapHomologicalComplex (cechComplexFunctor 𝔘 applied to F). |
| `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_eq_zero_of_isAlmostZero` | relation | Almost zero sheaves have almost zero cohomology in all degrees; almostH factors through toAlmost. |
| `Almost.Sheaf.almostH_localization` | compatibility | For ϖ ∈ S.ideal: almostH F n X ≅ 0 ⇒ H^n(X, F) ⊗ V[1/ϖ] = 0 (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion). |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `Almost.Sheaf.test_point` (degenerate): For the site with one object and only the trivial covering, Almost.Sheaf J S ≌ Almost.Module S and almostH F n X = 0 for n > 0.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_constant_residue` (computation): For S = ofValuationRing K° and the constant sheaf k = K°/K°° on any site, F is almost zero, so almostH F n X ≅ 0 for all n, even when H^n(X, k) ≠ 0.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_not_acyclic` (non-example): On the site of open subsets of the circle S¹, the constant sheaf k has H¹(S¹, k) = k ≠ 0 but is almost acyclic: IsAlmostAcyclic must not be defined as vanishing of H^n.
- `Almost.Sheaf.test_classical` (compatibility): For S = classical V, almostH F n X is Mathlib's Sheaf.H' of the underlying abelian sheaf with its V-module structure, via Almost.Module.classicalEquiv.

**Uses.**

#### `almost-cech-acyclicity-criterion` — Almost Čech acyclicity on a basis implies almost acyclicity

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/Algebra/Almost/Sheaf`.

**Statement.** Let (C, J) be a site, S a basic setup, F a sheaf of V-modules, and 𝔅 a full subcategory of C stable under fibre products such that every covering of an object of 𝔅 is refined by a covering by objects of 𝔅 (e.g. rational subsets of an affinoid adic space with finite rational covers, or affinoid perfectoid objects of a pro-étale or v-site). If for every U ∈ 𝔅 and every covering 𝔘 of U by objects of 𝔅 the augmented Čech complex F(U) → Č(𝔘, F) is almost exact, then H^n(U, F) is almost zero for all U ∈ 𝔅 and n > 0 (and H^0(U, F) = F(U)).

**Hypotheses.**

- S a basic setup; 𝔅 as stated; F a sheaf of V-modules.

**Construction, or proof, in steps.**

1. Almostify DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison: the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence Ȟ^p(𝔘, H^q(F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, F) is a spectral sequence of V-modules; the exact functor toAlmost S carries it to a spectral sequence in Almost.Module S.
2. Induction on n (Cartan's argument, ECD proof of Proposition 8.8): suppose H^q(V, F)^a = 0 for 0 < q < n and all V ∈ 𝔅; for α ∈ H^n(U, F) and ε ∈ m choose a covering 𝔘 by objects of 𝔅 on which α dies (locality of cohomology); the spectral sequence and the almost exactness of the Čech complexes of 𝔘 and of its fibre products show ε·α = 0.

**Acceptance.**

- Berkeley Theorem 7.4.4 and Sch12 Proposition 6.14: almost exact Čech complexes of O⁺ for finite rational covers of a perfectoid affinoid give H^i(X, O⁺)^a = 0 for i > 0.
- In the classical setup this is Cartan's lemma on acyclic bases (D0).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-serre-class`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison`

**Sources.**

- Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds* (arXiv:1709.07343v4), arXiv v4, §8, proof of Proposition 8.8, p. 42.

  > is almost exact. As everything is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsionfree, where ϖ ∈ R+ is a

  The almost exactness of Čech complexes; the proof continues with the induction on the minimal non-almost-vanishing degree.

- Scholze–Weinstein, *Berkeley lectures on p-adic geometry*, Lecture 7, proof of Theorem 7.4.4, p. 53.

  > We will show that for any finite rational covering X = i Ui , all cohomology groups of the Cech complex

  Almost Čech exactness as the route to almost acyclicity.


### Acceptance tests of the layer

- For the classical setup `(V, V)` every construction reduces to ordinary commutative algebra: `M ↦ M^a` is an
  equivalence, almost flat/projective/finitely presented are Mathlib's notions, finite étale almost algebras are
  Mathlib's finite étale algebras, and almost henselian pairs are Mathlib's henselian pairs.
- For `S = (K°, K°°)`, `K` the completion of `ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})`: the residue field is almost zero; `K°a` is not a
  projective object; `((K°/ϖ)^a)_* = Hom_{K°}(K°°, K°/ϖ) ⊋ K°/ϖ`; for `L = K(√p)` (`p ≠ 2`) `L°a` is uniformly almost
  finitely presented with bound 2, finite étale over `K°a` with an almost (not honest) diagonal idempotent, and has
  perfect almost trace form.
- For `A` a `ϖ`-adically complete almost algebra (`ϖ ∈ m`), `A_fet ≃ (A/ϖ)_fet`; with `A = K°a` this is the middle
  link of Sch12's chain `K_fet ≃ K°a_fet ≃ (K°a/ϖ)_fet = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)_fet ≃ K♭°a_fet ≃ K♭_fet`.
- A complex of `ϖ`-torsion-free, `ϖ`-adically complete modules that is almost exact modulo `ϖ` is almost exact,
  and exact after inverting `ϖ`; the complex `V[1/ϖ]` in degree 0 shows that completeness cannot be dropped.
- On a site, a sheaf of `V`-modules whose Čech complexes on a basis are almost exact has almost zero higher
  cohomology on the basis (the form in which P2 and D2 prove almost acyclicity of `O⁺`).

PerfectoidSpaces:P0 builds the almost cotangent complex L_{B/A} := B_!! ⊗ L_{(V^a×B)!!/(V^a×A)!!} and its deformation theory on these. Needed by: `almost-cotangent-complex`, `almost-cotangent-comparison-classical`, `cotangent-transitivity`, `cotangent-flat-base-change`, `almost-exal-ext-comparison`.
- **`tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0e-effective-descent-and-spreading-out`** — Effective faithfully flat descent for modules and for commutative algebras along a faithfully flat ring map A → B: the functor from A-modules (A-algebras) to B-modules (B-algebras) with descent data (isomorphism p₂*N ≅ p₁*N over B ⊗_A B satisfying the cocycle condition) is an equivalence, with descent of flatness, finite generation, finite presentation, finite projectivity and (weak) étaleness. Mathlib has comonadicity of extension of scalars (`comonadicExtendScalars`) and the Amitsur equalizer for rings, but not the descent-data formulation; PerfectoidSpaces:P0 transports this statement to almost modules and almost algebras along A_!! → B_!!. Needed by: `almost-faithfully-flat-descent`.

Reason: The remark constructs (L, φ′, ψ′) from (N, φ, ψ) by the push-out (2.3.3) whose arrows are named φ′ and ψ′; the condition must concern these two maps, and the second map is called ψ′ in (2.3.3). - **PerfectoidSpaces/E2** (misprint, Gabber–Ramero, *Almost ring theory* (arXiv:math/0201175v3), §4.1, proof of Lemma 4.1.2(i), p. 72 (arXiv:math/0201175v3)). ## P1. Perfectoid Tate rings, tilts and marked untilts


**Coverage: source_decomposed.** This layer defines perfectoid Tate rings in the generality of ECD Definition 3.1 — complete, uniform, with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ such that ϖ^p divides p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective — with no perfectoid base field and in characteristic 0 and p alike. It constructs the tilt with its topology, limiting addition, sharp map and functoriality, proves the Frobenius-surjectivity criterion (with the condition ϖ^p | p kept), the characteristic-p characterisation and the perfectoid-field characterisation, identifies Fontaine's θ with the map Mathlib already has and proves that its kernel is generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor, classifies marked untilts of a characteristic-p perfectoid pair by primitive ideals of degree 1 — including the converse construction with its topology and plus ring — and deduces the tilting equivalence between perfectoid algebras over R and over R♭, with unit and counit. It instantiates the almost mathematics of P0 with the setup (R°, R°°) and gives the almost-integral form of the tilting equivalence over an arbitrary base. For the stages that transport perfectoidness along maps it adds the tilt of a uniform (not yet perfectoid) Tate ring, the metric perfectoid criterion, Euclidean division and sharp approximation, the correspondence of strict inclusions under tilting, and completed filtered colimits with their tilts.

**What the pinned libraries already contain.** Mathlib (082e2d3): `Perfection M p` (the monoid lim_{x↦x^p} M, a ring in characteristic p), `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` (lim_{x↦x^p} R ≅ lim_Φ R/I multiplicatively for I-adically complete R), `Perfection.teichmuller`, `PreTilt O p` = Perfection (O/p) p, `PreTilt.untilt` (the sharp map for p-adically complete O), `PreTilt.val` and `Tilt K v O hv p` (the tilt of a real-valued field as a fraction field), `WittVector.fontaineTheta` with `surjective_fontaineTheta`, `fontaineThetaInvertP` and `BDeRhamPlus`. Mathlib has no perfectoid predicate, no ring structure on lim_{x↦x^p} R in characteristic 0, no tilt of a Tate ring, no kernel statement for θ and no untilt. Tau Ceti (f790474): `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `IsPseudoUniformizer`, `powerBoundedSubring`, `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `IsBounded`, `Pair`, `Pair.Hom`, `IsRingOfIntegralElements`, the open mapping theorem `IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion`, and Tate structures on ℚ_p and K((X)). It has no perfectoid material. Every comparison node below says which half of a statement the libraries supply.

**Conventions pinned for this layer.**
- p is a fixed prime (`[Fact p.Prime]`). A Tate ring is a commutative topological ring with `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`; "complete" means `CompleteSpace` and `T2Space` for the uniform structure of the additive group (anchor convention 3).
- R° is `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring R`, R°° its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements; uniform means `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded (R° : Set R)`; a pseudo-uniformizer is a topologically nilpotent unit. Rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained in R° (`IsRingOfIntegralElements`); the plus ring is always explicit.
- For ideals I, J ⊆ A with p ∈ J and x^p ∈ J for x ∈ I, Φ: A/I → A/J is the ring homomorphism x ↦ x^p (`Perfectoid.frobeniusQuot`).
- ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n denotes a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R°; exponents ϖ^q are taken for q ∈ ℤ[1/p]. The spectral gauge |x|_ϖ = inf{2^{-q} : ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°} is normalised by |ϖ| = 1/2.
- R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R has elements (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} with (x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}, and x♯ = x^{(0)}; ♯ is multiplicative and continuous and is never used as if it were additive.
- For a perfect ring R+ of characteristic p, W(R+) is written with Teichmüller coordinates Σp^n[x_n]; A_inf(R, R+) = W(R+). An element ξ is primitive of degree 1 if ξ_0 is topologically nilpotent and ξ_1 is a unit; primitive ideals are principal with a primitive generator (equivalently generated by p + [ϖ]α, ECD 3.15).
- Almost mathematics is P0's, over the basic setup (R°, R°°) of P1/perfectoid-almost-setup; M_* denotes almost elements. R°a-Perf consists of ϖ-adically complete R°a-algebras A with A_* ϖ-torsion free and Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ; (R°a/ϖ)-Perf consists of (R°/ϖ)^a-algebras flat over ℤ[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) (x ↦ ϖ) with Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B. Over a general base, flatness over R°a or (R°/ϖ)^a is not the right condition (perfectoid quotients are not flat).
- Lean names are in the namespace `Perfectoid` (written without the `TauCeti.` prefix), in modules `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/*`; the Banach-field theorem is in `TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/BanachField`.

**Dependencies.** Anchor Layer 0 (`tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`: Tate rings, power-bounded elements, open mapping), anchor Layer 4.2 (uniformity), anchor Layer 6 (`…#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve`: the perfect field F and A_inf, compared in P1/anchor-layer-6-compatibility), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0` (classical cotangent complex), `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0` (Berkovich spectra, for Kedlaya's Banach-field theorem and the pointwise form of the sharp approximation lemma), P0 (`P0/almost-basic-setup`, `P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`, `P0/almost-zero-serre-class`, `P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `P0/almost-algebras`, `P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `P0/almost-deformation-theory`). P1 does not depend on P2–P7 or on PerfectoidQuotients: the integral perfectoid rings of BMS1 are defined inline in P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison, and PerfectoidQuotients Q0 imports that comparison.

**Consumers served.** AdicSpacesPartII R5 (perfectoid frames with no base field; perfected Tate algebras over any perfectoid Tate ring — P1/perfected-tate-algebra; ℚ_p^cycl — P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), DiamondsAndVStacks D3/D4/D6 (tilting equivalence and its almost form, Perf, marked untilts and θ), PadicHodgeTheory R06.1/P7 (tilt of ℂ_p via PreTilt and Tilt, the generator of ker θ, base change of ξ), AdicEtaleGeometry A3/A4 (characteristic-p perfectoid rings, construction of perfectoid rings from ϖ with surjective Frobenius), RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 (untilts); within PerfectoidSpaces, P2 (the dense-image criterion: tilt of a uniform ring, strict inclusions, metric criterion; perfected Tate algebras in infinitely many variables), P3 (completed colimits and their untilts in the Krasner step and for finite étale algebras over completed colimits), P4 (sharp approximation for surjections of perfectoid rings) and P5 (perfectoidness of completed direct limits).

**Planets of this layer** (6): *Perfectoid Tate ring*, *Tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring*, *Perfectoid field*, *Fontaine's map θ*, *Untilts and primitive ideals*, *Tilting equivalence*.

### P1.1 Perfectoid Tate rings

The definition is ECD Definition 3.1 verbatim in content, over a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with no perfectoid base field. The criteria below show that the four formulations in the sources (ECD 3.1, Berkeley 6.1.1, Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.1, Kedlaya AWS 2.1.1) and BMS's integral notion agree, and they keep the condition ϖ^p | p visible: surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p alone does not make ℚ_p perfectoid. The metric criterion (`metric-perfectoid-criterion`, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3) recognises perfectoid rings among uniform Tate rings with a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots by approximating every element by p-th powers for the spectral gauge.

#### `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras` — Perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1), perfectoid algebras and perfectoid Tate pairs

*definition.* **Planet:** *Perfectoid Tate ring*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Fix a prime p. Let R be a commutative topological ring which is a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing), complete and Hausdorff, with power-bounded subring R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring). For a commutative ring A and ideals I, J ⊆ A with p ∈ J and x^p ∈ J for every x ∈ I, write Φ: A/I → A/J for the ring homomorphism x mod I ↦ x^p mod J (ECD §3 notational convention). R is a perfectoid Tate ring if (a) R is uniform, i.e. R° is a bounded subset of R (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded), and (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ of R (a topologically nilpotent unit, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer; necessarily ϖ ∈ R°) such that ϖ^p divides p in R° and Φ: R°/ϖR° → R°/ϖ^pR° is bijective. No perfectoid base field is fixed; characteristic 0 and characteristic p are both allowed (for pR = 0 the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous), and p may be a nonzero nonunit (e.g. in a product K × K♭). A perfectoid R-algebra is a perfectoid Tate ring S with a continuous ring homomorphism R → S; morphisms are continuous R-algebra homomorphisms. A perfectoid Tate pair is a Huber pair (R, R+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair) with R perfectoid; the condition depends only on R (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Completeness includes separatedness (anchor convention): CompleteSpace R and T2Space R, with the uniform structure of the topological additive group.
- Uniformity is boundedness of R° in R (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the uniformity of anchor Layer 4.2); it is not implied by (b) (test IsPerfectoidTateRing.not_of_not_uniform).
- The divisibility ϖ^p | p holds in R°, not merely in R; together with (b) it cannot be replaced by surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p alone (ℚ_p, ECD Remark 3.3).

*Proof outline.*
- Φ is well defined and additive: for i ∈ I, (x + i)^p − x^p ∈ (p, i^p) ⊆ J, and (x + y)^p − x^p − y^p ∈ pA ⊆ J by divisibility of the binomial coefficients.
- A pseudo-uniformizer ϖ lies in R°, and in every ring of integral elements R+ (ECD §3 preamble; tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).
- The listed equivalent formulations (Berkeley 6.1.1, Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.1, Kedlaya AWS 2.1.1, BMS1 "Fontaine's sense") agree by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer and P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.frobeniusQuot` (data): For a commutative ring A, ideals I, J with (p : A) ∈ J and ∀ x ∈ I, x^p ∈ J: the ring homomorphism A ⧸ I →+* A ⧸ J, [x] ↦ [x^p].
- `Perfectoid.frobeniusQuot_mk` (simp): frobeniusQuot I J hp hIJ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk J (x ^ p).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing` (structure): Prop-valued class on a commutative topological ring R with [UniformSpace R] [IsUniformAddGroup R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [NonarchimedeanRing R] [IsTateRing R] [CompleteSpace R] [T2Space R], with the two fields below.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` (projection): IsBounded (powerBoundedSubring R : Set R).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.exists_pseudoUniformizer` (projection): ∃ ϖ ∈ R°, IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ ∧ ϖ ^ p ∣ p in R° ∧ Function.Bijective (frobeniusQuot (span {ϖ}) (span {ϖ ^ p}) _ _).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_surjective` (constructor): A complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, ϖ^p | p in R°, for which Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective, is perfectoid (injectivity is automatic, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.frobenius_bijective` (characterisation): If R is perfectoid, Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_frobenius_surjective_modP` (characterisation): A complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff it has a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isReduced` (other): A perfectoid Tate ring is reduced (P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.iff_perfectRing` (characterisation): If CharP R p: R is perfectoid iff PerfectRing R p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.of_ringEquiv` (functoriality): The class transports along a ring isomorphism that is a homeomorphism (via tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.map_powerBoundedSubring).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod` (instance): R × S is perfectoid when R and S are: (R × S)° = R° × S° and (ϖ_R, ϖ_S) is a pseudo-uniformizer with the required properties.
- `Perfectoid.map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (other): For a Tate ring A, a uniform Tate ring S and a continuous ring homomorphism f: A → S, f(A°) ⊆ S°: for x ∈ A° and ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of A, f(ϖ)f(x)^N is topologically nilpotent for all N, so {f(x)^N} ⊆ f(ϖ)^{-1}S°, which is bounded.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.frobenius_surjective_plus` (other): For every ring of integral elements R+, Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.isUniform` (compatibility): Condition (a) is the uniformity predicate of anchor Layer 4.2 (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3); the two propositions are equal.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidPair` (structure): For a Huber pair P = (R, R+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair), the proposition IsPerfectoidTateRing R; perfectoid pairs with Huber-pair morphisms form the category of the untilt classification.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_padic` (non-example): ¬ IsPerfectoidTateRing ℚ_[p]: a pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p has |ϖ| = p^{-k} with k ≥ 1, so |ϖ^p| < |p| and ϖ^p ∤ p in ℤ_p, although Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidTateRing.not_of_not_uniform` (non-example): R = ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) (product topology on ℂ_p ⊕ ℂ_pε) is a complete Tate ring with ϖ = p^{1/p}, ϖ^p = p, and Frobenius surjective on R°/p = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}/p (as ℂ_pε ⊆ R° and ℂ_pε = p·ℂ_pε), but R° ⊇ ℂ_pε is unbounded, so R is not perfectoid; a definition omitting uniformity would accept it.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_zero` (degenerate): The zero ring is a perfectoid Tate ring (0 is a topologically nilpotent unit and all quotients vanish).
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_padicComplex` (computation): For ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p) with ϖ = p^{1/p}: ϖ^p = p and Φ: 𝒪/ϖ → 𝒪/p is bijective because every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_iff_perfect_laurent` (characterisation): For the t-adic completion R of the perfection of F_p((t)): IsPerfectoidTateRing R ↔ PerfectRing R p, and both hold; for F_p((t)) itself (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing) both fail.

*Uses.*
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-ring: a perfectoid frame (R̃, ι, σ) takes R̃ perfectoid in exactly this sense, with no base field and characteristic p allowed.
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-uniform: uses that R̃° is bounded (isBounded_powerBoundedSubring) and that R̃ is reduced.
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc: proves S⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid by non-surjectivity of Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/split-tate-ring-is-perfectoid, A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion: build perfectoid rings from ϖ with ϖ^p | p and surjective Φ, injectivity being automatic (of_surjective).
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product: C^0(G^k, Â∞) is perfectoid: products and continuous maps with a common ϖ.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field, A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p: in characteristic p a perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid (iff_perfectRing).
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond, D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond: Perf is built on perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p; perfectoidness of a completed tower is checked via ϖ^p | p and surjective Frobenius on the integral quotient.
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras: perfectoid affinoid algebras over a perfectoid field are perfectoid Tate rings.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel, P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids: the tilt, θ and rational localisation are stated for this class.
- ECD Definition 3.1; Berkeley Definition 6.1.1; Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.3.1; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.1.1: the four formulations in the sources, identified by the criteria of this layer.

*Acceptance.*
- ℚ_p^cycl (ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1), the completed perfection of F_p((t)) (ϖ = t), ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and the non-field ring ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ECD Example 3.4) are perfectoid Tate rings (P1/perfectoid-examples).
- ℚ_p is a complete uniform Tate ring whose Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective, and it is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
