#### `integral-elements-adically-complete` — Rings of integral elements of a complete uniform Tate ring are ϖ-adically and p-adically complete

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements; R+ = R° allowed) and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then (a) the subspace topology of R+ is the ϖ-adic topology and R+ is ϖ-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {ϖ}) R+); (b) ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R+ and R = R+[1/ϖ]; (c) if ϖ divides p in R+, then R+ is p-adically complete and separated (IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+); (d) if R ≠ 0 and p is topologically nilpotent in R, then p is not a unit of R+. In particular, for R ≠ 0 perfectoid, R+ satisfies the hypotheses [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+)] and [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+] of Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt and WittVector.fontaineTheta.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R complete and Hausdorff; uniformity is used to know that R+ ⊆ R° is bounded.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) R+ is open, hence closed, hence complete; it is bounded, so by tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero (for any pair of definition (A_0, I)) the open sets ϖ^nR+ are cofinal among the neighbourhoods ϖ^nA_0 of 0; completeness plus Hausdorffness give IsAdicComplete.
- (b) ϖ is a unit of R; for x ∈ R, ϖ^nx → 0, so ϖ^nx ∈ R+ for n large because R+ is open.
- (c) (p) ⊆ (ϖ) are finitely generated ideals of R+, so ϖ-adic completeness implies p-adic completeness (Stacks Tag 090T; the same step in BMS1 §3.1).
- (d) If p were a unit of R+, then p^{-n} ∈ R+ (bounded) and p^n → 0 would give 1 = p^{-n}p^n → 0, so 1 lies in the closure of 0 and R = 0.

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K° (or an open valuation subring K+) this is the ϖ-adic and p-adic completeness of K+ used in Sch12 Lemma 3.4.
- For R = ℚ_p and R+ = ℤ_p with ϖ = p: ℤ_p is p-adically complete (the lemma needs no perfectoid hypothesis).

*Depends on:* `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:IsTopologicallyNilpotent`, `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`.

*Sources:* Stacks-Project, Stacks Project, Tag 090T (Lemma 10.96.8); BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 §3.1, before Definition 3.1, p. 19.

#### `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion` — Frobenius-surjectivity criterion with the pseudo-uniformizer condition kept

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ R° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in R°. The following are equivalent: (i) Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective (every element of R°/ϖ^p is a p-th power); (ii) Frobenius on R°/p is surjective; (iii) every element of R°/ϖpR° is a p-th power. The same equivalences hold for any ring of integral elements R+ in place of R° when ϖ ∈ R+ and ϖ^p | p in R+. The divisibility hypothesis is essential: surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p without any ϖ with ϖ^p | p does not give perfectoidness (ℚ_p), and surjectivity of the Frobenius endomorphism of R°/ϖ is weaker than (i) (ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p}, Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- ϖ^p | p in R° is a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
- R° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).

*Proof outline.*
- (iii) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (i): ϖpR° ⊆ pR° ⊆ ϖ^pR°, so surjectivity passes to coarser quotients.
- (i) ⇒ (iii): by successive ϖ^p-adic approximation using (i), every x ∈ R° is a convergent sum x = x_0^p + ϖ^px_1^p + ϖ^{2p}x_2^p + ⋯ with x_i ∈ R° (R° is ϖ-adically complete); then x ≡ (x_0 + ϖx_1 + ϖ²x_2 + ⋯)^p modulo pϖR°, since every mixed term of the p-th power is divisible by p and by ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.9 (iii) ⇒ (i)).
- For R+ the same argument applies to the ϖ-adically complete ring R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).

*Acceptance.*
- ℚ_p: Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is surjective, but no pseudo-uniformizer ϖ has ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p, so the criterion does not apply and ℚ_p is not perfectoid.
- ℤ_p[p^{1/p}] with ϖ = p^{1/p} (ϖ^p = p): Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/ϖ = F_p is surjective, but Frobenius on ℤ_p[p^{1/p}]/p = F_p[ϖ]/(ϖ^p) is not (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.4.9).

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Remark 3.2, p. 14; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.9, p. 22; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.9 (i)–(iii), p. 22; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Remark 6.1.3, p. 42; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Remark 3.4.9, p. 81; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.1.5, p. 50.

#### `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer` — Injectivity of Frobenius is automatic and the perfectoid condition is independent of the pseudo-uniformizer

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. (a) For every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R°, Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is injective. (b) If R is moreover uniform, then for pseudo-uniformizers ϖ, ϖ' with ϖ^p | p and ϖ'^p | p in R°, Φ is bijective for ϖ iff it is bijective for ϖ'; equivalently R is perfectoid iff there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius on R°/p is surjective, and then Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective for every such ϖ (ECD Remark 3.2; Berkeley Remark 6.1.3). (c) The same holds for a ring of integral elements R+ in place of R°: if ϖ ∈ R+, ϖ^p | p in R+ and x ∈ R+ with x^p ∈ ϖ^pR+, then x ∈ ϖR+.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- (a) and (c) use only that R° (resp. R+) is integrally closed in R and ϖ is a unit of R; (b) uses uniformity and completeness through P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) If x ∈ R° and x^p = ϖ^py with y ∈ R°, then (x/ϖ)^p = y, so x/ϖ ∈ R is integral over R° and lies in R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral), i.e. x ∈ ϖR° (ECD Remark 3.2; BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof).
- (c) Same argument with the integrally closed R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
- (b) By (a), bijectivity of Φ for ϖ is its surjectivity, which by P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion is equivalent to surjectivity of Frobenius on R°/p, a condition independent of ϖ.

*Acceptance.*
- In ℚ_p^cycl, ϖ = ζ_{p²} − 1 and ϖ' = ζ_{p³} − 1 both satisfy ϖ^p | p, and Φ is bijective for both.
- In ℂ_p the conditions for ϖ = p^{1/p} and ϖ' = p^{1/p²} coincide.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isIntegrallyClosedIn_powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Remark 3.2, p. 14; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Remark 3.2, p. 14; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 26; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 5.5, proof, p. 23.

#### `frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring` — Every ring of integral elements of a perfectoid Tate ring satisfies the Frobenius condition

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and R+ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then (a) Frobenius on R+/p is surjective, and every element of R+/ϖpR+ is a p-th power for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+; (b) there is a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+ and p/ϖ^p ∈ R°° (topologically nilpotent), and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p in R+, Φ: R+/ϖ → R+/ϖ^p is bijective; (c) consequently (R, R+) satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 with R+ in place of R°, which is the formulation of Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.1.1 and Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.3.1, and these definitions agree with ECD's: the perfectoid condition on a Huber pair (R, R+) depends on R alone.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid; R+ open and integrally closed, so R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).

*Proof outline.*
- (b) existence: take ϖ_0 with compatible p-power roots and ϖ_0^p | p in R° (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), write p = ϖ_0^pu with u ∈ R°, and set ϖ := ϖ_0^{1 − 1/p²}; then p = ϖ^p·ϖ_0^{1/p}u with ϖ_0^{1/p}u ∈ R°° ⊆ R+.
- (a) (BMS1 Lemma 3.20 proof) For x ∈ R+ write x = y^p + pϖz with y, z ∈ R° (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (iii) for R°); ϖz ∈ R°° ⊆ R+, so y^p = x − pϖz ∈ R+ and y ∈ R+ by integral closedness; hence x ≡ y^p mod pR+. Surjectivity modulo ϖpR+ then follows from P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion applied to R+.
- (b) bijectivity: surjectivity from (a) since pR+ ⊆ ϖ^pR+; injectivity from P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (c).
- (c) is (b) together with P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion; conversely a Huber pair satisfying the R+-condition has R perfectoid by BMS1 Lemma 3.20 (P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison) or Kedlaya–Liu II Proposition 3.3.3.

*Acceptance.*
- For K a perfectoid field and K+ ⊆ K° an open valuation subring of rank 2, Frobenius on K+/p is surjective.
- Mathlib's surjective_fontaineTheta applies to R+ with hypothesis Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R+ p) p) supplied by (a) (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`.

*Sources:* BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 27; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.12, p. 55; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Proposition 3.3.3, p. 58; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Corollary 2.3.10, p. 55.

#### `perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced` — Uniform (in particular perfectoid) Tate rings are reduced

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

A Hausdorff uniform Tate ring R is reduced; in particular every perfectoid Tate ring is reduced (Sch12 Proposition 5.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6 proof).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Uniformity is essential: ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is a complete Tate ring that is not reduced.

*Proof outline.*
- If x ∈ R is nilpotent, then λx is nilpotent, hence power-bounded, for every λ ∈ R; for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ this gives ϖ^{-n}x ∈ R° for all n, i.e. x ∈ ⋂_n ϖ^nR°.
- R° is ϖ-adically separated (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), so x = 0.

*Acceptance.*
- ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is not reduced, hence not uniform, hence not perfectoid, although ϖ = p^{1/p} satisfies ϖ^p | p and Frobenius on its power-bounded subring modulo p is surjective.
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-uniform deduces that sousperfectoid rings are reduced from this lemma applied to a perfectoid frame.

*Depends on:* `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `mathlib:IsReduced`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 5.8, proof, pp. 23–24; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 6.1.6, proof, p. 43.

#### `perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform` — A perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p is uniform (open mapping theorem)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CharP`.

Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pR = 0 which is perfect (PerfectRing R p: Frobenius R → R bijective). Then R° is bounded, i.e. R is uniform.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R complete, Hausdorff and Tate; no uniformity is assumed.

*Proof outline.*
- Φ: R → R is a continuous bijective ring homomorphism. Make the target an R-module through Φ (a·y := a^py); then Φ is R-linear, surjective and continuous, both sides are complete, first countable (a Huber ring has a countable neighbourhood basis of 0) and nonarchimedean, the target is Hausdorff and scalar multiplication on it is continuous, so Φ is open by the open mapping theorem over a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap; ECD Proposition 3.5 proof; Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.0.3 phrases the same step with two norms).
- Choose a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R_0 for a ring of definition R_0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero). Openness gives n ≥ 1 with ϖ^nR_0 ⊆ Φ(R_0); since Φ(ϖ^jR_0) = ϖ^{pj}Φ(R_0), this yields Φ^{-1}(ϖ^mR_0) ⊆ ϖ^{⌊(m−n)/p⌋}R_0 for every integer m.
- If y is topologically nilpotent then y^{p^k} ∈ R_0 for some k; applying Φ^{-1} k times and the previous inclusion gives y ∈ ϖ^{-c}R_0 with c = ⌈(n + p)/(p − 1)⌉, independent of y (if m ≥ −c then ⌊(m − n)/p⌋ ≥ −c). For x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so R° ⊆ ϖ^{-c-1}R_0 is bounded. (This integral-exponent estimate replaces the chain Φ^{-k}(R_0) ⊆ ϖ^{-n/p-⋯-n/p^k}R_0 ⊆ ϖ^{-n}R_0 of ECD and Berkeley, whose last inclusion needs ϖ^{q}R_0 ⊆ R_0 for fractional q; see sourceIssues.)

*Acceptance.*
- The t-adic completion of the perfection of F_p((t)) is uniform with R° the completion of F_p[[t]]^{perf} (ECD Example 3.4(ii)).
- A non-uniform complete Tate ring of characteristic p, such as F_p((t))[ε]/(ε²), is not perfect (ε is nilpotent, and Frobenius is not injective), consistently with the lemma.

*Depends on:* `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.exists_hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.5, proof, p. 15; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 6.1.6, proof, p. 43; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 3.0.3, p. 54; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Example 2.1.2, p. 49.

#### `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect` — In characteristic p, perfectoid Tate rings are exactly the perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CharP`.

Let R be a topological ring with pR = 0. Then R is a perfectoid Tate ring iff R is a perfect complete Hausdorff Tate ring. For such R, R° and every ring of integral elements R+ are perfect, Φ: R° → R° is an automorphism, and every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ satisfies the condition of ECD Definition 3.1 (ϖ^p | p = 0 is vacuous).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- pR = 0; completeness includes Hausdorffness.

*Proof outline.*
- (⇐) R is uniform (P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform). x is power-bounded iff x^p is, so Φ restricts to an automorphism of R°; hence Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective, and it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a).
- (⇒) If Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism, so is R°/ϖ^n → R°/ϖ^{np} for all n by induction; passing to the limit with R° ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete) gives Φ: R° ≅ R°, and inverting ϖ shows R is perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5 proof).
- R+ is perfect: if x^p ∈ R+ then x is integral over R+, so x ∈ R+ (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.2).

*Acceptance.*
- The completed perfection of F_p((t)) is a perfectoid field; F_p((t)) is a complete Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing) that is not perfect, hence not perfectoid.
- A nonarchimedean field of characteristic p is a perfectoid field iff it is perfect (Sch12 §3; Bhatt Example 3.1.2(3)).

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform`, `perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`, `mathlib:CharP`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.LaurentSeries.isTateRing`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.5, p. 15; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.5, proof, p. 15; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 3.3.4, p. 59; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Example 2.1.2, p. 49; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 5.9, p. 24; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Example 3.1.2(3), p. 10.

#### `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots` — Pseudo-uniformizers with compatible p-power roots and the spectral gauge

*definition.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. A pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots is an element ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_{n≥0} of the multiplicative monoid lim_{x↦x^p} R (Mathlib Perfection R p) such that ϖ := ϖ^{1/p^0} is a pseudo-uniformizer of R lying in R° with ϖ^p | p in R°. Then every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer in R°, ϖ^q := (ϖ^{1/p^n})^m is well defined for q = m/p^n ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0} (and for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] as a unit of R), and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of the tilt R♭ with (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Attached to ϖ♭ is the spectral gauge |x|_ϖ := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ R°}: a power-multiplicative, submultiplicative, ultrametric norm defining the topology of R, with |ϖ^qx|_ϖ = 2^{-q}|x|_ϖ, R° = {x : |x|_ϖ ≤ 1} and R°° = {x : |x|_ϖ < 1}. Existence is P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid; the normalisation |ϖ|_ϖ = 1/2 is a convention, and changing ϖ changes |·|_ϖ by a power.

*Proof outline.*
- ϖ^{1/p^n} is a unit because its p^n-th power is, topologically nilpotent because its p^n-th power is, and power-bounded because R° is integrally closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).
- Gauge: |x|_ϖ is finite since R = R°[1/ϖ]; submultiplicative and ultrametric since R° is a ring; power-multiplicativity |x^n|_ϖ = |x|_ϖ^n: if x^n ∈ ϖ^{q'}R° and q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with nq ≤ q' then (x/ϖ^q)^n ∈ R°, so x/ϖ^q ∈ R° by integral closedness, and ℤ[1/p] is dense in ℚ.
- Topology: the balls {|x|_ϖ ≤ 2^{-q}} = ϖ^qR° form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); R°° = ⋃_q ϖ^qR° is P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots` (structure): Structure on a perfectoid Tate ring R with a field roots : Perfection R p and proofs that coeff 0 roots ∈ R°, IsPseudoUniformizer (coeff 0 roots) and (coeff 0 roots)^p ∣ p in R°.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.root` (data): root n := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n ϖ♭ = ϖ^{1/p^n}.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.root_pow` (simp): (root (n + 1)) ^ p = root n; root 0 = ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.isPseudoUniformizer_root` (characterisation): Each root n is a pseudo-uniformizer lying in R°.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.zpow` (data): ϖ^q for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] as a unit of R, with zpow_add and zpow_natCast; ϖ^q ∈ R° for q ≥ 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.exists` (constructor): Every perfectoid Tate ring admits one, starting from any ϖ_1 with ϖ_1^p | p (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.toTilt` (projection): ϖ♭ regarded as an element of the ring tilt R; a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭ with sharp ϖ♭ = ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge` (data): |x|_ϖ = inf {2^{-q} | q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q} x ∈ R°} ∈ ℝ≥0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_mul_le` (structure): |xy|_ϖ ≤ |x|_ϖ |y|_ϖ and |x + y|_ϖ ≤ max |x|_ϖ |y|_ϖ; |x|_ϖ = 0 iff x = 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_pow` (characterisation): |x^n|_ϖ = |x|_ϖ^n (power-multiplicativity).
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_zpow_mul` (simp): |ϖ^q x|_ϖ = 2^{-q} |x|_ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_gauge_le_one` (characterisation): x ∈ R° ↔ |x|_ϖ ≤ 1, and IsTopologicallyNilpotent x ↔ |x|_ϖ < 1.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.hasBasis_nhds_zero` (other): The sets ϖ^q R°, q ∈ ℤ[1/p], form a neighbourhood basis of 0 (the gauge defines the topology).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.gauge_padicComplex` (computation): For ℂ_p and ϖ♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n: gauge x = 2^{-v_p(x)} for x ≠ 0.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.isEmpty_padic` (non-example): IsEmpty (PseudoUniformizerRoots ℚ_[p]): a pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p has valuation k ≥ 1, which is not divisible by every p^n, so it has no compatible system of p-power roots; and none satisfies ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.subsingleton_of_charP` (degenerate): If CharP R p then for a fixed pseudo-uniformizer ϖ the compatible system of roots is unique (R is perfect), so PseudoUniformizerRoots over ϖ is a subsingleton.
- `Perfectoid.PseudoUniformizerRoots.iUnion_zpow_eq` (characterisation): ⋃_{q > 0} ϖ^q R° = R°° (the topologically nilpotent elements), P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring: R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] and the ring structure on the tilt.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup: the almost setup m = ⋃ ϖ^{1/p^n} R°.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel: ϖ♭ with (ϖ♭♯)^p | p gives the generator p + [ϖ♭]α of ker θ.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field, P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp: the spectral gauge compares R and R♭.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: estimates with ϖ^{1/p^n} and the spectral norm (Sch12 Lemma 6.5).
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field: t^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n} defines F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ → R.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: "after replacing ϖ by a p-power root".
- Sch12 Remark 3.5; ECD Lemma 3.10: the standing convention ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ with compatible roots.

*Acceptance.*
- In ℂ_p, (p^{1/p^n})_n with a compatible choice of roots is such an element and |x|_ϖ = 2^{-v_p(x)} (normalised valuation v_p(p) = 1).
- ℚ_p admits none: no pseudo-uniformizer of ℚ_p satisfies ϖ^p | p in ℤ_p.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:Perfection`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, p. 16; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Remark 3.5, p. 16; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44.

#### `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots` — Every perfectoid Tate ring has a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (ECD Lemma 3.10)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Basic`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ_1 a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ_1^p | p in R°. There is ϖ♭ ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R° with ϖ := ϖ♭^{(0)} ≡ ϖ_1 mod ϖ_1^pR°; then ϖ = ϖ_1·u with u ∈ (R°)^×, ϖR° = ϖ_1R°, ϖ^p | p in R°, and ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible p-power roots (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). If pR = 0 every pseudo-uniformizer has unique compatible roots.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid; the zero ring is allowed (then everything is 0).

*Proof outline.*
- Put ϖ_0 := ϖ_1^p, which divides p. Frobenius on R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i)), so the zeroth projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 → R°/ϖ_0 is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective); by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius choose ϖ♭ ∈ lim R° whose image in R°/ϖ_0 is ϖ_1 (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof).
- Then ϖ = ϖ_1 + ϖ_1^py = ϖ_1(1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y) with y ∈ R°, and 1 + ϖ_1^{p−1}y is a unit of the ϖ_1-adically complete ring R° (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete).
- All components ϖ^{1/p^n} are units and topologically nilpotent because their p^n-th power ϖ is.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℂ_p and ϖ_1 = p^{1/p}, the construction returns a unit multiple of p^{1/p} with compatible roots.
- For R of characteristic p, ϖ = ϖ_1 and ϖ^{1/p^n} = Φ^{-n}(ϖ_1).

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, p. 16; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, proof, p. 44; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.9, p. 22.

#### `metric-perfectoid-criterion` — Metric criterion: a uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff every element is a p-th power up to a fixed factor c < 1 (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c))

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/MetricCriterion`.

Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ ∈ B° a pseudo-uniformizer with ϖ^p | p in B° admitting a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ B° ((ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}, ϖ^{1/p^0} = ϖ). Let |x| := inf{2^{-q} : q ∈ ℤ[1/p], ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B°} be the spectral gauge of ϖ (the formula of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, here on a ring not assumed perfectoid). Then (a) |·| is an ultrametric, submultiplicative, power-multiplicative norm defining the topology of B, with |ϖ^q x| = 2^{-q}|x| and B° = {x : |x| ≤ 1}; (b) B is a perfectoid Tate ring if and only if there is c ∈ (0, 1) such that for every x ∈ B there is y ∈ B with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|; (c) if B is perfectoid, every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) = (|ϖ|^p, 1) has this property, and y can be taken in B° when x ∈ B°. Kedlaya states the criterion for a uniform analytic Huber pair (A, A⁺) with an ideal of definition I, p ∈ I^p, and the norm attached to I; this node is its Tate-ring form with the gauge of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, which every perfectoid Tate ring has (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots) and which every Tate ring receiving a continuous map from a perfectoid Tate ring has (the image of such a ϖ). Power-multiplicativity of the norm is used: the criterion is a statement about the spectral gauge.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- B complete, Hausdorff and uniform (B° bounded); ϖ^p | p in B° and the roots ϖ^{1/p^n} lie in B.
- No perfectoid base field; B may have characteristic 0, p, or neither (then |p| may be 0 on some factors).

*Proof outline.*
- (a) Ultrametricity and submultiplicativity are inherited from B° being an additive subgroup and a subring. Power-multiplicativity: if ϖ^{-nq}x^n ∈ B° then (ϖ^{-q}x)^n ∈ B°, so ϖ^{-q}x is integral over B° and lies in B° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral); rounding exponents in ℤ[1/p] gives |x^n| = |x|^n. If |x| ≤ 1 then ϖ^{1/p^k}x ∈ B° for all k, hence x^n ∈ ϖ^{-1}B° for all n, a bounded set by uniformity, so x ∈ B°. |x| = 0 forces x ∈ ⋂_q ϖ^qB° = 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); the sets ϖ^qB° are a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero).
- (c), hence ⇒ of (b): if B is perfectoid, Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion). Given c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) and x ≠ 0, choose q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with u := ϖ^{-q}x ∈ B° and 2^{-q} ≤ 2^p c|x|, choose w ∈ B° with u − w^p ∈ ϖ^pB° and put y := ϖ^{q/p}w; then |x − y^p| = 2^{-q}|u − w^p| ≤ 2^{-q-p} ≤ c|x| (Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c), second paragraph).
- ⇐ of (b): given c and u ∈ B°, put u_0 := u and choose inductively y_k with |u_k − y_k^p| ≤ c|u_k|, u_{k+1} := u_k − y_k^p. Then |y_k^p| ≤ |u_k| ≤ c^k, so y_k ∈ B° by (a). For c^k ≤ 2^{-p}, u − (y_0 + ⋯ + y_{k−1})^p = u_k − (mixed binomial terms), and the mixed terms lie in pB° ⊆ ϖ^pB°; as {|x| ≤ 2^{-p}} = ϖ^pB° by (a), u is a p-th power modulo ϖ^pB°. So Φ: B°/ϖ → B°/ϖ^p is surjective, it is injective by P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a), and B is perfectoid by P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras.
- Kedlaya AWS proves ⇐ through Lemma 2.8.2, whose hypothesis is that the pair is already perfectoid (recorded in sourceIssues); the successive approximation above replaces it.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: perfectoidness of a uniform ring receiving an isometric dense-image map from a perfectoid ring (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4).
- Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.8.3–2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c), Theorem 3.6.17(b): the metric form of the perfectoid condition in the sources.

*Acceptance.*
- B = ℂ_p with ϖ = p^{1/p} (so |p| = 2^{-p}): every c ∈ (2^{-p}, 1) works, matching "any c ∈ (p^{-1}, 1)" of Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c) for the normalisation |p| = p^{-1}.
- Non-example: for a perfectoid field K, B = K⟨T⟩ (Gauss norm, uniform, ϖ ∈ K with roots) fails the criterion at x = T: the reduction of y^p in (K°/K°°)[T] is a p-th power, so |T − y^p| ≥ 1 = |T| for every y; B is not perfectoid.
- P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: the criterion passes along isometric continuous maps with dense image, since |x − x′| < |x| implies |x′| = |x|.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`.

#### `perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid` — An integral perfectoid ring with a nonzerodivisor π gives a perfectoid Tate ring R_0[1/π] (BMS1 Lemma 3.21)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Integral`.

Let R_0 be π-adically complete and π-torsion free for some π with π^p | p, with Frobenius surjective on R_0/p and Φ: R_0/π → R_0/π^p bijective (equivalently R_0 is integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5, with π a nonzerodivisor: BMS1 Lemma 3.10). Then R := R_0[1/π], with R_0 open and π-adic, is a complete Hausdorff perfectoid Tate ring; after replacing π by a unit multiple with compatible p-power roots π^{1/p^n} ∈ R_0 (BMS1 Lemma 3.9), R° = {x ∈ R : π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0 for all n} (the almost elements of R_0), R_0 ⊆ R° and πR° ⊆ R_0; R°/R_0 is killed by every π^{1/p^n}.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- π a nonzerodivisor; π^p | p in R_0.

*Proof outline.*
- Roots: BMS1 Lemma 3.9 gives a unit u with uπ admitting compatible p-power roots in R_0; replace π.
- Topology: (R_0, πR_0) is a pair of definition; R is complete Hausdorff and Tate with pseudo-uniformizer π.
- Let R_0* := {x ∈ R : π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0 ∀n}. Φ: R_0*/π^{1/p} → R_0*/π is injective, and x ∈ R, x^p ∈ R_0* ⇒ x ∈ R_0* by descending induction on k with π^{k/p}x ∈ R_0* (Sch12 Lemma 5.7).
- R° = R_0*: R_0* ⊆ π^{-1}R_0 is bounded; if x is power-bounded then π^{1/p^n}x is topologically nilpotent, so (π^{1/p^n}x)^{p^N} ∈ R_0 for large N, hence π^{1/p^n}x ∈ R_0* by p-root closedness, for all n, so x ∈ R_0* (Sch12 Lemma 5.6).
- R is uniform, π^p | p in R°, and Frobenius on R°/π is surjective (almost surjectivity from R_0 plus the Sch12 Lemma 5.6 argument with z = y/π^{1/p²}); so R is perfectoid (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer).

*Acceptance.*
- R_0 = ℤ_p^cycl, π = ζ_{p²} − 1: R = ℚ_p^cycl and R° = R_0.
- R_0 = the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}]: R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with R° = R_0 (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

*Sources:* BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.21, p. 27; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.21, p. 27; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.21, proof, p. 27; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.9, p. 22; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.6, p. 23; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.7, p. 23.

#### `integral-perfectoid-comparison` — R perfectoid Tate ⇔ R+ integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.20)

*comparison.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Integral`.

(BMS1 Lemma 3.20) Let R be a complete Hausdorff Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements. If R is a perfectoid Tate ring, then R+ (and R°) is an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5 (π-adically complete for some π with π^p dividing p up to a unit, Frobenius surjective on R₀/p, and the kernel of θ : A_inf(R₀) → R₀ principal). Conversely, if R+ is integral perfectoid and bounded in R, then R is a perfectoid Tate ring. Together with P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.21) this is the comparison between the integral notion of BMS1 Definition 3.5, on which PerfectoidQuotients Q0 builds, and the Tate-ring notion of this layer; the Q0 node records it as unproved in its own sources and imports it from here.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R Tate; boundedness of R+ is needed for the converse (a non-bounded R+ cannot occur inside a uniform R).

*Proof outline.*
- (⇒) R+ is ϖ-adically complete for ϖ ∈ R+ with ϖ^p | p (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete, P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (a)); ker θ is principal (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel, or BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii) from bijectivity of Φ: R+/ϖ → R+/ϖ^p and ϖ a nonzerodivisor).
- (⇐) ϖR° ⊆ R+ for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, so R° is bounded; a pseudo-uniformizer π with π^p | p in R° exists by the BMS1 argument (a unit multiple of a pseudo-uniformizer is θ([π♭]), and a high p-power root works); then Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (write πx = y^p + pπz with y, z ∈ R+ and y/π^{1/p} ∈ R°).

*Acceptance.*
- ℤ_p^cycl, 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}] are integral perfectoid (BMS1 Example 3.6), and ℚ_p^cycl, ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ are perfectoid Tate rings.
- Perfect F_p-algebras are integral perfectoid with π = 0, but with the discrete topology they are not Tate: the comparison needs R Tate.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring`, `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`, `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`.

*Sources:* BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.20, p. 26; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 §3.2, before Lemma 3.20, p. 26; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Definition 3.5, p. 21; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii), p. 22; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.20, proof, p. 27.

### P1.2 The tilt and the sharp map

The tilt is the monoid lim_{x↦x^p} R (Mathlib's `Perfection R p`) with the limiting addition. Its ring structure is transported from lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0, which Mathlib's `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` identifies with lim_{x↦x^p} R° multiplicatively; Mathlib's `PreTilt R+ p` is the integral tilt R♭+ and `PreTilt.untilt` is ♯ on it. The sharp map is continuous and multiplicative and is never asserted to be additive. The same limit construction applies to every complete uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (`tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring`, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1); it is Tate, hence perfectoid of characteristic p, as soon as the ring receives a map from a perfectoid Tate ring, which is how the dense-image criterion of P2 uses it.

#### `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius` — lim_{x↦x^p} R+ ≅ lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 ≅ lim_Φ R+/p (ECD Lemma 3.10, first part)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

Let R be a nonzero complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring, R+ a ring of integral elements and ϖ_0 ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer dividing p in R+. Then projection (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (x^{(n)} mod ϖ_0)_n is a multiplicative bijection lim_{x↦x^p} R+ → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0R+, and a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (R+ with its topology, R+/ϖ_0 discrete); the inverse sends (x̄_0, x̄_1, …) to (x^{(i)})_i with x^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞} x_{n+i}^{p^n} for arbitrary lifts x_j ∈ R+ of x̄_j. The same holds for p in place of ϖ_0, and the ring homomorphism lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 induced by the quotient map is an isomorphism. In Mathlib terms: Perfection.quotientMulEquiv p (span {ϖ_0}) : Perfection R+ p ≃* Perfection (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p, and Perfection (ModP R+ p) p is PreTilt R+ p.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R ≠ 0, so ϖ_0 and p are not units of R+ and R+/ϖ_0 has characteristic p (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (d)).

*Proof outline.*
- R+ is ϖ_0-adically and p-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a), (c)), and CharP (R+ ⧸ span {ϖ_0}) p holds; Mathlib's Perfection.quotientMulEquiv applies to I = ϖ_0R+ and to I = pR+. Its inverse is built from Perfection.teichmuller, i.e. the limit x^{(i)} = lim_n x_{n+i}^{p^n}, which converges because x ≡ y mod ϖ_0^n implies x^p ≡ y^p mod ϖ_0^{n+1} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof; Perfection.teichmuller_spec).
- Continuity of the inverse: x^{(i)} mod ϖ_0^{n+1} depends only on x̄_{i+n} (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
- The map lim_Φ R+/p → lim_Φ R+/ϖ_0 is a ring homomorphism compatible with the two multiplicative bijections from lim R+, hence bijective (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i)).

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K and R+ = K°, this is Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i).
- For R of characteristic p (so R+ perfect), projection to the zeroth factor identifies lim_{x↦x^p} R+ with R+.

*Depends on:* `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:Perfection`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:Perfection.teichmuller`, `mathlib:Perfection.teichmuller_spec`, `mathlib:PreTilt`, `mathlib:ModP`, `mathlib:Perfection.map`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 16; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Remark 3.4.10, p. 82; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i), proof, p. 16.

#### `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring` — The tilt R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.9, Lemma 3.10)

*construction.* **Planet:** *Tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Its tilt is R♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} R, the multiplicative monoid Perfection R p of compatible sequences (x^{(n)})_{n≥0} with (x^{(n+1)})^p = x^{(n)}, with the inverse-limit topology (induced from ∏_ℕ R), pointwise multiplication and addition (x + y)^{(i)} = lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. The limit exists and R♭ is a topological ring of characteristic p which is perfect (ECD Lemma 3.10; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1). Concretely, for ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ_0 | p, the submonoid lim_{x↦x^p} R° is identified with the ring lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius), R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭] as monoids, and the ring structure of R♭ is that of this localisation; it is given by the limit formula and does not depend on ϖ_0 or ϖ♭. For a Huber pair (R, R+) with R perfectoid, the tilt pair is (R♭, R♭+) with R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting). If pR = 0 then x ↦ x^{(0)} is an isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid; the construction of the ring structure uses ϖ_0 | p and completeness of R°.
- Additivity of the zeroth projection is not asserted (P1/sharp-map).

*Proof outline.*
- Ring structure on lim R°: transport along the multiplicative bijection with lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); the resulting sum has i-th component lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} because at level i + n both reduce to x̄_{i+n} + ȳ_{i+n} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec characterises the limit), and this formula shows independence of ϖ_0.
- R♭ = (lim R°)[1/ϖ♭]: for x ∈ lim R, ϖ^Nx^{(0)} ∈ R° for some N; then (ϖ^{N/p^n}x^{(n)})^{p^n} ∈ R° and, R° being integrally closed, ϖ♭^N x ∈ lim R° (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof, "R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] as multiplicative monoids, and in fact as rings").
- Characteristic p and perfectness: p·1 = 0 in lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 since ϖ_0 | p; Frobenius is (x^{(n)}) ↦ ((x^{(n)})^p), with inverse the shift (x^{(n)}) ↦ (x^{(n+1)}).
- Topology: the inverse-limit topology on lim R° equals that of lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 with discrete factors (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius); it is a ring topology (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)).
- Characteristic p: R is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), so projection to the zeroth factor is bijective, and the limit formula is constant, hence the projection is additive.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt` (data): tilt R := Perfection R p (type synonym) carrying the ring structure above; notation R♭.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.instCommRing` (instance): CommRing (tilt R), with the monoid structure of Perfection R p; together with instTopologicalSpace (induced from ℕ → R) and instIsTopologicalRing.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.charP` (instance): CharP (tilt R) p and PerfectRing (tilt R) p.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff` (projection): coeff n : tilt R →* R, the n-th coordinate (Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p n); coeff_pow: coeff (n + 1) x ^ p = coeff n x.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.ext` (extensionality): x = y ↔ ∀ n, coeff n x = coeff n y.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_add` (characterisation): Tendsto (fun m ↦ (coeff (i + m) x + coeff (i + m) y) ^ p ^ m) atTop (𝓝 (coeff i (x + y))).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_mul` (simp): coeff n (x * y) = coeff n x * coeff n y; coeff n 1 = 1; coeff n 0 = 0.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_frobeniusEquiv_symm` (simp): coeff n ((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm x) = coeff (n + 1) x.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): tilt R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (characterisation): x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ ∀ n, coeff n x ∈ R° ↔ coeff 0 x ∈ R° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.equivOfCharP` (equivalence): If CharP R p: tilt R ≃+* R, x ↦ coeff 0 x, a homeomorphism.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp` (data): The sharp map tilt R →* R (P1/sharp-map).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map` (functoriality): Tilt of a continuous ring homomorphism (P1/tilt-functoriality).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.integralEquivPreTilt` (compatibility): (tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt).
- `Perfectoid.Pair.tilt` (constructor): For a Huber pair P = (R, R+) with R perfectoid: the Huber pair (tilt R, lim_{x↦x^p} R+) (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt.equivOfCharP_laurent` (compatibility): For R the t-adic completion of the perfection of F_p((t)), tilt R ≃+* R via coeff 0, a homeomorphism.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_epsilon` (computation): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl, ε := (ζ_{p^n})_n with ζ_{p^{n+1}}^p = ζ_{p^n}, ζ_1 = 1 satisfies coeff n ε = ζ_{p^n} and ε ≠ 1.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_zero_sub_ne` (non-example): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl, coeff 0 (ε − 1) ≠ coeff 0 ε − coeff 0 1 = 0: coordinatewise subtraction is not the ring structure.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.nontrivial_iff` (degenerate): Nontrivial (tilt R) ↔ Nontrivial R; tilt of the zero ring is zero.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_charP` (characterisation): tilt R is a perfectoid Tate ring and CharP (tilt R) p, for every perfectoid R.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt, P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel, P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals: the tilt functor S ↦ S♭ and A_inf = W(S♭+).
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair: an untilt is a pair (X♯, ι) with ι an identification of the tilt of X♯ with X.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: tilts of cofiltered systems with R♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ R+/ϖ.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: the map x ↦ x♭ with |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|.
- ECD Definition 3.9; Berkeley Definition 6.2.1; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.1: the definition in the sources.

*Acceptance.*
- (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ is the completed perfection of F_p((t)) with t = ε − 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over a perfectoid field K, R♭ = K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (Sch12 Proposition 5.20; P1/perfected-tate-algebra).

#### `tilt-integral-subrings` — R♭° = lim R° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ, R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (ECD Lemma 3.10)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. Then (a) R♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} R° = {x ∈ R♭ : x^{(n)} ∈ R° for all n} = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°}, and for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ_0 of R dividing p in R° projection is a topological ring isomorphism R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 (discrete factors) ≅ lim_Φ R°/p; (b) ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of R♭, R♭° is an open and bounded subring whose subspace topology is the ϖ♭-adic one, and R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭]; (c) for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with 0 < q ≤ p, x ↦ x^{(0)} mod ϖ^qR° induces a ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭^qR♭° ≅ R°/ϖ^qR°, in particular R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ; (d) the kernel of R♭° → R°/ϖ^q is ϖ♭^qR♭°.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- ϖ^p | p in R°, so ϖ^q | p for q ≤ p.

*Proof outline.*
- (c),(d) Kernel: if x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^qR°, then (x^{(n)}/ϖ^{q/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° gives x^{(n)} ∈ ϖ^{q/p^n}R° by integral closedness, i.e. x/ϖ♭^q ∈ lim R°. Surjectivity: Frobenius on R°/ϖ^q is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the projection lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q → R°/ϖ^q is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective). Ring homomorphism: it is the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/ϖ^q (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius).
- (b) By (d), ker(pr_n: lim_Φ R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ) = ϖ♭^{p^n}R♭°, so the inverse-limit topology on lim R° is ϖ♭-adic; ϖ♭ is a unit (each coordinate is a unit of R) and topologically nilpotent; lim R° = {x : x^{(0)} ∈ R°} (integral closedness) is the preimage of the open R° under the continuous zeroth projection, hence open; it is bounded because (ϖ♭^My)^{(i)} = ϖ^{M/p^i}y^{(i)}; and x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NR° for i ≤ n iff x^{(0)} ∈ ϖ^{Np^n}R°, so the two topologies agree; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring.
- (a) lim R° is a bounded open subring, so it consists of power-bounded elements; conversely if x ∈ R♭ is power-bounded, {x^m} ⊆ ϖ♭^{-c}lim R°, so {(x^{(0)})^m} ⊆ ϖ^{-c}R° and x^{(0)} ∈ R°, and x^{(n)} ∈ R° since (x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x^{(0)} (ECD Lemma 3.10 proof: lim R° "agrees with the powerbounded elements R♭°").

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K: K♭° = lim K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ and K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (Sch12 Lemma 3.4(iii)).
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: R♭°/ϖ♭ = (K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}] (Sch12 Proposition 5.20 proof).

*Depends on:* `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, p. 16; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD after Lemma 3.10, p. 16; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.10, proof, p. 23; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.4(iii), p. 16.

#### `tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring` — The tilt of a perfectoid Tate ring is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the tilt R♭ is a complete Hausdorff uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Lemma 3.10, "a perfectoid F_p-algebra"); ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer, (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition, and R♭ ≠ 0 iff R ≠ 0.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*
- Huber and Tate: (R♭°, ϖ♭R♭°) is a pair of definition (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b)), and ϖ♭ is a topologically nilpotent unit.
- Complete Hausdorff: R♭° ≅ lim_Φ R°/ϖ_0 is an inverse limit of discrete rings; R♭ = R♭°[1/ϖ♭] with R♭° open.
- Uniform: R♭° is bounded (it is a ring of definition).
- Perfect of characteristic p (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect.
- 1 ≠ 0 in R♭ iff 1 ≠ 0 in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ iff R ≠ 0 (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)).

*Acceptance.*
- (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = ε − 1 (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- The tilt of a perfectoid ring of characteristic p is itself (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, equivOfCharP).

*Depends on:* `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.10, p. 16; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.2, p. 44; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.7.1(b), p. 66.

#### `sharp-map` — The sharp map ♯: R♭ → R (continuous, multiplicative, not additive)

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

For a perfectoid Tate ring R, the sharp map ♯: R♭ → R, x ↦ x♯ := x^{(0)} (Mathlib Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0 on the underlying monoid Perfection R p) is continuous and multiplicative with 0♯ = 0, and is not additive in general. It satisfies (x^{1/p^n})♯ = x^{(n)}; x ∈ R♭° iff x♯ ∈ R°; x♯ = 0 iff x = 0; for x, y ∈ R♭°, (x + y)♯ ≡ x♯ + y♯ mod pR°; every element of R° is congruent modulo pR° to some y♯ with y ∈ R♭°; reduction of ♯ modulo ϖ is the ring isomorphism R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ of P1/tilt-integral-subrings; and (ϖ♭)♯ = ϖ. If pR = 0, ♯ is the ring isomorphism R♭ ≅ R.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*
- Multiplicativity and continuity: ♯ is a coordinate projection of the inverse limit (ECD after Lemma 3.10; Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i) proof).
- Additivity modulo p: the reduction R♭° → R°/p, x ↦ x♯ mod p, is the zeroth projection of the ring lim_Φ R°/p (P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius, P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a)).
- Surjectivity modulo p: Frobenius on R°/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion), so the zeroth projection of lim_Φ R°/p is surjective (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_surjective).
- x♯ = 0 ⇒ x = 0: x^{(n)} is nilpotent ((x^{(n)})^{p^n} = x♯) hence 0 as R is reduced (P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp` (data): sharp : tilt R →* R := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom R p 0; notation x♯.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp₀` (data): The same map as a MonoidWithZeroHom (sharp 0 = 0).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.continuous_sharp` (structure): Continuous (sharp : tilt R → R).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow` (simp): sharp (((frobeniusEquiv (tilt R) p).symm)^[n] x) ^ p ^ n = sharp x (mirrors Mathlib PreTilt.untilt_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_sharp` (characterisation): x ∈ (tilt R)° ↔ sharp x ∈ R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_zero_iff` (characterisation): sharp x = 0 ↔ x = 0.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_add_sub_mem` (relation): For x, y ∈ (tilt R)°: sharp (x + y) − sharp x − sharp y ∈ p • R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.exists_sharp_sub_mem` (other): ∀ x ∈ R°, ∃ y ∈ (tilt R)°, x − sharp y ∈ p • R°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharpQuotEquiv` (equivalence): The ring isomorphism (tilt R)° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* R° ⧸ (ϖ) induced by sharp (P1/tilt-integral-subrings).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_toTilt` (simp): sharp ϖ♭.toTilt = ϖ for a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.gauge_sharp` (compatibility): |sharp x|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭} (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_untilt` (compatibility): Under (tilt R)° ≃+* PreTilt R° p, sharp corresponds to Mathlib PreTilt.untilt (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_sub_ne` (non-example): In tilt ℚ_p^cycl: sharp (ε − 1) ≠ sharp ε − sharp 1 = 0 (a ring homomorphism sharp would fail this).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_epsilon` (computation): sharp ε = 1 in tilt ℚ_p^cycl, and sharp p♭ = p in tilt ℂ_p for p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_ringEquiv_of_charP` (degenerate): If CharP R p, sharp is additive and is the ring isomorphism tilt.equivOfCharP.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_eq_zero_iff_test` (characterisation): For R = ℂ_p × ℂ_p♭ (a perfectoid Tate ring), sharp x = 0 only for x = 0.

*Uses.*
- ECD after Lemma 3.10: "continuous, multiplicative (but not additive)" map, and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel: θ([x]) = x♯ and θ(Σ[r_n]p^n) = Σ r_n♯p^n.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field: |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets: |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: approximation of functions by sharps of tilted functions (Sch12 Lemma 6.5, Corollary 6.7).
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: ε♯ = 1 and (p♭)♯ = p.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: f(ϖ) is a pseudo-uniformizer after composing with θ.

*Acceptance.*
- In (ℚ_p^cycl)♭: ε♯ = 1 while (ε − 1)♯ ≠ 0, so ♯ is not additive.
- In (ℂ_p)♭: p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) has (p♭)♯ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements).

*Depends on:* `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeffMonoidHom`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_surjective`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD after Lemma 3.10, p. 16; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD after Lemma 3.10, p. 16; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, §6.2, p. 45; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.3.14, p. 56; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.4(i), proof, p. 16.

#### `spectral-norm-under-sharp` — The spectral gauge is preserved by the sharp map: |x♯|_R = |x|_{R♭}

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, and |·|_ϖ, |·|_{ϖ♭} the spectral gauges of R and R♭ (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots, the second for R♭ with its pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ and roots ϖ♭^{1/p^n}), both normalised by |ϖ| = |ϖ♭| = 1/2. Then |x♯|_ϖ = |x|_{ϖ♭} for all x ∈ R♭ (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, "easy to check", over a perfectoid field; it is the norm Kedlaya–Liu put on the tilt by pullback along ♯).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- None beyond the setting.

*Proof outline.*
- For q ∈ ℤ[1/p]: x ∈ ϖ♭^qR♭° iff ϖ♭^{-q}x ∈ R♭° iff (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯ ∈ R° (P1/sharp-map: membership in R♭° is detected by ♯, and ♯ is multiplicative with (ϖ♭^q)♯ = ϖ^q), so the two infima run over the same set of q.

*Acceptance.*
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and ε = (ζ_{p^n})_n: |(ε − 1)♯| = lim |ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)}, which is |ε − 1| in K♭ (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

*Depends on:* `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `sharp-map`, `tilt-integral-subrings`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.21, proof, p. 27; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 3.3.8, proof, p. 60.

#### `tilt-functoriality` — Functoriality of tilting: f ↦ f♭

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

A continuous ring homomorphism f: R → S between perfectoid Tate rings induces f♭: R♭ → S♭, (x^{(n)})_n ↦ (f(x^{(n)}))_n (Mathlib Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f on the underlying monoids), a continuous ring homomorphism with (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), f♭(R♭°) ⊆ S♭°, id♭ = id and (g ∘ f)♭ = g♭ ∘ f♭; on R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ it induces the reduction of f. A morphism of Huber pairs (R, R+) → (S, S+) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom) with R, S perfectoid induces a morphism of the tilt pairs. Hence tilting is a functor from perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) to perfectoid Tate rings (resp. pairs) of characteristic p, and a perfectoid R-algebra S gives a perfectoid R♭-algebra S♭.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- f continuous; no condition on plus rings for the ring-level statement.

*Proof outline.*
- Multiplicativity is clear. Additivity: f is continuous and a ring homomorphism, so it commutes with the limit formula of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring. Continuity: coordinatewise.
- f(R°) ⊆ S° for any continuous homomorphism from a Tate ring to a uniform Tate ring (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so f♭ maps lim R° into lim S° = S♭° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); similarly lim R+ into lim S+ when f(R+) ⊆ S+.
- Functor laws hold coordinatewise; compatibility with ♯ is the zeroth coordinate.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map` (data): map f : tilt R →+* tilt S for f : R →+* S continuous, with underlying monoid hom Perfection.mapMonoidHom p f.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.coeff_map` (simp): coeff n (map f x) = f (coeff n x).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.sharp_map` (simp): sharp (map f x) = f (sharp x).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_id` (functoriality): map (RingHom.id R) = RingHom.id (tilt R).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_comp` (functoriality): map (g.comp f) = (map g).comp (map f).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.continuous_map` (structure): Continuous (map f).
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_mem_powerBoundedSubring` (other): x ∈ (tilt R)° → map f x ∈ (tilt S)°.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mapQuot_comm` (compatibility): The square (tilt R)°/(ϖ♭) ≅ R°/(ϖ) → S°/(f ϖ) ≅ (tilt S)°/(map f ϖ♭) commutes.
- `Perfectoid.Pair.tiltHom` (functoriality): Pair.Hom P Q ↦ Pair.Hom P.tilt Q.tilt, compatible with id and comp.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.mapEquiv` (equivalence): A ring isomorphism R ≃+* S that is a homeomorphism induces tilt R ≃+* tilt S.
- `Perfectoid.tiltFunctor` (functoriality): The functor from the category of perfectoid Tate rings (continuous ring homomorphisms) to perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p, and its slice version from perfectoid R-algebras to perfectoid R♭-algebras.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_id_test` (degenerate): tilt.map (RingHom.id ℂ_p) = RingHom.id.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_inclusion_epsilon` (computation): For the continuous inclusion ι : ℚ_p^cycl → ℂ_p, tilt.map ι ε = ε.
- `Perfectoid.tilt.map_equivOfCharP` (characterisation): For f : R → S continuous between perfectoid rings of characteristic p, tilt.equivOfCharP ∘ tilt.map f = f ∘ tilt.equivOfCharP.
- `Perfectoid.Pair.tiltHom_plus` (compatibility): For a Pair.Hom f : (R, R+) → (S, S+), Pair.tiltHom f carries lim R+ into lim S+.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt: the functor S ↦ S♭ on perfectoid R-algebras.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/theta-kernel-base-change: W(f♭) carries ker θ_R into ker θ_S.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting: tilts of rational restriction maps glue.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: tilts of transition maps of cofiltered systems.
- PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: G_F acts on C♭ through its action on C.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair: functoriality of untilts along X' → X uses tilting of maps.

*Acceptance.*
- For the inclusion ℚ_p^cycl → ℂ_p, f♭ maps ε ∈ (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ to ε ∈ (ℂ_p)♭.
- For g ∈ Gal(ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p) with cyclotomic character χ(g), g♭(ε) = ε^{χ(g)} (Berkeley Example 6.2.4: γ(t) = (1+t)^γ − 1).

*Depends on:* `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `sharp-map`, `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `mathlib:Perfection.mapMonoidHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

*Sources:* ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.3.2, p. 54; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Theorem 3.13, p. 17.

#### `rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting` — Rings of integral elements correspond under tilting: R+ ↦ R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Tilt`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯. (a) R+ ↦ R♭+ := lim_{x↦x^p} R+ = {x ∈ R♭ : x♯ ∈ R+} is an inclusion-preserving bijection from rings of integral elements of R to those of R♭; the inverse sends R♭+ to the preimage in R° of the image of R♭+ in R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (b) R♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ R+/ϖ compatibly with R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ. (c) On both sides, rings of integral elements correspond to integrally closed subrings of the common quotient R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ (equivalently of R°/R°° ≅ R♭°/R♭°°). Hence a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R+) has tilt pair (R♭, R♭+), and R° ↦ R♭°.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid; rings of integral elements are open, integrally closed and contained in R°.

*Proof outline.*
- An open integrally closed R+ ⊆ R° contains R°° ⊇ ϖR° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn), so R+ is the preimage of R+/ϖR° ⊆ R°/ϖR°; R+ is integrally closed in R iff R+/ϖR° is integrally closed in R°/ϖR° (lift, resp. reduce, a monic equation; ϖR° ⊆ R+), and R+ is open iff it contains ϖR° (ECD before Lemma 3.11).
- The same holds for R♭, and R♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ R°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c)) transports integrally closed subrings; x ∈ R♭+ iff x♯ mod ϖ ∈ R+/ϖ iff x♯ ∈ R+, and then x^{(n)} = (x^{1/p^n})♯ ∈ R+ by integral closedness, so R♭+ = lim R+ (ECD Lemma 3.11; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.5).

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K and an open valuation subring K+ ⊆ K°, K♭+ is the open valuation subring of K♭ with the same image in the common residue field K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (Sch12 Proposition 3.6 proof).
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and R+ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = R°, R♭+ = K♭°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.

*Depends on:* `tilt-integral-subrings`, `sharp-map`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosedIn`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.11, p. 17; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.5, p. 45; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 6.2, proof, p. 30; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.7.10, p. 69.

#### `tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt` — The integral tilt R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p, and ♯ is PreTilt.untilt

*comparison.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Mathlib`.

Let R be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements (e.g. R°). Then R+ satisfies Mathlib's standing hypotheses Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+) and IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), and: (a) the subring R♭+ = lim_{x↦x^p} R+ of R♭ is isomorphic as a topological ring to Mathlib's PreTilt R+ p = Perfection (ModP R+ p) p via x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod p)_n, with inverse built from Perfection.teichmuller / Perfection.quotientMulEquiv; (b) under this isomorphism x ↦ x♯ on R♭+ is Mathlib's PreTilt.untilt : PreTilt R+ p →* R+, and PreTilt.coeff 0 is ♯ mod p (PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero); (c) R♭ ≅ (PreTilt R+ p)[1/ϖ♭] (Localization.Away). Mathlib's PreTilt is thus the integral tilt of this layer; Mathlib has no ring structure on lim_{x↦x^p} R and no tilt of a non-field Tate ring, which this layer supplies (the field case, Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val, is compared in P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R ≠ 0 (otherwise p is a unit of R+ = 0 and Mathlib's hypothesis fails).

*Proof outline.*
- (a) Both rings are lim_Φ R+/p: PreTilt R+ p by definition, R♭+ by P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with ϖ_0 replaced by p, and both ring structures are the inverse-limit ones (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (a) for R+ = R°, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting in general).
- (b) PreTilt.untilt is defined as teichmuller p (span {p}), the zeroth coordinate of the inverse of the reduction map (Mathlib Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv), i.e. x ↦ x♯.
- (c) R♭ = R♭+[1/ϖ♭] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (b), since ϖ♭R♭° ⊆ R♭+).

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℂ_p, PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ (ℂ_p)♭° and PreTilt.untilt p♭ = p (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements realises 𝒪_{C}♭ through PreTilt).
- WittVector p (PreTilt R+ p) is Mathlib's A_inf(R+), the source of WittVector.fontaineTheta (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib).

*Depends on:* `inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `sharp-map`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:PreTilt`, `mathlib:PreTilt.untilt`, `mathlib:PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero`, `mathlib:PreTilt.coeff`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:Perfection.coeff_zero_symm_quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:ModP`, `mathlib:Localization.Away`.

*Sources:* BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.2(i), p. 19; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Remark 3.4.10, p. 82; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Theorem 6.2.7(2), p. 47.

#### `tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring` — The tilt B♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} B of a complete uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1)

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/UniformTilt`.

Let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring in which p is topologically nilpotent (B is not assumed perfectoid) and B⁺ ⊆ B° a ring of integral elements. Its tilt is B♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} B (Mathlib `Perfection B p`) with the inverse-limit topology, pointwise multiplication, x♯ := x^{(0)}, and addition (x + y)^{(i)} := lim_{n→∞}(x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n}. Then: (a) the limit exists and makes B♭ a perfect topological ring of characteristic p; ♯ is continuous and multiplicative; B♭⁺ := lim_{x↦x^p} B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} is an open subring and B♭° := lim_{x↦x^p} B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°}; B♭ is complete and Hausdorff; (b) for every ideal of definition I ⊆ B⁺ with p ∈ I (for instance I = (p, ϖ) for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ B⁺; Kedlaya asks p ∈ I^p), reduction x ↦ (x^{(n)} mod I)_n is an isomorphism of topological rings B♭⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I (discrete factors), and B♭⁺ ≅ PreTilt B⁺ p; (c) if B has a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p in B° and compatible p-power roots, i.e. ϖ = ϖ♭♯ for some ϖ♭ ∈ B♭, then ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer of B♭, B♭° is open and bounded with the ϖ♭-adic topology, B♭ = B♭°[1/ϖ♭], the spectral gauges satisfy |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ, and B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, hence a perfectoid Tate ring; this applies whenever there is a continuous ring homomorphism f: A → B from a perfectoid Tate ring A, with ϖ♭ := f♭(ϖ_A♭); the closure in B♭ of a perfect subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is then a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p; (d) a continuous ring homomorphism g: B → C of such rings induces g♭: B♭ → C♭, (x^{(n)}) ↦ (g(x^{(n)})), a continuous ring homomorphism with (g♭x)♯ = g(x♯), functorially; (e) there is a unique ring homomorphism θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ with θ_B([x]) = x♯ (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` for the p-adically complete ring B⁺), natural in B: θ_C ∘ W(g♭) = g ∘ θ_B; it is not surjective in general; (f) if B is perfectoid, B♭ with ♯, g♭ and θ_B is the tilt of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring with the sharp map, functoriality and θ of P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- B complete, Hausdorff, uniform, p topologically nilpotent in B; no perfectoid condition.
- In (c) B♭ is Tate only because ϖ has compatible p-power roots in B; without them B♭ need not be Tate (test uniformTilt_padic).

*Proof outline.*
- (b), and the ring structure: B⁺ is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)), hence I-adically complete for I = (p, ϖ) because p^N ∈ ϖB⁺ for large N; Mathlib `Perfection.quotientMulEquiv` (hypotheses IsAdicComplete I B⁺ and CharP (B⁺/I) p) gives the multiplicative bijection lim B⁺ ≅ lim_Φ B⁺/I, a homeomorphism for the inverse-limit topologies (the argument of P1/inverse-limit-of-integral-elements-along-frobenius with I in place of ϖ_0). Transport the ring structure of the perfect F_p-algebra lim_Φ B⁺/I; its sum has i-th coordinate lim_n (x^{(i+n)} + y^{(i+n)})^{p^n} (Mathlib `Perfection.teichmuller_spec`), which does not depend on I. For I = (p) this is Mathlib `PreTilt B⁺ p` (B⁺ is p-adically complete, Stacks Tag 090T).
- (a): Kedlaya's identity [x + y] = lim_m ([x^{p^{-m}}] + [y^{p^{-m}}])^{p^m} in W(F_p[x^{p^{-∞}}, y^{p^{-∞}}]) (Kedlaya AWS (2.7.1.2)), specialised to the coordinates of x, y ∈ B♭, gives existence of the limit, associativity and continuity of the addition on all of B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1(a)–(b) and proof); on B♭⁺ it is the ring structure of (b). B♭⁺ is the preimage of the open B⁺ under the continuous ♯, hence open; it is complete by (b), so B♭ is complete and Hausdorff. lim B⁺ = {x : x♯ ∈ B⁺} and lim B° = {x : x♯ ∈ B°} because B⁺ and B° are integrally closed in B (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
- (c): (ϖ♭^{-q}x)♯ = ϖ^{-q}x♯, so {x : x^{(i)} ∈ ϖ^NB° for i ≤ n} = ϖ♭^{Np^n}B♭°: the topology of B♭° is ϖ♭-adic, ϖ♭ is a unit (coordinatewise) and topologically nilpotent, and |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ (same set of exponents q, as in P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp). Hence B♭ is a complete uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p, perfectoid by P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. For f: A → B, f(ϖ_A) = (f♭ϖ_A♭)♯ has compatible roots and f(ϖ_A)^p | p in B° (continuous homomorphisms into a uniform Tate ring preserve power-bounded elements, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A closed subring containing ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is complete and Tate, and the closure of a perfect subring is perfect because x ↦ x^{1/p} (the shift of coordinates) is continuous.
- (d): g commutes with the limit formula and with the coordinates (Mathlib `Perfection.mapMonoidHom`); continuity is coordinatewise.
- (e): B⁺ is p-adically complete, so θ_B exists and is unique as the Witt-vector lift of x ↦ x♯ mod p (Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta` on PreTilt B⁺ p, via (b)); naturality follows from uniqueness. For B = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) (p odd) the image of θ_B is ℤ_p ≠ ℤ_p[p^{1/p}].
- (f): for perfectoid B the construction and the formulas are those of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/sharp-map, P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (θ is determined by θ([x]) = x♯).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt` (data): uniformTilt B : Type := Perfection B p with CommRing (limiting addition), TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, CharP p, PerfectRing, CompleteSpace and T2Space instances, for B complete Hausdorff uniform Tate with IsTopologicallyNilpotent (p : B).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.sharp` (projection): sharp : uniformTilt B →* B := Perfection.coeffMonoidHom B p 0, continuous; sharp (x^{1/p^n})^{p^n} = sharp x.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.coeff_add` (characterisation): coeff i (x + y) = lim_{n→∞} (coeff (i + n) x + coeff (i + n) y)^{p^n} (Filter.Tendsto form).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.plusEquiv` (equivalence): For an ideal of definition I of B⁺ with p ∈ I: lim B⁺ ≃+* Perfection (B⁺ ⧸ I) p, a homeomorphism for discrete factors (from Perfection.quotientMulEquiv); and lim B⁺ ≃+* PreTilt B⁺ p.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff` (characterisation): x ∈ (uniformTilt B)° ↔ sharp x ∈ B°; likewise x ∈ lim B⁺ ↔ sharp x ∈ B⁺.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.map` (functoriality): map g : uniformTilt B →+* uniformTilt C for g : B →+* C continuous; continuous; sharp (map g x) = g (sharp x); map_id, map_comp.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isTateRing_of_sharp` (instance): If ϖ♭ : uniformTilt B has sharp ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer of B with (sharp ϖ♭)^p ∣ p in B°, then IsTateRing (uniformTilt B), IsBounded (uniformTilt B)°, IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B), and gauge ϖ♭ x = gauge (sharp ϖ♭) (sharp x).
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_closure` (other): Under isTateRing_of_sharp, the closure of the range of a ring homomorphism from a perfect ring whose range contains ϖ♭ and ϖ♭⁻¹ is a closed subring that is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.theta` (compatibility): theta B : 𝕎 (lim B⁺) →+* B⁺ with theta [x] = sharp x, equal to WittVector.fontaineTheta B⁺ p under plusEquiv; theta C ∘ WittVector.map (map g) = g ∘ theta B.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.equivTilt` (compatibility): For B perfectoid, uniformTilt B ≃+* tilt B (the identity of Perfection B p), a homeomorphism commuting with sharp and map (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_equiv_tilt` (compatibility): For B perfectoid, uniformTilt B and tilt B are the same ring structure on Perfection B p: the identity is a topological ring isomorphism commuting with sharp, with map and with θ.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_padic` (non-example): uniformTilt ℚ_p ≃+* 𝔽_p (Teichmüller representatives {0} ∪ μ_{p−1}, p odd) with the discrete topology: it is not a Tate ring, and ℚ_p has no pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with ϖ^p | p, so (c) does not apply; a construction asserting that the tilt of every uniform Tate ring is Tate fails here.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt_charP` (degenerate): If B is a perfect uniform Tate ring of characteristic p, sharp : uniformTilt B ≃+* B is a topological ring isomorphism; uniformTilt of the zero ring is zero.
- `Perfectoid.uniformTilt.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_hom` (characterisation): For f: A → B continuous with A perfectoid and B uniform, IsPerfectoidTateRing (uniformTilt B), CharP (uniformTilt B) p, and map f ϖ♭ is a pseudo-uniformizer with sharp (map f ϖ♭) = f ϖ.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: the tilt B♭ of the uniform target B, the closure of f♭(A♭) in it, and θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ for the map from the untilt B₀ to B (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(ii)).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting (b): the gauge |x|_{ϖ♭} = |x♯|_ϖ on the tilt of a uniform target.
- Kedlaya AWS §2.7 (Lemmas 2.7.1, 2.7.7, 2.7.8): calculations with the tilt of a pair before it is known to be perfectoid or analytic.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (a): tilts of uniform quotients of perfectoid rings (through the dense-image criterion).

*Acceptance.*
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4: for f: A → B continuous with A perfectoid and B uniform, B♭ is a uniform perfect Tate ring of characteristic p receiving f♭: A♭ → B♭, and the closure of f♭(A♭) is a perfectoid Tate ring (the first two steps of P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion).
- For B = ℚ_p, B♭ ≅ 𝔽_p with the discrete topology: an element with compatible p-power roots has valuation 0, and the only units of ℤ_p with p^n-th roots for all n are the Teichmüller representatives (p odd).
