### P1.3 The almost setup of a perfectoid Tate ring

P0 develops almost mathematics over an abstract basic setup; this layer instantiates it with (R°, R°°) and shows independence of all choices (ECD 3.21–3.23).

#### `topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal` — R°° = ⋃ ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is an idempotent flat ideal

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Almost`.

Let R be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and ϖ♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n a pseudo-uniformizer of R with compatible p-power roots (for R perfectoid, P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots). Then the ideal R°° of topologically nilpotent elements of R° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal) equals ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ⋃_{q∈ℤ[1/p]_{>0}} ϖ^qR°; it satisfies (R°°)² = R°° and is flat as an R°-module (a filtered union of the free rank-one modules ϖ^{1/p^n}R°). For every ring of integral elements R+, R°° ⊆ R+ and R°° = ⋃_n ϖ^{1/p^n}R+. Hence (R°, R°°) and (R+, R°°) satisfy the hypotheses of P0/root-ideal-basic-setup.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Uniformity is used through P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0).

*Proof outline.*
- ⊇: ϖ^{1/p^n} is topologically nilpotent and R° is power-bounded, so ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R°° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul).
- ⊆: for x ∈ R°°, x^N ∈ ϖR° for N large because ϖR° is an open neighbourhood of 0 (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (a)); for p^n ≥ N, x^{p^n} ∈ ϖR°, so (x/ϖ^{1/p^n})^{p^n} ∈ R° and x/ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R° by integral closedness (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral).
- Idempotence: ϖ^{1/p^n} = (ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p ∈ (R°°)². Flatness: ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ≅ R° since ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of R°, and a filtered colimit of flat modules is flat.
- R+: R°° ⊆ R+ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° = ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}·ϖ^{1/p^n − 1/p^{n+1}}R° ⊆ ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R+.

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K, K°° = m_K with m_K² = m_K (Bhatt notes Lemma 3.1.3(2)).
- For ℚ_p, ℤ_p°° = pℤ_p and (pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p: without p-power roots the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements is not idempotent.

*Depends on:* `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded.isTopologicallyNilpotent_mul`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isPowerBounded_of_isIntegral`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Definition 3.21, p. 19; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Lemma 3.1.3(2), p. 10; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD §3 preamble, p. 14.

#### `perfectoid-almost-setup` — The almost setup (R°, R°°) of a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD 3.21–3.23)

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Almost`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. The pair (R°, R°°) is a basic setup for almost mathematics (P0/almost-basic-setup: R°° idempotent and R°° ⊗_{R°} R°° ≅ R°° flat), and so is (R+, R°°) for every ring of integral elements R+. For an R+-module M the following are equivalent: (i) M is almost zero, R°°M = 0; (ii) ϖ'M = 0 for every pseudo-uniformizer ϖ' of R; (iii) ϖ^{1/p^n}M = 0 for all n, for one (equivalently any) pseudo-uniformizer ϖ with compatible p-power roots (ECD Definition 3.21; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.9.4). The almost-zero modules form the Serre class of P0/almost-zero-serre-class, the almost categories R°a-Mod and R+a-Mod are the Serre quotients of P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base (ECD Definition 3.23), and restriction of scalars along R+ → R°, which is injective with almost zero cokernel (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), induces an equivalence R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod. The construction depends only on R. For a perfectoid field K it is the classical setup (K°, m_K), with K°/m_K almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(i)).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid (compatible roots exist, P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).

*Proof outline.*
- Basic setup: R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R° is idempotent and flat (P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal), so P0/root-ideal-basic-setup applies to R° and to R+.
- (i) ⇔ (ii) ⇔ (iii): every pseudo-uniformizer lies in R°°, every ϖ^{1/p^n} is a pseudo-uniformizer, and R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R°.
- R°/R+ is almost zero: for x ∈ R° and ϖ' a pseudo-uniformizer, ϖ'x is topologically nilpotent, hence in R+ (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
- R°a-Mod ≃ R+a-Mod: R+ → R° is an almost isomorphism of rings, so extension and restriction of scalars induce inverse equivalences of the Serre quotients (P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup` (constructor): almostSetup R : Almost.BasicSetup with ring R° and ideal topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R (P0/almost-basic-setup).
- `Perfectoid.almostSetupPlus` (constructor): almostSetupPlus (R+) : Almost.BasicSetup with ring R+ and ideal R°° ∩ R+ = R°°.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_ideal` (simp): (almostSetup R).ideal = topologicallyNilpotentIdeal R.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_forall_pseudoUniformizer` (characterisation): M is almost zero ↔ ∀ ϖ', IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ' → ϖ' • M = 0.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_forall_root` (characterisation): M is almost zero ↔ ∀ n, ϖ^{1/p^n} • M = 0, for any ϖ♭ with compatible roots.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_powerBounded_quotient_plus` (other): R° ⧸ R+ is almost zero (as R+-module).
- `Perfectoid.almostModuleEquivPlus` (equivalence): Restriction of scalars induces an equivalence of the almost categories of R° and R+.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_ringEquiv` (functoriality): An isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings (topological) induces an isomorphism of basic setups; the setup does not depend on ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_field` (compatibility): For a perfectoid field K, almostSetup K is (K°, m_K), the field case of P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base.
- `Perfectoid.almostSetup_tilt_quot` (compatibility): The isomorphism R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ carries R°°/ϖ onto R♭°°/ϖ♭, identifying the almost categories of R°/ϖ and R♭°/ϖ♭ (used in P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_residueField` (computation): For K a perfectoid field, K° ⧸ m_K is almost zero and ϖ^{1/p^n} acts by 0 on it for all n.
- `Perfectoid.not_idempotent_padic` (non-example): For ℚ_p, (pℤ_p)² ≠ pℤ_p, so (ℤ_p, ℤ_p°°) is not a basic setup; ℤ_p/p is killed by p but not by an idempotent ideal containing p.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_of_subsingleton` (degenerate): For R = 0 every module is almost zero.
- `Perfectoid.isAlmostZero_iff_root_test` (characterisation): For K = ℂ_p, the 𝒪-module 𝒪/m is almost zero while 𝒪/p^{1/p}𝒪 is not (p^{1/p²} does not kill it).
- `Perfectoid.almostModuleEquivPlus_test` (compatibility): For K = ℂ_p and K+ an open rank-2 valuation subring, K°a-Mod ≃ K+a-Mod.

*Uses.*
- ECD Definitions 3.21, 3.23 and Theorem 3.24: almost zero modules, R°a-mod, and almost acyclicity of O+.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base: its perfectoid instantiation is this node.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary, P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence: R°a-Perf and (R°a/ϖ)-Perf.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity, P2/integral-almost-acyclicity: H^i(X, O+)^a = 0.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem: almost finite étale R°a-algebras.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/higher-v-acyclicity, D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected: almost vanishing and almost faithfully flat descent over (R+/ϖ)^a.

*Acceptance.*
- For a perfectoid field K: the residue field K°/m_K is almost zero, and every almost zero K°-module is a k-vector space (ECD Example 3.22(i)).
- Theorem-level consumers: H^i(Spa(R, R+), O+) is almost zero for i > 0 (ECD Theorem 3.24; P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity).

### P1.4 Perfectoid fields

Perfectoid fields are the perfectoid Tate rings that are nonarchimedean fields (ECD 3.6). A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is automatically one (Kedlaya); in characteristic 0 this layer deduces it from the characteristic-p case through the tilt and the spectral gauge.

#### `perfectoid-field-definition` — Perfectoid fields (ECD Definition 3.6)

*definition.* **Planet:** *Perfectoid field*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring K (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) whose underlying topological ring is a nonarchimedean field: K is a field, complete with respect to a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value |·| defining its topology (ECD Definition 3.6). Equivalently (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation; ECD Proposition 3.8; the original definition Sch12 Definition 3.1): K is a nonarchimedean field which is not discretely valued, |p| < 1, and Frobenius is surjective on K°/p. Its value group is p-divisible (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible). In characteristic p a perfectoid field is the same as a complete perfect nonarchimedean field. A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is automatically a perfectoid field (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field). ℚ_p and all discretely valued fields are not perfectoid.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Nonarchimedean field: in Lean, NontriviallyNormedField K with IsUltrametricDist K and CompleteSpace K; its Tate structure has ring of definition K° (closed unit ball) and any 0 < |ϖ| < 1 as pseudo-uniformizer.
- Residue characteristic p is forced by |p| < 1.

*Proof outline.*
- The Tate structure of a nonarchimedean field (API isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField) is routine: K° is open and bounded, and the ϖ-adic topology on K° is the norm topology.
- Uniformity is automatic (K° is the closed unit ball), so the definition reduces to condition (b) of ECD Definition 3.1.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField` (structure): class IsPerfectoidField (K) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] : Prop := IsPerfectoidTateRing K (for the Tate structure below).
- `Huber.isTateRing_of_nontriviallyNormedField` (instance): A complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field is a Tate ring with ring of definition the closed unit ball and pseudo-uniformizer any 0 < |ϖ| < 1; its power-bounded subring is the closed unit ball and its topologically nilpotent ideal the open unit ball.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.toIsPerfectoidTateRing` (coercion): A perfectoid field is a perfectoid Tate ring.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.iff` (characterisation): IsPerfectoidField K ↔ (valuation not discrete) ∧ ‖p‖ < 1 ∧ Surjective (frobenius (K°/p) p) (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.norm_p_lt_one` (projection): ‖(p : K)‖ < 1.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.exists_pow_dvd_p` (projection): ∃ ϖ, 0 < ‖ϖ‖ < 1 ∧ ‖p‖ ≤ ‖ϖ‖ ^ p.
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.valueGroup_pDivisible` (characterisation): Every element of the value group |K^×| has a p-th root in it (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.iff_perfectRing` (characterisation): If CharP K p: IsPerfectoidField K ↔ PerfectRing K p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.of_isPerfectoidTateRing_of_isField` (constructor): A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field carries a nonarchimedean absolute value making it a perfectoid field (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field).
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.tilt` (compatibility): The tilt of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field of characteristic p (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_padicComplex` (example): ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p) is a perfectoid field.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidField_padic` (non-example): ¬ IsPerfectoidField ℚ_[p]: ℚ_p is discretely valued (ECD Remark 3.3), although Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is surjective.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_padicComplex_test` (computation): IsPerfectoidField (PadicComplex p): the value group is |p|^ℚ and every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidField_iff_perfect_laurent` (characterisation): For the completed perfection K of F_p((t)): IsPerfectoidField K holds; F_p((t)) is not perfect and not a perfectoid field.
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidField_trivial` (degenerate): The perfect field F̄_p with the trivial absolute value is not a nonarchimedean field in this sense (the absolute value must be nontrivial), so it is not a perfectoid field.
- `Perfectoid.isPerfectoidTateRing_of_isPerfectoidField` (compatibility): IsPerfectoidField K → IsPerfectoidTateRing K, and conversely for K a field (Kedlaya).

*Uses.*
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements; PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: C = ℂ_p is a perfectoid field; its tilt C♭.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field: the completed perfection of F_p((t)) is a perfectoid field.
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-p-adic-field: K^cycl is a perfectoid field.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field, P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields, P3/fontaine-wintenberger: tilting and Galois theory of perfectoid fields.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: completed residue fields of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid fields.
- ECD Definition 3.6; Sch12 Definition 3.1; Berkeley Definition 6.1.7; Bhatt Definition 3.1.1: the definition in the sources.

- ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and the completed perfection of F_p((t)) are perfectoid fields (P1/perfectoid-examples); ℚ_p is not.

#### `perfectoid-field-characterisation` — Characterisation of perfectoid fields (ECD Proposition 3.8)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

Let K be a nonarchimedean field. Then K is a perfectoid field iff (i) K is not discretely valued, (ii) |p| < 1, and (iii) Frobenius Φ: K°/p → K°/p is surjective (ECD Proposition 3.8; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9). Condition (i) cannot be dropped (ℚ_p and its unramified extensions satisfy (ii) and (iii)). Hence Sch12 Definition 3.1 agrees with ECD Definition 3.6, and a nonarchimedean field is a perfectoid ring in Kedlaya's sense iff it is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- K complete with a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value.

*Proof outline.*
- K is uniform (K° is the closed unit ball) and Tate.
- (⇒) (ii): ϖ^p | p with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 gives |p| ≤ |ϖ|^p < 1. (iii): P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion (i) ⇒ (ii). (i): if K were discretely valued with uniformizer π and ϖ = uπ^k (k ≥ 1), then K°/ϖ and K°/ϖ^p are Artin local rings of lengths k and pk, so Φ could not be bijective (ECD Remark 3.3).
- (⇐) A nondiscrete subgroup of ℝ_{>0} is dense, so there is ϖ ∈ K with |p|^{1/p} ≤ |ϖ| < 1, i.e. ϖ^p | p in K° (Berkeley Proposition 6.1.9 proof); then P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion and P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer give bijectivity of Φ: K°/ϖ → K°/ϖ^p.

*Acceptance.*
- ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) satisfy (i)–(iii) (P1/perfectoid-examples).
- ℚ_p satisfies (ii) and (iii) (Frobenius on ℤ_p/p = F_p is bijective) but not (i); Sch12 notes that nondiscreteness is needed to exclude unramified extensions of ℚ_p.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-field-definition`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:NontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.8, p. 15; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.8 (i)–(iii), p. 15; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Remark 3.3, p. 14; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 6.1.9, proof, p. 43; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 §3, after Definition 3.1, p. 15; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Corollary 2.3.11, p. 55.

#### `perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible` — The value group of a perfectoid field is p-divisible (Sch12 Lemma 3.2)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

Let K be a perfectoid field with value group Γ = |K^×| ⊆ ℝ_{>0}. Then Γ is p-divisible, and it is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 (in characteristic 0).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- K perfectoid; in characteristic p the statement follows from perfectness.

*Proof outline.*
- Characteristic p: every x has a p-th root x^{1/p}, so |x| = |x^{1/p}|^p.
- Characteristic 0 (Sch12 Lemma 3.2): Γ ≠ |p|^ℤ by nondiscreteness (P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), so Γ is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1; for such x choose y with |x − y^p| ≤ |p| (Frobenius surjective on K°/p); then |y|^p = |y^p| = |x|.

*Acceptance.*
- |ℂ_p^×| = |p|^ℚ is p-divisible; |ℚ_p^×| = |p|^ℤ is not, consistently with ℚ_p not being perfectoid.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-field-characterisation`, `perfectoid-field-definition`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.2, p. 15; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.2, proof, p. 15; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Lemma 3.1.3(1), p. 10.

#### `uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field` — A uniform Banach field over a nondiscretely valued field is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/BanachField`.

Let F be a nonarchimedean field whose value group |F^×| is dense in ℝ_{>0}, and let A be a uniform Banach F-algebra (complete, with topology defined by a power-multiplicative norm; equivalently the spectral seminorm |·|_sp is a norm defining the topology) whose underlying ring is a field. Then |·|_sp is multiplicative, so A is a nonarchimedean field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 3.7). The criterion used: a uniform Banach field A is a nonarchimedean field iff |t|_sp |t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ∈ A^× (Remark 3.3), because then |x|_sp = |xy·y^{-1}|_sp ≤ |xy|_sp/|y|_sp.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- |F^×| dense in ℝ_{>0}; the discretely valued case is not covered by the proof (Kedlaya, Remark 3.9).
- Uniformity is essential: Kedlaya's Example 2.15 is a Banach field that is not a nonarchimedean field.
- The proof uses the Berkovich spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms: M(A) ≠ ∅ for A ≠ 0, f is a unit iff α(f) ≠ 0 for all α, and |x|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(x) (Berkovich, Theorems 1.2.1 and 1.3.1), requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0.

*Proof outline.*
- Criterion (Remark 3.3): if |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp = 1 for all t ≠ 0 then |·|_sp is multiplicative; conversely a multiplicative norm satisfies it.
- Lemma 3.6: if A is not a nonarchimedean field, there are t ∈ A with |t|_sp|t^{-1}|_sp > 1 and an interval [γ, δ] meeting |F^×| such that |λ|·|(t − λ)^{-1}|_sp ≤ c² for all λ ∈ F with |λ| ∈ [γ, δ]; the proof builds a convergent sequence μ_n = Σλ_i in F by contradiction.
- Theorem 3.7: with ρ_n ↑ δ and polynomials P_n(t) = ∏(t − λ_{n,i}) whose roots have norms in [ρ_n^-, ρ_n^+], set x_n = (Σ_{j<m_n} P_{n,j}t^j)/P_n(t) and y_n = x_1⋯x_n; estimate α(y_n − y_{n−1}) for every α ∈ M(A) with α(t) = ρ, pass to |·|_sp = max_α α, and obtain a limit y which is neither zero nor a unit, a contradiction.

*Acceptance.*
- Applied with F the completed perfection of F_p((z)) (value group dense) to a perfect uniform Banach field of characteristic p (P1/perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field).
- Kedlaya Example 2.15 (Gauss norm on F(T_1, T_2, …)): the completion is a Banach field whose norm is not multiplicative, and it is not uniform.

*Depends on:* `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`, `mathlib:NontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:IsUltrametricDist`, `mathlib:CompleteSpace`.

*Sources:* Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7, p. 10; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Remark 3.3, p. 8; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7, proof, p. 10; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7, proof, p. 11; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Lemma 2.4, proof, p. 4; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, introduction, p. 1.

#### `perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field` — A perfectoid Tate ring is a field iff its tilt is (Sch12 Lemma 5.21, general base)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. Then R is a perfectoid field (a nonarchimedean field) iff its tilt R♭ is; in that case the absolute values satisfy |x|_{R♭} = |x♯|_R when normalised by |ϖ♭|_{R♭} = |ϖ|_R (Sch12 Lemma 5.21 over a perfectoid base field; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.5.2 and Example 3.3.8 in characteristic 0; Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.3.11).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid with ϖ♭ with compatible roots; the spectral gauges are those of P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

*Proof outline.*
- A uniform Tate ring R is a nonarchimedean field iff R is a field and its spectral gauge |·|_ϖ is multiplicative (then |·|_ϖ is an absolute value defining the topology).
- (⇒) |·|_{R♭} = |·♯|_R (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp) is multiplicative because ♯ is. R♭ is a field: for x ≠ 0, every x^{(n)} ≠ 0 (P1/sharp-map: x♯ = 0 iff x = 0, applied to x^{1/p^n}), and ((x^{(n)})^{-1})_n ∈ lim_{x↦x^p} R is a multiplicative inverse (the argument of Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2).
- (⇐) (Sch12 Lemma 5.21) Scale x, y ≠ 0 by powers ϖ^{k/p} into R° ∖ ϖ^{1/p}R°, choose x♭, y♭ ∈ R♭° with x − (x♭)♯, y − (y♭)♯ ∈ ϖR° (P1/sharp-map); then |x| = |x♭|, |y| = |y♭|, |xy| = |x♭y♭|, so multiplicativity transfers. x is a unit: |1 − x·((x♭)^{-1})♯| < 1 and R is complete.

*Acceptance.*
- (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ is the field F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- For a perfectoid field K, the product K × K♭ is perfectoid but not a field, and its tilt K♭ × K♭ is not a field.

*Depends on:* `spectral-norm-under-sharp`, `sharp-map`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `perfectoid-field-definition`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.21, p. 27; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.21, proof, p. 28; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.21, proof, p. 27; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 3.5.2(a), p. 82; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Example 3.3.8, p. 78.

#### `perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field` — A perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya; ECD Remark 3.7)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring whose underlying ring is a field. Then the topology of A is defined by a multiplicative absolute value, so A is a perfectoid field (Kedlaya, On commutative nonarchimedean Banach fields, Theorem 4.2; answers ECD Remark 3.7; Berkeley Remark 6.1.8; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.1).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field (Kedlaya, Remark 4.3: such A need not be an algebra over any perfectoid field).

*Proof outline.*
- Characteristic p: A is perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) and uniform; for a pseudo-uniformizer z, A is a uniform Banach algebra over the completed perfection of F_p((z)), whose value group is dense (Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2 proof; Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.1.8), so P1/uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field applies.
- General case: A♭ is a field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field, (⇒) argument for fields: coordinatewise inverses in lim_{x↦x^p} A) and a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring), hence a perfectoid field by the characteristic-p case; so A is a perfectoid field by P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field (⇐). This replaces Kedlaya's appeal to the homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(A♭) of Berkovich spectra by the spectral-gauge comparison P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp.

*Acceptance.*
- Every perfectoid Tate ring that is a field, e.g. ℚ_p^cycl or ℂ_p with their Tate topologies, is a perfectoid field; the theorem is needed when the topology is given only by a ring of definition.
- Kedlaya Remark 4.3 constructs a perfectoid ring over ℚ_p admitting quotients ℚ_p^cycl and the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), which is not an algebra over any perfectoid field; the theorem applies to its field quotients.

*Depends on:* `uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field`, `perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`, `tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `sharp-map`, `perfectoid-field-definition`.

*Sources:* Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2, p. 13; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2, proof, p. 13; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 4.2, proof, p. 13; Kedlaya-BanachFields-2018, Kedlaya, Banach fields, Remark 4.3, p. 13; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Remark 3.7, p. 15; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Remark 6.1.8, p. 43; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.9.1, p. 73.

#### `tilt-of-perfectoid-field` — Tilt of a perfectoid field; comparison with Mathlib's Tilt and PreTilt.val

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

Let K be a perfectoid field. Its tilt K♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) is a perfectoid field of characteristic p with absolute value |x|_♭ := |x♯|; K♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ is its valuation ring for any ϖ ∈ K with |p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1; |K♭^×| = |K^×|; K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ and K♭°/m♭ ≅ K°/m; K♭ = K if char K = p. Replacing ϖ by (ϖ♭)♯ one may assume ϖ has compatible p-power roots (Sch12 Lemma 3.4, Remark 3.5). For v : Valuation K ℝ≥0 the absolute value, O = K° and hv : v.Integers O, the tilt is isomorphic to Mathlib's Tilt K v O hv p = FractionRing (PreTilt O p), and Mathlib's valuation PreTilt.val K v O hv p satisfies PreTilt.val x = v(x♯) for x ∈ PreTilt O p ≅ K♭°.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- K perfectoid; ϖ | p in K° for the identification with lim_Φ K°/ϖ.

*Proof outline.*
- K♭ is a perfectoid Tate ring (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) and a nonarchimedean field (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field) with absolute value |x♯| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp).
- K♭° = lim K° (P1/tilt-integral-subrings) is a valuation ring: x or x^{-1} lies in it according as |x♯| ≤ 1 or ≥ 1.
- Value groups: |K♭^×| ⊆ |K^×|; conversely for x ∈ K° with |p| < |x| ≤ 1 there is y ∈ K♭° with x ≡ y♯ mod pK° (P1/sharp-map), so |x| = |y♯|, and such |x| generate |K^×| (P1/perfectoid-field-value-group-p-divisible, proof).
- Residue fields: K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings), and m, m♭ are the nilradicals of these rings.
- Mathlib: K♭° ≅ PreTilt O p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt) and K♭ = Frac(K♭°) = FractionRing (PreTilt O p); PreTilt.val x = preVal(x_n)^{p^n} for n with x_n ≠ 0, and a lift z of x_n satisfies z^{p^n} ≡ x♯ mod p^{n+1} (Mathlib Perfection.teichmuller_spec), so for v(z) > v(p) both sides equal v(x♯).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.IsPerfectoidField.tilt_isPerfectoidField` (instance): For K a perfectoid field, tilt K is a perfectoid field (with the absolute value below).
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.norm_def` (characterisation): ‖x‖_{K♭} = ‖x♯‖_K.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.valueGroup_eq` (characterisation): The value groups |K♭^×| and |K^×| coincide as subgroups of ℝ_{>0}.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.integerEquiv` (equivalence): K♭° ≃+* lim_Φ K°/ϖ for ϖ | p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.quotEquiv` (equivalence): K♭° ⧸ (ϖ♭) ≃+* K° ⧸ (ϖ).
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.residueFieldEquiv` (equivalence): The residue fields of K♭ and K are identified.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.equivMathlibTilt` (compatibility): tilt K ≃+* Tilt K v O hv p (Mathlib), restricting to (tilt K)° ≃+* PreTilt O p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.preTiltVal_eq` (compatibility): PreTilt.val K v O hv p x = v (PreTilt.untilt x) for x ∈ PreTilt O p.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.equivSelfOfCharP` (equivalence): If CharP K p then tilt K ≃+* K isometrically.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField.map` (functoriality): A continuous embedding of perfectoid fields induces an isometric embedding of tilts (P1/tilt-functoriality).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.tiltField_padicComplex_pflat` (computation): In tilt ℂ_p, p♭ = (p^{1/p^n})_n has ‖p♭‖ = ‖p‖ and ‖ε − 1‖ = ‖p‖^{p/(p−1)}.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField_equivMathlibTilt_test` (compatibility): For K = ℂ_p: tilt ℂ_p ≃+* Tilt ℂ_p v 𝒪_{ℂ_p} hv p and PreTilt.val corresponds to the absolute value of the tilt.
- `Perfectoid.tiltField_equivSelf_laurent` (degenerate): For K the completed perfection of F_p((t)), tilt K ≃+* K.
- `Perfectoid.preTilt_padicInt_trivial` (non-example): For ℚ_p (not perfectoid), PreTilt ℤ_p p = Perfection F_p p ≅ F_p and Mathlib's Tilt ℚ_p … p ≅ F_p carries the trivial valuation: without the perfectoid hypothesis the tilt is not a nonarchimedean field.

*Uses.*
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: O_C♭ = PreTilt O_C p, v♭(x) = v_p(x♯), Frac(O_C♭) = Tilt; ε and p♭.
- PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action: C♭ with its G_F-action through the action on C.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting: continuous valuations of K and K♭.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields, P3/fontaine-wintenberger: tilting finite extensions of perfectoid fields.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields: tilts of completed residue fields.
- Sch12 Lemma 3.4; Berkeley Remark 6.2.3; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.5.2: the construction in the sources.

*Acceptance.*
- For K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = (p, p^{1/p}, …) and t♯ = p.
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl, |(ε − 1)♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements: v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1)).

#### `continuous-valuations-under-tilting` — Continuous valuations of K and K♭ correspond (Sch12 Proposition 3.6)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field`.

For a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, |·| ↦ |·|♭, |x|♭ := |x♯|, is a bijection between continuous valuations of K up to equivalence and continuous valuations of K♭ up to equivalence (points of Spa(K, K°) ∪ … of higher rank included); it is the field case of the tilting homeomorphism P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- K perfectoid; continuity in Huber's sense (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont): continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m.

*Proof outline.*
- |·|♭ is a valuation: only the ultrametric inequality is nontrivial and follows from |x + y|♭ = lim |(x^{1/p^n})♯ + (y^{1/p^n})♯|^{p^n} ≤ max(|x♯|, |y♯|).
- Continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K+ ⊆ K°, which contain m, hence to valuation subrings of K°/m = K♭°/m♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting); this bijection is the one described.

*Acceptance.*
- The rank-one valuation of K maps to the rank-one valuation of K♭ of P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; higher-rank continuous valuations correspond to valuation subrings of the common residue field K°/m.

*Depends on:* `tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `mathlib:Valuation.IsEquiv`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 3.6, p. 17; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 3.6, proof, p. 17.

### P1.5 A_inf, primitive ideals and Fontaine's θ

For a perfectoid pair (R, R+) of characteristic p, A_inf = W(R+) is a strict p-ring, (p,[ϖ])-adically complete. Mathlib already defines θ as a ring homomorphism `WittVector.fontaineTheta` and proves `surjective_fontaineTheta`; this layer identifies it with ECD's θ and proves the kernel statement. Euclidean division by a primitive generator of ker θ gives prepared representatives, whose Gauss norm is the spectral gauge, and hence the approximation of every element by sharp elements, globally and at every point of the Gel'fand spectrum (`sharp-approximation-lemma`, Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.7, 2.6.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7).

#### `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring` — A_inf = W(R+) for a perfectoid pair of characteristic p: strict p-ring, (p,[ϖ])-adically complete

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Ainf`.

Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then R+ is perfect, ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free, and A_inf(R, R+) := W(R+) satisfies: (a) W(R+) is p-torsion free and p-adically complete with W(R+)/p = R+ (a strict p-ring; Mathlib WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP); (b) every element is uniquely Σ_{n≥0} p^n[x_n] with x_n ∈ R+; (c) [ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor, W(R+) is [ϖ]-adically and (p,[ϖ])-adically complete and separated, and W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ; (d) Σ p^n[x_n] is a unit iff x_0 is a unit of R+; (e) the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology does not depend on ϖ; (f) W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] is the ring W^b(R) of Witt vectors with bounded Teichmüller coordinates, independent of ϖ and of R+ up to the evident inclusions; (g) for every p-adically complete ring S and ring homomorphism R+ → S/p there is a unique ring homomorphism W(R+) → S lifting it; Frobenius W(Φ) is an automorphism.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- pR = 0 and R perfectoid, so R and R+ are perfect (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).

*Proof outline.*
- (a), (b), (g): R+ is perfect, so W(R+) is the strict p-ring with residue ring R+ (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.2.1, Corollary 2.2.6, Lemma 2.2.7; Mathlib WittVector, WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP).
- (c): [ϖ]·Σp^n[x_n] = Σp^n[ϖx_n] and ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R+ (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete (b)); completeness from W_r(ϖ^{p^{r−1}}R+) ⊆ [ϖ]W_r(R+) ⊆ W_r(ϖR+) and ϖ-completeness of R+ (BMS1 Lemma 3.2(ii); Bhatt Example 6.1.6).
- (d): reduction modulo p is R+ and W(R+) is p-adically complete; (e): two pseudo-uniformizers divide powers of each other in R+; (f): [ϖ]^{-n}Σp^m[x_m] = Σp^m[ϖ^{-n}x_m] (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.2, Remark 2.3.3).

*Acceptance.*
- For R = F the perfect field of anchor Layer 6 and R+ = 𝒪_F, this is the (p,[ϖ])-adic completeness of A_inf = W(𝒪_F) packaged in anchor Layer 6.1 (P1/anchor-layer-6-compatibility).
- For R+ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}, A_inf = W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) is (p,[p♭])-adically complete; Mathlib's BDeRhamPlus 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p is built on W(PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p) ≅ this ring.

*Depends on:* `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:Localization.Away`.

*Sources:* Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Example 6.1.6, p. 43; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.2(ii), p. 19; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.2.1, p. 51; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.2.10, p. 52; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.2.7, p. 52; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Remark 5.14, p. 25.

#### `primitive-degree-one-ideals` — Primitive (distinguished) elements and ideals of degree 1 in W(R+) (ECD Definition 3.15)

*definition.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Primitive`.

Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. An element ξ = Σ_{n≥0} p^n[ξ_n] ∈ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 (distinguished) if ξ_0 is topologically nilpotent and ξ_1 is a unit of R+; equivalently ξ = [ξ_0] + p·u with u ∈ W(R+)^× (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Definition 3.2.3). An ideal J ⊆ W(R+) is primitive of degree 1 if it is principal with a primitive generator. Equivalently (ECD Definition 3.15), J is generated by an element p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W(R+): every such element is primitive, and every primitive element is a unit multiple of one of this form, because a topologically nilpotent element of R+ is divisible by a pseudo-uniformizer (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2; Kedlaya AWS Exercise 2.3.6). ξ = p is primitive (ξ_0 = 0): it corresponds to the untilt R itself. In the notation of an untilt S, R = S♭ and R+ = S♭+.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- ξ_0 = 0 is allowed (Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.2.5); p² and [ϖ] are not primitive.

*Proof outline.*
- p + [ϖ]α = [ϖα_0] + p(1 + [ϖ]α') with α − [α_0] = pα'; 1 + [ϖ]α' is a unit because its reduction 1 + ϖα'_0 is a unit of the ϖ-adically complete R+ (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)).
- Conversely ξ = [ξ_0] + pu with u a unit: u^{-1}ξ = p + [ξ_0]u^{-1}, and ξ_0 = ϖc for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.2), so u^{-1}ξ = p + [ϖ]([c]u^{-1}).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive` (structure): For ξ : WittVector p R+: IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0 : R) ∧ IsUnit (ξ.coeff 1).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitiveIdeal` (structure): J : Ideal (WittVector p R+) with ∃ ξ, IsPrimitive ξ ∧ J = Ideal.span {ξ}.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.iff_teichmuller_add` (characterisation): IsPrimitive ξ ↔ ∃ u : (W R+)ˣ, ξ = teichmuller p (ξ.coeff 0) + p * u ∧ IsTopologicallyNilpotent (ξ.coeff 0).
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_add` (constructor): IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ → IsPrimitive (p + teichmuller p ϖ * α) for every α.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.exists_associated_p_add` (characterisation): IsPrimitive ξ → ∃ u unit, ϖ pseudo-uniformizer, α, ξ = u * (p + [ϖ] α).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.mul_unit` (other): Associates of primitive elements are primitive.
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.isUnit_of_eq_mul` (relation): IsPrimitive ξ → IsPrimitive ξ' → ξ' = y * ξ → IsUnit y (P1/distinguished-element-criterion).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.isRegular` (other): Primitive elements are nonzerodivisors (P1/distinguished-element-criterion).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.map` (functoriality): For a morphism of perfectoid pairs of characteristic p, WittVector.map f carries primitive elements to primitive elements, hence primitive ideals J to generators of J·W(R'+).
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p` (example): IsPrimitive (p : W R+) (coefficients (0, 1, 0, …)).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitive.frobenius` (other): φ(ξ) and φ^{-1}(ξ) are primitive (ξ_0^{p^{±1}} topologically nilpotent, ξ_1^{p^{±1}} a unit).
- `Perfectoid.IsPrimitiveIdeal.iff_distinguished` (compatibility): A generator of ker θ is primitive iff it is distinguished in the sense of BMS1 Remark 3.11 and of PerfectoidQuotients:Q0 (the conditions coincide).

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_sub_pflat` (computation): In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}), p − [p♭] = p + [p♭]·(−1) is primitive; so is Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p} (its image in W(F̄_p) is p).
- `Perfectoid.not_isPrimitive_p_sq` (non-example): p² is not primitive (its Witt coordinate ξ_1 is 0), and neither is [ϖ]; a definition requiring only ξ ∈ (p, [ϖ]) would accept them.
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_p_test` (degenerate): p is primitive, and the untilt along (p) is (R, R+) itself.
- `Perfectoid.isPrimitive_iff_associated_test` (characterisation): In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}), Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} is a unit multiple of an element p + [ϖ]α.

*Uses.*
- ECD Definition 3.15 and Theorem 3.17: untilts ↔ primitive ideals of degree 1.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel: ker θ is primitive, and any primitive element of ker θ generates it.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction, P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, P1/marked-untilt: the inverse construction and the classification.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: ξ primitive of degree one, congruent to p times a unit up to [ϖ]-multiples.
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta: w ∈ ker θ generates it iff its first Witt coordinate is a unit.
- PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings: distinguished generators of ker θ for integral perfectoid rings.
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: untilts of S as degree-one points of Y_S.

*Acceptance.*
- In W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): p − [p♭] and Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[ε]^{i/p} are primitive (Kedlaya AWS Examples 2.3.7–2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.5).

*Depends on:* `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:WittVector`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Definition 3.15, p. 17; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.3.4, p. 54; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Exercise 2.3.6, p. 54; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 3.2.3, p. 57; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 3.2.5, p. 57; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.2.2, p. 56; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Remark 3.11, p. 23.

#### `distinguished-element-criterion` — Primitive elements are nonzerodivisors and divide each other only up to units (ECD Lemma 3.16)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Primitive`.

Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. (a) Every primitive element ξ ∈ W(R+), in particular every p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer of R+ and α ∈ W(R+), is a nonzerodivisor (ECD Lemma 3.16; in ECD's notation α ∈ W(R♭+), the printed "W(R+)" being a misprint; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.10). (b) If ξ, ξ' are primitive and ξ' = yξ with y ∈ W(R+), then y is a unit (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.5); so two primitive elements generating comparable ideals are associate.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R+ perfect, ϖ-adically separated and ϖ-torsion free (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring).

*Proof outline.*
- (a) Reduce to ξ = p + [ϖ]α (P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals). If ξ·Σ_n[c_n]p^n = 0, then modulo [ϖ] this reads Σ[c_n]p^{n+1} ≡ 0, so all c_n ∈ ϖR+; divide all c_n by ϖ and induct; since R+ is ϖ-adically separated, all c_n vanish (ECD Lemma 3.16 proof).
- (b) Comparing Witt coordinates (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.2.8), ξ'_1 − y_0ξ_1 is topologically nilpotent; ξ_1, ξ'_1 are units, so y_0 is a unit of R+, and y is a unit (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)).

*Uses.*
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras: (a): the image of Scholze's ξ in W(R♭+), a primitive element, is a nonzerodivisor (RT-AREA-padic-2/21).

*Acceptance.*
- p − [p♭] ∈ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) is a nonzerodivisor (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).
- With p♭ a compatible system of p-power roots of p and ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, p − [p♭] and ξ_cyc = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} both generate ker θ in W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}); hence they are associates and each divides the other by a unit (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel; Scholze 2013 Lemma 6.3).
- Negative example: μ = [ε] − 1 = ([ε]^{1/p} − 1)·ξ_cyc lies in ker θ but does not generate it. The factor [ε]^{1/p} − 1 is not a unit: its zeroth Witt coefficient ε^{1/p} − 1 lies in the maximal ideal of 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭} (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (d)). Regularity of ξ_cyc implies (μ) is strictly smaller than (ξ_cyc), so μ is not primitive. Membership in ker θ alone does not imply primitivity.

*Depends on:* `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.16, p. 17; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.16, proof, p. 17; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.10, p. 46; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.5, p. 54; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i), p. 22.

#### `quotient-by-primitive-element` — W(R+)/ξ is [ϖ]-torsion free and [ϖ]-adically complete (the facts ECD Lemma 3.14 uses)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Primitive`.

Let ξ ∈ W(R+) be primitive, (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. Then A+ := W(R+)/ξ satisfies: (a) the image of [ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor; (b) A+ is [ϖ]-adically complete and separated, and its [ϖ]-adic and (p,[ϖ])-adic topologies coincide; (c) A+/[ϖ] ≅ W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ; (d) A+ is p-adically complete; (e) ξW(R+)[1/[ϖ]] ∩ W(R+) = ξW(R+). These are the two properties ECD Lemma 3.14 uses without proof ("W(R♭+)/ξ is [ϖ♭]-torsion free and [ϖ♭]-adically complete").

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- ξ primitive; by P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals we may take ξ = p + [ϖ]α.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) If [ϖ]x = ξy, then modulo p: ϖx_0 = ϖα_0y_0, so x_0 = α_0y_0 and x − αy = pz; then p[ϖ]z = [ϖ](x − αy) = ξy − [ϖ]αy = py, so y = [ϖ]z (W(R+) is p-torsion free) and x = ξz ([ϖ] is a nonzerodivisor, P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (c)). (e) is (a) iterated.
- (c) (ξ, [ϖ]) = (p, [ϖ]) since ξ ≡ p mod [ϖ]; W(R+)/(p,[ϖ]) = R+/ϖ.
- (b),(d) ξW(R+) is closed for the (p,[ϖ])-adic topology (by (a), ξW ∩ [ϖ]^nW = [ϖ]^nξW), so A+ is complete for the finitely generated ideal (p,[ϖ]); since p = ξ − [ϖ]α ∈ ([ϖ]) + (ξ), the topology on A+ is [ϖ]-adic; p-adic completeness follows as (p) ⊆ ([ϖ]) in A+ (Stacks Tag 090T).

*Acceptance.*
- For ξ = p − [p♭] in W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): W/ξ ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p} is p-torsion free and p-adically complete.
- For ξ = p: W(R+)/p = R+ is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free.

*Depends on:* `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `distinguished-element-criterion`, `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 18; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.2(ii), p. 19; Stacks-Project, Stacks Project, Tag 090T.

#### `fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib` — ECD's θ is Mathlib's WittVector.fontaineTheta; surjectivity from surjective_fontaineTheta

*comparison.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Mathlib`.

Let R be a nonzero perfectoid Tate ring and R+ a ring of integral elements. Mathlib's WittVector.fontaineTheta R+ p : 𝕎(PreTilt R+ p) →+* R+ (defined under [Fact ¬IsUnit (p : R+)] and [IsAdicComplete (span {p}) R+], both supplied by P1/integral-elements-adically-complete) corresponds, under R♭+ ≅ PreTilt R+ p (P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt), to ECD's θ: W(R♭+) → R+, Σ_n p^n[r_n] ↦ Σ_n p^n r_n♯. In particular θ([x]) = x♯ (WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller) and θ mod p is x ↦ x♯ mod p (WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta). Mathlib's surjective_fontaineTheta applies because Frobenius on R+/p is surjective (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring), so θ is surjective. θ is the unique ring homomorphism W(R♭+) → R+ lifting x ↦ x♯ mod p (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7, Definition 2.7.3). Mathlib's fontaineThetaInvertP and BDeRhamPlus R+ p are built on this θ.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R ≠ 0 and R perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*
- Both maps are ring homomorphisms W(R♭+) → R+ sending [x] to x♯ (Mathlib fontaineTheta_teichmuller with PreTilt.untilt = ♯, P1/tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt); a ring homomorphism out of the strict p-ring W(R♭+) into a p-adically complete ring is determined by its reduction mod p, which is x ↦ x♯ mod p for both (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7).
- Surjectivity: Mathlib surjective_fontaineTheta with hypothesis Function.Surjective (frobenius (ModP R+ p) p) from P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (a).
- ECD's check that θ is a ring map modulo ϖ^m through the m-th ghost map factoring over W(R+/ϖ) is Mathlib's construction fontaineThetaModPPow (ghost component factoring over W(R/p)).

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℂ_p: fontaineTheta sends [p♭] to p and [ε] to 1 (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).
- For R of characteristic p (R♭ = R): θ is reduction modulo p, W(R+) → R+ (Bhatt Proposition 6.1.8 proof).

*Depends on:* `tilt-comparison-with-mathlib-pretilt`, `frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:surjective_fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller`, `mathlib:WittVector.mk_fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:fontaineThetaInvertP`, `mathlib:BDeRhamPlus`, `mathlib:PreTilt.untilt`, `mathlib:WittVector.ghostComponent`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14(i), p. 17; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 17; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.7.3, p. 67; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 3.3.6, p. 59; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Definition 3.5, p. 21.

#### `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel` — Fontaine's θ: W(S♭+) → S+ is surjective with kernel generated by a primitive nonzerodivisor (ECD Lemma 3.14)

*theorem.* **Planet:** *Fontaine's map θ*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Theta`.

Let (S, S+) be a perfectoid Tate pair (any characteristic) with tilt (S♭, S♭+). (a) θ: W(S♭+) → S+, Σ[r_n]p^n ↦ Σ r_n♯p^n, is a surjective ring homomorphism (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib). (b) ker θ is generated by a primitive element of degree 1, which can be taken of the form ξ = p + [ϖ♭]α with ϖ♭ ∈ S♭+ a pseudo-uniformizer such that (ϖ♭♯)^p | p in S+, and α ∈ W(S♭+); ξ is a nonzerodivisor. (c) An element of ker θ generates ker θ iff it is primitive (BMS1 Remark 3.11). (d) θ extends to a surjection W(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]] → S with kernel ξW(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]], and W(S♭+)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = S♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ S+/ϖ♭♯. If pS = 0 then ker θ = (p). (ECD Lemma 3.14; Berkeley Lemma 6.2.8; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.5; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.6.3 in characteristic 0.)

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- (S, S+) perfectoid; no perfectoid base field.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib.
- Construction of ξ: choose ϖ♭ with compatible roots (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots) and ϖ := ϖ♭♯ with ϖ^p | p in S+ (P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); put α_0 := p/ϖ ∈ S+, choose β ∈ S♭+ with β♯ ≡ α_0 mod pS+ (P1/sharp-map, surjectivity of ♯ mod p on S+), so f := ϖ♭β has f♯ ≡ p mod pϖS+; write p = f♯ + pϖ Σ_n r_n♯p^n with r_n ∈ S♭+ (θ surjective) and put ξ := p − [f] − [ϖ♭]Σ_n[r_n]p^{n+1} ∈ ker θ, of the form p + [ϖ♭]α (ECD Lemma 3.14 proof).
- Generation: θ induces a surjection W(S♭+)/ξ → S+, which is an isomorphism modulo [ϖ♭] because W(S♭+)/(ξ, [ϖ♭]) = W(S♭+)/(p, [ϖ♭]) = S♭+/ϖ♭ ≅ S+/ϖ (P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting (b)); W(S♭+)/ξ is [ϖ♭]-torsion free and complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element) and S+ is ϖ-torsion free, so the map is an isomorphism (a surjection of such modules that is injective modulo ϖ has kernel in ⋂ϖ^n = 0).
- Nonzerodivisor: P1/distinguished-element-criterion (a). (c): a primitive ξ' ∈ ker θ is yξ with y a unit by P1/distinguished-element-criterion (b); a generator is associate to ξ, hence primitive.
- (d) Invert [ϖ♭], θ([ϖ♭]) = ϖ being a unit of S. Characteristic p: S♭ = S and θ is reduction mod p.

*Uses.*
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair, D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: kernel of θ generated by a primitive ξ.
- PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/bdr-plus-of-perfectoid-affinoid-algebras, R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta: surjectivity of θ and generation of ker θ by any primitive element ((a)–(c)), imported by R06.1 instead of re-proving the generation step of Scholze 2013, Lemma 6.3; R06.1 proves only that Scholze's ξ is a unit times p + [π]α, hence primitive (RT-AREA-padic-2/21).
- AInfCohomology:AI.0 (AI.0:integral): principality of ker θ with a nonzerodivisor primitive generator, specialized to O_C to identify ξ, through PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra; Mathlib lists it as a TODO (RT-AREA-padic-2/17).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals: the functor (S, S+) ↦ (S♭, S♭+, ker θ).

*Acceptance.*
- For S = ℂ_p: ker θ = (p − [p♭]), and Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} is another generator (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/explicit-generator-of-ker-theta).
- For S a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, ker θ = (p).

*Depends on:* `fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `distinguished-element-criterion`, `quotient-by-primitive-element`, `rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring`, `sharp-map`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14(ii), p. 17; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 18; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 18; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Lemma 3.14, proof, p. 18; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Lemma 6.2.8, proof, p. 46; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.7.5, p. 67; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 3.6.3, p. 88; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Remark 3.11, p. 23; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Proposition 6.1.8, p. 43.

#### `theta-kernel-base-change` — ker θ is compatible with base change: ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭+)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Theta`.

Let f: (R, R+) → (S, S+) be a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs with tilt f♭. Then θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R and ker θ_S = W(f♭)(ker θ_R)·W(S♭+); every generator ξ of ker θ_R maps to a generator of ker θ_S. For R = K a perfectoid field this is the statement that one ξ ∈ A_inf(K, K+) generates ker θ for every perfectoid (K, K+)-algebra (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- f continuous with f(R+) ⊆ S+.

*Proof outline.*
- θ_S ∘ W(f♭) and f ∘ θ_R are ring homomorphisms W(R♭+) → S+ agreeing on Teichmüller elements (θ_S([f♭x]) = (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), P1/tilt-functoriality), hence equal (P1/fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib, uniqueness); so W(f♭)(ξ) ∈ ker θ_S.
- W(f♭)(ξ) is primitive (IsPrimitive.map, P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals), hence generates ker θ_S (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c)).

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℂ_p and S = ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: ker θ_S = (p − [p♭]).
- For S = R/I a perfectoid quotient, ker θ_S is generated by the image of ξ.

*Depends on:* `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `tilt-functoriality`, `fontaine-theta-comparison-with-mathlib`.

*Sources:* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.17, p. 56; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Remark 3.11, p. 23.

#### `sharp-approximation-lemma` — Euclidean division by a primitive element and approximation by sharp elements (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.7, 2.6.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/EuclideanDivision`.

Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no base field), ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯, and |·| the spectral gauges |·|_ϖ of A and |·|_{ϖ♭} of A♭ (P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), so that |y♯| = |y| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp). Let z = [z̄_0] + p·z_1 (z_1 ∈ W(A♭°)^×) be a primitive generator of ker(θ: W(A♭°) → A°) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), extend θ to W^b(A♭) := W(A♭°)[1/[ϖ♭]] → A, and give W^b(A♭) the Gauss norm |Σ_n p^n[x_n]| := sup_n |x_n|. An element x = Σ_n p^n[x_n] is prepared if |x_0| ≥ |x_n| for all n ≥ 1. Then: (a) (Euclidean division) for x ∈ W^b(A♭) put x′ := p^{-1}(x − [x_0]) and r(x) := x − z_1^{-1}x′z = [x_0] − [z̄_0]z_1^{-1}x′; if x ∉ zW^b(A♭), the terms of the sequence x, r(x), r(r(x)), … are congruent to x modulo z and are prepared from some term on; no nonzero element of zW^b(A♭) is prepared; (b) (norms) |θ(x)| ≤ |x| for every x, with equality when x is prepared; hence the quotient norm of the Gauss norm on W^b(A♭)/(z) ≅ A is the spectral gauge, and |z̄_0| = |p| (|p| < 1, and |p| = 0 iff pA = 0); (c) (sharp approximation) for every a ∈ A there is y ∈ A♭ with |a − y♯| ≤ |p|·|a|, so |y| = |a|; for a ∈ A° one can take y ∈ A♭°; (d) (pointwise form) α ↦ α ∘ ♯ maps the Gel'fand spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms on (A, |·|) into M(A♭), and for every a ∈ A and ε > 0 there is y ∈ A♭ with α(a − y♯) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a), ε} for all α ∈ M(A) simultaneously; with |·| = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α (Berkovich; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21) this refines (c) up to ε; (e) (quasi-additivity of ♯) |(x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯| ≤ |p|·max{|x|, |y|} for x, y ∈ A♭.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- A perfectoid; z any primitive generator of ker θ (all differ by units of W(A♭°), P1/primitive-degree-one-ideals).
- Part (d) uses the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring and the maximum formula for the spectral seminorm, requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0; parts (a)–(c) and (e) do not.

*Proof outline.*
- Gauss norm: Witt vector arithmetic is homogeneous in the Teichmüller coordinates (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.2.8; Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.1.4), so the Gauss norm is ultrametric and submultiplicative, |p·w| = |w| (a shift of coordinates), |[c]w| ≤ |c||w|, and units of W(A♭°) have norm 1 (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring (b), (d), (f)). As |z̄_0| < 1, |zw| = |w| for all w (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.6.2).
- (a): r(x) ≡ x mod z by construction and |r(x) − [x_0]| ≤ |z̄_0||x|. If |r^{m+1}(x)| > |z̄_0||r^m(x)| for some m, the zeroth coordinate of r^{m+1}(x) carries its norm and r^{m+1}(x) is prepared, and so are all further terms; otherwise |r^m(x)| ≤ |z̄_0|^m|x| and the Euclidean quotients sum to q with x = qz. A nonzero prepared zw would satisfy |zw| = |w| ≥ |w_0| > |z̄_0w_0|, the norm of its zeroth coordinate, contradicting preparedness (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.6, 2.6.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(a)).
- (b): θ(Σp^n[x_n]) = Σp^n x_n♯ (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (a)), so |θ(x)| ≤ sup_n |x_n♯| = |x|. If x is prepared, θ(x) = x_0♯ + p·θ(x′) with |p·θ(x′)| ≤ |p||x_0| < |x_0| = |x_0♯| unless pA = 0, so |θ(x)| = |x|. Every class has a prepared representative by (a) (θ is surjective onto A, P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (d)), which gives the quotient norm (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.6.7, Corollary 2.6.10). θ(z) = 0 gives z̄_0♯ = −p·θ(z_1) with θ(z_1) a unit of A°, so |z̄_0| = |p| (the constant c := |z̄_0| of the proof of Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3).
- (c): for a prepared representative x of a, a − x_0♯ = p·θ(x′) with |θ(x′)| ≤ |x_0| = |a|; take y := x_0. If |a| ≤ 1 then |x_0| ≤ 1, so x_0 ∈ A♭° (gauge ≤ 1 characterises A♭°, P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots).
- (d): α ∘ ♯ is multiplicative, bounded by |·| on A♭, and ultrametric by continuity of α and the limit formula for the addition of A♭ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring). Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.2.7(b): after enough Euclidean steps the representative y of a satisfies β(y_n) ≤ max{ε, β(y_0)} for all β ∈ M(A♭) and n ≥ 1. For α ∈ M(A) and β = α ∘ ♯, α(a − y_0♯) ≤ sup_{n≥1} α(p)^n α(y_n♯) ≤ α(p)·max{ε, α(y_0♯)}; if α(y_0♯) > ε this bound is < α(y_0♯) (α(p) ≤ |p| < 1), so α(a) = α(y_0♯). The maximum formula is TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0 (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21).
- (e): choose q ∈ ℤ[1/p] with ϖ♭^{-q}x, ϖ♭^{-q}y ∈ A♭° and 2^{-q} arbitrarily close to max{|x|, |y|}; ♯ is multiplicative and (x′ + y′)♯ − x′♯ − y′♯ ∈ pA° for x′, y′ ∈ A♭° (P1/sharp-map), so (x + y)♯ − x♯ − y♯ ∈ ϖ^q·pA°, of gauge ≤ 2^{-q}|p|.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings: approximation of a lift of b^p by a sharp element at every point of the Gel'fand spectrum, (d) (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.5, (2.8.5.1)).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting: sharp approximation (c) and quasi-additivity (e) in the lifting argument of Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.6.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting: sharp approximation (c) transfers isometry from f♭ to f.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: prepared representatives compute the norm of the untilt B₀ (b).

*Acceptance.*
- A = ℂ_p, z = p − [p♭]: every a ∈ ℂ_p is y♯ up to |p||a|, i.e. O_{ℂ_p}/p ≅ O_{ℂ_p♭}/p♭ lifted along ♯; a − y♯ need not vanish.
- Characteristic p: z = p, z̄_0 = 0 and |p| = 0; r(x) = [x_0] is prepared after one step and a = y♯ exactly.
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3 ("only if", with c = |z̄_0|) and Lemmas 2.8.5–2.8.6 use (c)–(e): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings and P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting.

*Depends on:* `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`, `spectral-norm-under-sharp`, `pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `sharp-map`, `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:WittVector.teichmuller`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller`.

*Sources:* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.6.5, p. 64; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.6.9, p. 64; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.6.7, p. 64; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.3, proof, p. 70; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.5, proof, p. 70; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 1.5.21, p. 25; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.2.7(a), p. 57; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.2.7, proof, p. 57; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 3.3.18, proof of case (ii), p. 65.

### P1.6 Untilts and their classification

The converse construction W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/J is given with its topology and plus ring, proved perfectoid through the integral (BMS) route, and the classification of ECD 3.17 is proved in Tate generality (Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.8, Kedlaya AWS 2.3.9). Strict inclusions correspond under tilting (`strict-inclusions-under-tilting`, Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2), also when the target is only uniform: a map is strict iff it is isometric for the spectral gauges, and isometry passes between f and f♭ through the sharp map.

#### `untilt-construction` — The untilt of (R, R+) along a primitive ideal J: (W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R+)/J)

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt`.

Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p, J ⊆ W(R+) a primitive ideal of degree 1 and ϖ ∈ R+ a pseudo-uniformizer. The untilt of (R, R+) along J is the pair (A, A+) with A+ := W(R+)/J and A := A+[1/π], π the image of [ϖ], topologised so that A+ is open with its π-adic (equivalently (p,[ϖ])-adic) topology; equivalently A = W^b(R)/J·W^b(R) with W^b(R) = W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]. A is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer π and ring of definition A+, independent of ϖ; the construction is functorial for morphisms of pairs f with W(f)(J) ⊆ J' (then J' = W(f)(J)·W(R'+)), and comes with the multiplicative map ♯_J: R → A, x ↦ θ_J([x]) (θ_J the quotient map), with ♯_J(ϖ) = π. That (A, A+) is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R, R+) is P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- J primitive of degree 1; the choice of ϖ does not matter.

*Proof outline.*
- A+ is [ϖ]-torsion free and [ϖ]-adically complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element), so (A+, πA+) is a pair of definition of the complete Hausdorff Huber ring A = A+[1/π], and π is a topologically nilpotent unit.
- Independence of ϖ: two pseudo-uniformizers of R+ divide powers of each other.
- W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] = W^b(R): [ϖ]^{-n}Σp^m[x_m] = Σp^m[ϖ^{-n}x_m] (Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.2).
- Functoriality: W(f) induces the map; J' = W(f)(J)W(R'+) by P1/distinguished-element-criterion (b).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.untilt` (data): untilt (P : Pair R) (J) : Type — the ring A = W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] ⧸ J·W(R+)[1/[ϖ]], with a canonical choice-free description as W^b(R)/J W^b(R).
- `Perfectoid.untiltPlus` (data): The subring A+ = image of W(R+) ≅ W(R+) ⧸ J.
- `Perfectoid.untilt.instIsTateRing` (instance): IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space and NonarchimedeanRing instances, with pair of definition (A+, πA+).
- `Perfectoid.untilt.mk` (projection): θ_J : W(R+)[1/[ϖ]] →+* untilt P J, surjective, kernel J·W(R+)[1/[ϖ]].
- `Perfectoid.untilt.sharp` (data): sharp_J : R →* untilt P J, x ↦ θ_J([x]); continuous and multiplicative; sharp_J ϖ is a pseudo-uniformizer.
- `Perfectoid.untilt.quotEquiv` (characterisation): untiltPlus ⧸ (sharp_J ϖ) ≃+* R+ ⧸ (ϖ).
- `Perfectoid.untilt.map` (functoriality): A morphism of triples induces a continuous ring homomorphism of untilts; map_id, map_comp.
- `Perfectoid.untilt.congr_pseudoUniformizer` (other): Canonical isomorphism between the constructions for two choices of ϖ.
- `Perfectoid.untilt.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): The untilt is perfectoid with ring of integral elements untiltPlus (P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair).
- `Perfectoid.untilt.tiltEquiv` (equivalence): tilt (untilt P J) ≃+* R, identifying the plus rings and ker θ with J (P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair).
- `Perfectoid.untilt.equivSelf` (example): untilt P (span {p}) ≃+* R.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.untilt_p` (degenerate): untilt (R, R+) (span {p}) ≅ R as topological rings, with untiltPlus = R+.
- `Perfectoid.untilt_pflat` (computation): For R = the completed perfection of F_p((t)) and J = span {p − [t]}: the untilt is the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) with sharp_J t = p.
- `Perfectoid.untilt_cyclotomic` (computation): For J = span {Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}} the untilt is ℚ_p^cycl (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.8).
- `Perfectoid.untilt_not_primitive` (non-example): For J = span {p²} (not primitive) the analogous quotient W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/(p²) is not reduced (p ≠ 0 = p²), hence not perfectoid.
- `Perfectoid.untilt_quotEquiv_test` (characterisation): For J = span {p − [p♭]} ⊆ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): untiltPlus/(p^{…}) ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}/p♭ ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p}/p.

*Uses.*
- ECD Theorem 3.17; Berkeley Theorem 6.2.11; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.3.9: the inverse functor of the classification.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: R♯ = W(R+)/ξ with ϖ♯ inverted.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair: untilts of affinoid perfectoid spaces.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt: the inverse functor T ↦ untilt along J_R W(T+).
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: untilts of S parametrise points of Y_S.
- Sch12 Remark 5.19: the converse functor over a perfectoid field.

*Acceptance.*
- J = (p) returns (R, R+) (Berkeley Lemma 6.2.8 remark).
- For R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, J = (p − [t]) gives the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7).

*Depends on:* `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `quotient-by-primitive-element`, `distinguished-element-criterion`, `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`, `mathlib:Localization.Away`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Theorem 3.17, p. 18; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Theorem 6.2.11, p. 47; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.3.9, p. 55; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.3, p. 54; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Remark 5.19, p. 27.

#### `untilt-tilt-identification` — The tilt of W(R+)/J is R+, and θ for W(R+)/J is the quotient map

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt`.

In the situation of P1/untilt-construction, let A+ = W(R+)/J and θ_J: W(R+) → A+ the quotient map. Then (a) A+/p ≅ R+/ξ_0R+ for a generator ξ (ξ_0 its zeroth Witt coordinate), Frobenius on A+/p is surjective, and x ↦ (θ_J([x^{1/p^n}]))_n is a multiplicative bijection R+ → lim_{x↦x^p} A+ whose composite with reduction is a ring isomorphism R+ ≅ lim_Φ A+/p = PreTilt A+ p; (b) under this identification Mathlib's θ for A+ (WittVector.fontaineTheta A+ p) is θ_J, so ker θ_{A+} = J; (c) R = R+[1/ϖ] ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A as monoids (Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.3.7; Kedlaya AWS Definition 2.3.14: ♯ = θ ∘ [·]).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- J = ξW(R+) primitive; A+ is p-adically complete (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element (d)).

*Proof outline.*
- (a) W(R+)/(ξ, p) = R+/ξ_0 with ξ_0 topologically nilpotent; lim_Φ R+/ξ_0 = R+ because R+ is perfect and ξ_0-adically complete (ξ_0 ∈ ϖ'R+ for a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ', Stacks Tag 090T; Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.4.2); Frobenius on R+/ξ_0 is surjective.
- lim_{x↦x^p} A+ ≅ lim_Φ A+/p multiplicatively (Mathlib Perfection.quotientMulEquiv for the p-adically complete A+), and the composite of x ↦ (θ_J[x^{1/p^n}])_n with it is x ↦ (x^{1/p^n} mod ξ_0)_n, the isomorphism R+ ≅ lim_Φ R+/ξ_0.
- (b) θ_J and Mathlib's θ for A+ are ring maps W(R+) → A+ with [x] ↦ θ_J([x]) = x♯; uniqueness (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.2.7) gives equality. (c) invert ϖ and π = θ_J([ϖ]).

*Acceptance.*
- For J = (p): A+ = R+ and the identification is the identity.
- For J = (p − [p♭]) ⊆ W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}): A+ = 𝒪_{ℂ_p} and this is PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p ≅ 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}.

*Depends on:* `untilt-construction`, `quotient-by-primitive-element`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`, `mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `mathlib:PreTilt`.

*Sources:* KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.3.7, p. 60; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Remark 3.3.9, p. 60; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Definition 2.3.14, p. 56; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.16, p. 56; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 3.4.2, p. 79.

#### `untilt-is-perfectoid-pair` — The untilt along a primitive ideal is a perfectoid Tate pair with tilt (R, R+) (converse construction of ECD 3.17)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt`.

For (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and J ⊆ W(R+) primitive of degree 1, the untilt (A, A+) of P1/untilt-construction is a perfectoid Tate pair: A is a perfectoid Tate ring, A+ = W(R+)/J is a ring of integral elements of A (open, integrally closed, contained in A°), A°/A+ is almost zero, and the identification R+ ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} A+ of P1/untilt-tilt-identification extends to an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (R, R+) ≅ (A♭, A♭+) under which ker θ_A = J (Kedlaya AWS Lemmas 2.6.14 and 2.7.9; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.8; the converse functor of ECD Theorem 3.17 and Berkeley Theorem 6.2.11 "with its topology and plus ring").

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- J primitive.

*Proof outline.*
- A+ is integral perfectoid: π-adically complete and π-torsion free for π := θ_J([ϖ^{1/p}]) (P1/quotient-by-primitive-element), π^p | p (p = ξ − [ϖ]α maps to −θ_J([ϖ])θ_J(α)), Frobenius surjective on A+/p, and θ for A+ has principal kernel J (P1/untilt-tilt-identification (b)); Φ: A+/π → A+/π^p is bijective by BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i).
- By P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid, A = A+[1/π] is a perfectoid Tate ring with A+ ⊆ A° and πA° ⊆ A+ (A°/A+ almost zero).
- Tilt: A♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} A ≅ R compatibly with the ring structures (P1/untilt-tilt-identification (a), (c); the ring structure of A♭ is transported from lim_Φ A+/π, which is R+ as a ring), and ker θ_A = J.
- A+ is a ring of integral elements: it is open (it contains πA°) and it is the preimage of its image in A°/π ≅ A♭°/ϖ ≅ R°/ϖ, which is R+/ϖ, integrally closed in R°/ϖ; so A+ is the ring of integral elements corresponding to R+ under P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.

*Acceptance.*
- (the completed perfection of F_p((t)), J = (p − [t])) gives (ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7).
- J = (p) returns (R, R+).

*Depends on:* `untilt-construction`, `untilt-tilt-identification`, `perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`, `quotient-by-primitive-element`, `rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`.

*Sources:* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.3.9, p. 55; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Theorem 3.3.8, p. 60; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD before Theorem 3.17, p. 18; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Lemma 3.21, p. 27.

#### `untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals` — Untilts are classified by primitive ideals of degree 1 (ECD Theorem 3.17)

*theorem.* **Planet:** *Untilts and primitive ideals*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt`.

(ECD Theorem 3.17; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.8; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.3.9; Berkeley Theorem 6.2.11) The functors (S, S+) ↦ (S♭, S♭+, ker θ_S) and (R, R+, J) ↦ (W(R+)[1/[ϖ]]/J, W(R+)/J) are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between (i) perfectoid Tate pairs (S, S+) with morphisms of Huber pairs and (ii) triples (R, R+, J) with (R, R+) a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p and J ⊆ W(R+) primitive of degree 1, a morphism being a morphism f of pairs with W(f)(J) ⊆ J' (then J' = W(f)(J)W(R'+)). The unit is induced by θ_S: W(S♭+)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ker θ ≅ S, the counit is the identification of P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair, and both are natural. Characteristic-p pairs correspond to J = (p).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- No perfectoid base field; both characteristics.

*Proof outline.*
- Forward functor: P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, P1/tilt-functoriality; ker θ is primitive (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel) and morphisms respect kernels (P1/theta-kernel-base-change).
- Backward functor: P1/untilt-construction and P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.
- Unit: θ_S induces W(S♭+)/ker θ ≅ S+ and, after inverting [ϖ♭], S, compatibly with topologies and plus rings (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (d)). Counit: P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair.
- Naturality: θ is natural (θ_S ∘ W(f♭) = f ∘ θ_R, P1/theta-kernel-base-change).

*Uses.*
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair, D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: untilts of X ∈ Perf and their descent.
- DiamondSixOperations:S5; FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F1: Spd ℤ_p as the functor of untilts.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt: restriction to slice categories gives the tilting equivalence.

*Acceptance.*
- For (K♭, K♭°) with K a perfectoid field and J = ker θ, the construction returns (K, K°).
- Over F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: J = (p) gives the field itself, J = (p − [t]) the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), J = (Σ_{i<p}[1+t]^{i/p}) the field ℚ_p^cycl; φ(J) gives Frobenius-twisted markings.

#### `marked-untilt` — Marked untilts of a perfectoid pair of characteristic p

*definition.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt`.

Let (R, R+) be a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p. A marked untilt of (R, R+) is a triple (S, S+, ι) with (S, S+) a perfectoid Tate pair and ι: (S♭, S♭+) ≅ (R, R+) an isomorphism of Huber pairs; a morphism (S, S+, ι) → (S', S'+, ι') is a morphism f of Huber pairs with ι' ∘ f♭ = ι. By P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, (S, S+, ι) ↦ W(ι)(ker θ_S) is an equivalence from marked untilts to the discrete category of primitive ideals J ⊆ W(R+): a marked untilt has no nontrivial automorphisms and isomorphic marked untilts are uniquely isomorphic. Marked untilts pull back along morphisms of pairs (R, R+) → (R', R'+) (J ↦ J·W(R'+)); marked untilts of (R, R+) and of (R, R°) correspond (plus rings correspond, P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting); pS = 0 iff J = (p), the marked untilt (R, R+, id).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- (R, R+) of characteristic p; the marking ι is part of the data.

*Proof outline.*
- Equivalence: fully faithful because morphisms of untilts over (R, R+) are determined by their tilts (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals); the primitive ideal is an invariant, and ofPrimitive realises every J.
- No automorphisms: an automorphism of (S, S+, ι) has f♭ = id, hence f = id.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt` (structure): MarkedUntilt (P : Pair R): a perfectoid Tate ring S with instances, a ring of integral elements S+, and ι : (Pair.tilt (S, S+)) ≅ P as Huber pairs.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.Hom` (structure): Morphisms: Pair.Hom f with ι' ∘ Pair.tiltHom f = ι; Category instance.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.primitiveIdeal` (data): W(ι)(ker θ_S), a primitive ideal of W(R+) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel).
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.ofPrimitive` (constructor): J ↦ (untilt P J, untiltPlus, tiltEquiv) (P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair).
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.primitiveIdeal_ofPrimitive` (simp): primitiveIdeal (ofPrimitive J) = J.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.equivPrimitive` (equivalence): Isomorphism classes of marked untilts ≃ {J : IsPrimitiveIdeal J}.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.subsingleton_hom` (characterisation): Subsingleton (X ⟶ Y); in particular Unique (Aut X).
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.pullback` (functoriality): For a morphism of pairs P → P' of characteristic p: MarkedUntilt P → MarkedUntilt P', J ↦ J W(R'+), compatible with id and comp up to unique isomorphism.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.self` (example): The characteristic-p untilt (R, R+, id) with primitiveIdeal = span {p}.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.plusEquiv` (compatibility): MarkedUntilt (R, R+) ≃ MarkedUntilt (R, R°) by changing plus rings along P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.charP_iff` (characterisation): CharP S p ↔ primitiveIdeal = span {p}.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.self_primitiveIdeal` (degenerate): primitiveIdeal (MarkedUntilt.self P) = span {p}.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.padicComplex_primitiveIdeal` (computation): For P = (ℂ_p♭, 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) and the canonical marking of ℂ_p: primitiveIdeal = span {p − [p♭]}.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.aut_trivial` (characterisation): Every automorphism of a marked untilt is the identity.
- `Perfectoid.MarkedUntilt.frobenius_twist_ne` (non-example): For the marked untilt (ℂ_p, ι), the marking φ_R ∘ ι gives primitive ideal φ(J) ≠ J, so (ℂ_p, ι) and (ℂ_p, φ ∘ ι) are non-isomorphic marked untilts with isomorphic underlying rings: the marking cannot be dropped.

*Uses.*
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair: Spd ℤ_p(X) = isomorphism classes of (X♯, ι); marked untilts have no automorphisms, so these are sheaves not stacks.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers: untilt of X whose pullback to Y is Y♯.
- DiamondSixOperations:S5; FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F1: Spd ℤ_p and its products.
- RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0: untilts as points.
- Berkeley Lemma 6.2.8: the definition of an untilt of (R, R+).

*Acceptance.*
- (ℂ_p, 𝒪_{ℂ_p}, can) is the marked untilt of (ℂ_p♭, 𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) with ideal (p − [p♭]).
