#### `strict-inclusions-under-tilting` — Strict inclusions correspond under tilting (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/StrictInclusion`.

A continuous ring homomorphism f: A → B of complete Hausdorff Tate rings is a strict inclusion if it is injective and a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology (equivalently, as A is complete, a topological ring isomorphism onto a closed subring). Let A be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯, and f: A → B continuous. (a) If B is a perfectoid Tate ring, f is a strict inclusion if and only if f♭: A♭ → B♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality) is (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2). (b) More generally, let B be a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and B♭ its tilt (P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring; f(ϖ) = (f♭ϖ♭)♯ has compatible roots and f(ϖ)^p | p in B°). For the spectral gauges |·|_ϖ, |·|_{f(ϖ)}, |·|_{ϖ♭}, |·|_{f♭ϖ♭}: f is a strict inclusion iff |f(a)| = |a| for all a ∈ A; f♭ is a strict inclusion iff it is isometric; and f is a strict inclusion iff f♭ is. The analogous statement for injections that are not strict is Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.9.13 and is not part of this node.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- A perfectoid; in (b) B only complete, Hausdorff and uniform (p is topologically nilpotent in B because it is in A).
- Strictness is a topological condition; injectivity alone does not suffice (acceptance).

*Proof outline.*
- Strict ⇔ isometric: f(A°) ⊆ B° (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) gives |f(a)| ≤ |a|. If f is a strict inclusion, {a : f(a) ∈ B°} is bounded in A, so it lies in ϖ^{-N}A° and |a| ≤ 2^N|f(a)|; applied to a^{p^n} with power-multiplicativity (P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion (a)) this gives |a| ≤ 2^{N/p^n}|f(a)| for all n, so |a| ≤ |f(a)|. Conversely an isometry is injective and a homeomorphism onto its image, because the gauges define the topologies. The same applies to f♭ between the perfect uniform Tate rings A♭ and B♭.
- f isometric ⇒ f♭ isometric: |f♭(x)| = |(f♭x)♯| = |f(x♯)| = |x♯| = |x| (P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp for A; P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c) for B; (f♭x)♯ = f(x♯), P1/tilt-functoriality and P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (d)). This is the direction "obvious from the definition of A♭ as a topological space" in Kedlaya's proof.
- f♭ isometric ⇒ f isometric: for a ≠ 0 take y ∈ A♭ with |a − y♯| ≤ |p||a| (P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c)). If pA = 0 then a = y♯ and |f(a)| = |f♭(y)| = |y| = |a|. Otherwise |y| = |a|, |f(y♯)| = |f♭(y)| = |a|, and |f(a) − f(y♯)| ≤ |a − y♯| < |a|, so |f(a)| = |a|.
- Kedlaya's proof of ⇐ in (a) untilts instead: A = W^b(A♭)/(z) and B = W^b(B♭)/(z) for a primitive generator z of ker θ_A (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, P1/theta-kernel-base-change), and zW(B♭⁺) ∩ W(A♭⁺) = zW(A♭⁺) by [z̄_0]-adic successive approximation (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.1; its second displayed equality has a misprint, recorded in sourceIssues). The gauge argument above covers the uniform target of (b), which the untilting argument does not.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion: B₀ → B is a strict inclusion (isometric) because B₀♭ → B♭ is, with B only uniform, (b).
- Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3(b), Lemma 2.8.4: density and strictness transported between a perfectoid ring and its tilt.

*Acceptance.*
- A finite extension K ⊆ L of perfectoid fields is a strict inclusion, and so is K♭ ⊆ L♭ (absolute values extend).
- Non-example of strictness: for a perfectoid field K, the continuous injection K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{1/p^n} ↦ (ϖT)^{1/p^n}, is not strict (|T^N| = 1 while |(ϖT)^N| = 2^{-N}), and its tilt T ↦ ϖ♭T is not strict either.
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4: the untilt B₀ of the closure of f♭(A♭) maps to a uniform B by a strict inclusion because B₀♭ → B♭ is one, by (b) (P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion).

*Sources:* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.4.2, p. 57; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Theorem 2.4.2, proof, p. 57; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.1, p. 69; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.1, p. 69; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Lemma 2.8.4, proof, p. 70; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.3.23, p. 66.

### P1.7 The tilting equivalence and its almost-integral form

Over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring R the tilting equivalence is the restriction of the untilt classification to slice categories. Its almost-integral form R-Perf ≃ R°a-Perf ≃ (R°a/ϖ)-Perf, used by DiamondsAndVStacks D3, is proved by tilting to characteristic p, where perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ♭ lift by the inverse limit along Frobenius; the deformation-theoretic proof of Sch12 is kept for the flat subcategories. Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings (ring of definition the completed colimit of the R_j°) are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with them (`completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings`, Bhatt Remark 6.2.9, Sch12 Theorem 5.2), because reduction modulo ϖ determines a perfectoid algebra and commutes with filtered colimits.

#### `almost-integral-dictionary` — Perfectoid R-algebras are equivalent to perfectoid R°a-algebras (Sch12 §5, over an arbitrary perfectoid base)

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/AlmostDictionary`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, and (R°, R°°) its almost setup (P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). Call an R°a-algebra A perfectoid if A_* (P0 almost elements) is ϖ-torsion free, A is ϖ-adically complete, and Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} → A/ϖ is an isomorphism; for R = K a perfectoid field, ϖ-torsion freeness is flatness over K°a and this is Sch12 Definition 5.1(ii). Then: (a) for a ϖ-torsion-free R°-module N, (N^a)_* = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : ϖ^{1/p^n}x ∈ N for all n}; for M with M_* ϖ-torsion free and q ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}: (ϖ^qM)_* = ϖ^qM_*, M_*/ϖ^qM_* ⊆ (M/ϖ^qM)_* and every ε ∈ R°° maps (M/ϖ^qM)_* into M_*/ϖ^qM_*, and M is ϖ-adically complete iff M_* is (Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii)–(iv)); (b) for a perfectoid R-algebra S, S°a is a perfectoid R°a-algebra and Φ: S°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ S°/ϖ (Sch12 Proposition 5.5); (c) for a perfectoid R°a-algebra A, S := A_*[1/ϖ] with A_* open and ϖ-adic is a perfectoid R-algebra with S° = A_* and Φ: A_*/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A_*/ϖ (Sch12 Lemmas 5.6–5.7); (d) S ↦ S°a and A ↦ A_*[1/ϖ] are inverse equivalences R-Perf ≃ R°a-Perf.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Over a general base R°, flatness over R°a is not the right condition (perfectoid quotients R → R/I are not flat); ϖ-torsion freeness of A_* replaces it, and coincides with flatness when R° is a valuation ring.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) (N^a)_* = Hom(R°°, N) = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : εx ∈ N ∀ε ∈ R°°} with R°° = ⋃ϖ^{1/p^n}R° (P1/topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal); (ϖ^qM)_* = ϖ^qM_* as ϖ^qM_* is ϖ-torsion free; left exactness of (·)_* (right adjoint of (·)^a, P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints) gives the inclusion, and the ε-image statement is Sch12 Lemma 5.3(iii)'s argument; completeness transfer: (·)_* and (·)^a commute with inverse limits (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
- (b) Φ is surjective on S°/ϖ^{1/p} → S°/ϖ (P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion) and injective: x^p/ϖ power-bounded ⇒ x/ϖ^{1/p} power-bounded (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (a)); S° is ϖ-complete and ϖ-torsion free (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete); apply (a).
- (c) Sch12 Lemma 5.7: x ∈ S, x^p ∈ A_* ⇒ x ∈ A_*, by descending induction with ϖ^{k/p}x, using injectivity of Φ on A_* and ϖ-torsion freeness. Sch12 Lemma 5.6: a power-bounded x has (εx)^{p^N} ∈ A_* for large N, so εx ∈ A_* for all ε ∈ R°°, so x ∈ A_* by (a); Φ surjective on A_*/ϖ: from almost surjectivity ϖ^{1/p}x ≡ y^p mod ϖA_*, z := y/ϖ^{1/p²} satisfies z^p ≡ x mod ϖ^{(p−1)/p}A_*, z ∈ A_* by Lemma 5.7. S is uniform (S° = A_* bounded) and perfectoid.
- (d) The two constructions are inverse by (b), (c) and A = (A_*)^a.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over a perfectoid field, R° is the ϖ-adic completion of K°[T^{1/p^∞}] and R°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra (Sch12 Proposition 5.20).
- The non-surjectivity of M_*/xM_* → (M/xM)_* (Sch12 Remark 5.4) shows that (a) cannot be strengthened to an equality.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-almost-setup`, `topologically-nilpotent-elements-as-root-ideal`, `integral-elements-adically-complete`, `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `frobenius-surjectivity-criterion`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.6, p. 23; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.7, p. 23; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii), p. 22; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 5.3(i), p. 22; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 5.5, proof, p. 23.

#### `cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi` — Frobenius criterion for vanishing of the (almost) cotangent complex; perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Cotangent`.

(a) (Gabber–Ramero, arXiv Lemma 6.5.9(i) = LNM 1800 Lemma 6.5.13(i); Sch12 Proposition 5.13(ii); Bhatt Proposition 6.1.4) Let A_0 → B be a map of F_p-algebras such that the relative Frobenius A_0(Φ) ⊗^L_{A_0} B → B(Φ) is an isomorphism in D(A_0). Then L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0. In particular L_{B/F_p} ≃ 0 for B perfect, and L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0 whenever A_0 → B is flat and relatively perfect. (b) The almost version holds over any basic setup (V, m) with V an F_p-algebra: if the relative Frobenius of a map of almost algebras is an isomorphism in the almost derived category, then the almost cotangent complex L^a (P0/almost-cotangent-complex) vanishes. (c) Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ with compatible roots, and A a (R°/ϖ)^a-algebra which is (almost) flat over (R°/ϖ)^a with Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A. Then L^a_{A/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0. For R = K a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Corollary 5.16.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- OPTIONAL ALTERNATIVE ROUTE (Scholze 2012's deformation-theoretic proof). No node of this packet needs it: the tilting equivalence (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) and the mod-ϖ equivalence (P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence) are derived from P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals. Keep the node and its sources, but do not schedule it as a prerequisite (RT-AREA-padic-1/5).
- The hypothesis in (a) is on the derived relative Frobenius, not on Ω¹ alone.
- The classical cotangent complex, its simplicial description, transitivity and Tor-independent base change are requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0; the almost version is P0/almost-cotangent-complex.

*Proof outline.*
- (a) Take a simplicial resolution P• of B by free A_0-algebras; the relative Frobenius A_0(Φ) ⊗_{A_0} P• → P•(Φ) sends X_i ↦ X_i^p and is by hypothesis a quasi-isomorphism of simplicial A_0(Φ)-algebras, hence induces A_0(Φ) ⊗^L L_{B/A_0} ≃ L_{B(Φ)/A_0(Φ)} ≃ L_{B/A_0}; on differentials it sends dX_i ↦ d(X_i^p) = 0, so the isomorphism is the zero map and L_{B/A_0} ≃ 0 (GR Lemma 6.5.9 proof; Sch12 Proposition 5.13 proof).
- (b) The same argument with almost algebras (Sch12 before Corollary 5.16, "the previous theorems stay true in the almost world"), or apply (a) to B_!! as in Sch12 Corollary 5.16 proof.
- (c) A_0 := R°/ϖ is an F_p-algebra (ϖ | p); A_0(Φ) ≅ R°/ϖ^{1/p} as A_0-module via Φ: R°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ R°/ϖ; by flatness A_0(Φ) ⊗^L A = A/ϖ^{1/p}, and the relative Frobenius is the given isomorphism Φ; apply (b).

*Acceptance.*
- Ω¹_{R/F_p} = 0 for perfect R, since dx = d(y^p) = py^{p−1}dy = 0 (Sch12 Remark 5.14); the degree 0 and 1 parts are Mathlib's KaehlerDifferential and Algebra.H1Cotangent, which vanish for perfect R.
- W(R) is the unique flat p-adically complete deformation of a perfect R (Sch12 Remark 5.14; Bhatt Example 6.1.6).

*Depends on:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `perfectoid-almost-setup`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `mathlib:KaehlerDifferential`, `mathlib:Algebra.H1Cotangent`.

#### `deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras` — Unique flat deformation of perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ (Sch12 Theorem 5.10, over a perfectoid Tate base)

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Cotangent`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots. Reduction modulo ϖ, A ↦ A/ϖ, is an equivalence between (i) ϖ-adically complete R°a-algebras A that are (almost) flat over R°a with Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ, and (ii) (almost) flat (R°/ϖ)^a-algebras B with Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B. Concretely B lifts uniquely, through the square-zero extensions (R°/ϖ^n)^a → (R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, to a compatible system of flat (R°/ϖ^n)^a-algebras B_n with B_n/ϖ^{n−1} ≅ B_{n−1}, and A = lim B_n. For R = K a perfectoid field every perfectoid K°a-algebra is flat and this is Sch12 Theorem 5.10, the step K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf of Sch12 Theorem 5.2. Over a general base the flat objects form full subcategories; the full categories are compared, without deformation theory, in P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- OPTIONAL ALTERNATIVE ROUTE (Scholze 2012's deformation-theoretic proof). No node of this packet needs it: the tilting equivalence (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) and the mod-ϖ equivalence (P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence) are derived from P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals. Keep the node and its sources, but do not schedule it as a prerequisite (RT-AREA-padic-1/5).
- Flatness is over R°a (resp. (R°/ϖ)^a); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R° and ϖ^{n−1}R°/ϖ^nR° ≅ R°/ϖ is square-zero in R°/ϖ^n for n ≥ 2.
- Illusie–Gabber–Ramero deformation theory (obstructions in Ext², torsor under Ext¹, automorphisms Hom; lifting of morphisms) in the almost setting is P0/almost-deformation-theory.

*Proof outline.*
- L^a_{B/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0 (P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi (c)).
- For a flat lift B_{n−1} over (R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a, flat base change gives L^a_{B_{n−1}/(R°/ϖ^{n−1})^a} ⊗^L (R°/ϖ)^a ≃ L^a_{B/(R°/ϖ)^a} ≃ 0, so L^a_{B_{n−1}} ≃ 0 by derived Nakayama for the nilpotent ideal (Bhatt Corollary 6.1.5; Sch12 Theorem 5.10 proof via the transitivity triangle for 0 → B → B_n → B_{n−1} → 0).
- All obstructions and ambiguities for lifting B_{n−1} to a flat (R°/ϖ^n)^a-algebra, and for lifting morphisms, lie in Ext groups of this vanishing complex (P0/almost-deformation-theory; Sch12 Theorems 5.11–5.12), so lifts exist and are unique up to unique isomorphism.
- A := lim B_n is ϖ-adically complete with A/ϖ^n = B_n, flat, and Φ: A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ is inherited from B (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

*Acceptance.*
- Sch12 Proposition 5.20: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ have the same reduction (K°/ϖ)[T^{1/p^∞}] and are therefore tilts of each other.
- Uniqueness: two flat deformations with the same reduction are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the reduction.

*Depends on:* `cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-deformation-theory`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cotangent-complex`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `perfectoid-almost-setup`, `exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Theorem 5.10, p. 24; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Theorem 5.10, proof, p. 26; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Theorem 5.11, p. 24; gr-almost, Gabber–Ramero arXiv v3, Corollary 3.2.11(i), p. 42; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Corollary 6.1.5, p. 42; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Theorem 6.1.3, p. 42; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, proof of Theorem 6.2.10, p. 48.

#### `frobenius-inverse-limit-lifting-in-characteristic-p` — In characteristic p, perfectoid algebras modulo ϖ lift explicitly by the inverse limit along Frobenius

*lemma.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/AlmostDictionary`.

Let T be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, t = (t♭)♯ a pseudo-uniformizer (its p-power roots are unique) and (T°, T°°) its almost setup. Let Λ := F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) with x ↦ t. (a) For a (T°/t)^a-algebra B that is flat over Λ (equivalently, for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] ∩ (0, 1), the kernel of t^q on B_* is t^{1−q}B_* up to almost zero) with Φ: B/t^{1/p} → B an isomorphism, the inverse limit B̃ := lim_Φ B (in almost T°a-algebras) is perfect, t-adically complete and t-torsion free with B̃/t ≅ B; (b) conversely lim_Φ(B̃/t) ≅ B̃ for such B̃; (c) hence reduction mod t is an equivalence between perfect, t-adically complete, t-torsion-free T°a-algebras (the perfectoid T°a-algebras, Bhatt Example 6.2.4(1)) and Λ-flat (T°/t)^a-algebras with Φ: B/t^{1/p} ≅ B; (d) with P1/almost-integral-dictionary, T-Perf ≃ these categories (Sch12 Remark 5.18: the lifting "can be made explicit by means of the inverse limit over the Frobenius").

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- pT = 0; Λ-flatness replaces flatness over (T°/t)^a, which fails for quotients.

*Proof outline.*
- (b) For B̃ perfect and t-adically complete, lim_Φ B̃/t = lim_{x↦x^p} B̃ = B̃ (Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 3.4.2 and Remark 3.4.10; Mathlib Perfection.quotientMulEquiv, the ring structures agreeing as p = 0).
- (a) The transition maps Φ: B → B are surjective with kernel t^{1/p}B (Φ factors through B/t^{1/p} ≅ B), so B̃ → B is surjective; its kernel is {(b_n) : b_0 = 0}, and Λ-flatness gives unique compatible b_n/t^{1/p^n} (well defined modulo t^{1−1/p^n}B, whose p-th powers vanish), so the kernel is t♭B̃; t-torsion freeness and completeness follow in the same way (Sch12 Proposition 5.17 proof; Kedlaya–Liu II Lemma 3.3.7).
- (c),(d) Bhatt Example 6.2.4(1) and P1/almost-integral-dictionary.

*Acceptance.*
- For B = (T°/t)[X^{1/p^∞}]: lim_Φ B = T°⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- For B = T°/t: lim_Φ B = T°.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-almost-setup`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `almost-integral-dictionary`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `mathlib:Perfection`, `mathlib:Perfection.quotientMulEquiv`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Remark 5.18, p. 26; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Lemma 3.4.2, p. 79; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Example 6.2.4(1), p. 45; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, Kedlaya–Liu II, Lemma 3.3.7, p. 60.

#### `tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt` — Tilting equivalence Perf_R ≃ Perf_{R♭} over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring, with the explicit tilt

*theorem.* **Planet:** *Tilting equivalence*. Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/TiltingEquivalence`.

(ECD Theorem 3.13; Berkeley Theorem 6.2.7; Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.17; Sch12 Theorem 5.2 over a perfectoid field) Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ and J_R := ker(θ_R: W(R♭°) → R°), a primitive ideal (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel). The tilting functor S ↦ S♭ (R♭ → S♭ the tilt of R → S, P1/tilt-functoriality) is an equivalence from perfectoid R-algebras to perfectoid R♭-algebras, with quasi-inverse T ↦ T♯ := W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]]/J_R·W(T°)[1/[ϖ♭]], the untilt along J_R·W(T°) (P1/untilt-construction); the unit S ≅ (S♭)♯ is induced by θ_S and the counit (T♯)♭ ≅ T by P1/untilt-is-perfectoid-pair, both natural. Explicitly S♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} S, S♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} S° ≅ lim_Φ S°/ϖ and S♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ S°/ϖ; the functor is independent of choices, extends to pairs (S, S+) ↦ (S♭, S♭+), and S is a perfectoid field iff S♭ is (P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field). For R = K a perfectoid field, T♯ = W(T°) ⊗_{W(K♭°)} K°[1/ϖ] (Sch12 Remark 5.19; Bhatt Remark 6.2.8), and the functor agrees with Sch12's chain K-Perf ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf ≃ K♭°a-Perf ≃ K♭-Perf.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- No perfectoid base field; continuous homomorphisms between Tate rings preserve power-bounded elements into uniform targets (API of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so R-algebras are pairs over (R, R°).

*Proof outline.*
- Slice categories: perfectoid R-algebras are perfectoid pairs (S, S°) with a morphism from (R, R°); under P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals they correspond to triples (T, T°, J) with a morphism from (R♭, R♭°, J_R), i.e. J = J_R·W(T°) (P1/theta-kernel-base-change), i.e. to perfectoid R♭-algebras T (Kedlaya AWS Remark 2.3.17).
- Explicit tilt: P1/tilt-integral-subrings applied to S; field case: P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field.
- Consistency with Sch12 for R = K: both functors send S to the unique T with (T°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (S°/ϖ)^a over K°/ϖ ≅ K♭°/ϖ♭ (Bhatt Corollary 6.2.6; P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence).

*Uses.*
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected: a perfectoid (R+/ϖ)^a-algebra is (R̃°/ϖ)^a for a perfectoid R-algebra R̃ (with P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence).
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: tilting equivalences over perfectoid Tate rings.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting, P2/tilting-slice-equivalence: globalisation (ECD Corollary 3.20).

*Acceptance.*
- (Sch12 Proposition 5.20; Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15) The tilt of R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ is R♭⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ with T_i♯ = T_i (P1/perfected-tate-algebra).
- The sharp map is multiplicative and continuous; additivity is not asserted.

*Depends on:* `untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`, `theta-kernel-base-change`, `tilt-functoriality`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`, `untilt-construction`, `untilt-is-perfectoid-pair`, `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Theorem 3.13, p. 17; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Theorem 3.13, proof, p. 17; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD after Theorem 3.13, p. 17; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Theorem 6.2.7, p. 45; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Remark 2.3.17, p. 56; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Theorem 5.2, p. 22; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Proposition 5.17, p. 26; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Remark 5.19, p. 27.

#### `perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence` — Perf_R ≃ R°a-Perf ≃ (R°a/ϖ)-Perf over an arbitrary perfectoid Tate ring

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/AlmostDictionary`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring and ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ with compatible roots. A perfectoid (R°a/ϖ)-algebra is an (R°/ϖ)^a-algebra B that is flat over Λ = ℤ[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) (x ↦ ϖ; equivalently the kernel of ϖ^q on B_* is ϖ^{1−q}B_* up to almost zero for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] ∩ (0, 1)) with Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} → B an isomorphism. Then S ↦ S°a ↦ (S°/ϖ)^a are equivalences Perf_R ≃ R°a-Perf ≃ (R°a/ϖ)-Perf (R°a-Perf as in P1/almost-integral-dictionary), and (R°a/ϖ)-Perf = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf via R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭, compatibly with tilting: (S♭°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (S°/ϖ)^a. This is the general-base form of Sch12 Theorem 5.2's chain used by ECD Theorem 3.13 and Proposition 9.3; for R = K a perfectoid field Λ-flatness is flatness over K°a/ϖ (Sch12 Definition 5.1(iii)).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Λ-flatness, not flatness over (R°/ϖ)^a: for a perfectoid quotient R → R/I, (R/I)°/ϖ is not flat over R°/ϖ but is Λ-flat.

*Proof outline.*
- Tilt side: R♭-Perf ≃ R♭°a-Perf (P1/almost-integral-dictionary for R♭) ≃ (R♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf (P1/frobenius-inverse-limit-lifting-in-characteristic-p).
- (R°a/ϖ)-Perf = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf: the isomorphism R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings) carries ϖ^{1/p^n} to ϖ♭^{1/p^n} and R°°/ϖ to R♭°°/ϖ♭, so it matches the Λ-structures and almost setups (P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
- Perf_R ≃ Perf_{R♭} (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), and the composite Perf_R → (R°a/ϖ)-Perf is S ↦ (S♭°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (S°/ϖ)^a (P1/tilt-integral-subrings for S), hence an equivalence; with Perf_R ≃ R°a-Perf (P1/almost-integral-dictionary), reduction R°a-Perf → (R°a/ϖ)-Perf is an equivalence.
- Optional comparison, not used by the proof: on the flat subcategories the inverse is also the deformation-theoretic lift of P1/deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras, Scholze 2012's route (RT-AREA-padic-1/5).

*Acceptance.*
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/effective-descent-affinoid-over-totally-disconnected: the (R+/ϖ)^a-algebra descended from (S̃+/ϖ)^a along an almost faithfully flat map is Λ-flat with bijective Frobenius, hence of the form (R̃°/ϖ)^a (ECD Proposition 9.3).
- For R = K a perfectoid field this recovers K-Perf ≃ K°a-Perf ≃ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf (Sch12 Theorem 5.2; Bhatt Theorem 6.2.5).

*Depends on:* `almost-integral-dictionary`, `frobenius-inverse-limit-lifting-in-characteristic-p`, `tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `tilt-integral-subrings`, `perfectoid-almost-setup`.

*Sources:* sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Definition 5.1(iii), p. 22; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 9.3, proof, p. 44; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Corollary 6.2.6, p. 46; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Theorem 5.10, p. 24.

#### `completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings` — Completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings are perfectoid, and tilting commutes with them (Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2)

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FilteredColimit`.

Let J be a small filtered category and j ↦ R_j a functor from J to perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms φ_a: R_i → R_j (no injectivity, flatness or density assumed; characteristic 0, p or neither; no perfectoid base field). Fix j₀ ∈ J and a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭ ∈ R_{j₀}♭ with compatible roots, ϖ = ϖ♭♯ (P1/exists-pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots); on the tail J_{j₀} = Under j₀ (final in J, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget`) the images of ϖ and of its roots are pseudo-uniformizers with compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in every R_j° (a compatible pseudo-uniformizer). Put A := colim_j R_j° (filtered colimit of rings, Mathlib `CommRingCat.FilteredColimits`), R_0 := its ϖ-adic completion lim_n A/ϖ^nA, and R := R_0[1/ϖ], topologised with R_0 open carrying its ϖ-adic topology. Then: (a) R is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and ring of definition R_0; ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R_0 and R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = colim_j R_j°/ϖ^n; the canonical maps ι_j: R_j → R are continuous and compatible, and the image of colim R_j is dense; for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring S and compatible continuous ring homomorphisms ψ_j: R_j → S there is a unique continuous ψ: R → S with ψ ∘ ι_j = ψ_j; R is independent of j₀ and ϖ, and replacing R_j° by rings of integral elements R_j⁺ (compatible under the φ_a) gives the same R, since ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j⁺ ⊆ R_j°; (b) R is a perfectoid Tate ring; R_0 is ϖ-adically complete and integral perfectoid, R_0 ⊆ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n}R° ⊆ R_0 for all n; so R, with the ι_j, is the colimit of the R_j in perfectoid Tate rings and in complete Hausdorff uniform Tate rings; (c) tilting commutes with completed filtered colimits: the R_j♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality) form a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p with compatible pseudo-uniformizer ϖ♭, and the continuous homomorphism from their completed colimit T (as in (a), with ring of definition the ϖ♭-adic completion of colim R_j♭°) to R♭ induced by the ι_j♭ is an isomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings, compatible with ♯; dually, for a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and a filtered system of perfectoid R′♭-algebras T_j, the untilt over R′ (P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) of their completed colimit is the completed colimit of the untilts T_j♯. PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs builds the same ring from plus rings along a cofiltered diagram of pairs and P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid adds the statements about the plus ring.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- J small and filtered (hence nonempty); every R_j a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1; transition maps continuous.
- The R_j must be perfectoid: a completed colimit of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid (ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n})) without its tilt being the colimit of the tilts (test completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower); such limits are tilde-limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P7).

*Proof outline.*
- Compatible pseudo-uniformizer: continuous ring homomorphisms map units to units, topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent ones and R_{j₀}° into R_j° (API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so the images of ϖ♭'s coordinates are compatible roots and ϖ^p | p in R_j°; parallel morphisms j₀ ⇉ j may give different images, which agree in A. Restricting to Under j₀ does not change the colimit (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Under.final_forget).
- (a) A exists (mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A as it is a unit in each R_j. The ϖ-adic completion R_0 is ϖ-adically complete with R_0/ϖ^nR_0 = A/ϖ^nA (Stacks Tag 05GG for the finitely generated ideal ϖA; mathlib:AdicCompletion) and ϖ-torsion free (if ϖ·(x_n)_n = 0 in lim A/ϖ^n then x_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^nA, so x_n = 0). R := R_0[1/ϖ] with basis {ϖ^nR_0} is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring. R_j° is open and bounded in R_j with its ϖ-adic topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero), so R_j° → A → R_0 is continuous and extends to ι_j on R_j = R_j°[1/ϖ]. Universal property: ψ_j(R_j°) ⊆ S° (S uniform), S° is open, bounded and ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so the induced A → S° extends uniquely to R_0 and to R; uniqueness from density of A in R_0. Independence: two compatible pseudo-uniformizers define cofinal filtrations on A (at a common stage each divides a power of the other), and colim R_j⁺ ⊆ A ⊆ ϖ^{-1}·colim R_j⁺ because ϖR_j° ⊆ R_j°° ⊆ R_j⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), so both completions give the same R.
- (b) ϖ^p | p in A, hence in R_0. Φ: A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is the filtered colimit of the bijections Φ_j: R_j°/ϖ → R_j°/ϖ^p (P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer, P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), hence bijective, and so is Φ: R_0/ϖ → R_0/ϖ^p since R_0/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n. By the successive-approximation argument of P1/frobenius-surjectivity-criterion ((i) ⇒ (ii), which uses only ϖ-adic completeness) Frobenius on R_0/p is surjective. So R_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii), P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison), and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes R = R_0[1/ϖ] a perfectoid Tate ring with R_0 ⊆ R° and R°/R_0 killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}. The colimit statement is (a) together with perfectoidness.
- (c) The R_j♭ are perfectoid of characteristic p (P1/tilt-is-perfectoid-tate-ring) with transition maps φ_a♭ (P1/tilt-functoriality); by (a) and (b) their completed colimit T is perfectoid, with ring of definition T_0 and T_0/ϖ♭ = colim_j R_j♭°/ϖ♭. The ι_j♭ induce χ: T → R♭ (universal property (a); R♭ is uniform). Modulo ϖ♭, T_0/ϖ♭ = colim R_j♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ colim R_j°/ϖ = R_0/ϖ (P1/tilt-integral-subrings (c), compatibly with the φ_a), and R_0/ϖ → R°/ϖ ≅ R♭°/ϖ♭ is an almost isomorphism (its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, by (b)); likewise T_0/ϖ♭ → T°/ϖ♭. So χ induces an isomorphism (T°/ϖ♭)^a ≅ (R♭°/ϖ♭)^a of perfectoid (R_{j₀}♭°a/ϖ♭)-algebras, and χ is an isomorphism by P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence over the base R_{j₀}♭ (Sch12 Theorem 5.2: perfectoid algebras are determined by their reduction modulo ϖ; Bhatt Remark 6.2.9). Compatibility with ♯ holds coordinatewise.
- (c) dual form: apply (c) to the system T_j♯, whose tilts are the T_j (counit of P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt), and use full faithfulness of untilting.

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit` (data): completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ : Type, for F : J ⥤ (perfectoid Tate rings, continuous homomorphisms) with J filtered and ϖ♭ a pseudo-uniformizer with roots of F.obj j₀; CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition` (structure): R_0 = AdicCompletion (span {ϖ}) (colim (F ⋙ powerBoundedSubring)), an open bounded subring with its ϖ-adic topology; R = Localization.Away ϖ R_0; R_0 ⧸ ϖ^n ≃+* colim (R_j° ⧸ ϖ^n).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ι` (constructor): ι j : F.obj j →+* completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, continuous, with (ι j).comp (F.map a) = ι i for a : i ⟶ j in Under j₀.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.lift` (universal-property): For S complete Hausdorff uniform Tate and compatible continuous ψ j : F.obj j →+* S: lift ψ continuous with (lift ψ).comp (ι j) = ψ j (lift_comp_ι), and hom_ext for two continuous maps agreeing on all ι j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): IsPerfectoidTateRing (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.ringOfDefinition_almostEq` (characterisation): R_0 ≤ R° and ϖ^{1/p^n} • R° ≤ R_0 for all n (R°/R_0 is almost zero for P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.denseRange` (other): The ring homomorphism colim F → completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭ has dense range.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.tiltEquiv` (equivalence): tilt (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭) ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (F ⋙ tiltFunctor) ϖ♭.toTilt, a homeomorphism commuting with sharp and sending tilt.map (ι j) to ι j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.untiltEquiv` (equivalence): For a perfectoid Tate ring R′ and G : J ⥤ perfectoid R′♭-algebras: the untilt over R′ of completedFilteredColimit G is isomorphic to completedFilteredColimit (G ⋙ untiltFunctor R′), naturally in G.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.equivOfChoice` (compatibility): Changing (j₀, ϖ♭) or restricting along a final functor J′ ⥤ J gives canonically isomorphic rings, compatibly with ι and lift; using compatible rings of integral elements instead of R_j° gives the same ring.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit.isColimit` (universal-property): The cocone (completedFilteredColimit F ϖ♭, ι) is a colimit in the category of perfectoid Tate rings with continuous ring homomorphisms.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_const` (degenerate): For J with a terminal object j (in particular a one-object J), completedFilteredColimit F ≃+* F.obj j as topological rings, compatibly with ι_j.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_locallyConstant` (computation): For a perfectoid field K and a profinite set S = lim S_i (finite S_i), the completed colimit of the perfectoid rings K^{S_i} = C(S_i, K) is C^0(S, K) with the sup norm, and its ring of definition is C^0(S, K°).
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_tilt_algebraicClosure` (compatibility): For a perfectoid field K, tiltEquiv identifies (completion of an algebraic closure of K♭) with the tilt of the completed colimit of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L of K♭ inside it; the union of the L♯ is dense in the untilt.
- `Perfectoid.completedFilteredColimit_nonPerfectoid_tower` (non-example): For p odd, the fields ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n}) are not perfectoid and their tilts in the sense of P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring are 𝔽_p, while the completion ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ is perfectoid with tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: tilting does not commute with completed colimits of non-perfectoid rings, so the hypothesis that every R_j be perfectoid cannot be dropped.

*Uses.*
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields: the Krasner step: the untilt of the completed algebraic closure M of K♭ is the completed colimit of the untilts of the finite extensions of K♭ in M, (c).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit: the completed colimit of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings, with ring of definition the completed colimit of the R_j°, is perfectoid, (a)–(b).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid: perfectoidness and tilt of the completed direct limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces; P5 adds the plus rings.
- Bhatt Remark 6.2.9; Sch12 Theorem 5.2 and proof of Theorem 3.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22: filtered colimits of perfectoid algebras and their tilts in the sources.

*Acceptance.*
- Sch12 proof of Theorem 3.7 and Bhatt, proof of almost purity over a field: for M the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭, M is the completed colimit of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ and the union of the L♯ is dense in M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 4.6: the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebras is perfectoid; here without a base field.
- Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22: the completion of a filtered direct limit of Fontaine perfectoid Banach rings, for the infimum of the spectral norms, is perfectoid.

### P1.8 Examples and compatibility with the anchor

The stage's tests: perfected Tate algebras over any perfectoid Tate ring in any set of variables (finitely many for AdicSpacesPartII, infinitely many for the uniform completed tensor products of P2), the cyclotomic field, the field ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, the completed perfection of F_p((t)), ℂ_p, the non-field ring of ECD 3.4(iv), and the non-examples; and the identification of the anchor's perfect field and A_inf.

#### `perfected-tate-algebra` — Perfected Tate algebras R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ in any set of variables over any perfectoid Tate ring

*construction.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/PerfectedTateAlgebra`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ (ϖ^p | p in R°) and Σ an arbitrary set, possibly infinite. The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is A_0[1/ϖ], where A_0 is the ϖ-adic completion of the monoid algebra R°[T^a : a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}] (AddMonoidAlgebra over the finitely supported exponent vectors Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}, T^a = Π_s T_s^{a(s)}), topologised with A_0 open and ϖ-adic; equivalently the completion of the perfect polynomial ring R[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] for the topology in which R°[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ] is open with its ϖ-adic topology (the Gauss norm). It is a perfectoid Tate ring with R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩° = A_0 = {Σ_a c_aT^a : c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on exponents}; R⁺⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a ring of integral elements for every R⁺. Universal property: for every complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and every family, indexed by s ∈ Σ, of compatible systems (t_s^{(m)})_{m≥0} in S° with (t_s^{(m+1)})^p = t_s^{(m)}, there is a unique continuous R-algebra map R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ t_s^{(m)}; for S perfectoid such families are families (x_s) in S♭°, via t_s^{(m)} = (x_s^{1/p^m})♯. Its tilt is R♭⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ with T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, so T_s♯ = T_s. The construction is functorial in Σ, and R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is the completed filtered colimit (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings) of the algebras in finitely many of the variables. For Σ = {1, …, n} it is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩, which contains Tau Ceti's R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ as the closed subring of series with exponents in ℕ^n, with a continuous R-linear retraction σ(Σ x_aT^a) = Σ_{a ∈ ℕ^n} x_aT^a; the Laurent variant R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid as well (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12 for arbitrary index sets).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- R perfectoid with no base field; Σ any set (Σ = ∅ gives R).
- Infinite Σ is used: P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base takes Σ = C♭° (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21), and Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7 takes Σ = C♭⁺.

*Proof outline.*
- A_0 is ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (a completed free R°-module on the monomials, with c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter), with A_0/ϖ = (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ]; Φ: A_0/ϖ → A_0/ϖ^p is bijective coefficientwise (R° perfectoid) and on monomials (a ↦ pa is bijective on ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}^{(Σ)}), and Frobenius on A_0/p is surjective; so A_0 is integral perfectoid (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)) and P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid makes A_0[1/ϖ] perfectoid with A_0 ⊆ A° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_0.
- A° = A_0: if ϖ^{1/p^m}x ∈ A_0 for all m then every coefficient c_a satisfies ϖ^{1/p^m}c_a ∈ R° for all m, hence c_a ∈ R° (R° = its own almost elements, P1/almost-integral-dictionary (a)).
- Universal property: T^a ↦ Π_s (t_s^{(m)})^{k_s} for a = (k_s/p^m)_s is a well-defined R°-algebra map R°[T^a] → S° (compatibility of the systems; continuous maps into the uniform S send R° into S°, API map_mem_powerBoundedSubring of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); it is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, and S° is ϖ-adically complete (P1/integral-elements-adically-complete), so it extends uniquely to A_0 and to A_0[1/ϖ]; uniqueness from density of R[T_s^{1/p^∞}].
- Tilt: the ring map R♭°⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ → lim_{x↦x^p} A_0, T_s^{1/p^m} ↦ (T_s^{1/p^{m+k}})_k, reduces modulo ϖ♭ to the identity of (R°/ϖ)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] = (R♭°/ϖ♭)[T_s^{1/p^∞}] (P1/tilt-integral-subrings); both sides are ϖ♭-adically complete and torsion free, so it is an isomorphism; invert ϖ♭ (P1/sharp-map for T_s♯ = T_s).
- Finitely many variables: for finite Σ_0 ⊆ Σ, A_0(Σ_0) ⊆ A_0(Σ), the union is dense and A_0(Σ)/ϖ^n = colim_{Σ_0} A_0(Σ_0)/ϖ^n, which is the description of the completed colimit in P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (a). A map g: Σ → Σ′ induces T_s ↦ T_{g(s)} by the universal property.
- The subring R⟨T⟩ and σ for Σ = {1, …, n}: σ is continuous and R-linear and splits the inclusion (it is not multiplicative).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra` (data): perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ : Type for Σ : Type*, with CommRing, TopologicalSpace, IsTopologicalRing, IsTateRing, CompleteSpace, T2Space instances and an R-algebra structure.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.isPerfectoidTateRing` (instance): IsPerfectoidTateRing (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X` (constructor): X s a = T_s^a for s : Σ and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}; X s (a + b) = X s a * X s b, (X s (a/p))^p = X s a, X s a ∈ A°.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.powerBoundedSubring_eq` (characterisation): (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ)° = {Σ c_a T^a | c_a ∈ R°, c_a → 0 along the cofinite filter on Σ →₀ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}}.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift` (universal-property): For a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate R-algebra S and a family t : Σ → Perfection S° p (compatible p-power roots in S°), the unique continuous R-algebra map with X s (1/p^m) ↦ coeff m (t s); lift_X and uniqueness (hom_ext).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.liftTilt` (universal-property): For S perfectoid: continuous R-algebra maps perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ → S correspond to maps Σ → (tilt S)°, x ↦ lift (fun s ↦ x s), with sharp (tilt.map (liftTilt x) (X s 1)) = sharp (x s).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tiltEquiv` (equivalence): tilt (perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ) ≃+* perfectedTateAlgebra (tilt R) Σ, a homeomorphism with sharp (X s a) = X s a.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.mapIndex` (functoriality): For g : Σ → Σ′, the continuous R-algebra map with X s a ↦ X (g s) a; mapIndex id = id, mapIndex (g′ ∘ g) = mapIndex g′ ∘ mapIndex g.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.equivCompletedColimit` (compatibility): perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ ≃+* completedFilteredColimit (Σ₀ ↦ perfectedTateAlgebra R Σ₀) over finite subsets Σ₀ ⊆ Σ (P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.restrictedIncl` (compatibility): For Σ = Fin n: the continuous injective R-algebra map from TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R (R⟨T⟩) with closed image, T_i ↦ X i 1.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.retraction` (other): For Σ = Fin n: the continuous R-linear map σ onto integral exponents with σ ∘ restrictedIncl = id (the frame of AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.plus` (constructor): For a ring of integral elements R+, R+⟨T_s^{1/p^∞}⟩ is a ring of integral elements; the resulting perfectoid pair.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.laurent` (other): The Laurent variant R⟨T_s^{±1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is perfectoid.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.emptyEquiv` (example): perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_empty_test` (degenerate): perfectedTateAlgebra R PEmpty ≃+* R as topological rings.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.X_pow` (computation): (X s (1/p^{m+1}))^p = X s (1/p^m), and Frobenius on A_0/ϖ sends the class of X s (1/p) to that of X s 1; for Σ = ℕ the series Σ_k ϖ^k X k 1 converges while Σ_k X k 1 does not.
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.tilt_cyclotomic` (compatibility): tilt (ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≃+* (tilt ℚ_p^cycl)⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (ECD Example 3.4(iii); Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra_fin_test` (compatibility): For Σ = Fin n, perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) is R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ of the AdicSpacesPartII request, restrictedIncl embeds TauCeti.Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R with retraction σ, and for Fin n ⊆ ℕ the map perfectedTateAlgebra R (Fin n) → perfectedTateAlgebra R ℕ is a strict inclusion.
- `Perfectoid.not_isPerfectoidTateRing_restricted` (non-example): For n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0, R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ is not perfectoid: T_1 is not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-polydisc).
- `Perfectoid.perfectedTateAlgebra.lift_one` (characterisation): lift with t_s^{(m)} = 1 for all s, m is evaluation at T = 1, a continuous R-algebra map to R; two continuous R-algebra maps agreeing on all X s (1/p^m) are equal.

*Uses.*
- AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings (request (a) to P1): R̃⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ over an arbitrary perfectoid R̃ with ι and σ is a perfectoid frame of R⟨T⟩ (Σ = {1, …, n}).
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: the perfectoid relative ball B^{N,perf}_X = Spa(A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, A+⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩).
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma: the perfectoid polydisc.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base: the perfectoid ring B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩ in infinitely many variables and its universal property, mapping densely to B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21).
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13: C̃ = A⟨T_s^{p^{-∞}} : s ∈ C♭⁺⟩ surjecting onto C, for completed tensor products of perfectoid rings.
- ECD Example 3.4(iii); Sch12 Proposition 5.20; Kedlaya AWS Example 2.1.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12: the example in the sources.

*Acceptance.*
- ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = A[1/p] with A the p-adic completion of ℤ_p^cycl[T^{1/p^∞}] (ECD Example 3.4(iii)).

#### `cyclotomic-perfectoid-field` — The completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field; its tilt and primitive ideal

*theorem.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Examples`.

The completion ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is a perfectoid field: its valuation ring is the p-adic completion ℤ_p^cycl of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}], its value group |p|^{ℤ[1/p]/(p−1)} is nondiscrete and Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective. Its tilt is the completed perfection of F_p((t)) with t = ε − 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …), with |t♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)} (Berkeley Example 6.2.4), and it is the untilt of (F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, F_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]^) along the primitive ideal generated by Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}[1 + t]^{i/p} (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.8; Kedlaya–Liu I Example 3.3.8). ℤ_p^× acts compatibly, by γ(t) = (1 + t)^γ − 1 on the tilt.

For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}) is a finite extension of ℚ_p^cycl and is perfectoid by the stability of perfectoid fields under finite extensions: `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension` (AdicSpacesPartII's request (b)).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- p any prime; ζ_{p^n} a compatible system of primitive p^n-th roots of unity.

*Proof outline.*
- ℤ_p[ζ_{p^n}] is the valuation ring of ℚ_p(ζ_{p^n}) with |ζ_{p^n} − 1| = |p|^{1/(p^{n−1}(p−1))}, so the value group is nondiscrete and |p| < 1.
- Every element of ℤ_p[μ_{p^∞}] is Σa_iζ^i with a_i ∈ ℤ_p and ζ ∈ μ_{p^n}, and Σa_iζ^i ≡ (Σa_iζ'^i)^p mod p for ζ'^p = ζ, as a^p ≡ a mod p for a ∈ ℤ_p; so Frobenius on ℤ_p^cycl/p is surjective (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.5.12: "trivial to check") and P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation applies.
- Tilt: ε ∈ lim ℤ_p^cycl, t = ε − 1 has |t♯| = lim|ζ_{p^n} − 1|^{p^n} = |p|^{p/(p−1)} < 1, is a pseudo-uniformizer, and K♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field; Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- Primitive generator: z = Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p} maps to p under W(K♭°) → W(F_p), so z_1 is a unit, and θ(z) = Σ_{i<p}ζ_p^i = 0; hence ker θ = (z) (P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel (c)).

*Acceptance.*
- For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the completion of K(μ_{p^∞}) is the finite extension K·ℚ_p^cycl of ℚ_p^cycl, perfectoid by stability of perfectoid fields under finite extension (Sch12 Theorem 3.7(i), Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.5.6), the P3 node P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.
- v♭(ε − 1) = p/(p − 1) in PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements.

*Depends on:* `perfectoid-field-characterisation`, `tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `mathlib:Padic`, `mathlib:PadicInt`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Example 3.4(i), p. 14; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Example 3.3.8, p. 78; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Example 3.3.8, p. 78; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, Kedlaya–Liu I, Remark 3.5.12, p. 86; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Kedlaya AWS notes, Example 2.3.8, p. 54; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Berkeley Lectures, Example 6.2.4, p. 44; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, BMS1 Example 3.6, p. 21.

#### `perfectoid-examples` — Examples and non-examples of perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Remark 3.3, Example 3.4)

*application.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Examples`.

The following are perfectoid Tate rings, each a declaration of the library: (1) ℂ_p (Mathlib PadicComplex p), a perfectoid field whose tilt contains p♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) with (p♭)♯ = p; (2) the completion K_1 of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), a perfectoid field with valuation ring the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}] and tilt F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t♯ = p, the untilt along (p − [t]) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.7); (3) the completed perfection F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, a perfectoid field of characteristic p equal to its own tilt; (4) ℚ_p^cycl (P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); (5) ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (P1/perfected-tate-algebra); (6) the ring R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ϖ^p = T divides p in R°), which does not contain a nonarchimedean field (ECD Example 3.4(iv); Berkeley Example 6.1.5(4)); (7) products such as K × K♭ for a perfectoid field K, where p is a nonzero nonunit. Non-examples: ℚ_p and every discretely valued nonarchimedean field (ECD Remark 3.3), F_p((t)) (not perfect), ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) (not uniform), R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ for n ≥ 1 and R ≠ 0 (T_1 not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p).

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- Each example is checked against ECD Definition 3.1 through the criteria of this layer.

*Proof outline.*
- (1) ℂ_p is algebraically closed with value group |p|^ℚ, so every element of 𝒪_{ℂ_p} has a p-th root (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(2)); P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation.
- (2) K_1° = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^ is generated by the p^{1/p^n}, whose classes are p-th powers modulo p (Bhatt Example 3.1.2(1)); its tilt is computed by P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field and it is the untilt along (p − [t]) (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals).
- (3) P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect. (4) P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field. (5) P1/perfected-tate-algebra.
- (6) R° is the displayed ring (bounded); ϖ = T^{1/p} has ϖ^p = T and p = T·(p/T) with p/T ∈ R°; Frobenius R°/T^{1/p} → R°/T is surjective as all topological generators T^{1/p^n}, (p/T)^{1/p^n} and ℤ_p^cycl have p-th roots modulo p (ECD Example 3.4(iv)).
- (7) API IsPerfectoidTateRing.prod of P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras. Non-examples: P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation, P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-is-reduced, P1/perfected-tate-algebra.

*Acceptance.*
- These realise the tests of the stage: completed F_p((t^{1/p^∞})), cyclotomic and compatible-root mixed-characteristic fields, perfected Tate balls and tori, and a non-field perfectoid Tate ring.

#### `anchor-layer-6-compatibility` — Compatibility with the anchor's perfect field F and A_inf = W(𝒪_F) (Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6.1)

*comparison.* Lean module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Ainf`.

Let F be a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of characteristic p with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ, as in anchor Layer 6.1. Then (a) F is a perfectoid field of characteristic p (P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect, P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation), its tilt is F itself with ♯ the identity (P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring), and (F, 𝒪_F) is a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p; (b) the anchor's A_inf = W(𝒪_F), with pair of definition (A_inf, (p, [ϖ])), is the ring W(F♭+) = W(𝒪_F) of this layer, and the anchor's (p, [ϖ])-adic completeness and separatedness of W(𝒪_F) is P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring for (F, 𝒪_F); (c) the untilts of F are the pairs (W(𝒪_F)[1/[ϖ]]/(ξ), W(𝒪_F)/(ξ)) for primitive ξ ∈ A_inf (P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). The anchor's curve 𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf) and its Frobenius windows are not re-planned; P1 only identifies the input objects.

*Hypotheses and conventions.*
- F as in anchor Layer 6 (no algebraic closedness).

*Proof outline.*
- (a) A complete nontrivially valued perfect field is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid; its value group is p-divisible (perfectness), so not discrete.
- (b) Same ring; the completeness statements coincide.
- (c) The classification with (R, R+) = (F, 𝒪_F).

*Acceptance.*
- For F the completed perfection of F_p((t)): untilts include ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ (ξ = p − [t]) and ℚ_p^cycl (ξ = Σ_{i<p}[1 + t]^{i/p}).

*Depends on:* `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve`, `characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `perfectoid-field-characterisation`, `tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring`, `primitive-degree-one-ideals`, `untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`.

*Sources:* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, ECD Proposition 3.5, p. 15; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 Lemma 3.4(iv), p. 16; sch12-perfectoid, Sch12 §3, p. 15; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Bhatt notes, Example 6.1.6, p. 43.

P1 proves that F is a perfectoid field equal to its tilt and that A_inf = W(F♭+) with the same completeness statement (P1/witt-vectors-of-perfect-plus-ring), and needs the anchor objects to be stated for a Tau Ceti nonarchimedean field so that the comparison is an identification of declarations. Needed by `anchor-layer-6-compatibility`.
- **`DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`** — The classical cotangent complex L_{B/A} of a ring map via simplicial polynomial resolutions, with functoriality in the pair (A → B), the transitivity triangle, derived (Tor-independent) base change and flat base change, and the identification of the effect of a map of simplicial resolutions (used for the relative Frobenius criterion L_{B/A} ≃ 0 when A(Φ) ⊗^L_A B → B(Φ) is an isomorphism, Gabber–Ramero Lemma 6.5.9). P0 builds the almost version on it. Needed by `cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi`, `deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras`.
- **`TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0`** — For a commutative nonarchimedean Banach ring A (or a uniform Banach algebra over a nonarchimedean field): the Berkovich spectrum M(A) of bounded multiplicative seminorms is nonempty for A ≠ 0; f ∈ A is a unit iff α(f) ≠ 0 for all α ∈ M(A) (Berkovich Theorem 1.2.1, Corollary 1.2.4); and the spectral seminorm satisfies |f|_sp = max_{α ∈ M(A)} α(f) (Berkovich Theorem 1.3.1). These are the inputs of Kedlaya's Theorem 3.7 (Banach fields). The same maximum formula for an arbitrary nonarchimedean Banach ring B (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.5.21: the spectral seminorm of B equals the supremum of α over the Gel'fand spectrum M(B), attained since M(B) is compact) is used to pass between pointwise and global forms of the sharp approximation lemma for perfectoid Tate rings of any characteristic. Needed by `uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field`, `sharp-approximation-lemma`.

### Gaps

- **Berkovich spectral theory for Kedlaya's Banach-field theorem** (`uniform-banach-field-over-nondiscrete-field`, `perfectoid-ring-field-is-perfectoid-field`). Kedlaya, Banach fields, Theorem 3.7 (read in full, pp. 9–11) uses Berkovich's theorems that M(A) is nonempty, detects units, and computes the spectral seminorm as a maximum (Berkovich, Spectral theory, Theorems 1.2.1 and 1.3.1), which were not read and are not in the pinned libraries; requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0. The characteristic-0 step of Kedlaya's Theorem 4.2 (homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(A♭)) is replaced in this layer by the spectral-gauge comparison P1/spectral-norm-under-sharp, which needs no Berkovich theory.
- **Illusie–Gabber–Ramero almost deformation theory and the almost cotangent complex** (`cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi`, `deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras`). Sch12 Theorems 5.11–5.12 cite Illusie III.2.1.2.3, III.2.2.2 and Gabber–Ramero Propositions 3.2.9, 3.2.16 (arXiv numbering; read as statements, Corollary 3.2.11 quoted); the almost cotangent complex and its transitivity triangle ("Theorem 2.5.36" of the book, not the arXiv 2.5.36) are P0/almost-cotangent-complex and P0/almost-deformation-theory, built on DD.0. The general-base equivalence P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence does not use deformation theory. Off the critical path of P1 since FIX-RT-AREA-padic-1: both P1 nodes are an optional alternative route. P0's own finite-étale lifting still uses P0/almost-deformation-theory (through P0/nilpotent-lifting-of-etale-almost-algebras and P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), so P0 keeps the almost cotangent/deformation extension; this answers the question RT-AREA-padic-1/5 left to P0's blueprint.

### Mistakes found in the sources

- **PerfectoidSpaces/E5** (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Lemma 3.16, p. 17 (arXiv v4); misprint, affects nothing). Printed: "Any ξ of the form ξ = p + [ϖ♭ ]α, with ϖ♭ ∈ R♭+ a pseudo-uniformizer and α ∈ W (R+ ), is a non-zero-divisor." Correction: α ∈ W(R♭+): ξ must lie in W(R♭+), where [ϖ♭] lives; W(R+) is the Witt ring of the untilt's plus ring. Reason: Definition 3.15 immediately before, and Lemma 3.14(ii), take α ∈ W(R♭+); the proof divides Teichmüller coordinates by ϖ♭ ∈ R♭+.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E6** (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Remark 3.2, p. 14 (arXiv v4); misprint, affects nothing). Printed: "Thus, if Φ : R◦ /p → R◦ /p is surjective, then R is perfectoid." Correction: Keep the standing hypothesis that some pseudo-uniformizer ϖ has ϖ^p | p in R°: if such a ϖ exists and Φ is surjective on R°/p, then R is perfectoid. Reason: Read without that hypothesis the sentence is false: ℚ_p is a complete uniform Tate ring with Φ on ℤ_p/p = F_p bijective, and Remark 3.3 right after says ℚ_p is not perfectoid. The remark is written in the context of a fixed ϖ with ϖ^p | p, so the intended meaning is clear.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E7** (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Proposition 3.5, proof, p. 15 (arXiv v4); the same chain in Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6, p. 43; gap, affects the proof). Printed: "Φ−k (R0 ) ⊂ ϖ−n/p−n/p −...−n/p R0 . In particular, for all k ≥ 0, Φ−k (R0 ) ⊂ ϖ−n R0 ." Correction: Either replace R_0 by a ring of definition stable under multiplication by ϖ^q for q ∈ ℤ[1/p] ∩ [0, 1], or use the integral-exponent estimate Φ^{-1}(ϖ^mR_0) ⊆ ϖ^{⌊(m−n)/p⌋}R_0, which gives every topologically nilpotent element in ϖ^{-c}R_0 with c = ⌈(n + p)/(p − 1)⌉ and hence R° ⊆ ϖ^{-c-1}R_0. Reason: The inclusion ϖ^{-a}R_0 ⊆ ϖ^{-n}R_0 for fractional 0 < a < n needs ϖ^{n−a}R_0 ⊆ R_0, i.e. ϖ^{n−a} ∈ R_0 acting on R_0, which is not known for an arbitrary ring of definition before uniformity is proved; ϖ^{n−a} is only known to be power-bounded.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E8** (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Proposition 9.3, proof, p. 44, and Theorem 3.13, proof, p. 17 (arXiv v4); gap, affects the proof). Printed: "which is perfectoid in the sense of [Sch12, Definition 5.1 (iii)], and thus, by [Sch12, Theorem 5.2], is of the form" Correction: Over a base (R+/ϖ)^a that is not the ring of integers of a perfectoid field modulo ϖ, Sch12 Definition 5.1(iii) must be read with flatness over Λ = ℤ[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) (x ↦ ϖ), not over (R+/ϖ)^a, and the equivalence with perfectoid R-algebras is then P1/perfectoid-mod-varpi-equivalence (tilt to characteristic p, lift by lim_Φ, untilt). Reason: Sch12 fixes a perfectoid field K and requires flatness over K°a/ϖ; for a general perfectoid R, perfectoid quotients R → R/I (ECD §5) give (R/I)°/ϖ which is not flat over R°/ϖ, so flatness over the base is the wrong condition, and "the proof works in general" (Theorem 3.13) needs this adjustment. For the algebra in Proposition 9.3 (descended from (S̃+/ϖ)^a) Λ-flatness holds, so the conclusion stands.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E9** (BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, Lemma 3.21, proof, p. 27 (arXiv v3); gap, affects nothing). Printed: "Proof. Argue as in [57, Lemma 5.6]." Correction: The argument needs a unit multiple of π with compatible p-power roots (Lemma 3.9) to form the almost elements, and Sch12 Lemma 5.7 (p-root closedness) as well as Lemma 5.6; P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid writes the steps out. Reason: Sch12 Lemma 5.6 is over a perfectoid field K, whose elements ϖ^{1/p^n} and flatness over K° are used; neither is given in Lemma 3.21's setting without Lemma 3.9.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E10** (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lemma 2.8.1, displayed equalities, p. 69; misprint, affects nothing: P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting proves Theorem 2.4.2 through spectral gauges and sharp approximation and records Lemma 2.8.1 as the source's route). Printed: "zW (B [+ ) ∩ W (A[+ ) = zW (A[+ ), zW b (B [ ) ∩ W b (A[ ) = zW (B [ )" Correction: The second equality should read zW^b(B♭) ∩ W^b(A♭) = zW^b(A♭), parallel to the first. Reason: The right-hand side zW(B♭) is not contained in W^b(A♭) in general, so it cannot equal an intersection with W^b(A♭); the proof, "the second being similar", gives zW^b(A♭).
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E11** (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lemma 2.8.3, proof of "if", p. 70; gap, affects nothing: P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion gives an independent proof). Printed: "If there exists some c as described, then for m sufficiently large, the ideal of definition Im given by Lemma 2.8.2 has the property that ϕ : A◦ /Im → A◦ /Im^p is surjective, so A is perfectoid." Correction: Lemma 2.8.2 assumes that (A, A+) is perfectoid, which is what is being proved; the "if" direction follows instead by successive approximation from the metric condition (P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion, the argument of Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2(c)), or by rerunning the proof of Lemma 2.8.2 with the metric condition in place of Remark 2.1.5. Reason: As written the argument is circular: the ideals I_m of Lemma 2.8.2 are produced from Frobenius surjectivity (Remark 2.1.5), i.e. from perfectoidness.

### Acceptance tests of the layer

- ℚ_p is not perfectoid although Frobenius on F_p is bijective; ℂ_p[ε]/(ε²) is not perfectoid (not uniform); R⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid for R ≠ 0.
- ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, the completed perfection of F_p((t)), ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] are perfectoid; K × K♭ is perfectoid and not a field.
- In (ℚ_p^cycl)♭, ε♯ = 1 and (ε − 1)♯ ≠ 0 = ε♯ − 1♯; |(ε − 1)♯| = |p|^{p/(p−1)}; (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t = ε − 1.
- ker(θ: W(𝒪_{ℂ_p♭}) → 𝒪_{ℂ_p}) = (p − [p♭]) = (Σ_{i<p}[ε]^{i/p}); for characteristic-p rings ker θ = (p).
- Untilts of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^: (p) gives the field itself, (p − [t]) gives ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, (Σ_{i<p}[1+t]^{i/p}) gives ℚ_p^cycl.
- The tilt of R⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ is R♭⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ Σ⟩ for every perfectoid Tate ring R and every set Σ, finite or not.
- K⟨T⟩ is uniform with a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots and fails the metric criterion at T; the tilt of ℚ_p as a uniform Tate ring is the discrete field 𝔽_p; the completed colimit of the non-perfectoid ℚ_p(p^{1/p^n}) is perfectoid but its tilt is not the colimit of their tilts.
- Mathlib's PreTilt 𝒪_{ℂ_p} p, PreTilt.untilt, Tilt and fontaineTheta are identified with the objects of this layer.

<a id="p2"></a>

## P2. Rational localization, sheafiness, and perfectoid spaces


**Dependencies.** PerfectoidSpaces P0 (almost modules over a basic setup, the Serre class of almost
zero modules, almost Čech and sheaf cohomology) and P1 (perfectoid Tate rings, the tilt and the sharp
map, the integral subrings modulo ϖ, the tilting equivalence over a perfectoid base, the almost
setup of a perfectoid ring); the anchor `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces` Layers 2 (Spa, rational
subsets), 3 (rational localisation and the structure presheaf), 4 (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Tate
acyclicity) and 0.5 (strong noetherianness of affinoid algebras); `AdicSpacesPartII:R3` (Čech
acyclicity of O on sheafy Tate affinoids, Kedlaya–Liu 2.4.23) and `AdicSpacesPartII:R0` (reduced
affinoid algebras); `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0` (Čech-to-derived comparison, spectral spaces). The
perfectoid-space half of P2 (perfectoid spaces, glued tilting, fibre products, completed tensor
products) is written separately and builds on this part.

This part proves, for an **arbitrary perfectoid Tate pair** — no perfectoid base field, residue
characteristic p, characteristic 0, p, or neither — that the adic spectrum and its structure
presheaf are controlled by the tilt: the map `x ↦ x♭` is a homeomorphism identifying rational
subsets, rational localisations are perfectoid with tilt the rational localisation of the tilt, the
structure presheaf is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology, and `O⁺` is almost acyclic. These are
ECD Theorems 3.12, 3.18 and 3.24 in the generality of ECD Definition 3.1; Scholze 2012 proves them
over a perfectoid field and Kedlaya–Liu I over `ℚ_p`-algebras, and the general case is Kedlaya–Liu
II §3.3. The proofs follow Scholze's route (ECD: "the proof works in general"), with the Frobenius
argument of the Berkeley lectures for almost acyclicity in characteristic p and the tilting
reduction for the general case; Scholze's p-finite route through Tate's acyclicity theorem is kept
because the étale theory (P3) and AdicEtaleGeometry A3 reduce to p-finite algebras.

### Conventions

1. A prime p is fixed. A **perfectoid Tate pair** `(R, R⁺)` is a perfectoid Tate ring R (ECD
   Definition 3.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ such that `ϖ^p | p` in `R°` and
   `Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p` bijective) with a ring of integral elements `R⁺ ⊆ R°` (open, integrally closed;
   Tau Ceti `Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `Huber.Pair`). No base field is fixed.
2. `(R♭, R♭⁺)` is the tilt and `♯ : R♭ → R` the sharp map (continuous, multiplicative, not
   additive, additive modulo ϖ). We fix a pseudo-uniformizer `ϖ♭ ∈ R♭⁺` with `ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯` and
   `ϖ^p | p` in `R°`, and write `ϖ^r := ((ϖ♭)^r)♯` for `r ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{≥0}`.
3. `X = Spa(R, R⁺)` is Tau Ceti's `ValuationSpectrum.spa R⁺`, `X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)`. For `x ∈ X`,
   `|f(x)|` is the value of f in `Γ_x ∪ {0}`; inequalities between values are inequalities in the
   value group of the one point x.
4. `U(f₁, …, f_n / g) = {x : |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| ≠ 0}` with `f₁, …, f_n` generating the unit ideal
   (Tau Ceti `rationalSubset`). `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is the anchor's rational localisation
   (`PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `completedPlusSubring`), which must be presentation
   independent (anchor Layer 3.1).
5. **Almost zero** means killed by every topologically nilpotent element of `R⁺`, equivalently by
   all `ϖ^{1/p^n}` (P1, ECD Definition 3.21); a complex is almost exact if its cohomology is almost
   zero. `Mᵃ` is the image in the almost category (P0).
6. Sheaf cohomology is that of the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on the topological space
   (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`); Čech complexes are augmented and alternating.

### P2.1 The tilting map of spectra

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra` (construction). For `x ∈ X`, `v_x ∘ ♯` is a
continuous valuation of `R♭` bounded by 1 on `R♭⁺`; its class is `x♭`, characterised by

```text
|f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|        (f ∈ R♭).
```

The strong triangle inequality uses `(f + g)♯ = lim ((f^{1/p^n})♯ + (g^{1/p^n})♯)^{p^n}` and continuity of
`v_x` (Kedlaya AWS 2.6.12). The map `τ_R : X → X♭` has `supp(x♭) = ♯⁻¹ supp(x)`, is continuous, and
if some numerator is a unit of `R♭` (for instance `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`, a normalisation every rational
subset admits) then `τ⁻¹ U(f/g) = U(f♯/g♯)`. It is natural in morphisms of perfectoid pairs and is
the identity in characteristic p. It is not `Spa` of any ring map: for `K = ℚ_p^cycl` there is no ring
homomorphism `K♭ → K`.

API (derived from the uses listed in the node: P2b's perfectoid spaces, P3, DiamondsAndVStacks D1-D6, AdicSpacesPartII R5, AdicEtaleGeometry A3):

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt` | data | The map spa R⁺ → spa R♭⁺, x ↦ x♭, sending the valuation v_x to v_x ∘ ♯. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_vle_iff` | characterisation | For f g : R♭, (spaTilt x).vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.supp_spaTilt` | projection | The support of spaTilt x is the preimage under ♯ of the support of x. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.continuous_spaTilt` | other | spaTilt is continuous. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset` | compatibility | If some f_i ∈ T is a unit of R♭, then spaTilt ⁻¹' rationalSubset R♭⁺ T s = rationalSubset R⁺ (T.image ♯) s♯. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.exists_rationalSubset_eq_insert_pseudoUniformizer_pow` | other | Every rational subset of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) equals rationalSubset R♭⁺ (insert ((ϖ♭)^N) T) s with T ⊆ R♭⁺, s ∈ R♭⁺, for some N. |
