Unit tests (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `spaTilt_test_perfectoidDisc_point` (computation): For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and x the point T ↦ ϖ, spaTilt x is the point T ↦ ϖ♭ of Q_p^cycl♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: |T(x♭)| = |T♯(x)| = |ϖ(x)|.
- `spaTilt_test_charP_eq_id` (degenerate): For R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (characteristic p), spaTilt is the identity of Spa(R, R⁺).
- `spaTilt_test_preimage_disc` (compatibility): On the perfectoid disc over Q_p^cycl, spaTilt ⁻¹' U({T, ϖ♭}/ϖ♭) = U({T, ϖ}/ϖ), the instance of spaTilt_preimage_rationalSubset with f₂ = ϖ♭.
- `spaTilt_test_no_ringHom` (non-example): There is no ring homomorphism Q_p^cycl♭ → Q_p^cycl, so spaTilt is not Pair.Hom.spaComap of any morphism of Huber pairs; a definition of x♭ as the pullback of x along a ring map cannot typecheck in mixed characteristic.
- `spaTilt_test_vle_characterisation` (characterisation): x♭ is the unique point y of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) with y.vle f g ↔ x.vle f♯ g♯ for all f g; two points of Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) with the same relation coincide.


### P2.2 Rational localisation in characteristic p

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-in-characteristic-p` (lemma). If `pR = 0`, every rational
localisation of `(R, R⁺)` is perfect (Frobenius extends through the universal property and is
inverted by the extension of `Φ⁻¹`), hence perfectoid (ECD 3.5), hence uniform: `(R, R⁺)` is stably
uniform (Kedlaya–Liu I 3.1.7). For `f_i, g ∈ R⁺`, `f_n = ϖ^N`, the ϖ-adic completion
`A_U = R⁺⟨(f/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩` is perfect, ϖ-torsion free, `A_U ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)°` with almost zero
quotients, and the presentation `R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}] → R⁺[(f/g)^{1/p^∞}]` has kernel almost equal to the ideal
generated by the `g^{1/p^m}T_i^{1/p^m} − f_i^{1/p^m}` (a ϖ-power-torsion ideal of a perfect ring is
almost zero; Sch12 6.4, Bhatt 9.2.3).

### P2.3 Lifting almost exactness from reduction modulo ϖ

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-exactness-from-reduction-mod-pseudouniformizer` (lemma). For an ideal m with
`m² = m`: (a) a bounded complex of ϖ-torsion-free, ϖ-adically complete and separated modules whose
reduction modulo ϖ is almost exact is almost exact — the Milnor sequence
`0 → lim¹ H^{q−1}(C/ϖ^n) → H^q(C) → lim H^q(C/ϖ^n) → 0` is used and its `lim¹` term is almost zero because
it is a quotient of a product of almost zero modules; (b) conversely for torsion-free terms; (c) a map
from a separated module to a torsion-free one which is almost surjective and an almost isomorphism
modulo ϖ is an almost isomorphism (Bhatt's footnote to 9.2.5). Completeness is necessary:
`[ℚ_p → 0]` is exact modulo p but not exact.

### P2.4 Untilted rational localisation

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/almost-integral-model-of-untilted-rational-localization` (lemma). For
`f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺` with `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`, `U = U(f/g) ⊆ X♭` and `U♯ = τ⁻¹U = U(f♯/g♯)`:

```text
O_X(U♯)°ᵃ = R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩ᵃ,       O_X(U♯) perfectoid,       (O_X(U♯), O_X⁺(U♯))♭ = (O_{X♭}(U), O_{X♭}⁺(U)).
```

Proof: untilt `O_{X♭}(U)` over R to `(S, S⁺)` (P1's tilting equivalence over R); `Spa(S, S⁺)` lands in
`U♯` by naturality of τ, giving `O_X(U♯) → S`; modulo ϖ the composite from the presentation is the
characteristic-p presentation of P2.2 (♯ is additive modulo ϖ), hence an almost isomorphism, and
P2.3(c) lifts it. This is Sch12 Lemma 6.4 and Bhatt Lemma 9.2.5 over a perfectoid base; Kedlaya AWS
2.8.8 gives the exact (not almost) presentation of the untilted localisation.

### P2.5 Approximation

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-on-perfectoid-polydisc` (lemma). Over any perfectoid Tate ring
`R₀`, for `P = R₀⟨T₀^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩` graded by T-degree and `f ∈ P°` homogeneous of degree d, for
rational `c ≥ 0` and `ε ∈ ℤ[1/p] ∩ (0, 1)` there is a homogeneous `g ∈ P♭°` of degree d with

```text
|f(x) − g♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ^{1−ε}(x)| · max(|f(x)|, |ϖ^c(x)|)        (x ∈ Spa(P, P°)),
```

by Scholze's induction on c, losing `ε(c)` at each step through the almost model of P2.4 on
`U_c = {|g_c| ≤ |ϖ♭|^c}`; the base case lifts f modulo ϖ.

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma` (lemma). The same estimate for every `f ∈ R` on `X`, with
`g ∈ R♭` (reduce to rank-one points and to `f = Σ_{j ≤ c} ϖ^j g_j♯`, then pull back from the polydisc over
R); and for `f, h ∈ R` and `c ∈ ℕ` there are `a, b ∈ R♭` with
`{|f| ≤ |h|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |h|} = {|a♯| ≤ |b♯|, |ϖ^c| ≤ |b♯|}`. Independently: Kedlaya–Liu II 3.2.7 and Kedlaya
AWS 2.6.17 by Euclidean division in `W(R♭⁺)`.

### P2.6 The tilting homeomorphism

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets` (theorem, planet *The tilting
homeomorphism*). `τ_R : Spa(R, R⁺) → Spa(R♭, R♭⁺)` is a homeomorphism, natural in the pair; U is
rational iff `τ(U)` is, with `τ(U(f♯/g♯)) = U(f/g)` for `f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺`, `f_n = (ϖ♭)^N`, and every rational
subset of X has this form. Proof: every rational subset is a preimage (P2.5 and `rationalSubset_inter`),
so τ is injective (X is spectral, hence `T₀`); surjectivity untilts the perfectoid completed residue
field of a point of `X♭` over R and then its valuation ring; rational images give openness. Hypotheses:
ECD 3.12 in general; Sch12 6.3(i) is the field case; Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.16 and Kedlaya AWS 2.5.1 give
independent proofs. The rational-subset clause needs the approximation lemma: without it one only gets
preimages of quasi-compact opens (Bhatt Remark 9.2.8).

### P2.7 Rational localisation of perfectoid Tate pairs

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids` (construction, planet *Rational
localization*). For every rational `U ⊆ X`, `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is a perfectoid Tate pair and

```text
(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU))      (unique, compatible with the maps from (R♭, R♭⁺) and with ♯),
```

with almost integral model `R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩` for a presentation `U = U(f♯/g♯)`. It is the rational
localisation among perfectoid pairs, and tilting is an equivalence between the rational localisations
of `(R, R⁺)` and of `(R♭, R♭⁺)` (Kedlaya AWS 2.5.3(b)). This answers the AdicSpacesPartII request
(R5/sousperfectoid-rational-localisation, R5/sousperfectoid-stably-uniform): no base field is needed.
The tilt cannot be read off by tilting the universal property, which quantifies over all Huber pairs;
it comes from P2.4.

API (derived from the uses listed in the node: P2b's perfectoid spaces, P3, DiamondsAndVStacks D1-D6, AdicSpacesPartII R5, AdicEtaleGeometry A3):

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization` | data | The perfectoid Tate pair (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) of a rational subset U of Spa(R, R⁺), bundled with its structure morphism of Huber pairs from (R, R⁺). |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.isPerfectoidTateRing` | instance | O_X(U) is a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD 3.18; no base field). |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv` | equivalence | The isomorphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ ≅ (O_{X♭}(τ U), O_{X♭}⁺(τ U)). |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_comp_structureMap` | compatibility | tiltEquiv composed with the tilt of the structure map R → O_X(U) is the structure map R♭ → O_{X♭}(τ U); equivalently sharp commutes with the structure maps. |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.lift` | universal-property | For a morphism φ : (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) of Huber pairs with S complete and Spa(φ)(Spa(S, S⁺)) ⊆ U, the unique morphism (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) → (S, S⁺) over (R, R⁺); lift_comp_structureMap and hom_ext. |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.image_spaTilt` | compatibility | τ(U(f♯/g♯)) = U(f/g) for f_i, g ∈ R♭⁺ with f_n = (ϖ♭)^N, and every rational U has such a presentation. |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.almostEquivIntegralModel` | characterisation | O_X⁺(U)ᵃ ≅ (R⁺⟨(f♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩)ᵃ as R⁺ᵃ-algebras for such a presentation. |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.tiltEquivalence` | equivalence | Tilting is an equivalence from the category of rational localisations of (R, R⁺) to that of (R♭, R♭⁺), U ↦ τ U (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.3(b)). |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.isUniform` | instance | O_X(U) is uniform: O_X(U)° is bounded (consumed by stable uniformity). |
| `Perfectoid.rationalLocalization.tiltEquiv_of_charP` | simp | If pR = 0, tiltEquiv is the identity under the identification of a characteristic-p perfectoid pair with its tilt. |

Unit tests (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `rationalLocalization_test_perfectoidDisc` (computation): For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, rationalLocalization R⁺ U ≅ Q_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩ and tiltEquiv identifies its tilt with Q_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- `rationalLocalization_test_noBaseField` (compatibility): For R of ECD Example 3.4(iv) and U = {|T| ≤ |p|}, isPerfectoidTateRing holds for O_X(U) and p is a unit there; the statement must not require an algebra structure over a perfectoid field.
- `rationalLocalization_test_charP` (degenerate): If pR = 0 then tiltEquiv is the identity of (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) and the almost integral model is R⁺⟨(f/g)^{1/p^∞}⟩ itself.
- `rationalLocalization_test_naiveModel` (non-example): The naive model R°⟨f♯/g♯⟩ without p-power roots is not almost equal to O_X(U)°: for R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, (T/ϖ)^{1/p} ∈ O_X(U)° but ϖ^{1/p}(T/ϖ)^{1/p} ∉ R°⟨T/ϖ⟩, so a definition of almostIntegralModel without the roots (f♯/g♯)^{1/p^m} fails.
- `rationalLocalization_test_whole_space` (characterisation): For U = X = U({1}/1), rationalLocalization is (R, R⁺) itself (the anchor's O_X(X) ≅ R) and tiltEquiv is the identity of (R♭, R♭⁺).


### P2.8 The presheaf of perfectoid pairs on rational subsets

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction` (construction). `U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` is a
functor on rational subsets with values in perfectoid Tate pairs; each restriction `ρ_{U,V}` is the
rational localisation of `(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))` at V; `O_X⁺(U) = {f : |f(x)| ≤ 1 on U}`,
`O_X(U)°° ⊆ O_X⁺(U) ⊆ O_X(U)°` and `O_X(U)°/O_X⁺(U)` is almost zero; tilting is a natural isomorphism of
functors, so the ♯-isomorphisms `O_{X♭}⁺(τU)/ϖ♭ ≅ O_X⁺(U)/ϖ` commute with restriction (for `U = X` this
is ECD 3.11); and the identifications `Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U` intertwine the tilting maps. The plus
ring is not `O°` in general: for `R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`, `T ∈ R° \ R⁺`.

API (derived from the uses listed in the node: P2b's perfectoid spaces, P3, DiamondsAndVStacks D1-D6, AdicSpacesPartII R5, AdicEtaleGeometry A3):

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor` | data | The functor (rational subsets of Spa(R, R⁺), ⊇) → perfectoid Tate pairs, U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)), with the anchor's restriction maps. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.map_comp` | functoriality | ρ_{V,W} ∘ ρ_{U,V} = ρ_{U,W} and ρ_{U,U} = id, as morphisms of Huber pairs. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.isRationalLocalization_map` | universal-property | For V ⊆ U, ρ_{U,V} is the rational localisation of (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) at V (transitivity). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.mem_plus_iff` | characterisation | f ∈ O_X⁺(U) ↔ ∀ x ∈ U, \|f(x)\| ≤ 1. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.isAlmostZero_powerBounded_quot_plus` | relation | O_X(U)°/O_X⁺(U) is almost zero; hence O_X⁺(U)ᵃ = O_X(U)°ᵃ. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.tiltIso` | equivalence | The natural isomorphism between U ↦ (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U))♭ and U ↦ (O_{X♭}(τU), O_{X♭}⁺(τU)). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.plusModEquiv` | compatibility | The ring isomorphisms O_{X♭}⁺(τU)/ϖ♭ ≅ O_X⁺(U)/ϖ induced by ♯, natural in U. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.rationalPairFunctor.spaTilt_comm` | compatibility | Under Spa(O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) ≅ U and its tilt, spaTilt of O_X(U) is the restriction of spaTilt of R. |

Unit tests (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `rationalPairFunctor_test_restriction_disc` (computation): For R = Q_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|²} ⊆ U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, the restriction sends (T/ϖ)^{1/p^m} to ϖ^{1/p^m}(T/ϖ²)^{1/p^m}, and tiltIso transports it to the same formula over Q_p^cycl♭ with ϖ♭.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_plusModEquiv_whole` (compatibility): For U = X, plusModEquiv is the ring isomorphism R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ induced by ♯ (ECD Lemma 3.11), and naturality for V ⊆ X is the commutation with R⁺/ϖ → O_X⁺(V)/ϖ.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_plus_ne_powerBounded` (non-example): For K = Q_p^cycl, R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and R⁺ = K° + K°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (open, integrally closed), T ∈ R° \ R⁺ while ϖ^{1/p^n}T ∈ R⁺ for all n; a definition of the plus presheaf by O_X(U)° would violate mem_plus_iff at the points of Spa(R, R⁺) where |T| > 1.
- `rationalPairFunctor_test_charP` (degenerate): If pR = 0, tiltIso is the identity natural transformation and plusModEquiv is the identity of O_X⁺(U)/ϖ.


### P2.9 Completed residue fields

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields` (theorem). For `x ∈ X`, the completed residue affinoid
field `(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺)` (anchor Layer 3) is a perfectoid field with an open valuation ring, and its tilt
is `(k(x♭)^, k(x♭)^⁺)`, compatibly with `R → k(x)^`, `R♭ → k(x♭)^` and ♯; value groups of x and `x♭`
agree. Proof: `k(x)^` receives a dense-image map from the completed colimit of the perfectoid
`O_X(U)`, `U ∋ x`, and a uniform ring with such a map is perfectoid (Kedlaya–Liu II 3.3.18(ii),
3.3.22; Kedlaya AWS 2.5.7); a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field is a perfectoid field
(ECD 3.6).

### P2.10 Stable uniformity and sheafiness

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy` (theorem). `(R, R⁺)` is stably uniform and
sheafy (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, anchor Layer 4.2), `O_X⁺` is a sheaf, and for every finite rational
covering of a rational U the Čech complex of O is exact in all degrees with `H^i(U, O_X) = 0` for
`i > 0` (`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity`); none of this depends on `R⁺`. Kedlaya–Liu I
3.6.15, II 3.3.19, Berkeley 6.1.10, Hansen–Kedlaya 3.15, Kedlaya AWS 2.5.4.

### P2.11 Integral Čech cohomology

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-cech-cohomology-bounded-torsion` (lemma). For any stably uniform sheafy
complete Tate pair, the `O⁺`-Čech complex of a finite rational covering of a rational U (and the
`O°`-complex) has cohomology killed by one power `ϖ^N`: the O-complex is exact, its terms are complete
metrisable with `O⁺` open and bounded, and the open mapping theorem over a Tate ring (Tau Ceti
`IsTateRing.isOpenMap`) makes subspace and quotient topologies on `ker d = im d` agree (Sch12 6.10,
Berkeley 7.4.4). Example: the Laurent covering of the closed disc gives `N = 0`.

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity` (theorem). For every rational `U ⊆ X` and every finite
rational covering 𝔘 of U, the augmented Čech complex `C⁺(𝔘)` of `O_X⁺` is almost exact (and exact at its
first two terms). In characteristic p, Frobenius is bijective on `C⁺(𝔘)` and semilinear, so a bound
`ϖ^N` improves to `ϖ^{N/p^k}` for all k. In general, τ transports 𝔘 to `τ𝔘`, P2.8 identifies
`C⁺(𝔘)/ϖ` with `C⁺(τ𝔘)/ϖ♭`, and P2.3 lifts almost exactness. With P2.12 this gives `H^i(U, O_X⁺)` almost zero for every rational U and `i > 0`.

### P2.12 From Čech to sheaf cohomology

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/cech-to-sheaf-cohomology-on-rational-basis` (lemma). On a space with a basis ℬ of
quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersections, if every finite ℬ-covering of every member of ℬ
has almost zero higher Čech cohomology for a sheaf F of V-modules (`m² = m`), then `H^q(U, F)` is almost
zero for `U ∈ ℬ`, `q ≥ 1`. The proof is Cartan's (Stacks 01EW) run modulo almost zero modules: with
`0 → F → I → G → 0`, I injective, `H¹(U, F)` is almost zero by gluing ε-multiples of local lifts, G
inherits the hypothesis, and one inducts. For `m = V` this is Cartan's criterion
(`DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison`).

### P2.13 The sheaf theorem

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity` (theorem, planet *The sheaf theorem*). For
every perfectoid Tate pair `(R, R⁺)` and `X = Spa(R, R⁺)`:

```text
O_X and O_X⁺ are sheaves;   O_X(U) perfectoid with tilt O_{X♭}(U♭) for rational U;
H⁰(X, O_X) = R,  H^i(X, O_X) = 0  (i > 0);   H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺,  H^i(X, O_X⁺) almost zero  (i > 0),
```

and the same on every rational U; equivalently `H^i(X, O_X⁺ᵃ) = H^i(X, O_X°ᵃ) = 0` for `i > 0` (Sch12
Remark 6.12). This is ECD 3.18 and 3.24; the degree-0 statement `H⁰(X, O_X⁺) = R⁺` is Wedhorn 7.52(1)
(Tau Ceti `mem_iff_forall_vle_one`). Almost zero cannot be replaced by zero in general.

### P2.14 The p-finite route (Scholze 2012)

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate` (lemma). Over a perfectoid field K of
characteristic p, a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra is **p-finite** if it is the completed perfection of
a reduced affinoid K-algebra `(S, S⁺)` of topologically finite type (Sch12 6.9). Then `S°` is open and
bounded (AdicSpacesPartII:R0), rational localisations of S are reduced affinoid (BGR 7.3.2; requested),
the O°-Čech complexes of Y = Spa(S, S⁺) have bounded torsion (anchor Layer 4.1 and P2.11),
`Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Y` with rational subsets, rational localisations are completed perfections, and the
`O°ᵃ`-Čech complexes of `Spa(R, R⁺)` are exact.

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids` (lemma). If `R⁺` is a `K°`-algebra
(always arranged with `K = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^∧`, `t ↦ ϖ`), `(R, R⁺)` is the completed filtered colimit of the
p-finite `(R_I, R_I⁺)` built from finite `I ⊆ R⁺` (`R⁺/ϖ^n = colim R_I⁺/ϖ^n`), `Spa(R, R⁺) = lim Spa(R_I, R_I⁺)`,
rational subsets and their localisations come from a finite stage, and a quasi-compact open containing
the image of X contains the image of some `X_J`. Consumers: P3 (Sch12 7.6, 7.7, 7.13), P5, and
AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/char-p-perfectoid-base-field.

### Acceptance tests of the part

- `ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩`: `τ{|T| ≤ |ϖ|} = {|T| ≤ |ϖ♭|}`; `O_X({|T| ≤ |ϖ|}) = ℚ_p^cycl⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩` with tilt
  `ℚ_p^cycl♭⟨(T/ϖ♭)^{1/p^∞}⟩`; completed residue field at the Gauss point perfectoid; Laurent covering
  integrally exact.
- ECD Example 3.4(iv), `R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T]`, which lives over no field: the
  homeomorphism, the rational localisation at `U = {|T| ≤ |p|}` (perfectoid, with p a unit there) and the
  sheaf theorem apply.
- Characteristic p: every construction degenerates to the identity under tilting, and stable
  uniformity follows from perfectness alone.
- Sch12 Theorem 6.3, Corollaries 6.7-6.8, Proposition 6.14 are recovered over a perfectoid field.

### Requests and gaps of this part

Requested: anchor Layer 3 (presentation-independent rational localisation, structure presheaves,
`IsSheafyPair`, completed residue affinoid fields), Layer 4 (pair-level Buzzard–Verberkmoes; all-degree
Tate acyclicity for strongly noetherian pairs), Layer 2 (Wedhorn 7.48 and 8.2(2), normal form of rational
subsets), Layer 0.5 (strong noetherianness of affinoid algebras), `AdicSpacesPartII:R0` (reducedness of
rational localisations of reduced affinoid algebras). Gaps: the general-base write-up of Sch12 6.4-6.5,
the tilt of completed residue fields, and BGR 7.3.2 (the general-base tilting equivalence is
PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt). Source issues: ECD's attribution of 3.12/3.18/3.24 to [KL15] (the general case is [KL16]); small
misprints in Sch12 6.10(i) and 6.13(iv), Kedlaya AWS 2.9.5, Kedlaya–Liu I 3.6.14 and II 3.3.16.


**Dependencies:** anchor Layers 2, 3 and 5 (`tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces`: adic spectra and rational
subsets, rational localisation and global sections, the category of adic spaces with open subspaces, gluing
and maps into affinoids), anchor Layer 4.2 (uniformity; Buzzard–Verberkmoes, through P2's affinoid part),
AdicSpacesPartII R0 (completed and uniform completed tensor products of Huber pairs, the affinoid fibre
product, uniformisation), PerfectoidSpaces P0 (almost mathematics), P1 (perfectoid Tate rings, tilts,
untilts, the ring-level tilting equivalence, the tilt of a uniform Tate ring, strict inclusions under tilting, the
metric perfectoid criterion, perfected Tate algebras in any set of variables), and the affinoid half of this layer (rational localisation of
perfectoid Tate pairs, the tilting homeomorphism, sheafiness and almost acyclicity, completed residue fields).

This half of P2 turns perfectoid Tate rings into geometry. A perfectoid space is an adic space in the anchor's
sense — nothing else — which is locally the adic spectrum of a perfectoid Huber pair; the category **Perfd**
of perfectoid spaces is a *full subcategory* of the anchor's category of adic spaces, so open subspaces,
gluing and the sheaf property of morphisms are imported, not rebuilt. On top of this the layer constructs the
tilt X ↦ X♭ by gluing the affinoid tilts along rational subsets, proves Scholze's tilting equivalence of
slice categories Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭ (ECD Corollary 3.20) over an arbitrary perfectoid base, shows that
completed tensor products of perfectoid Tate pairs are perfectoid, uniform and commute with tilting, and deduces
that Perfd has all fibre products, computed in adic spaces. It also treats the two neighbouring
constructions that consumers need and that are *not* fibre products over a perfectoid base: fibre products
over a non-perfectoid analytic base (which exist in Perfd through the uniform completed tensor product), and
absolute products in Perf, which exist although Perf has no final object and although the discrete
Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) over which they are fibre products is not a perfectoid space. Scholze's original notion of
perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K is identified with the slice over Spa(K, K⁺₀), K⁺₀ the smallest
ring of integral elements of K.

No perfectoid base field is fixed anywhere in this part: every statement holds over perfectoid Tate rings
in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, in characteristic 0 and p. The field-level statements of Scholze's
*Perfectoid spaces* (Propositions 6.17 and 6.18) are acceptance tests.

### Conventions

1. p is a fixed prime. A *perfectoid Tate ring* is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring R with a
   pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective (ECD Definition 3.1;
   P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). The zero ring is perfectoid. A *perfectoid Tate pair* is a complete
   Hausdorff Huber pair (R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with R perfectoid; R⁺ is any ring of integral
   elements, and it need not contain the ring of integers of any field.
2. *Adic spaces* are the objects of the anchor's category (Layer 5: objects of Huber's category 𝒱 locally
   isomorphic to Spa of a sheafy pair), with its morphisms. **Perfd** and **Perf** are full subcategories
   (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`); no second carrier is introduced.
3. *Affinoid perfectoid* means isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) for a perfectoid Tate pair (Berkeley Remark 7.1.3), a
   condition on a presentation, not "affinoid and perfectoid"; the two agree in characteristic p (Mihara)
   and their agreement in characteristic 0 is not asserted.
4. The completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C is AdicSpacesPartII R0's: the completion of B ⊗_A C for the topology
   of the image of rings of definition, with plus ring the **closure of the integral closure** of the image of
   B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺. For perfectoid A it is automatically uniform; over a non-perfectoid base the uniformisation
   B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C is used and named explicitly.
5. Almost mathematics is with respect to the basic setup (A°, A°°) of a perfectoid Tate ring A
   (P1/perfectoid-almost-setup): almost zero means killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}.
6. The tilt of a pair is (R♭, R♭⁺) = (lim_{x ↦ x^p} R, lim_{x ↦ x^p} R⁺); the sharp map f ↦ f♯ is continuous
   and multiplicative, never assumed additive.
7. Perf is the full subcategory of Perfd of spaces with p = 0 in O_X(X). The discrete adic space
   Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) is an adic space but not a perfectoid space; Perf has no final object.


### P2b.1 Affinoid perfectoid spaces: adic spectra of perfectoid Huber pairs

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space` (definition). An adic space X is affinoid perfectoid if X ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) for a perfectoid Tate pair. Spa(R, R⁺) is an adic space because perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), and it recovers the pair: (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) ≅ (R, R⁺) (anchor Layer 3.5; ECD Theorem 3.24 for O⁺). By Wedhorn Proposition 8.25, Spa is an anti-equivalence from complete perfectoid Tate pairs (morphisms `Huber.Pair.Hom`) to affinoid perfectoid spaces.

**Statement.** An adic space X (an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces, Layer 5: an object of Huber's category 𝒱 locally isomorphic to the adic spectrum of a sheafy Huber pair) is *affinoid perfectoid* if there are a complete Hausdorff Huber pair (R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`: R⁺ ⊆ R° open and integrally closed) with R a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective) and an isomorphism of adic spaces X ≅ Spa(R, R⁺). Here Spa(R, R⁺) is an adic space because perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy). For such X the global sections recover the pair: (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) ≅ (R, R⁺) as topological rings with plus rings (anchor Layer 3.5, and O_X⁺(X) = {f : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} = R⁺ by Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)), so X is affinoid perfectoid iff X is affinoid in the anchor's sense and O_X(X) is a perfectoid Tate ring, and then X ≅ Spa(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) canonically. By Wedhorn Proposition 8.25, Spa is an anti-equivalence from complete perfectoid Huber pairs with morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`: continuous ring maps carrying plus ring into plus ring) to the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Pinned conventions: (1) the predicate asks for a presentation by a perfectoid ring (Berkeley Remark 7.1.3); it is not the conjunction 'affinoid and a perfectoid space', the two agree in characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion), and their agreement in characteristic 0 is not asserted; (2) no perfectoid base field is fixed, R⁺ is an arbitrary ring of integral elements, and the zero ring is allowed, so the empty adic space is affinoid perfectoid; (3) morphisms are morphisms of adic spaces. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsAffinoidPerfectoid X`.

**Hypotheses.** X is an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces (Layer 5). (R, R⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair and R is a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1).

**Proof outline.**

1. Spa(R, R⁺) is an adic space: rational localisations of (R, R⁺) are perfectoid, hence uniform, so (R, R⁺) is stably uniform and sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy, which uses the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem of anchor Layer 4.2).
2. Global sections: for a complete Hausdorff sheafy pair O_X(X) ≅ R as topological rings (anchor Layer 3.5), and O_X⁺(X) = {f ∈ R : v(f) ≤ 1 for all v ∈ Spa(R, R⁺)} = R⁺ (anchor Layer 2.3, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)); ECD Theorem 3.24 (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity) gives the same for H⁰(X, O_X⁺).
3. Anti-equivalence: morphisms Y → Spa(R, R⁺) from an adic space Y correspond to morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25, requested from anchor Layer 5); with the previous step, Spa is fully faithful on complete perfectoid Tate pairs, and essentially surjective onto affinoid perfectoid spaces by definition.
4. Closure under isomorphisms and the analytic and spectral properties of |X| follow from the Tau Ceti results on Spa of a Tate Huber ring (every point analytic; Spa spectral).

**API** (derived from the uses: ECD Definition 1.1 and §7 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6); ECD Proposition 8.3 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/perfectoid-sheaf-topoi-are-algebraic); ECD Proposition 6.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces); DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient; DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/automatic-flatness; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids; Berkeley Remark 7.1.3).

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spa_Cp` (computation): Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) is affinoid perfectoid and its underlying space is a single point (the rank-one valuation).
- `not_isAffinoidPerfectoid_spa_Qp` (non-example): Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is an affinoid adic space (strongly noetherian, anchor Layer 4.1) but not affinoid perfectoid: any isomorphism Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) gives R ≅ O(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)) = ℚ_p, which is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3). A definition asking only for surjective Frobenius on the residue field would accept it.
- `isAffinoidPerfectoid_empty` (degenerate): The empty adic space is affinoid perfectoid, presented by the zero ring with the zero plus ring (0 is a pseudouniformiser of the zero ring and ECD Definition 3.1 holds vacuously); a definition requiring a nonzero ring or a base field fails this.
- `IsAffinoidPerfectoid.spa_ecd34iv` (computation): For R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] with ϖ = T^{1/p} (ECD Example 3.4(iv); PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), Spa(R, R°) is affinoid perfectoid; the definition does not require a perfectoid base field.
- `spaHomEquiv_perfectoidField` (characterisation): For a perfectoid field K and a complete perfectoid Tate pair (S, S⁺), morphisms Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(K, K°) are exactly the continuous ring maps K → S carrying K° into S⁺.
- `isAffinoidPerfectoid_iff_affinoid_sections` (compatibility): An adic space X is affinoid perfectoid iff it is isomorphic to the anchor's Spa of a complete sheafy Huber pair (an affinoid adic space, anchor Layer 5) and O_X(X) is a perfectoid Tate ring.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) is affinoid perfectoid, and it has exactly one point.
- Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is an affinoid adic space that is not affinoid perfectoid, because O(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)) = ℚ_p is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
- For the perfectoid Tate ring R = ℤ_p^cycl[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] of ECD Example 3.4(iv), which does not live over a perfectoid field, Spa(R, R°) is affinoid perfectoid.

### P2b.2 Perfectoid spaces: the full subcategory Perfd of adic spaces, and Perf in characteristic p

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space` (definition, planet *Perfectoid space*). A perfectoid space is an adic space covered by affinoid perfectoid open subspaces (ECD Definition 3.19). Every point is analytic, so every morphism into a perfectoid space is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism). Perf is cut out by p = 0 in O_X(X), equivalently by the existence of the (unique) morphism to the discrete Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p); in characteristic p, perfectoid means locally Spa of a perfect complete Tate ring (ECD Proposition 3.5).

**Statement.** A *perfectoid space* is an adic space X (anchor Layer 5) covered by open subspaces that are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space): every x ∈ X has an open neighbourhood U such that the open adic subspace (U, O_X|_U, (v_y)_{y ∈ U}) is isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring and R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements (ECD Definition 3.19). The category Perfd of perfectoid spaces is the full subcategory of the anchor's category of adic spaces on these objects (Mathlib `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`): morphisms are morphisms of adic spaces; open subspaces, gluing and the sheaf property of morphisms are the anchor's, and no second carrier (no separate locally ringed space and no second gluing theory) is introduced. Perf ⊆ Perfd is the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p, those with p = 0 in O_X(X); equivalently, X admits a morphism (necessarily unique) to the discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p), which is an adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy) but not a perfectoid space, and which Perf does not contain. Properties pinned with the definition: every point of a perfectoid space is analytic, so every morphism of adic spaces into a perfectoid space is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism); an adic space with p = 0 in its structure sheaf is perfectoid iff it is covered by open subspaces Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfect complete Tate ring (ECD Proposition 3.5). Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.IsPerfectoidSpace X`, the category `PerfectoidSpace`, and `PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.

**Hypotheses.** X is an object of the anchor's category of adic spaces. p is a fixed prime.

**Proof outline.**

1. The predicate is local on X and invariant under isomorphisms; Perfd := ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory IsPerfectoidSpace with the fully faithful inclusion ObjectProperty.ι (Mathlib).
2. Analyticity: an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R⁺) has R Tate, so all its points are analytic (Tau Ceti ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing); being analytic is local, so every perfectoid space is analytic and every morphism into it is adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus).
3. Characteristic p: p = 0 in O_X(X) iff p = 0 in O_X(U) for all U (restriction maps are ring maps and O_X is a sheaf), iff there is a morphism of Huber pairs (𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) → (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) (continuity is automatic from the discrete topology and 𝔽_p is integral over ℤ), iff X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) exists (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25); uniqueness because 𝔽_p has only one ring map to a ring of characteristic p.
4. Perfect-ring criterion: ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) identifies perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p with perfect complete Tate rings, chart by chart.

**API** (derived from the uses: ECD Definition 8.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site); ECD §1 and Definition 8.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond); DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/totally-disconnected-perfectoid-space; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces; PerfectoidSpaces:P4 (ECD §5); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting).

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `isPerfectoidSpace_empty` (degenerate): The empty adic space is a perfectoid space (it is covered by the empty family).
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_spa_Qp` (non-example): Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is not a perfectoid space: its only nonempty open subset is the whole space, whose ring ℚ_p is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_closedUnitDisc_Qp` (non-example): The closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) is not a perfectoid space: the classical point T = 0 has completed residue field ℚ_p, which is discretely valued and not perfectoid, whereas every completed residue field of a perfectoid space is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields; Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7).
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_spa_Fp` (non-example): The discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) is an adic space of characteristic p (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy) and is not perfectoid: its unique point has open support, so it is not analytic. Hence a construction that treats Spa 𝔽_p as a perfectoid Tate space, e.g. as a final object of Perf, is wrong.
- `isPerfectoidSpace_discWithDoubledOrigin` (computation): Gluing two copies of the perfectoid closed disc Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) along the open complement of the point T = 0 (anchor Layer 5.3) gives a perfectoid space which is quasi-compact but not quasi-separated: the two affinoid perfectoid charts meet in a non-quasi-compact open.
- `isSousperfectoid_of_isPerfectoidSpace` (compatibility): Every perfectoid space is a sousperfectoid adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space), a perfectoid ring being its own perfectoid frame (identity section); both notions are full subcategories of the same anchor category.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}), Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl) and the perfectoid closed disc Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) are perfectoid spaces; Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) lies in Perf.
- Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p), the closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and the discrete Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) are adic spaces that are not perfectoid.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ι`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.fullyFaithfulι`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`, `mathlib:CharP`.

**Sources.** Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Definition 3.19, p. 18; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 7, §7.1, Definition 7.1.2, printed p. 49; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 1, p. 3; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Proposition 3.5, p. 15.

### P2b.3 Rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid opens are affinoid perfectoid, and affinoid perfectoid opens form a basis

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis` (lemma). Rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid opens are affinoid perfectoid, with rings the rational localisations; affinoid perfectoid opens form a basis; two of them share, around each common point, an open rational in both (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3)); and O_X(V) is perfectoid with V ≅ Spa(O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) for every affinoid perfectoid open V. The intersection of two affinoid perfectoid opens need not be quasi-compact.

**Statement.** Let X be a perfectoid space. (i) If V ⊆ X is an open subspace with an isomorphism V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid, then for every rational subset W = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, T·R open) the open subspace W ⊆ X is affinoid perfectoid: W ≅ Spa(R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺), where (R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) is the rational localisation of anchor Layer 3.1, a perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), and (O_X(W), O_X⁺(W)) ≅ (R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) compatibly with restriction from V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction). (ii) The affinoid perfectoid open subspaces of X form a basis of the topology of |X|; every quasi-compact open subset of X is a finite union of them. (iii) For affinoid perfectoid opens V, V' ⊆ X and x ∈ V ∩ V' there is an open W with x ∈ W ⊆ V ∩ V' that is a rational subset of V and of V' (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3)), hence affinoid perfectoid by (i). (iv) For every affinoid perfectoid open V ⊆ X, O_X(V) is a perfectoid Tate ring and V ≅ Spa(O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) canonically (the observation in the proof of Sch12 Proposition 6.17). The intersection of two affinoid perfectoid opens need not be affinoid, nor quasi-compact.

**Hypotheses.** X a perfectoid space; V ⊆ X an open subspace with V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid. W = R(T/s) a rational subset of Spa(R, R⁺) with T·R open (for R Tate: T generates the unit ideal).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) The open subspace W ⊆ V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) is isomorphic to Spa of the rational localisation (anchor Layer 3.1: Spa(R⟨T/s⟩, R⟨T/s⟩⁺) ≅ W matching valuations and rational subsets, Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph` on underlying spaces), and the rational localisation of a perfectoid Tate pair is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
2. (ii) Rational subsets form a basis of Spa(R, R⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`) and are quasi-compact (`isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`); combine with the affinoid perfectoid cover of X from the definition and (i).
3. (iii) Wedhorn Remark 8.23(3) for the open affinoid subspaces V, V' of the adic space X, then (i).
4. (iv) By definition V ≅ Spa(R, R⁺) for some perfectoid Tate pair; global sections give (O_X(V), O_X⁺(V)) ≅ (R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space, `spaGlobalSectionsIso`).

**Acceptance.**

- For the perfectoid closed disc X = Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), the annulus {|p| ≤ |T| ≤ 1} = R({p, T}/T) is affinoid perfectoid with ring ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- In the perfectoid disc with doubled origin (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space, test isPerfectoidSpace_discWithDoubledOrigin) the two charts are affinoid perfectoid and meet in a non-quasi-compact open.

**Used by.** DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site (every covering refines to one by affinoid perfectoid spaces, since quasi-compact opens are covered by affinoid perfectoids); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting (the glued tilt is built on the family of affinoid perfectoid opens and their common rational refinements); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (fibre products are glued from affinoid perfectoid pieces).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_spaRationalFamily`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`.

**Sources.** sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.17, p. 38; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, Remark 8.23(3), p. 80; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Theorem 3.18, p. 18.

### P2b.4 Open subspaces of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid; open immersions in Perfd

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces` (lemma). Open adic subspaces of perfectoid spaces are perfectoid; open immersions in Perfd are the anchor's, with the universal property against all adic spaces; being perfectoid is local.

**Statement.** Let X be a perfectoid space and U ⊆ |X| open. The open adic subspace X|_U = (U, O_X|_U, (v_x)_{x ∈ U}) of anchor Layer 5.1 (Wedhorn Remark 8.23(2)) is a perfectoid space, and the inclusion j : X|_U → X is an open immersion of perfectoid spaces with the universal property in Perfd and in adic spaces: a morphism f : Y → X from an adic space Y factors through j, uniquely, iff f(|Y|) ⊆ U. Conversely: (a) the source of an open immersion of adic spaces into a perfectoid space is perfectoid; (b) an adic space covered by open subspaces that are perfectoid spaces is perfectoid; (c) for open U' ⊆ U, (X|_U)|_{U'} = X|_{U'}. Consequently Perfd is closed under open subspaces, the open immersions in Perfd are the anchor's open immersions between perfectoid spaces, and Perf is closed under open subspaces.

**Hypotheses.** X a perfectoid space; U ⊆ |X| open.

**Proof outline.**

1. Every x ∈ U has an affinoid perfectoid open neighbourhood inside U: take an affinoid perfectoid V ∋ x and a rational W ⊆ V ∩ U containing x; W is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (i)); hence X|_U is perfectoid.
2. The universal property of open subspaces is the anchor's (Layer 5.1); since Perfd is a full subcategory (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) it holds in Perfd.
3. (a) An open immersion V → X is an isomorphism onto X|_U, U its image; apply the first step and closure under isomorphisms. (b) The perfectoid property is local by definition. (c) Anchor Layer 5.1.
4. Characteristic p passes to open subspaces because restriction O_X(X) → O_X(U) is a ring map.

**Acceptance.**

- For X = Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) the punctured disc {T ≠ 0} is an open perfectoid subspace of X in Perf, which is not quasi-compact and so not affinoid.
- A morphism Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) → Spa(ℂ_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{ℂ_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) given by T^{1/p^n} ↦ a^{1/p^n} for a compatible system of p-power roots of a ∈ O_{ℂ_p} factors through the annulus {|p| ≤ |T| ≤ 1} iff |p| ≤ |a|.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) is the fibre product of the open subspaces); ECD §1 (analytic topology on Perf) (covers in the analytic topology are jointly surjective families of open immersions in Perf); PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison (open immersions of perfectoid spaces are the anchor's open immersions).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

**Sources.** Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, Remark 8.23(2), p. 80; sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.17, p. 38.

### P2b.5 Characteristic p: perfectoid spaces are adic spaces locally Spa of perfect Tate rings, and affinoid perfectoid spaces are the affinoid ones

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion` (lemma). In characteristic p: X is perfectoid iff locally Spa of perfect complete Tate rings; O_X(U) is perfect for every open U; and an affinoid adic space Spa(A, A⁺) (A sheafy complete Tate) that is a perfectoid space has A perfect, hence is affinoid perfectoid (Mihara; Bhatt Exercise 9.3.12). The proof glues p-th roots, which are unique in perfect rings.

**Statement.** Let X be an adic space with p = 0 in O_X(X). (i) X is a perfectoid space iff X is covered by open subspaces isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfect complete Tate ring. (ii) If X is a perfectoid space, then O_X(U) is a perfect ring (Mathlib `PerfectRing (O_X(U)) p`) for every open U ⊆ X. (iii) (Mihara; Bhatt, Exercise 9.3.12) If X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺) for a complete Hausdorff sheafy Huber pair (A, A⁺) with A Tate, and X is a perfectoid space, then A is perfect, hence a perfectoid Tate ring, and X is affinoid perfectoid. The analogue of (iii) in characteristic 0 is not asserted: whether an affinoid adic space that is a perfectoid space is affinoid perfectoid is recorded as unclear in Bhatt, Remark 9.3.11.

**Hypotheses.** X an adic space with p = 0 in O_X(X). (iii): (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff, sheafy, A Tate, X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) Chart by chart, ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect): a topological ring of characteristic p is a perfectoid Tate ring iff it is a perfect complete Tate ring.
2. (ii) Cover U by affinoid perfectoid opens V_i and each V_i ∩ V_j by affinoid perfectoid opens V_ijk (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis); O_X(V_i) and O_X(V_ijk) are perfectoid of characteristic p, hence perfect. By the sheaf property O_X(U) is the equalizer of ∏ O_X(V_i) ⇉ ∏ O_X(V_ijk); Frobenius commutes with the restriction maps, so it is injective on O_X(U), and p-th roots, unique in each O_X(V_i), agree on the V_ijk and glue. Hence O_X(U) is perfect.
3. (iii) A ≅ O_X(X) for the complete Hausdorff sheafy pair (anchor Layer 3.5), which is perfect by (ii) with U = X; a perfect complete Tate ring is perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5, uniformity being automatic by the open mapping argument of Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6), so X ≅ Spa(A, A⁺) is affinoid perfectoid.

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: X is a perfectoid space and A is perfect.
- For A = 𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩ (not perfect), Spa(A, A°) is not a perfectoid space, by (iii).

**Used by.** DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamond (objects of Perf have perfect rings of functions on every open); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (the characteristic-p characterisation in its API); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/products-in-perf (the charts of absolute products are shown perfectoid by perfectness).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`.

**Sources.** Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, Exercise 9.3.12 (Mihara), printed p. 111; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, Remark 9.3.11, printed p. 111; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.1, Example 2.1.2, p. 49.

### P2b.6 The glued tilt X ↦ X♭ of a perfectoid space

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting` (construction). For every perfectoid space X the tilt X♭ ∈ Perf is glued from the tilts Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) of the affinoid perfectoid opens along the tilts of their common rational refinements; |X♭| = |X|, affinoid perfectoid opens correspond, sections tilt, and f ↦ f♭ makes tilt a functor Perfd ⥤ Perf. In characteristic p, X♭ ≅ X canonically. X is not determined by X♭.

**Statement.** For every perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space; any characteristic, no base field) there is a perfectoid space X♭ of characteristic p, the *tilt* of X, with a homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭|, x ↦ x♭, constructed by gluing (ECD, the sentence after Definition 3.19; Sch12 Definition 6.16 and Proposition 6.17 over a perfectoid field). Affinoid case: for X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid, X♭ := Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), where (R♭, R♭⁺) is the tilt of the pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring: R♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting: R♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} R⁺), and x ↦ x♭ is the tilting homeomorphism |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets), which matches rational subsets U ↔ U♭ and satisfies (O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭ compatibly with restrictions (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids). General case: X♭ is glued (anchor Layer 5.3) from the tilts V♭ of all affinoid perfectoid open subspaces V ⊆ X, along the tilts of their common rational refinements (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)); since this family is canonical, X♭ is defined up to unique isomorphism, and |X♭| = |X| as sets with the same open subsets. A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces gives f♭ : Y♭ → X♭, affinoid-locally Spa of the tilt of the corresponding morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality), glued because morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf; this makes X ↦ X♭ a functor Perfd ⥤ Perf with |f♭| = |f| under the homeomorphisms. Properties: (a) for U ⊆ X open, (X|_U)♭ = X♭|_{U♭}, where U♭ is U viewed in |X♭|; U is affinoid perfectoid iff U♭ is, and then (O_{X♭}(U♭), O⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) ≅ (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U))♭; (b) the sharp maps glue to a continuous multiplicative map of sheaves of topological monoids O_{X♭} → O_X on |X| = |X♭|, f ↦ f♯, with |f♯(x)| = |f(x♭)|, carrying O⁺_{X♭} into O⁺_X; it is not additive; (c) for X of characteristic p, projection to the zeroth coordinate R♭ → R is a ring isomorphism, giving a natural isomorphism X♭ ≅ X; (d) X is not determined by X♭ (the tilt forgets the untilt); the equivalence of slice categories, and with it the description of maps into X♭ by untilts, is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.tilt : PerfectoidSpace ⥤ PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.

**Hypotheses.** X, Y perfectoid spaces; f : Y → X a morphism of adic spaces. Perfectoid pairs are complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (R, R⁺) with R perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1).

**Proof outline.**

1. Affinoid case: X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) is affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring, ECD Lemma 3.10: R♭ is a perfectoid 𝔽_p-algebra); the homeomorphism and the matching of rational subsets are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets (ECD Theorem 3.12), and the identification of the rational localisations of the tilt with the tilts of the rational localisations is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids (ECD Theorem 3.18).
2. Transition data: for affinoid perfectoid opens V, V' ⊆ X and W ⊆ V ∩ V' rational in both (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)), the two open embeddings W♭ → V♭, W♭ → V'♭ are Spa of the tilts of the restriction maps O_X(V) → O_X(W) and O_X(V') → O_X(W) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality); they agree with the identification of |W| inside |V| and |V'|, and the cocycle condition holds because it holds after composing with the homeomorphisms to |X| (the tilting maps are compatible with restriction).
3. Glue with the anchor's gluing of adic spaces (Layer 5.3; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GlueData` underneath) to obtain X♭, a perfectoid space of characteristic p covered by the V♭, with |X♭| identified with |X|.
4. Morphisms: given f : Y → X, cover Y by affinoid perfectoid V with f(V) ⊆ U, U affinoid perfectoid; f|_V corresponds to a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) → (O_Y(V), O⁺_Y(V)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25); tilt it (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality) and glue the resulting morphisms (Wedhorn Remark 8.24); functoriality and |f♭| = |f| are checked on affinoids, where they are the naturality of the tilting homeomorphism.
5. (b): the sharp map R♭ → R is continuous and multiplicative and compatible with rational localisations (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map); it glues as a map of sheaves of sets.
6. (c): for R of characteristic p, (x^{(i)})_i ↦ x^{(0)} is a ring isomorphism R♭ → R with inverse x ↦ (x^{1/p^i})_i, natural in R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring); glue.

**API** (derived from the uses: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor; DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/components-of-totally-disconnected; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product; Berkeley §7.2).

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `tilt_spa_cyclotomic` (computation): Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]), t = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) − 1, and the homeomorphism is the identity of the one-point space.
- `tilt_spa_perfectedDisc` (computation): For a perfectoid Tate ring R: Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa(R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with T ↦ (T, T^{1/p}, …).
- `tilt_empty` (degenerate): The tilt of the empty perfectoid space is empty.
- `tiltIsoOfCharP_spa` (compatibility): For X ∈ Perf the natural isomorphism X♭ ≅ X holds; e.g. Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})))♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))) via the zeroth coordinate.
- `tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes` (non-example): Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl) and Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) are not isomorphic (their rings have different characteristic) but have isomorphic tilts; so the tilt functor Perfd ⥤ Perf is not an equivalence, and a construction claiming to recover X from X♭ without a chosen base is wrong.
- `tiltHomeomorph_rationalSubset` (characterisation): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) perfectoid and f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ R♭ generating the unit ideal, the tilting homeomorphism maps the rational subset U(f_1♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) of X onto the rational subset U(f_1, …, f_n / g) of X♭.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) with t = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) − 1 (Berkeley Example 6.2.4).
- For a perfectoid Tate ring R, Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa(R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with T ↦ (T, T^{1/p}, …) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.3.15).
- Affinoid perfectoid open subspaces of X are exactly the U with U♭ ⊆ X♭ affinoid perfectoid (Sch12 Proposition 6.17).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.GlueData`, `mathlib:Homeomorph`.
