### P2b.7 Tilting is an equivalence between perfectoid Tate pairs over (A, A⁺) and over (A♭, A♭⁺), compatible with rational localisation

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence` (lemma). Over a perfectoid Tate pair (A, A⁺), tilting is an equivalence between perfectoid Tate pairs under (A, A⁺) and under (A♭, A♭⁺), with quasi-inverse the untilt W(S⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ along a generator ξ of ker θ_A (ECD Lemma 3.14, Theorem 3.17), compatible with rational localisation. This upgrades P1's ring-level equivalence (ECD Theorem 3.13) to pairs.

**Statement.** Let (A, A⁺) be a complete perfectoid Tate pair (A perfectoid Tate ring, A⁺ ⊆ A° a ring of integral elements) with tilt (A♭, A♭⁺). Let Perfd_{(A,A⁺)} be the category of complete perfectoid Tate pairs (B, B⁺) with a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), morphisms being morphisms of Huber pairs under (A, A⁺); define Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)} likewise. Then the tilt (B, B⁺) ↦ (B♭, B♭⁺) is an equivalence Perfd_{(A,A⁺)} ≃ Perfd_{(A♭,A♭⁺)}. A quasi-inverse sends (S, S⁺) to the untilt (W(S⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ, W(S⁺)/ξ) along a generator ξ of ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺), with ϖ♭ ∈ A♭ a pseudouniformiser (ECD Lemma 3.14 and Theorem 3.17; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). The equivalence carries rational localisations to rational localisations: for f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ B♭ generating the unit ideal, (B⟨f♯/g♯⟩)♭ ≅ B♭⟨f/g⟩ over B♭, and every rational localisation of B arises so. Through Spa (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space) it gives an equivalence between affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(A, A⁺) and over Spa(A♭, A♭⁺), compatible with the tilting homeomorphisms.

**Hypotheses.** (A, A⁺) a complete perfectoid Tate pair; no perfectoid base field.

**Proof outline.**

1. Rings: the tilt is an equivalence between perfectoid A-algebras and perfectoid A♭-algebras with unit and counit (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt; ECD Theorem 3.13, which asserts the general case).
2. Plus rings: B⁺ ↦ B♭⁺ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} B⁺ is an inclusion-preserving bijection between rings of integral elements with B♭⁺/ϖ♭ = B⁺/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, ECD Lemma 3.11), natural in B; a morphism B → C carries B⁺ into C⁺ iff its tilt carries B♭⁺ into C♭⁺, since both conditions can be read modulo ϖ♭ ≅ ϖ on the common quotients B♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ B°/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10).
3. Quasi-inverse: B ≅ W(B♭⁺)[[ϖ♭]⁻¹]/ξ for the image of the primitive generator ξ of ker θ_A (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction), functorially in (B, B⁺) under (A, A⁺).
4. Rational localisations: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids (ECD Theorem 3.18; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.5.3(b)).
5. Spaces: Spa is an anti-equivalence on complete perfectoid Tate pairs (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and morphisms over Spa(A, A⁺) are morphisms of pairs under (A, A⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- For (A, A⁺) = (K, K°) a perfectoid field: Scholze's Lemma 6.2 (perfectoid affinoid K-algebras ≃ perfectoid affinoid K♭-algebras, for pairs whose plus ring contains K°).
- For (A, A⁺) = (ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl): (𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, 𝔽_p[[t^{1/p^∞}]]⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) untilts to (ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩).

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence (the affinoid case of ECD Corollary 3.20, glued there); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (the untilt of the characteristic-p completed tensor product over (A♭, A♭⁺)).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**Sources.** Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Theorem 3.13 and its proof, p. 17; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.3, Remark 2.3.17, p. 56; sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, Lemma 6.2, p. 30; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Theorem 3.17, p. 18.

### P2b.8 Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces: Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭ (ECD Corollary 3.20)

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence` (theorem, planet *Tilting equivalence of perfectoid spaces*). ECD Corollary 3.20: for every perfectoid space X, (Y → X) ↦ (Y♭ → X♭) is an equivalence Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭. Equivalently, every T → X♭ with T ∈ Perf has an untilt T♯ → X, unique up to unique isomorphism. There is no untilting functor without a base.

**Statement.** Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting). (a) The functor Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ = Perfd/X♭ on slice categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over`), (f : Y → X) ↦ (f♭ : Y♭ → X♭), is an equivalence of categories (a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence`). (b) It commutes with restriction to open subspaces of X, and a perfectoid space Y over X is affinoid perfectoid iff Y♭ is; for X = Spa(A, A⁺) it restricts on affinoid perfectoid spaces to the equivalence of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence. (c) Untilts over X: for every perfectoid space T of characteristic p and every morphism g : T → X♭ there are a perfectoid space T♯ with a morphism T♯ → X and an isomorphism ι : (T♯)♭ ≅ T over X♭, and the pair (T♯ → X, ι) is unique up to unique isomorphism; so Hom_Perf(T, X♭) is in natural bijection with isomorphism classes of such pairs, functorially in T. (d) Under the homeomorphisms |Y| ≅ |Y♭| the structure maps correspond. The quasi-inverse depends on X: there is no untilting functor Perf → Perfd without a chosen base (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting, test tilt_not_injective_on_iso_classes).

**Hypotheses.** X a perfectoid space (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field).

**Proof outline.**

1. Full faithfulness: for Y, Y' over X, the map Hom_X(Y, Y') → Hom_{X♭}(Y♭, Y'♭) is a map of sheaves on |Y| = |Y♭| (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24), so it suffices to treat Y affinoid perfectoid mapping into an affinoid perfectoid open V' ⊆ Y' lying over an affinoid perfectoid open U ⊆ X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis); there morphisms are morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs under (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence gives bijectivity.
2. Essential surjectivity: given g : T → X♭, cover T by affinoid perfectoid T_i with g(T_i) ⊆ U_i♭, U_i ⊆ X affinoid perfectoid; the pair-level equivalence gives affinoid perfectoid untilts T_i♯ over U_i with (T_i♯)♭ ≅ T_i over U_i♭; on overlaps, refined to opens rational in both charts (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iii)), the restricted untilts are canonically isomorphic by full faithfulness, and these isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition by uniqueness; glue (anchor Layer 5.3) to T♯ → X with (T♯)♭ ≅ T.
3. (b) and (d) follow from the construction of the glued tilt (open subspaces, affinoid criterion, homeomorphisms); (c) is (a) restated for objects of Perf/X♭.

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Proposition 6.17: for a perfectoid field K, perfectoid spaces over K and over K♭ are equivalent (the case X = Spa(K, K⁺₀), see PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison).
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl), the perfectoid disc over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) untilts to Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), and Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))) itself (with the identity to X♭) untilts to X.
- Unit and counit are isomorphisms compatible with restriction to open subspaces of X.

**Used by.** DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair (functoriality of Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A, A⁺) in T comes from untilts over X♯ (part (c))); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity (restricted to étale maps it gives X_ét ≅ X♭_ét); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products (equivalences preserve products in slice categories); DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor (for Y perfectoid, perfectoid spaces over Y are identified with perfectoid spaces of characteristic p over Y♭, the diamond of Y).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

**Sources.** Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Corollary 3.20, p. 19; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 7, §7.1, Theorem 7.1.4, printed pp. 49-50; sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, Proposition 6.17, p. 38; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, Theorem 9.3.10(2), printed p. 111.

### P2b.9 Characteristic p: the completed tensor product of perfect complete Tate rings is perfect, uniform and perfectoid

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor` (lemma). In characteristic p, B ⊗̂_A C is perfect, hence uniform and perfectoid; the completed image of B° ⊗ C° is almost equal to its power-bounded subring and the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗_{A°} C° is almost zero (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.18; Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 3.1.6(c)).

**Statement.** Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings of characteristic p, equivalently perfect complete Tate rings (ECD Proposition 3.5). Both maps are adic (continuous maps out of a Tate ring are adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so the completed tensor product (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product is defined. Let ϖ ∈ A be a pseudouniformiser, F ⊆ B ⊗_A C the image of B° ⊗_{A°} C° (a ring of definition for R0's topology, because ϖB° ⊆ B⁺ ⊆ B° and likewise for C) and F̂ ⊆ D its ϖ-adic completion. Then: (i) D and F̂ are perfect rings; (ii) D is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence uniform and perfectoid, and the uniformisation D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism; (iii) ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D° for all n ≥ 0, where ϖ^{1/p^n} are the p-power roots in the perfect ring A; in particular ϖD° ⊆ F̂, and F̂ → D° is injective with cokernel killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, i.e. an almost isomorphism for the almost setup of A (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); (iv) the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗_{A°} C° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}.

**Hypotheses.** A, B, C perfect complete Tate rings of characteristic p with morphisms of complete Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺).

**Proof outline.**

1. B ⊗_A C is perfect: Frobenius b ⊗ c ↦ b^p ⊗ c^p is bijective with inverse b ⊗ c ↦ b^{1/p} ⊗ c^{1/p}, well defined because the inverse Frobenii of A, B, C are compatible with A → B and A → C (routine).
2. F is a perfect subring: B° and C° are perfect (x is power-bounded iff x^p is), so Frobenius and its inverse preserve the generators b ⊗ c (b ∈ B°, c ∈ C°); F is open and bounded for R0's topology.
3. Frobenius and its inverse are continuous for the ϖ-adic topology of F (Φ⁻¹(ϖ^{pk}F) = ϖ^k F), so they extend to F̂ and to D = F̂[1/ϖ]: (i).
4. (ii) A perfect complete Tate ring is uniform and perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6 proves uniformity by the open mapping argument); a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pair is its own uniformisation (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (e)).
5. (iii) For x ∈ D° choose N with ϖ^N x^m ∈ F̂ for all m ≥ 0 (F̂ open, {x^m} bounded); then (ϖ^{N/p^n} x)^{p^n} ∈ F̂ and F̂ is perfect, so ϖ^{N/p^n} x ∈ F̂ for all n; taking n with N/p^n ≤ ε gives ϖ^ε x ∈ F̂ for every ε ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{>0}.
6. (iv) M := B° ⊗_{A°} C° is perfect by the argument of the first step. If ϖ^k f = 0 in M, applying the inverse Frobenius gives ϖ^{k/p} f^{1/p} = 0, and multiplying by f^{(p-1)/p} gives ϖ^{k/p} f = 0; iterating, ϖ^{k/p^n} f = 0 for all n (Sch12 proof of Proposition 6.18).

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K of characteristic p: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩ with F̂ = K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- Without perfectness the conclusion fails: 𝔽_p((t))⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_{𝔽_p((t))} 𝔽_p((t))⟨S⟩ is uniform but not perfect.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (the characteristic-p case, which is then untilted); Bhatt, Corollary 9.3.13 (fibre products of perfectoid spaces are reduced to characteristic p).

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft`, `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`.

**Sources.** KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.1, Remark 3.1.6(c), p. 67; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.1, Remark 3.1.6(c), p. 67; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, proof of Corollary 9.3.13, printed p. 111; sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.18, p. 38.

### P2b.10 A uniform Tate ring receiving a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion` (lemma). A complete uniform Tate ring receiving a continuous dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18(ii)); uniformity of the target cannot be dropped.

**Statement.** Let f : A → B be a continuous ring homomorphism with dense image from a perfectoid Tate ring A to a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring B (B° bounded). Then B is a perfectoid Tate ring and f♭ : A♭ → B♭ has dense image (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3 and Lemma 2.8.4; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.18, class (ii); over ℚ_p Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.6.17(b)). Uniformity of B is a hypothesis: K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) (closure of the ideal) is surjective, but the target is not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).

**Hypotheses.** A a perfectoid Tate ring; B a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with B° bounded; f continuous with dense image.

**Proof outline.**

1. B♭ := lim_{x ↦ x^p} B with the limiting addition is a perfect complete uniform Tate ring of characteristic p with pseudo-uniformizer f♭(ϖ_A♭), where ϖ_A♭ ∈ A♭ has compatible roots, and θ_B: W(B♭⁺) → B⁺ is defined and natural (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c), (e); Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.7.1). Only completeness, uniformity and topological nilpotence of p in B are used.
2. B₀♭ := the closure of f♭(A♭) in B♭ is a closed perfect subring containing f♭(ϖ_A♭), hence a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (c); ECD Proposition 3.5, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
3. B₀ := the untilt of B₀♭ along the image of the primitive ideal ker(θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel), with maps A → B₀ → B, the second induced by θ_B, which kills the image of ker θ_A by naturality of θ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring (e)); B₀ → B has dense image since W(A♭⁺) → A → B does.
4. B₀ → B is a strict inclusion, indeed an isometry for the spectral gauges of the images of ϖ_A, because B₀♭ → B♭ is one (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting (b), which needs only that B is uniform; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.2).
5. Metric criterion (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion; Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.3, after Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.2): for the spectral gauge of a pseudo-uniformizer with compatible roots, a uniform Tate ring is perfectoid iff there is c ∈ (0, 1) with: for every x there is y with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|. B₀ satisfies it; by density and isometry B does, so B is perfectoid; then B₀ → B is a dense strict inclusion of complete rings, hence an isomorphism, and f♭ has dense image.

**Acceptance.**

- If B is the completed residue field of a point of Spa(A, A⁺) (a uniform nonarchimedean field receiving a dense-image map from the completed colimit of rational localisations), B is perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7, second proof).
- The uniformisation of a completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C with B, C perfectoid receives a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base).

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base (the uniform completed tensor product over a non-perfectoid base is perfectoid); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields (completed residue fields and completed stalks are perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Corollary 2.5.7)); PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (completed direct limits of perfectoid rings are perfectoid (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.22)).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-uniform-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/metric-perfectoid-criterion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`.

**Sources.** Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.8, Lemma 2.8.4, p. 70; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.4, Theorem 2.4.3(a), p. 58; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, §3.3, Theorem 3.3.18(ii), p. 64; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.6, Theorem 3.6.17(b), p. 95; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.4, Example 2.4.9, p. 59.

### P2b.11 Completed tensor products of perfectoid Tate pairs are perfectoid, uniform, and commute with tilting

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid` (theorem). For perfectoid (B, B⁺) ← (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺), R0's B ⊗̂_A C is perfectoid, uniform (so equal to its uniformisation), the pushout among perfectoid Tate pairs, and its tilt is B♭ ⊗̂_{A♭} C♭ (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13). The proof untilts the characteristic-p pushout and compares integral models modulo ϖ with almost mathematics, controlling the lim¹ term (P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).

**Statement.** Let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`) with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Definition 3.1; any characteristic; no perfectoid base field). Both maps are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so the completed tensor product (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C with inl, inr (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product; D⁺ the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺) is defined. Then: (i) D is a perfectoid Tate ring; in particular D is uniform and the uniformisation D → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is an isomorphism (the tensor-product norm is the spectral norm, Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13(b)); (ii) (D, D⁺) with inl, inr is a pushout of (B, B⁺) ← (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) in the category of complete perfectoid Tate pairs; (iii) tilting commutes with it: there is a unique isomorphism of Huber pairs (D♭, D♭⁺) ≅ (B♭, B♭⁺) ⊗̂_{(A♭, A♭⁺)} (C♭, C♭⁺) whose composites with inl♭, inr♭ are inl, inr (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; Kedlaya–Liu II Theorem 3.3.13(a)); (iv) for a pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p in A° and compatible p-power roots (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), the ϖ-adic completion F̂ of the image F of B° ⊗_{A°} C° in B ⊗_A C satisfies ϖ^{1/p^n} D° ⊆ F̂ ⊆ D° for all n, and the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗_{A°} C° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}; so F̂ → D° is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), which over a perfectoid field K is Scholze's statement that A°a ⊗̂_{B°a} C°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra (Sch12 Proposition 6.18). The perfectoid base A is essential: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (recorded in AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product).

**Hypotheses.** (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A, B, C perfectoid Tate rings. (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.

**Proof outline.**

1. Adicness: continuous maps out of a Tate ring are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing`), so (D, D⁺) is defined (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product).
2. Characteristic p: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor.
3. Candidate untilt: let (R, R⁺), (S, S⁺), (T, T⁺) be the tilts of (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) and (U, U⁺) = S ⊗̂_R T, a perfectoid Tate pair of characteristic p (previous step) which is a pushout among complete perfectoid Tate pairs (universal property AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property). By PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence there are a perfectoid Tate pair (E, E⁺) under (A, A⁺) with (E♭, E♭⁺) ≅ (U, U⁺) and morphisms (B, B⁺) → (E, E⁺) ← (C, C⁺) untilting S → U ← T; as tilting is an equivalence under (A, A⁺), (E, E⁺) is a pushout among complete perfectoid Tate pairs.
4. Comparison map: the universal property of (D, D⁺) (E complete Hausdorff, E⁺ closed and integrally closed) gives χ : (D, D⁺) → (E, E⁺) compatible with inl, inr; χ(F̂) ⊆ E°.
5. Modulo ϖ: the functorial isomorphisms B°/ϖ ≅ S°/ϖ♭, C°/ϖ ≅ T°/ϖ♭ over A°/ϖ ≅ R°/ϖ♭ and E°/ϖ ≅ U°/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality) identify the composite (B° ⊗_{A°} C°)/ϖ → F/ϖ → E°/ϖ with (S° ⊗_{R°} T°)/ϖ♭ → F_U/ϖ♭ → U°/ϖ♭, which is an almost isomorphism by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor (iii)-(iv). The first arrow is surjective, so F/ϖ → E°/ϖ is an almost isomorphism and the kernel of (B° ⊗ C°)/ϖ → F/ϖ is almost zero.
6. Completion: F̂ and E° are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (F lies in B ⊗_A C, where ϖ is a unit, and the ϖ-adic completion of a ϖ-torsion-free module is ϖ-torsion free); a map of such modules that is an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ is an almost isomorphism modulo ϖ^n for all n (induction with the exact sequences 0 → M/ϖ^n → M/ϖ^{n+1} → M/ϖ → 0) and then an almost isomorphism: apply PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion to the two-term complex F̂ → E° (its Milnor sequence keeps the lim¹ term, which is almost zero, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits).
7. Conclusion: F̂ → E° is injective (torsion free and almost injective) with ϖE° ⊆ F̂, so χ : D = F̂[1/ϖ] → E°[1/ϖ] = E is an isomorphism of topological rings; the plus rings agree because the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ contains D°° (by (iv), as ϖ^ε B° ⊆ B⁺ and ϖ^ε C° ⊆ C⁺) and is integrally closed (Wedhorn Remark 7.15(3)). This gives (i)–(iv); the uniformisation statement is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (e).

**Acceptance.**

- B ⊗̂_A A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ B⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ for every perfectoid Tate pair (B, B⁺) under (A, A⁺) (perfected Tate algebras, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), compatibly with tilting; in particular A⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_A A⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≅ A⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- For a finite Galois extension L/K of perfectoid fields with group G (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), L ⊗̂_K L ≅ ∏_{g ∈ G} L, a perfectoid Tate ring that is not a field.
- Over a perfectoid field K this is Sch12 Proposition 6.18 (affinoid case).

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property (the affinoid fibre product Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) is perfectoid, hence sheafy); PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products (the affinoid case of tilting compatibility); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product (discharges its sheafiness hypothesis on B ⊗̂_A C in the perfectoid case); AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product (X' = X ×_L Spa L' is perfectoid for perfectoid fields L ⊆ L'); DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair (fibre products of affinoid perfectoid v-covers Z = Y ×_X Y).

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfect-uniform-completed-tensor`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-pairs-tilting-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-zero-limits-and-colimits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`, `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`, `mathlib:integralClosure`.

**Sources.** Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.4, Theorem 2.4.1, p. 57; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, §3.3, Theorem 3.3.13(b), p. 61; KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, §3.3, Remark 3.3.14, p. 62; sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.18, p. 38; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.6, Proposition 3.6.11, p. 92.

### P2b.12 The plus ring of a perfectoid completed tensor product: almost equal to the completed tensor product of plus rings, but not equal

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula` (lemma). The completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ maps to D⁺ by an almost isomorphism (Bhatt Exercise 9.3.14) but not an isomorphism: for K the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), ℓ ∤ p(p − 1), the image of L° ⊗_{K°} L° in L ⊗̂_K L = L^ℓ is not integrally closed. This is why the plus ring convention takes the integral closure.

**Statement.** In the situation of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid, with ϖ ∈ A as there: (i) the ϖ-power torsion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}; (ii) the natural map from the ϖ-adic completion (B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺)^∧ to D⁺ has kernel and cokernel killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, i.e. it is an almost isomorphism of A⁺-modules (Bhatt, Exercise 9.3.14); (iii) D⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of the integral closure in B ⊗_A C of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺, it contains D°° and ϖ^{1/p^n} D° for all n. The map in (ii) is not an isomorphism in general (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed).

**Hypotheses.** As in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ → B° ⊗_{A°} C° has kernel and cokernel killed by ϖ^{1/p^n}, since B°/B⁺ and C°/C⁺ are almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii); PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), and the ϖ-power torsion of B° ⊗ C° is almost zero (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iv)).
2. (ii) Combine (i) with the almost isomorphism F̂ → D° of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iv) and D°/D⁺ almost zero; completion preserves almost isomorphisms of ϖ-torsion-free modules (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion).
3. (iii) R0's plus ring is the closure of the integral closure of the image (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product); the closure of an open subring is its completion; it contains ϖ^ε D° by (ii).

**Acceptance.**

- Over a perfectoid field K and B = C = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with plus rings K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, the map of (ii) is an isomorphism onto K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (pins the plus ring of the affinoid fibre product); DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/automatic-flatness (integral statements S⁺/ϖ over R⁺/ϖ are made up to almost isomorphism).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-exactness-passes-to-completion`, `mathlib:integralClosure`.

**Sources.** Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, Exercise 9.3.14, printed p. 112; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Example 3.22(ii), p. 19; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.8, proof of Lemma 2.8.7, p. 71.

### P2b.13 The uniform completed tensor product of perfectoid rings over an arbitrary Tate ring is perfectoid

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base` (theorem). Over an arbitrary Tate base A, the uniform completed tensor product of perfectoid A-algebras is perfectoid (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21): a perfected Tate algebra over B maps to it with dense image, and the dense-image criterion applies. The non-uniform completed tensor product need not be perfectoid (ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p).

**Statement.** Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with A a Tate ring (not necessarily perfectoid, uniform or of characteristic p), and let (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of Huber pairs with B, C perfectoid Tate rings. Then the uniform completed tensor product B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product) is a perfectoid Tate ring (Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.21; Kedlaya–Liu I Corollary 3.6.18 over ℚ_p). If A is perfectoid it equals B ⊗̂_A C (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (i)); otherwise the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C need not be uniform (ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not), and the uniformisation cannot be omitted.

**Hypotheses.** (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff with A Tate; B, C perfectoid Tate rings; morphisms of Huber pairs from (A, A⁺).

**Proof outline.**

1. D^u := B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate ring and the image of B ⊗_A C is dense in it (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (a)-(b), R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product).
2. Let P := B⟨T_s^{1/p^∞} : s ∈ C♭°⟩, the perfected Tate algebra over B in the (infinite) set C♭° of variables, a perfectoid Tate ring (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra with Σ = C♭°; Kedlaya–Liu II Example 3.3.12). The continuous B-algebra map P → D^u with T_s^{1/p^n} ↦ inr((s^{1/p^n})♯) exists by the universal property of P (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra, `lift`), the images being power-bounded and compatible with p-th powers (the sharp map is multiplicative, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).
3. Its image is dense: it contains inl(B) and inr(x♯) for x ∈ C♭°; every c ∈ C° is a convergent sum Σ_i ((ϖ♭)^i x_i)♯ with x_i ∈ C♭°, obtained by successive approximation from the surjectivity of C♭° → C°/ϖ, x ↦ x♯ mod ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.10), for ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯; so inr(C°), hence inr(C) = inr(C°)[1/ϖ], lies in the closure of the image, and so does the image of B ⊗_A C.
4. By the dense-image criterion (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion) D^u is perfectoid.
5. In characteristic p a direct argument also works: the Frobenius of D^u has dense image (it contains b ⊗ c = (b^{1/p} ⊗ c^{1/p})^p), satisfies |x^p| = |x|^p for the spectral norm, hence has closed image and is surjective, and is injective as D^u is reduced; so D^u is perfect, hence perfectoid (ECD Proposition 3.5).

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℚ_p and B = C = ℚ_p^cycl: ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid Tate ring over the non-perfectoid base ℚ_p.
- ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is perfectoid although ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base (affinoid pieces of fibre products of perfectoid spaces over a non-perfectoid analytic base); PerfectoidSpaces:P8/analytically-separated (the fibre product over Spa(K, K⁺) for a non-perfectoid nonarchimedean field K is perfectoid).

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfected-tate-algebra`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

**Sources.** KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings, §3.3, Corollary 3.3.21, p. 66; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.6, Corollary 3.6.18, p. 96; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.1, Remark 3.1.6(c), p. 67.

### P2b.14 Affinoid perfectoid fibre products: Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) is a fibre product in adic spaces, compatible with open subspaces

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property` (theorem). For affinoid perfectoid Y → X ← Z, Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) is a fibre product in the category of all adic spaces (R0's affinoid fibre product with its sheafiness hypothesis discharged), it is affinoid perfectoid, and its open subspaces p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) are the fibre products of the open subspaces.

**Statement.** Let X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺), Z = Spa(C, C⁺) be affinoid perfectoid spaces and Y → X ← Z morphisms, corresponding (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25) to morphisms of complete perfectoid Tate pairs (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺). Let (D, D⁺) = B ⊗̂_A C, a complete perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), hence sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy). Then (a) W = Spa(D, D⁺) with p = Spa(inl) and q = Spa(inr) is a fibre product Y ×_X Z in the anchor's category of adic spaces (a Mathlib `IsPullback` square there), hence in Perfd, and W is affinoid perfectoid; this is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product with its sheafiness hypothesis discharged. (b) For rational subsets U' ⊆ X, U ⊆ Y, V ⊆ Z with U and V mapping into U', the open p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) ⊆ W is a rational subset and equals Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation). (c) For arbitrary open subspaces U ⊆ Y, V ⊆ Z, the open subspace p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) with the restricted projections is a fibre product U ×_X V in adic spaces. (d) The map |W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points) and not injective in general.

**Hypotheses.** Y → X ← Z morphisms of affinoid perfectoid spaces (any characteristic, no base field).

**Proof outline.**

1. (D, D⁺) is a complete perfectoid Tate pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and so sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy); (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) are sheafy for the same reason.
2. (a) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product applies (adicness of the ring maps: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) and gives the universal property against every adic space T; W is affinoid perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space.
3. (b) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation identifies p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) with a rational subset whose ring is O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V); the rational localisations are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so (a) applies to them.
4. (c) A pair of morphisms T → U, T → V over X is a pair of morphisms to Y, Z whose images lie in U, V; the induced T → W factors through the open p⁻¹(U) ∩ q⁻¹(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces, universal property of open subspaces), uniquely.
5. (d) AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points; non-injectivity: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces, test pullback_galois_points.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa K} Spa(K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩) for every perfectoid Tate ring K, with the rational subset {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} × {|S| ≤ |ϖ|} corresponding to Spa(K⟨(T/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}, (S/ϖ)^{1/p^∞}⟩).
- The universal property holds against all adic spaces T, not only perfectoid ones.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (the affinoid pieces and their compatibilities for the global gluing); DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/perfectoid-sheaf-topoi-are-algebraic (fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (quasi-separatedness of affinoids)); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (base change of finite étale maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsPullback`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.

**Sources.** sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.18, p. 38; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.4, before Theorem 2.4.1, p. 57; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 8, Proposition 8.3, p. 41.

### P2b.15 Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist in adic spaces and are perfectoid

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces` (construction, planet *Fibre products of perfectoid spaces*). Perfd has all fibre products, computed in adic spaces and preserved by the inclusion: glue the affinoid fibre products. Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Proposition 6.18. The underlying space of Y ×_X Z surjects onto |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| but is not the fibre product of spaces (Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L has [L : K] points for L/K finite Galois).

**Statement.** Let f : Y → X and g : Z → X be morphisms of perfectoid spaces (any characteristic; no perfectoid base field). The fibre product W = Y ×_X Z exists in the anchor's category of adic spaces and is a perfectoid space; with its projections p : W → Y, q : W → Z it is therefore also a fibre product in Perfd, Perfd has all fibre products (Mathlib `HasPullbacks`), and the inclusion Perfd ⥤ AdicSpace preserves them. Construction: W is glued (anchor Layer 5.3) from the affinoid perfectoid spaces W_{U,U',V} = Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂_{O_X(U')} O_Z(V)) = U ×_{U'} V (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property), for affinoid perfectoid opens U' ⊆ X, U ⊆ f⁻¹(U'), V ⊆ g⁻¹(U'), along their common open subspaces, which are fibre products of the intersections (open compatibility (c) there). Pinned conventions: the affinoid formula uses AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product with plus ring the closure of the integral closure of the image of O_Y⁺(U) ⊗ O_Z⁺(V), which is almost, but not in general exactly, the completed tensor product of the plus rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula); the ring is already uniform, so no uniformisation is performed. Affinoid perfectoid spaces and Perf are closed under fibre products; tilting commutes with them (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products); |W| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| is surjective but not injective in general. Over a perfectoid field this is Sch12 Proposition 6.18. Fibre products over a non-perfectoid analytic base are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base, and absolute products in Perf are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/products-in-perf. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.pullback f g` with `HasPullbacks PerfectoidSpace`.

**Hypotheses.** f : Y → X, g : Z → X morphisms of perfectoid spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Affinoid pieces: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property (a) gives W_{U,U',V} = U ×_{U'} V in adic spaces; since U' ⊆ X is open, U ×_{U'} V = U ×_X V (open subspace universal property, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. Gluing data: for two index triples, the open subspaces p⁻¹(U ∩ Ũ) ∩ q⁻¹(V ∩ Ṽ) of W_{U,U',V} and of W_{Ũ,Ũ',Ṽ} are both fibre products (U ∩ Ũ) ×_X (V ∩ Ṽ) (part (c) there), hence canonically isomorphic, and the cocycle condition follows from uniqueness of the comparison isomorphisms (the pattern of EGA I (3.2.6)); glue with anchor Layer 5.3.
3. Universal property: given a : T → Y, b : T → Z with f a = g b from an adic space T, cover T by the opens a⁻¹(U) ∩ b⁻¹(V) ∩ (f a)⁻¹(U'); on each the morphism to W_{U,U',V} is unique, the local morphisms agree on overlaps, and they glue (morphisms of adic spaces form a sheaf, Wedhorn Remark 8.24).
4. W is perfectoid (covered by affinoid perfectoid W_{U,U',V}); p and q are adic (every morphism into a perfectoid space is adic); if X, Y, Z have characteristic p so does W (inl is a ring map).
5. Points: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points on each affinoid piece.

**API** (derived from the uses: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map (ECD Proposition 5.9); PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition (ECD Corollary 5.5); PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces; DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/perfectoid-sheaf-topoi-are-algebraic; DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/perfectoid-times-smooth-fibre-product; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding; ECD Definition 1.20).

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `pullback_perfectedDiscs` (computation): For a perfectoid Tate ring R: Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa(R, R⁺)} Spa(R⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩) over the two projections.
- `pullback_galois_points` (computation): For a finite Galois extension L/K of perfectoid fields with group G, Spa(L, L°) ×_{Spa(K, K°)} Spa(L, L°) ≅ ⊔_{g ∈ G} Spa(L, L°) has |G| points while |Spa L| ×_{|Spa K|} |Spa L| is one point: the underlying space of a fibre product is not the fibre product of underlying spaces.
- `pullback_id` (degenerate): Y ×_X X ≅ Y via p, for the identity of X; and Y ×_X ∅ = ∅.
- `pullback_plus_ne_completedTensor_plus` (non-example): For K the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}) (ℓ a prime not dividing p(p − 1)), the plus ring of Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L is (L°)^ℓ, which strictly contains the image of L° ⊗_{K°} L° (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed); a construction using the completed tensor product of plus rings as plus ring produces a pair that is not a Huber pair.
- `pullback_isPullback_adicSpace` (compatibility): The square (W, p, q, f, g) is a pullback (Mathlib `IsPullback`) in the anchor's category of adic spaces, and on affinoid pieces the canonical map Spa(B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C) → Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) from AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product is an isomorphism.
- `pullback_tilt` (characterisation): For Y → X ← Z in Perfd, the fibre product of Y♭ → X♭ ← Z♭ in Perf is (Y ×_X Z)♭ with the tilted projections (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products).

**Acceptance.**

- Sch12 Proposition 6.18: for perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K, Y ×_X Z exists in adic spaces over K and is perfectoid.
- Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa R} Spa(R⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩) for any perfectoid Tate ring R.
- For a finite Galois extension L/K of perfectoid fields with group G, Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L ≅ ⊔_{g ∈ G} Spa L.

### P2b.16 Tilting commutes with fibre products of perfectoid spaces

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products` (lemma). (Y ×_X Z)♭ ≅ Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭: fibre products are products in Perfd/X, and the tilting equivalence preserves limits; on affinoids it is the ring-level tilt isomorphism.

**Statement.** For morphisms Y → X ← Z of perfectoid spaces, the tilts of the projections exhibit (Y ×_X Z)♭ as the fibre product Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ in Perf and in adic spaces: the canonical morphism (Y ×_X Z)♭ → Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ is an isomorphism. On affinoid pieces it is the isomorphism (B ⊗̂_A C)♭ ≅ B♭ ⊗̂_{A♭} C♭ of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iii). More generally the tilting equivalence Perfd/X ≃ Perf/X♭ preserves every limit that exists in Perfd/X.

**Hypotheses.** Y → X ← Z morphisms of perfectoid spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Y ×_X Z, with its map to X, is the binary product of Y and Z in Perfd/X (Mathlib `Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`: pullbacks give binary products in the slice category).
2. The tilting functor Perfd/X → Perf/X♭ is an equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence) and equivalences preserve limits (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isEquivalencePreservesLimits`), so it sends this product to the product of Y♭ and Z♭ in Perf/X♭, which is Y♭ ×_{X♭} Z♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces in Perf).
3. On affinoid pieces, uniqueness of morphisms into a fibre product identifies the resulting isomorphism with the ring-level tilt isomorphism of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (iii).

**Acceptance.**

- For K perfectoid: (Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ×_{Spa K} Spa K⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩)♭ ≅ Spa K♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- For L/K finite Galois of perfectoid fields: (Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L)♭ ≅ Spa L♭ ×_{Spa K♭} Spa L♭, both ⊔_{g ∈ G} of the tilt.

**Used by.** PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity (base change of étale maps commutes with tilting); DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor (the diamond functor is compatible with fibre products, which on perfectoid spaces is this lemma).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isEquivalencePreservesLimits`.

**Sources.** Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, §2.4, Theorem 2.4.1, p. 57; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, Section 3, Corollary 3.20, p. 19.

### P2b.17 Fibre products of perfectoid spaces over an analytic adic space, in Perfd, via uniform completed tensor products

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base` (construction). For perfectoid Y, Z over an analytic adic space S (for instance Spa(K, K⁺) with K not perfectoid) the fibre product exists in Perfd, affinoid-locally Spa(B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C). It is a fibre product in all adic spaces only when S is perfectoid. This is the fibre product used for analytic separatedness in P8.

**Statement.** Let S be an analytic adic space (anchor Layer 5; every point analytic, e.g. Spa(K, K⁺) for any nonarchimedean field K, or any rigid space) and f : Y → S, g : Z → S morphisms from perfectoid spaces. Then the fibre product Y ×_S Z exists in Perfd: there is a perfectoid space W with morphisms p : W → Y, q : W → Z, f p = g q, such that for every perfectoid space T, Hom(T, W) = Hom(T, Y) ×_{Hom(T, S)} Hom(T, Z). Affinoid-locally, for an open affinoid U' = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ S with A a complete Tate ring (the analytic locus is covered by such, anchor Layer 2.3) and affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ f⁻¹(U'), V ⊆ g⁻¹(U'), the piece of W over U, V is Spa(O_Y(U) ⊗̂ᵘ_A O_Z(V)), the uniform completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product), which is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/uniform-completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-over-any-base). If S is perfectoid, W is the fibre product of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (in all adic spaces). If S is not perfectoid, W is asserted to be a fibre product only in Perfd: the test objects are uniform, the completed tensor product itself need not be uniform (ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not) and its sheafiness is not known. The diagonal Y → Y ×_S Y is defined. Lean: `PerfectoidSpace.pullbackOverAnalytic f g`.

**Hypotheses.** S an analytic adic space; f : Y → S, g : Z → S morphisms with Y, Z perfectoid spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Every morphism into the analytic space S is adic and the ring maps O_S(U') → O_Y(U) are adic (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus), so R0's (uniform) completed tensor products are defined.
2. Affinoid universal property in Perfd: for a perfectoid T = Spa(R, R⁺) (R uniform), morphisms T → Spa(D^u) are morphisms of pairs D^u → (R, R⁺) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), which are pairs of morphisms from O_Y(U), O_Z(V) agreeing on A (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (b): pushout among complete Hausdorff uniform Tate pairs); for general perfectoid T glue over an affinoid perfectoid cover (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis, Wedhorn Remark 8.24).
3. Compatibility with rational subsets: the rational localisation of D^u at the preimages of rational U₁ ⊆ U, V₁ ⊆ V is O_Y(U₁) ⊗̂ᵘ_A O_Z(V₁), since both are initial among complete uniform pairs with the same maps (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation and the universal property of the uniformisation, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (c)-(d)).
4. Glue the pieces as in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces (anchor Layer 5.3).
5. If S is perfectoid, D^u = D (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid (i)) and both constructions agree.

**API** (derived from the uses: PerfectoidSpaces:P8/analytically-separated; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/analytically-separated-affinoid-intersections).

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `pullbackOverAnalytic_Cp_Qp` (non-example): For S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and Y = Z = Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}), the affinoid piece is Spa(ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p) and not Spa(ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p): the completed tensor product is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu I Remark 2.8.5), so a construction without uniformisation does not produce a perfectoid ring.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_perfectoidBase` (compatibility): If S is perfectoid, pullbackOverAnalytic f g ≅ PerfectoidSpace.pullback f g over Y and Z.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_empty` (degenerate): If Y = ∅ then Y ×_S Z = ∅.
- `pullbackOverAnalytic_cyclotomic` (computation): For S = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and Y = Z = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl), Y ×_S Z = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p^cycl), a perfectoid space mapping to Y by p; it is nonempty and its points surject onto |Y| ×_{|S|} |Z| (a point).

**Acceptance.**

- For K a nonarchimedean field that is not perfectoid (e.g. ℚ_p) and perfectoid spaces Y, Z over Spa(K, K°), Y ×_{Spa K} Z is a perfectoid space; this is the fibre product used for analytic separatedness in PerfectoidSpaces:P8.
- Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) ×_{Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)} Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) = Spa of the perfectoid ring ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p.

### P2b.18 Absolute products in Perf: X × Y exists, is perfectoid, and is not a fibre product over any perfectoid space

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/products-in-perf` (construction). Absolute products exist in Perf (Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5): X × Y is covered by charts Spa(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}), completions of A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B for the ring of definition (A° ⊗ B°)[ϖ^m/ϖ', ϖ'^n/ϖ], with plus ring the completed integral closure of (A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[ϖ^m/ϖ', ϖ'^n/ϖ] (the printed plus ring is not open). X × Y is the fibre product over the non-perfectoid discrete Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) in adic spaces and is not a fibre product in Perf. The absolute product of two perfectoid fields is a perfectoid punctured open disc, not a point (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4).

**Statement.** Let X, Y be perfectoid spaces of characteristic p. The product X × Y exists in Perf (Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5; ECD proof of Proposition 11.4). It is also the fibre product X ×_{Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p)} Y in the anchor's category of adic spaces, over the discrete adic space Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p), which is not a perfectoid (nor Tate, nor analytic) space; the structure maps X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) are not adic, so neither PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces nor AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence applies, and Perf has no final object (Berkeley Remark 8.3.6), so the absolute product is not a fibre product in Perf. Affinoid charts: for X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺) affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p with pseudouniformisers ϖ ∈ A, ϖ' ∈ B, and integers m, n ≥ 1, put E = A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B, u_m = (ϖ^m ⊗ 1)(1 ⊗ ϖ')⁻¹ and v_n = (1 ⊗ ϖ'^n)(ϖ ⊗ 1)⁻¹ in E, D_{m,n} = (A° ⊗ B°)[u_m, v_n] ⊆ E; topologise E so that D_{m,n} is open with the (ϖ ⊗ 1)-adic topology (equal to the (1 ⊗ ϖ')-adic one, since ϖ^m = u_m ϖ' and ϖ'^n = v_n ϖ in D_{m,n}); let C_{m,n} be the completion and C⁺_{m,n} the completion of the integral closure in E of the image of (A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[u_m, v_n], an open integrally closed subring. Then (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}) is a complete perfectoid Tate pair (C_{m,n} is a perfect complete Tate ring); a morphism of pairs (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}) → (R, R⁺) to a complete Huber pair with R Tate is the same as morphisms φ : (A, A⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ(ϖ)^m ψ(ϖ')⁻¹ ∈ R⁺ and ψ(ϖ')^n φ(ϖ)⁻¹ ∈ R⁺; for m ≤ m', n ≤ n', Spa(C_{m,n}) is the rational subset {|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1} of Spa(C_{m',n'}); and X × Y = ⋃_{m,n} Spa(C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}), glued along these rational open immersions (anchor Layer 5.3). For general X, Y the affinoid products glue. The plus ring must contain u_m and v_n: the integral closure of the image of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺ alone, as written in Berkeley's proof, is not open (see sourceIssues). The absolute product of two perfectoid fields need not be a point: Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) is the perfectoid punctured open unit disc {0 < |s| < 1} over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4), which is not quasi-compact and has infinitely many points. Lean: `HasBinaryProducts PerfectoidSpace.Perf`.

**Hypotheses.** X, Y perfectoid spaces of characteristic p. ϖ ∈ A, ϖ' ∈ B pseudouniformisers of the affinoid charts.

**Proof outline.**

1. E = A ⊗_{𝔽_p} B is perfect (𝔽_p, A, B perfect); ϖ ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ ϖ' are units of E; D_{m,n} is a subring containing both ϖ^m ⊗ 1 ∈ (1 ⊗ ϖ')D_{m,n} and 1 ⊗ ϖ'^n ∈ (ϖ ⊗ 1)D_{m,n}, so the two adic topologies agree and E is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ ⊗ 1 and ring of definition D_{m,n}.
2. Frobenius Φ of E satisfies Φ⁻¹((ϖ ⊗ 1)^{pk} D_{m,n}) ⊇ (ϖ ⊗ 1)^k D_{m,n}, so Φ is a homeomorphism and extends to an automorphism of C_{m,n}: C_{m,n} is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid and uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion, ECD Proposition 3.5; Berkeley Proposition 6.1.6).
3. C⁺_{m,n} is a ring of integral elements: it lies in C°_{m,n} (D_{m,n} is bounded), it is integrally closed, and it is open because (ϖ ⊗ 1)^{m+1} D_{m,n} ⊆ image((A⁺ ⊗ B⁺)[u_m, v_n]) (as (ϖ ⊗ 1)^{m+1}(a ⊗ b) = u_m (ϖa ⊗ ϖ'b) with ϖa ∈ A⁺, ϖ'b ∈ B⁺ for a ∈ A°, b ∈ B°) — Wedhorn Remark 7.15.
4. Universal property of (C_{m,n}, C⁺_{m,n}): a ring map E → R from φ, ψ is continuous for the D_{m,n}-topology iff it maps D_{m,n} into a bounded set, which holds when u_m, v_n map into R⁺; it extends to the completion (Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`) and maps C⁺_{m,n} into R⁺ (integral closure, closedness of R⁺).
5. Rational charts: the universal property identifies Spa(C_{m,n}) → Spa(C_{m',n'}) with the rational localisation at {|u_m| ≤ 1, |v_n| ≤ 1} (anchor Layer 3.1 universal property).
6. Every pair (φ, ψ) into a complete Tate pair (R, R⁺) factors through some chart: φ(ϖ)^m ψ(ϖ')⁻¹ → 0 as m → ∞ (φ(ϖ) is topologically nilpotent), so it lies in the open R⁺ for m ≫ 0, and likewise for n. Hence ⋃ Spa(C_{m,n}) represents pairs of morphisms from Tate affinoids; a test adic space T with morphisms to X is analytic, since morphisms send non-analytic points to non-analytic points (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (iii)), so it is covered by Tate affinoids (anchor Layer 2.3), and morphisms glue (Wedhorn Remark 8.24). This gives the product in adic spaces over Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) (an adic space by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy), hence in Perf.
7. General X, Y: glue the affinoid products over affinoid perfectoid covers, with the open-subspace compatibility (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces) as for fibre products.

**Unit tests** (a plausible wrong definition fails one of them):

- `prod_perfectoidFields` (computation): Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) ≅ {0 < |s| < 1} ⊆ Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))⟨s^{1/p^∞}⟩, the union of the affinoid perfectoid annuli Spa(C_{m,n}) = {|t|^m ≤ |s| ≤ |t|^{1/n}}; in particular the absolute product of two perfectoid fields is not a point and not quasi-compact.
- `prod_empty` (degenerate): X × ∅ = ∅ for every X ∈ Perf.
- `not_isPerfectoidSpace_spa_Fp_final` (non-example): Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) with the discrete topology is not an object of Perf (its point is not analytic), Perf has no final object (Berkeley Remark 8.3.6), and X × Y is not X ×_Z Y for any Z ∈ Perf in general; a definition of the product as a fibre product over a perfectoid 'Spa 𝔽_p' is ill-typed.
- `prodChart_plus_open` (non-example): For A = B = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) with ϖ = t, ϖ' = s: (t ⊗ 1)^k u_m^j is not integral over the image of A° ⊗ B° for j ≥ 1 (reduce modulo 1 ⊗ s^j: A° ⊗ (B°/s^j) is free over A°), so the integral closure of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺ is not open in E and (E, integral closure of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺) is not a Huber pair; the plus ring must contain u_m, v_n.
- `prod_isPullback_spaFp` (compatibility): X × Y with its projections is a pullback of X → Spa(𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) ← Y in the anchor's category of adic spaces, and it agrees with the absolute product of Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5.
- `prod_reduction_to_fields` (characterisation): For morphisms X → Spa K_t, Y → Spa K_s with K_t = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), K_s = 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) (which exist locally: t^{1/p^n} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^n}), X × Y ≅ X ×_{Spa K_t} (Spa K_t × Spa K_s) ×_{Spa K_s} Y, fibre products over perfectoid bases (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4).

**Acceptance.**

- Spa 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) × Spa 𝔽_p((s^{1/p^∞})) ≅ the perfectoid punctured open unit disc over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) in the coordinate s, the union of the perfectoid annuli {|t|^m ≤ |s| ≤ |t|^{1/n}} (ECD proof of Proposition 11.4).
- For X, Y ∈ Perf over a common perfectoid Z, the canonical morphism X ×_Z Y → X × Y is not an isomorphism in general: for K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})), Spa K ×_{Spa K} Spa K = Spa K is a point, while Spa K × Spa K is not.

### P2b.19 Scholze's perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K are the perfectoid spaces over Spa(K, K⁺₀)

`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison` (comparison). Scholze's perfectoid spaces over K (objects with a K-algebra structure on O_X, no condition K° ⊆ O_X⁺) form the slice Perfd/Spa(K, K⁺₀) with K⁺₀ the integral closure of ℤ + K°° (Wedhorn Remark 7.15(2)); Bhatt's Perfd/Spa(K, K°) is the same when the residue field of K is algebraic over 𝔽_p and a proper full subcategory otherwise. Scholze's tilt and fibre products are this layer's.

**Statement.** Let K be a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition), K° its valuation ring and K⁺₀ ⊆ K° the smallest ring of integral elements of K, the integral closure of ℤ·1 + K°° in K (Wedhorn Remark 7.15(2)); K⁺₀ = K° iff the residue field of K is algebraic over 𝔽_p. (i) Sch12's perfectoid K-algebras (Definition 5.1) and perfectoid affinoid K-algebras (Definition 6.1) are the perfectoid Tate rings, respectively complete perfectoid Tate pairs (R, R⁺), with a continuous K-algebra structure; no condition K° ⊆ R⁺ is imposed. (ii) Sch12's category of perfectoid spaces over K (Definition 6.15: objects of Huber's category of triples whose structure sheaf is a sheaf of complete topological K-algebras, locally affinoid perfectoid; morphisms continuous K-linear) is equivalent to the slice category Perfd/Spa(K, K⁺₀): a morphism X → Spa(K, K⁺₀) is a continuous ring map K → O_X(X) (Wedhorn Proposition 8.25), and every such map sends K⁺₀ into O_X⁺(X), which contains all topologically nilpotent elements and is integrally closed. The full subcategory Perfd/Spa(K, K°) (Bhatt Definition 9.3.9) consists of those X with K° ⊆ O_X⁺(X); it is all of Sch12's category when the residue field of K is algebraic over 𝔽_p (e.g. K = ℂ_p, ℚ_p^cycl, 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))), and a proper full subcategory otherwise. (iii) Sch12's tilt (Definition 6.16) of X over K is the glued tilt X♭ with its structure map to Spa(K♭, K♭⁺₀) (tilting preserves the smallest ring of integral elements, ECD Lemma 3.11), and Sch12 Proposition 6.17 is PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence for the base Spa(K, K⁺₀): the functorial bijection Hom(Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), X♭) = Hom(Spa(R, R⁺), X) over K♭, resp. K, holds. (iv) Sch12's fibre products (Proposition 6.18) are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces.

**Hypotheses.** K a perfectoid field.

**Proof outline.**

1. (i) Sch12 Definition 5.1 (R° open and bounded, Frobenius surjective on R°/ϖ) agrees with ECD Definition 3.1 for Banach K-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras records the comparison); Definition 2.6(ii) asks only R⁺ ⊆ R° open and integrally closed.
2. (ii) Wedhorn Proposition 8.25 identifies morphisms X → Spa(K, K⁺₀) with continuous ring maps K → O_X(X) carrying K⁺₀ into O_X⁺(X); the latter condition is automatic (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, integral closedness); a morphism of adic spaces over Spa(K, K⁺₀) is exactly a morphism whose ring maps are K-linear. Sch12's category (V) of triples with K-algebra structure is therefore the slice of the anchor's category over Spa(K, K⁺₀), and the perfectoid objects correspond (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space).
3. Non-surjectivity onto the slice over Spa(K, K°): if the residue field k of K is not algebraic over 𝔽_p, choose a valuation ring V ⊊ k (the residue field of K⁺₀ is the algebraic closure of 𝔽_p in k), and let R⁺ ⊆ K° be its preimage; then (K, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra in Sch12's sense and K° ⊄ R⁺.
4. (iii) ECD Lemma 3.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting) is an inclusion-preserving bijection, so it maps the smallest ring of integral elements of K to that of K♭; apply PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence with X = Spa(K, K⁺₀); Sch12's Definition 6.16 is the case T = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) of part (c) there.
5. (iv) Both are fibre products in the same category.

**Acceptance.**

- For K = ℂ_p: Sch12's perfectoid spaces over ℂ_p are the perfectoid spaces over Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}).
- For K the completed perfection of 𝔽_p(x)((t)) and R⁺ the preimage in K° of the valuation ring 𝔽_p[x]^{perf}_{(x)} of the residue field 𝔽_p(x)^{perf}: Spa(K, R⁺) is a perfectoid space over K in Sch12's sense with no morphism to Spa(K, K°).

**Used by.** Sch12 §§6-7 and all consumers stated over a perfectoid field K (PadicHodgeTheory, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties) (results stated for 'perfectoid spaces over K' transfer to Perfd/Spa(K, K⁺₀)); Bhatt, Definition 9.3.9 and Theorem 9.3.10 (the slice over Spa(K, K°) used in lecture notes).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over`.

**Sources.** sch12-perfectoid, Section 6, Definition 6.15, p. 38; sch12-perfectoid, Section 2, before Definition 2.18, p. 10; sch12-perfectoid, Section 2, Definition 2.6(ii), p. 8; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.3, Definition 9.3.9, printed p. 111; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §7.3, Remark 7.15(2), p. 60.

### Acceptance tests of the layer (spaces part)

- Sch12 Propositions 6.17 and 6.18 over a perfectoid field K (with the base Spa(K, K⁺₀)).
- Spa(ℚ_p^cycl)♭ ≅ Spa(𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))), and the perfectoid disc over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞})) untilts over ℚ_p^cycl to
  Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩).
- Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ×_{Spa R} Spa(R⟨S^{1/p^∞}⟩) ≅ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩) for every perfectoid Tate ring R,
  compatibly with tilting.
- Spa L ×_{Spa K} Spa L ≅ ⊔_{Gal(L/K)} Spa L for a finite Galois extension of perfectoid fields.

### Problems found in the sources

- Berkeley Lemma 8.3.5 (proof): the plus ring "integral closure of A⁺ ⊗ B⁺" of the product charts is not open
  for the chart topology, so the printed pair is not a Huber pair, and "A◦" should read R⁺; corrected in
  `P2/products-in-perf` (PerfectoidSpaces/E18).
- Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.7: the plus ring of B ⊗̂_A C is identified with the completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺, which
  holds only up to almost isomorphism and after integral closure; counterexample with a tamely ramified
  extension of perfectoid fields (PerfectoidSpaces/E19).
- Kedlaya–Liu I Proposition 3.6.11: the proof is incomplete (injectivity), as Kedlaya–Liu II Remark 3.3.14
  records; the statement is correct (PerfectoidSpaces/E20).

- Whether fibre products over a non-perfectoid analytic base exist in the category of all adic spaces: only

## P3. Almost purity and étale tilting


**Dependencies.** PerfectoidSpaces P0 (almost mathematics over a basic setup: almost finite
projective and almost finite étale algebras, the trace-form criterion, lifting of almost finite
étale algebras along ϖ-adically complete flat almost algebras, uniform finite projectivity modulo ϖ,
almost faithfully flat descent and the almost Amitsur complex, inversion of ϖ, almost Čech
cohomology), P1 (perfectoid Tate rings in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, the tilt and the sharp
map, pseudouniformisers with compatible p-power roots, the integral subrings modulo ϖ, the almost
setup (R°, R°°), the almost-integral dictionary, the tilting equivalence of perfectoid algebras over
a perfectoid base, the Witt-vector untilt, completed filtered colimits of perfectoid Tate rings and their tilts), P2 (rational localisation of perfectoid Tate pairs, the
tilting homeomorphism identifying rational subsets, completed residue fields, stable uniformity and
sheafiness, integral almost acyclicity, perfectoid spaces, the tilting slice equivalence, fibre
products of perfectoid spaces and over analytic bases); `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1` (finite étale Huber
pairs, strongly sheafy rings, finite étale and étale morphisms of analytic adic spaces, rational
descent of finite étale algebras, the local-to-global theorem, the étale and finite étale sites,
their structure sheaves, basis and covering reduction); `AdicSpacesPartII:R3` (traces of finite
projective algebras, the trace criterion for étaleness, Kiehl gluing and finite étale descent of
finite projective modules, split injections into stably uniform rings); `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`
(Čech-to-derived comparison); the anchor `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces` Layers 0, 2, 3, 4, 5
(requested). Mathlib supplies henselian pairs, étale and smooth algebras, the naive cotangent complex
and the Jacobian criterion, finite étale algebras as a category with base change, traces, Krasner's
lemma, infinite Galois theory, sites, sheaves, stacks, sheaf cohomology and faithfully flat descent of
modules.

**Consumers.** PerfectoidSpaces P4, P5 (ECD 6.4(o)–(iii) imports the henselian approximation and the
affinoid description of finite étale maps), P6, P7 (tilde-limits: finite étale maps descend to a
finite level); AdicSpacesPartII R5 (finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings are perfectoid);
AdicEtaleGeometry A3 (tilting of affinoid étale objects, strongly étale maps, ECD 6.2) and A4 (the
Tate-ring form of the henselian comparison); DiamondsAndVStacks D1–D3, D6 (étale sites, their tilting
equivalence, almost acyclicity, the finite étale and separated étale prestacks); PadicHodgeTheory P8
(almost purity for Ô⁺, tilting of étale sites, Sch12 5.25 and 7.5(i)); RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0,
RF4 and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3 (the finite étale site, étale descent of vector bundles).

P3 proves Faltings' almost purity theorem in the form of ECD Theorem 6.1 — for an **arbitrary
perfectoid Tate ring** R (ECD Definition 3.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that
ϖ^p divides p in R° and Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is bijective; characteristic 0, characteristic p, or
neither, as in ECD Example 3.4(iv); **no perfectoid base field**) — and globalises it to the étale site
of a perfectoid space, its tilting equivalence and the almost acyclicity of O⁺ (ECD Theorem 6.3).
Scholze 2012 proves these statements over a perfectoid field; Kedlaya–Liu I proves them for
perfectoid Banach ℚ_p-algebras and Kedlaya–Liu II §3.3 for Fontaine perfectoid Tate rings; the
Berkeley lectures and Kedlaya's Arizona notes state them for perfectoid Tate (and analytic) rings.
The three conclusions of Theorem 6.1 are three distinct nodes, and none of them is replaced by a
stronger-looking but different statement: the integral conclusion is *almost* finite étaleness of S°
over R°, never étaleness of S° over R° (false: K(p^{1/2})° over K° for K = ℚ_p^cycl is ramified) and
never finite freeness of S over R.

**Proof architecture.**

1. *Henselian prefix (algebraic, no perfectoid input).* Finite étale algebras over R[t⁻¹] and over
   R^∧[t⁻¹] agree when (R, tI) is henselian and t is a non-zero-divisor (Gabber–Ramero Proposition
   5.4.54 = book 5.4.53). This is decomposed along Gabber–Ramero §5.4: Newton approximation over
   complete rings, Elkik's noetherian theorem, approximation over henselian pairs via henselisation,
   density of sections of smooth quasi-projective schemes and openness of smooth maps on sections,
   the orbit comparison for smooth groupoids, projective modules, and the smooth scheme of étale
   algebra structures with its étale GL-action. Corollaries in Tate-ring language: FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â)
   for a topologically henselian Tate ring (Berkeley 7.4.8), FÉt of a completed filtered colimit is
   the 2-colimit (Sch12 7.5(i)), completed perfection does not change FÉt in characteristic p (Sch12
   7.5(ii)), and finite étale algebras over k(x)^ spread out to a rational neighbourhood of x
   (Berkeley 7.4.6). This prefix is placed in P3 because the local-to-global step of almost purity
   uses it; P5 and P7 import it.
2. *Characteristic p.* Étale algebras over perfect rings are perfect (relative Frobenius), finite
   étale algebras over uniform rings are uniform with S° the integral closure, and the Frobenius
   argument on the diagonal idempotent gives almost finite étaleness with a uniform bound (Sch12
   5.23, Bhatt 4.3.4, Gabber–Ramero 3.5.28); inverting ϖ is then an equivalence
   (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R).
3. *Untilting.* The chain FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet →
   FÉt(R) defines T ↦ T♯; it is fully faithful with image the S having perfectoid S and almost finite
   étale S°a (Sch12 5.25). Over a perfectoid field every finite extension is in the image (Sch12 3.7,
   via the algebraically closed case and Krasner), which gives Fontaine–Wintenberger.
4. *Local to global (ECD 6.1(ii)).* For S ∈ FÉt(R) and x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺), S ⊗ k(x)^ untilts from
   k(x♭)^; spreading out on the tilt side, untilting over a rational neighbourhood and spreading out
   again identify S over a rational U ∋ x with an untilt; finitely many U cover; the untilted pieces
   glue on the tilt side by effective descent of finite étale algebras along rational coverings
   (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent, Kedlaya–Liu 2.6.9), which needs no
   sheafiness. Then (i) and (iii) follow (every S is an untilt).
5. *Geometry.* Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy, so A1's theory applies to perfectoid
   spaces; finite étale and étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are A1's classes (no second notion),
   and almost purity shows they are strongly (finite) étale, satisfy ECD Definition 6.2 in its
   'for all affinoids' form, tilt, and form the étale site X_ét. Tilting is an equivalence of sites;
   almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét reduces, by the covering reduction and the Čech-to-derived
   comparison, to rational coverings (P2) and finite étale surjections (the almost Amitsur complex of
   the almost faithfully flat R⁺a → S⁺a).

No proof depends on diamonds or v-descent (the latter is DiamondsAndVStacks D3's, which imports this
stage).

### Conventions

1. A prime p is fixed. A *perfectoid Tate ring* is as in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras
   (ECD Definition 3.1). A *perfectoid Tate pair* (R, R⁺) adds a ring of integral elements
   R⁺ ⊆ R° (open, integrally closed; Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`). No base field is fixed anywhere in P3;
   statements over a perfectoid field K appear only as special cases and tests.
2. (R♭, R♭⁺) is the tilt, f ↦ f♯ the sharp map (multiplicative, continuous, not additive). A
   pseudouniformiser ϖ♭ ∈ R♭⁺ is fixed with ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p in R°, so that R°/ϖ = R♭°/ϖ♭ and
   R⁺/ϖ = R♭⁺/ϖ♭.
3. FÉt(A) is Mathlib's `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A`: A-algebras B with `Module.Finite A B` and
   `Algebra.Etale A B`. For a complete Tate ring A, B carries its natural module topology; for a
   Huber pair (A, A⁺) its plus ring is the integral closure of A⁺ in B (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`,
   AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) — never B° when A⁺ ≠ A°.
4. Almost mathematics is taken for the basic setup (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup);
   an R°-module is almost zero iff it is killed by every pseudouniformiser, equivalently by all
   ϖ^{1/pⁿ}; R⁺a = R°a. (A)_afet denotes almost finite étale A-algebras (almost finitely presented,
   almost projective, unramified: PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).
   *Uniformly* almost finite projective means: a fixed n such that every ε ∈ R°° factors through
   (R°)ⁿ.
5. Perfectoid spaces are the full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space;
   affinoid perfectoid means Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid (Berkeley Remark 7.1.3).
   `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale` and `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale` *are* A1's `AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale`
   and `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription` on the underlying morphisms; ECD's, Scholze 2012's and the
   Berkeley lectures' formulations are theorems (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale).
6. X_ét is A1's small étale site (objects all adic spaces étale over X, automatically perfectoid;
   coverings jointly surjective on all points). Cohomology is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.
7. Gabber–Ramero is cited in the arXiv v3 numbering; Scholze 2012 and ECD cite the LNM 1800 book, in
   which the finite étale comparison is Proposition 5.4.53 (arXiv 5.4.54).

### Henselian finite étale approximation (the algebraic prefix)

#### `henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions` — Henselian pairs: adic completeness, filtered colimits, and independence of the ring of definition of a Tate ring

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Pairs (A, I) (a commutative ring and an ideal) are henselian in Mathlib's sense `HenselianRing A I` (I ⊆ Jacobson radical and simple roots modulo I lift). (a) If A is I-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete I A`), then (A, I) is henselian (Mathlib instance `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing`; Stacks Tag 0ALJ). (b) If (A_j, I_j)_{j ∈ J} is a directed system of henselian pairs (ring maps A_j → A_k carrying I_j into I_k), then (colim A_j, colim I_j) is a henselian pair (colimit in rings, Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`; Stacks Tag 0FWT). In particular, if every A_j is henselian along the ideal generated by the image of a fixed element ϖ ∈ A_{j₀}, so is colim A_j. (c) Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`), ϖ ∈ A a pseudouniformiser and A₀, A₀' ⊆ A rings of definition containing ϖ. Then (A₀, ϖA₀) is henselian if and only if (A₀', ϖA₀') is henselian, if and only if (A°, A°°) is henselian, if and only if (A⁺, A°°) is henselian for one (equivalently every) ring of integral elements A⁺ ⊆ A°. A Tate ring with this property is called topologically henselian (`Huber.IsTopologicallyHenselian A`). Every complete Tate ring is topologically henselian, by (a) applied to a ϖ-adically complete ring of definition; and a filtered colimit of Tate rings A_j along continuous maps, with the colimit topology in which colim A_{j,0} is a ring of definition for compatible rings of definition A_{j,0} containing ϖ, is topologically henselian when each A_j is, by (b).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- All rings commutative; ϖ a pseudouniformiser (a topologically nilpotent unit) of the Tate ring A; rings of definition are open and bounded subrings.
- (c) uses only the abstract ring maps A₀ → A and the topology through the choice of rings of definition; completeness is not assumed in the equivalence.

*Proof outline.*
1. (a) is Mathlib's instance: an I-adically complete ring is Hausdorff and precomplete, I lies in the Jacobson radical (IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot) and Newton iteration converges (Stacks 0ALJ proof, lifting factorisations modulo Iⁿ).
2. (b): an element of 1 + I comes from 1 + I_j for some j, where it is a unit; a monic polynomial with a coprime factorisation modulo I comes, with the factorisation and a Bezout identity, from some A_j, where it lifts; map the lift to A (Stacks 0FWT proof). The simple-root formulation of Mathlib's `HenselianRing` is equivalent to the factorisation formulation (Stacks Lemma 15.11.6), so the argument is run in whichever form Mathlib provides.
3. (c): two rings of definition containing ϖ are commensurable: A₀ ⊆ ϖ^{-N}A₀' and conversely; the ideal ϖA₀ and ϖA₀' generate the same topology and, by the invariance of henselian pairs under replacing the ring by one sharing the ideal as a non-unital ring (Gabber–Ramero Remark 5.1.9(ii), used in Bhatt's proof of Lemma 7.2.3(3)), henselianity transfers along A₀ ∩ A₀' ⊆ A₀, A₀'. A⁺ and A° are filtered colimits of open bounded subrings containing ϖ (Bhatt Lemma 7.2.3(1)); combine with (b).
4. Completeness of A implies that its rings of definition are ϖ-adically complete (anchor Layer 0: completion of Huber rings), so (a) gives topological henselianity.

*Acceptance.*
- (ℤ_p, pℤ_p) and (ℤ_p⟦T⟧, (p, T)) are henselian by (a); the henselisation ℤ_(p)^h of ℤ_(p) is henselian but not p-adically complete.
- For K a perfectoid field and K_i the finite subextensions of a Galois extension L/K, colim K_i° = L° is henselian along ϖ by (b), although L is not complete.
- Non-example: ℤ_(3) (localisation of ℤ at (3)) is not henselian along 3: X² − 7 has the simple root 1 modulo 3 (derivative 2, a unit) but no root in ℤ_(3); accordingly the Tate ring ℚ with the 3-adic topology (ring of definition ℤ_(3)) is not topologically henselian.
