*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation — the henselian hypothesis of the Tate-ring form, and colimits of complete rings; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit — colim A_i° is henselian along ϖ; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit — the colimit of the O⁺(U), x ∈ U, is henselian along ϖ.

*Prerequisites.* `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit`, `mathlib:Ideal.jacobson`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`.

*Sources.* The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 0FWT (Lemma 15.11.13), Section 15.11 Henselian pairs; The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 0ALJ (Lemma 15.11.4); Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, paragraph before Lemma 7.5, p. 40; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 7, Lemma 7.2.3 (3) and (5), p. 57.

#### `finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings` — Finite étale algebras over a filtered colimit of rings are defined at a finite stage

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Let (R_j)_{j ∈ J} be a directed system of commutative rings with colimit R = colim R_j (Mathlib `Ring.DirectLimit`), and write FÉt(A) for Mathlib's category `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale A` of finite étale A-algebras (`Module.Finite A B` and `Algebra.Etale A B`). Then the base change functors FÉt(R_j) → FÉt(R) (`CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`) induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_j FÉt(R_j) ≃ FÉt(R), compatible with tensor products. Concretely: (a) every finite étale R-algebra is isomorphic to S_j ⊗_{R_j} R for some j and some finite étale R_j-algebra S_j; (b) for S_j, T_j ∈ FÉt(R_j) the map colim_{k ≥ j} Hom_{R_k}(S_j ⊗ R_k, T_j ⊗ R_k) → Hom_R(S_j ⊗ R, T_j ⊗ R) is bijective; (c) the rank function of S_j ⊗ R on Spec R, faithful flatness, and the existence of a section of S_j ⊗ R → R descend to some R_k (k ≥ j).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- J directed; no noetherian hypothesis.
- Finite étale = finite, flat, finitely presented and unramified; equivalently finite projective with perfect trace pairing.

*Proof outline.*
1. (a): a finite étale R-algebra is finitely presented, hence comes from a finitely presented R_j-algebra S_j (EGA IV 8.8.2); finiteness, flatness and unramifiedness of S_j ⊗ R_k over R_k hold for k ≫ j (EGA IV 8.10.5, 11.2.6, 17.7.8(ii); Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9).
2. (b): Hom-sets of finitely presented algebras commute with filtered colimits: a map S_j ⊗ R → T_j ⊗ R is determined by the images of finitely many generators satisfying finitely many relations, all defined over some R_k; two maps agreeing over R agree over some R_k.
3. (c): the rank is read off from the characteristic polynomial of the multiplication on a projective presentation, defined at a finite stage; faithful flatness of a finite étale algebra is surjectivity on Spec, equivalently the rank is everywhere positive, a condition on finitely many idempotents; a section is an algebra map, handled by (b).

*Acceptance.*
- For R_j = ℚ(ζ_{3^j}) with colimit R = ℚ(μ_{3^∞}): S = R[U]/(U³ − 2) comes from R_0 = ℚ, and its automorphism U ↦ ζ_3U is defined over R_1 = ℚ(ζ_3) but not over R_0 — (b) needs the passage to a larger index.
- For a perfectoid field K and its finite subextensions K_i of a Galois L/K, FÉt(colim K_i) = FÉt(L) is 2-colim FÉt(K_i) (used in the Fontaine–Wintenberger node).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit — first half: FÉt(colim A_i) = 2-colim FÉt(A_i); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit — FÉt of the colimit of the O(U), x ∈ U; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger — finite étale algebras over an algebraic extension.

*Prerequisites.* `mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`, `mathlib:Algebra.FinitePresentation`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

*Sources.* Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §1.2, Remark 1.2.9, p. 15; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, proof of Lemma 7.5 (i), p. 41; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 10, proof of Corollary 10.0.5, p. 119.

#### `approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings` — Newton approximation: approximate solutions with Jacobian control lift to true solutions over (t, I)-adically complete rings

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Let R be a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal, F = R[X_1, …, X_N], J ⊆ F a finitely generated ideal and S = F/J. Let H ⊆ F be the Jacobian ideal of the presentation: H := H_R(F, J) = Ann_F Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, J/J²), computed from the naive cotangent complex J/J² → S ⊗_F Ω_{F/R} (Mathlib `Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`), which contains Elkik's ideal H_S = Σ_p Σ_{|α| = p} Δ_α (J_α : J) generated by p × p Jacobian minors times colon ideals (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.6). For a ∈ R^N write p_a = (X_1 − a_1, …, X_N − a_N). (i) (one step; Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.8) If n, h ≥ 0 with n > 2h and t^h ∈ H + p_a and J ⊆ p_a + tⁿIF, then there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b + (t^{n−h}I)²F. (ii) (complete case; Gabber–Ramero Claim 5.4.14) If moreover R is complete for the tI-adic topology, there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b, i.e. f(b) = 0 for every f ∈ J: approximate solutions of a system that is smooth up to t^h lift to exact solutions congruent modulo t^{n−h}I. Elkik's Théorème 1 is the noetherian version with an arbitrary ideal of definition, and Tougeron's lemma (Elkik Lemme 2) the version with the maximal Jacobian minors.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- t a non-zero-divisor; I an arbitrary ideal (not necessarily finitely generated); J finitely generated.
- H depends only on the presentation (F, J); smoothness of S over R away from V(H·S) (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2(ii)) is not used in (i)–(ii).

*Proof outline.*
1. (0) (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2) Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, N) only involves the naive cotangent complex J/J² → S ⊗_F Ω_{F/R} (Gabber–Ramero (5.4.3)), so h ∈ H iff multiplication by h on J/J² factors through ∂; hence S_h is smooth over R for h ∈ H (Jacobian criterion, Mathlib `Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_split_injection`), and H annihilates Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, N) for every S-module N.
2. (i): an approximate solution is an R-algebra map σ: S → R/tⁿI. Lifting σ modulo t^{n−h}I to R/(t^{n−h}I)² is the Newton step: writing f(a + δ) = f(a) + Σ_i ∂_i f(a) δ_i + (terms quadratic in δ) for generators f of J, one needs δ ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N solving the linearised system modulo (t^{n−h}I)²; since t^h ∈ H + p_a, multiplication by t^h on the conormal module factors through the Jacobian map ∂ evaluated at a, and δ is obtained by applying this factorisation to the vector (f(a)) ∈ tⁿI (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.8, phrased there as the vanishing of an obstruction class in Ext¹_S(L_{S/R}, t^{n−h}I/(t^{n−h}I)²), killed by t^h because it is killed by p_a and by H).
3. (ii): iterate (i): starting from a₀ = a, obtain a_{m+1} ≡ a_m modulo ever higher powers of tI with the hypothesis of (i) preserved (the inequality n > 2h improves at each step); the sequence converges tI-adically to b with J ⊆ p_b.
4. Alternative for complete-intersection presentations (Tougeron, Elkik Lemme 2): write the equations with the Jacobian matrix M(a) and matrices N_i with M(a)N_i = d_i·Id; the system in the correction vectors u_i is étale at u = 0 modulo t^{n−2h}, hence has a true solution by Hensel's lemma in the complete ring.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℤ_p, t = p, I = R, f = X² − 7 ∈ ℤ_p[X] (p odd, 7 a square mod p): a = any square root of 7 modulo p is an approximate solution with h = 0, and (ii) produces the square root of 7 in ℤ_p (Hensel's lemma).
- For R = ℤ_p, f = X² with a = 0 modulo p^n: H ∌ unit powers of p near a (the derivative vanishes at 0) and the lemma makes no claim; the double root is not isolated, as it must be.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-approximate-solutions — the complete case of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.13; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation — Elkik's Théorème 1, applied on the completions.

*Prerequisites.* `mathlib:Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex`, `mathlib:Algebra.H1Cotangent`, `mathlib:Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_split_injection`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Matrix.det`, `mathlib:Algebra.FinitePresentation`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.8 and the paragraph after its proof, p. 118 (arXiv v3 numbering); Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.13 and Claim 5.4.14, p. 119; Renée Elkik (Elkik-SolutionsHenselien-1973), Introduction and §I, Théorème 1, pp. 553 and 558–560.

#### `elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation` — Elkik's approximation theorem for noetherian henselian pairs (Théorème 2 bis)

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Let (A, 𝔍) be a henselian pair with A noetherian, Â its 𝔍-adic completion, B a finitely generated A-algebra and B̂ = B ⊗_A Â. Let V ⊆ Spec B be an open subset smooth over Spec A and V̂ its preimage in Spec B̂. Then for every integer n and every Â-section ε̂: Spec Â → Spec B̂ whose restriction to Spec Â ∖ V(𝔍Â) factors through V̂, there is an A-section ε: Spec A → Spec B with ε ≡ ε̂ modulo 𝔍ⁿ whose restriction to Spec A ∖ V(𝔍) factors through V. Equivalently (Elkik Théorème 2): for h ≥ 0 there are n₀, r such that for every presentation B = A[X_1, …, X_N]/J, every n ≥ n₀ and every a⁰ ∈ A^N with J(a⁰) ⊆ 𝔍ⁿ and H_B(a⁰) ⊇ 𝔍^h there is a ∈ A^N, a ≡ a⁰ modulo 𝔍^{n−r}, with J(a) = 0. This is the noetherian input (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.12) of the non-noetherian approximation.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- A noetherian; (A, 𝔍) henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing A 𝔍`); B of finite type over A.
- The smooth locus V is given; smoothness is Mathlib's `Algebra.Smooth` on affine opens.

*Proof outline.*
1. (Remark after the statement) It suffices to find, for every n, a section congruent to ε̂ modulo 𝔍ⁿ: if V = Spec B ∖ V(I) and ε̂*(I) ⊇ 𝔍^a Â, any section congruent modulo 𝔍ⁿ, n > a, factors through V over Spec A ∖ V(𝔍).
2. Tougeron's lemma (Elkik Lemme 2): if the q × q minors Δ of the Jacobian of generators f_1, …, f_q of J satisfy J(a) ⊆ 𝔍ⁿ and Δ(a) ⊇ 𝔍^h with n > 2h, there is a' ≡ a modulo 𝔍^{n−h} with J(a') = 0; the correction system is étale at the origin modulo 𝔍^{n−2h}, and henselianity lifts its approximate zero.
3. Elkik Lemme 3: replacing Spec B by the vector bundle of the conormal sheaf J/J² of a closed embedding, V becomes smooth of constant relative dimension and is, near every affine open of V, cut out by exactly as many equations as its codimension (a local complete intersection presentation) — this reduces to Tougeron's situation.
4. Elkik Lemme 4 (𝔍 = (t) principal): choose h ∈ A[X] invertible along ε̂ and inside the lci locus, generators f_1, …, f_{N−d} of J over D(h), and apply Tougeron's lemma to get a section s with s*(f_1, …, f_{N−d}) = 0 congruent to ε̂; by Artin–Rees (Mathlib `Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul`) the t-power-torsion part of s*(J) vanishes, so s*(J) = 0.
5. General 𝔍 = (a_1, …, a_l): induction on l. Over A_1 = the a_1-adic completion apply Théorème 1 (the complete case, P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings in Elkik's noetherian form) and the induction hypothesis for (A/a_1^m, 𝔍/a_1^m) to produce an A_1-section congruent to ε̂; then Lemme 4 for the principal ideal (a_1) approximates it by an A-section.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = ℤ_(p)^h (the henselisation of ℤ at p, noetherian, henselian along p) and B = A[X]/(X² − 7) (p odd, 7 a nonzero square mod p): the square root of 7 in ℤ_p = Â is approximated by, and in fact equals, an A-point, as the equation is étale.
- The corollary (Elkik §II, Corollaire 1 and the theorem following it): a smooth A-algebra B has an A-section lifting any section modulo 𝔍ⁿ.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-approximate-solutions — the noetherian approximation step for general henselian pairs.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings`, `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `mathlib:Matrix.det`.

*Sources.* Renée Elkik (Elkik-SolutionsHenselien-1973), §II, Théorème 2 bis, p. 560; Renée Elkik (Elkik-SolutionsHenselien-1973), §II, Lemme 2 (Tougeron) and proof of Théorème 2 bis, pp. 561 and 566–567; Renée Elkik (Elkik-SolutionsHenselien-1973), §II, proof of Lemme 4, p. 564; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.12 and its proof, p. 119.

#### `henselisation-of-pairs` — The henselisation of a pair (A, I)

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

For a pair (A, I) (a commutative ring and an ideal) the henselisation is a henselian pair (A^h, I^h) (Mathlib `HenselianRing A^h I^h`) with a map of pairs (A, I) → (A^h, I^h) that is universal among maps from (A, I) to henselian pairs: the functor (A, I) ↦ (A^h, I^h) is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs (Stacks Tag 0A02). It is constructed as the filtered colimit of the étale A-algebras B with A/I ≅ B/IB. Properties: A → A^h is flat, I^h = IA^h, and A/Iⁿ → A^h/IⁿA^h is an isomorphism for every n (Tag 0AGU); henselisation commutes with filtered colimits of pairs (Tag 0A04); if A is noetherian, A^h is noetherian, A and A^h have the same I-adic completion, A → A^h → A^∧ are flat and A^h → A^∧ is faithfully flat (Tag 0AGV).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- (A, I) arbitrary; the noetherian statements need A noetherian.

*Proof outline.*
1. Construction: the category of étale A-algebras B with A/I ≅ B/IB is filtered (fibre products and equalisers of such are again such), and its colimit A^h with I^h = IA^h is henselian: a monic polynomial with a simple root modulo I^h is defined over some B, and adjoining the root gives a further étale B' with the same reduction (Stacks proof of 0A02).
2. Universal property: for (A, I) → (C, J) with (C, J) henselian, each such B has a unique A-map B → C compatible with the reductions (henselian pairs lift sections of étale algebras, Stacks Tag 09XI; Mathlib `HenselianRing` in its simple-root form, P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions), and these assemble to A^h → C.
3. Flatness and A/Iⁿ ≅ A^h/IⁿA^h: étale maps are flat and each B satisfies A/Iⁿ ≅ B/IⁿB (étale and an isomorphism modulo I).
4. Colimits: both sides satisfy the same universal property; P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b) shows the colimit of henselisations is henselian.
5. Noetherian case: the completions agree by A/Iⁿ ≅ A^h/Iⁿ; A^h is noetherian because its completion is and A^h → A^∧ is faithfully flat (Stacks 0AGV proof).

*API.*
- `Ring.henselization` (constructor): The henselisation A^h of a pair (A, I), with its ideal I^h = IA^h.
- `Ring.henselization.algebraMap` (data): The canonical map A → A^h of pairs.
- `Ring.henselization.henselianRing` (instance): HenselianRing (A^h) (I^h).
- `Ring.henselization.lift` (universal-property): For (A, I) → (C, J) with (C, J) henselian, the induced A^h → C.
- `Ring.henselization.lift_comp_algebraMap` (universal-property): lift ∘ algebraMap = the given map.
- `Ring.henselization.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two maps A^h → C to a henselian pair agreeing on A are equal.
- `Ring.henselization.flat` (instance): A^h is flat over A.
- `Ring.henselization.quotientPowEquiv` (equivalence): A/Iⁿ ≃ A^h/IⁿA^h for all n.
- `Ring.henselization.isNoetherianRing` (instance): A noetherian ⇒ A^h noetherian.
- `Ring.henselization.adicCompletionEquiv` (compatibility): For A noetherian, AdicCompletion I A ≃ AdicCompletion I^h A^h.
- `Ring.henselization.directLimitEquiv` (functoriality): Henselisation commutes with filtered colimits of pairs.

*Unit tests.*
- `Ring.henselization_test_self` (degenerate): If (A, I) is henselian then A → A^h is an isomorphism; for I = 0, A^h = A.
- `Ring.henselization_test_Zp` (computation): The henselisation of (ℤ, pℤ) is the subring of ℤ_p of elements algebraic over ℚ, and (ℤ^h)/pⁿ = ℤ/pⁿ.
- `Ring.henselization_test_completion` (compatibility): For A noetherian, the I-adic completions of A and A^h coincide and A^h → A^∧ is faithfully flat.
- `Ring.henselization_test_lift` (characterisation): Every map of pairs (A, I) → (C, J) with (C, J) henselian factors uniquely through (A^h, I^h).
- `Ring.henselization_test_not_completion` (non-example): A^h ≠ A^∧ in general: ℤ_(p)^h is countable while ℤ_p is not.

*Acceptance.*
- The henselisation of (ℤ, pℤ) is ℤ_(p)^h, the ring of p-adic integers algebraic over ℚ; it is countable, so it differs from ℤ_p.
- If (A, I) is henselian, A → A^h is an isomorphism.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-approximate-solutions — noetherian henselian subrings R_λ^h → R to which Elkik applies; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization — henselisation of the pair (D, I) of a ring of definition; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation — noetherian henselian pairs with the same completion.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit`.

*Sources.* The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 0A02 (Lemma 15.12.1), Section 15.12 Henselization of pairs; The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 0AGV (Lemma 15.12.4); The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 0A04 (Lemma 15.12.5); Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, proof of Proposition 5.4.13, p. 119.

#### `henselian-approximate-solutions` — Approximate solutions over henselian pairs (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.13)

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

In the situation of P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings (R a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal, S = R[X_1, …, X_N]/J with J finitely generated, H = H_R(F, J)), assume that the pair (R, tI) is henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing R (t • I)`). If a ∈ R^N and n, h ≥ 0 satisfy n > 2h, t^h ∈ H + p_a and J ⊆ p_a + tⁿIF, then there is b ∈ R^N with b − a ∈ t^{n−h}I·R^N and J ⊆ p_b: every approximate solution of a system smooth up to t^h is close to a true solution in R itself, not only in its completion.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- t a non-zero-divisor; (R, tI) henselian; R not assumed noetherian or complete.

*Proof outline.*
1. Complete case: P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings (ii).
2. General R: choose a finitely generated H' ⊆ H with t^h ∈ H' + p_a; write R as the filtered union of its finitely generated (hence noetherian) subrings R_λ containing t, a, the coefficients of generators of J and H', with I_λ = I ∩ R_λ; after replacing R_λ by their henselisations along tI_λ (P3/henselisation-of-pairs: noetherian, mapping to R by the universal property since (R, tI) is henselian, with the same completion) all pairs (R_λ, tI_λ) are henselian and noetherian and the hypotheses hold over R_λ.
3. Over the completion R̂_λ, the complete case gives c ≡ a with J_λ ⊆ p_c; the locus U_λ = Spec S_λ ∖ V(H_λ) is smooth over R_λ (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.2(ii)) and c factors through it away from V(tI_λ). Elkik's theorem (P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation) gives an R_λ-section congruent to c modulo (tI_λ)^{n−h}; its image in R is the required b.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = ℤ_(p)^h[p^{1/p^∞}] = colim_n ℤ_(p)^h[p^{1/pⁿ}] (henselian along p by P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b), neither noetherian nor complete), t = p, I = R: the equation X² − 7 (p odd, 7 a nonzero square modulo p) has its simple approximate root modulo p refined to a root in R itself.
- The conclusion fails for non-henselian pairs: over ℤ_(p) the equation X² = 7 (p odd, 7 a square mod p, not a square in ℚ) has approximate solutions modulo every p^n but no solution.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs — density of R[t⁻¹]-points of smooth affine schemes.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/approximate-solutions-over-complete-rings`, `P3/elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation`, `P3/henselisation-of-pairs`, `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.13 with proof, p. 119.

#### `smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs` — Sections of smooth quasi-projective schemes over R[t⁻¹] are dense in those over R^∧[t⁻¹]; smooth maps are open on sections

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Let t ∈ R be a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal with (R, tI) henselian, R^∧ = lim_n R/tⁿI the (t, I)-adic completion and I^∧ the closure of I in R^∧. For a finitely generated R[t⁻¹]-module (or the set of sections X(R[t⁻¹]) of an affine R[t⁻¹]-scheme of finite type embedded in affine space) the (t, I)-adic topology is the linear topology with basis tᵏI·N₀ for a finitely generated R-lattice N₀ (independent of the lattice and of the embedding; Gabber–Ramero 5.4.10–5.4.16), and it glues on quasi-projective schemes (5.4.19). Then: (a) (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.21) for every smooth quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-scheme X, the map X(R[t⁻¹]) → X(R^∧[t⁻¹]) has dense image for the (t, I)- and (t, I^∧)-adic topologies; (b) (Proposition 5.4.30) for a morphism φ: X → Y of quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-schemes, φ_*: X(R[t⁻¹]) → Y(R[t⁻¹]) is continuous, and it is open when φ is smooth.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- t a non-zero-divisor, (R, tI) henselian, X, Y quasi-projective over R[t⁻¹], topologies as described.

*Proof outline.*
1. (a), affine X = Spec S (Claim 5.4.22): choose a finitely presented R-model S₀ = R[X]/J with S₀[t⁻¹] = S; smoothness gives t^h ∈ H_R(R[X], J) + J; approximate a given R^∧-section by an R-point σ₀ agreeing modulo tⁿI; then t^h ∈ H + p and J ⊆ p + tⁿIR[X] for p = ker σ₀, and P3/henselian-approximate-solutions produces a true R-point close to σ₀.
2. (a), projective space (Claim 5.4.27): a section of P^r over R^∧[t⁻¹] is a rank-one projective quotient, i.e. an idempotent matrix; the scheme of idempotent matrices U_n is smooth over ℤ (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20) and affine, so the affine case applies near it; quasi-projective X (Claim 5.4.29) reduces to open subschemes of projective ones.
3. (b): continuity by factoring through the graph (closed immersion) and a projection; openness for smooth φ: a section ξ of Y near φ_*(σ) extends over an R-model (Claim 5.4.31), and the fibre X ×_Y ξ is smooth over R[t⁻¹] with an approximate section, which P3/henselian-approximate-solutions makes exact.

*Acceptance.*
- X = 𝔾_m with R = ℤ_(p)^h, t = p, I = R (so R^∧[1/p] = ℚ_p): the units of ℤ_(p)^h[1/p] are dense in ℚ_p^×.
- Openness in (b) fails for non-smooth φ: X = Spec R[t⁻¹][x], Y = Spec R[t⁻¹][y], φ: y = x²; near y = 0 the image of φ_* is not a neighbourhood.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs — density and openness drive the orbit comparison.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/henselian-approximate-solutions`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.21, p. 121; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.21, conclusion, p. 121; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.30, pp. 122–123.

#### `groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs` — Isomorphism classes of points of a smooth groupoid do not change from R[t⁻¹] to R^∧[t⁻¹]

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Keep the hypotheses of P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs. Let (X₀, X₁, s, t, c, ι) be a groupoid in quasi-projective R[t⁻¹]-schemes (objects X₀, morphisms X₁ with source and target s, t: X₁ → X₀, composition c, identity ι), and for an R[t⁻¹]-algebra T let π₀(X₀(T)) denote the set of isomorphism classes of the groupoid of T-points. If X₀ is smooth over R[t⁻¹] and (s, t): X₁ → X₀ ×_{R[t⁻¹]} X₀ is smooth, then the natural map π₀(X₀(R[t⁻¹])) → π₀(X₀(R^∧[t⁻¹])) is bijective (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 5.4.38).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- Hypotheses of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.21; X₀ smooth and (s, t) smooth.

*Proof outline.*
1. Surjective: for σ ∈ X₀(R^∧[t⁻¹]) choose σ₀ ∈ X₀(R[t⁻¹]) close to σ (density, P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs (a)); (σ, σ) = (s, t)(ι(σ)) lies in the image of (s, t)_*, which is open ((b), (s, t) smooth), so (σ, σ₀) is in the image when σ₀ is close enough: σ ≅ σ₀.
2. Injective: if σ, τ ∈ X₀(R[t⁻¹]) become isomorphic via α ∈ X₁(R^∧[t⁻¹]), approximate α by α₀ ∈ X₁(R[t⁻¹]) (X₁ is smooth, being smooth over the smooth X₀ × X₀); by continuity (s, t)(α₀) = (σ₀, τ₀) is close to (σ, τ); openness of (s, t)_* near (σ, σ) and (τ, τ) makes σ ≅ σ₀ and τ ≅ τ₀ over R[t⁻¹], so σ ≅ τ.

*Acceptance.*
- The groupoid of idempotent matrices under conjugation (P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion) and of étale algebra structures under GL(P) (P3/etale-algebra-structure-schemes) are the two instances used.
- Without smoothness of (s, t) the map can fail to be injective: for the trivial groupoid of a non-smooth X₀ with two points identified only formally, orbits split.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion — applied to the groupoid F_n ⇉ U_n; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation — applied to Aut_P acting on U_P.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, 5.4.36 and Theorem 5.4.38, p. 124.

#### `projective-modules-over-henselian-completion` — Finitely generated projective modules over R[t⁻¹] and over R^∧[t⁻¹] correspond (Gabber–Ramero Corollary 5.4.42)

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Keep the hypotheses of P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs. Then base change M ↦ M ⊗_R R^∧ induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-modules and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R^∧[t⁻¹]-modules. The groupoid used: U_n = the scheme of idempotent n × n matrices (smooth over ℤ, Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20), F_n = the scheme of quadruples (S, T, φ, ψ) with S, T idempotent and φ, ψ mutually inverse isomorphisms Coker S ⇄ Coker T (smooth over U_n × U_n, Lemma 5.4.41).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- Hypotheses of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.21.

*Proof outline.*
1. U_n is of finite presentation and formally smooth: an idempotent matrix modulo a square-zero ideal lifts (lift M, pass to the commutative algebra R₀[M], lift the idempotent; Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.20 via Proposition 2.5.13(i)).
2. F_n → U_n ×_ℤ U_n is smooth: given (S, T) and an isomorphism of cokernels modulo a nilpotent ideal, lift it by projectivity and Nakayama (Lemma 5.4.41).
3. (U_n, F_n, s, t) with the evident identity and composition is a groupoid in affine schemes of finite type over ℤ satisfying the hypotheses of P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs; its π₀ over a ring T is the set of isomorphism classes of projective T-modules generated by n elements (every such module is the cokernel of an idempotent), so the orbit comparison is the claim.

*Acceptance.*
- Degenerate case: if R is already (t, I)-adically complete, R^∧ = R and the bijection is the identity.
- The bijection is compatible with direct sums and tensor products of projective modules, since base change is; it is the input that makes the underlying module of a finite étale R^∧[t⁻¹]-algebra descend.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation — the underlying projective module of a finite étale R^∧[t⁻¹]-algebra descends.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs`, `P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`, `mathlib:Algebra.Smooth`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Corollary 5.4.42, p. 125; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.41, p. 124.

#### `etale-algebra-structure-schemes` — The scheme of étale algebra structures on a projective module is smooth, and GL acts on it étale-ly

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Henselian/FiniteEtaleCompletion`, namespace `TauCeti`.

Let R, t be as in P3/smooth-sections-dense-over-henselian-pairs and P a finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-module; for an R[t⁻¹]-scheme S write P_S = O_S ⊗ P. (a) The functor S ↦ {commutative unital O_S-algebra structures (µ, 1) on P_S} is represented by an affine R[t⁻¹]-scheme X_P of finite presentation (Gabber–Ramero Lemma 5.4.45). (b) The subfunctor of étale algebra structures is represented by an affine open U_P ⊆ X_P — the non-vanishing locus of the discriminant of the trace form — and U_P is smooth over R[t⁻¹] (Lemma 5.4.46). (c) S ↦ Aut_{O_S}(P_S) is represented by a group scheme Aut_P of finite presentation, locally GL_n (Lemma 5.4.50). (d) The morphism Aut_P ×_{R[t⁻¹]} U_P → U_P ×_{R[t⁻¹]} U_P, (g, µ) ↦ (µ^g, µ), with µ^g the transported structure, is étale (Lemma 5.4.53); in particular (U_P, Aut_P × U_P) is a groupoid satisfying the hypotheses of P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs, and its π₀ over T is the set of isomorphism classes of finite étale T-algebras whose underlying module is isomorphic to P_T.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- P finitely generated projective over R[t⁻¹]; étale = finite étale here, the module being finite projective.

*Proof outline.*
1. (a): Zariski-locally P is free with basis e_1, …, e_n; a multiplication is given by structure constants a_{ijk} and a unit by b_l subject to finitely many polynomial identities (associativity, commutativity, unit); the functor is an fppf sheaf, so the local representing schemes glue.
2. (b): a finite projective algebra is étale iff the discriminant of its trace form is a unit (Mathlib `Algebra.traceForm`, `traceForm_nondegenerate` for fields; Gabber–Ramero Theorem 4.1.14), an open condition; formal smoothness: an étale algebra over a nilpotent thickening's base lifts, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, and its underlying module is forced to be P (étale algebras deform uniquely — Stacks Tag 039R, 'une équivalence remarquable de catégories'; Gabber–Ramero Proposition 3.2.30).
3. (d): of finite presentation; formally étale because an isomorphism of étale algebras over a nilpotent thickening Z₀ ⊆ Z extends uniquely to Z (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.2.18(iii); Stacks 039R).

*Acceptance.*
- For P = R[t⁻¹]² over a field-valued point: U_P(K) is the set of étale K-algebra structures on K², i.e. K × K or quadratic separable field extensions, and Aut_P = GL_2 acts with orbits the isomorphism classes.
- The discriminant locus is proper in general: the structure K[ε]/(ε²) on K² lies in X_P ∖ U_P.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation — the groupoid whose orbit comparison is the finite étale comparison.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:traceForm_nondegenerate`, `mathlib:Module.Projective`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.46, pp. 125–126; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.53, p. 126; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Lemma 5.4.45, p. 125; The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 039R (Theorem 41.15.2, Une equivalence remarquable de catégories).

#### `henselian-finite-etale-approximation` — Finite étale algebras do not change under henselian completion: FÉt(R[t⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(R^∧[t⁻¹]), and FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â) for a topologically henselian Tate ring

*theorem*. **Planet:** *Henselian approximation*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/FiniteEtale/Henselian`, namespace `TauCeti.Huber`.

(a) (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.54; book numbering 5.4.53) Let R be a ring, t ∈ R a non-zero-divisor, I ⊆ R an ideal with (R, tI) henselian, and R^∧ the (t, I)-adic completion. Then base change B ↦ B ⊗_{R[t⁻¹]} R^∧[t⁻¹] is an equivalence of categories FÉt(R[t⁻¹]) ≃ FÉt(R^∧[t⁻¹]) (Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`), compatible with tensor products; it preserves and reflects ranks, faithful flatness and splitness. (b) (Tate-ring form; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8) Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`) which is topologically henselian (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c): a ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ, ϖ a pseudouniformiser, is henselian along ϖA₀), and Â its completion (Tau Ceti completion of Huber rings), with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion Â₀. Then B ↦ B ⊗_A Â is an equivalence FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â). This is (a) with R = A₀, t = ϖ, I = A₀, since A = A₀[ϖ⁻¹] and Â = Â₀[ϖ⁻¹]. (c) (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.4) For a perfectoid field K and a flat K°-algebra A henselian along (ϖ), A[ϖ⁻¹]_fét ≃ Â[ϖ⁻¹]_fét, Â the ϖ-adic completion — the special case R = A, t = ϖ, I = A of (a). No perfectoid, base-field or noetherian hypothesis enters (a) or (b).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- t a non-zero-divisor (automatic for t = ϖ a unit of A inside a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ A).
- Finite étale algebras are those of Mathlib's `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`; the topology on B ⊗_A Â is not part of the statement (it is the natural module topology, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra).

*Proof outline.*
1. Essential surjectivity in (a): the underlying module P^∧ of a finite étale R^∧[t⁻¹]-algebra is finite projective, so P^∧ ≅ P ⊗ R^∧[t⁻¹] for a finitely generated projective R[t⁻¹]-module P (P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion).
2. The étale algebra structures on P form the smooth groupoid of P3/etale-algebra-structure-schemes; by P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs isomorphism classes of finite étale structures on P and on P ⊗ R^∧[t⁻¹] correspond, so (P^∧, µ^∧) comes from R[t⁻¹].
3. Full faithfulness: for finite étale Y₁, Y₂ over X = Spec R[t⁻¹], the functor Z ↦ Hom_Z(Z ×_X Y₁, Z ×_X Y₂) is represented by a finite étale X-scheme H (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 8.2.23); viewed as a trivial groupoid its (s, t) is the diagonal, an open immersion, so P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs gives H(R[t⁻¹]) = H(R^∧[t⁻¹]).
4. (b) is (a) for (A₀, ϖ): A₀ is ϖ-torsion free (ϖ is a unit of A ⊇ A₀), A₀[ϖ⁻¹] = A, and the ϖ-adic completion of A₀ inverted at ϖ is Â (anchor Layer 0 completion of Huber rings); independence of the ring of definition is P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c).
5. (c) is the instance R = A flat over K° (so ϖ is a non-zero-divisor), I = R.

*Acceptance.*
- Every complete Tate ring is topologically henselian, so (b) is vacuous there; the content is for non-complete ones: for a perfectoid field K and an algebraic extension L/K, FÉt(L) ≃ FÉt(L̂) (L° = colim of the valuation rings of finite subextensions is henselian along ϖ).
- For A = colim_U O_X(U) over the rational neighbourhoods U of a point x (P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), (b) identifies FÉt(A) with FÉt of the completion.
- Non-example: A = ℚ with the 3-adic topology (ring of definition ℤ_(3), not henselian) and Â = ℚ_3: B = ℚ(√7) is finite étale over ℚ with Hom_ℚ(B, ℚ) = ∅, while B ⊗ ℚ_3 ≅ ℚ_3 × ℚ_3 has two ℚ_3-points, so base change FÉt(ℚ) → FÉt(ℚ_3) is not full.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit — FÉt(colim A_i) ≃ FÉt of its completion; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit — passage from the local ring colim O(U) to k(x)^; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects — ECD 6.4(i); PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison — finite-level descent of finite étale maps; AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-invariance-along-tower — FÉt(A_∞) ≃ FÉt(Â_∞) for a topologically henselian A_∞; AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/uniform-completion-etale-comparison — the Tate-ring form for the spectral topology.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-algebra-structure-schemes`, `P3/groupoid-orbits-over-henselian-pairs`, `P3/projective-modules-over-henselian-completion`, `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`, `mathlib:HenselianRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, Proposition 5.4.54 (arXiv v3; Proposition 5.4.53 in the LNM 1800 book), pp. 126–127; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.4.8, p. 54; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Proposition 7.4, p. 40; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §5.4, introduction, p. 116; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (i), p. 27.

#### `finite-etale-completed-direct-limit` — Finite étale algebras over a completed filtered colimit of complete Tate rings come from a finite stage

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/FiniteEtale/Henselian`, namespace `TauCeti.Huber`.

Let (A_i)_{i ∈ I} be a filtered system of complete Tate rings along continuous ring maps, with compatible rings of definition A_{i,0} and a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i₀,0} mapping to pseudouniformisers (for instance A_{i,0} = A_i° when all A_i are uniform, or A_{i,0} = A_i⁺ for Huber pairs (A_i, A_i⁺)). Give A_∞ = colim A_i the Tate topology with ring of definition colim A_{i,0} and ϖ-adic topology on it, and let A = Â_∞ be its completion. Then the base change functors 2-colim_i FÉt(A_i) → FÉt(A_∞) → FÉt(A) are equivalences of categories compatible with tensor products. In particular (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5(i), generalised): if (R_i) is a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings and R is the completion of colim R_i with ring of definition the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i° (a perfectoid Tate ring, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings), then R_fét ≃ 2-colim_i (R_i)_fét; and the same holds for the rational localisations of affinoid perfectoid spaces along cofiltered limits (the form used by ECD Proposition 6.4(i)).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- The A_i complete; the rings of definition compatible and containing the image of one pseudouniformiser.
- No perfectoid hypothesis for the first statement.

*Proof outline.*
1. 2-colim_i FÉt(A_i) ≃ FÉt(A_∞): P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings.
2. colim A_{i,0} is henselian along ϖ: each A_{i,0} is ϖ-adically complete, hence henselian (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (a)), and filtered colimits of henselian pairs are henselian ((b)).
3. FÉt(A_∞) ≃ FÉt(A): P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b), A_∞ being topologically henselian with completion A.
4. Perfectoid case: with A_{i,0} = R_i° (the R_i are uniform), A = R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings, a perfectoid Tate ring by (b) there; the equivalence is the first statement for this system.

*Acceptance.*
- For perfectoid K and the perfectoid closed disc R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ written as the completed colimit of K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ (not perfectoid), every finite étale R-algebra is defined over some K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩.
- Uniqueness is part of the equivalence: two finite-level models of the same finite étale A-algebra become isomorphic at a further finite stage, with a unique isomorphism compatible with the given one over A.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids — finite-level descent of finite étale covers; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects — ECD 6.4(i) for cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces; PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison — descent of finite étale maps to a finite level (Sch12 7.17); PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — Sch12 7.5(i) for the completed tower Â_∞.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`, `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Lemma 7.5 (i), pp. 40–41; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, corollary after Theorem 7.4.8, p. 54; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 10, Corollary 10.0.5 with proof, p. 119.

#### `finite-etale-under-completed-perfection` — In characteristic p, finite étale algebras are insensitive to completed perfection

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/FiniteEtale/Henselian`, namespace `TauCeti.Huber`.

Let S be a complete Tate ring of characteristic p with a ring of definition S₀ ∋ ϖ, and let R = (S^{perf})^ be the completed perfection: the completion of S^{perf} = colim(S → S → ⋯) (transition maps Frobenius x ↦ x^p) for the Tate topology with ring of definition colim S₀^{1/pⁿ}; R is a perfect complete Tate ring, hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect) when uniform. Then base change is an equivalence FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(R). In particular (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5(ii)) for a p-finite perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺), the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid (S, S⁺) of topologically finite type over a characteristic-p perfectoid field, R_fét ≃ S_fét; the base field is not needed.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- Characteristic p; S complete Tate.
- The absolute Frobenius S → S is a ring map, and S^{1/pⁿ} denotes S viewed as an S-algebra through Frobenius n times.

*Proof outline.*
1. Each transition map S → S^{1/p} (Frobenius) induces an equivalence FÉt(S) ≃ FÉt(S^{1/p}): it is integral, universally injective and surjective on spectra (a universal homeomorphism), so topological invariance of the étale site applies (Stacks Tag 04DZ); concretely B ↦ B ⊗_{S, Frob} S has quasi-inverse given by Frobenius twist, the relative Frobenius of an étale algebra being an isomorphism (P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect).
2. FÉt(S^{perf}) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(S^{1/pⁿ}) ≃ FÉt(S) by P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings, and FÉt(S^{perf}) ≃ FÉt(R) by P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit.

*Acceptance.*
- S = K⟨T⟩ for a perfectoid field K of characteristic p: finite étale K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras are exactly the completed perfections of finite étale K⟨T⟩-algebras, e.g. the Artin–Schreier cover u^p − u = T.
- The inseparable extension S → S[T^{1/p}]... is not étale and is not in the image: the equivalence concerns étale algebras only.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison — comparison of finite étale covers of p-finite perfectoid spaces with those of their tft models; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects — reduction of perfectoid finite étale covers to finite type models.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`, `P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit`, `P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `mathlib:frobenius`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Lemma 7.5 (ii), p. 41; The Stacks project authors (Stacks-Project), Tag 04DZ (Theorem 59.45.2), topological invariance of the étale site.

#### `residue-field-finite-etale-colimit` — Finite étale algebras over the completed residue field spread out to a rational neighbourhood

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/FiniteEtale/Henselian`, namespace `TauCeti.Huber`.

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`, A complete, `Huber.IsTateRing`), X = Spa(A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa`) and x ∈ X with completed residue field k(x)^ (a complete nonarchimedean field; the completion of k(x) = Frac(A/supp x) for the valuation topology of x). For rational subsets U ∋ x (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`) let O(U) be the rational localisation (anchor Layer 3). Then base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(O(U)) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^), compatible with tensor products. Concretely: every finite étale k(x)^-algebra is L ⊗ k(x)^ for some U ∋ x and L ∈ FÉt(O(U)); and for L, L' ∈ FÉt(O(U)), every k(x)^-algebra map L ⊗ k(x)^ → L' ⊗ k(x)^ comes from an O(V)-algebra map over some rational V with x ∈ V ⊆ U, two maps agreeing over k(x)^ agree over some such V. No sheafiness of (A, A⁺) is required.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- (A, A⁺) complete Tate; rational subsets containing x form a filtered (downward directed) family, and O(U) → O(V) for V ⊆ U are the restriction maps.

*Proof outline.*
1. Let A_x = colim_{U ∋ x} O(U) with ring of definition A_{x,0} = colim O⁺(U) ∋ ϖ; A_{x,0} is henselian along ϖ (each O⁺(U) is ϖ-adically complete; P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (a), (b)), and FÉt(A_x) = 2-colim FÉt(O(U)) (P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings).
2. The kernel N of A_{x,0} → k(x)⁺ (the valuation ring of x, completed) is ϖ-divisible: if f ∈ O⁺(U) has |f(x)| = 0, then V = {|f| ≤ |ϖ|} ∩ U is a rational neighbourhood of x on which f ∈ ϖO⁺(V); so N = ϖN, ϖ is invertible on N, and the ϖ-adic completion of A_{x,0} is the ϖ-adic completion of A_{x,0}/N, which is the completion of the valuation ring k(x)⁺, the image being dense (Berkeley, argument after Theorem 7.4.8).
3. Hence the completion of the Tate ring A_x is k(x)^, and FÉt(A_x) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^) by P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b).

*Acceptance.*
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and x the Gauss point, the quadratic extension k(x)^(√T) of k(x)^ spreads out to the finite étale O(U)-algebra O(U)[S]/(S² − T) on U = {|T| = 1}, and to no neighbourhood of the point T = 0 (T is not a unit there).
- Rank-one and higher-rank points have the same completed residue field as their maximal generalisation, and the statement holds at every point.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence — the local step at each point x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺).

*Prerequisites.* `P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`, `P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Lemma 7.4.6 and the argument after Theorem 7.4.8, pp. 53–55; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, proof of Theorem 7.9 (ii), p. 42; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §2.2, Lemma 2.2.3 (a), p. 28.


### Characteristic p

#### `etale-over-perfect-is-perfect` — Relative Frobenius of a weakly étale map is an isomorphism; étale algebras over perfect rings are perfect

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/CharP`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

(a) Let A → B be a weakly étale map of 𝔽_p-algebras (A → B flat and the multiplication B ⊗_A B → B flat; every étale map is weakly étale). Then the square formed by A → B and the absolute Frobenius endomorphisms (Mathlib `frobenius A p`, `frobenius B p`) is a pushout: the relative Frobenius F_{B/A}: B ⊗_{A, Frob} A → B, b ⊗ a ↦ b^p a, is an isomorphism. In particular, if A is perfect (Mathlib `PerfectRing A p`), then so is B, and B ⊗_{A, Frob^{-n}} A ≅ B for all n. (b) (almost version, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.13(ii)) The same holds for a weakly étale morphism A → B of almost algebras over a basic setup (V, 𝔪) of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup): the Frobenius square of almost V-algebras is cocartesian. Consequently, for a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformiser ϖ, ϖ^p | p, a finite étale (R°a/ϖ)-algebra B is relatively perfect over R°a/ϖ: Φ: B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B (the input of Scholze 2012 Proposition 5.22).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- Characteristic p; weakly étale: flat with flat diagonal.
- In (b), almost algebras and weak étaleness are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P0 (Gabber–Ramero §3.1).

*Proof outline.*
1. Weakly étale maps are stable under base change and composition, and every map between weakly étale A-algebras is weakly étale (Bhatt, proof of Lemma 4.3.8; Stacks Tag 092A).
2. F_{B/A} is a map of weakly étale A-algebras, hence weakly étale; a diagram chase shows it factors a power of Frobenius on source and target.
3. A weakly étale map α: R → S that factors a power of Frobenius on R and on S is an isomorphism: it is faithfully flat (if M ⊗_R S = 0, then Frob^n kills M ⊗ R) and a flat epimorphism-up-to-Frobenius; the multiplication S ⊗_R S → S is weakly étale and invertible up to Frobenius, hence an isomorphism (Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.13(i), Bhatt Lemma 4.3.8). Apply to F_{B/A}.
4. Perfectness: if Frob_A is bijective, B ⊗_{A,Frob} A ≅ B and the pushout of the bijection Frob_A is the bijection Frob_B.
5. (b): the same argument in the category of almost algebras (Gabber–Ramero 3.5.10–3.5.13), using PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness for weak étaleness.

*Acceptance.*
- For A = 𝔽_p(t^{1/p^∞}) and the Artin–Schreier extension B = A[u]/(u^p − u − t) (étale): B is a perfect field and the relative Frobenius B ⊗_{A,Frob} A → B is an isomorphism of A-algebras of dimension p.
- Non-example: A = 𝔽_p is perfect and B = 𝔽_p[ε]/(ε²) is finite flat but not étale; B is not perfect (ε^p = 0), so flatness alone does not suffice.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p — S is perfect; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor — finite étale (R°a/ϖ)-algebras are perfectoid; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection — Frobenius twists do not change finite étale algebras.

*Prerequisites.* `mathlib:frobenius`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobeniusEquiv`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-basic-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`.

*Sources.* Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Lemma 4.3.8, p. 29; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Lemma 4.3.8, conclusion, p. 29; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §3.5, Theorem 3.5.13, pp. 66–67 (arXiv v3); Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, Proposition 5.22 with proof, p. 28.

#### `finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform` — Finite étale algebras over a uniform complete Tate ring are uniform, and their power-bounded elements are the integral closure

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/FiniteEtale/Uniform`, namespace `TauCeti.Huber`.

Let A be a complete uniform Tate ring (A° bounded; Tau Ceti `Huber.powerBoundedSubring`), A⁺ ⊆ A° a ring of integral elements, and B ∈ FÉt(A) with its natural topology and plus ring B⁺ = integral closure of A⁺ in B (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra). Then: (a) B is uniform: if b_1, …, b_n ∈ B⁺ generate B as an A-module, then B° ⊆ {b ∈ B : Tr_{B/A}(b b_i) ∈ A° for all i}, a bounded set because the trace pairing is perfect; (b) B° is the integral closure of A° in B; (c) Tr_{B/A}(B°) ⊆ A°. The pair (B, B⁺) is a complete uniform Tate Huber pair.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- A complete, uniform, Tate; B finite étale over A as a ring.

*Proof outline.*
1. Generators in B⁺: B is finite over A and every element of B becomes integral over A⁺ after multiplication by a power of ϖ, so generators can be chosen in B⁺.
2. Trace bound: for b ∈ B° the element b b_i is power bounded; its characteristic polynomial over A has coefficients of spectral norm ≤ 1 at every point x of Spa(A, A°) (they are elementary symmetric functions of the eigenvalues of multiplication in the finite étale k(x)^-algebra B ⊗ k(x)^, each of absolute value ≤ 1), hence in A° by uniformity (A° = {a : |a(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, anchor Layer 2); so Tr(b b_i) ∈ A°. This proves (c) and the inclusion in (a).
3. The set {b : Tr(b b_i) ∈ A° ∀i} is bounded: the perfect trace pairing identifies B with Hom_A(B, A) topologically (open mapping for finite projective modules), and the image lies in a bounded set (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 1.10.1; Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16).
4. (b): elements integral over A° are power bounded since B° is an integrally closed subring containing A°; conversely the characteristic polynomial of b ∈ B° has coefficients in A° by the trace-bound step, so b is integral over A° (Cayley–Hamilton).

*Acceptance.*
- For A = ℚ_p and B = ℚ_p(√p): B° = ℤ_p[√p] is the integral closure of ℤ_p, bounded, and Tr(B°) = 2ℤ_p ⊆ ℤ_p.
- Non-example: B = A[ε]/(ε²) is finite projective but not étale, and not uniform: λε is power bounded for every λ ∈ A, so B° is unbounded; its trace pairing is degenerate.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p — S is uniform and S° is the integral closure of R°; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale — S° is the integral closure of R° in S.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/trace-geometric-point-formula`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.

*Sources.* Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 1, §1.10, Lemma 1.10.1 with proof, p. 46; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 1, §1.10, proof of Lemma 1.10.1, p. 46; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, proof of Proposition 5.23, p. 28.

#### `finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p` — Almost purity in characteristic p: finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p

*theorem*. **Planet:** *Almost purity in characteristic p*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/CharP`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (equivalently a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect; no base field), ϖ ∈ R a pseudouniformiser (it has all p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} in R°), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, and S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology and plus ring S⁺ = integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S is perfect, complete and uniform, hence a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, and (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair; (ii) S° is the integral closure of R° in S and S°/S⁺ is almost zero, so S°a = S⁺a; (iii) S°a is an almost finite étale R°a-algebra (almost finitely presented projective and unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S lies in (S°a ⊗_{R°a} S°a)_*); (iv) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° whose composite is multiplication by ε; (v) if S is faithfully flat over R, then Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° and R°a → S°a is almost faithfully flat and almost split. The statement specialises to Scholze 2012 Proposition 5.23 for R a perfectoid K-algebra, K a perfectoid field of characteristic p, and to the finite separable extensions of a perfectoid field of characteristic p.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfect, complete, Tate, characteristic p; no perfectoid base field.
- Almost mathematics for the basic setup (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup), equivalently the ideal (ϖ^{1/p^∞}); almost finite étale in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras (Gabber–Ramero §3.1).
- Not claimed: S° finite, flat or étale over R°; S free over R.

*Proof outline.*
1. (i): S is perfect by P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect; complete Tate with its natural topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) and uniform (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform; alternatively PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform, S being perfect and complete); perfect complete uniform Tate rings of characteristic p are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect); (S, S⁺) is a Huber pair by A1.
2. (ii): S° = integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b)); S°° ⊆ S⁺ since S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
3. (iii) unramified: the diagonal idempotent e ∈ S ⊗_R S satisfies ϖ^N e ∈ im(S° ⊗_{R°} S°) for some N; as Frobenius is bijective on S° ⊗_{R°} S° (both perfect), ϖ^{N/p^m} e ∈ im(S° ⊗ S°) for every m, so e is an almost element (Scholze 2012 proof of 5.23; Bhatt Proposition 4.3.4).
4. (iv): write ϖ^N e = Σ_{i=1}^n x_i ⊗ y_i with x_i, y_i ∈ S°; then ϖ^{N/p^m} e = Σ x_i^{1/p^m} ⊗ y_i^{1/p^m} with the same n. For a finite étale algebra and e = Σ a_i ⊗ b_i one has Σ_i Tr_{S/R}(f a_i) b_i = f (Bhatt Construction 4.3.3: Tr of the diagonal factor is 1), so s ↦ (Tr(s x_i^{1/p^m}))_i, (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i y_i^{1/p^m} are maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° (Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c)) composing to ϖ^{N/p^m}: uniform almost finite projectivity. Almost finitely presented projective with an almost idempotent is almost finite étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras).
5. (v): Tr(S) = R for faithfully flat S, so ϖ^c = Tr(f) with f ∈ S°; compatibility of the trace with Frobenius gives ϖ^{c/p^n} = Tr(f^{1/p^n}) with f^{1/p^n} ∈ S°, whence R°° ⊆ Tr(S°°) up to almost zero and R°a → S°a is almost split (Bhatt Remark 4.3.5).

*Acceptance.*
- Reviewer-authored test (no source example): for K = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ and the Artin–Schreier extension S = K[u]/(u^p − u − t^{-1}), S is a perfectoid field and S°a is finite étale and uniformly almost finite projective (n = p) over K°a; S° is not finite free over K° at any finite level, and this is not claimed.
- The bound n on the number of generators is independent of ε (uniformity); for S of constant rank d one can take n = d², and n = d after localising where S is free.
- A non-field instance: R = 𝔽_p[[T^{1/p^∞}]]⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T] (the characteristic-p analogue of ECD Example 3.4(iv)) and S = R[u]/(u^p − u − T^{-1}): the theorem applies without any perfectoid base field.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence — essential surjectivity of A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor — the characteristic-p leg of the untilting functor; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields — the characteristic-p case; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p — in characteristic p étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`, `P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfect-complete-tate-ring-is-uniform`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-locally-free-algebra-trace`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/algebra-trace-base-change`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:PerfectRing`, `mathlib:frobenius`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, Proposition 5.23, p. 28; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Proposition 4.3.4, p. 27; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Remark 4.3.5, p. 28; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §3.5, Theorem 3.5.28 with the opening of its proof, pp. 69–70.

#### `characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence` — Characteristic p: inverting ϖ is an equivalence between almost finite étale R°a-algebras and finite étale R-algebras

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/CharP`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser ϖ. Let (R°a)_afet be the category of almost finite étale R°a-algebras (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). Then the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* the ring of almost elements, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints), with its natural topology, is an equivalence of categories, compatible with tensor products; a quasi-inverse is S ↦ S°a. Moreover every A ∈ (R°a)_afet is uniformly almost finite projective, A_* is perfect, ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete, and A_* is the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; almost faithful flatness of A corresponds to faithful flatness of A_*[ϖ⁻¹].

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfect complete Tate of characteristic p; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).
- This is Gabber–Ramero Theorem 3.5.28 for V = R°, ε = ϖ (V perfect, m = ∪ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}V).

*Proof outline.*
1. Well defined: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective over R (almost finite projective modules become finite projective after inverting ϖ, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion) and unramified (the almost idempotent becomes an idempotent), hence finite étale.
2. Essential surjectivity: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] with S°a ∈ (R°a)_afet by P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p.
3. Full faithfulness (Bhatt Lemma 4.3.7): A ≅ T^a for T the integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹]. A is perfect (the almost version of P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect, almost finite étale maps being weakly étale), so A_* is perfect; ϖ is a non-zero-divisor on A_* (almost flatness). For f ∈ T, the R-span of f^ℕ lies in ϖ^{-c}A_*, so ϖ^{c/pⁿ} f ∈ A_* for all n by perfectness, i.e. f ∈ A_*; conversely almost finite generation gives ϖ g^ℕ ⊆ ϖ^{-c}T, whence g ∈ T_*. As T is functorial in the R-algebra A_*[ϖ⁻¹], the functor is fully faithful.
4. Uniformity and completeness: P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv) for S = A_*[ϖ⁻¹]; A_* = S° is ϖ-adically complete.

*Acceptance.*
- R = K a perfectoid field of characteristic p: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) ≃ finite products of finite separable extensions L, via L ↦ L°a.
- Degenerate: A = R°a ↦ R, A = 0 ↦ 0, A = (R°a)ⁿ ↦ Rⁿ.
- Non-example of the integral statement: the functor from finite étale R°-algebras (honest, not almost) to FÉt(R) is not essentially surjective — the Artin–Schreier cover of 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ has no finite étale model over the valuation ring.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor — FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence — the characteristic-p case.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`, `P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

*Sources.* Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §3.5, 3.5.26 and Theorem 3.5.28, p. 69; Ofer Gabber (gr-almost), §3.5, Theorem 3.5.28, p. 69; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 4, §4.3, Theorem 4.3.6, p. 28.


### Untilting finite étale algebras; perfectoid fields

#### `finite-etale-untilting-functor` — The untilting functor on finite étale algebras, T ↦ T♯, via almost finite étale integral structures

*construction* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/Untilt`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) and choose a pseudouniformiser ϖ♭ ∈ R♭ with ϖ := (ϖ♭)♯ satisfying ϖ^p | p in R° (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), so that R♭°/ϖ♭ = R°/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings). Define the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) as the composite FÉt(R♭) ≃ (R♭°a)_afet → (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet = (R°a/ϖ)_afet ≃ (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), T ↦ T°a ↦ T°a/ϖ♭ ↦ A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] =: T♯, where the first equivalence is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence, the middle equivalence is the unique flat deformation of almost finite étale algebras along the ϖ-adically complete flat R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras), and the last functor inverts ϖ (natural module topology on T♯). Properties: T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring, finite étale over R, with a canonical isomorphism (T♯)♭ ≅ T of R♭-algebras (so (−)♯ is inverse to tilting on its image; compatible with the untilting of perfectoid algebras of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt); (T♯)°a = A is almost finite étale over R°a; the functor is independent of ϖ♭ up to canonical isomorphism, preserves tensor products, finite products, ranks (rank of T♯ at x ∈ Spa R equals the rank of T at x♭) and faithful flatness; and it commutes with base change along every map of perfectoid Tate rings R → R' (for example a rational localisation or the completed residue field at a point): (T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'. Equivalently (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 3.6.20, Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.10) T♯ = W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ for a generator ξ of ker(θ: W(R♭⁺) → R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction), which shows finite étaleness without almost mathematics.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.
- ϖ♭ with ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯, ϖ^p | p; different choices give canonically isomorphic functors.

*Proof outline.*
1. Middle identification: the categories of almost finite étale algebras over R♭°a/ϖ♭ and R°a/ϖ coincide because the rings coincide (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings) and R♭°a = R♭⁺a, R°a = R⁺a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).
2. Lifting: R°a is flat over the basic setup and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary), so reduction modulo ϖ is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 5.3.27), and the lift A is flat and ϖ-adically complete (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete).
3. Perfectoidness and tilt: A/ϖ = T°a/ϖ♭ is a perfectoid (R°a/ϖ)-algebra (relative Frobenius isomorphism, P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect (b)); A is its unique flat deformation, hence a perfectoid R°a-algebra, and A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is a perfectoid R-algebra whose tilt has the same reduction modulo ϖ♭, i.e. is T (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).
4. Finite étale: A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is finite projective and unramified after inverting ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
5. Base change: each step commutes with base change along R°a → R'°a (flat deformations are unique, reduction modulo ϖ and inverting ϖ commute with tensor products); the tilt of R → R' is R♭ → R'♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality).
6. Ranks: the rank of an almost finite projective module is read off modulo ϖ and after inverting ϖ, and Spa R ≅ Spa R♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets).

*API.*
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt` (constructor): The functor CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R♭ ⥤ CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R, T ↦ T♯.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_isPerfectoid` (instance): T♯ with its natural topology is a perfectoid Tate ring.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.tiltUntiltIso` (equivalence): (T♯)♭ ≅ T naturally in T.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_almostFiniteEtale` (projection): (T♯)°a is almost finite étale over R°a, uniformly almost finite projective.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltBaseChangeIso` (functoriality): For a map of perfectoid Tate rings R → R', (T ⊗_{R♭} R'♭)♯ ≅ T♯ ⊗_R R'.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_rank` (simp): rank_x(T♯) = rank_{x♭}(T) for x ∈ Spa R.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltTensorIso` (structure): (T₁ ⊗ T₂)♯ ≅ T₁♯ ⊗ T₂♯ (monoidal functor).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_faithfullyFlat_iff` (characterisation): T♯ is faithfully flat over R iff T is faithfully flat over R♭.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untiltIsoWitt` (compatibility): T♯ ≅ W(T⁺)[1/[ϖ♭]]/ξ with ξ a generator of ker θ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_independent` (other): Different choices of ϖ♭ give canonically isomorphic functors.

*Unit tests.*
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_self` (degenerate): untilt R (R♭ as a finite étale R♭-algebra) ≅ R, and untilt 0 = 0, untilt (T₁ × T₂) ≅ untilt T₁ × untilt T₂.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_quadratic` (computation): For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^, K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ with t♯ = p and p odd: untilt (K♭[u]/(u² − t)) ≅ K[u]/(u² − p).
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_tilt` (compatibility): tilt (untilt T) ≅ T as R♭-algebras, and untilt T agrees with PerfectoidSpaces:P1's untilt of the perfectoid R♭-algebra T.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_mod_varpi` (characterisation): untilt T is the unique finite étale R-algebra S with (S°a)/ϖ ≅ (T°a)/ϖ♭ as (R°a/ϖ)-algebras.
- `Perfectoid.FiniteEtale.untilt_test_not_basechange` (non-example): There is no ring map R♭ → R along which untilt T = T ⊗ R: the sharp map is multiplicative but not additive, and for R = ℚ_p^cycl the untilt of the Artin–Schreier extension is not obtained by substituting ♯ into an equation.

*Acceptance.*
- The untilt of R♭ is R, of R♭ × R♭ is R × R, of 0 is 0.
- For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p, and p odd: the untilt of K♭(t^{1/2}) is K(p^{1/2}) (Bhatt Example 3.2.9).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful — the functor whose full faithfulness is proved; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence — untilting the local finite étale algebras T_U over O(U♭); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields — untilting finite extensions of K♭; Scholze 2012 Theorem 5.25 — the fully faithful functor R♭_fét → R_fét; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 3.6.21 / AWS Lemma 2.8.11 — the untilting functor whose essential surjectivity is the tilting equivalence.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`, `P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lift-flat-and-complete`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilt-construction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.baseChange`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, Proposition 5.22 and the diagram following it, p. 28; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 6, §6.2, construction of functors after Theorem 6.2.10, p. 49; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 2, §2.8, Lemma 2.8.10, p. 72; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §3.6, Lemma 3.6.20, p. 97.

#### `tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful` — The untilting functor FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) is fully faithful, inverse to tilting on its image, with image the S having almost finite étale integral structure

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/Untilt`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭ (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field). The untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is fully faithful and, on its essential image, inverse to tilting: for S = T♯, S is perfectoid and S♭ ≅ T. Its essential image consists exactly of the finite étale R-algebras S such that S (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a; for such S, S°a is uniformly almost finite projective over R°a. The functor preserves degrees (rank functions), tensor products and faithful flatness. For R = K a perfectoid field this is the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; for R of characteristic p (R♭ = R) it is the identity.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- No claim of essential surjectivity here; that is P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence (ECD 6.1(ii)).
- Neither étaleness of S° over R° nor freeness of S over R is asserted or needed.

*Proof outline.*
1. Full faithfulness: each functor in the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor except the last is an equivalence; the last, (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹], is fully faithful because A_* is recovered functorially as the total integral closure of R° in A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (A_* is the power-bounded subring of the perfectoid, uniform A_*[ϖ⁻¹], PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; almost finite generation gives the reverse inclusion; Bhatt, proof of Theorem 6.2.10, functor (d)).
2. Image: T♯ has the stated properties (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor). Conversely, if S ∈ FÉt(R) is perfectoid with S°a almost finite étale, then S°a/ϖ is almost finite étale over R°a/ϖ = R♭°a/ϖ♭; let T := the characteristic-p finite étale algebra with T°a/ϖ♭ ≅ S°a/ϖ (P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence and PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras on the tilt side); uniqueness of flat lifts gives S°a ≅ (T♯)°a and S ≅ T♯.
3. Uniformity: uniform almost finite projectivity lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi, for the root setup of ϖ^{1/p^∞}) from the characteristic-p case (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)).
4. Degrees, tensor products, faithful flatness: P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.

*Acceptance.*
- For R = K a perfectoid field this gives a fully faithful, degree-preserving functor FÉt(K♭) → FÉt(K), the input of Scholze 2012 Theorem 3.7; when K♭ is algebraically closed its image is all of FÉt(K) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and T = R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − t) (ℓ ≠ p prime, t♯ = T): T♯ ≅ R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), a Kummer cover, in the image with S°a almost finite étale.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence — full faithfulness over O(U) and O(U_ij) in the gluing; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields — full faithfulness over K; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — Sch12 5.25 for the completed tower.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`, `P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, Theorem 5.25, p. 29; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 6, proof of Theorem 6.2.10 over a field, p. 49.

#### `untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field` — If the tilt of a perfectoid field is algebraically closed, so is the field

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let K be a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) with tilt K♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field). If K♭ is algebraically closed (Mathlib `IsAlgClosed K♭`), then K is algebraically closed.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- K perfectoid field of any characteristic (in characteristic p, K♭ = K and the statement is trivial).

*Proof outline.*
1. Let P ∈ K°[X] be monic irreducible of degree d ≥ 1. The Newton polygon of P is a line (P irreducible over the complete field K, unique extension of the absolute value: Mathlib `spectralNorm`), and as |K^×| = |K♭^×| is divisible (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) one may rescale so that |a₀| = 1.
2. Choose Q ∈ K♭°[X] monic with the same image in K°/ϖ[X] = K♭°/ϖ♭[X] (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field) and a root y ∈ K♭° of Q (K♭ algebraically closed). Then P(y♯) ≡ 0 modulo ϖ (sharp map, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map).
3. P(X + y♯) is irreducible with constant term P(y♯); rescale P₁(X) = c^{-d}P(cX + y♯) with |c|^d = |P(y♯)| ≤ |ϖ|, integral again by the straight Newton polygon; iterate to get a Cauchy sequence x_n with |P(x_n)| ≤ |ϖ|ⁿ converging to a root of P (Scholze 2012 Proposition 3.8; Kedlaya's argument in Bhatt Proposition 3.2.10).

*Acceptance.*
- The completed algebraic closure ℂ_p of ℚ_p is algebraically closed, with tilt ℂ_p♭ algebraically closed; this lemma recovers the first from the second.
- The converse also holds (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields — the untilt of the completed algebraic closure of K♭ is algebraically closed.

*Prerequisites.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed`, `mathlib:spectralNorm`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §3, Proposition 3.8, p. 17; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §3, proof of Proposition 3.8, p. 18; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 3, Proposition 3.2.10, p. 14.

#### `finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields` — Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid, and tilting is a degree-preserving equivalence of finite extensions

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let K be a perfectoid field (characteristic 0 or p) with tilt K♭. (i) Every finite extension L/K, with its natural topology (the unique extension of the absolute value, Mathlib `spectralNorm`), is a perfectoid field. (ii) The untilting functor (−)♯ of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor is an equivalence FÉt(K♭) ≃ FÉt(K) with quasi-inverse L ↦ L♭; it restricts to an equivalence between finite field extensions of K♭ and of K, preserving degrees, automorphism groups and Galois extensions. (iii) K is algebraically closed if and only if K♭ is. (iv) For every finite extension L/K, L°a is almost finite étale over K°a (Tate, Gabber–Ramero §6.6 for deeply ramified fields), uniformly almost finite projective.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- K perfectoid field; finite extensions carry their natural topology; finite étale K-algebras are finite products of finite separable extensions (Mathlib `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`).
- An alternative, ramification-theoretic proof (Gabber–Ramero Propositions 6.6.2 and 6.6.6: L°a/K°a étale for deeply ramified K; 6.3.6: finite projectivity) is not the route planned here.

*Proof outline.*
1. Characteristic p: (i) and (iv) are P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p for R = K; (ii) is the identity; (iii) trivial.
2. (ii) full faithfulness and degrees: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful for R = K.
3. Essential surjectivity: let M be the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭ (perfect and complete, hence a perfectoid field); its untilt M♯ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt) is a perfectoid field over K (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field: R is a perfectoid field iff R♭ is) and algebraically closed (P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field).
4.
