The union N ⊆ M♯ of the untilts L♯ of the finite extensions L ⊆ M of K♭ is a subfield algebraic over K and dense in M♯ (M is the completed colimit of the perfectoid fields L, so M♯ is the completed colimit of the L♯ over K, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings (c), and the colimit of the L♯ is dense in it, (a)); by Krasner's lemma (Mathlib `IsKrasner.of_completeSpace`, applied over finite subextensions of N/K, which are complete) N is separably closed; as K has characteristic 0 in this step, every finite extension F/K is separable and embeds in some L♯ with L/K♭ finite Galois.
5. L♯/K is Galois with Gal(L♯/K) ≅ Gal(L/K♭) (untilting preserves degrees and automorphisms); F = (L♯)^H for a subgroup H, and F♭ := L^H satisfies (F♭)♯ ⊆ (L♯)^H = F with equal degrees, so F is an untilt. General finite étale K-algebras are finite products of such F.
6. (i): F ≅ (F♭)♯ is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) and a field; its topology is the natural one (finite-dimensional K-vector space).
7. (iii): if K♭ is algebraically closed, apply P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field; if K is, every finite extension of K♭ untilts to a finite extension of K of the same degree, hence is trivial, so K♭ (perfect) is algebraically closed.
8. (iv): L is in the essential image of (−)♯, so L°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful).

*Acceptance.*
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ and 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ have equivalent categories of finite extensions (P3/fontaine-wintenberger).
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd), L is perfectoid, L♭ is a quadratic extension of K♭, and L°a/K°a is almost finite étale although L°/K° is ramified (the different of K(p^{1/2p^n})/K_n has valuation 1/(2pⁿ) → 0, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).
- Non-example: ℚ_p is not perfectoid and its finite extensions are not either (discretely valued, ECD Remark 3.3); the theorem needs K perfectoid.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence — the field case at each completed residue field; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger — Galois groups; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/tilt-of-cp-and-special-elements — ℂ_p♭ algebraically closed.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`, `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `P3/untilt-of-algebraically-closed-field`, `P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-iff-tilt-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings`, `mathlib:IsKrasner.of_completeSpace`, `mathlib:spectralNorm.nontriviallyNormedField`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod`, `mathlib:IsGalois`, `mathlib:IsAlgClosed`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §3, Theorem 3.7 (i), p. 17; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §3, Theorem 3.7 (ii), p. 17; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §5, proof of Theorem 3.7 reducing to algebraically closed K♭, p. 29; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.3, Theorem 7.3.2, p. 50; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §3.5, Theorem 3.5.6, p. 84.

#### `fontaine-wintenberger` — Fontaine–Wintenberger: the absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and of its tilt are isomorphic

*theorem*. **Planet:** *Fontaine–Wintenberger theorem*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let K be a perfectoid field with tilt K♭. Fix an algebraic closure K̄ of K with completion C, so that C♭ is an algebraically closed perfectoid field containing K♭ (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (iii)), and let K♭^sep be the separable closure of K♭ in C♭. Then L ↦ L♭ (for finite Galois L/K inside K̄, with L♭ ⊆ C♭ by functoriality of tilting) defines an isomorphism of profinite groups Gal(K̄/K) ≅ Gal(K♭^sep/K♭) (Mathlib `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup` up to the choice of closures), compatible with the Galois correspondences (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`): finite subextensions of K̄/K correspond to finite subextensions of K♭^sep/K♭ with the same degrees. Application (Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1): the absolute Galois groups of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and of 𝔽_p((t)) are canonically isomorphic; this uses in addition that an algebraic extension F of a complete field and its completion F̂ have the same absolute Galois group (FÉt(F) ≃ FÉt(F̂), F° being henselian: P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b)), and that 𝔽_p((t)) → 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) is purely inseparable (Frobenius twists do not change finite étale algebras, P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- K perfectoid field; closures fixed as described; continuity is part of the claim (isomorphism of profinite groups).

*Proof outline.*
1. For finite Galois L/K ⊆ K̄, L is perfectoid and L♭/K♭ is finite Galois with Gal(L/K) ≅ Gal(L♭/K♭) (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii): equivalence preserving degrees and automorphisms).
2. The embeddings: L ⊆ C induces L♭ ⊆ C♭, landing in K♭^sep (L♭ is separable over K♭); every finite separable extension of K♭ inside C♭ arises (essential surjectivity), and inclusions correspond.
3. Gal(K̄/K) = lim_L Gal(L/K) over finite Galois subextensions (Mathlib `InfiniteGalois.algEquivToLimit`), likewise for K♭; the isomorphisms of the finite quotients are compatible with restriction (functoriality), so their limit is an isomorphism of profinite groups.
4. Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_K for K its completion, and G_{𝔽_p((t))} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{K♭} (completion and purely inseparable extension), then apply the main statement with K♭ = 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t♯ = p.

*Acceptance.*
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1: G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))}.
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})), G_K ≅ G_{K♭} with K♭ ≅ 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^, t = ε − 1 for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ K♭°: the Fontaine–Wintenberger field-of-norms isomorphism.
- Consequence: for C algebraically closed perfectoid, Spa(C, C⁺) and Spa(C♭, C♭⁺) both have trivial finite étale covers (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).

*Uses.* PadicHodgeTheory:P7/extended-robba-ring-with-galois-action — G_K acting through G_{K♭}.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`, `P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field`, `mathlib:Field.absoluteGaloisGroup`, `mathlib:InfiniteGalois.IntermediateFieldEquivClosedSubgroup`, `mathlib:InfiniteGalois.algEquivToLimit`, `mathlib:IsGalois`, `mathlib:AlgebraicClosure`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §1, discussion after Theorem 1.1, p. 2; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.3, Theorem 7.3.1 (2), p. 50; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 2, Remark 2.5.13, p. 62.

#### `cyclotomic-completion-of-finite-extension` — The completed cyclotomic extension of a finite extension of ℚ_p is perfectoid

*lemma*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/Cyclotomic`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p inside a fixed algebraic closure, and C its completion. The closure L of K(μ_{p^∞}) in C is a perfectoid field: L = K·ℚ_p^cycl is the compositum of K with the completed cyclotomic field ℚ_p^cycl (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field), a finite extension of ℚ_p^cycl of degree at most [K : ℚ_p], and K(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in it. Its tilt is the finite extension of (ℚ_p^cycl)♭ corresponding to L under the tilting equivalence of finite extensions.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- K a finite extension of ℚ_p; no ramification hypothesis.
- The perfectoid condition is checked once, for ℚ_p^cycl (P1), and transported along the finite extension L/ℚ_p^cycl by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.

*Proof outline.*
1. K·ℚ_p^cycl is a finite extension of the complete field ℚ_p^cycl (generated by a primitive element of K over ℚ_p), hence complete for the unique extension of the absolute value; so it is closed in C.
2. K(μ_{p^∞}) = K·ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in K·ℚ_p^cycl: ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) is dense in ℚ_p^cycl and K·ℚ_p^cycl = Σ K·ℚ_p^cycl over a K-basis, so L = K·ℚ_p^cycl.
3. ℚ_p^cycl is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field); a finite extension of a perfectoid field is a perfectoid field and tilting matches finite extensions (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (i), (ii)).

*Acceptance.*
- For K = ℚ_p this is ℚ_p^cycl itself.
- For K = ℚ_p(p^{1/p}), L = ℚ_p^cycl(p^{1/p}) is a perfectoid field of degree p over ℚ_p^cycl (a Kummer extension: p^{1/p} ∉ ℚ_p^cycl because ℚ_p^cycl/ℚ_p is abelian and ℚ_p(p^{1/p}) is not Galois over ℚ_p), while K itself is not perfectoid.

*Uses.* AdicSpacesPartII:R5 — its request (b): the completed cyclotomic field of a finite K/ℚ_p as a perfectoid base.

*Prerequisites.* `P1/cyclotomic-perfectoid-field`, `P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`, `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension`

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), Section 3, Theorem 3.7(i), p. 17; Kedlaya–Liu (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), Remark 3.5.12, p. 86.

#### `completed-tensor-plus-ring-not-integrally-closed` — The completed tensor product of plus rings need not be integrally closed

*lemma*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Field/FiniteExtension`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let K be a perfectoid field with algebraically closed residue field, for instance the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) with ℚ̆_p the completion of the maximal unramified extension of ℚ_p, let ℓ be a prime with ℓ ∤ p(p − 1), and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), a cyclic Galois extension of degree ℓ which is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields) with trivial residue extension. With A = K, B = C = L and plus rings the rings of integers, D = L ⊗̂_K L ≅ L^ℓ and D⁺ = (L°)^ℓ, while L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ is injective and not surjective. So the map from the ϖ-adic completion of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ to D⁺ in PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) is an almost isomorphism that is not an isomorphism, and the completed tensor product of plus rings is not integrally closed in D, hence not a ring of integral elements.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- K perfectoid with algebraically closed residue field; ℓ a prime not dividing p(p − 1).
- The perfectoidness of L is the finite-extension theorem of this layer; the rest is the formula of P2.

*Proof outline.*
1. (iv) K contains μ_ℓ (Hensel's lemma over the algebraically closed residue field) and p^{1/ℓ} ∉ K (1/ℓ is not in the value group (p − 1)⁻¹ℤ[1/p]), so L/K is cyclic of degree ℓ and L ⊗_K L ≅ L^ℓ, a ⊗ b ↦ (a g(b))_g. As the value group of K is dense, 𝔪_K L° = 𝔪_L, so L°/𝔪_K L° is the residue field of L, which equals that of K. If L° ⊗_{K°} L° → (L°)^ℓ (injective, the source being K°-flat) were surjective, K° → L° would be a Galois extension of rings with group Gal(L/K), hence L° would be finite projective, thus free, of rank ℓ over the local ring K°, contradicting dim L°/𝔪_K L° = 1.
2. The formula of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii) identifies D⁺ with (L°)^ℓ up to the almost isomorphism, which is therefore not an isomorphism.

*Acceptance.*
- The example with K the completion of ℚ̆_p(μ_{p^∞}) and L = K(p^{1/ℓ}), ℓ ∤ p(p − 1).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces — the plus ring of a fibre product is the completed integral closure, not the completed tensor product of plus rings.

*Prerequisites.* `P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula`, `P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`

*Sources.* Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), §2.8, proof of Lemma 2.8.7, p. 71 — the plus-ring claim this example refutes (see the source issues).


### ECD Theorem 6.1 over a perfectoid Tate ring

#### `finite-etale-tilting-equivalence` — Tilting is an equivalence between finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring and over its tilt (ECD 6.1(ii))

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/AlmostPurity`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras: any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭. Then the untilting functor (−)♯: FÉt(R♭) → FÉt(R) (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor) is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse the tilting functor S ↦ S♭ (S being perfectoid). It is compatible with tensor products, with base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings (in particular rational localisations and completed residue fields), and preserves ranks and faithful flatness. For every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R° with tilt R♭⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting), it induces an equivalence between finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) and (R♭, R♭⁺) → (S♭, S♭⁺) (plus rings the integral closures; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), i.e. between finite étale affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(R, R⁺) and over Spa(R♭, R♭⁺).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic; FÉt = Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale` with natural topologies.
- The gluing uses rational coverings of Spa(R, R⁺) and the effective descent of finite étale algebras along them (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent), which needs no sheafiness; the sheaf property of O is not used.

*Proof outline.*
1. Full faithfulness: P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful.
2. Local essential surjectivity: fix S ∈ FÉt(R), X = Spa(R, R⁺), x ∈ X. The completed residue field k(x)^ is a perfectoid field with tilt k(x♭)^ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). By P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii), S ⊗_R k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ for some T_x ∈ FÉt(k(x♭)^). By P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X♭ there are a rational U♭ ∋ x♭ and T_U ∈ FÉt(O_{X♭}(U♭)) with T_U ⊗ k(x♭)^ ≅ T_x; U♭ is the tilt of a rational U ∋ x with O_X(U) perfectoid of tilt O_{X♭}(U♭) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).
3. Then (T_U)♯ ∈ FÉt(O_X(U)) satisfies (T_U)♯ ⊗ k(x)^ ≅ T_x♯ ≅ S ⊗ k(x)^ (base change compatibility of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor); by the full faithfulness half of P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit on X, after shrinking U, (T_U)♯ ≅ S ⊗_R O_X(U).
4. Quasi-compactness of X (anchor Layer 2) gives a finite rational covering X = ∪ U_i with T_i ∈ FÉt(O(U_i♭)) and φ_i: T_i♯ ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i). On the rational U_ij = U_i ∩ U_j, φ_j⁻¹ ∘ φ_i descends uniquely to T_i ⊗ O(U_ij♭) ≅ T_j ⊗ O(U_ij♭) (full faithfulness over the perfectoid O(U_ij), whose tilt is O(U_ij♭)); the cocycle condition holds by faithfulness over U_ijk.
5. Glue: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent on X♭ gives T ∈ FÉt(R♭) with T ⊗ O(U_i♭) ≅ T_i compatibly; then T♯ ⊗ O(U_i) ≅ S ⊗ O(U_i) compatibly on overlaps, and the full faithfulness of descent on X gives T♯ ≅ S.
6. Quasi-inverse: T♯ is perfectoid with (T♯)♭ ≅ T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor), so S ↦ S♭ is quasi-inverse. Plus rings: the integral closure of R⁺ in S tilts to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭, both being the elements of absolute value ≤ 1 at the points over Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).

*Acceptance.*
- For R = K a perfectoid field this is P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields (ii).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (tilt 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩): the finite étale R-algebras are the untilts of finite étale algebras over the characteristic-p ring; e.g. the Kummer cover R[u]/(u^ℓ − T), ℓ ≠ p, is the untilt of R♭[u]/(u^ℓ − T♭).
- The non-field example of ECD Example 3.4(iv), R = ℤ_p^cycl⟦T^{1/p^∞}⟧⟨(p/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/T], is covered: no base field is used.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid — every S is an untilt; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — tilting of finite étale maps; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale — finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`, `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields`, `P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.
