#### `finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid` — Finite étale algebras over a perfectoid Tate ring are perfectoid (ECD 6.1(i))

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/AlmostPurity`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field) and S a finite étale R-algebra (Mathlib `Module.Finite R S`, `Algebra.Etale R S`) with its natural topology as a finite R-module. Then S is a perfectoid Tate ring; S ≅ (S♭)♯ with S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); for every ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R°, with S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S (the finite étale pair `Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S` of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), (S, S⁺) is a perfectoid Huber pair whose tilt (S♭, S♭⁺) has S♭⁺ the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭. Consequently Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is a finite étale morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces. This serves AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.5(1), Hansen–Kedlaya Proposition 2.15(a)).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale as a ring; the topology on S is the natural module topology (complete, since S is finite projective).

*Proof outline.*
1. By P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S ≅ T♯ for T := S♭ ∈ FÉt(R♭); T♯ is a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt T (P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor).
2. The natural topology on S agrees with the topology of T♯ (both are the natural finite R-module topology; any R-linear isomorphism of finite projective modules is a homeomorphism).
3. Plus rings: as in the last step of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence, S⁺ corresponds to the integral closure of R♭⁺ in S♭ under PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting.
4. (S, S⁺) is sheafy (perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so Spa(S, S⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space finite étale over Spa(R, R⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism).

*Acceptance.*
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and S = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): S is a perfectoid field (P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields).
- For R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R[u]/(u² − (1 + pT)) (p odd; étale since 1 + pT is a unit and 2 is invertible): S is perfectoid.
- Non-example (why étale matters): S = R[u]/(u²) is finite but not reduced, hence not uniform and not perfectoid; S = R[u]/(u² − p) over R = ℚ_p^cycl is finite étale and perfectoid, but the analogous extension ℚ_p(√p) of the non-perfectoid ℚ_p is not perfectoid.

*Uses.* AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale — R̃ ⊗_R S is perfectoid for R̃ perfectoid and S finite étale (the AdicSpacesPartII request); PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale — adic spaces finite étale over perfectoid spaces are perfectoid; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids — preimages of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p — a rational subset of a finite étale space over a perfectoid is perfectoid.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`, `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`, `mathlib:Module.Finite`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1 (i), p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4); Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.4.5, and its sketch, p. 53; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 2, §2.5, Theorem 2.5.9 (a), p. 62; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §3.6, Theorem 3.6.21, p. 97; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings), §3.3, Theorem 3.3.18 (b), case (iv), p. 64.

#### `almost-finite-etale-equivalence` — Almost purity, categorical form: (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) by inverting ϖ, compatibly with tilting

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/AlmostPurity`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring with tilt R♭, ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p, and R⁺ ⊆ R° any ring of integral elements. Then: (a) the functor (R°a)_afet → FÉt(R), A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] (natural topology), is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse S ↦ S°a = S⁺a, compatible with tensor products and base change along maps of perfectoid Tate rings; (b) the six categories FÉt(R) ≃ (R°a)_afet ≃ (R°a/ϖ)_afet = (R♭°a/ϖ♭)_afet ≃ (R♭°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R♭) of Scholze's diagram are equivalent by the functors of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor, and the composite is the tilting equivalence of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence; (c) (R⁺a)_afet = (R°a)_afet, since R⁺a = R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup; ECD Definition 3.23). In Bhatt's notation: inverting p (resp. t) gives R°a_afet ≃ R_fet (resp. S°a_afet ≃ S_fet) and tilting gives R°a_afet ≃ S°a_afet for S = R♭.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate, any characteristic, no base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°).

*Proof outline.*
1. Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is T♯ for some T (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence), so S°a is almost finite étale (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful: the essential image consists of S with almost finite étale S°a).
2. A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is fully faithful (P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful, proof) and essentially surjective: S = (S°a)_*[ϖ⁻¹] since (S°a)_* = S° for perfectoid S (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary; S perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).
3. (b): each functor of the chain is an equivalence: P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence on the tilt side, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras for the two reductions modulo ϖ, (a) on the untilt side.
4. (c): S⁺ ⊆ S° with S°/S⁺ almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii) applied to the perfectoid S).

*Acceptance.*
- R = K a perfectoid field: (K°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(K) via L ↦ L°a (Berkeley Theorem 7.3.2 and the diagram following it).
- Characteristic p: this is P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence (Gabber–Ramero 3.5.28).
- Non-example: the analogous functor on honest (non-almost) finite étale R°-algebras is not essentially surjective: over K = ℚ_p^cycl, K(p^{1/2})° is not étale over K°.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale — the objectwise statement; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity — (S ⊗_R S)°a = S°a ⊗ S°a for the Čech complex of a finite étale cover; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations — Ô^{+a}(W̃) as a completed tensor product via almost purity; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — almost faithfully flat descent of the almost finite étale integral structures.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`, `P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful`, `P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `P3/characteristic-p-almost-purity-equivalence`, `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Theorem 7.9 (i), p. 42; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 6, Theorem 6.2.10 (2), p. 49; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.3, discussion after Theorem 7.3.2, p. 51; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §3, after Definition 3.23, p. 19.

#### `integral-closure-almost-finite-etale` — The integral closure is almost finite étale: S° over R° for S finite étale over a perfectoid Tate ring R (ECD 6.1(iii))

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/AlmostPurity`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (any characteristic, no perfectoid base field), R⁺ ⊆ R° a ring of integral elements, ϖ a pseudouniformiser, S ∈ FÉt(R) and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S. Then: (i) S° is the integral closure of R° in S, S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S°, and S°a = S⁺a is an almost finite étale R°a = R⁺a-algebra: almost finitely presented, almost projective, and unramified (the diagonal idempotent of S ⊗_R S is an almost element of S° ⊗_{R°} S°); (ii) S°a is uniformly almost finite projective: there is n ≥ 0 such that for every ε ∈ R°° there are R°-linear maps S° → (R°)ⁿ → S° composing to multiplication by ε; (iii) Tr_{S/R}(S°) ⊆ R° and the trace pairing induces an almost isomorphism S°a → alHom_{R°a}(S°a, R°a); (iv) if S is faithfully flat over R, S°a is almost faithfully flat over R°a, Tr_{S/R}(S°°) ⊇ R°° (up to almost zero), and R°a → S°a is almost split. Not claimed, and false in general: S° finite, flat or étale over R°, or S free over R.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate; S finite étale; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup).

*Proof outline.*
1. (i): by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence, S ≅ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] with A almost finite étale and A = S°a; S° is the integral closure of R° (P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (b), S being uniform); S°°⊆ S⁺ ⊆ S° as S⁺ is open and integrally closed (ECD Example 3.22(ii)).
2. (ii): uniformity holds in characteristic p (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (iv)) and lifts along the ϖ-adic deformation (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi) through the chain of P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor.
3. (iii): an almost finite projective algebra is almost finite étale iff its trace pairing is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion, Gabber–Ramero Theorem 4.1.14); Tr(S°) ⊆ R° by P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (c).
4. (iv): faithful flatness of S is positivity of ranks, preserved by tilting; in characteristic p, R°a → S°a is almost split with trace surjective onto R°° (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p (v)); reduce modulo ϖ and lift: almost splitting modulo ϖ of an almost projective map lifts, and trace surjectivity is checked modulo ϖ by Nakayama for the ϖ-adically complete R°.

*Acceptance.*
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}) (p odd): L°a is almost finite étale over K°a though L°/K° is ramified; the trace of L° contains every element of positive valuation (Tate's computation, Berkeley Example 7.3.3).
- Kedlaya–Liu's formulation: o_B is uniformly almost finite projective and almost étale over o_A for B ∈ FÉt(A), A perfectoid (Theorem 5.5.9); Kedlaya–Liu II Corollary 3.3.24: Tr: B°° → A°° surjective for B faithfully finite étale.
- For R of characteristic p this is P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids — every finite étale map of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity — almost faithful flatness of O⁺ along finite étale covers; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations — Ô_Y⁺(U) almost flat over the perfectoid base; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — descent of the integral structure S⁺a.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`, `P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform`, `P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`, `P3/finite-etale-untilting-functor`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-flat-projective-finiteness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/trace-form-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/uniform-finite-projectivity-mod-varpi`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `mathlib:Algebra.traceForm`, `mathlib:integralClosure`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1 (iii), p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4); Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §5.5, Theorem 5.5.9, p. 133; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §5.5, Definition 5.5.8, p. 132; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings), §3.3, Corollary 3.3.24, p. 67; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.4.5 (3), p. 53; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Theorem 7.9 (iii), p. 42.

#### `almost-purity-theorem` — The almost purity theorem for perfectoid Tate rings (ECD Theorem 6.1)

*theorem*. **Planet:** *Almost purity theorem*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FiniteEtale/AlmostPurity`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1; characteristic 0, p, or neither; no perfectoid base field) with tilt R♭, and FÉt(R) the category of finite étale R-algebras with their natural topologies. (i) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid). (ii) Tilting S ↦ S♭ is an equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭), with quasi-inverse the untilting functor (P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence). (iii) For every S ∈ FÉt(R), S° is almost finite étale over R° (equivalently S⁺a over R⁺a for any ring of integral elements and S⁺ its integral closure), and uniformly almost finite projective (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale); categorically, A ↦ A_*[ϖ⁻¹] is an equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence). The three conclusions are distinct statements: (iii) is about the integral structure up to almost zero and is neither étaleness of S° over R° nor finite freeness of S over R. Consequences recorded elsewhere: every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale); for R = K a perfectoid field, (i)–(iii) are P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1: complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ such that ϖ^p | p in R° and Φ: R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is an isomorphism.

*Proof outline.*
1. (i): P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid.
2. (ii): P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.
3. (iii): P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale, with the categorical form P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence.
4. The declaration bundles the three conclusions as consumers cite them (ECD Theorem 6.1).

*Acceptance.*
- Every finite étale R-algebra S, for R perfectoid, is itself perfectoid with S°a almost finite étale over R°a; 'almost finite étale' means finite étale in the almost category, not étaleness of S° over R°.
- R = ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ with the Kummer cover S = R[T^{1/ℓ}] (ℓ ≠ p) and a wildly ramified Artin–Schreier–Witt-type cover: both have S°a uniformly almost finitely generated over R°a.
- Faltings' original almost purity (toric charts over a discretely valued field) is recovered by base change to the perfectoid tower (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 5.5.10).

*Uses.* DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — v-descent of (finite) étale maps rests on (i)–(iii); PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — finite étale covers of the perfectoid tower; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/relative-completed-structure-sheaf-computations — almost purity for Ô⁺; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p — étale over perfectoid is perfectoid; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 — almost purity and the finite étale site; VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3 — pro-étale local systems rest on almost purity.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`, `P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`, `P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1, p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4); Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.1 (iii), p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §1, Theorem 1.10, p. 4; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.4, Theorem 7.4.5 (3), p. 53.


### Finite étale and étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces

#### `perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy` — Perfectoid Tate rings are strongly sheafy; perfectoid spaces are locally strongly sheafy

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/StronglySheafy`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

Let R be a perfectoid Tate ring. For every n ≥ 0 the Tate algebra R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ (Tau Ceti `Huber.restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n R`) is stably uniform, hence sheafy for every ring of integral elements; that is, R is strongly sheafy in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (`Huber.IsStronglySheafy R`). Consequently every perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) is a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (`AdicSpace.IsLocallyStronglySheafy`), and every rational localisation and every finite étale algebra of a perfectoid Tate ring is strongly sheafy. This makes available, for perfectoid spaces, A1's local-to-global description of finite étale maps, fibre products of étale maps inside adic spaces, and the étale and finite étale sites with their structure sheaves.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- R perfectoid Tate (ECD Definition 3.1); p is topologically nilpotent in R because ϖ^p | p, so R is a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra.

*Proof outline.*
1. The perfected Tate algebra R⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples), hence stably uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy).
2. R⟨T⟩ → R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ splits as a map of topological R⟨T⟩-modules: R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the completed direct sum of the free rank-one modules R⟨T⟩·T^b over b ∈ (ℤ[1/p] ∩ [0, 1))ⁿ, and the projection onto b = 0 is continuous and R⟨T⟩-linear.
3. A complete Tate ring admitting a topologically split map to a stably uniform complete Tate ring is stably uniform, hence sheafy by Buzzard–Verberkmoes (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy; anchor Layer 4).
4. Closure under rational localisation and finite étale algebras: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair (b), (d); alternatively they are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids, P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and the first step applies.
5. Locally strongly sheafy: a perfectoid space is covered by Spa(R, R⁺) with R perfectoid.

*Acceptance.*
- ℚ_p^cycl⟨T_1, T_2⟩ is sheafy (it is even strongly noetherian); the content is for non-noetherian R such as ℚ_p^cycl⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨T⟩ and the ring of ECD Example 3.4(iv).
- Non-example of the hypothesis: Buzzard–Verberkmoes' non-sheafy uniform Tate rings are not strongly sheafy; perfectoidness is what excludes them.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale — A1's local-to-global theorem over perfectoid affinoids; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space — A1's site applies to perfectoid spaces; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair — A1 defers the membership of perfectoid rings to PerfectoidSpaces.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/stably-uniform-sheafy`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 6, §6.3, Proposition 6.3.3 (3), p. 47; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 6, §6.3, Proposition 6.3.4, p. 48; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 1, §1.10, Hypothesis 1.10.3, p. 47; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §8.3, Definition 8.3.1 and discussion, p. 166.

#### `finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces` — Finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(i))

*definition* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X, Y be perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: the full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces locally of the form Spa(R, R⁺), R perfectoid). A morphism f: Y → X is finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f`) if it is finite étale as a morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism: X has a cover by open affinoids V = Spa(A, A⁺) with f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(B, B⁺) over V, B ∈ FÉt(A) with its natural topology and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺). No second notion is introduced: `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` is A1's `AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale` of the underlying morphism. ECD's defining condition — for every open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X the preimage f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid with R → S finite étale and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S — is equivalent (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale), as are Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (a cover of X by such affinoids) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1). X_fét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces finite étale over X (all X-morphisms); for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, global sections give X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. Conventions: the plus ring is the integral closure, never S° when R⁺ ≠ R°; f need not be surjective; the degree x ↦ dim_{k(x)}(O_Y ⊗ k(x)) is locally constant.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X, Y perfectoid; for Y an arbitrary adic space with Y → X finite étale, Y is automatically perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).

*Proof outline.*
1. Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale f := AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f` on the underlying morphism (perfectoid spaces are analytic, their charts being Tate).
2. The affinoid model Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(R), R perfectoid, is an affinoid perfectoid space: S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and sheafy.

*API.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class on morphisms of perfectoid spaces: A1's AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale of the underlying morphism.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_adic` (compatibility): IsFiniteEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f.toAdicSpaceHom.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_forall_affinoidPerfectoid` (characterisation): ECD Definition 6.2(i): for every open affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ X the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with integral-closure plus ring (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.iff_exists_cover` (characterisation): Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii): the same condition over the members of one open affinoid perfectoid cover of X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.spa` (constructor): For R perfectoid and S ∈ FÉt(R), Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is finite étale (S⁺ the integral closure).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of finite étale morphisms are finite étale (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along any morphism of perfectoid spaces is finite étale, with affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C, D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.of_comp` (other): If g and g ∘ f are finite étale, so is f.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f is finite étale iff f♭ is (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.isStronglyFiniteEtale` (relation): Finite étale morphisms are strongly finite étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.finiteEtaleAffinoidEquiv` (equivalence): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X_fét ≃ (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R)ᵒᵖ via global sections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.isFinite` (projection): Finite étale morphisms are finite (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-morphism) and hence closed; they are open (étale).

*Unit tests.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_fold` (degenerate): For every perfectoid space X, X ⊔ X → X and ∅ → X are finite étale, and the identity is finite étale of degree 1.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_kummer` (computation): Over X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩), Spa(R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) → X (ℓ ≠ p prime) is finite étale of degree ℓ, and its source is perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_rational` (non-example): The inclusion of the rational subset {|T| ≤ |p|} into the perfectoid closed disc is étale but not finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_plus_ring` (non-example): For (K, K⁺) with K⁺ ⊊ O_K of rank 2, Spa(K × K, O_K × O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺) is not finite étale although K → K × K is a finite étale ring map: the plus ring must be the integral closure (K⁺ × K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): IsFiniteEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsFiniteEtale f.toAdicSpaceHom (definitional).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsFiniteEtale.test_ecd` (characterisation): IsFiniteEtale f iff for every open affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) = Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(R) and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ (ECD Definition 6.2(i)).

*Acceptance.*
- The fold map X ⊔ X → X and ∅ → X are finite étale; an open immersion that is not closed is not.
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) and ℓ ≠ p, the Kummer cover T ↦ T^ℓ (Spa of R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)) is finite étale of degree ℓ.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces — the middle factor of the local description of étale maps; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space — objects of X_fét; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid — finite étale morphisms descend along étale covers; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — the prestack of finite étale perfectoid spaces; DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected — finite étale covers of strictly totally disconnected spaces split; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover — the finite étale factor of an étale map, affinoid perfectoid over rational subsets; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-finite-etale — finite étale covers of perfectoid spaces.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Definition 6.2 (i), p. 26; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Definition 7.1 (i), p. 39; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, Definition 7.5.1 (1), p. 55.

#### `etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces` — Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 6.2(ii))

*definition*. **Planet:** *Étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces*. Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f`) if it is étale in A1's local sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, `AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription`): every y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood V ⊆ Y such that f|_V factors as V ↪ W → U ↪ X with V → W an open immersion, W → U finite étale (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces) and U ⊆ X open. W is then automatically perfectoid. This is ECD Definition 6.2(ii) (whose printed condition 'y ∈ Y' is read as y ∈ V), Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(iii) and Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(2). Equivalent local form: U may be taken a rational subset of an affinoid perfectoid open of X, W = Spa(S, S⁺) with S ∈ FÉt(O(U)), and V a rational subset of W; so étale morphisms are locally composites 'rational embedding, finite étale, rational embedding' of affinoid perfectoid spaces. X_ét denotes the category of perfectoid spaces étale over X (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). Étale morphisms need not be separated or quasi-compact.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X, Y perfectoid; an adic space étale over a perfectoid X is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)).

*Proof outline.*
1. Define `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale f := AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f` on the underlying morphism.
2. W perfectoid: W → U finite étale with U perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid, locally on U); rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids).

*API.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class on morphisms of perfectoid spaces: A1's local description.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.iff_adic` (compatibility): IsEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f.toAdicSpaceHom.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_isOpenImmersion` (instance): Open immersions are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_isFiniteEtale` (instance): Finite étale morphisms are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.exists_standardAffinoid` (characterisation): Local standard form: rational ⊆ finite étale over rational ⊆ affinoid perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of étale morphisms are étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Base change along any morphism of perfectoid spaces is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.of_comp` (other): If g and g ∘ f are étale, so is f.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.isOpenMap` (projection): Étale morphisms are open on underlying spaces.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f is étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.isStronglyEtale` (relation): Étale morphisms are strongly étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.isPerfectoid_of_isEtaleLocalDescription` (instance): An adic space étale over a perfectoid space is perfectoid.

*Unit tests.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_openImmersion` (degenerate): Open immersions of perfectoid spaces are étale; the identity is étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_rational_in_cover` (computation): For R perfectoid, S ∈ FÉt(R) and a rational subset V ⊆ Spa(S, S⁺), the composite V → Spa(R, R⁺) is étale (standard affinoid étale map).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_not_finite` (non-example): The inclusion of the open unit disc (a non-quasi-compact open) into the closed perfectoid disc is étale but not finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_proetale` (non-example): Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}) → Spa(ℚ_p^cycl, ℤ_p^cycl) is not étale (it is pro-étale, PerfectoidSpaces:P6), nor is the Zariski closed immersion {T = 0} into the perfectoid disc (not open).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): IsEtale f ↔ AdicSpace.IsEtaleLocalDescription f.toAdicSpaceHom (definitional).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsEtale.test_standard` (characterisation): IsEtale f iff f is locally on Y a composite of a rational embedding, a finite étale map and a rational embedding of affinoid perfectoid spaces.

*Acceptance.*
- Open immersions and finite étale morphisms are étale.
- Two copies of the perfectoid closed disc glued along the complement of the origin map étale, not separatedly, to the disc.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space — objects of X_ét; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — étale maps tilt to étale maps; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — the prestack of separated étale perfectoid spaces; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison — Y_ét of the perfectoid covers; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover — ECD Definition 6.2(ii) and its local standard form; PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map — affinoid étale maps as building blocks of pro-étale maps.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism`, `P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Definition 6.2 (ii), p. 26; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Definition 6.2 (ii), continued, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Definition 7.1 (iii), p. 39; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, remark after Definition 7.5.1, p. 55.

#### `strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change` — Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces; tilting invariance and base change

*definition* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

(Scholze 2012 Definition 7.2, over an arbitrary perfectoid base) A morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) of perfectoid Huber pairs is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale (S ∈ FÉt(R) with its natural topology, S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras). A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale f`) if X has a cover by open affinoid perfectoid V with f⁻¹(V) affinoid perfectoid and (O_X(V), O⁺_X(V)) → (O_Y(f⁻¹V), O⁺_Y(f⁻¹V)) strongly finite étale; strongly étale (`PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale f`) if locally on Y it factors as an open immersion, a strongly finite étale map and an open immersion. Properties: (a) f is strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭ is (the almost finite étale condition is transported by P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b)); (b) base change along arbitrary maps Z → X of perfectoid spaces preserves both classes, with affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C (already complete, being finite projective over C), D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺ in D, and |Y ×_X Z| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |Z| surjective (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(i)–(ii), with the printed |X ×_Z Y| read as the fibre product of the base change); (c) composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.8); (d) in characteristic p every (finite) étale map is strongly (finite) étale, and by almost purity this holds in general (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale), so the strong classes coincide with P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces and P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- Perfectoid spaces without base field; almost mathematics for (R°, R°°) on each chart (R°a = R⁺a).

*Proof outline.*
1. Definition: the affinoid condition is stable under restriction to rational subsets (base change of almost finite étale algebras, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras, and rational localisation of the perfectoid pair, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction), so the global notion is well defined.
2. (b), affinoid case: A ⊗_B C is finite projective over C, hence complete; it is finite étale over C and D°a = A°a ⊗ C°a is almost finite étale (base change); the universal property among perfectoid spaces follows from that of Spa of a finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv)); surjectivity on points from Huber's argument (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).
3. (a): the tilting slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence) matches affinoid perfectoid covers; strongly finite étale affinoid maps correspond under P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence (b).

*API.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class: affinoid-locally strongly finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale` (structure): Prop-valued class: locally open immersion, strongly finite étale, open immersion.
- `Perfectoid.Pair.IsStronglyFiniteEtale` (data): The affinoid condition on a map of perfectoid pairs: finite étale with S°a almost finite étale over R°a.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f strongly finite étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.tilt_iff` (equivalence): f strongly étale iff f♭ is.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Stable under base change along any map of perfectoid spaces, with the affinoid formula.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.baseChange` (functoriality): Stable under base change; surjective on topological fibre products.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.comp` (functoriality): Composites of strongly finite étale maps are strongly finite étale.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.isOpenMap` (projection): Strongly étale maps are open.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.iff_isFiniteEtale` (characterisation): Strongly finite étale ↔ finite étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.iff_isEtale` (characterisation): Strongly étale ↔ étale (P3/etale-is-strongly-etale).

*Unit tests.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_charp` (characterisation): For X of characteristic p, IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsFiniteEtale f (P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyEtale.test_open` (degenerate): Open immersions are strongly étale; they are strongly finite étale only when also closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_tilt` (compatibility): IsStronglyFiniteEtale f ↔ IsStronglyFiniteEtale f♭.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_plus_ring` (non-example): (K, K⁺) → (K × K, O_K × O_K) with K⁺ ⊊ O_K is not strongly finite étale: the plus ring is not the integral closure.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyFiniteEtale.test_basechange` (computation): For Spa(A, A⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) strongly finite étale and Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺), the fibre product is Spa(A ⊗_B C, integral closure of C⁺).

*Acceptance.*
- The strong notion is a priori stronger: it requires S°a almost finite étale; in characteristic 0 the equality with finite étale is a theorem (almost purity), not part of the definition.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids — the affinoid statement is about this class; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — the strong classes are manifestly tilting invariant; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p — in characteristic p étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/fs-iv-4-19-zariski-closed-char-p — strongly étale maps and their base change; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv — base change of affinoid étale maps; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover — strongly finite étale pieces.

*Prerequisites.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Definition 7.2 (i), p. 39; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, after Definition 7.2, p. 40; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Lemma 7.3 (ii), p. 40; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Corollary 7.8, p. 42; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, after Definition 7.2, p. 40.

#### `strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids` — Preimages of affinoid perfectoid opens under finite étale maps are affinoid perfectoid, with strongly finite étale ring map

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let f: Y → X be a finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces (P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), or more generally a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces with X perfectoid, and let V = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X be an open affinoid perfectoid subspace (arbitrary perfectoid Tate R, no base field). Then f⁻¹(V) is affinoid perfectoid: f⁻¹(V) = Spa(S, S⁺) with S = O_Y(f⁻¹V) ∈ FÉt(R) perfectoid and S⁺ the integral closure of R⁺ in S, and (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) is strongly finite étale (S°a almost finite étale over R°a). Global sections give an equivalence V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op, and strongly finite étale covers of V correspond to finite étale R-algebras (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.6 and Theorem 7.9(i)–(ii), Bhatt Proposition 10.0.6 and Corollary 10.0.7, in general). In particular every finite étale morphism of perfectoid spaces satisfies ECD Definition 6.2(i). Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.7 (in characteristic p, étale maps are locally base changes of étale maps of noetherian affinoid adic spaces) is not needed for this.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid; f finite étale in A1's sense; V affinoid perfectoid open.

*Proof outline.*
1. R is strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), so AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (a), (c) gives f⁻¹(V) ≅ Spa(`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale R⁺ S`) with S ∈ FÉt(R), and V_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op. (The descent of finite étale algebras along the rational cover of V on which f is known to be affinoid is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent; Scholze's noetherian approximation, via P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit and p-finite affinoids, is replaced by it.)
2. S is perfectoid (P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid) and S°a is almost finite étale over R°a (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale), so the map of pairs is strongly finite étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change).

*Acceptance.*
- A finite étale cover of the perfectoid closed disc glued from covers of two rational pieces with compatible gluing is Spa of a single finite étale algebra over R = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, with plus ring the integral closure of R⁺.
- Openness of strongly étale maps follows (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); it is not assumed.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale — ECD's 'for all affinoids' form; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects — finite étale covers of affinoid perfectoids are algebraic; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4 — affinoid finite étale pieces over the limit; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover — W_y affinoid perfectoid with finite étale ring map.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`, `P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`, `P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Proposition 7.6, p. 41; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 10, Proposition 10.0.6, p. 119; Bhargav Bhatt (Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017), Chapter 10, Corollary 10.0.7 with proof, p. 120; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 26.

#### `etale-is-strongly-etale` — Every finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale)

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let f: Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then f is finite étale iff it is strongly finite étale, and étale iff it is strongly étale (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change). In characteristic p this is P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p; in general it is a consequence of almost purity (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale). Hence the tilting invariance and base-change properties of the strong classes hold for all (finite) étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X, Y perfectoid spaces over no fixed base.

*Proof outline.*
1. Strongly ⇒ plain: by definition.
2. Finite étale ⇒ strongly finite étale: over each affinoid perfectoid V ⊆ X, P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids.
3. Étale ⇒ strongly étale: the finite étale factor W → U of the local description is strongly finite étale by the previous step.

*Acceptance.*
- For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}), Spa(L) → Spa(K) is strongly finite étale although L° is not étale over K°.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — étale maps tilt because strongly étale maps do; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/jacobian-criterion-char-p — étale maps of perfectoid spaces are strongly étale.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p`, `P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, after Theorem 7.9, p. 43; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, after Definition 7.2, p. 40.

#### `perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale` — Comparison of perfectoid finite étale and étale morphisms with AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and with finite étale algebras

*comparison* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X be a perfectoid space. (a) (Perfectoidness) If g: Y → X is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of analytic adic spaces in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), then Y is a perfectoid space. (b) (Morphism classes) For morphisms of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: finite étale in A1's sense (= P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); ECD Definition 6.2(i) (for every open affinoid perfectoid U the preimage is affinoid perfectoid, finite étale with integral-closure plus ring); Scholze 2012 Definition 7.1(ii) (for one open affinoid perfectoid cover); Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(1); strongly finite étale. Likewise étale in A1's sense ⇔ ECD 6.2(ii) ⇔ Scholze 2012 7.1(iii) ⇔ Berkeley 7.5.1(2) ⇔ strongly étale. (c) (Algebraic comparison) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, the functors X_fét → FÉt(R)^op (global sections), FÉt(R) → {finite étale morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺)} (`Huber.Pair.finiteEtale`, plus ring forced to be the integral closure) and the latter → Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` (forget topology and plus ring) are equivalences; every finite étale R-algebra is perfectoid for its natural topology. (d) (Sites) The category of perfectoid spaces étale (resp. finite étale) over X is the small étale (resp. finite étale) site of the underlying adic space in A1's sense (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site), with the same coverings; A1's structure sheaves O, O⁺ on it (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), its Galois category of finite étale objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category) and its basis of affinoid objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison) apply. (e) (Base change from adic spaces; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv) and Proposition 7.10) If Y' → X' is a finite étale (resp. étale) morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (e.g. locally noetherian ones) and Z → X' is a morphism from a perfectoid space, then Y' ×_{X'} Z exists, is perfectoid, and is finite étale (resp. étale) over Z; for affinoids its ring is D = A ⊗_B C with D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid, hence locally strongly sheafy (P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy); A1's notions are defined for all analytic adic spaces.

*Proof outline.*
1. (a): locally on X, Y is Spa(S, S⁺) with S finite étale over a perfectoid R (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global over the strongly sheafy affinoid perfectoid charts), perfectoid by P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid; for étale maps, Y is locally an open subspace of such a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. (b): A1 ⇔ Scholze 7.1(ii) by definition; A1 ⇒ ECD 6.2(i) by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids; ECD 6.2(i) ⇒ A1 trivially; ⇔ strongly by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale; Berkeley 7.5.1(1) quantifies over opens of the target and is equivalent by the same lemma. The étale case follows from the finite étale case and the definitions.
3. (c): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (iv) (morphisms of the pairs are the algebra maps); the forgetful functor to CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R is an equivalence because the topology and the plus ring are determined.
4. (d): objects étale over X in A1's sense are perfectoid by (a); the morphism classes agree by (b); coverings are jointly surjective families in both.
5. (e): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change for the fibre product with locally strongly sheafy Z; perfectoidness by (a) applied over Z; it is the fibre product in perfectoid spaces over the analytic base X' of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base (the uniform completion is unnecessary, the algebra being finite projective over the perfectoid factor).

*Acceptance.*
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) and the pullback of the Kummer cover 𝔾_m → 𝔾_m, z ↦ z^ℓ, of the rigid torus along X → Spa(ℚ_p⟨T^{±1}⟩): the fibre product is Spa(R[u]/(u^ℓ − T)), perfectoid and finite étale over X ((e)).
- For X = Spa(C, C⁺), C algebraically closed perfectoid: X_fét is equivalent to finite sets (every finite étale C-algebra is split, Mathlib `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.equivOfIsSepClosed`).
- Non-example: a finite étale map of adic spaces over a non-perfectoid base (Spa ℚ_p(p^{1/2}) → Spa ℚ_p) has non-perfectoid source; (a) requires X perfectoid.

*Uses.* AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-standard-piece-cover — ECD 6.2(i) for W_y; AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/perfectoid-cover-presentation — étale maps over perfectoid covers stay perfectoid; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison — the perfectoid étale site is A1's.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`, `P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `P3/etale-is-strongly-etale`, `P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-over-analytic-base`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale.equivOfIsSepClosed`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 26; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Proposition 7.10, p. 43; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §8.3, Definition 8.3.1, p. 166.

#### `etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open` — Étale and finite étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces: composition, base change, cancellation, openness, tilting

*lemma* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

For morphisms of perfectoid spaces (Berkeley Proposition 7.5.2; ECD after Definition 6.2; Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.8, Proposition 7.10): (1) composites of (finite) étale morphisms are (finite) étale; (2) for f: Y → X (finite) étale and any g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces, the fibre product Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is (finite) étale over X', agrees with A1's fibre product of adic spaces, has the affinoid formula D = A ⊗_B C, D⁺ = integral closure of C⁺ (no completion needed), and |Y ×_X X'| → |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| is surjective; (3) if g and g ∘ f are (finite) étale, so is f; (4) f is (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭: Y♭ → X♭ is; (5) étale morphisms are open; quasi-compact étale morphisms have quasi-compact open image; the diagonal of an étale morphism is an open immersion, and of a finite étale morphism an open and closed immersion.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- All spaces perfectoid; fibre products in perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2.

*Proof outline.*
1. (1), (3), (5): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal, applied to the underlying adic spaces (locally strongly sheafy by P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy), with P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale identifying the classes.
2. (2): AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change gives the fibre product of adic spaces with its affinoid formula; it is perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)) and therefore satisfies the universal property among perfectoid spaces, so it is the perfectoid fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property); surjectivity on points from A1.
3. (4): by P3/etale-is-strongly-etale, f is (finite) étale iff strongly (finite) étale, and the strong classes are tilting invariant (P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (a)) — on affinoids by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence with plus rings, and the tilting slice equivalence PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence matches open covers.

*Acceptance.*
- For X' = Spa(k(x)^, k(x)^⁺) → X at a point x, the fibre of a finite étale Y → X is Spa of the finite étale k(x)^-algebra O_Y(f⁻¹V) ⊗ k(x)^.
- For the Kummer cover f of the perfectoid torus over ℚ_p^cycl, f♭ is the Kummer cover u ↦ u^ℓ of the tilted torus over 𝔽_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space — the site axioms; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — étale maps tilt; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4 — finite étale and affinoid étale objects are stable under base change; DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site — étale maps of perfectoid spaces as building blocks.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`, `P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `P3/etale-is-strongly-etale`, `P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-composition`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-cancellation`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, Proposition 7.5.2 (1), p. 55; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, Proposition 7.5.2 (2), p. 55; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, Proposition 7.5.2 (3), p. 55; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, Proposition 7.5.2 (4), p. 55; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, paragraph after Definition 6.2, p. 26.

#### `etale-descent-perfectoid` — Étale descent for finite étale morphisms and finite projective modules on perfectoid spaces

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Site`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X be a perfectoid space with étale site X_ét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). (a) (Locality) A morphism f: Y → X of perfectoid spaces is finite étale if, for some covering {X_i → X} in X_ét, every base change Y ×_X X_i → X_i is finite étale; étaleness of f is local on Y and on X for open coverings. (b) (Stack) The prestack U ↦ U_fét (finite étale perfectoid spaces over U, with isomorphisms) on X_ét is a stack for the étale topology (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`): finite étale spaces with descent data along an étale covering descend uniquely. (c) (Vector bundles; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22(b), (d)) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, M ↦ M ⊗_R O_{X_ét} is an equivalence between finitely generated projective R-modules and finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules, and M ⊗ O is a sheaf on X_ét with M ⊗ O(Y) = M ⊗_R O(Y) on affinoid perfectoid Y ∈ X_ét. Descent along v-covers is not part of this node (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid; coverings jointly surjective families of étale maps.

*Proof outline.*
1. Reduction: every covering in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object can be refined by composites of rational coverings and single surjective finite étale maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction, after Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.20 and de Jong–van der Put); it suffices to prove the claims for these two kinds of coverings.
2. Rational coverings: effective descent of finite étale algebras (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent) and of finite projective modules (Kiehl gluing on sheafy Tate affinoids, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing; perfectoid pairs are sheafy).
3. Surjective finite étale Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺): R → S is faithfully flat; faithfully flat descent of modules (Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars`, `ModuleCat.reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.4) descends the module and its multiplication; finiteness, projectivity and étaleness descend (Mathlib `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, `Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`; Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 1.3.5). The descended algebra is finite étale over R, hence perfectoid with the integral-closure plus ring (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (c)); finite projective modules descend along the sheafy finite étale surjection by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent.
4. (a) follows from (b) applied to the base-changed family with its canonical descent datum, together with full faithfulness (the equaliser property of O, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf).

*Acceptance.*
- For a finite Galois étale cover Y → X with group G and a G-equivariant finite étale Y' → Y, Y' descends to a finite étale X' → X with Y' = X' ×_X Y (Galois descent).
- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every finite locally free O_{X_ét}-module is free (c).

*Uses.* DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks — the étale-local step of v-descent; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors/three-descriptions-of-G-torsors — vector bundles are étale sheaves (Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22(c), (d)); VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3 — pro-étale local systems and vector bundles on perfectoid spaces.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`, `mathlib:comonadicExtendScalars`, `mathlib:ModuleCat.reflectsIsomorphisms_extendScalars_of_faithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Algebra.Etale.of_etale_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

*Sources.* Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §1.3, Theorem 1.3.4, p. 16; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §1.3, Theorem 1.3.5, p. 16; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §8.2, Theorem 8.2.22 (d), p. 165; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §9, proof of Proposition 9.7, p. 48.


### The étale site, its tilting equivalence, and étale almost acyclicity

#### `etale-site-of-perfectoid-space` — The étale site X_ét and the finite étale site X_fét of a perfectoid space

*construction*. **Planet:** *Étale site of a perfectoid space*. Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Site`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X be a perfectoid space. Its étale site X_ét (`PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale X`) is the small étale site of the underlying locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site; P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy): objects the adic spaces étale over X — all perfectoid (P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (a)), i.e. the perfectoid spaces étale over X of ECD — with all X-morphisms (étale by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (3)), and the topology generated by jointly surjective families (on all points, including higher-rank ones). The finite étale site X_fét is the full subcategory of finite étale objects with the induced jointly-surjective topology (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site). Structure: (i) X_ét has finite limits (fibre products of perfectoid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and a basis X_ét^aff of affinoid perfectoid objects étale over X, closed under rational subsets, finite étale maps and fibre products (Kedlaya–Liu 8.3.1: perfectoid spaces are stably adic), which is a dense subsite (Mathlib `Functor.IsDenseSubsite`); (ii) a morphism g: X' → X of perfectoid spaces induces a morphism of sites X'_ét → X_ét by base change, functorially; a morphism X → Y to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (e.g. locally noetherian) induces a morphism of sites X_ét → Y_ét (Scholze 2012 after Definition 7.11); (iii) O_{X_ét}: U ↦ O_U(U) and O⁺_{X_ét}: U ↦ O⁺_U(U) are sheaves of rings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), as are O⁺/ϖ and O^{+a}; (iv) for X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X_fét ≃ FÉt(R)^op; (v) for X connected and a geometric point, X_fét is a Galois category with fundamental group π₁(X) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category), and for X = Spa(K, K⁺), K a perfectoid field, π₁ = Gal(K^sep/K).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid; sites are those of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 with the coverings of ECD (jointly surjective).

*Proof outline.*
1. Take A1's site of the underlying adic space; perfectoidness of all objects and the equality of the morphism classes is P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale.
2. Site axioms, morphisms of sites: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (i)–(iv) with the fibre products identified by P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (2).
3. Basis: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison; affinoid objects are affinoid perfectoid by P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids.
4. Sheaves: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf; O⁺/ϖ and the almost sheaves by sheafification (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology).

*API.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale` (constructor): The category of perfectoid spaces étale over X (A1's AdicSpace.smallEtale of the underlying adic space).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtaleTopology` (structure): The Grothendieck topology of jointly surjective families.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.isPerfectoid` (instance): Every object of X_ét is a perfectoid space.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.hasFiniteLimits` (instance): X_ét has finite limits, computed by perfectoid fibre products.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtaleAffinoid` (data): The dense subsite of affinoid perfectoid objects étale over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.map` (functoriality): A morphism X' → X induces the base change functor X_ét → X'_ét and a morphism of sites, with map_id and map_comp.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.toAdic` (functoriality): A morphism X → Y to a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space induces a morphism of sites X_ét → Y_ét.
- `PerfectoidSpace.structureSheafEtale` (data): The sheaves O_{X_ét} and O⁺_{X_ét}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale` (constructor): The finite étale site X_fét.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale.affinoidEquiv` (equivalence): For X = Spa(R, R⁺): X_fét ≃ (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R)ᵒᵖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallFiniteEtale.galoisCategory` (instance): For connected X, X_fét is a Galois category.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.adicEquiv` (compatibility): X_ét ≃ AdicSpace.smallEtale of the underlying adic space, compatible with coverings.

*Unit tests.*
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_point` (computation): For K a perfectoid field, Spa(K, O_K)_fét ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets (via AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category and P3/fontaine-wintenberger).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_empty` (degenerate): For X = ∅ the site has a single object (∅) covered by the empty family; for X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every finite étale object is a finite disjoint union of copies of X, so X_fét ≃ FintypeCat.
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_adic` (compatibility): PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale X = AdicSpace.smallEtale X.toAdicSpace as sites (same objects up to the full embedding of perfectoid spaces, same coverings).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_basis` (characterisation): The affinoid perfectoid objects form a dense subsite: Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff).
- `PerfectoidSpace.smallEtale.test_not_fpqc` (non-example): Spa(ℂ_p) → Spa(ℚ_p^cycl) is not a covering in X_ét (not étale), although it is a v-cover: X_ét is not the pro-étale or v-site.

*Acceptance.*
- For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed, every covering of X in X_ét has a member with a section near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split).
- For X = Spa(K, O_K), K perfectoid field, X_fét ≃ finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets.

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence — the sites compared; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity — cohomology on X_ét; DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves — ν: X_proét → X_ét and the sheaves O, O⁺ on X_ét; DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected — étale covers of a perfectoid space; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison — X_ét for the perfectoid charts of Y^◇; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — X_ét → X_fét and cohomology of F_p on the perfectoid tower; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2 — étale topoi of perfectoid spaces over algebraically closed fields.

#### `etale-site-tilting-equivalence` — Tilting identifies the étale sites: X_ét ≃ X♭_ét, compatibly with affinoids, fibre products, coverings and O⁺/ϖ

*comparison* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Site`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting). The tilting functor Y ↦ Y♭ of the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence: perfectoid spaces over X ≃ perfectoid spaces over X♭) restricts to equivalences of categories X_ét ≃ X♭_ét and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). These equivalences preserve and reflect affinoid perfectoid objects (with Spa(S, S⁺)♭ = Spa(S♭, S♭⁺)), fibre products, and covering families (|Y| ≅ |Y♭| compatibly with the maps to |X| ≅ |X♭|); hence they are equivalences of sites and induce equivalences of topoi Sh(X_ét) ≃ Sh(X♭_ét) (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`). They are functorial in X: compatible with the morphisms of sites induced by maps X' → X and their tilts. For a pseudouniformiser ϖ = (ϖ♭)♯ of X (locally), they identify the sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ and O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and the almost sheaves O⁺a/ϖ and O⁺a_{X♭}/ϖ♭, on the identified sites. For affinoid X = Spa(R, R⁺) the restriction to X_fét is the tilting equivalence FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R♭) of P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid over no fixed base; ϖ chosen on affinoid perfectoid opens as in PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots.

*Proof outline.*
1. Objects: Y → X is étale iff Y♭ → X♭ is (P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (4)); essential surjectivity from the slice equivalence (every perfectoid space over X♭ is Y♭ for a perfectoid Y over X).
2. Affinoid perfectoid objects: Spa(S, S⁺) ↦ Spa(S♭, S♭⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting); finite étale objects over affinoids correspond by P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence.
3. Coverings: |Y| ≅ |Y♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets, glued), compatibly with the projections, so joint surjectivity is preserved; fibre products are preserved by the slice equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products).
4. Topoi: an equivalence of sites preserving and reflecting coverings induces an equivalence of sheaf categories (Mathlib `Equivalence.sheafCongr`).
5. O⁺/ϖ: on affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(S, S⁺), S⁺/ϖ = S♭⁺/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting, ECD Lemma 3.11), compatibly with rational restriction and finite étale base change; sheafify.

*Acceptance.*
- The site isomorphism is compatible with the homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭| (open subspaces correspond to open subspaces).
- For X = Spa(ℚ_p^cycl), X_ét ≃ X♭_ét recovers Fontaine–Wintenberger (P3/fontaine-wintenberger) on the finite étale part.
- Non-example: tilting is not a morphism of ringed sites (O_X and O_{X♭} are not identified; only O⁺/ϖ is).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity — first half of ECD 6.3; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits — tilting preserves affinoid perfectoid objects and commutes with base change; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison — Y^◇_ét is computed on tilts; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — X_∞,ét ≅ X_∞♭,ét.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Equivalence.sheafCongr`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.3, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, Theorem 7.12, p. 43; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §3, Corollary 3.20, p. 19; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §3.6, Remark 3.6.23, p. 99; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, before Corollary 7.5.3, p. 55.

#### `etale-almost-acyclicity` — Almost acyclicity of O⁺ and acyclicity of O on the étale site of an affinoid perfectoid space

*theorem* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Site`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space (R perfectoid Tate, no base field) with étale site X_ét, and write H^i(X_ét, −) for sheaf cohomology of abelian sheaves on X_ét (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`). Then: (a) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is almost zero (killed by R°°) for i > 0; (b) H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0; (c) for every finite covering {U_j → U} in X_ét of an affinoid perfectoid object U by affinoid perfectoid objects, the augmented Čech complex of O⁺ is almost exact and that of O is exact; (d) H⁰(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ)^a = (R⁺/ϖ)^a and H^i(X_ét, O⁺/ϖ) is almost zero for i > 0; (e) for every finitely generated projective R-module M, H^i(X_ét, M ⊗_R O) = 0 for i > 0. The same holds on the analytic site (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity) and for every affinoid perfectoid object of X_ét.

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X affinoid perfectoid; almost zero = killed by every pseudouniformiser (ECD Definition 3.21).

*Proof outline.*
1. Reduction to Čech complexes: the affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis of X_ét stable under fibre products (P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space); by the Čech-to-derived comparison on an acyclic basis (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison; its almost version PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology) and the covering reduction of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.21), it suffices to show (c) for rational coverings and for single surjective finite étale maps Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺).
2. Rational coverings: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity for O⁺, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy (c) for O.
3. Surjective finite étale R → S: S is faithfully flat and finite étale; the n-fold fibre products are Spa of S^{⊗_R n} with plus rings whose almost versions are (S⁺a)^{⊗ n} over R⁺a (P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence: the equivalence (R°a)_afet ≃ FÉt(R) respects tensor products). The Čech complex of O⁺ is the Amitsur complex of R⁺a → S⁺a, which is almost faithfully flat (P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale (iv)), hence almost exact (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact, within PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent); the complex of O is the Amitsur complex of the faithfully flat R → S, exact (Mathlib `CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat` in degree 0; faithfully flat descent).
4. H⁰ exactly: O⁺ is a sheaf with O⁺(X) = R⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf), not merely almost.
5. (b) from (a) by inverting ϖ on the Čech complexes of finite coverings (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion), or directly from the exactness in (c).
6. (d): O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free; the long exact sequence of 0 → O⁺ → O⁺ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (multiplication by ϖ) and (a). (e): M ⊗ O is a direct summand of Oⁿ.

*Acceptance.*
- For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and O⁺(Y)^G = R⁺ (the Čech complex of the cover is the complex of inhomogeneous cochains).
- In characteristic p, H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i ≥ 1 gives, with the Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → 𝔽_p → O → O → 0, H^i(X_ét, 𝔽_p) = 0 for i ≥ 2 (used by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion).
- For X = Spa(K, O_K), K a perfectoid field, H^i(X_ét, O⁺) is the Galois cohomology H^i(Gal(K̄/K), O_{K̄}) of the discrete module O_{K̄}; it is almost zero for i > 0 because each finite Galois L/K has L°a almost finite étale and almost faithfully flat over K°a (Tate's computation, recovered from almost purity).

*Uses.* PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity — second half of ECD 6.3; DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves — almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét feeds the pro-étale computation; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — H^j(X_ét, O) = 0 in characteristic p; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors/three-descriptions-of-G-torsors — vector bundles are acyclic étale sheaves.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `P3/almost-finite-etale-equivalence`, `P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-cech-and-sheaf-cohomology`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-faithfully-flat-descent`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-amitsur-complex-exact`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, `mathlib:CommRingCat.isLimitForkPushoutSelfOfFaithfullyFlat`, `mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.3, second paragraph, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, proof of Proposition 7.13, p. 43; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §8.3, Proposition 8.3.2 (b), p. 166; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeII-ImperfectPeriodRings), §3.3, Corollary 3.3.20 (c), p. 65; Kiran S. Kedlaya (KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015), §8.2, Proposition 8.2.21 (b), p. 164; Kiran S. Kedlaya (Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017), Lecture 2, §2.9, Theorem 2.9.5, p. 73.

#### `etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity` — ECD Theorem 6.3: the tilting equivalence of étale sites and the almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét

*comparison* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/PerfectoidSpace/Etale/Site`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

(ECD Theorem 6.3, over an arbitrary perfectoid base.) Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭. (i) Tilting induces an equivalence of sites X_ét ≃ X♭_ét (and X_fét ≃ X♭_fét), functorial in X, preserving affinoid perfectoid objects, fibre products and coverings, identifying O⁺/ϖ with O⁺_{X♭}/ϖ♭, and inducing an equivalence of étale topoi (P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence). (ii) If X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, then H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺ and the R⁺-modules H^i(X_ét, O⁺) are almost zero for i > 0; moreover H⁰(X_ét, O) = R and H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0, and the sheaf U ↦ O_U(U) on X_ét is a sheaf (P3/etale-almost-acyclicity). Here X_ét is the étale site of P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space (= A1's site of the underlying adic space).

*Hypotheses and scope.*
- X perfectoid; no base field; cohomology is sheaf cohomology on X_ét.

*Proof outline.*
1. (i): P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence.
2. (ii): P3/etale-almost-acyclicity (a), (b); the sheaf property is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf via P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space.
3. The declaration bundles the two halves as ECD Theorem 6.3 and its consumers cite them.

*Acceptance.*
- For a finite étale Galois cover Y → X of affinoid perfectoids with group G, H^i(G, O_Y⁺(Y))^a = 0 for i > 0 and (O_Y⁺(Y))^G = O_X⁺(X) (a special case of the Čech statement).
- The site equivalence is compatible with the homeomorphism |X| ≅ |X♭| and, for X of characteristic p, is the identity.
- Scholze 2012 Theorem 7.12 and Proposition 7.13 (over a perfectoid field K) are the instance X over Spa(K, K°).

*Uses.* DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected — étale covers of perfectoid spaces and their tilts; DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves — almost acyclicity of O⁺ on X_ét; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/etale-site-comparison — X_ét ≃ X♭_ét; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion — tilting of the étale site of the perfectoid tower and Artin–Schreier; PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison — étale topoi of perfectoid spaces; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits — ECD Theorem 6.3; RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0 — the finite étale site.

*Prerequisites.* `P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence`, `P3/etale-almost-acyclicity`, `P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf`.

*Sources.* Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.3, p. 26; Peter Scholze (Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds), §6, Theorem 6.3, second paragraph, p. 26; Peter Scholze (sch12-perfectoid), §7, proof of Proposition 7.13, p. 43; Peter Scholze (ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020), Lecture 7, §7.5, before Corollary 7.5.3, p. 55.

Used to translate Gabber–Ramero's (t, I)-adic statements into the Tate-ring statements of the henselian comparison.
