Used for the finite rational coverings of the tilting equivalence and for the trace bound of finite étale algebras over uniform rings. Used by the spreading-out of finite étale algebras from the completed residue field. (needed by `residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`)

(needed by `perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`, `etale-descent-perfectoid`)

### Gaps

- **Representability of Hom between finite étale schemes (Gabber–Ramero Proposition 8.2.23) is not read** (`henselian-finite-etale-approximation`). The full-faithfulness half of Gabber–Ramero Proposition 5.4.54 applies the orbit comparison to the functor Z ↦ Hom_Z(Z ×_X Y₁, Z ×_X Y₂) for finite étale Y₁, Y₂ over X = Spec R[t⁻¹], which Gabber–Ramero represent by a finite étale X-scheme (their Proposition 8.2.23, not read). Equivalently: morphisms of finite étale algebras correspond to idempotents of the tensor product (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 1.2.3), and the scheme of idempotents of a finite étale algebra is finite étale over the base. Neither statement is in the pinned libraries or in a packet node; the node records the argument, and this representability is an open proof obligation of the node.
- **Detailed estimates of Elkik's noetherian approximation are recorded at the level of the source's steps** (`elkik-noetherian-henselian-approximation`). Elkik's Théorème 2 bis is decomposed along its proof (Théorème 1 for complete rings, Tougeron's Lemme 2, the conormal-bundle Lemme 3, the principal case Lemme 4, induction on the number of generators). The exponent bookkeeping (the choice of n₀, r, the auxiliary element h in Lemme 4 and the Artin–Rees constant) is transcribed from the numdam text layer, which renders hats and script letters imperfectly; a formalisation should work from the printed article (Ann. Sci. ENS 6 (1973), pp. 558–567).

Affects: nothing. Known: recorded independently as AdicEtaleGeometry/E-A1a-1 (AdicEtaleGeometry packet, PR #2930).
- PerfectoidSpaces/E22 (misprint, sch12-perfectoid, §7, Lemma 7.3(i), p. 40, arXiv:1111.4914v1): printed “Moreover, the map of underlying topological spaces |X ×Z Y | → |X| ×|Z| |Y | is surjective.” — |X ×_Y Z| → |X| ×_{|Y|} |Z|: the fibre product is taken over Y, the target of f and g. Affects: nothing. Known: recorded by the reviewed decomposition of this roadmap (REVIEW-EXT-03, item (c)).
- PerfectoidSpaces/E23 (gap, sch12-perfectoid, §1, Theorem 1.1 and the paragraph after it, p. 2, arXiv:1111.4914v1): printed “Let K be the completion of Qp (p1/p ) and let K [ be the completion ... of Fp ((t))(t1/p ); it is enough to prove that the absolute Galois groups of K and K [ are isomorphic.” — Two steps are used without comment: an algebraic extension F of ℚ_p (resp. of 𝔽_p((t))) and its completion have the same absolute Galois group (F is henselian; Krasner), and the purely inseparable extension 𝔽_p((t)) ⊆ 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) does not change the absolute Galois group. Affects: the proof. Known: recorded by the reviewed decomposition of this roadmap (REVIEW-EXT-03, item (d)).
- PerfectoidSpaces/E24 (gap, Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, Chapter 10, proof of Proposition 10.0.6, p. 120, notes dated April 23, 2017): printed “It is a classical theorem (INSERT BACKWARDS REFERENCE) that all finite étale maps Z → Spa(R, R+ ) are of the form Z = Spa(S, S + ) with R → S finite étale and S + being the integral closure of R+ in S.” — The reference is Huber's description of finite étale maps to noetherian affinoid adic spaces (Huber 1996, Example 1.6.6(ii)), i.e. AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-etale-algebra-comparison; in the general sheafy strongly sheafy setting it is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global. Affects: nothing. Known: new.

Affects: nothing. Known: new.

### Boundaries

- Owned here: the henselian finite étale comparison and its Tate-ring corollaries (including the
  henselisation of pairs, filtered colimits of henselian pairs and of finite étale algebras, which
  AdicEtaleGeometry A4 restates and should import), almost purity for perfectoid Tate rings in all
  three forms, perfectoid fields' finite extensions and Fontaine–Wintenberger, the perfectoid
  finite étale and étale morphism classes (as A1's classes), strongly étale maps, étale descent of
  finite étale maps and vector bundles, the étale site of a perfectoid space, its tilting
  equivalence, and étale almost acyclicity.
- Imported, never re-planned: almost mathematics (P0), perfectoid rings and tilting (P1), rational
  localisation, sheafiness and perfectoid spaces (P2), finite étale and étale morphisms of analytic
  adic spaces and their sites (AdicEtaleGeometry A1), traces and Kiehl gluing (AdicSpacesPartII R3),
  Čech-to-derived comparison (DiamondsAndVStacks D0), and the anchor's adic geometry.
- Not in this stage: ECD 6.4 (P5 for (o)–(iii), AdicEtaleGeometry A3 for (iv)); pro-étale maps (P6);
  v-descent of étale maps (DiamondsAndVStacks D3); the comparison Y^◇_ét ≃ Y_ét (DiamondsAndVStacks
  D6); Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.7 (the characteristic-p noetherian local description of étale
  maps), which the general route does not use.

### Acceptance tests for the stage

1. For every perfectoid Tate ring R (in particular ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and the non-field ring of ECD
   Example 3.4(iv)) and every finite étale R-algebra S: S is perfectoid, S ≅ (S♭)♯, and S°a is
   almost finite étale and uniformly almost finite projective over R°a, with Tr(S°°) ⊇ R°° when S is
   faithfully flat.
2. For K = ℚ_p^cycl and L = K(p^{1/2}): L is a perfectoid field, L♭ is quadratic over K♭, L°a/K°a is
   almost finite étale although L°/K° is ramified.
3. G_{ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})} ≅ G_{𝔽_p((t))} (Scholze 2012 Theorem 1.1), with the completion and
   purely-inseparable steps supplied.
4. For a Tate ring A topologically henselian (e.g. colim of the O(U) over the rational neighbourhoods
   of a point), FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â); ℚ with the 3-adic topology fails it (non-example).
5. For a perfectoid space X: finite étale maps satisfy ECD Definition 6.2(i); X_ét ≃ X♭_ét as sites,
   compatibly with O⁺/ϖ; for affinoid perfectoid X, H⁰(X_ét, O⁺) = R⁺, H^i(X_ét, O⁺) almost zero and
   H^i(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0; in characteristic p, H^i(X_ét, 𝔽_p) = 0 for i ≥ 2 by Artin–Schreier.

<a id="p4"></a>

## P4. Morphisms and perfectoid quotients


This stage develops the elementary morphism theory of perfectoid spaces of ECD §5 (Scholze, *Étale cohomology of
diamonds*, arXiv v4, Definition 5.1 – Proposition 5.11), with Scholze's Zariski closed embeddings (torsion paper
§II.2) and the integral perfectoid criteria that recognise perfectoid Tate rings from integral models. Everything is
stated for perfectoid spaces in the sense of ECD Definition 3.19 (`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`: adic spaces of
the anchor roadmap `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces`, locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring of either
characteristic), with **no perfectoid base field**. Morphisms, open subspaces and gluing are the anchor's (Layer 5);
fibre products, completed residue fields, rational localization and almost acyclicity are P2's; tilting is P1's.

The notions of this stage are defined through the category Perfd and the underlying spectral spaces, not through ideal
sheaves. This is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent structure: an injection (a monomorphism of
Perfd) is determined by its image as a topological space, so an immersion is an injection whose underlying map is a
locally closed embedding. Two boundaries are pinned.

- **Closed immersions are not Zariski closed immersions.** A closed immersion (ECD 5.6) is any injection with closed
  image; a Zariski closed immersion (ECD 5.7(i)) is one whose image is a vanishing locus V(I). The closure of the annulus
  {|T| = 1} in the perfectoid disc is the image of a closed immersion and is not Zariski closed, and a closed subset that
  is not stable under generalization is not the image of any immersion. The Zariski statements never extend to arbitrary
  closed subsets (`P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed`).
- **ECD Theorem 5.8 is imported.** "Zariski closed ⇒ strongly Zariski closed" (surjectivity of R → S for the universal
  perfectoid Zariski closed subspace) is `PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed`,
  proved there by surjectivity of perfectoidization. This stage proves the converse direction, from an already given
  surjective perfectoid quotient, and records the equivalence in one comparison node on which no other node of the stage
  depends. The universal Zariski closed subspace itself (Scholze Lemma II.2.2) is constructed here without using 5.8.

### Conventions

- p is a fixed prime. A *perfectoid Tate ring* is ECD Definition 3.1 (`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`);
  a *perfectoid field* is ECD Definition 3.6. Pseudouniformizers ϖ are chosen with ϖ^p | p in R° and a compatible system of
  p-power roots (`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`); ϖ-adic completions do not depend on the
  choice.
- An *affinoid perfectoid field* (K, K⁺) is a perfectoid field with an open and bounded valuation subring; X(K, K⁺) :=
  Hom(Spa(K, K⁺), X). Its points form the chain of valuation rings between K⁺ and K°, K⁺ is the closed point and K° the
  unique rank-one point.
- For x ∈ X, (K(x), K(x)⁺) is the completed residue field (`PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`); x has *rank one*
  if K(x)⁺ = K(x)°. Every point of a perfectoid space is analytic, its generalizations form a chain, and all morphisms are
  generalizing.
- *Almost* always refers to the ideal 𝔪 = ⋃ₙ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}R⁺ (`PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`); "almost surjective"
  means that the cokernel is killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}.
- For an affinoid perfectoid X = Spa(R, R⁺) and an ideal I ⊆ R, V(I) = {x : |g(x)| = 0 for g ∈ I} and U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1
  for g ∈ F}, F ⊆ I finite; V(I) = ⋂ U_F.
- Lean names live in the namespaces `PerfectoidSpace` (geometry) and `Perfectoid` (rings); `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion`,
  `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion` are distinct from the anchor's adic-space notions and are compared with them.

```text
   Zariski closed  ⊂  closed immersions  ⊂  immersions  ⊂  injections (= monomorphisms of Perfd)
        ‖ (ECD 5.8, imported from Q4;  ⇐ proved here)
   strongly Zariski closed  =  Spa of the anchor quotient pair (R/I, integral closure of R⁺) with R/I perfectoid
```

### Organisation

- P4.1 points and test objects: affinoid perfectoid fields, generalization, qcqs maps, injections (4 nodes; planet
  "Injection of perfectoid spaces").
- P4.2 integral perfectoid criteria and intersections of rational subsets (3 nodes).
- P4.3 residue-field points and the injection and isomorphism criteria, ECD 5.2–5.5 (13 nodes).
- P4.4 immersions and their comparison with the anchor (3 nodes; planet "Immersion of perfectoid spaces").
- P4.5 Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions, perfectoid quotients and tilting of surjections (13 nodes;
  planets "Zariski closed immersion", "Universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace").
- P4.6 diagonals, separatedness and the valuative criterion, ECD 5.9–5.11 (5 nodes; planets "Separated map of perfectoid
  spaces", "Valuative criterion for separatedness"), and the tilting comparison.


### P4.1 Points, test objects and injections

#### `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField` — Affinoid perfectoid fields and (K, K⁺)-valued points of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points` (definition); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FieldPoints`.

An affinoid perfectoid field is a pair (K, K⁺) of a perfectoid field K (a perfectoid Tate ring that is a nonarchimedean field, ECD Definition 3.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition) and an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K; equivalently K⁺ is a valuation subring with K°° ⊂ K⁺ ⊂ K° = O_K, so (K, K⁺) is a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) and Spa(K, K⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid space. It is algebraically closed if K is. A morphism (K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺) is a morphism of Huber pairs (a continuous field homomorphism carrying K⁺ into L⁺), also called an extension of affinoid perfectoid fields. The points of Spa(K, K⁺) are the valuation subrings V with K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°; they form a chain under inclusion, K⁺ is the unique closed point, K° is the unique rank-one point, every point is a specialization of K° and a generalization of K⁺, and the quasicompact open subsets are the Spa(K, K'⁺) for valuation subrings K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K°. For a perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) the set of (K, K⁺)-valued points is X(K, K⁺) := Hom_Perfd(Spa(K, K⁺), X); it is covariant in X, contravariant in (K, K⁺), and carries the closed-point map X(K, K⁺) → |X|. For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X(K, K⁺) is the set of morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺), and the closed-point map sends φ to spaComap φ of the closed point.

*Hypotheses.* p is a fixed prime; perfectoid fields are those of ECD Definition 3.6, of either characteristic, with no base field. K⁺ is a valuation subring. Open integrally closed subrings that are not valuation subrings (they occur in ECD Lemma 9.9) do not give affinoid perfectoid fields.

*Proof outline.*

1. Open and bounded subrings of K lie between K°° and K°: an open integrally closed subring contains every topologically nilpotent element (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`) and a bounded one consists of power-bounded elements; conversely K°° is open and K° bounded because K is a nonarchimedean field.
2. Points of Spa(K, K⁺): a continuous valuation v with v ≤ 1 on K⁺ has valuation ring V ⊇ K⁺; if x ∈ V had |x|_K > 1 then x⁻¹ would be topologically nilpotent, so v(x⁻¹) < 1 by continuity, contradicting v(x) ≤ 1; hence V ⊆ K°. Overrings of the valuation ring K⁺ are its localizations at primes, hence a chain. Quasicompact opens are the rational subsets {|f| ≤ 1}, f ∈ K, which are the Spa(K, K⁺[f]) (anchor Layer 2 rational subsets).
3. The description of X(K, K⁺) for affinoid X is the universal property of affinoid adic spaces (morphisms W → Spa(R, R⁺) are the morphisms of Huber pairs (R, R⁺) → (O_W(W), O_W⁺(W)); requested from the anchor, Layer 5) applied to W = Spa(K, K⁺), with O(W) = K and O⁺(W) = K⁺.

*Uses.* ECD Proposition 5.3 (ii), Lemma 5.4 (iii)-(iv), Proposition 5.11 (iii): the injection, isomorphism and separatedness criteria are tests on (K, K⁺)-valued points; Berkeley Lectures Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 and Proposition 17.4.4: injectivity is tested on algebraically closed affinoid fields (C, C⁺); the valuative criterion for v-sheaves; DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks, D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves: the isomorphism criteria for diamonds and v-stacks reduce to (K, K⁺)-points of qcqs perfectoid spaces; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness: the valuative criterion for v-stacks uses the same lifting problems Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺); ECD Proposition 1.15 and Lemma 7.19: connected components of totally disconnected spaces are Spa(K, K⁺); rank-one points are Spa(C, O_C).

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField` (structure): A perfectoid field K together with an open and bounded valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.toPair` (coercion): The underlying Tau Ceti Huber pair (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.ofRankOne` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid field (K, K°).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.spa` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid space Spa(K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.closedPoint` (data): The point K⁺ of |Spa(K, K⁺)|, its unique closed point; every point specializes to it.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.mem_spa_iff` (characterisation): Points of Spa(K, K⁺) correspond to valuation subrings V with K⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K°; they form a chain with maximum K°, the unique rank-one point.
- `PerfectoidSpace.AffinoidField.isOpen_iff` (characterisation): The quasicompact open subsets of Spa(K, K⁺) are the Spa(K, K'⁺) with K⁺ ⊆ K'⁺ ⊆ K° a valuation subring; every open subset is a union of these.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints` (data): X(K, K⁺) := Hom(Spa(K, K⁺), X) for a perfectoid space X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.map` (functoriality): A morphism f : Y → X induces f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺); map_id and map_comp hold.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.restrict` (functoriality): An extension (K, K⁺) → (L, L⁺) induces X(K, K⁺) → X(L, L⁺), natural in X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints.closedPointImage` (projection): The natural map X(K, K⁺) → |X| sending a point to the image of the closed point.
- `PerfectoidSpace.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv` (universal-property): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, X(K, K⁺) ≃ Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺).

*Unit tests.*

- `AffinoidField.subsingleton_spa_ofRankOne` (computation): For every perfectoid field K, |Spa(K, K°)| has exactly one point.
- `AffinoidField.card_spa_eq_two` (computation): If K⁺ ⊊ K° is the preimage of a rank-one valuation ring k⁺ ⊊ k of the residue field k = K°/K°°, then |Spa(K, K⁺)| has exactly two points and only K⁺ is closed.
- `AffinoidField.fieldPoints_affinoidEquiv_closedPoint` (compatibility): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) = Huber.Pair.Hom (R, R⁺) (K, K⁺), the closed-point image of φ is Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap φ` applied to the closed point of Spa(K, K⁺).
- `AffinoidField.not_padic` (non-example): (ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is not an affinoid perfectoid field, because ℚ_p is not perfectoid (ECD Remark 3.3).
- `AffinoidField.not_of_intersection` (non-example): If the residue field k of a perfectoid field K has incomparable nontrivial valuation rings k₁⁺, k₂⁺, the preimage K⁺ of k₁⁺ ∩ k₂⁺ is open, bounded and integrally closed but not a valuation subring, and Spa(K, K⁺) has at least two closed points.

*Acceptance.* Spa(K, K°) is a single point, and for X affinoid perfectoid X(K, K°) is the set of continuous ring maps R → K with R⁺ → K°. If K⁺ has rank two, Spa(K, K⁺) has exactly two points: the open rank-one point K° and the closed point K⁺.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `ValuationSubring`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.3 (ii), p. 21 (arXiv v4); ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (2)-(3), p. 61.

#### Morphisms of perfectoid spaces are generalizing and spectral

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Generalizing`.

Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces (more generally of analytic adic spaces). Then the continuous map |f| : |Y| → |X| is generalizing (Mathlib `GeneralizingMap`: for y ∈ Y and a generalization x' of f(y) there is a generalization y' of y with f(y') = x'), and it is spectral on spectral opens (for open affinoids V ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, V → U is a spectral map, Mathlib `IsSpectralMap`). Consequently the image of every morphism, and of every quasicompact open under a morphism, is stable under generalization, and the image of a quasicompact open is pro-constructible in any spectral open containing it.

*Hypotheses.* X and Y are perfectoid spaces, so every point is analytic (every point of Spa of a Tate ring is analytic, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isAnalyticPoint_of_isTateRing`).

*Proof outline.*

1. Generalizations of an analytic point: for y ∈ Spa(B, B⁺) with B Tate, the generalizations of y form a chain in bijection with the valuation subrings V of the completed residue field with K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° (vertical generalization; horizontal generalizations do not occur at analytic points). This description is requested from the anchor, Layer 2.
2. Lifting: with x = f(y), the field map K(x) → K(y) satisfies K(y)⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and K(y)° ∩ K(x) = K(x)°. A generalization x' of x is a valuation ring V' with K(x)⁺ ⊆ V' ⊆ K(x)°; it is the localization of K(x)⁺ at a prime 𝔭. The extension K(x)⁺ ⊆ K(y)⁺ of valuation rings is local, so Spec K(y)⁺ → Spec K(x)⁺ is a surjective order-preserving map of chains; let 𝔮 be the largest prime over 𝔭. It contains 𝔪(K(y)°), which lies over 𝔪(K(x)°) ⊆ 𝔭, so V := K(y)⁺_𝔮 satisfies K(y)⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ K(y)° and V ∩ K(x) = V'. The point y' given by V is the required lift.
3. Spectrality: the preimage of a rational subset under a morphism of affinoid adic spaces is rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`), and quasicompact opens of an affinoid are finite unions of rational subsets; for spectral (qcqs) opens cover by finitely many affinoids.
4. Images: a generalizing map has generalization-stable image; the image of a pro-constructible subset under a spectral map of spectral spaces is pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets).

*Acceptance.* The inclusion of a rational subset U ⊆ X is generalizing: U is open, hence stable under generalization. For the map Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, K⁺) induced by an extension of perfectoid fields, the image is the rank-one point, which is stable under generalization but not closed when K⁺ ≠ K°.

*Dependencies.* `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.
 Library: `GeneralizingMap`, `IsSpectralMap`, `StableUnderGeneralization`, `ValuationSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isAnalyticPoint_of_isTateRing`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §2, sentence before Lemma 2.5, p. 11; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Corollary 5.5, p. 24.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact` — Quasicompact and quasiseparated morphisms of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps` (definition); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/QuasiCompact`.

A perfectoid space X is quasicompact (resp. quasiseparated) if |X| is quasicompact (resp. a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`). A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is quasicompact if f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every quasicompact open U ⊆ |X|, equivalently for every open affinoid U ⊆ X; it is quasiseparated if the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal` in the category of perfectoid spaces, whose fibre products are PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is quasicompact; qcqs means both. Equivalently, f is quasiseparated if and only if for every open affinoid U ⊆ X and all open affinoids V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) the intersection V ∩ W is quasicompact; if X is affinoid (or quasiseparated), f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is quasiseparated. By ECD Proposition 8.3 these agree with the topos-theoretic notions of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos for the sheaves represented by perfectoid spaces.

*Hypotheses.* Fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), and open affinoids of a fibre product V ×_U W are the affinoid perfectoid spaces given by the P2 affinoid formula.

*Proof outline.*

1. Quasicompactness is local on the target and testable on affinoids because affinoids form a basis of quasicompact opens stable under finite intersection inside an affinoid (rational subsets, anchor Layer 2).
2. Diagonal criterion: the open subsets V ×_U W (V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U) affinoid, U ⊆ X affinoid) cover Y ×_X Y and are affinoid; Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_U W) = V ∩ W; so Δ_f is quasicompact if and only if all V ∩ W are quasicompact.
3. If X is quasiseparated the same criterion shows that f is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is.

*Uses.* ECD Lemma 5.4: the isomorphism criterion is stated for qcqs morphisms; ECD Proposition 5.11 (iii): the valuative criterion assumes f quasiseparated; ECD Lemma 11.11 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks: qcqs maps of diamonds are tested against qcqs perfectoid spaces; PerfectoidSpaces:P5 (ECD Proposition 6.4): finite-stage descent is stated for qcqs étale objects; DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base: quasicompact separated maps to a strictly totally disconnected base.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact` (structure): f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every quasicompact open U ⊆ |X|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated` (structure): The diagonal Δ_f is quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiCompact_iff_affinoid` (characterisation): f is quasicompact iff f⁻¹(U) is quasicompact for every open affinoid U ⊆ X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiSeparated_iff_affinoid_inter` (characterisation): f is quasiseparated iff V ∩ W is quasicompact for all open affinoids V, W ⊆ f⁻¹(U), U ⊆ X open affinoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace` (compatibility): For X quasiseparated, f is quasiseparated iff |Y| is a Mathlib QuasiSeparatedSpace.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact.comp` (structure): Composites of quasicompact morphisms are quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated.comp` (structure): Composites of quasiseparated morphisms are quasiseparated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiCompact.baseChange` (functoriality): The base change of a quasicompact morphism along any morphism is quasicompact.
- `PerfectoidSpace.QuasiSeparated.baseChange` (functoriality): The base change of a quasiseparated morphism along any morphism is quasiseparated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.quasiCompact_of_affinoid` (instance): Morphisms between affinoid perfectoid spaces are quasicompact and quasiseparated.

*Unit tests.*

- `quasiCompact_affinoid` (computation): Every morphism Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces is quasicompact and quasiseparated.
- `not_quasiCompact_openDisc` (non-example): The open immersion of the open unit disc ⋃_n {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|} into Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is not quasicompact (the preimage of the whole disc is not quasicompact).
- `quasiSeparated_id` (degenerate): The identity of any perfectoid space is qcqs.
- `quasiSeparated_iff_quasiSeparatedSpace` (compatibility): For X affinoid, f : Y → X is quasiseparated if and only if |Y| is a Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`.

*Acceptance.* Every morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is qcqs. The inclusion of the open unit disc (the union of the rational subsets {|T|^n ≤ |ϖ|}) into the perfectoid closed unit disc is quasiseparated but not quasicompact.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.
 Library: `CompactSpace`, `QuasiSeparatedSpace`, `IsQuasiSeparated`, `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, remark after Proposition 5.11, p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §8, Proposition 8.3, p. 41.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection` — Injections of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces` (definition); planet “Injection of perfectoid spaces”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Injection`.

A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if for every perfectoid space Z the map f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective (ECD Definition 5.1). It suffices to test affinoid perfectoid Z, because two morphisms Z → Y that agree on an open affinoid cover of Z agree. In the category Perfd of perfectoid spaces this says exactly that f is a monomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Mono`), and, fibre products existing in Perfd (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), it is equivalent to the diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y being an isomorphism (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`). Injections are not determined by |f| being injective: the characterisations on points, residue fields and underlying spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria.

*Hypotheses.* Perfectoid spaces are those of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (ECD Definition 3.19): adic spaces of the anchor, locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring; Perfd is a full subcategory of the anchor's adic spaces.

*Proof outline.*

1. Reduction to affinoid Z: morphisms of adic spaces are determined locally on the source (anchor Layer 5 gluing).
2. Mono ⇔ Δ_f iso is Mathlib `pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff` applied in Perfd, which has pullbacks by P2.

*Uses.* ECD Example 5.2: the residue-field points i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X are injections; ECD Definition 5.6: immersions are injections whose underlying map is a locally closed immersion; ECD Proposition 11.3 / Berkeley Proposition 8.3.4: an equivalence relation R → X × X is an injection; ECD Lemma 7.19, Lemma 9.9: maps over (strictly) totally disconnected bases and compactifications of étale maps are shown to be injections before being identified; DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness and D4 isomorphism criteria: injections of v-sheaves restrict to injections of perfectoid spaces.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection` (structure): f_* : Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) is injective for every perfectoid space Z.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isInjection_iff_mono` (compatibility): IsInjection f ↔ Mono f in Perfd.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_affinoid` (constructor): If f_* is injective on Hom(Z, −) for every affinoid perfectoid Z, then f is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isInjection_iff_isIso_diagonal` (characterisation): f is an injection iff Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an isomorphism.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.id` (instance): Identities, and more generally isomorphisms, are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.comp` (structure): Composites of injections are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_comp` (other): If g ∘ f is an injection then f is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.of_isSplitMono` (instance): Split monomorphisms (for instance sections and diagonals) are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.fieldPoints_injective` (relation): An injection induces injective maps Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsInjection.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes of injections are injections (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition).

*Unit tests.*

- `isInjection_rationalOpen` (computation): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and U ⊆ X rational, the open immersion U → X is an injection.
- `isInjection_diagonal` (degenerate): For every morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces, Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an injection.
- `not_isInjection_quadraticExtension` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K and a separable quadratic extension L/K (L is perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields), Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is bijective on underlying spaces but not an injection: the two K-embeddings of L into a completed algebraic closure C give distinct (C, O_C)-points with the same image.
- `isInjection_iff_mono` (compatibility): IsInjection f ↔ CategoryTheory.Mono f in the category of perfectoid spaces.

*Acceptance.* Rational open immersions U ⊆ Spa(R, R⁺) are injections (universal property of rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`). Diagonals are injections, being split monomorphisms (Mathlib instance `IsSplitMono (pullback.diagonal f)`).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.
 Library: `CategoryTheory.Mono`, `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`, `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`, `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.isIso_diagonal_iff`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.1 and following sentence, p. 21; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Definition/Proposition 8.3.3, p. 61.


### P4.2 Integral perfectoid criteria and intersections of rational subsets

#### Almost integral perfectoid criterion: a ϖ-complete ring with almost bijective Frobenius gives a perfectoid Tate ring

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/IntegralCriterion`.

Let A⁺ be a ring and ϖ ∈ A⁺ a non-zero-divisor such that (i) ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/pⁿ} ∈ A⁺ and ϖ^p divides p in A⁺; (ii) A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete and separated; (iii) the Frobenius Φ : A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ, x ↦ x^p, is an almost isomorphism for the basic setup (A⁺, 𝔪) with 𝔪 = ⋃ₙ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup): its kernel and cokernel are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Let A := A⁺[1/ϖ], topologized so that A⁺ is open with the ϖ-adic topology. Then A is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 with pseudouniformizer ϖ; its power-bounded subring is A° = A⁺_* := {x ∈ A : ϖ^{1/pⁿ}x ∈ A⁺ for all n}; A⁺ ⊆ A° and A°/A⁺ is almost zero; the integral closure of A⁺ in A is a ring of integral elements; and Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is an isomorphism. This is the Tate-ring form of Sch12 Lemma 5.6 (stated there over a perfectoid field K for perfectoid K°ᵃ-algebras).

*Hypotheses.* No base field: A⁺ is an arbitrary ring; in characteristic p the condition ϖ^p | p is vacuous. Almost mathematics is taken for the idempotent ideal 𝔪 = ⋃ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}A⁺ (flat because ϖ is a non-zero-divisor).

*Proof outline.*

1. A⁺_* = (A⁺ᵃ)_* is the module of almost elements; for the ϖ-torsion-free A⁺ it is {x ∈ A : εx ∈ A⁺ for all ε ∈ 𝔪}, ϖ-torsion free, ϖ-adically complete, and almost equal to A⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base, P0/almost-inversion-and-completion; Sch12 Lemma 5.3(ii),(iv)).
2. Φ : A⁺_*/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺_*/ϖ is injective: if x ∈ A⁺_* and x^p ∈ ϖA⁺_*, almost injectivity gives ε^{1/p}x ∈ ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* for all ε ∈ 𝔪, so x ∈ (ϖ^{1/p}A⁺)_* = ϖ^{1/p}A⁺_* (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).
3. If x ∈ A and x^p ∈ A⁺_* then x ∈ A⁺_* (Sch12 Lemma 5.7): with y = ϖ^{k/p}x ∈ A⁺_*, injectivity of Φ lowers k by one while k ≥ 1, using that A⁺_* has no ϖ-torsion.
4. A° = A⁺_*: elements of A⁺_* are power-bounded; if x is power-bounded then εx is topologically nilpotent for ε ∈ 𝔪, so (εx)^{p^N} ∈ A⁺_* for large N, hence εx ∈ A⁺_* by the previous step, for all ε; hence x ∈ A⁺_*. In particular A° ⊆ ϖ⁻¹A⁺ is bounded, so A is uniform, complete and Tate with pseudouniformizer ϖ.
5. Φ : A°/ϖ^{1/p} → A°/ϖ is surjective: it is almost surjective, so for x ∈ A° there is y ∈ A° with ϖ^{1/p}x ≡ y^p mod ϖA°; z := y/ϖ^{1/p²} has z^p ∈ A° and x ≡ z^p mod ϖ^{(p−1)/p}A°, hence z ∈ A° by the root lemma, and the residual error lies in 𝔪A°, which gives surjectivity modulo ϖ (Sch12 proof of Lemma 5.6).
6. ϖ^p divides p in A°, and Φ is an isomorphism A°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A°/ϖ; replacing ϖ by ϖ^{1/p} is harmless, so A satisfies ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). The integral closure of A⁺ is open (it contains A⁺) and contained in A° (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`).

*Acceptance.* For a perfectoid field C with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting p-power roots and A⁺ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective, and A = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid with A° = A⁺. Non-example: for A⁺ = O_C⟨T⟩ Frobenius modulo ϖ^{1/p} is not almost surjective (no element ϖ^εT is a p-th power modulo ϖ), and C⟨T⟩ is not perfectoid. The ϖ-adic completion of a filtered colimit of rings of integral elements of perfectoid pairs satisfies the hypotheses (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/root-ideal-basic-setup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary`.
 Library: `IsAdicComplete`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure`.

*Sources.* sch12-perfectoid, §5, Lemma 5.6, p. 23 (arXiv v1); sch12-perfectoid, §5, Definition 5.1 (ii), p. 21; sch12-perfectoid, §5, Lemma 5.7, p. 23; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, statement of Lemma II.2.2, p. 13.

#### Integral perfectoid criterion: integral perfectoid rings give perfectoid Tate rings (compatible-root annuli)

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/integral-perfectoid-criterion-for-annuli` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/IntegralCriterion`.

Let R₀ be a ring and π ∈ R₀ a non-zero-divisor with π^p | p such that R₀ is π-adically complete, and suppose that R₀ is an integral perfectoid ring (BMS1 Definition 3.5, PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings) — for instance because Frobenius R₀/π → R₀/π^p is an isomorphism (BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii)). Then R := R₀[1/π], with the π-adic topology on R₀, is a complete Tate ring that is perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1), R₀ ⊆ R°, πR° ⊆ R₀, and after replacing π by a unit multiple admitting compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9) the cokernel R°/R₀ is killed by every π^{1/pⁿ}. The criterion is about the pair (R₀, π): it is never inferred from the name of an integral model. Application (compatible-root period annuli): for a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots and a ∈ ℤ[1/p]_{>0}, the ϖ-adic completion A⁺ of R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) satisfies the hypotheses (it is free over R° on the monomials T^α, S^β modulo the relations, and Frobenius is bijective from A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} to A⁺/ϖ on that basis; for a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊊ R° in place of R° it is almost bijective and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion applies), so the annulus ring A⁺[1/ϖ] = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}, (ϖ^a/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ is perfectoid; the same holds after base change of an annulus along a compatible-root extension, which is how perfectoidness of the chart cover of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 is checked. Without the roots of T the Frobenius criterion fails and R⟨T, ϖ^a/T⟩ is not perfectoid.

*Hypotheses.* π is a non-zero-divisor; without this the localization loses information and the conclusion fails. Integral perfectoid is the BMS1 notion (π-adically complete for some π with π^p | p, Frobenius surjective on R₀/p, ker θ principal), owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; its comparison with rings of integral elements of perfectoid Tate rings (BMS1 Lemma 3.20) is PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison.

*Proof outline.*

1. BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i),(ii) (inside PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison): an integral perfectoid R₀ has Φ : R₀/π → R₀/π^p an isomorphism, and conversely a π-torsion-free π-complete R₀ with that isomorphism is integral perfectoid.
2. Replace π by uπ, u ∈ R₀^×, with compatible p-power roots (BMS1 Lemma 3.9, 'moreover' part).
3. Apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion with A⁺ = R₀ and ϖ = π: Frobenius is bijective, a fortiori almost bijective; this gives R perfectoid, R° = (R₀)_* and R°/R₀ almost zero; since π·(R₀)_* ⊆ R₀ one gets πR° ⊆ R₀ (BMS1 Lemma 3.21, whose proof is 'as in Sch12 Lemma 5.6').
4. Annuli: R°[T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}]/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{a/pⁿ}) is a free R°-module on the monomials T^α (α ≥ 0) and S^β (β > 0) in ℤ[1/p], hence ϖ-torsion free; Frobenius sends c·T^α to c^p·T^{pα}, and R°/ϖ^{1/p} → R°/ϖ is bijective (ECD Definition 3.1 and Remark 3.2 for the pseudouniformizer ϖ^{1/p}), so Frobenius A⁺/ϖ^{1/p} → A⁺/ϖ is bijective.

*Acceptance.* Perfectoid annulus: for C a perfectoid field and a = 1, R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T^{1/pⁿ}S^{1/pⁿ} − ϖ^{1/pⁿ}) gives the perfectoid ring of the annulus |ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1, which is the rational localization C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨(ϖ/T)^{1/p^∞}⟩ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids). BMS1 Example 3.6: ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is integral perfectoid, and ℚ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ = ℤ_p^cycl⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩[1/p] is perfectoid (ECD Example 3.4(iii)). Non-example: R₀ = O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) has compatible roots of T, but Φ : R₀/ϖ^{1/p} → R₀/ϖ kills the nonzero class of T^{1/p}; R₀[1/ϖ] = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T) is not reduced, hence not perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-examples`.
 Library: `IsAdicComplete`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

*Sources.* BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, §3.2, Lemma 3.21, p. 27 (arXiv v3); BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, §3.2, Lemma 3.21 and proof, p. 27; BMS-IntegralPadicHodge-2018, §3.2, Lemma 3.10 (ii), p. 22; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Example 2.4.9.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace` — The perfectoid space attached to a filtered intersection of rational subsets

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets` (construction); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProRational`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space, ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformizer with ϖ^p | p admitting compatible p-power roots (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots), and 𝒰 a nonempty family of rational subsets of X that is filtered (for U, V ∈ 𝒰 some W ∈ 𝒰 lies in U ∩ V); put T := ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U ⊆ |X|. Let S⁺_𝒰 be the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U) and S_𝒰 := S⁺_𝒰[1/ϖ], topologized by the ϖ-adic topology on S⁺_𝒰, and let ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 := Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) → X be induced by the compatible maps O_X(U) → S_𝒰. Then: (a) S_𝒰 is a perfectoid Tate ring, S⁺_𝒰 is a ring of integral elements, S⁺_𝒰 ⊆ S_𝒰° with almost zero cokernel, S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ = colim_U O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ, and each O_X(U) → S_𝒰 has dense image; (b) |ι_𝒰| is a homeomorphism of |Z_𝒰| onto T with its subspace topology, and T is pro-constructible and stable under generalization; (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_𝒰 if and only if |g|(|W|) ⊆ T, and then uniquely; in particular ι_𝒰 is an injection and Z_𝒰 is the limit of the U ∈ 𝒰 in the category of perfectoid spaces; (d) Z_𝒰 depends, up to unique isomorphism over X, only on the subset T. The residue-field points of ECD Example 5.2 and the universal Zariski closed subspaces of Scholze's torsion paper Lemma II.2.2 are the cases 𝒰 = {rational neighbourhoods of x} and 𝒰 = {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}.

*Hypotheses.* X affinoid perfectoid; the family 𝒰 consists of rational subsets and is filtered; no base field. Completions are ϖ-adic; they do not depend on the choice of ϖ among pseudouniformizers of R.

*Proof outline.*

1. Valuative description of the colimit: s ∈ O_X(U₀) (U₀ ∈ 𝒰) has image in colim O⁺ iff |s| ≤ 1 on T. Indeed {x ∈ U₀ : |s(x)| ≤ 1} is a rational subset, O⁺_X(U) = {f : |f| ≤ 1 on U} (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one` on O(U)), and by compactness of the constructible topology (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets) T ⊆ V for a quasicompact open V forces some U ∈ 𝒰 to lie in V.
2. Frobenius: each (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is a perfectoid pair (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so Φ : O⁺(U)/ϖ^{1/p} → O⁺(U)/ϖ is an almost isomorphism (bijective on O(U)°, and O(U)°/O⁺(U) is almost zero, ECD Example 3.22(ii), PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup). Filtered colimits and ϖ-adic completion preserve almost isomorphisms modulo ϖ, ϖ-torsion freeness and ϖ^p | p; apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/almost-integral-perfectoid-criterion to A⁺ = S⁺_𝒰.
3. Points: a point z of Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰) restricts to each O(U) with |O⁺(U)| ≤ 1, hence (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`) to a point of every U, so to a point of T; conversely a point x ∈ T defines compatible continuous valuations on the O(U), bounded by 1 on colim O⁺(U), which extend continuously to the completion. The resulting continuous bijection |Z_𝒰| → T is spectral and generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), T is spectral as a pro-constructible subset (anchor Layer 1.3), so it is a homeomorphism (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient).
4. Ring of integral elements: S⁺_𝒰 is open; if s ∈ S_𝒰 is integral over S⁺_𝒰 then |s| ≤ 1 on Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰); approximating s modulo ϖS⁺_𝒰 by s₀ in the image of some O(U) gives |s₀| ≤ 1 on T, so s₀, and then s, lies in S⁺_𝒰 by the valuative description.
5. Universal property: for W = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid with |g| ⊆ T, g factors uniquely through every U ∈ 𝒰 (rational localization, Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`), the compatible maps O⁺(U) → A⁺ extend uniquely to S⁺_𝒰 because A⁺ is ϖ-adically complete; general W by gluing (anchor Layer 5). Uniqueness makes ι_𝒰 an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Hom(W, Z_𝒰) = lim Hom(W, U).
6. Independence: the universal property depends only on T.

*Uses.* ECD Example 5.2: the completed residue field point is the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods; Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.2 and ECD Remark 7.9: a Zariski closed subset is the limit of the rational subsets {|f₁|, …, |f_k| ≤ 1}, f_i ∈ I; ECD Lemma 7.6 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid: pro-constructible generalizing subsets of totally disconnected spaces are intersections of {|f| ≤ 1}; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: the special case of a cofiltered system of rational open immersions into a fixed affinoid; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed: the closure of an annulus is the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski closed.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace` (constructor): The affinoid perfectoid space Z_𝒰 = Spa(S_𝒰, S⁺_𝒰).
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.ι` (data): The morphism ι_𝒰 : Z_𝒰 → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.plus_mod_pow` (simp): S⁺_𝒰/ϖⁿ ≅ colim_{U∈𝒰} O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ for every n.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.range_ι` (characterisation): |ι_𝒰| is a homeomorphism onto ⋂_{U∈𝒰} U with the subspace topology.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.lift` (universal-property): For g : W → X with |g| ⊆ ⋂𝒰, the unique lift W → Z_𝒰; lift_ι and lift_unique.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isInjection` (other): ι_𝒰 is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isLimit` (universal-property): Z_𝒰 with the maps to the U ∈ 𝒰 is a limit cone in Perfd.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.congr` (extensionality): If ⋂𝒰 = ⋂𝒱 then Z_𝒰 ≅ Z_𝒱 uniquely over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.isPerfectoid` (instance): S_𝒰 is a perfectoid Tate ring and S⁺_𝒰 a ring of integral elements.
- `PerfectoidSpace.proRationalSubspace.denseRange` (other): O_X(U) → S_𝒰 has dense image for U ∈ 𝒰.

*Unit tests.*

- `proRationalSubspace_singleton` (degenerate): For 𝒰 = {U}, ι_𝒰 is isomorphic over X to U → X.
- `proRationalSubspace_rationalNhds` (compatibility): For 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x ∈ X, Z_𝒰 ≅ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) over X, compatibly with PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection.
- `proRationalSubspace_annulusClosure` (computation): For X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) and 𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|} : n ≥ 0}: S_𝒰 = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and S⁺_𝒰 is the ϖ-adic completion of O_C[T^{1/p^∞}] + 𝔪_C[T^{−1/p^∞}]; T is the annulus {|T| = 1} together with the rank-two point y with |T(y)| = 1⁻.
- `proRationalSubspace_empty` (degenerate): If ⋂𝒰 = ∅ then S_𝒰 = 0.
- `proRationalSubspace_not_open` (non-example): For 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of the Gauss point η of the perfectoid disc, T = {η} is not open, so ι_𝒰 is an injection that is not an open immersion.

*Acceptance.* 𝒰 = {U}: Z_𝒰 = U. 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of a point x: Z_𝒰 = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (ECD Example 5.2). If T = ∅ then S_𝒰 = 0 and Z_𝒰 is empty.

### P4.3 Residue-field points; injection and isomorphism criteria

#### `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint` — The completed residue field point i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection` (construction); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FieldPoints`.

For a perfectoid space X and a point x ∈ X, the completed residue field K(x) with its open and bounded valuation subring K(x)⁺ is an affinoid perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), and there is a canonical morphism i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X sending the closed point to x: on an affinoid perfectoid neighbourhood U = Spa(R, R⁺) of x it is given by (R, R⁺) → (K(x), K(x)⁺), independently of U. Moreover (ECD Example 5.2): (a) i_x is isomorphic over U to the pro-rational subspace ι_𝒰 for 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x in U (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets), so K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V) and K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ; (b) i_x is an injection and |i_x| is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of x; (c) every (K, K⁺)-valued point φ of X whose closed point maps to x factors uniquely as φ = i_x ∘ φ' with φ' : Spa(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) given by a morphism of affinoid perfectoid fields; (d) for f : Y → X and y ∈ Y with f(y) = x, f ∘ i_y = i_x ∘ Spa(K(x) → K(y)).

*Hypotheses.* X is a perfectoid space; x is any point (not necessarily of rank one).

*Proof outline.*

1. Independence of U: two affinoid neighbourhoods contain a common rational neighbourhood, and restriction maps are compatible with the maps to K(x) (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields).
2. (a),(b): the intersection of the rational neighbourhoods of x is the set of generalizations of x (in a spectral space the generalizations of x are the intersection of its quasicompact open neighbourhoods); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets, whose ring S⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim O⁺(V), which is K(x)⁺ (ECD Example 5.2).
3. (c): φ maps |Spa(K, K⁺)| into the generalizations of x (the closed point goes to x, every point of Spa(K, K⁺) generalizes the closed point, and continuous maps preserve specialization), so it factors uniquely through i_x by the universal property of (a); the factorization is a morphism (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) because both are affinoid.
4. (d) follows from the construction of completed residue fields and uniqueness in (c).

*Uses.* ECD Proposition 5.3, proof of (ii) ⇒ (iii) and (iii) ⇒ (iv): base change along i_x reduces to X = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺); ECD Lemma 5.4, proof of (ii) ⇔ (iii): every (K, K⁺)-point factors over the immersion i_x; ECD Proposition 5.11, proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii): specializations are witnessed by injections Spa(K, K⁺) → Y ×_X Y; ECD Lemma 7.3 and Proposition 1.15: connected components of totally disconnected spaces are Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺); PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field: (K, K⁺)-points are determined by their closed point and a map of residue fields.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint` (constructor): The morphism i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (simp): i_x maps the closed point to x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_isInjection` (other): i_x is an injection.
- `PerfectoidSpace.range_residueFieldPoint` (characterisation): |i_x| is a homeomorphism onto the set of generalizations of x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_factor` (universal-property): A (K, K⁺)-point with closed point x factors uniquely through i_x via a morphism (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_naturality` (functoriality): f ∘ i_y = i_{f(y)} ∘ Spa(K(f(y)) → K(y)) for f : Y → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_plus_mod` (simp): K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{V∋x} O⁺_X(V)/ϖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` (compatibility): i_x is the pro-rational subspace of the rational neighbourhoods of x.
- `PerfectoidSpace.residueFieldPoint_isRankOne_iff` (characterisation): x is a rank-one point iff K(x)⁺ = K(x)° iff |Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| is a single point.

*Unit tests.*

- `residueFieldPoint_closedPoint` (degenerate): For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x the closed point, i_x is the identity of X.
- `residueFieldPoint_gauss` (computation): For the Gauss point η of Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), K(η) is the completion of C(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm and K(η)⁺ = K(η)°; |i_η| has image {η}.
- `residueFieldPoint_not_isOpenImmersion` (non-example): i_η is an injection whose image {η} is not open (and not locally closed), so i_η is not an immersion.
- `residueFieldPoint_eq_proRationalSubspace` (compatibility): i_x is isomorphic over X to ι_𝒰 for 𝒰 the rational neighbourhoods of x in an affinoid neighbourhood.

*Acceptance.* For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x its closed point, i_x is the identity. For the Gauss point η of the perfectoid closed unit disc over a perfectoid field C, K(η) is the completion of C(T^{1/p^∞}) for the Gauss norm and K(η)⁺ = K(η)°.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Example 5.2, p. 21; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Example 5.2, p. 21.

#### A qcqs perfectoid space with a unique closed point is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FieldPoints`.

Let X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated perfectoid space with a unique closed point x. Then i_x : Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → X is an isomorphism; in particular X is affinoid, O_X(X) = K(x) and O⁺_X(X) = K(x)⁺.

*Hypotheses.* X qcqs (|X| is then a spectral space, being quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally spectral).

*Proof outline.*

1. In the spectral space |X| every point specializes to a closed point, which is x; so every open neighbourhood of x is all of X.
2. An affinoid open neighbourhood U of x therefore equals X, so X = Spa(R, R⁺) is affinoid, and every rational neighbourhood of x is X.
3. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (a), K(x)⁺ is the ϖ-completion of colim_{V∋x} O⁺(V) = R⁺, hence K(x)⁺ = R⁺, K(x) = R and i_x is the identity.

*Acceptance.* X = Spa(K, K⁺) itself. A quasicompact open subset of Spa(K, K⁺) containing the closed point is all of Spa(K, K⁺).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space`.
 Library: `SpectralSpace`, `specializes_iff_mem_closure`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Example 5.2, last paragraph, p. 21.

#### Points of fibre products of perfectoid spaces surject onto compatible pairs

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FibreProductPoints`.

Let Y₁ → X ← Y₂ be morphisms of perfectoid spaces and W = Y₁ ×_X Y₂ their fibre product (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then |W| → |Y₁| ×_{|X|} |Y₂| is surjective, and it is spectral on spectral opens. Consequently, for points y₁ ∈ Y₁, y₂ ∈ Y₂ with the same image x ∈ X there are an affinoid perfectoid field (L, L⁺) and (L, L⁺)-valued points ỹ_i ∈ Y_i(L, L⁺) whose closed points map to y_i and whose images in X(L, L⁺) agree: take w ∈ W over (y₁, y₂), (L, L⁺) = (K(w), K(w)⁺) and ỹ_i = pr_i ∘ i_w.

*Hypotheses.* Fibre products are those of Perfd (the uniform completion of the completed tensor product on affinoids).

*Proof outline.*

1. Reduce to affinoid X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y_i = Spa(B_i, B_i⁺) containing y_i (open subspaces of fibre products are fibre products).
2. W = Spa(D, D⁺) with D the uniform completion of B₁ ⊗̂_A B₂ (P2 affinoid formula); uniformization does not change the adic spectrum (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization (d)), and the adic spectrum of a completion is that of the uncompleted pair.
3. Amalgamation: there is a valuation v on B₁ ⊗_A B₂ restricting to y₁ and y₂ (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation); restricting v to the convex subgroup generated by the value groups of y₁, y₂ gives a continuous valuation bounded by 1 on the image of B₁⁺ ⊗ B₂⁺, hence on its integral closure, as in the proof of AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points.
4. Spectrality: preimages of rational subsets are rational (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`).
5. The (L, L⁺)-points: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection applied to w.

*Acceptance.* For a separable quadratic extension L/K of perfectoid fields, |Spa(L, O_L) ×_{Spa(K, O_K)} Spa(L, O_L)| has two points over the single point of |Spa(L, O_L)| × |Spa(L, O_L)|: the map is surjective and not injective.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/valuation-amalgamation`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 22; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Corollary 5.5, p. 24.

#### Every affinoid perfectoid field embeds into an algebraically closed one, and (K, K⁺)-points are detected there

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FieldPoints`.

Let (K, K⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid field. (a) Let C be the completion of an algebraic closure of K and C⁺ ⊆ C° the preimage of a valuation subring of the residue field of C° dominating the image of K⁺. Then C is an algebraically closed perfectoid field, (C, C⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid field, K → C is a morphism (K, K⁺) → (C, C⁺), and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺. (b) The induced map π : Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) sends the closed point to the closed point. (c) For every perfectoid space Y the restriction map Y(K, K⁺) → Y(C, C⁺), φ ↦ φ ∘ π, is injective. In particular a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is injective on (K, K⁺)-points for all affinoid perfectoid fields as soon as it is injective on (C, C⁺)-points for all algebraically closed ones.

*Hypotheses.* No assumption on the characteristic of K.

*Proof outline.*

1. C is perfectoid: its value group is divisible, it is not discretely valued, and Frobenius is surjective on C°/p because every element of the ring of integers of the algebraic closure has a p-th root (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition).
2. C is algebraically closed: in characteristic 0 by Mathlib `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange` applied to the dense algebraic closure; in characteristic p this is the classical continuity-of-roots argument (Krasner), not covered by that Mathlib lemma (recorded gap).
3. C⁺: K⁺ is the preimage of a valuation ring k⁺ of the residue field k = K°/K°°; the residue field k_C of C° is an algebraic closure of k; a valuation subring k_C⁺ of k_C dominating the local ring of the integral closure of k⁺ exists (Mathlib `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`), and k_C⁺ ∩ k = k⁺ because valuation rings are maximal for domination; put C⁺ = preimage of k_C⁺. It contains C°°, so it is open and bounded.
4. (b): the closed point of Spa(C, C⁺) is C⁺ and C⁺ ∩ K = K⁺.
5. (c): if φ ∘ π = ψ ∘ π then φ and ψ send the closed point to the same y (by (b)), so both factor through i_y (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)) by morphisms (K(y), K(y)⁺) → (K, K⁺) whose composites with the injective map K → C agree; hence φ = ψ.

*Acceptance.* For K = ℚ_p^cycl (completed) and K⁺ = K°, C = ℂ_p and C⁺ = O_{ℂ_p}. If K⁺ has rank two, C⁺ has rank two and π is a bijection on closed points and on rank-one points.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition`.
 Library: `AlgebraicClosure`, `IsAlgClosed`, `IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange`, `UniformSpace.Completion`, `ValuationSubring`, `LocalSubring.exists_le_valuationSubring`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Lemma 5.4, p. 23; sch12-perfectoid, §3, proof of Theorem 3.7, p. 29.

#### Completed tensor products over a nonarchimedean field preserve kernels and strictness

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel` (lemma); module `TauCeti/Analysis/Nonarchimedean/CompletedTensorField`.

Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value (an analytic field) and V, W, X Banach K-modules, with ⊗̂_K the completed projective tensor product. (a) V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective. (b) For a bounded K-linear f : V → W with f_X := f ⊗̂ id_X : V ⊗̂_K X → W ⊗̂_K X, the natural map ker(f) ⊗̂_K X → ker(f_X) is a bijection. (c) If f is strict then so is f_X. Consequently, for an isometric embedding K → L of analytic fields and every Banach K-module V, the map V → L ⊗̂_K V is injective; in particular L ⊗̂_K V = 0 implies V = 0.

*Hypotheses.* K complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; Banach modules are complete normed K-vector spaces.

*Proof outline.*

1. Kedlaya–Liu I Lemma 2.2.9: all three parts reduce to Banach modules containing dense subspaces of countable dimension; there (a) follows from Schauder bases of V and W, and (b), (c) from a Schauder basis of X ([Ked10, Lemma 1.3.11], unread; the reduction to countable type is recorded as a gap).
2. Consequence: apply (b) to the inclusion K → L (injective and strict) tensored with V: the kernel of V = K ⊗̂_K V → L ⊗̂_K V is 0 ⊗̂_K V = 0.

*Acceptance.* For V finite-dimensional over K, V ⊗̂_K X = V ⊗_K X and (b) is the exactness of V ⊗_K − over a field. For a closed subspace V' ⊆ V, V' ⊗̂_K X → V ⊗̂_K X is injective with closed image.

*Dependencies.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/countable-type-closed-subspace-section`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.2, Lemma 2.2.9, p. 29 (arXiv v5); KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.2, proof of Lemma 2.2.9; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 22.

#### A map of perfectoid fields that is injective on geometric points is an isomorphism

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/InjectionCriteria`.

Let K → L be a continuous homomorphism of perfectoid fields (it is injective and, after normalisation, isometric). Suppose that for every algebraically closed perfectoid field C, any two continuous homomorphisms L → C that agree on K are equal; equivalently Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is injective on (C, O_C)-valued points. Then K → L is an isomorphism. The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is required for all perfectoid fields C instead of algebraically closed ones.

*Hypotheses.* Both fields perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.6), of the same characteristic.

*Proof outline.*

1. D := L ⊗̂_K L is a perfectoid Tate ring, already uniform before any uniformization (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1; KL15 Proposition 3.6.11 for ℚ_p-algebras; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid).
2. For a ∈ L the element a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a maps to 0 in K(z) for every rank-one point z of Spa(D, D°): K(z) is a perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields), it embeds into an algebraically closed perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field), and the two composites L → C agree on K.
3. Hence its spectral seminorm, the maximum over the Gel'fand spectrum, i.e. over the rank-one points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm), vanishes, and it is 0 because D is uniform. So the multiplication D → L, whose kernel is topologically generated by these elements, is an isomorphism, and inl : L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism.
4. With V := L/K (a K-Banach space, K being closed in L), the strict exact sequence 0 → K → L → V → 0 stays strict exact after L ⊗̂_K − (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel (b), (c)); as L → L ⊗̂_K L is an isomorphism, V ⊗̂_K L = 0, hence V = 0 and K = L.

*Acceptance.* For a nontrivial finite separable extension L/K, the hypothesis fails: two distinct K-embeddings L → C exist. For K → K the hypothesis holds trivially and the conclusion is the identity.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, p. 22; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.1; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.6, Proposition 3.6.11 (arXiv v5).

#### (K, K⁺)-points of a map that is injective on points with isomorphic rank-one residue fields

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/InjectionCriteria`.

Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is injective and, for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x, the map of completed residue fields K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism. Then for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map f_* : Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective, and its image consists of the φ whose closed point maps into f(|Y|).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y perfectoid spaces; the hypothesis is condition (iii) of ECD Proposition 5.3.

*Proof outline.*

1. Every φ ∈ X(K, K⁺) factors uniquely through i_x, x = image of the closed point (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection (c)); replace X by X' := Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by Y' := Y ×_X X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. The hypothesis passes to Y' → X': Y' → Y is a base change of the injection i_x; along a chain of generalizations the completed residue fields coincide, and by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective each point of |Y| ×_{|X|} |X'| has exactly one preimage, because the fibre product of two affinoid fields with the same field over a third is Spa of that field with the larger of the two valuation rings.
3. Now |Y'| ⊆ |X'| is stable under generalization (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing) inside the chain |X'|; every quasicompact open V ⊆ Y' has a unique closed point v, so V = Spa(K(v), K(v)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point) with K(v) = K(x); thus Y' is an increasing union of open subspaces Spa(K(x), K'⁺) ⊆ Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points).
4. For each such open, Spa(K(x), K'⁺)(K, K⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)(K, K⁺) is injective with image the morphisms (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K, K⁺) carrying K'⁺ into K⁺, i.e. those whose closed point lands in Spa(K(x), K'⁺). Taking the union gives the claim for Y' → X', hence for Y → X.

*Acceptance.* For f = i_x, (K, K⁺)-points of Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) are the (K, K⁺)-points of X whose closed point is a generalization of x.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.3, (iii) ⇒ (iv), p. 22.

#### The stalk of O⁺/ϖ at x is K(x)⁺/ϖ

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Stalks`.

Let X be a perfectoid space (more generally an analytic adic space), U ⊆ X open, ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(U) a pseudouniformizer and x ∈ U. The natural map O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺ has dense image, its kernel I satisfies I = ϖI, and the induced map O⁺_{X,x}/ϖ → K(x)⁺/ϖ is an isomorphism. Consequently the stalk at x of the sheaf O⁺_X/ϖ is K(x)⁺/ϖ.

*Hypotheses.* O⁺_X(V) = {f ∈ O_X(V) : |f(y)| ≤ 1 for all y ∈ V} (anchor Layer 3.3).

*Proof outline.*

1. Dense image: the residue field of the local ring O_{X,x} is dense in K(x), and O⁺_{X,x} maps onto a dense subring of K(x)⁺ (completed residue field construction, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields). Since ϖK(x)⁺ is open, O⁺_{X,x} → K(x)⁺/ϖ is surjective.
2. Kernel: if f ∈ O⁺_X(V) has f(x) = 0 then V' := {y ∈ V : |f(y)| ≤ |ϖ(y)|} is a rational neighbourhood of x on which f/ϖ ∈ O⁺_X(V') with (f/ϖ)(x) = 0; so I = ϖI.
3. Injectivity modulo ϖ: if g ∈ O⁺_{X,x} maps into ϖK(x)⁺, lift the quotient to h ∈ O⁺_{X,x}; then g − ϖh ∈ I = ϖI.

*Acceptance.* For X = Spa(K, K⁺) and x the closed point, O⁺_{X,x} = K⁺ and the lemma is trivial.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.
 Library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.3.1, Lemma II.3.1, p. 16 (arXiv v2); Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.3.1, before Lemma II.3.1; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.3.1, proof of Lemma II.3.1.

#### A homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue pairs is an isomorphism

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/IsomorphismCriterion`.

Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces such that |f| is a homeomorphism and, for every y ∈ Y with x = f(y), the map (K(x), K(x)⁺) → (K(y), K(y)⁺) is an isomorphism of affinoid perfectoid fields. Then f is an isomorphism.

*Hypotheses.* No quasicompactness is assumed: over an open affinoid U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to U, hence qcqs.

*Proof outline.*

1. Work over a rational subset U ⊆ X with pseudouniformizer ϖ; put V = f⁻¹(U). By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer the map of sheaves O⁺_X/ϖ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖ) on |U| is an isomorphism on stalks (f is a homeomorphism), hence an isomorphism; by dévissage along 0 → O⁺/ϖ^{n−1} → O⁺/ϖⁿ → O⁺/ϖ → 0 (O⁺ is ϖ-torsion free) so is O⁺_X/ϖⁿ → f_*(O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ).
2. Taking sections: O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) is an almost isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity), and O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ → H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) is injective; comparing through the isomorphism H⁰(U, O⁺_X/ϖⁿ) ≅ H⁰(V, O⁺_Y/ϖⁿ) shows that O⁺_X(U)/ϖⁿ → O⁺_Y(V)/ϖⁿ is an almost isomorphism.
3. Both O⁺_X(U) and O⁺_Y(V) are ϖ-adically complete (V is covered by finitely many affinoids); passing to the limit (the lim and lim¹ of almost zero systems are almost zero) and inverting ϖ gives O_X(U) ≅ O_Y(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion).
4. The valuations at y and f(y) agree by hypothesis, O⁺ = {|·| ≤ 1} on both sides, so f is an isomorphism of structure sheaves compatible with the stalk valuations over the homeomorphism |f|, i.e. an isomorphism in the anchor's category of adic spaces (anchor Layers 3.4 and 5).

*Acceptance.* The identity of any perfectoid space. Non-example: Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite extension L ≠ K is a homeomorphism of one-point spaces but K → L is not an isomorphism.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/stalk-of-plus-sheaf-modulo-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/integral-almost-acyclicity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Lemma 5.4, p. 23.

#### Isomorphism criterion for qcqs maps: bijectivity on points and on (C, C⁺)-points

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/IsomorphismCriterion`.

Let f : Y → X be a quasicompact and quasiseparated morphism of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps). The following are equivalent: (i) f is an isomorphism; (ii) |f| : |Y| → |X| is bijective and for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x the map K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism; (iii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) the map Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is a bijection; (iv) for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺) the map Y(C, C⁺) → X(C, C⁺) is a bijection. (ECD Lemma 5.4.)

*Hypotheses.* f quasicompact and quasiseparated; this is used in (ii)+(iii) ⇒ (i) to make |f| a spectral map of spectral spaces over an affinoid.

*Proof outline.*

1. (i) ⇒ (ii), (iii), (iv) are clear; (iii) ⇒ (iv) is trivial.
2. (ii) ⇒ (iii): a (K, K⁺)-point of X with closed point x factors through i_x (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); replace X by Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) and Y by the base change. Then Y has a unique closed point y, so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point); K(x) = K(y) by (ii), and bijectivity of |f| forces K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.
3. (iii) ⇒ (ii): it suffices that Y ×_X Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) → Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) is an isomorphism; (iii) gives a unique section; i_y for its image y still satisfies (iii), so Y = Spa(K(y), K(y)⁺), and K(x) → K(y) → K(x) composing to the identity forces K(y) = K(x) and K(y)⁺ = K(x)⁺.
4. (iv) ⇒ (ii): |f| is surjective (extend (K(x), K(x)⁺) to an algebraically closed (C, C⁺) with C⁺ ∩ K(x) = K(x)⁺ and lift, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field); |f| is injective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective gives two (L, L⁺)-points with equal image, extended to (C, C⁺)); for rank-one y ↦ x, Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (C, O_C)-points because f and i_y are, so K(x) = K(y) by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity. (ECD argues instead by Galois equivariance; see sourceIssues.)
5. (ii) + (iii) ⇒ (i): reduce to X affinoid, so Y is qcqs; |f| is a bijective, generalizing (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), spectral map of spectral spaces, hence a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient) and a homeomorphism; the residue pairs agree by the proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii), so f is an isomorphism by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs.

*Acceptance.* ECD Lemma 7.19: a qcqs map to a strictly totally disconnected space that is a bijective injection is an isomorphism. Quasicompactness is needed: for an infinite profinite set S and X = S × Spa(C, O_C) = Spa(C⁰(S, C), C⁰(S, O_C)), the map Y = ⊔_{s∈S} Spa(C, O_C) → X is bijective on underlying sets and on all (K, K⁺)-points (Spa(K, K⁺) is connected) but is not an isomorphism; it is not quasicompact. A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is qcqs and bijective on points but fails (ii) and (iv).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-with-unique-closed-point-is-a-field-point`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/isomorphism-from-homeomorphism-and-residue-pairs`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Lemma 5.4, p. 23; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Lemma 5.4 (iv), p. 23; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, remark after Lemma 7.19, p. 38.

#### Characterisations of injections of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/InjectionCriteria`.

Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces); (ii) for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺), Y(K, K⁺) → X(K, K⁺) is injective; (ii') the same for every algebraically closed affinoid perfectoid field (C, C⁺); (iii) |f| is injective and K(x) → K(y) is an isomorphism for every rank-one point y ∈ Y with image x; (iv) |f| is injective and, for every perfectoid space Z, Hom(Z, Y) → Hom(Z, X) ×_{C⁰(|Z|, |X|)} C⁰(|Z|, |Y|) is a bijection, i.e. f is final among morphisms g : Z → X for which |g| factors through a continuous map |Z| → |Y|. In particular injections Y → X are determined, up to unique isomorphism over X, by the continuous injection |Y| → |X|; |Y| need not carry the subspace topology of |X|. (ECD Proposition 5.3; (ii') is Berkeley Lectures Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3).)

*Hypotheses.* No quasicompactness hypothesis.

*Proof outline.*

1. (i) ⇒ (ii) ⇒ (ii') are clear; (ii') ⇒ (ii) is PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field (c); (iv) ⇒ (i) is clear.
2. (ii) ⇒ (iii), injectivity of |f|: if y₁ ≠ y₂ map to x, base change along i_x and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective give (L, L⁺)-points ỹ₁ ≠ ỹ₂ with the same image.
3. (ii) ⇒ (iii), residue fields: for rank-one y ↦ x, g : Spa(K(y), O) → Spa(K(x), O) is injective on (K, K⁺)-points because f and the injection i_y are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); conclude by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity.
4. (iii) ⇒ (iv): by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps, f_* is injective on (K, K⁺)-points with image the points whose closed point lies in f(|Y|). Given g : Z → X with |g| factoring continuously through |Y|, work locally on Z so that X, Y, Z are affinoid; the qcqs map Y ×_X Z → Z is then bijective on all (K, K⁺)-points, hence an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion), and its inverse gives the unique factorization; uniqueness glues.
5. Determination by |Y| → |X| is (iv).
