*Acceptance.* Rational open immersions and the residue-field points i_x satisfy (iii). Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a finite separable extension L ≠ K fails (ii') and (iii) although |f| is injective. ECD Lemma 9.9 applies (ii) together with the valuative criterion to recognise an injection.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/algebraically-closed-extension-of-affinoid-field`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/rank-one-residue-field-rigidity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/field-points-of-residually-injective-maps`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/qcqs-isomorphism-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.3 (iii), p. 21; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.3 (iv), p. 21; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Proposition 5.3, p. 21; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Definition/Proposition 8.3.3 (3), p. 61.

#### Base change of injections, and the underlying space of a pulled-back injection

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Injection`.

Let f : Y → X be an injection of perfectoid spaces and X' → X any morphism, with base change f' : Y' = X' ×_X Y → X'. Then f' is an injection, and the natural map |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is a homeomorphism (the target with the fibre product topology). Moreover composites of injections are injections, and if g ∘ f is an injection then so is f. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (i).)

*Hypotheses.* f an injection; X' → X arbitrary.

*Proof outline.*

1. f' is an injection: monomorphisms are stable under pullback (in any category with pullbacks).
2. |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is injective because |f| and |f'| are (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii)); it is surjective and spectral (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective) and generalizing, both sides being generalization-stable subsets of |X'| (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing).
3. On spectral opens a bijective generalizing spectral map of spectral spaces is a quotient map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient), hence a homeomorphism.
4. Composition and cancellation are formal from the definition.

*Acceptance.* For f a rational open immersion U ⊆ X, Y' is the preimage of U in X' with its open subspace structure.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.
 Library: `CategoryTheory.Mono`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24.

#### Injections are exactly the universally injective maps

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-iff-universally-injective` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Injection`.

A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an injection if and only if it is universally injective: for every morphism X' → X the base change f' : X' ×_X Y → X' is injective on underlying spaces. (ECD Corollary 5.5 (ii).)

*Hypotheses.* None beyond the existence of fibre products.

*Proof outline.*

1. ⇒: PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iii).
2. ⇐: given g : Z → X, pull back along g to reduce to Z = X; it suffices that f has at most one section. A section h is an injection (split monomorphism), and |X| → |Y| → |X| is the identity with both maps injective, so |h| is a homeomorphism with inverse |f|.
3. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv) applied to h, every morphism into Y factors uniquely through h; so h is an isomorphism, f is its inverse, and the section is unique.

*Acceptance.* A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K), L ≠ K, is injective on points but not universally injective: its self-fibre product has two points over one.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Corollary 5.5 (ii), p. 24.


### P4.4 Immersions

#### `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion` — Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion` (definition); planet “Immersion of perfectoid spaces”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Immersion`.

A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is an immersion if f is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces) and |f| : |Y| → |X| is a locally closed immersion, i.e. a topological embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsEmbedding`) with locally closed image (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed`). It is an open immersion (resp. closed immersion) if moreover |f| is an open (resp. closed) embedding (Mathlib `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`) (ECD Definition 5.6). The definition is possible because perfectoid spaces carry no nilpotent structure: an injection is determined by its image as a space (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)), so an immersion is determined up to unique isomorphism over X by the locally closed subset f(|Y|). These notions live in the namespace `PerfectoidSpace` and are compared with the anchor's open and closed immersions in PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/anchor-closed-immersion-comparison; closed immersions are strictly more general than Zariski closed immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed).

*Hypotheses.* Topology of |Y| is its own spectral-space topology; the embedding condition says it is the subspace topology.

*Proof outline.*

1. The definition is a conjunction of an injection with a topological condition; nothing to construct.
2. Uniqueness given the image: two immersions with the same image are injections with homeomorphic images, hence uniquely isomorphic over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).

*Uses.* ECD Definition 5.10: separatedness asks the diagonal to be a closed immersion; ECD Proposition 5.9: diagonals are immersions; ECD Definition 10.7 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness: open and closed immersions of pro-étale stacks are tested on perfectoid spaces; for maps of perfectoid spaces the notions agree with these; Berkeley Lectures Definition 17.4.2: closed immersions of v-sheaves restrict to these; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding and P8/analytically-separated-is-separated: Zariski-closed embeddings are closed immersions; the diagonal of an analytically separated space; PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed: ECD Theorem 5.8 is stated for the closed immersions of this node.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is an embedding with locally closed range.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is an open embedding.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion` (structure): f is an injection and |f| is a closed embedding.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion.isImmersion` (relation): Open immersions are immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion.isImmersion` (relation): Closed immersions are immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.isInjection` (projection): Immersions are injections.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.isLocallyClosed_range` (projection): The image of an immersion is locally closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.ext` (extensionality): Two immersions into X with the same image are uniquely isomorphic over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.stableUnderGeneralization_range` (other): The image of an immersion is stable under generalization.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsClosedImmersion.quasiCompact` (instance): Closed immersions are quasicompact: the preimage of a quasicompact open is closed in it.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.comp` (structure): Composites of (open, closed) immersions are (open, closed) immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsImmersion.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes of (open, closed) immersions are (open, closed) immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsOpenImmersion.of_isOpen` (constructor): For U ⊆ |X| open, the open perfectoid subspace U → X is an open immersion.

*Unit tests.*

- `isOpenImmersion_rationalSubset` (computation): For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid and U ⊆ X rational, U → X is an open immersion.
- `isClosedImmersion_origin` (computation): The point T^{1/pⁿ} = 0 (all n), i.e. Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), is a closed immersion.
- `isImmersion_empty` (degenerate): The empty perfectoid space maps to every X by an open and closed immersion; the identity is both.
- `not_isImmersion_residueFieldPoint` (non-example): For the Gauss point η of the perfectoid disc, i_η is an injection but not an immersion: {η} is not locally closed (every open neighbourhood of η contains all but finitely many of its rank-two specializations).
- `not_isImmersion_image_closedPoint` (non-example): The closed point of Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank two is a closed subset that is not the image of any immersion: images of morphisms are stable under generalization.
- `isImmersion_iff_scheme_analog` (compatibility): Like Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion` (embedding with locally closed range plus a local condition), IsImmersion f ↔ IsInjection f ∧ IsEmbedding |f| ∧ IsLocallyClosed (range |f|); here the local condition is the injection property.

*Acceptance.* The inclusion of a rational subset, and of any open subset with its open subspace structure, is an open immersion. Diagonals are immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`.
 Library: `Topology.IsEmbedding`, `IsLocallyClosed`, `Topology.IsOpenEmbedding`, `Topology.IsClosedEmbedding`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.6, p. 24; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Definition 5.6, p. 24.

#### Immersions are stable under base change and composition; closed immersions are quasicompact

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Immersion`.

Immersions, open immersions and closed immersions of perfectoid spaces are stable under composition and under base change along arbitrary morphisms; for an immersion f : Y → X and X' → X, the image of the base change is the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|. Closed immersions are quasicompact; an immersion is a closed immersion if and only if its image is closed.

*Hypotheses.* Morphisms of perfectoid spaces; fibre products as in P2.

*Proof outline.*

1. Base change: by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition the base change f' is an injection and |Y'| ≅ |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y|; since |Y| → |X| is an embedding, the fibre product topology is the subspace topology of the preimage of f(|Y|) in |X'|, which is locally closed (open, closed) when f(|Y|) is.
2. Composition: composites of injections are injections, and composites of embeddings with locally closed (open, closed) images have locally closed (open, closed) images (Mathlib `IsLocallyClosed.image` for embeddings with locally closed range).
3. Quasicompactness: for a quasicompact open U ⊆ X, f⁻¹(U) is homeomorphic to the closed subset f(|Y|) ∩ U of U.

*Acceptance.* The preimage of a rational subset under any morphism is rational, and the base change of its inclusion is that rational open immersion.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injections-base-change-composition`.
 Library: `IsLocallyClosed`, `Topology.IsEmbedding`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Corollary 5.5 (i), p. 24; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, before Definition 5.6, p. 24.

#### Open immersions of perfectoid spaces agree with the anchor's open immersions

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/open-immersion-comparison` (comparison); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Immersion`.

For a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces the following are equivalent: (a) f is an open immersion in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion; (b) f is an open immersion of adic spaces in the sense of the anchor (Layer 5.1): an isomorphism onto the open adic subspace X|_U, U = f(|Y|). Every open subset U ⊆ |X| underlies the perfectoid open subspace X|_U (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), rational subsets of affinoid perfectoid spaces are open affinoid perfectoid subspaces, and the open immersions into X correspond bijectively to the open subsets of |X|.

*Hypotheses.* Perfectoid spaces are adic spaces of the anchor (P2), so both notions apply to the same morphisms.

*Proof outline.*

1. (b) ⇒ (a): X|_U → X is a monomorphism, because a morphism Z → X factors through X|_U if and only if |Z| lands in U, and then uniquely (anchor Layer 5.1 universal property of open subspaces); |X|_U| → |X| is an open embedding.
2. (a) ⇒ (b): X|_U → X is an injection with the same image and topology as f, so Y ≅ X|_U over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv).

*Acceptance.* For X = Spa(R, R⁺) and U = X(T/s) rational, (O_X(U), O⁺_X(U)) is the rational localization and U → X is an open immersion in both senses.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Proposition 5.3, p. 21; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §10, after Remark 10.8, p. 51.


### P4.5 Zariski closed immersions and perfectoid quotients

#### `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus` — Zariski closed subsets and Zariski closed immersions into affinoid perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion` (definition); planet “Zariski closed immersion”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. For an ideal I ⊆ R put V(I) := {x ∈ |X| : |g(x)| = 0 for all g ∈ I}; a subset Z ⊆ |X| is Zariski closed if Z = V(I) for some ideal I (Scholze torsion paper Definition II.2.1). A morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces is a Zariski closed immersion (defined by I) if f is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion) and f(|Z|) = V(I) (ECD Definition 5.7 (i)). Conventions: V(I) depends only on the closure of I and on its radical; V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F with U_F := {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F} rational, because I is an ideal and |ϖ(x)|ⁿ → 0 cofinally at every continuous valuation; V(I) is closed, pro-constructible and stable under generalization; V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J) and V(IJ) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J). Every Zariski closed subset is the image of exactly one Zariski closed immersion up to unique isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal). A Zariski closed immersion defined by I is not Spa(R/I, ·): the perfectoid structure on V(I) kills all compatible p-power roots.

*Hypotheses.* X affinoid perfectoid; the global notion over non-affinoid X (locally Zariski closed) is PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding.

*Proof outline.*

1. V(I) = ⋂ U_F: '⊆' is clear; if |g(x)| ≠ 0 for some g ∈ I then |ϖ^{−n}g(x)| > 1 for n large, as |ϖ(x)|ⁿ is eventually below every element of the value group of the continuous valuation x (anchor Layer 1.5), and ϖ^{−n}g ∈ I.
2. Closedness: V(I) = ⋂_{g∈I} {|g| = 0} and each {|g| = 0} is the complement of ⋃_n {|ϖⁿ| ≤ |g|}, a union of rational subsets; pro-constructibility and generalization-stability follow from the intersection formula.
3. The formula V(I) = image of the anchor's quotient pair: Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom` identifies {v : I ⊆ supp v} with V(I).

*Uses.* ECD Theorem 5.8 and PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed: the statement that Zariski closed immersions are strongly Zariski closed; ECD Remark 7.9 and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale: Zariski closed immersions of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid pro-étale; ECD Proposition 5.9: diagonals of maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are Zariski closed; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: the global notion is local on the target; Scholze torsion paper §§II.3, III.2 and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties: Hodge-type Shimura varieties at infinite level are Zariski closed in the Siegel case, hence perfectoid; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: comparison with Fargues–Scholze's Zariski closed immersions into relative balls.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus` (data): V(I) ⊆ |Spa(R, R⁺)| for an ideal I ⊆ R.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_eq_iInter_rational` (characterisation): V(I) = ⋂_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isClosed_zeroLocus` (other): V(I) is closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.stableUnderGeneralization_zeroLocus` (other): V(I) is stable under generalization.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_sup` (simp): V(I + J) = V(I) ∩ V(J).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_mul` (simp): V(I·J) = V(I ∩ J) = V(I) ∪ V(J).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zeroLocus_closure` (simp): V(closure I) = V(I) and V(√I) = V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosed` (structure): A subset of |X| of the form V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion` (structure): f : Z → Spa(R, R⁺) is a closed immersion with f(|Z|) = V(I) for some ideal I.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.isClosedImmersion` (projection): Zariski closed immersions are closed immersions.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.iso_zariskiClosedSubspace` (characterisation): A Zariski closed immersion defined by I is uniquely isomorphic over X to Z_I → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes along maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are Zariski closed, defined by IR'.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsZariskiClosedImmersion.of_isStronglyZariskiClosed` (relation): Strongly Zariski closed immersions are Zariski closed.

*Unit tests.*

- `zeroLocus_T` (computation): For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V((T)) = {origin}, and the Zariski closed immersion is Spa(C, O_C) → X; its kernel is the closure of the ideal generated by all T^{1/pⁿ}, not (T).
- `zeroLocus_T_sub_one` (computation): For C ∋ μ_{p^∞}, V((T − 1)) ⊆ Spa(C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) is homeomorphic to ℤ_p (compatible systems of p-power roots of unity).
- `zeroLocus_bot_top` (degenerate): V(0) = |X| and V(R) = ∅.
- `not_isZariskiClosed_annulusClosure` (non-example): The closure of the annulus {|T| = 1} in the perfectoid closed disc is closed, generalizing and the image of a closed immersion, but it is not Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed).
- `zeroLocus_eq_range_quotient` (compatibility): V(I) equals the range of Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap (quotientHom S I)`, i.e. {v : I ⊆ supp v}.

*Acceptance.* For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, V((T)) is the single point T = 0, and V((T − 1)) is the profinite set of classical points (T^{1/pⁿ}) = (ζ_{pⁿ}^a)_n, a ∈ ℤ_p, when C contains all p-power roots of unity.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.
 Library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Definition II.2.1, p. 13 (arXiv v2); Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.7 (i), p. 24.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed` — Strongly Zariski closed immersions: surjective perfectoid quotients

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion` (definition); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space. A morphism f : Z → X is strongly Zariski closed if Z = Spa(S, S⁺) is affinoid perfectoid, f is induced by a morphism (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with R → S surjective, and S⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺ in S (ECD Definition 5.7 (ii)). Equivalently (by the open mapping theorem, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), with I := ker(R → S) closed, (S, S⁺) is isomorphic to the anchor's quotient pair Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I` and R/I is perfectoid. The plus-ring clause is part of the definition: it is what makes a strongly Zariski closed map a closed immersion. Scholze's earlier Definition II.2.6 (R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective) omits it and is strictly weaker (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion).

*Hypotheses.* X affinoid perfectoid; S perfectoid is part of the data (a quotient R/I of a perfectoid R is perfectoid iff it is uniform, Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4(a)).

*Proof outline.*

1. Equivalence with the quotient pair: R → S is a continuous surjection of complete Tate rings, hence open (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`), so R/I ≅ S topologically, I closed; the plus rings agree by definition of Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` (integral closure of the image of R⁺).

*Uses.* ECD Proposition 5.9: the diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed; ECD Theorem 5.8 via PerfectoidQuotients:Q4: Zariski closed implies strongly Zariski closed; AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/zariski-closed-immersion-ecd-comparison: affinoid étale perfectoid spaces embed strongly Zariski closed into perfectoid relative balls; Scholze torsion paper §III (boundary of Shimura varieties): the boundary is strongly Zariski closed; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: the affinoid pieces of a Zariski-closed embedding.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed` (structure): Z = Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) with R → S surjective and S⁺ the integral closure of the image of R⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.surjective` (projection): R → S is surjective.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.plus_eq` (projection): S⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R⁺.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.isClosed_ker` (other): ker(R → S) is closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.iff_quotient` (compatibility): Equivalent to being Spa of the anchor quotient pair Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I with R/I perfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.isZariskiClosedImmersion` (relation): Strongly Zariski closed maps are Zariski closed immersions defined by ker(R → S).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.almostSurjective_plus` (relation): R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.comp` (structure): Composites are strongly Zariski closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes along maps of affinoid perfectoid spaces are strongly Zariski closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsStronglyZariskiClosed.tilt` (compatibility): f is strongly Zariski closed iff its tilt is (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-tilting).

*Unit tests.*

- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_origin` (computation): C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C, T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0, with plus rings O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → O_C, is strongly Zariski closed.
- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_id` (degenerate): The identity of X and the map from the empty space Spa(0, 0) are strongly Zariski closed.
- `not_isStronglyZariskiClosed_ofPowerBounded` (non-example): For R⁺ ⊊ R°, Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺) has R → R surjective and R⁺ → R° almost surjective (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), but R° is not the integral closure of R⁺, so it is not strongly Zariski closed (nor a closed immersion).
- `isStronglyZariskiClosed_iff_quotient` (compatibility): f is strongly Zariski closed iff (S, S⁺) ≅ Tau Ceti Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) (ker(R → S)) over (R, R⁺) with S perfectoid.

*Acceptance.* The diagonal Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(S, S⁺) ×_{Spa(R, R⁺)} Spa(S, S⁺) of any map of affinoid perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotientHom`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.7 (ii), p. 24; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24.

#### A surjection of perfectoid Tate rings is almost surjective on integral elements

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Surjections`.

Let ψ : R → S be a surjective continuous homomorphism of perfectoid Tate rings and R⁺ ⊆ R°, S⁺ ⊆ S° rings of integral elements with ψ(R⁺) ⊆ S⁺. Then R° → S° and R⁺ → S⁺ are almost surjective: for every pseudouniformizer ϖ of R admitting compatible p-power roots, S°/ψ(R°) and S⁺/ψ(R⁺) are killed by every ϖ^{1/pⁿ}. Equivalently, the quotient seminorm on S induced by the spectral norm of R equals the spectral norm of S. In particular, for a strongly Zariski closed Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺), R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.8).

*Hypotheses.* R, S perfectoid Tate rings of any characteristic, not necessarily over a field or over ℚ_p.

*Proof outline.*

1. Promote R and S to uniform Banach rings with their spectral norms; ψ is submetric, and by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`) the quotient norm is at most c times the spectral norm of S for some c > 1.
2. Improvement c ↦ c^{1/p}: given b ∈ S, lift b^p to a₀ with |a₀| ≤ c|b|^p, approximate a₀ by a sharp element ♯(x) with x ∈ R♭ and α(a₀ − ♯(x)) ≤ α(p)·max{α(a₀), |b|^p} for every α in the Gel'fand spectrum of R (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (d); Kedlaya AWS (2.8.5.1), whose factor p⁻¹ is α(p) for the normalisation |p| = p⁻¹), and take a = ♯(x^{1/p}) (♯ is multiplicative, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map); the p-th power map estimate in a nonarchimedean field gives |b − ψ(a)| ≤ p^{−1/p}|b| at every point of the Gel'fand spectrum, the case β(p) = 0 being trivial (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.5, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(c)).
3. Iterating, the quotient norm is ≤ c^{1/pⁿ}·(spectral norm) for all n, so it equals the spectral norm; hence ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°) + ϖS° for all n, and completeness gives ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(R°).
4. For plus rings: ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S⁺ ⊆ ϖ^{1/pⁿ}S° ⊆ ψ(ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}}R°) ⊆ ψ(R°°) ⊆ ψ(R⁺).

*Acceptance.* R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S = C (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0): R° → S° = O_C is surjective. Characteristic p: a strict surjection of perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebras is almost optimal (KL15 Remark 3.1.6(a)).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Lemma 2.8.5; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.6, Proposition 3.6.9 (c) (arXiv v5); KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §3.1, Remark 3.1.6 (a); Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Lemma II.2.8, p. 15.

#### Surjectivity and closed ideals with perfectoid quotient under tilting

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Surjections`.

Let f : A → B be a continuous homomorphism of Tate rings with A perfectoid. (a) If B is uniform and f is surjective then B is perfectoid. (b) If B is perfectoid then f is surjective if and only if its tilt f♭ : A♭ → B♭ is surjective. (c) I ↦ I♭ := ker(A♭ → (A/I)♭) is a bijection between closed ideals I ⊆ A with A/I uniform (equivalently perfectoid) and closed perfect ideals of A♭; the inverse sends J to the closure of the ideal generated by {♯(x) : x ∈ J}. (d) A closed ideal I ⊆ A has A/I perfectoid if and only if I is the closure of the ideal generated by ♯(x^{1/pⁿ}) for x in some subset of A♭ and all n ≥ 0. (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.4, Corollaries 2.4.5–2.4.6.)

*Hypotheses.* Tate rings; A perfectoid in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a): a uniform ring with a dense-image map from a perfectoid ring is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion; Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.3(a) via Lemma 2.8.4).
2. (b) ⇐: θ : W(A♭⁺) → A⁺ is surjective, so the composite W(A♭) → W(B♭) → B is surjective when f♭ is (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel). ⇒: from PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings, lift ♯(b) with norm ≤ p^{1/2}|b| and correct by sharp approximations (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma (c), with (e) bounding ♯(b) − ♯(f♭(a)) − ♯(b − f♭(a))); iterating lifts every b ∈ B♭ (Kedlaya AWS Lemma 2.8.6, adapting KL15 Proposition 3.6.9(d)).
3. (c): by (b), closed ideals with perfectoid quotient correspond to surjections of perfectoid rings, hence to surjections of their tilts, i.e. to closed ideals of A♭ with perfect uniform quotient; a quotient of a perfect uniform ring by a closed perfect ideal is perfect and uniform (x̃^{1/p} lifts x^{1/p}), and conversely the kernel of a map to a perfect ring is perfect.
4. (d) follows from (c) with the subset {♯(x) : x ∈ I♭}.

*Acceptance.* For A = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I the closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0), A/I = K and I♭ is the closure of (T♭^{1/pⁿ}).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-functoriality`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-approximation-lemma`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/sharp-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.4; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.4; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Corollary 2.4.6.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace` — The universal perfectoid space over a Zariski closed subset

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed` (construction); planet “Universal perfectoid Zariski closed subspace”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and I ⊆ R an ideal. Let 𝒰_I := {U_F : F ⊆ I finite}, U_F = {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ F}, and let ι_I : Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) → X be the pro-rational subspace of 𝒰_I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets): S_I⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of colim_F O⁺_X(U_F) and S_I = S_I⁺[1/ϖ]. Then: (a) Z_I is affinoid perfectoid and R → S_I has dense image; (b) |ι_I| is a homeomorphism onto V(I); (c) a morphism g : W → X from a perfectoid space factors through ι_I if and only if g^*(h) = 0 in O_W(W) for all h ∈ I, if and only if |g| lands in V(I), and then uniquely; (d) ι_I is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion); (e) I^perf := ker(R → S_I) is a closed ideal containing I, equal to {h ∈ R : |h| = 0 on V(I)}, and Z_{I^perf} = Z_I; (f) Z_I depends only on V(I). In characteristic-free generality this is Scholze's Lemma II.2.2 with Remark II.2.3 (stated over a perfectoid field) and Bhatt's Proposition 9.4.1 (1)–(3). Surjectivity of R → S_I is ECD Theorem 5.8 and is imported (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed); it is not used in this construction.

*Hypotheses.* X affinoid perfectoid with a pseudouniformizer ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots; I arbitrary (not necessarily closed or finitely generated).

*Proof outline.*

1. V(I) = ⋂ U_F (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion), and 𝒰_I is filtered (U_F ∩ U_G = U_{F∪G}); apply PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets for (a), (b) and the topological universal property.
2. (c): if |g| lands in V(I), each g^*(h), h ∈ I, vanishes at every point of W; on an affinoid perfectoid open of W (uniform) its spectral seminorm, a maximum over points (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm), is 0, so g^*(h) = 0. Conversely g^*(h) = 0 forces |h| = 0 on the image.
3. (d): ι_I is an injection with |ι_I| a homeomorphism onto the closed subset V(I), hence a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion), with image V(I).
4. (e), (f): h ∈ ker(R → S_I) iff |h| = 0 on |Z_I| = V(I) (S_I uniform); both Z_I and Z_{I^perf} are pro-rational subspaces with intersection V(I) = V(I^perf).

*Uses.* Scholze torsion paper §III.3 (Hodge type): Zariski closed subsets of perfectoid Siegel spaces are perfectoid; ECD Remark 7.9 and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale: Z = lim U_F is a pro-étale presentation; PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed: the closed perfectoid quotient R' = S_perfd[1/ϖ] is identified with S_I; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding: affinoid Zariski-closed subsets are affinoid perfectoid; PerfectoidSpaces:P8 (compatible-root closed locus): the kernel of R → S_I kills all compatible roots.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace` (constructor): Z_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) for an ideal I ⊆ R.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.ι` (data): ι_I : Z_I → X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.range_ι` (characterisation): |ι_I| is a homeomorphism onto V(I).
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.lift` (universal-property): A morphism W → X killing I factors uniquely through ι_I; lift_ι, lift_unique.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.isZariskiClosedImmersion` (relation): ι_I is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.denseRange` (other): R → S_I has dense image.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.ker_eq` (characterisation): ker(R → S_I) = {h : |h| = 0 on V(I)}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.congr` (extensionality): V(I) = V(J) ⇒ Z_I ≅ Z_J uniquely over X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace_sup` (simp): Z_{I+J} ≅ Z_I ×_X Z_J.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace.plus_mod` (simp): S_I⁺/ϖ = colim_F O⁺_X(U_F)/ϖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (simp): Z_0 = X, Z_R = ∅.

*Unit tests.*

- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T` (computation): R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, I = (T): S_I = C, and ker(R → S_I) is the closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) ⊋ (T); R/(T) is not reduced (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_T_sub_one` (computation): C = ℂ_p, R = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, I = (T − 1): S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p), with T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ (γ ↦ ζ_{pⁿ}^γ) (Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.10).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_bot` (degenerate): Z_0 = X and Z_R = ∅.
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_ne_quotient` (non-example): Spa(R/I, ·) is not Z_I in general: for I = (T), R/I is not uniform, so Spa(R/(T), ·) is not a perfectoid space, while Z_I = Spa(C, O_C).
- `zariskiClosedSubspace_eq_proRational` (compatibility): Z_I is the pro-rational subspace of the family {U_F}; if I is generated by g₁, …, g_k admitting compatible p-power roots g_i = ♯(g_i♭), then S_I = R/J with J the closure of the ideal generated by all g_i^{1/pⁿ} (R/J is perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (d), and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed identifies Spa(R/J, ·) with Z_I).

*Acceptance.* For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and I = (T): S_I = C, and I^perf is the closure of the ideal generated by all T^{1/pⁿ}. For I = 0: Z_I = X; for I = R: Z_I = ∅.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Lemma II.2.2, p. 13 (arXiv v2); Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Remark II.2.3, p. 14; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Remark 7.9, p. 32; Bhatt-PerfectoidNotes-2017, §9.4, Proposition 9.4.1 (1), p. 111.

#### Every Zariski closed immersion is the universal one

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let f : Z → X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a Zariski closed immersion defined by an ideal I. Then there is a unique isomorphism Z ≅ Z_I over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed). Consequently Z is affinoid perfectoid, Z = lim_{F ⊆ I finite} U_F, and a Zariski closed immersion is determined by its image V(I).

*Hypotheses.* X affinoid perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*

1. f and ι_I are injections whose underlying maps are homeomorphisms onto the same subset V(I) with its subspace topology (f is a closed immersion; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed (b)).
2. By PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv), injections into X are determined up to unique isomorphism by the continuous injection of underlying spaces.

*Acceptance.* The Zariski closed immersion Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) at the origin is Z_{(T)}.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, after Remark II.2.3, p. 14; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Remark 7.9, p. 32.

#### A surjective perfectoid quotient is a Zariski closed immersion (the direction proved here)

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be affinoid perfectoid, ψ : R → S a surjective continuous homomorphism onto a perfectoid Tate ring, I := ker ψ and S⁺ the integral closure of ψ(R⁺). Then: (a) I is closed and (S, S⁺) ≅ Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) I`; (b) Z := Spa(S, S⁺) → X is a Zariski closed immersion defined by I, and |Z| → V(I) is a homeomorphism; (c) Z ≅ Z_I over X, so S = S_I and I = I^perf. Thus every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed. The converse is ECD Theorem 5.8, imported in PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed.

*Hypotheses.* S perfectoid; ψ surjective.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a): ψ is open by the open mapping theorem (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`), so S ≅ R/I topologically; I is closed as the kernel of a continuous map to a Hausdorff ring; S⁺ matches Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient` by definition.
2. (b): maps W → Z from affinoid perfectoid W are morphisms (S, S⁺) → (O_W(W), O⁺_W(W)); as ψ is surjective they are determined by the composite with ψ, so Z → X is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces). |Z| → |X| is a closed embedding with image {v : I ⊆ supp v} = V(I) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`).
3. (c): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal.

*Acceptance.* The diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map). C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C, T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0: Z = Z_{(T)}.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isQuotientMap`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotientHom`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.range_spaComap_quotientHom`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, after Definition II.2.6, p. 15.

#### Criteria for strong Zariski closedness in terms of almost surjectivity on plus rings

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let f : Z = Spa(S, S⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) be a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces, ϖ a pseudouniformizer of R with compatible p-power roots, and let T⁺ denote the integral closure of the image of R⁺ in S. The following are equivalent: (a) f is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion); (b) R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjective and S⁺ = T⁺; (c) R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ is almost surjective and S⁺ = T⁺. Scholze's Definition II.2.6 (R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective, with no condition on S⁺) is strictly weaker: Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ ⊊ R° satisfies it, but is not a closed immersion.

*Hypotheses.* Z, X affinoid perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) ⇒ (b): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings.
2. (b) ⇒ (c) is clear.
3. (c) ⇒ (b): successive approximation, using that R⁺ and S⁺ are ϖ-adically complete and the exponents ε/2, ε/4, … sum to less than ε: ϖ^{ε/2}s = r₀ + ϖs₁, ϖ^{ε/4}s₁ = r₁ + ϖs₂, … converges to a lift of ϖ^ε s.
4. (b) ⇒ (a): ϖ^εS⁺ ⊆ image(R⁺) gives S = S⁺[1/ϖ] = image(R), so R → S is surjective, and S⁺ = T⁺ holds by hypothesis.
5. Non-example: R → R is surjective and R°/R⁺ is almost zero (ECD Example 3.22(ii)), while the image of Spa(R, R°) in Spa(R, R⁺) is the set {x : |g(x)| ≤ 1 for g ∈ R°}, which is not closed when R⁺ ≠ R° (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`).

*Acceptance.* The diagonal of a map of affinoid perfectoid spaces satisfies (a)–(c).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`.
 Library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`, `IsAdicComplete`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Definition II.2.6, p. 15 (arXiv v2); Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, proof of Lemma II.2.7, p. 15; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24.

#### Base change of Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-base-change` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

Let Z → X be a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces, X' = Spa(R', R'⁺) → X = Spa(R, R⁺) any morphism, and Z' = Z ×_X X' = Spa(S', S'⁺). (i) If Z → X is Zariski closed defined by I ⊆ R, then Z' → X' is Zariski closed defined by IR'; more precisely Z_I ×_X X' ≅ Z_{IR'} over X'. (ii) If Z → X is strongly Zariski closed, so is Z' → X', and with I⁺ := ker(R⁺ → S⁺), I'⁺ := ker(R'⁺ → S'⁺) the maps I⁺/ϖⁿ ⊗_{R⁺/ϖⁿ} R'⁺/ϖⁿ → I'⁺/ϖⁿ are almost surjective for all n ≥ 0. (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.9.)

*Hypotheses.* Affinoid perfectoid spaces; fibre products as in P2.

*Proof outline.*

1. (i): a morphism W → X' factors through Z_I ×_X X' iff W → X kills I iff W → X' kills IR' (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed (c)); both are Zariski closed by PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal.
2. (ii): S'⁺/ϖ is almost isomorphic to S⁺/ϖ ⊗_{R⁺/ϖ} R'⁺/ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula (ii), reduced modulo ϖ), so R'⁺/ϖ → S'⁺/ϖ is almost surjective, R' → S' is surjective and S'⁺ is the integral closure of the image of R'⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion (c) ⇒ (a), after identifying S'⁺ with that integral closure through PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed and (i)).
3. Ideals: 0 → I⁺/ϖ → R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ → 0 is almost exact (S⁺ is ϖ-torsion free and R⁺ → S⁺ almost surjective, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings); tensoring with R'⁺/ϖ over R⁺/ϖ is right exact, which gives the almost surjectivity for n = 1, and dévissage gives all n.

*Acceptance.* Restriction of a Zariski closed immersion to a rational subset U ⊆ X is Zariski closed in U, defined by I·O_X(U) (the case used in PerfectoidSpaces:P8/zariski-closed-embedding).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-plus-ring-almost-formula`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-inversion-and-completion`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Lemma II.2.9 (i), p. 15; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Lemma II.2.9 (ii), p. 15; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, proof of Lemma II.2.9, p. 16.

#### Comparison with the anchor's closed immersions

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/anchor-closed-immersion-comparison` (comparison); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

(a) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) affinoid perfectoid, a morphism f : Z → X of perfectoid spaces is strongly Zariski closed if and only if it is isomorphic over X to the anchor's closed immersion Spa(Huber.Pair.quotient (R, R⁺) J) → Spa(R, R⁺) (anchor Layer 2.4 and Layer 5.1; Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.quotient`) for a closed ideal J ⊆ R with R/J perfectoid; then J = ker(R → S). (b) For arbitrary X, a morphism of perfectoid spaces is a closed immersion in the anchor's sense (affinoid-locally Spa(A/J) → Spa(A) with J closed and A/J sheafy) if and only if it is, locally on X, strongly Zariski closed; such a morphism is a closed immersion in the sense of ECD Definition 5.6 whose restrictions over open affinoids are Zariski closed. (c) The anchor's closed immersion defined by a closed ideal J of a perfectoid R need not have perfectoid source: for R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and J = (T), R/J is not reduced, whereas the Zariski closed subspace V(T) is Spa(C, O_C). (d) That every Zariski closed immersion into an affinoid is of the form (a) is ECD Theorem 5.8 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-equals-strongly-zariski-closed).

*Hypotheses.* Perfectoid spaces are adic spaces of the anchor (P2); the anchor's closed immersions are those of its Layer 5.1.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion (equivalence with the quotient pair) and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed.
2. (b): both notions are affinoid-local on X (anchor Layer 5.1 independence of the affinoid cover; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition for ECD closed immersions); combine with (a) on each affinoid.
3. (c): Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.9; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed for V(T).

*Acceptance.* The diagonal of a morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is an anchor closed immersion with perfectoid source.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/closed-adic-subspaces-and-embeddings`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.
 Library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.isClosedEmbedding_spaComap_quotientHom`.

*Sources.* Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Example 2.4.9; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.7 (ii), p. 24.

#### Closed immersions and Zariski closed immersions are different notions

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/closed-immersion-vs-zariski-closed` (comparison); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/ZariskiClosed`.

(a) Every strongly Zariski closed map is Zariski closed, and every Zariski closed immersion is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion). (b) The image of an immersion is stable under generalization, so a closed subset of |X| that is not (the closed point of Spa(K, K⁺) for K⁺ of rank two) is not the image of any immersion: the Zariski statements do not extend to arbitrary closed subsets. (c) A closed immersion need not be Zariski closed: for X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) with C a perfectoid field and ϖ ∈ C a pseudouniformizer with compatible roots, the subset T := ⋂_n {|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|} (the closed annulus {|T| = 1} together with the rank-two point y with |T(y)| = 1⁻) is the complement of the open unit disc, hence closed, and ι : Z_𝒰 → X for 𝒰 = {{|ϖ^{1/pⁿ}| ≤ |T|}} (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets) is a closed immersion with image T; but T is not Zariski closed, since every g ∈ C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ vanishing on T vanishes at the Gauss point, hence is 0 (the Gauss norm is the spectral norm), while T ≠ X. (d) Equivalently, a closed immersion Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces does not force R → S to be surjective (Berkeley Lectures, remark after Definition 17.4.2).

*Hypotheses.* Perfectoid spaces over no fixed base; C any perfectoid field in (c).

*Proof outline.*

1. (b): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing; the closed point K⁺ has the generalization K°.
2. (c): T is an intersection of rational subsets, so ι is an injection with |ι| a homeomorphism onto T (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets); the complement of T is ⋃_n {|T| < |ϖ^{1/pⁿ}|}, a union of rational subsets, so T is closed and ι is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion).
3. (c), not Zariski closed: if T = V(I) then every g ∈ I vanishes at the Gauss point η ∈ T, whose value is the spectral (Gauss) norm of g, so I = 0 and V(I) = X ∋ 0 ∉ T.
4. (d): here S = C⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and R → S is not surjective (T⁻¹ is not in the image), matching Berkeley's remark.

*Acceptance.* The closed point of Spa(K, K⁺) (rank two) is closed but not the image of an immersion; the closure of the annulus is the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski closed.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm`.

*Sources.* ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 17, remark after Definition 17.4.2, p. 155; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, before Definition 5.7, p. 24.

### P4.6 Diagonals, separatedness, valuative criterion; tilting

#### The diagonal of a morphism of perfectoid spaces is an immersion

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Separated`.

Let f : Y → X be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. Then Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion). More precisely: (a) Δ_f is a split monomorphism, hence an injection; (b) for open affinoids V ⊆ Y and U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, the restriction V → V ×_U V is strongly Zariski closed: the multiplication map from the affinoid ring of V ×_U V onto O_Y(V) is surjective and O⁺_Y(V) is the integral closure of the image of the plus ring; (c) the open subsets V ×_U V cover an open W ⊆ |Y ×_X Y| containing Δ_f(|Y|), and Δ_f(|Y|) is closed in W, with |Δ_f| a homeomorphism onto its image. (ECD Proposition 5.9.)

*Hypotheses.* Fibre products of perfectoid spaces (P2); on affinoids V ×_U V = Spa of the completed tensor product of O(V) with itself over O(U), which is already perfectoid (Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.4.1).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a): Mathlib instance `IsSplitMono (pullback.diagonal f)` and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces.
2. (b): the multiplication m satisfies m ∘ inl = id, so it is surjective and O⁺_Y(V) = m(inl(O⁺_Y(V))) is contained in the integral closure of m(plus ring), which is contained in O⁺_Y(V); hence V → V ×_U V is strongly Zariski closed (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion), so a Zariski closed, in particular closed, immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed).
3. (c): Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_U V) = V and Δ_f(|Y|) ∩ |V ×_U V| = Δ_f(|V|), which is closed in |V ×_U V| by (b); hence Δ_f(|Y|) is closed in W = ⋃ |V ×_U V| and locally closed in |Y ×_X Y|; pr₁ ∘ Δ_f = id shows that |Δ_f| is an embedding.

*Acceptance.* For Y = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) over X = Spa(C, O_C), Δ_f is the Zariski closed immersion defined by (T^{1/pⁿ} ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) in C⟨T^{1/p^∞}, S^{1/p^∞}⟩; the single equation T − S cuts out the larger set where T^{1/pⁿ} and S^{1/pⁿ} differ by p-power roots of unity. ECD Remark 7.9: Δ_f is therefore affinoid pro-étale locally.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-tensor-of-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`.
 Library: `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`, `CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono`, `IsLocallyClosed`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.9, p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.9, p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Remark 7.9, p. 32.

#### `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated` — Separated morphisms of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map` (definition); planet “Separated map of perfectoid spaces”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Separated`.

A morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is separated if its diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y is a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion) (ECD Definition 5.10); it is quasiseparated if Δ_f is quasicompact (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps). In Mathlib's vocabulary, IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion on Perfd, the pattern of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`. Since Δ_f is always an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map), f is separated if and only if Δ_f(|Y|) is closed. The category Perfd has no final object, so separatedness is a relative notion.

*Hypotheses.* Fibre products as in P2.

*Proof outline.*

1. The definition applies the closed-immersion notion to Δ_f; the reformulation uses that immersions with closed image are closed immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).

*Uses.* ECD Lemma 1.18 / Lemma 7.19 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-etale-maps-over-std-base: quasicompact separated maps to strictly totally disconnected spaces are classified by their fibres; ECD Theorem 1.19 and DiamondsAndVStacks:D3: separated étale and separated pro-étale maps form v-stacks; ECD Proposition 6.4 (iii) and PerfectoidSpaces:P5: separatedness descends to a finite stage of a limit; ECD Lemma 9.9: compactification of quasicompact separated étale maps over Spa(K, K⁺); ECD Definition 10.7 (iii) and DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/immersions-separatedness-and-truncatedness: for maps of perfectoid spaces separatedness of v-stacks agrees with this notion; PerfectoidSpaces:P8/analytically-separated-is-separated: analytically separated spaces are separated; Berkeley Lectures Definition 17.4.3 and Proposition 17.4.4: separated maps of v-sheaves.

*API.*

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated` (structure): Δ_f is a closed immersion.
- `PerfectoidSpace.isSeparated_iff_isClosed_range_diagonal` (characterisation): f is separated iff the image of |Δ_f| is closed.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.quasiSeparated` (relation): Separated morphisms are quasiseparated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.of_affinoid` (instance): Morphisms of affinoid perfectoid spaces are separated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.of_isInjection` (instance): Injections are separated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.comp` (structure): Composites of separated morphisms are separated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.baseChange` (functoriality): Base changes of separated morphisms are separated (closed immersions are stable under base change).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.of_comp` (other): If g ∘ f is separated then f is separated.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion` (characterisation): The valuative criterion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsSeparated.eq_of_eq_on_rankOne` (other): Uniqueness of extensions from Spa(R, R°) to Spa(R, R⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus).
- `PerfectoidSpace.isSeparated_eq_diagonal` (compatibility): IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion.

*Unit tests.*

- `isSeparated_affinoid` (computation): Every morphism Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) of affinoid perfectoid spaces is separated.
- `isSeparated_of_isInjection` (degenerate): Injections, in particular identities and open immersions, are separated: their diagonal is an isomorphism.
- `not_isSeparated_gluedDisc` (non-example): Glue two copies of the perfectoid closed disc over a perfectoid field C along the rational subset {|ϖ| ≤ |T|}; the result Y is quasiseparated over Spa(C, O_C) but not separated: for the rank-two point y of the disc with |T(y)| = |ϖ|⁻ (in the closure of the overlap, not in it), the point Δ_D(y) of the chart D₁ ×_C D₂ = D ×_C D lies in the closure of Δ_Y(|Y|) but not in Δ_Y(|Y|).
- `isSeparated_eq_diagonal` (compatibility): IsSeparated = MorphismProperty.diagonal IsClosedImmersion on Perfd, as for Mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.isSeparated_eq_diagonal_isClosedImmersion`.
- `isSeparated_iff_isClosed_range_diagonal` (characterisation): f is separated iff Δ_f(|Y|) is closed in |Y ×_X Y|.

*Acceptance.* Every morphism of affinoid perfectoid spaces is separated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces-are-separated). Separated maps are quasiseparated, and injections are separated (their diagonal is an isomorphism).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.
 Library: `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.diagonal`, `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.diagonal`, `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Definition 5.10, p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §1, before Lemma 1.18, p. 8.

#### Morphisms of affinoid perfectoid spaces are separated

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces-are-separated` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Separated`.

Every morphism f : Y → X between affinoid perfectoid spaces is separated; more precisely Δ_f is strongly Zariski closed, hence a Zariski closed immersion.

*Hypotheses.* X and Y affinoid perfectoid.

*Proof outline.*

1. PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map (b) with V = Y, U = X: Δ_f is strongly Zariski closed, hence a closed immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed), i.e. f is separated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map).

*Acceptance.* The structure map of the perfectoid closed disc to Spa(C, O_C) is separated.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, after Lemma 7.19, p. 37; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.9, p. 25.

#### Valuative criterion for separatedness of perfectoid spaces

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness` (theorem); planet “Valuative criterion for separatedness”; module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Separated`.

Let f : Y → X be a morphism of perfectoid spaces. The following are equivalent: (i) f is separated; (ii) |Δ_f| : |Y| → |Y ×_X Y| is a closed immersion of topological spaces; (iii) f is quasiseparated and for every affinoid perfectoid field (K, K⁺) and every commutative square formed by a : Spa(K, O_K) → Y and b : Spa(K, K⁺) → X with f ∘ a = b ∘ j (j : Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, K⁺) the inclusion of the rank-one point) there is at most one c : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y with c ∘ j = a and f ∘ c = b. (ECD Proposition 5.11.)

*Hypotheses.* No quasicompactness of f; quasiseparatedness appears in (iii).

*Proof outline.*

1. (i) ⇔ (ii): Δ_f is an immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map), so it is a closed immersion iff |Δ_f| is.
2. (ii) ⇒ (iii): closed immersions are quasicompact (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition), so f is quasiseparated. Two lifts give z : Spa(K, K⁺) → Y ×_X Y whose restriction to Spa(K, O_K) lands in Δ_f(|Y|); the rank-one point is dense in Spa(K, K⁺), so z lands in the closed set Δ_f(|Y|), and since Δ_f is an immersion z factors through it (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)); the two lifts agree.
3. (iii) ⇒ (ii): Δ_f is a quasicompact immersion, so locally its image is pro-constructible (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing), and its closure is the set of specializations (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible). A specialization w' of w = Δ_f(y) is the closed point of i_{w'} : Spa(K(w'), K(w')⁺) → Y ×_X Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection), whose rank-one point is the rank-one generalization of w, which lies in the generalization-stable set Δ_f(|Y|); so i_{w'} ∘ j factors through Δ_f, and uniqueness in (iii) applied to pr₁ ∘ i_{w'}, pr₂ ∘ i_{w'} shows that i_{w'} factors through Δ_f. Hence the image is closed under specialization, hence closed.

*Acceptance.* The glued disc of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map (test not_isSeparated_gluedDisc) violates (iii) at (K, K⁺) = (K(y), K(y)⁺): the rank-one point lies in the overlap and has two extensions. ECD Lemma 9.9: a separated étale map over Spa(K, K⁺) that is an isomorphism on rank-one points is an injection. Berkeley Proposition 17.4.4 and ECD Proposition 10.9 extend the criterion to v-sheaves and v-stacks (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3).

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/affinoid-perfectoid-field-points`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/maps-of-perfectoid-spaces-are-generalizing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets`.
 Library: `specializes_iff_mem_closure`, `StableUnderSpecialization`, `AlgebraicGeometry.ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.11 (i)-(ii), p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Proposition 5.11 (iii), p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.11, p. 26; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §9, proof of Lemma 9.9, p. 50.

#### Maps from Spa(R, R⁺) into a separated space are determined on Spa(R, R°)

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-unique-extension-from-rank-one-locus` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Separated`.

Let f : Y → X be a separated morphism of perfectoid spaces and (R, R⁺) a perfectoid Tate ring with a ring of integral elements R⁺ ⊆ R°. If a, b : Spa(R, R⁺) → Y satisfy f ∘ a = f ∘ b and a ∘ j = b ∘ j for the inclusion j : Spa(R, R°) → Spa(R, R⁺), then a = b. This is the perfectoid-space case of ECD Proposition 10.10, proved without reduction to totally disconnected spaces.

*Hypotheses.* f separated; (R, R⁺) any perfectoid pair (no base field).

*Proof outline.*

1. Let E := Spa(R, R⁺) ×_{(a,b), Y ×_X Y, Δ_f} Y → Spa(R, R⁺), the equalizer of a and b; it is a closed immersion, being a base change of Δ_f (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition).
2. Its image contains Spa(R, R°), which contains every rank-one point of Spa(R, R⁺): continuous rank-one valuations are ≤ 1 on power-bounded elements (Tau Ceti `Valuation.IsContinuous.le_one_of_isPowerBounded`).
3. Every point of Spa(R, R⁺) specializes its rank-one generalization, so the closed image is everything; E → Spa(R, R⁺) is then an injection that is a homeomorphism, hence an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria (iv)), and a = b.

*Acceptance.* For (R, R⁺) = (K, K⁺) an affinoid perfectoid field this is the uniqueness half of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/immersions-base-change-and-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`.
 Library: `Valuation.IsContinuous.le_one_of_isPowerBounded`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §10, Proposition 10.10, p. 52; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §10, proof of Proposition 10.10, p. 52; ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 17, after Definition 17.4.7, p. 157.

#### Tilting of injections, immersions, separatedness and strongly Zariski closed immersions

*Node* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-tilting` (comparison); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Morphisms/Tilting`.

Let X be a perfectoid space with tilt X♭ and f : Y → X a morphism with tilt f♭ : Y♭ → X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting; |Y| = |Y♭|, |X| = |X♭|). (a) f is an injection, an immersion, an open or closed immersion, quasiseparated or separated if and only if f♭ is. (b) For X = Spa(R, R⁺) and Z = Spa(S, S⁺) affinoid: f : Z → X is strongly Zariski closed if and only if f♭ is (Scholze torsion paper Lemma II.2.7). (c) Formulas for a strongly Zariski closed f with I := ker(R → S): I♭ := ker(R♭ → S♭) is a closed perfect ideal and I is the closure of the ideal generated by ♯(I♭); S♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} S⁺ and S♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ S⁺/ϖ compatibly with R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ; S⁺ = {s ∈ S : |s(z)| ≤ 1 for z ∈ |Z|}; and |Z| = V(I) = V(I♭) inside |X| = |X♭|.

*Hypotheses.* The tilt of a perfectoid space over X is taken through the slice equivalence Perfd/X ≅ Perfd/X♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a): tilting preserves fibre products (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products), so (Δ_f)♭ = Δ_{f♭}; injections are the maps with Δ an isomorphism (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces); the topological conditions only involve |f| = |f♭| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets); separatedness and quasiseparatedness are conditions on Δ.
2. (b): R → S surjective iff R♭ → S♭ surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (b)); almost surjectivity of R⁺ → S⁺ is almost surjectivity modulo ϖ (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion), and R⁺/ϖ → S⁺/ϖ is R♭⁺/ϖ♭ → S♭⁺/ϖ♭ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings, ECD Lemma 3.11); the plus-ring clause is preserved because R⁺ ↦ R♭⁺ is an inclusion-preserving bijection of rings of integral elements compatible with maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting).
3. (c): PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting (c); P1/tilt-integral-subrings; Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`; and |g(x♭)| = |g♯(x)| under the tilting homeomorphism, so V(I♭) = V(♯(I♭)) = V(I).

*Acceptance.* For R = C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = C (T^{1/pⁿ} ↦ 0), the tilt is C♭⟨T♭^{1/p^∞}⟩ → C♭ with I♭ the closure of (T♭^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0). Diagonals: (Δ_f)♭ = Δ_{f♭}, so f is separated iff f♭ is.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/perfectoid-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjections-and-closed-ideals-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/rings-of-integral-elements-under-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-map-of-spectra`.
 Library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_iff_forall_vle_one`.

*Sources.* Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, Lemma II.2.7, p. 15; Scholze-TorsionLocallySymmetric-2015, §II.2, proof of Lemma II.2.7, p. 15; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §3, Lemma 3.11, p. 17; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Theorem 2.4.4.

### Acceptance tests of the stage

- The origin of the perfectoid disc C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the Zariski closed subspace Z_{(T)} = Spa(C, O_C), with kernel the
  closure of (T^{1/pⁿ} : n ≥ 0) and not (T); R/(T) is not reduced.
- For I = (T − 1) in ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, Z_I = Spa(C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p), C⁰(ℤ_p, O_{ℂ_p})) and R → C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p) is surjective (via the
  imported ECD 5.8), correcting Scholze's Remark II.2.4 and Bhatt's Warning 9.4.2.
- The closure of the annulus {|T| = 1} is the image of a closed immersion that is not Zariski closed.
- A finite separable extension Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) is bijective on points but is not an injection, fails the
