  O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩/(T)[1/ϖ] are not perfectoid.

<a id="p5"></a>

## P5. Limits and étale finite-stage descent


This layer builds cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces and proves that étale objects over such a limit
come from a finite stage. It works over arbitrary perfectoid Tate rings in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 —
characteristic 0, characteristic p, or neither (products), with no perfectoid base field — and over the anchor's
adic spaces through the category Perfd of PerfectoidSpaces:P2. The source is Scholze, *Étale cohomology of
diamonds* (arXiv v4), Propositions 6.4 (o)–(iii) and 6.5 with their proofs, supplemented by Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.13,
Kedlaya–Liu I §2.6, the Berkeley lectures 7.4 and 8.2, Bhatt's notes §5.1 and BMS1 §3 where ECD leaves a step to the
reader.

Boundaries, stated once:

- The algebraic input on finite étale algebras — henselian pairs under completion and filtered colimits, finite
  étale algebras over a filtered colimit of rings, and over a completed direct limit of complete Tate rings (Elkik,
  Gabber–Ramero 5.4.54, Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8) — is PerfectoidSpaces:P3's (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions,
  P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings, P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit,
  P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation). It is needed already inside almost purity; this layer imports it.
- ECD Proposition 6.4 (iv), affinoid étale objects, is AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv; its
  assembly with (o)–(iii) is PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly. Nothing here claims (iv).
- The κ-small perfectoid spaces of ECD Definition 4.2 are PerfectoidSpaces:P6's; this layer proves the numerical
  bounds that make a limit κ-small. The cutoff cardinals themselves are DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal.
- Limits of towers of non-perfectoid spaces (Q_p(p^{1/p^n}), finite levels of Shimura varieties) are tilde-limits,
  PerfectoidSpaces:P7, with the general Huber carrier ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0.
- Pro-étale maps (ECD Definition 7.8, Proposition 7.10) are PerfectoidSpaces:P6; they are stated along the limits
  constructed here.

### Conventions

- *Standing setting.* I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of
  affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor Iᵒᵖ → CAff (complete Huber pairs,
  AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site) with every R_i perfectoid and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° a ring of integral
  elements; for a: j → i the map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous and carries R_i⁺ into R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`).
  Transition maps are not assumed injective, flat or of dense image.
- *Compatible pseudouniformiser.* A pair (i₀, ϖ) with ϖ ∈ R_{i₀}⁺ a pseudouniformiser, ϖ^p | p in R_{i₀}⁺, with
  compatible p-power roots; its images under all φ_a (a: j → i₀) are again such. Constructions are carried out on the
  tail I/i₀ (Mathlib `Over.initial_forget`) and are independent of the choices.
- *Completion.* R⁺ is always the ϖ-adic completion lim_n A/ϖ^nA of the uncompleted filtered colimit
  A = colim_i R_i⁺ (Mathlib `AdicCompletion`), and R = R⁺[1/ϖ] with R⁺ open carrying its ϖ-adic topology. Never the
  completion of colim R_i for another topology, never a uniformisation.

  ```text
      R_i⁺ ──→ colim_i R_i⁺ = A ──→ Â = R⁺ ⊂ R = R⁺[1/ϖ]        X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim_i X_i
  ```

- *ω₁-cofiltered* (ECD): every functor from a category with countably many morphisms to I extends to a cone; in
  Mathlib terms `IsCardinalFiltered Iᵒᵖ ℵ₁`.
- *2-colimits.* For a pseudofunctor from a filtered category to categories, 2-colim C_j has objects (j, x) and
  Hom((i, x), (j, y)) = colim over cospans of Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y) (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories).
  "Base change induces an equivalence 2-colim_i (X_i)_? → X_?" means: colim_j Hom_{X_j}(Y_j, Y_j') → Hom_X(Y, Y') is
  bijective and every object over X is a base change from some X_i.
- *Étale categories.* Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2,
  PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space); Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep are its full subcategories of
  finite étale, quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and
  quasicompact separated (ECD Definition 5.10) objects. Base change is the fibre product of
  PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces.

### Organisation

- P5.1 The completed direct limit (ring level): compatible pseudouniformiser, completion of integrally closed rings,
  the construction, perfectoidness, independence of choices (5 nodes; planet *Completed direct limit*).
- P5.2 The limit in Perfd and its underlying space: uniformity of perfectoid spaces, the limit (KEEP), the spectrum
  of a completed direct limit of Tate pairs, ECD 6.4(o), qcqs base changes, restriction to rational subsets,
  quasicompact opens in limits of spectral spaces and their descent (8 nodes; planet *Cofiltered limits*).
- P5.3 ω₁-cofiltered limits and topologically countably generated presentations, ECD 6.5 (3 nodes; planet
  *ω₁-cofiltered limits*).
- P5.4 Cardinal bounds (1 node).
- P5.5 Finite-stage descent, ECD 6.4 (i)–(iii): the filtered 2-colimit, finite étale objects, faithfulness,
  isomorphism detection, fullness, gluing, qcqs étale descent, separatedness, qc separated descent, and the KEEP
  assembly (10 nodes; planet *Finite-stage descent*).


### P5.1 The completed direct limit

#### `compatible-pseudouniformizer` — A compatible pseudouniformiser with p-power roots on a tail of a cofiltered system of perfectoid Tate pairs

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CompletedColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

**Statement.** Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Claim: for every object i₀ of I there is ϖ ∈ R_{i₀}⁺ such that (a) ϖ is a pseudouniformiser of R_{i₀} (a topologically nilpotent unit, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`), ϖ^p divides p in R_{i₀}⁺, and ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ R_{i₀}⁺ (ϖ^{1/p^{n+1}})^p = ϖ^{1/p^n}; (b) for every morphism a: j → i₀ of I, φ_a(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of R_j, φ_a(ϖ)^p divides p in R_j⁺, and the φ_a(ϖ^{1/p^n}) are compatible p-power roots of φ_a(ϖ) in R_j⁺. Such a pair (i₀, ϖ) is called a compatible pseudouniformiser of the system ('any compatible choice of pseudouniformizers for large i' in ECD 6.4). The comma category I/i₀ (objects j with a morphism to i₀; Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Over i₀`) is initial in I, so every limit over I may be computed on the tail I/i₀. For two parallel morphisms a, b: j ⇉ i₀ the elements φ_a(ϖ), φ_b(ϖ) of R_j need not agree; they have the same image in colim_i R_i⁺, which is the only place where compatibility is used.

**Hypotheses.**

- I small and cofiltered (in particular nonempty); every R_i a perfectoid Tate ring (ECD Definition 3.1) with a ring of integral elements R_i⁺.
- Transition maps are continuous ring maps carrying R_i⁺ into R_j⁺; no injectivity, flatness or density is assumed.

**Proof outline.**

1. By PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots applied to (R_{i₀}, R_{i₀}⁺) there is a pseudouniformiser ϖ₀ ∈ R_{i₀}° with ϖ₀^p | p in R_{i₀}° and compatible p-power roots ϖ₀^{1/p^n}; these roots are topologically nilpotent, hence lie in R_{i₀}⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).
2. Put ϖ := (ϖ₀^{1/p})^{p-1}. Writing p = ϖ₀^p u with u ∈ R_{i₀}°, one has p = ϖ^p · (ϖ₀ u) and ϖ₀u is topologically nilpotent, hence in R_{i₀}⁺; so ϖ^p | p in R_{i₀}⁺, and (ϖ₀^{1/p^{n+1}})^{p-1} is a compatible system of p-power roots of ϖ in R_{i₀}⁺. ϖ is a unit and topologically nilpotent, so a pseudouniformiser.
3. A continuous ring map sends units to units and topologically nilpotent elements to topologically nilpotent elements, and φ_a(R_{i₀}⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺; applying φ_a to p = ϖ^p·c and to the root relations gives (b).
4. Initiality of I/i₀ → I is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget` for cofiltered I; hence limits (and, dually, the colimits of rings over I^op used in P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs) are unchanged by passing to the tail.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD Proposition 6.4 and Proposition 6.5: the limit is formed with 'any compatible choice of pseudouniformizers for large i'
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: the ϖ-adic completion is taken with respect to the image of ϖ in colim R_i⁺
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/tilting-affinoid-etale-and-limits: chooses ϖ with compatible p-power roots on a tail to form ϖ♭
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit (R, R⁺) of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate pairs
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs is a perfectoid Tate pair
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit does not depend on the compatible pseudouniformiser or on the tail
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countable-perfectoid-hull: prerequisite of: Every countable subset of a perfectoid Tate ring lies in a closed, topologically countably generated perfectoid subring

**Acceptance.**

- For K = C_p and R_{i₀} = C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with R_{i₀}⁺ = O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, ϖ = p^{1/p} (with roots p^{1/p^{n+1}}) satisfies ϖ^p = p | p; its image under the continuous map T^{1/p^m} ↦ p^{1/p^{m+1}}T^{1/p^m} is again such a pseudouniformiser.
- In characteristic p (for instance R = F_p((t^{1/p^∞})) completed) the condition ϖ^p | p = 0 is empty and ϖ = t with roots t^{1/p^n} works, in accordance with ECD Proposition 3.5.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4, statement, p. 27: “Here, ϖ ∈ Ri+ denotes any compatible choice ... of pseudouniformizers for large i.” — The notion 'compatible choice of pseudouniformizers for large i' that this lemma makes precise (object i₀, element ϖ, the tail I/i₀).
- ECD, Section 3, Lemma 3.10, p. 16: “Furthermore, there exists a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R with ϖp |p in R◦ which admits a sequence” — Existence of a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p and p-power roots, the input of step 1.
- ECD, Section 3, Example 3.22 (ii), p. 19: “Indeed, if ϖ is a pseudo-uniformizer, and x ∈ R◦ , then ϖx is topologically nilpotent.” — Why ϖ₀u lies in the ring of integral elements in step 2.

#### `completion-preserves-integral-closedness` — The ϖ-adic completion of a ring integrally closed in its localisation away from a nonzerodivisor

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/IntegralClosure`, namespace `TauCeti`.

**Statement.** Let A be a commutative ring and ϖ ∈ A a nonzerodivisor such that A is integrally closed in A[1/ϖ] (Mathlib `IsIntegrallyClosedIn A (Localization.Away ϖ)`). Let Â := lim_n A/ϖ^nA be its ϖ-adic completion (Mathlib `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A`). Then: (a) Â is ϖ-adically complete and separated, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on Â, and A/ϖ^nA → Â/ϖ^nÂ is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 1; (b) the kernel of A → Â is J := ⋂_n ϖ^nA, which satisfies J = ϖJ, and A/J is again ϖ-torsion free and integrally closed in (A/J)[1/ϖ]; (c) Â is integrally closed in Â[1/ϖ]; (d) if A is p-root closed in A[1/ϖ] (g ∈ A[1/ϖ] and g^p ∈ A imply g ∈ A), so is Â in Â[1/ϖ]; (e) for the topology on Â[1/ϖ] in which Â is open with its ϖ-adic topology, the image of A[1/ϖ] is dense. No noetherian or separatedness hypothesis on A is made.

**Hypotheses.**

- ϖ a nonzerodivisor of A; A integrally closed in A[1/ϖ].
- A need not be ϖ-adically separated: filtered colimits of separated rings need not be separated, which is the case of interest.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Stacks Tag 05GG for the finitely generated ideal ϖA gives completeness of Â and Â/ϖ^nÂ = A/ϖ^nA (Mathlib `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete` for completeness). Torsion-freeness: if ϖ·(x_n)_n = 0 in lim A/ϖ^n then ϖx_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^{n+1}A, so x_{n+1} ∈ ϖ^nA because ϖ is a nonzerodivisor, hence x_n = 0 for all n.
2. (b) If x ∈ J then x = ϖy_n with y_n ∈ ϖ^{n-1}A, and y_n = y_m by torsion-freeness, so J = ϖJ; A/J is ϖ-torsion free and integrally closed in its localisation because J is uniquely ϖ-divisible, J = J[1/ϖ] (Bhatt, Lemma 5.1.2, first paragraph). Replace A by A/J; now A ⊆ Â and A = Â ∩ A[1/ϖ] inside Â[1/ϖ].
3. (c) Let g = ϖ^{-c}h (h ∈ Â, c ≥ 0) satisfy g^d + s_{d-1}g^{d-1} + … + s_0 = 0 with s_k ∈ Â, so h^d + Σ_k s_k h^k ϖ^{c(d-k)} = 0. Choose N ≥ c(d+1) and a, a_k ∈ A with a ≡ h and a_k ≡ s_k mod ϖ^NÂ (possible by (a)). Then e' := a^d + Σ_k a_k a^k ϖ^{c(d-k)} ∈ A has image in ϖ^NÂ; as A/ϖ^NA → Â/ϖ^NÂ is injective, e' = ϖ^N e with e ∈ A. Hence z := a/ϖ^c ∈ A[1/ϖ] satisfies z^d + Σ_k a_k z^k - ϖ^{N-cd}e = 0, a monic equation over A, so z ∈ A. Therefore g = z + ϖ^{-c}(h - a) ∈ A + ϖ^{N-c}Â ⊆ Â.
4. (d) The same approximation with the equation T^p - g^p (Bhatt, Lemma 5.1.1(1)).
5. (e) A → Â has dense image since Â/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n; inverting ϖ preserves density.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit (R, R⁺) of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate pairs
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs is a perfectoid Tate pair
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit: prerequisite of: ω₁-cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces need no completion

**Acceptance.**

- A = Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] (the union of the Z_p[p^{1/p^n}]) with ϖ = p: Â is the valuation ring of the completion of Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}), integrally closed in its fraction field.
- The hypothesis in (c) is needed: A = Z_p[pζ_p] ⊆ Q_p(ζ_p) is p-adically complete and ζ_p ∈ A[1/p] is integral over A but not in A.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:AdicCompletion`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosedIn`.

**Sources.**

- Bhatt, notes, Section 5.1, Lemma 5.1.2, printed p. 34 (PDF p. 35): “Lemma 5.1.2. Let A be a ring equipped with a nonzerodivisor f ∈ A. Assume that A ⊂ A[ f1 ] is integrally closed.” — Statement (c): the f-adic completion of a ring integrally closed in A[1/f] is integrally closed in Â[1/f].
- Bhatt, notes, Section 5.1, Lemma 5.1.1 and its proof, printed p. 33 (PDF p. 34): “We first check that we can replace A with its maximal separated quotient A/I, where I = ∩n f n A.” — Step (b), passage to the separated quotient, and (d) p-root closedness.
- Stacks, Tag 05GG (Lemma 10.96.3): “In particular $R^\wedge $ is $I$-adically complete, $I^ nR^\wedge = (I^ n)^\wedge $, and $R^\wedge /I^ nR^\wedge = R/I^ n$.” — Statement (a) for the finitely generated ideal ϖA.

#### `completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs` — The completed direct limit (R, R⁺) of a filtered system of perfectoid Tate pairs

*construction.* **Planet:** *Completed direct limit*. Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CompletedColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

**Statement.** Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Fix a compatible pseudouniformiser (i₀, ϖ) (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer). Put A := colim_{i ∈ I^op} R_i⁺, the filtered colimit of rings (Mathlib `CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimit`), and write ϖ for its image in A. Define R⁺ := Â = lim_n A/ϖ^nA, the ϖ-adic completion of A, and R := R⁺[1/ϖ], topologised so that R⁺ is an open subring with its ϖ-adic topology (so (R⁺, ϖR⁺) is a pair of definition and R is a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ). For i in the tail I/i₀ the canonical map ι_i: R_i = R_i⁺[1/ϖ] → R is continuous with ι_i(R_i⁺) ⊆ R⁺ and ι_j ∘ φ_a = ι_i; (R, R⁺) with the ι_i is the completed direct limit of the system. Conventions: the completion is the ϖ-adic completion of the uncompleted colimit of the plus rings, never a completion of colim R_i for some other topology; A need not be ϖ-adically separated, so the ι_i need not be injective; R⁺ is integrally closed in R and (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid); the construction is independent of (i₀, ϖ) and of the tail (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice). Universal property: for every complete Tate pair (S, S⁺) with S⁺ bounded in S (for instance S uniform) and every compatible family of morphisms of pairs ψ_i: (R_i, R_i⁺) → (S, S⁺), i ∈ I/i₀, there is a unique morphism of pairs ψ: (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with ψ ∘ ι_i = ψ_i.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting of this layer; a compatible pseudouniformiser (i₀, ϖ).
- The universal property is stated for targets whose plus ring is bounded (hence ϖ-adically complete); it is not claimed for arbitrary complete Huber pairs.

**Proof outline.**

1. A exists as a filtered colimit in CommRingCat (mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit); ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A since it is a unit in every R_i ⊇ R_i⁺ and multiplication by ϖ is injective at every stage of the filtered colimit.
2. A[1/ϖ] = colim R_i (localisation commutes with filtered colimits) and A is integrally closed in it: an integral equation lives at a finite stage, where R_i⁺ is integrally closed in R_i.
3. R⁺ := Â is ϖ-adically complete, ϖ-torsion free, with R⁺/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (a)); R := R⁺[1/ϖ] with basis of neighbourhoods {ϖ^nR⁺} is a complete Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing with pair of definition (R⁺, ϖR⁺), tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition).
4. Each R_i⁺ is bounded and open in the uniform ring R_i (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras), so its subspace topology is the ϖ-adic one (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero); hence R_i⁺ → A → Â is continuous, and so is its extension ι_i to R_i = R_i⁺[1/ϖ]; the ι_i are compatible by construction of the colimit.
5. Universal property: the ψ_i induce A → S⁺ (colimit property), which is continuous for the ϖ-adic topology because S⁺ is bounded and open, hence carries the ϖ-adic topology; S⁺ is closed in the complete S, so ϖ-adically complete, and the map extends uniquely to Â → S⁺; invert ϖ (a unit in S). Uniqueness follows from density of A in Â (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (e)).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD Proposition 6.4 and Proposition 6.5: the inverse limit is X = Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ]
- ECD proof of Proposition 8.5: the pullback of Y ↦ (O⁺(Y)/ϖ)^a to the pro-étale site sends lim Y_i to (colim O⁺(Y_i)/ϖ)^a, i.e. R⁺/ϖ = colim R_i⁺/ϖ
- Sch12 Lemma 6.13 and Lemma 7.5: perfectoid algebras are written as completed direct limits of p-finite ones, and R_fét is computed on the completion of the direct limit
- Berkeley Definition 8.2.1 and Example 8.2.2: affinoid pro-étale maps are completed filtered colimits of pairs; X × S for a profinite set S
- Scholze 2013 Lemma 4.5: Û = Spa of the completion of the direct limit of the (R_i, R_i⁺) for a pro-étale presentation
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization: O⁺ of X^wl is the ϖ-adic completion of the pullback of O⁺_X
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds: S × Spa(K, O_K) = Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K)) for profinite S
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond: the completion of A_∞ = colim A_i and its plus ring
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/cofiltered-limit-presentation-approximation: R⁺⟨T⟩/ϖ^M = colim (R_i⁺/ϖ^M)[T], i.e. the quotient formula
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/completed-tower-self-product: the completed colimit over open normal subgroups of products of Â_∞
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower: the limit of a tower of perfectoid pairs is the completed direct limit

**API.**

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Perfectoid.completedColimit` | data | For a functor D: Iᵒᵖ ⥤ CAff whose values are perfectoid Tate pairs and a compatible pseudouniformiser (i₀, ϖ): the topological ring R = R⁺[1/ϖ]. |
| `Perfectoid.completedColimitPlus` | data | The ring R⁺ = ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺, as an open subring of Perfectoid.completedColimit (Mathlib AdicCompletion of the CommRingCat filtered colimit). |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `completedColimit_test_initial` (degenerate): If I has an initial object i_* (so the diagram of rings has a terminal index), then ι_{i_*}: (R_{i_*}, R_{i_*}⁺) → (R, R⁺) is an isomorphism of Huber pairs.
- `completedColimit_test_profinite` (computation): For S = lim_n {0,1}^n and R_n = K^{S_n}, R_n⁺ = O_K^{S_n} over a perfectoid field K: R⁺ = C^0(S, O_K) and R = C^0(S, K); the function s ↦ Σ_k s_k ϖ^k lies in R⁺ but in no ι_n(R_n⁺).
- `completedColimit_test_plusQuotient` (characterisation): In the profinite example R⁺/ϖ^n = C^0(S, O_K/ϖ^n) equals the ring of locally constant functions S → O_K/ϖ^n = colim_n (O_K/ϖ^n)^{S_n}.
- `completedColimit_test_uncompleted` (non-example): In the profinite example the uncompleted colimit colim R_n = LC(S, K) with the ϖ-adic topology on LC(S, O_K) is not complete, so it is not the ring of functions of the limit.
- `completedColimit_test_compatibility_sch12` (compatibility): For a system of perfectoid affinoid K-algebras over a perfectoid field K, (R, R⁺) is the completed direct limit of Sch12 Lemma 6.13 and, for systems of uniform Banach algebras with submetric transition maps, the completion of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.6.1 (the infimum seminorm and the ϖ-adic topology on colim R_i⁺ agree).
- `completedColimit_test_not_injective` (non-example): For R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (all n) with transition maps T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m}, the element T ∈ R_0⁺ is divisible by every ϖ^n in colim R_n⁺, so ι_0(T) = 0 in R⁺ = O_K: the maps ι_i need not be injective.

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: K a perfectoid field, S = lim_n S_n with S_n = {0,1}^n, R_n = K^{S_n}, R_n⁺ = O_K^{S_n}; then A is the ring of locally constant functions S → O_K, R⁺ = C^0(S, O_K) and R = C^0(S, K).
- ECD Example 5.2: for x in an affinoid perfectoid X₀, the rational neighbourhoods U ∋ x give R⁺ = K(x)⁺, with K(x)⁺/ϖ = colim_{U ∋ x} O⁺(U)/ϖ.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site`, `mathlib:CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.colimitCoconeIsColimit`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4, statement, p. 27: “Consider the inverse limit X = Spa(R, R+ ), where R+ is the ϖ-adic completion of limi Ri+” — The formula R⁺ = ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺, R = R⁺[1/ϖ].
- Sch12, Section 6, proof of Lemma 6.13 (i), p. 37: “This shows that R+ is the completed direct limit of the RI+ , i.e. (R, R+ ) is the completed direct limit of the (RI , RI+ ).” — The notion of completed direct limit of perfectoid affinoid algebras, over a perfectoid field.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Definition 2.6.1, p. 53: “We will refer to the completion ... with respect to α as the completed direct limit of the system.” — The same notion for Banach algebras (affinoid systems).
- Bhatt, notes, Section 6.2, Remark 6.2.9, printed p. 48 (PDF p. 49): “Likewise, one checks that filtered colimits in Perf K ◦a are computed by simply π-adically completing the underlying filtered colimit of K ◦a -algebras.” — Filtered colimits of perfectoid algebras are π-adic completions of the uncompleted colimit.

#### `completed-colimit-is-perfectoid` — The completed direct limit of perfectoid Tate pairs is a perfectoid Tate pair

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CompletedColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

**Statement.** In the situation of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: (a) R⁺ is open and bounded in R and integrally closed in R, so R⁺ is a ring of integral elements and ϖR° ⊆ R⁺ ⊆ R°; (b) R is uniform; (c) ϖ^p divides p in R⁺, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R⁺, and Frobenius R⁺/ϖR⁺ → R⁺/ϖ^pR⁺, x ↦ x^p, is an isomorphism, so R⁺ is an integral perfectoid ring (BMS1 Definition 3.5); (d) R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings for the filtered system i ↦ R_i over (I/i₀)^op with the pseudouniformiser ϖ, hence a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 whose tilt R♭ is the completed direct limit of the R_i♭; so (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair and the ι_i are morphisms of perfectoid Tate pairs; (e) if all R_i have characteristic p then R is a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p; if the system lives over a perfectoid Tate ring B (compatible maps B → R_i) then R is a perfectoid B-algebra. No perfectoid base field is assumed. Perfectoidness of the ring and its tilt are the P1 theorem; this node adds the plus ring R⁺ = completion of colim R_i⁺.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; (i₀, ϖ) a compatible pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p in R_{i₀}⁺ (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer).
- The R_i are perfectoid; a completed colimit of non-perfectoid rings can be perfectoid, but that situation is a tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7) and is not covered here.

**Proof outline.**

1. (d): on the tail, i ↦ R_i is a filtered system of perfectoid Tate rings over (I/i₀)^op with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer). Since ϖR_i° ⊆ R_i°° ⊆ R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent), A = colim R_i⁺ ⊆ colim R_i° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A, so the ϖ-adic completions of the two colimits give the same complete Tate ring: R is the completed filtered colimit of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings, a perfectoid Tate ring by (b) there, with tilt the completed direct limit of the R_i♭ by (c) there. In particular R is uniform: (b).
2. By P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness applied to A (ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on A, being a unit in every R_i ⊇ R_i⁺; A is integrally closed in A[1/ϖ] = colim R_i because an integral equation lives at a finite stage, where R_i⁺ is integrally closed): R⁺/ϖ^n = A/ϖ^n, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on R⁺, and R⁺ is integrally closed in R.
3. (a): R⁺ is bounded (a ring of definition), hence R⁺ ⊆ R°. For x ∈ R°, ϖx is topologically nilpotent, so some power lies in the open R⁺, and ϖx ∈ R⁺ by integral closedness (the argument of ECD Example 3.22(ii); tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent).
4. (c): for i in the tail, Frobenius R_i⁺/ϖ → R_i⁺/ϖ^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring (b)); filtered colimits are exact, so Frobenius A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p is bijective, hence so is R⁺/ϖ → R⁺/ϖ^p (previous step), and ϖ^p | p in A ⊆ R⁺. With ϖ-adic completeness and ϖ a nonzerodivisor, R⁺ is integral perfectoid by BMS1 Lemma 3.10(ii) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison), as BMS1 Lemma 3.20 also gives from (d).
5. (d), pairs: R⁺ is a ring of integral elements of the perfectoid Tate ring R by (a), so (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras) and ι_i(R_i⁺) ⊆ R⁺ by construction.
6. (e): in characteristic p use ECD Proposition 3.5 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect); B-algebra structures pass to colimits and completions.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice: prerequisite of: The completed direct limit does not depend on the compatible pseudouniformiser or on the tail
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: prerequisite of: Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit: prerequisite of: ω₁-cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces need no completion
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation: prerequisite of: Finite étale objects over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces come from a finite stage (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i))

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: C^0(S, K) is a perfectoid Tate ring for every profinite S and perfectoid field K, with C^0(S, K)° = C^0(S, O_K).
- Scholze 2013, proof of Lemma 4.6: the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebras is perfectoid affinoid; this node proves it without a base field.
- Non-example of the hypothesis: the tower Q_p(p^{1/p^n}) consists of discretely valued, non-perfectoid fields (ECD Remark 3.3); its completed colimit is perfectoid but is not an instance of this theorem.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/frobenius-surjective-on-plus-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “As (R, R+ ) is perfectoid, it follows that X = Spa(R, R+ ) is the limit in perfectoid spaces.” — ECD asserts perfectoidness of the completed colimit without argument; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-tate-rings supplies it for the ring and this node for the plus ring (recorded in sourceIssues).
- Scholze 2013, Section 4, end of the proof of Lemma 4.6, p. 25: “But the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K + )-algebras is again perfectoid affinoid.” — The same assertion over a perfectoid field K.
- BMS1, Section 3, Lemma 3.20, p. 26: “Let R be a complete Tate ring with a ring of integral elements R+ ⊂ R. If R is perfectoid in Fontaine’s sense, then R+ is perfectoid. Conversely, if R+ is perfectoid and bounded in R, then R is perfectoid in Fontaine’s sense.” — The comparison between the perfectoid ring R and its plus ring R⁺, step (c).
- BMS1, Section 3, Lemma 3.10 (ii), p. 22: “(ii) Conversely, if ϕ : S/πS → S/π p S is an isomorphism and π is a non-zero-divisor, then Ker θ is a principal ideal (and hence S is perfectoid).” — The integral criterion applied to R⁺ in step (c).

#### `limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice` — The completed direct limit does not depend on the compatible pseudouniformiser or on the tail

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CompletedColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

**Statement.** In the situation of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs: (a) if (i₀, ϖ) and (i₀', ϖ') are two compatible pseudouniformisers, the ϖ-adic and ϖ'-adic topologies on A = colim R_i⁺ coincide, and the identity of A induces an isomorphism of Huber pairs (R_ϖ, R_ϖ⁺) ≅ (R_ϖ', R_ϖ'⁺) compatible with all ι_i; (b) for an initial functor u: I' → I (for instance the inclusion of a tail I/i₁, or of a cofinal subposet) the completed direct limit of the restricted system is canonically isomorphic to that of the original one, compatibly with the ι; (c) these isomorphisms compose (for three choices, the composite of two comparison isomorphisms is the third) and commute with the universal property `lift`; (d) consequently Spa(R, R⁺) with its projections to the X_i is well defined up to unique isomorphism.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; I cofiltered.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Choose k ∈ I with morphisms to i₀ and i₀'. In R_k both images are pseudouniformisers and ϖR_k⁺, ϖ'R_k⁺ are open neighbourhoods of 0; since ϖ' is topologically nilpotent, ϖ'^N ∈ ϖR_k⁺ for some N, and symmetrically ϖ^N ∈ ϖ'R_k⁺. Hence ϖ'^{Nn}A ⊆ ϖ^nA and ϖ^{Nn}A ⊆ ϖ'^nA for all n, the two filtrations are cofinal, the two completions of A coincide, and ϖ' becomes a unit in R_ϖ (it divides ϖ^N, a unit).
2. (b) Restriction along an initial functor does not change the colimit of rings (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.colimitIso` for the opposite functor; `CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget` for tails), and the pseudouniformiser is unchanged.
3. (c) Uniqueness in the universal property of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs.
4. (d) Apply Spa and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer (the perfectoid property does not depend on ϖ).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: prerequisite of: Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition: prerequisite of: Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)

**Acceptance.**

- In the profinite example, ϖ, ϖ^{1/p} and uϖ (u ∈ O_K^×) give the same C^0(S, O_K); restricting to S_n with n ≥ 5 gives the same pair.
- If I has a terminal object t, every object maps to t, the tail I/t is all of I, and (b) for this tail is the identity.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Over.initial_forget`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.colimitIso`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.5, statement, p. 29: “(for some compatible choice of ... pseudouniformizer ϖ for all large enough i)” — The construction depends a priori on a choice made for large i; this lemma removes the dependence.
- ECD, Section 3, Remark 3.2, p. 14: “The condition that Φ : R◦ /ϖ → R◦ /ϖp is an isomorphism is independent of the choice of a pseudo-uniformizer ϖ ∈ R such that ϖp |p.” — Independence of the perfectoid condition from ϖ, used in (d).

### P5.2 The limit in perfectoid spaces and its underlying space

#### `integral-sections-are-varpi-complete` — Uniformity of perfectoid spaces: global integral sections are ϖ-adically complete

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Let Y be a perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space) and ϖ ∈ O_Y(Y) a unit whose restriction to every affinoid perfectoid open U ⊆ Y is a pseudouniformiser of O_Y(U) (for instance the pullback of a pseudouniformiser along a morphism Y → Spa(R_{i₀}, R_{i₀}⁺)). Then O_Y⁺(Y) is ϖ-torsion free and ϖ-adically complete and separated, and the restriction maps O_Y⁺(Y) → O_Y⁺(U) to affinoid perfectoid opens are continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, the ϖ-adic topology of O_Y⁺(U) being its subspace topology in O_Y(U). Consequently, for every ring A containing ϖ, every ring map A → O_Y⁺(Y) extends uniquely to the ϖ-adic completion Â, and the induced maps Â[1/ϖ] → O_Y(U) are continuous.

**Hypotheses.**

- Y perfectoid; ϖ a pseudouniformiser on every affinoid perfectoid open of Y.

**Proof outline.**

1. Affinoid case: for U = Spa(S, S⁺) affinoid perfectoid, O_Y⁺(U) = S⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity, H^0(U, O⁺) = S⁺; anchor Layer 2.3, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)); S⁺ is bounded and open in the complete uniform ring S, hence ϖ-adically complete, separated and ϖ-torsion free with the ϖ-adic topology equal to the subspace topology.
2. Cover Y by affinoid perfectoid opens U_k and each U_k ∩ U_l by affinoid perfectoid opens W_{klm} (P2/perfectoid-space). O⁺_Y is a sheaf (the subsheaf of functions of absolute value ≤ 1, anchor Layer 3.3), so O⁺_Y(Y) is the kernel of ∏_k O⁺(U_k) ⇉ ∏ O⁺(W_{klm}).
3. Products of ϖ-adically complete ϖ-torsion-free modules are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free (ϖ^n∏M_k = ∏ϖ^nM_k); the kernel K of a map M → N of such modules satisfies K ∩ ϖ^nM = ϖ^nK because N is ϖ-torsion free, and K is closed, so K is ϖ-adically complete.
4. Extension: A → O⁺_Y(Y) is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, hence extends uniquely to Â (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`); continuity into O_Y(U) follows from step 1.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces: prerequisite of: Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces

**Acceptance.**

- For Y = S × Spa(K, O_K) with S profinite, O⁺(Y) = C^0(S, O_K) is ϖ-adically complete although it is a limit over the finite covers of S.
- The statement fails for non-uniform adic spaces: for a complete Tate ring S whose S⁺ is unbounded the ϖ-adic topology of S⁺ is strictly finer than its subspace topology, which is why the limit of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces is taken in perfectoid spaces.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “The first part follows from uniformity of perfectoid spaces, which means that whenever Y maps compatibly to all Xi , the map limi Ri+ → O+ (Y ) extends uniquely to the ϖ-adic completion” — The 'uniformity of perfectoid spaces' used for the universal property is exactly this lemma.

#### `cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces` — Cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (kept identifier)

*construction.* **Planet:** *Cofiltered limits*. Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Standing setting of this layer: p is a fixed prime; I is a small cofiltered category; X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, is a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces, given at ring level by a functor I^op → CAff (complete Huber pairs, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site), i ↦ (R_i, R_i⁺), with each R_i a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras; characteristic 0, p or mixed, no perfectoid base field) and R_i⁺ ⊆ R_i° open and integrally closed; for a morphism a: j → i of I the transition map φ_a: R_i → R_j is continuous with φ_a(R_i⁺) ⊆ R_j⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom`). Let (R, R⁺) be the completed direct limit for a compatible pseudouniformiser (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs), a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid), and put X := Spa(R, R⁺), an affinoid perfectoid space (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), with projections p_i: X → X_i induced by ι_i (i in the tail; for general i through any j → i, i₀). Then (X, (p_i)) is a limit of the diagram (X_i) in the category of perfectoid spaces: for every perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i) is bijective. In particular X is the limit in the full subcategory of affinoid perfectoid spaces, O_X(X) = R and O⁺_X(X) = R⁺, and X is independent of the choices up to unique isomorphism (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice). Companion statements: |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism, ECD 6.4(o)); rational subsets and their rings are computed at finite stages (P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets); for ω₁-cofiltered I no completion is needed (P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit); cardinal bounds (P5/limit-cardinal-bounds). The limit is claimed in perfectoid spaces only; for a non-uniform adic space Y a compatible family Y → X_i need not induce a map continuous for the ϖ-adic topology of colim R_i⁺.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; the X_i are affinoid perfectoid (the construction is not applied to non-perfectoid X_i: such towers are tilde-limits, PerfectoidSpaces:P7).
- Morphisms into affinoid perfectoid spaces are described by the adjunction of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids (Huber 1994, Proposition 2.1(ii)) for sheafy pairs; perfectoid pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy).

**Proof outline.**

1. X is an affinoid perfectoid space: (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair (P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid), sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy, so Spa(R, R⁺) is an affinoid adic space (anchor Layer 5) and perfectoid (P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), with (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) = (R, R⁺) (P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis (iv)).
2. For a perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, Spa(S, S⁺)) = Hom_CAff((S, S⁺), (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y))) naturally in Y for sheafy (S, S⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids).
3. A compatible family f_i: Y → X_i gives compatible morphisms (R_i, R_i⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)), hence A = colim R_i⁺ → O_Y⁺(Y); ϖ maps to a pseudouniformiser on every affinoid perfectoid open, so the map extends uniquely to R⁺ = Â → O_Y⁺(Y) (P5/integral-sections-are-varpi-complete) and then to R = R⁺[1/ϖ] → O_Y(Y), continuously into each O_Y(U).
4. Uniqueness: two maps (R, R⁺) → (O_Y(Y), O_Y⁺(Y)) agreeing on the dense images of the R_i agree (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs, API denseRange_ι, and Hausdorffness of O_Y(U)). Hence Hom(Y, X) = lim Hom(Y, X_i).
5. Independence of choices: P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid: an infinite intersection of sets {|f| ≤ 1} in an affinoid perfectoid space is a cofiltered limit of rational subsets, hence affinoid perfectoid with the intersection as underlying space
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization: X^wl = lim T over finite disjoint unions T of rational subsets, with O⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of the pullback of O⁺_X
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover: X_∞ = lim_J X_J over finite subsets J of the affinoid étale surjections, and its κ-smallness
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence: presentations of κ'-small affinoids as cofiltered limits of κ-small affinoids (through the ω₁-presentation of P5/countably-generated-decomposition)
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds: S × Spa(K, O_K) is the limit of S_i × Spa(K, O_K)
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond: Spd of the completion of A_∞ is the inverse limit, with |Spa| the limit of the |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)|
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv and A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4: ECD 6.4(iv) is stated along these limits and assembled with P5's (o)-(iii)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6 (ECD Definition 7.8, Proposition 7.10): affinoid pro-étale maps are cofiltered limits of affinoid étale maps
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison: a limit of perfectoid affinoids in perfectoid spaces is a tilde-limit
- ECD Lemma 7.13, Lemma 7.18, Proposition 8.2: w-localisation, the universally open strictly totally disconnected cover and cutoff independence are built from such limits

**API.**

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `cofilteredLimit_test_profinite` (computation): For a perfectoid field K and S = lim_n {0,1}^n: cofilteredLimit (n ↦ {0,1}^n × Spa(K, O_K)) ≅ Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K)), with underlying space S × |Spa(K, O_K)|.
- `cofilteredLimit_test_initial` (degenerate): If I has an initial object i_*, then p_{i_*}: cofilteredLimit X → X_{i_*} is an isomorphism.
- `cofilteredLimit_test_residueField` (characterisation): For x ∈ X₀ affinoid perfectoid, the limit over the rational neighbourhoods of x is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺), and the induced map to X₀ is the injection i_x of ECD Example 5.2 (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection); for a filtered family of rational subsets the limit is the pro-rational subspace of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets.
- `cofilteredLimit_test_fibreProduct` (compatibility): For an affinoid perfectoid Y_i → X_i, Y_i ×_{X_i} cofilteredLimit X ≅ cofilteredLimit (j ↦ Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j) over the tail, compatibly with the fibre products of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces.
- `cofilteredLimit_test_notPerfectoidTower` (non-example): The system n ↦ Spa(Q_p(p^{1/p^n}), Z_p[p^{1/p^n}]) is not a diagram of perfectoid spaces, so the construction does not apply to it.
- `cofilteredLimit_test_uncompletedPair` (non-example): In the profinite example the Huber pair (LC(S, K), LC(S, O_K)) (uncompleted colimit) has the same Spa as the limit but is not complete, so Spa of it is not the limit perfectoid space.

**Acceptance.**

- Berkeley Example 8.2.2: for a perfectoid field K and a profinite set S = lim S_n, lim_n (S_n × Spa(K, O_K)) = Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K)); this is the S × Spa(K, O_K) of DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds.
- ECD Example 5.2: for x in an affinoid perfectoid X₀, lim_{U ∋ x rational} U = Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺) in perfectoid spaces; more generally, for a filtered family 𝒰 of rational subsets of an affinoid perfectoid X₀ (transition maps the restrictions), the construction specialises to PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets and PerfectoidSpaces:P4/residue-field-point-injection.
- The tower Spa(Q_p(p^{1/p^n}), Z_p[p^{1/p^n}]) is not a diagram of perfectoid spaces (ECD Remark 3.3); identifying Spa of the completion of Q_p(p^{1/p^∞}) with its limit is a tilde-limit statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P7, not an instance of this node.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/integral-sections-are-varpi-complete`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.5, statement, p. 29: “Then the inverse X = limi Xi in the category of perfectoid spaces exists, is affinoid perfectoid” — Existence of the limit in perfectoid spaces and its affinoid perfectoidness.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “The first part follows from uniformity of perfectoid spaces, which means that whenever Y maps compatibly to all Xi , the map limi Ri+ → O+ (Y ) extends uniquely to the ϖ-adic completion” — The proof of the universal property (steps 3-4).
- ECD, Section 5, Example 5.2, p. 21: “In fact, Spa(K(x), K(x)+ ) is the inverse limit of U (considered as a perfectoid space) in the category of perfectoid spaces, as” — The residue-field test.
- Berkeley lectures, Lecture 8, Example 8.2.2, printed p. 57: “If X is any perfectoid space and S is a profinite set, we can define a new perfectoid space X × S as the inverse limit of X × Si , where S = limi Si” — The profinite test and the D4 use.

#### `spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs` — The adic spectrum of a completed direct limit of Tate pairs is the inverse limit of the adic spectra

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/FilteredColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`.

**Statement.** Let I be small cofiltered and (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i ∈ I} an Iᵒᵖ-indexed diagram of Tate Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`, `Huber.IsTateRing`; complete or not) with continuous morphisms of pairs, together with i₀, a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i₀}⁺ and rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i⁺ (i ∈ I/i₀) containing the image of ϖ with φ_a(A_{i,0}) ⊆ A_{j,0} (for uniform A_i take A_{i,0} = A_i⁺). Let L := colim A_i, L⁺ := colim A_i⁺ and L_0 := colim A_{i,0}, with the topology on L in which L_0 is an open subring with its ϖ-adic topology, and let (L̂, L̂⁺) be the completion. Then: (a) (L, L⁺) is a Tate Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (L, L⁺) are morphisms of pairs; (b) the map Spa(L, L⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) given by the Tau Ceti maps `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap` is a homeomorphism onto the inverse limit in topological spaces; (c) every rational subset of Spa(L, L⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset R(T_i/s_i) of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺), with T_i a finite set generating the unit ideal of A_i; (d) composing with the homeomorphism Spa(L̂, L̂⁺) ≅ Spa(L, L⁺) (Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 = Huber 1993 Proposition 3.9; requested from anchor Layer 2), (b) and (c) hold for the completed direct limit; the limit is a spectral space and the projections are spectral. For perfectoid pairs with A_{i,0} = A_i⁺ the completion is the (R, R⁺) of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs.

**Hypotheses.**

- The rings of definition must be chosen compatibly; the ϖ-adic topology on L_0 is the colimit topology used by Kedlaya–Liu (infimum seminorm) and by Sch12 Lemma 6.13(ii).
- The completion step is imported: Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets (Wedhorn 7.48, Huber 1993, 3.9), which the anchor's Layer 2 references but does not list as a target (requests.json).

**Proof outline.**

1. Points of Spv: a valuative relation on L restricts along each A_i → L (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap), compatibly; conversely a compatible family of valuative relations on the A_i defines one on L, because any two elements of L come from a common stage (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.3). So Spv(L) → lim Spv(A_i) is bijective.
2. Membership in Spa: for a Tate pair with ring of definition B ∋ ϖ, a valuation v lies in Spa iff v ≤ 1 on the plus ring and v(ϖ) is cofinal in the value group (Wedhorn Remark 7.11(1) with I = ϖB, an ideal of definition of B because the ϖ^nB form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero); since A = A⁺[1/ϖ], cofinality holds iff for every a with v(a) ≠ 0 there is n with v(ϖ^n) < v(a). Each condition involves finitely many elements, so v ∈ Spa(L, L⁺) iff every restriction lies in Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff).
3. Topology: rational subsets R(T/s) with T ⊆ L finite generating L form a basis of Spa(L, L⁺). Choose i where T, s and a relation Σ t b_t = 1 are defined; then R(T/s) is the preimage of R(T_i/s_i) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset). Preimages of opens of Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are open (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap). Hence the bijection is a homeomorphism and (c) holds.
4. (d) Transfer along Spa(L̂, L̂⁺) ≅ Spa(L, L⁺) (anchor Layer 2 request), which matches rational subsets. Spectrality: each Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is spectral (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition) and the transition maps are spectral (preimages of rational subsets are rational), so the limit is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism: prerequisite of: The underlying space of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the inverse limit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (o))
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens: prerequisite of: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: |Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K))| = S × |Spa(K, O_K)| = lim_n S_n × |Spa(K, O_K)|.
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (a) is the case of Kedlaya–Liu affinoid systems; DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond uses the case of a finite étale tower over a Tate pair with compatible rings of definition.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_comp`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`.

**Sources.**

- Sch12, Section 6, proof of Lemma 6.13 (ii), p. 37: “Then one checks by hand that Spa(L, L+ ) ∼ = lim Spa(Ri , Ri+ ) ... But then the same thing holds true for the completed direct limit by Proposition 2.11.” — The two steps: uncompleted direct limit by hand, then completion.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Remark 2.6.3, p. 53: “and also bijective because specifying a compatible system of semivaluations on each Ai bounded by αi is equivalent to specifying a semivaluation on A bounded by α.” — Step 1 (bijectivity on points).
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Remark 2.6.3, p. 53: “Moreover, every rational subspace of Spa(R, R+ ) arises from some Spa(Ai , A+ i ) by Remark 2.4.7.” — Statement (c).
- Wedhorn, Section 7.2, Remark 7.11 (1), p. 59: “(1) The proof of Theorem 7.10 shows that a valuation v on A is continuous if and only if v(a) is cofinal for Γv for all a ∈ I.” — The continuity criterion of step 2.
- Wedhorn, Section 7.5, Proposition 7.48, p. 68: “The canonical map Spa Â → Spa A is a homeomorphism which maps rational subsets to rational subsets.” — The completion step (d), requested from the anchor.
- Huber 1993, §3, Proposition 3.9, printed p. 468 (GDZ OCR): “Proposition 3.9 The canonical mapping g Spa Ä -^ Spa A is a homeomorphism, and It maps rational subsets to rational subsets” — Huber's original statement [Hub93a, 3.9] cited by ECD for 6.4(o).

#### `limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism` — The underlying space of a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the inverse limit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (o))

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Let X = lim_i X_i be the limit of a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). Then the map |X| → lim_i |X_i| induced by the projections is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces: lim_i |X_i| (inverse limit in topological spaces) is spectral, the projections |X| → |X_i| and the transition maps are spectral, and the map is a homeomorphism. Moreover every rational subset U ⊆ X equals p_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and some rational subset U_i ⊆ X_i.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; X the limit of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs to the perfectoid pairs with rings of definition A_{i,0} = R_i⁺ (bounded because R_i is uniform, P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras); its completion is (R, R⁺) (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs), so Spa(R, R⁺) → lim Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) is a homeomorphism and rational subsets descend.
2. Spectrality of the limit and of the projections: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces, with each |X_i| spectral and transition maps spectral (preimages of rational subsets are rational).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/pro-constructible-generalizing-subsets-are-affinoid: the underlying space of an intersection of rational subsets is the intersection
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/w-localization: |X^wl| = lim |T| over finite disjoint unions of rational subsets
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond: |Spa| of the completed tower is the limit of the |Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)|
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens: prerequisite of: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets: prerequisite of: Restriction of a cofiltered limit to a rational subset of a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes: prerequisite of: Base changes of a qcqs perfectoid space along a cofiltered limit form a limit, with spectral underlying spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition: prerequisite of: Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: |S × Spa(K, O_K)| = S × |Spa(K, O_K)|, with S carrying its profinite topology.
- ECD Example 5.2: |Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺)| = ⋂_{U ∋ x} U with the subspace topology, U ranging over rational neighbourhoods of x in X₀.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4 (o), p. 27: “(o) The map ... is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces.” — The statement of part (o).
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 27: “Part (o) follows from [Hub93a, Proposition 3.9], cf. [Sch12, Lemma 6.13 (ii)].” — The proof route: completion (Huber) and the direct limit computation (Sch12 6.13(ii)).
- Sch12, Section 6, Lemma 6.13 (ii), p. 37: “and each rational ... comes as the preimage of some rational Ui ⊂ Xi = Spa(Ri , Ri+ ).” — Descent of rational subsets.

#### `limit-of-qcqs-base-changes` — Base changes of a qcqs perfectoid space along a cofiltered limit form a limit, with spectral underlying spaces

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let g_i: Y_i → X_i be a morphism of perfectoid spaces with Y_i quasicompact and quasiseparated (for instance a qcqs étale Y_i), and put Y_j := Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j (a: j → i) and Y := Y_i ×_{X_i} X, fibre products of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then Y = lim_{j ∈ I/i} Y_j in perfectoid spaces, |Y| → lim_j |Y_j| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces, and for every affinoid perfectoid open V_i ⊆ Y_i the V_j := V_i ×_{X_i} X_j are affinoid perfectoid with V := V_i ×_{X_i} X = lim V_j (so O(V) is the completed direct limit of the O(V_j)).

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; Y_i qcqs; fibre products of perfectoid spaces exist and fibre products of affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

**Proof outline.**

1. Limits commute with fibre products: for perfectoid T, Hom(T, Y_i ×_{X_i} X) = Hom(T, Y_i) ×_{Hom(T, X_i)} lim_j Hom(T, X_j) = lim_j Hom(T, Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property).
2. Cover Y_i by finitely many affinoid perfectoid opens V_i^1, …, V_i^m; the V_j^k are affinoid perfectoid and V^k = lim_j V_j^k (step 1 with Y_i replaced by V_i^k), so |V^k| = lim |V_j^k| (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism).
3. The |V^k| form an open cover of |Y|, and a point (y_j) of lim |Y_j| lies in lim_j |V_j^k| for any k with y_i ∈ V_i^k, since V_j^k is the preimage of V_i^k; so the homeomorphisms glue to |Y| ≅ lim |Y_j|. Y_j is qcqs, so |Y_j| is spectral (quasiseparated: Mathlib `QuasiSeparatedSpace`), and the limit is spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens: prerequisite of: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-faithfulness: prerequisite of: Faithfulness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph argument)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection: prerequisite of: Surjectivity and isomorphism of qcqs étale maps are detected at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness: prerequisite of: Fullness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph approximation)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage: prerequisite of: Separatedness of a qcqs étale map is recognised at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit

**Acceptance.**

- For Y_i = Y_i' ×_{X_i} Y_i'' with Y_i', Y_i'' qcqs étale (the Z_i of ECD's proof of 6.4(ii)), |Z| = lim |Z_j|.
- Profinite sets: for a finite étale Y_0 → Spa(K, O_K) = X_0, Y = S × Y_0 and |Y| = S × |Y_0|.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `mathlib:QuasiSeparatedSpace`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), pp. 27-28: “We know that after pullback along |Z| → |Zi |, Z = Zi ×Xi X, the two quasicompact open images Γfi (|Yi |), Γgi (|Yi |) agree. As |Z| = limj |Zj | is an inverse limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps, these” — The identification |Z| = lim |Z_j| for the qcqs Z_i = Y_i ×_{X_i} Y_i', used without proof in ECD.

#### `limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets` — Restriction of a cofiltered limit to a rational subset of a finite stage

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let U_i ⊆ X_i be a quasicompact open subset, U_j := X(a)^{-1}(U_i) for a: j → i, and U := p_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ X. Then U = lim_{j ∈ I/i} U_j in perfectoid spaces. If U_i is rational, then each U_j is a rational subset of X_j, hence affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), U is a rational subset of X, and (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) is the completed direct limit of the (O_{X_j}(U_j), O⁺_{X_j}(U_j)): the canonical map from the ϖ-adic completion of colim_j O⁺_{X_j}(U_j) to O⁺_X(U) is an isomorphism (Sch12 Lemma 6.13(iii), Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.6.5(a)).

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; U_i quasicompact open (rational for the ring statement).

**Proof outline.**

1. Base change of an open immersion is the open subspace on the preimage: U_j = U_i ×_{X_i} X_j and U = U_i ×_{X_i} X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. For a perfectoid space Y, Hom(Y, U) is the set of f: Y → X with f(|Y|) ⊆ U; by P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces and P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism this is the set of compatible families f_j: Y → X_j with f_j(|Y|) ⊆ U_j, i.e. lim Hom(Y, U_j). So U = lim U_j.
3. Rational case: U_j and U are rational (preimages of rational subsets are rational, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset), affinoid perfectoid; P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces applied to (U_j) gives lim U_j = Spa of the completed direct limit, and uniqueness of limits identifies it with (O(U), O⁺(U)) (restriction maps: PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: for a clopen C_n ⊆ S_n, the restriction of S × Spa(K, O_K) to C × Spa(K, O_K) (C the preimage of C_n) is Spa(C^0(C, K), C^0(C, O_K)).
- For X₀ affinoid perfectoid and x ∈ U_0 rational, restricting the system of rational neighbourhoods of x to those inside U_0 does not change the limit Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-pair-rational-restriction`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.

**Sources.**

- Sch12, Section 6, Lemma 6.13 (iii), p. 37: “is equal to the completion of the filtered direct limit of ... where Uj is the preimage of Ui in Xj for j ≥ i.” — The ring statement for rational subsets.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Lemma 2.6.5 (a), p. 54: “(a) For any rational localization (R, R+ ) → (S, S + ), there exist an index i ∈ I and a” — Rational localisations of the completed direct limit come from a finite stage.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Lemma 2.6.5 (a), p. 54: “form another affinoid system with completed direct limit (S, S + ).” — The rational localisations form a system with completed direct limit the rational localisation of the limit.

#### `quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces` — Quasicompact opens, constructible sets and clopen sets in cofiltered limits of spectral spaces come from a finite stage

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/Topology/Spectral/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti`.

**Statement.** Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ S_i a diagram of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps f_a: S_j → S_i (Mathlib `SpectralSpace`, `IsSpectralMap`), and S = lim_i S_i with projections p_i. Then: (a) every quasicompact open U ⊆ S equals p_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and some quasicompact open U_i ⊆ S_i; more generally every constructible subset of S is the preimage of a constructible subset of some S_i; (b) if U_i, U_i' ⊆ S_i are quasicompact opens with p_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ p_i^{-1}(U_i') (resp. =), there is a: j → i with f_a^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ f_a^{-1}(U_i') (resp. =); in particular, if p_i^{-1}(U_i) = S then f_a^{-1}(U_i) = S_j for some a, and if p_i^{-1}(U_i) = ∅ then f_a^{-1}(U_i) = ∅ for some a; (c) finite unions and intersections of such identities hold at a common finite stage; (d) if U_i ⊆ S_i is a quasicompact open and p_i^{-1}(U_i) is open and closed in S, then f_a^{-1}(U_i) is open and closed in S_j for some a: j → i.

**Hypotheses.**

- I cofiltered; all S_i spectral and all transition maps spectral.

**Proof outline.**

1. S is spectral and the p_i are spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); the sets p_i^{-1}(V), V ⊆ S_i quasicompact open, form a basis of S closed under finite intersections (cofilteredness), so a quasicompact open is a finite union of them, all defined at a common stage: (a) for opens. Constructible sets: Stacks Tag 0A2Y.
2. (b): D := U_i ∖ U_i' is constructible, hence closed in the constructible topology and compact Hausdorff there (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite; tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible.isCompact); the preimages D_j (j over I/i) form a cofiltered diagram of compact Hausdorff spaces, spectral maps being continuous for the constructible topologies, with limit p_i^{-1}(D) = ∅. A cofiltered limit of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces is nonempty (mathlib:TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system), so some D_j is empty.
3. (c) Finitely many applications of (b) at a common stage (cofilteredness).
4. (d) S ∖ p_i^{-1}(U_i) is closed in the spectral space S, hence quasicompact, and open, so by (a) it is p_j^{-1}(W_j); apply (b) to U_j ∪ W_j = S_j and U_j ∩ W_j = ∅ at a further stage (the argument of ECD's proof of 6.4(iii)).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens: prerequisite of: Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-faithfulness: prerequisite of: Faithfulness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph argument)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection: prerequisite of: Surjectivity and isomorphism of qcqs étale maps are detected at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness: prerequisite of: Fullness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph approximation)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage: prerequisite of: Separatedness of a qcqs étale map is recognised at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit

**Acceptance.**

- S = lim_n {0,1}^n (Cantor set): its clopen subsets are exactly the preimages of subsets of some {0,1}^n; the open subset S ∖ {s} is not quasicompact and is not the preimage of an open subset of any finite stage, so quasicompactness is needed in (a).
- Sch12 Lemma 6.13(iv): a quasicompact open U_i containing the image of S contains the image of S_j for some j — the case p_i^{-1}(U_i) = S of (b).

**Prerequisites.** `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite`, `mathlib:SpectralSpace`, `mathlib:IsSpectralMap`, `mathlib:WithConstructibleTopology`, `mathlib:TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system`, `tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible`, `tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible.isCompact`.

**Sources.**

- Stacks, Tag 0A30 (Lemma 5.24.6): “Given any quasi-compact open $U \subset X$ there exists an $i \in \mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}\nolimits (\mathcal{I})$ and a quasi-compact open $U_ i \subset X_ i$ such that $p_ i^{-1}(U_ i) = U$.” — Statement (a) for quasicompact opens; the lemma also contains (b) and (c).
- Stacks, Tag 0A2Y (Lemma 5.24.4): “Then there exists an $i \in \mathop{\mathrm{Ob}}\nolimits (\mathcal{I})$ and a constructible subset $E_ i \subset X_ i$ such that $p_ i^{-1}(E_ i) = E$.” — Statement (a) for constructible sets.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (iii), p. 28: “then if Ui ⊂ Si is a quasicompact open subset whose inverse image U ⊂ S is open and closed, then the inverse image Uj ⊂ Sj is open and closed for large j.” — Statement (d).
- Sch12, Section 6, Lemma 6.13 (iv), p. 37: “(iv) If Ui ⊂ Xi is some quasicompact open subset containing the image of X, then there is some j such that the image of Xj is contained in Ui .” — The special case p_i^{-1}(U_i) = S of (b).
- Berkeley lectures, Lecture 8, proof of Lemma 8.2.4, printed p. 58: “If the inverse limit is empty, one of the terms has to be empty: this is a version of Tychonoff’s theorem” — The compactness argument of step 2.

#### `descent-of-quasicompact-opens` — Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a cofiltered limit descend to a finite stage

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Let X = lim X_i be as in P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, or more generally Y = lim_j Y_j for a qcqs Y_i → X_i and its base changes (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes). Then: (a) every quasicompact open U ⊆ |Y| is p_j^{-1}(U_j) for some j and some quasicompact open U_j ⊆ |Y_j|, and the open perfectoid subspace U is U_j ×_{Y_j} Y; (b) two quasicompact opens of |Y_j| with the same preimage in Y have the same preimage in some Y_k; if a quasicompact open contains the image of Y, it contains the image of Y_k for some k; (c) a quasicompact open of |Y_j| whose preimage in Y is open and closed has open and closed preimage in Y_k for some k; (d) every finite cover of Y by quasicompact opens is the pullback of a finite cover of some Y_j by quasicompact opens; (e) for Y = X: every rational subset of X is p_i^{-1}(U_i) for a rational subset U_i ⊆ X_i, i.e. for T ⊆ R finite generating R and s ∈ R there are i, T_i ⊆ R_i finite generating R_i and s_i ∈ R_i with R(T/s) = R(ι_i(T_i)/ι_i(s_i)).

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; for (a)-(d) any qcqs Y_i → X_i.

**Proof outline.**

1. |Y| = lim |Y_j| as spectral spaces (P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism for Y = X; P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes in general).
2. (a)-(d) are P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces applied to this limit; the open subspace structure: the base change of an open immersion is the open subspace on the preimage (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces, fibre products P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
3. (e) is P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs (c) for the perfectoid system.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage

**Acceptance.**

- ECD, proof of 6.4(ii): the image of f_i: Y_i → Y_i' is a quasicompact open over which Y' → Y_i' factors, hence Y_j' → Y_i' factors over it for large j.
- Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.6.7: any rational covering of the completed direct limit is defined at a finite stage.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “a standard quasicompactness argument implies that Yj′ → Yi′ factors over this open subset for large enough j” — Descent of containment of quasicompact opens, used for surjectivity.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 2.6, Remark 2.6.7, p. 54: “any rational covering of Spa(A, A+ ) is defined over some” — Statement (d)/(e) for rational coverings.
- Sch12, Section 6, Lemma 6.13 (ii), p. 37: “and each rational ... comes as the preimage of some rational Ui ⊂ Xi = Spa(Ri , Ri+ ).” — Statement (e).

### P5.3 ω₁-cofiltered limits and countably generated presentations

#### `omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit` — ω₁-cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces need no completion

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces assume that I is ω₁-cofiltered: every functor J → I from a category J with countably many morphisms extends to a cone J^◁ → I (equivalently Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered Iᵒᵖ ℵ₁`, ℵ₁ regular by `Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`). Then A = colim_i R_i⁺ is ϖ-adically separated and complete, so the canonical maps colim_i R_i⁺ → R⁺ and colim_i R_i → R are ring isomorphisms (bijective). Equivalently, for an ℵ₁-filtered diagram of perfectoid Tate pairs the uncompleted colimit (colim R_i, colim R_i⁺), with colim R_i⁺ carrying its ϖ-adic topology, is a perfectoid Tate pair and O(lim X_i) = colim O(X_i). For countable index categories such as I = ℕᵒᵖ both properties fail in general: colim R_i⁺ → R⁺ need be neither surjective nor injective.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; I ω₁-cofiltered in ECD's sense (a countable diagram in I has a cone).

**Proof outline.**

1. Separated: if x ∈ ⋂_n ϖ^nA, choose for each n a stage i_n and y_n ∈ R_{i_n}⁺ witnessing x = ϖ^n y_n in the colimit, together with the morphisms relating these stages to a stage of x; these form a countable diagram in I, which has a cone j. In R_j⁺ the image x_j satisfies x_j ∈ ϖ^nR_j⁺ for all n, so x_j = 0 as R_j⁺ is ϖ-adically separated; hence x = 0 in A.
2. Complete: a Cauchy sequence (x_n) in A with x_{n+1} - x_n ∈ ϖ^nA involves countably many elements and relations, all realised in a single R_j⁺ by ω₁-cofilteredness; R_j⁺ is ϖ-adically complete, so the sequence has a limit in R_j⁺ whose image is a limit in A.
3. Hence A → Â = R⁺ is bijective (P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness (a)); inverting ϖ, colim R_i = A[1/ϖ] → R⁺[1/ϖ] = R is bijective (P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.6: O and O⁺ commute with ω₁-filtered colimits, so they are small sheaves
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence: a sheaf commuting with ω₁-filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid pairs is small
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition: prerequisite of: Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)

**Acceptance.**

- ECD Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.6: O and O⁺ commute with ω₁-filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid pairs, which is this theorem applied to X ↦ O(X).
- Non-examples for I = ℕᵒᵖ: for the profinite system (S_n = {0,1}^n) colim R_n⁺ = LC(S, O_K) ≠ C^0(S, O_K) = R⁺ (not surjective); for R_n = K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ with T^{1/p^m} ↦ ϖ^{1/p^m}T^{1/p^m} the element T is in ⋂ ϖ^n colim R_n⁺, so colim R_n⁺ → R⁺ = O_K is not injective.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completion-preserves-integral-closedness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered`, `mathlib:Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.5, statement, p. 29: “If the index category I is ω1 -cofiltered, the maps” — Statement of the ω₁-bijectivity.
- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.5, definition following the statement, p. 29: “Recall that the index category I is ω1 -cofiltered if for any countable category J with a map J → I, one can find an extension J ◁ → I” — The definition of ω₁-cofiltered used here.
