- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “When I is ω1 -cofiltered, the colimit limi Ri+ is already complete, as any Cauchy sequence is” — Step 2 of the proof.
- ECD, Section 8, end of the proof of Proposition 8.5, p. 42: “One also sees that O and O+ are small as they commute with ω1 -filtered colimits of affinoid perfectoid rings (R, R+ ), see Proposition 6.5.” — The use of the theorem in ECD.

#### `countable-perfectoid-hull` — Every countable subset of a perfectoid Tate ring lies in a closed, topologically countably generated perfectoid subring

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/CountablyGenerated`, namespace `TauCeti.Perfectoid`.

**Statement.** Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid Tate pair and ϖ ∈ R⁺ a pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p in R⁺ and compatible p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} (P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer for the constant system). For every countable subset C ⊆ R there is a closed subring R' ⊆ R such that: C ∪ {ϖ, ϖ^{-1}} ∪ {ϖ^{1/p^n}} ⊆ R'; R' has a countable dense subset (equivalently R' is the closure of a countably generated subring: R' is topologically countably generated); R' with the subspace topology is a perfectoid Tate ring with R'° = R' ∩ R°; R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺ is a ring of integral elements of R', and the inclusion (R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺) is a morphism of perfectoid Tate pairs. Moreover |R'| ≤ 2^{ℵ₀}.

**Hypotheses.**

- (R, R⁺) perfectoid Tate pair (ECD Definition 3.1); C countable.

**Proof outline.**

1. Choose countable subrings D_0 ⊆ D_1 ⊆ … of R: D_0 is generated by C, ϖ^{±1}, the ϖ^{1/p^n} and p/ϖ^p; D_{k+1} is generated by D_k and, for each d ∈ D_k ∩ R°, elements y_d, z_d ∈ R° with d = y_d^p + ϖ^p z_d, which exist because Frobenius R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ^p is surjective for every pseudouniformiser with ϖ^p | p (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras, P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer). Put D := ⋃_k D_k (countable) and R' := closure of D.
2. R' is a closed subring of the complete R, hence complete; ϖ is a unit of R' (ϖ^{-1} ∈ D) and topologically nilpotent; R' ∩ R⁺ is open in R' and bounded, a ring of definition, so R' is a Tate ring (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing). A subset of R' is bounded in R' iff it is bounded in R (both are 'contained in ϖ^{-n}(R ∩ R⁺)'), so R'° = R' ∩ R° is bounded: R' is uniform.
3. Frobenius: for x ∈ R'° choose d ∈ D with x - d ∈ ϖ^pR⁺ ∩ R' (density; an open neighbourhood of 0 in R'). Then d ∈ D ∩ R°, so y_d, z_d ∈ D ∩ R° ⊆ R'°, and x - y_d^p = (x - d) + ϖ^p z_d ∈ ϖ^p R'°. Also ϖ^p | p in R'° since p/ϖ^p ∈ D ∩ R°. Hence R' is perfectoid (ECD Definition 3.1).
4. R'⁺ = R' ∩ R⁺ is open in R', integrally closed in R' (R⁺ is integrally closed in R) and contained in R'° (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements).
5. Cardinality: R' is complete metrisable with a countable dense subset, so every element is the limit of a sequence in D and |R'| ≤ ℵ₀^{ℵ₀} = 2^{ℵ₀} (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound, the case λ = ℵ₀).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countably-generated-decomposition: prerequisite of: Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)

**Acceptance.**

- For R = C^0(S, K) with S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁} and K = C_p, and C a countable set of functions depending only on the coordinates in a countable J ⊆ ℵ₁, one may take R' = C^0({0,1}^J, C_p) pulled back to S.
- If R already has a countable dense subset (for example C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), one may take R' = R.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/compatible-pseudouniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-condition-independent-of-pseudouniformizer`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound`, `mathlib:Cardinal.power_le_power_left`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “For the final statement, write (R, R+ ) as the (automatically ω1 -filtered) colimit of all perfectoid (Ri , Ri+ ) ⊂ (R, R+ ) that admit a countable dense subset.” — The family of perfectoid sub-pairs with a countable dense subset, whose supply this lemma guarantees (ECD gives no argument for it).
- ECD, Section 4, Remark 4.3, p. 20: “If A has a dense subalgebra A0 ⊂ A of cardinality less than κ, then A has cardinality less than κ.” — The cardinality count of the last step.

#### `countably-generated-decomposition` — Every affinoid perfectoid space is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.5)

*theorem.* **Planet:** *ω₁-cofiltered limits*. Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space and ϖ as in P5/countable-perfectoid-hull. Let 𝒮(R) be the set of closed subrings R' ⊆ R containing ϖ^{±1} that are perfectoid Tate rings for the subspace topology and admit a countable dense subset, ordered by inclusion, and put R'⁺ := R' ∩ R⁺. Then: (a) 𝒮(R) is ω₁-directed (every countable subset of 𝒮(R) has an upper bound in 𝒮(R)) and ⋃_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} R' = R; (b) colim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} (R', R'⁺) → (R, R⁺) is an isomorphism of Huber pairs, without completion; (c) X = lim_{R' ∈ 𝒮(R)} Spa(R', R'⁺) in perfectoid spaces and |X| = lim |Spa(R', R'⁺)|: X is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces with topologically countably generated rings of functions; (d) every R' ∈ 𝒮(R) has cardinality ≤ 2^{ℵ₀}; hence, for every uncountable strong limit cardinal κ (in particular every cutoff cardinal of ECD Lemma 4.1), X is an ω₁-cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces whose rings have cardinality < κ. This ω₁-presentation is the form in which ECD's cutoff-independence argument (Proposition 8.2) can be carried out for singular cutoff cardinals (see sourceIssues).

**Hypotheses.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; no countability assumption on R.

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) Given countably many R'_k ∈ 𝒮(R) with countable dense subsets C_k, apply P5/countable-perfectoid-hull to ⋃_k C_k to get R'' ∈ 𝒮(R) containing every C_k, hence every R'_k (R'' is closed). Every x ∈ R lies in the hull of {x}.
2. (b) The union of an ω₁-directed family of subrings is the colimit, and it equals R and R⁺ by (a); no completion is needed (P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit), and the topologies agree because R'⁺ carries the subspace, i.e. ϖ-adic, topology.
3. (c) P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces and P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism for the ω₁-cofiltered diagram 𝒮(R)^op, whose completed direct limit is (R, R⁺) by (b) (P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice for the choice of ϖ).
4. (d) P5/countable-perfectoid-hull; 2^{ℵ₀} < κ for κ an uncountable strong limit (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence: presentations of κ′-small affinoids by κ-small ones, in the ω₁ form (sourceIssues PerfectoidSpaces/E34)
- Berkeley lectures, proof of Lemma 17.1.8: reduction of v-descent of vector bundles to topologically countably generated Banach algebras

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(C^0(S, C_p), C^0(S, O_{C_p})) with S = {0,1}^{ℵ₁}: the subrings C^0({0,1}^J, C_p), J ⊆ ℵ₁ countable, are cofinal in 𝒮(R), since a continuous function on S depends on countably many coordinates.
- Degenerate case: if R has a countable dense subset, R is the largest element of 𝒮(R) and the presentation is trivial.
- Non-example: if R has no countable dense subset, X is not the limit of an ℕᵒᵖ-indexed tower of topologically countably generated affinoid perfectoid spaces (the union of the countable dense subsets of the images would be a countable dense subset of R), so an uncountable ω₁-cofiltered index category is necessary.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/countable-perfectoid-hull`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/omega1-cofiltered-uncompleted-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-underlying-space-homeomorphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-independence-of-tail-and-choice`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCardinalFiltered`, `mathlib:Cardinal.isRegular_aleph_one`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.5, statement, p. 29: “Moreover, any affinoid perfectoid space X = Spa(R, R+ ) can be written as an ω1 -cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces Xi = Spa(Ri , Ri+ ) where Ri and Ri+ are topologically countably generated (equivalently, have countable dense subsets).” — The statement of the decomposition.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29: “For the final statement, write (R, R+ ) as the (automatically ω1 -filtered) colimit of all perfectoid (Ri , Ri+ ) ⊂ (R, R+ ) that admit a countable dense subset.” — The index family 𝒮(R).
- ECD, Section 8, proof of Proposition 8.2, p. 39: “Then any κ′ -small affinoid Y → X can be written as a κ-cofiltered limit of affinoid Yj → X, by writing its ring of functions as a κ-filtered colimit of κ-small perfectoid rings.” — The presentation ECD's cutoff argument needs; for singular κ it has to be replaced by the ω₁-presentation (d) (sourceIssues).

### P5.4 Cardinal bounds

#### `limit-cardinal-bounds` — Cardinal bounds for cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Limits`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** Let κ be a cutoff cardinal (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal, ECD Lemma 4.1), λ < κ a cardinal, I a cofiltered category with fewer than λ morphisms, and X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (i ∈ I) a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces such that |R_i| < κ' for all i, for some strong limit cardinal κ' < κ (this holds when all X_i are κ'-small in the sense of ECD Definition 4.2). Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim X_i. Then |colim R_i⁺| < κ, |R⁺| < κ, |R| < κ, |X| < κ, and |O_X(U)| < κ for every open affinoid U ⊆ X. These are the two conditions of ECD Definition 4.2, so X is κ-small; PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space defines κ-smallness by exactly these conditions.

**Hypotheses.**

- κ as in ECD Lemma 4.1; I λ-small with λ < κ; each |R_i| < κ' with κ' < κ a strong limit cardinal.

**Proof outline.**

1. By clause (iii) of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (the κ_μ being cofinal in κ) choose a strong limit cardinal κ'' with κ' ≤ κ'' < κ and cofinality of κ'' larger than λ.
2. |colim R_i⁺| ≤ Σ_{i} |R_i| is a sum of fewer than λ < cf(κ'') cardinals each < κ'', hence < κ''.
3. R⁺ is first countable (ϖ-adic) with a dense subring (the image of colim R_i⁺) of cardinality μ < κ'' < κ, so |R⁺| ≤ μ^{ℵ₀} ≤ 2^μ < κ (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound; κ strong limit); |R| ≤ |R⁺|·ℵ₀ since R = ⋃_n ϖ^{-n}R⁺.
4. |X| ≤ |Set(R × R)| = 2^{|R|} < κ: a point of Spa(R, R⁺) is a valuative relation on R, i.e. a subset of R × R (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum; mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set).
5. For U ⊆ X open affinoid, U is a finite union of rational subsets U_k of X (quasicompactness), O(U) ↪ ∏_k O(U_k) (sheaf property, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), and O(U_k) has a dense subring of the form R[1/s_k] of cardinality |R| (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), so |O(U_k)| < κ by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover: X_∞ = lim_J X_J is κ-small
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space: the numerical bounds are the two conditions of ECD Definition 4.2

**Acceptance.**

- I = ℕᵒᵖ, K = C_p, S = {0,1}^ℕ: |C^0(S, C_p)| = 2^{ℵ₀} < κ for every cutoff cardinal κ.
- ECD's proof of Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): X_∞ = lim_J X_J with fewer than κ finite subsets J and κ-small X_J is κ-small.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, `mathlib:Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set`, `mathlib:Cardinal.power_le_power_left`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4, final statement, p. 27: “Moreover, if κ is as in Lemma 4.1 and I is λ-small for λ < κ and all Xi are κ′ -small for some” — The size statement of ECD 6.4.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 27: “For the set-theoretic part, we can by Lemma 4.1 assume that κ′ = κλ has cofinality larger than λ, in which case the cardinality of the direct limit of the Ri+ is still less than κλ , and so R is κ-small.” — Steps 1-3.
- ECD, Section 4, Lemma 4.1 (iii), p. 19: “(iii) For all cardinals λ < κ, there is a strong limit cardinal κλ < κ such that the cofinality of κλ is larger than λ.” — The clause of the cutoff lemma used in step 1.
- ECD, Section 4, proof of Proposition 4.4, p. 20: “the space |U | is a subset of the space of binary relations on A” — The bound |X| ≤ 2^{|R|} of step 4.

### P5.5 Finite-stage descent (ECD 6.4 (i)–(iii))

#### `filtered-two-colimit-of-categories` — The 2-colimit of a filtered diagram of categories

*construction.* Library: `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/FilteredTwoColimit`, namespace `TauCeti.CategoryTheory`.

**Statement.** Let J be a small filtered category and F a pseudofunctor from J (as a locally discrete bicategory) to categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`): categories C_j, functors F_a: C_i → C_j for a: i → j, and coherent natural isomorphisms F_{ba} ≅ F_b ∘ F_a and F_{id} ≅ id. The filtered 2-colimit 2-colim_j C_j is the category whose objects are pairs (i, x) with x an object of C_i, whose morphisms are Hom((i, x), (j, y)) := colim_{(k, a: i → k, b: j → k)} Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y) (a filtered colimit of sets over the category of cospans under i and j), with composition and identities induced from the C_k (Berkeley Remark 7.4.7). It carries functors ι_i: C_i → 2-colim C_j and isomorphisms ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i, and is the pseudo-colimit of F: pseudo-cocones (G_i: C_i → D, G_j ∘ F_a ≅ G_i coherently) correspond, up to unique isomorphism, to functors G: 2-colim C_j → D. For a pseudo-cocone the induced G is faithful iff morphisms in some C_k with equal images in D become equal in some further C_{k'}; full iff every morphism G_i x → G_j y of D comes from a morphism in some C_k; essentially surjective iff every object of D is isomorphic to some G_i x. In this layer J = Iᵒᵖ, C_i = a category of objects over X_i and F_a = base change; 'the base change functors induce an equivalence 2-colim (X_i)_? → X_?' means that the induced G is an equivalence.

**Hypotheses.**

- J small and filtered; F a pseudofunctor (base change is only defined up to canonical isomorphism).

**Proof outline.**

1. Composition: representatives f ∈ Hom_{C_k}(F_a x, F_b y), g ∈ Hom_{C_l}(F_c y, F_d z) are pushed to a common k' under k, l compatible on j (filteredness) and composed there, using the coherence isomorphisms of F; independence of representatives and associativity are checked at a further common stage.
2. The ι_i and ι_j ∘ F_a ≅ ι_i are the identity on representatives; a pseudo-cocone defines G(i, x) := G_i x and G on representatives via the cocone isomorphisms; uniqueness up to unique isomorphism is formal.
3. The three criteria unwind the definition of Hom in 2-colim C_j and Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence` (fully faithful and essentially surjective).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- Berkeley Remark 7.4.7 and Theorem 7.4.8: the category 2-lim of finite étale algebras over a directed system of Tate rings
- Sch12 Lemma 7.5 and ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)-(iv): finite étale, qcqs étale, qc separated étale and affinoid étale objects over a limit form the 2-colimit
- ECD proofs of Proposition 7.10 and Proposition 11.23: Y_ét,qcqs = 2-lim (Y_i)_ét,qcqs; F(Y) = 2-lim F(Y_µ) for the étale prestacks of diamonds
- Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.2.9 and Proposition 2.6.8; Kedlaya AWS Definition 4.1.1(a): the direct 2-limit of FÉt over a direct system of rings
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons: 2-colimits of finite étale, qcqs étale and qc separated étale objects over diamonds
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv and A3/independence-of-presentations: 2-colim (X_i)_ét,aff → X_ét,aff and the well-definedness of finite-stage models
- P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation, P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent, P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent: statements of ECD 6.4 (i)-(iii)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings and P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit: the 2-colimit of finite étale algebras over a filtered colimit of rings and over a completed direct limit of Tate rings (stated there in the explicit form of the criterion isEquivalence_desc_iff)

**API.**

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit` | data | For a filtered J and a pseudofunctor F from J to Cat: the category 2-colim F with objects Σ j, F.obj j. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.ι` | constructor | The canonical functor ι_j: F.obj j ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompIso` | structure | For a: i → j, the isomorphism F_a ⋙ ι_j ≅ ι_i, compatible with the coherence isomorphisms of F. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.homEquiv` | characterisation | Hom((i, x), (j, y)) ≃ colimit over cospans (k, a, b) of Hom_{F k}(F_a x, F_b y). |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.desc` | universal-property | The functor FilteredTwoColimit F ⥤ D induced by a pseudo-cocone (G_i, G_j ∘ F_a ≅ G_i). |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.ιCompDescIso` | simp | ι_i ⋙ desc G ≅ G_i. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.descUniqueIso` | extensionality | Any functor H with isomorphisms ι_i ⋙ H ≅ G_i compatible with the cocone is uniquely isomorphic to desc G. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.isEquivalence_desc_iff` | characterisation | desc G is an equivalence iff (a) for all (i, x), (j, y) the map colim_k Hom(F_a x, F_b y) → Hom_D(G_i x, G_j y) is bijective and (b) every object of D is isomorphic to some G_i x. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.equivOfFinal` | functoriality | For a final functor u: J' ⥤ J, the induced functor FilteredTwoColimit (F ∘ u) ⥤ FilteredTwoColimit F is an equivalence (restriction to a tail). |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.fullSubcategory` | compatibility | If C'_j ⊆ C_j are full subcategories stable under the F_a, then 2-colim C'_j is equivalent to the full subcategory of 2-colim C_j on the (i, x) with x ∈ C'_i. |
| `CategoryTheory.FilteredTwoColimit.equivConst` | example | For the constant pseudofunctor at a category C (identity transition functors), FilteredTwoColimit ≌ C. |

**Unit tests.** A plausible wrong definition fails one of these.

- `filteredTwoColimit_test_const` (degenerate): For J the one-object category and F = C, FilteredTwoColimit F ≌ C.
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_discrete` (computation): For J = ℕ and C_n the discrete category on a set E_n with maps E_n → E_{n+1}, FilteredTwoColimit F is equivalent to the discrete category on colim_n E_n.
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_finitelyPresentedModules` (compatibility): For a filtered diagram of rings B_j with colimit B, base change 2-colim_j Mod^{fp}(B_j) → Mod^{fp}(B) (finitely presented modules) is an equivalence (EGA IV 8.5.2).
- `filteredTwoColimit_test_notNaive` (non-example): Let C_0 have two objects with no morphisms between them and C_n (n ≥ 1) have two isomorphic objects, with the evident functors: in 2-colim the two objects of C_0 become isomorphic, so the naive category with object set colim Ob(C_n) and morphisms taken in C_0 is not equivalent to the 2-colimit.

**Acceptance.**

- Berkeley Remark 7.4.7: for the filtered system of categories of finite étale algebras over complete Tate rings A_i, Hom in the 2-colimit is the colimit of Hom over common targets, and the comparison functor to finite étale algebras over the completed colimit is an equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit read through isEquivalence_desc_iff).
- For the constant pseudofunctor at a category C over a filtered J the 2-colimit is equivalent to C.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsFiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Grothendieck`.

**Sources.**

- Berkeley lectures, Lecture 7, Remark 7.4.7, printed p. 54: “One has here a directed system of categories Ci , indexed by a filtered category I, with functors Fij : Ci → Cj for each morphism i → j in I.” — The input datum.
- Berkeley lectures, Lecture 7, Remark 7.4.7, printed p. 54: “The 2-limit C = 2- lim Ci is a category whose objects are objects of any Ci .” — The description of objects and (in the displayed formula) of morphisms as a colimit over common targets.
- Kedlaya–Liu I, Section 1.2, Remark 1.2.9, p. 15: “We may then define the direct 2-limit limi FÉt(Ri ).” — The same construction for finite étale algebras.

#### `finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation` — Finite étale objects over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces come from a finite stage (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i))

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) = lim_i X_i be a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). Then the base change functors (X_i)_fét → X_fét induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories). Ring form: base change S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R (no completion; the tensor product is finite projective over R) induces an equivalence 2-colim_i FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R), compatible with tensor products and ranks, and the plus rings of the corresponding perfectoid spaces are the integral closures of R_i⁺, R⁺. Explicitly: (lifting) every finite étale R-algebra is S_i ⊗_{R_i} R for some i and some finite étale R_i-algebra S_i; (uniqueness) for finite étale R_i-algebras S_i, S_i', every R-algebra map S_i ⊗ R → S_i' ⊗ R is the base change of an R_j-algebra map for some j → i, and two R_j-algebra maps with the same base change to R agree over some R_k. The theorem concerns finite étale algebras; finitely presented algebras over R do not in general come from a finite stage.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; (i₀, ϖ) a compatible pseudouniformiser.
- The algebraic input — finite étale algebras over a completed direct limit of complete Tate rings, through the henselian approximation theorem (Elkik; Gabber–Ramero arXiv Proposition 5.4.54 = book 5.4.53; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8) — is owned by PerfectoidSpaces:P3 (P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit, P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation) and imported; this node adds the identification of the completion with the limit's ring and the passage to spaces.

**Proof outline.**

1. Ring form: apply PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit to the filtered system (R_i) with the compatible rings of definition A_{i,0} = R_i⁺ (bounded, as R_i is uniform) and the compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ. Its proof is: 2-colim FÉt(R_i) ≅ FÉt(L) for L := colim R_i (P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings), L is topologically henselian with ring of definition L_0 = colim R_i⁺ (P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b), (c)), and FÉt(L) ≅ FÉt(L̂) (P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b); Gabber–Ramero 5.4.54 with t = ϖ, I = L_0; Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8).
2. The completion L̂ of L for the ϖ-adic topology on L_0 is the ring R of P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs (L̂_0 = R⁺ and L̂ = R⁺[1/ϖ]), and the composite 2-colim FÉt(R_i) → FÉt(R) is S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R because (S_i ⊗_{R_i} L) ⊗_L R = S_i ⊗_{R_i} R.
3. Geometric form: for an affinoid perfectoid Z = Spa(T, T⁺), W ↦ O(W) is an anti-equivalence Z_fét ≅ FÉt(T)^op with inverse S ↦ Spa(S, integral closure of T⁺ in S) (ECD after Definition 6.2; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (c), P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces, P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids, P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), and base change of spaces corresponds to S_i ↦ S_i ⊗_{R_i} R (P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD proof of Lemma 7.16: a split finite étale cover over a component spreads out
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: finite étale objects over affinoid pro-étale limits come from a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects: prerequisite of: Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii))

**Acceptance.**

- Profinite sets: finite étale C^0(S, K)-algebras are, locally on S, constant: each is (S_n-indexed family of finite étale K-algebras) ⊗ C^0(S, K) for some n.
- A finite étale cover of a limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the pullback of one at a finite stage, unique up to unique isomorphism after enlarging the stage (ECD proof of Lemma 7.16: a splitting over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood).
- Non-example: C^0(S, K)/(f) with f(s) = Σ_k s_k ϖ^k is finitely presented but not flat, so not a base change from any finite stage; the theorem is special to finite étale algebras.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-of-perfectoid-pairs`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `mathlib:CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4 (i), p. 27: “(i) The base change functors (Xi )fét → Xfét induce an equivalence of categories” — The statement of part (i).
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (i), p. 27: “This is a consequence [Sch12, Lemma 7.5 (i)] of a theorem of Elkik, [Elk73], (in the noetherian case) and Gabber–Ramero, [GR03, Proposition 5.4.53], in general.” — The proof route: filtered colimit, henselian comparison.
- Sch12, Section 7, proof of Lemma 7.5 (i), p. 41: “Because finite étale covers, and morphisms between these, are finitely presented objects, we have” — Step 1.
- Berkeley lectures, Lecture 7, Theorem 7.4.8, printed p. 54: “As a corollary, let Ai be a filtered directed system of complete Tate rings,” — The Tate-ring form (no base field) of the corollary proved here.
- Gabber–Ramero, Section 5.4, Proposition 5.4.54, p. 126 (arXiv numbering; book 5.4.53): “Then the base change functor R[t−1 ]-Alg → R∧ [t−1 ]-Alg induces an equivalence of categories from the category of finite étale R[t−1 ]-algebras to the category of finite étale R∧ [t−1 ]-algebras.” — The imported henselian theorem, owned by PerfectoidSpaces:P3.

#### `finite-stage-faithfulness` — Faithfulness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph argument)

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs and f_i, g_i: Y_i → Y_i' morphisms over X_i. If their base changes f, g: Y → Y' over X are equal, then f_j = g_j for some a: j → i (f_j, g_j the base changes to X_j). Equivalently, the functor 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs is faithful.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; Y_i, Y_i' qcqs étale over X_i.

**Proof outline.**

1. The graph Γ_{f_i}: Y_i → Z_i := Y_i ×_{X_i} Y_i' is a section of the projection Z_i → Y_i, which is étale (base change of Y_i' → X_i, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); sections of étale maps are open immersions (a section is the base change of the diagonal, an open immersion for étale maps: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5); AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (b) via P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale). Γ_{f_i} is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), so it is determined by the quasicompact open image Γ_{f_i}(|Y_i|) ⊆ |Z_i| (ECD Proposition 5.3(iv), PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria). Likewise for g_i.
2. Z_i is qcqs, and Z = Z_i ×_{X_i} X = lim_j Z_j with |Z| = lim |Z_j| spectral (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes).
3. The two images agree after pullback to |Z| (f = g); by P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (b) they agree after pullback to |Z_j| for some j. The base changes Γ_{f_j}, Γ_{g_j} are the graphs of f_j, g_j and have these pulled-back images, so f_j = g_j.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness: prerequisite of: Fullness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph approximation)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent: prerequisite of: Quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (ii))

**Acceptance.**

- Two X_0-endomorphisms of a finite étale Y_0 → X_0 that agree over the limit agree at a finite stage.
- Faithfulness fails for non-quasicompact Y_i: the argument needs the images of the graphs to be quasicompact.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 27: “Then Γfi and Γgi are injections, and thus are determined by the quasicompact open image of |Yi | in |Zi |.” — Step 1.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “two quasicompact open images agree after pullback to |Zj | for large j, which means that Γfj = Γgj , as desired. This proves faithfulness.” — Step 3.
- ECD, Section 5, Proposition 5.3, p. 21: “In particular, by (iv), given X, injections Y ,→ X of perfectoid spaces are determined by the injective map of topological spaces |Y | → |X|.” — Injections are determined by their image.

#### `finite-stage-isomorphism-detection` — Surjectivity and isomorphism of qcqs étale maps are detected at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let h_i: Y_i → Y_i' be a morphism in (X_i)_ét,qcqs with base changes h_j over X_j and h over X. (a) If |h| is surjective, then |h_j| is surjective for some a: j → i; in particular, if a qcqs étale Y_i → X_i has surjective base change to X, then Y_j → X_j is surjective for some j. (b) If h is an isomorphism, then h_j is an isomorphism for some j.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; h_i a morphism of qcqs étale X_i-spaces (automatically étale by cancellation, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (3)).

**Proof outline.**

1. (a) h_i is étale with quasicompact source, so W_i := h_i(|Y_i|) is a quasicompact open subset of |Y_i'| (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5)). The image of h_j is the preimage of W_i in |Y_j'|, because |Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_j'| → |Y_i| ×_{|Y_i'|} |Y_j'| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective; Y_j = Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_j'); likewise over X. If h is surjective, the preimage of W_i in |Y'| is |Y'| = lim |Y_j'| (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes), so by P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (b) the preimage of W_i in |Y_j'| is all of |Y_j'| for some j.
2. (b) Apply (a) to h_i and to the diagonal Δ_{h_i}: Y_i → Y_i ×_{Y_i'} Y_i, a morphism of qcqs étale X_i-spaces and an open immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5)), whose base change Δ_h is an isomorphism. For large j, Δ_{h_j} is a surjective open immersion, hence an isomorphism, so h_j is an injection (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces), and h_j is surjective by (a).
3. A surjective étale injection is an isomorphism: |h_j| is a continuous open bijection, hence a homeomorphism; by ECD Proposition 5.3(iv) (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria) h_j is final among maps whose underlying map factors continuously through |Y_j|, so id_{Y_j'} factors through h_j, and h_j is an isomorphism.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations: finite-stage models of affinoid étale objects are unique
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: étale surjections descend to a finite level
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness: prerequisite of: Fullness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph approximation)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects: prerequisite of: Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii))

**Acceptance.**

- ECD's proof of 6.4(ii) (the intermediate step to fullness) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/independence-of-presentations use (b).
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover and D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves use (a): an étale surjection over the limit is an étale surjection at a finite stage.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/fibre-product-points-surjective`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/injection-criteria`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “As an intermediate step to fullness, we check that if fi : Yi → Yi′ is a morphism over X whose pullback f : Y → Y ′ to X is an isomorphism, then the pullback fj : Yj → Yj′ to Xj is an isomorphism for large enough j.” — Statement (b).
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “Note that the image of fi is a quasicompact open subset, over which Y ′ → Yi′ factors; a standard quasicompactness argument implies that Yj′ → Yi′ factors over this open subset for large enough j, so that fj is surjective for large enough j.” — Statement (a).
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “As ∆fj is always an injection, this implies that ∆fj is an isomorphism, which then implies that fj is an isomorphism.” — The diagonal step of (b).
- ECD, Section 5, Proposition 5.3 (iv), p. 21: “(iv) The map |f | : |Y | → |X| is injective, and the map f : Y → X is final in the category of maps g : Z → X for which |g| : |Z| → |X| factors over a continuous map |Z| → |Y |.” — The injection criterion used in the last step.

#### `finite-stage-fullness` — Fullness of base change to a cofiltered limit on qcqs étale objects (graph approximation)

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs and let f: Y → Y' be a morphism over X between their base changes. Then there are a: j → i and a morphism f_j: Y_j → Y_j' over X_j whose base change to X is f. Together with P5/finite-stage-faithfulness: 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs is fully faithful.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting.

**Proof outline.**

1. The graph Γ_f: Y → Y ×_X Y' is a section of the étale projection, hence an open immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5); AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal (b)), with quasicompact image since Y is quasicompact.
2. |Y ×_X Y'| = lim_j |Z_j|, Z_j = Y_j ×_{X_j} Y_j' (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes); by P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (a) the image of Γ_f is the preimage of a quasicompact open V_j ⊆ |Z_j|, and V_j is an open perfectoid subspace of Z_j (P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces), qcqs étale over X_j.
3. The projection V_j → Y_j is a morphism in (X_j)_ét,qcqs whose base change to X is the isomorphism Γ_f(Y) → Y; by P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection (b), V_k → Y_k is an isomorphism for some k → j. Put f_k := pr_2 ∘ (V_k → Y_k)^{-1}: Y_k → Y_k'; its base change is pr_2 ∘ Γ_f = f.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD proof of Proposition 7.10: Hom_X(Y, Z) = colim Hom_X(Y_i, Z) for affinoid pro-étale Y and étale Z (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity: prerequisite of: Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent: prerequisite of: Quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (ii))

**Acceptance.**

- ECD's proof of Proposition 7.10: Hom_X(Y, Z) = colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z) for an affinoid pro-étale Y = lim Y_i and an étale Z, which is this fullness applied to Y_i ×_X Z → Y_i.
- A section over the limit of an étale cover descends to a section over a finite stage.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-faithfulness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “The graph Γf : Y ,→ Y ×X Y ′ is a quasicompact open embedding. By approximation of quasicompact open subsets, we can find a quasicompact open immersion Vj ⊂ Yj ×Xj Yj′ whose pullback agrees with the image of Γf .” — Steps 1-2.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “By the intermediate step, we see that Vj → Yj becomes an isomorphism for large enough j; composing the inverse with the map Vj ,→ Yj ×Xj Yj′ → Yj′ gives the desired map” — Step 3.

#### `qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity` — Every qcqs étale space over a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces descends to a finite stage

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces, every Y ∈ X_ét,qcqs is isomorphic over X to Y_i ×_{X_i} X for some i and some Y_i ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; Y quasicompact and quasiseparated, étale over X.

**Proof outline.**

1. Local structure: every point of Y has an open neighbourhood V with V ⊆ W → U ⊆ X, where U is a rational subset of X, W → U is finite étale (so W is affinoid perfectoid) and V is a rational subset of W (ECD Definition 6.2(ii); standard affinoid form AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism via PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids). As Y is quasicompact, finitely many such V^1, …, V^m cover Y.
2. Each piece descends: U = p_i^{-1}(U_i) for a rational U_i ⊆ X_i (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (e)); U = lim_j U_j (P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets); W → U descends to a finite étale W_j → U_j (P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation applied to the system (U_j)); W = lim W_j (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes), so the rational V ⊆ W descends to a rational V_j ⊆ W_j (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (e)). Thus V^k ≅ V^k_j ×_{X_j} X with V^k_j qcqs étale over X_j.
3. Gluing: Y is quasiseparated, so V^k ∩ V^l is a quasicompact open of V^k = lim_j V^k_j and descends to a quasicompact open V^{kl}_j ⊆ V^k_j (P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (a)); the identifications V^{kl} ≅ V^{lk} descend to isomorphisms over some X_j (P5/finite-stage-fullness and P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection (b)), and the finitely many cocycle conditions hold at a further stage (P5/finite-stage-faithfulness). Glue (anchor Layer 5 gluing, P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces) to Y_j, qcqs and étale over X_j, with Y_j ×_{X_j} X ≅ Y.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent: prerequisite of: Quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (ii))

**Acceptance.**

- A rational subset of a finite étale cover of a rational subset of X descends; a finite union of such opens glued along quasicompact overlaps descends.
- Non-example: for X = S × Spa(K, O_K) (S profinite without isolated points), the open subspace Y = X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K)) is étale and quasiseparated but not quasicompact, and it is not the base change of an open subspace of any finite stage.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-faithfulness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “It is enough to cover Y be quasicompact open subsets which descend to Xi for large i, as by fully faithfulness (and the assumption that Y is qcqs), the pieces will automatically glue for large enough i.” — Step 3 (gluing).
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 28: “Thus, we can assume that f is a composite of a rational open subset, a finite étale map, and a rational open subset. Each of these maps descends to Xi for large enough i (using (i)), finishing the proof of (ii).” — Steps 1-2.
- ECD, Section 6, Definition 6.2 (ii), p. 26: “(ii) The morphism f is étale if for all y ∈ Y , there are open subsets V ⊂ Y , U ⊂ X such that y ∈ Y , f (V ) ⊂ U , and there is a factorization” — The local structure used in step 1.

#### `qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent` — Quasicompact quasiseparated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (ii))

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X = lim_i X_i be a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). Then the base change functors (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs (the 2-colimit of P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories for the base-change pseudofunctor on Iᵒᵖ). Explicitly: for Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs, colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_j, Y_j') → Hom_X(Y, Y') is bijective, and every qcqs étale Y → X is isomorphic to the base change of some qcqs étale Y_i → X_i.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting.

**Proof outline.**

1. Base change preserves qcqs étale objects (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open; P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), so it defines a pseudo-cocone and a comparison functor from the 2-colimit.
2. Faithful: P5/finite-stage-faithfulness; full: P5/finite-stage-fullness; essentially surjective: P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity; conclude by the criterion `isEquivalence_desc_iff` of P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD proof of Proposition 7.10: Y_ét,qcqs = 2-lim (Y_i)_ét,qcqs
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv: full faithfulness of the affinoid étale comparison
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent: prerequisite of: Quasicompact separated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (iii))
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects: prerequisite of: Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii))

**Acceptance.**

- ECD proof of Proposition 7.10: for Y = lim Y_i affinoid pro-étale over X, Y_ét,qcqs = 2-colim (Y_i)_ét,qcqs.
- ECD proof of Lemma 7.16 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected): a qcqs étale cover of X that splits over a connected component Spa(C, C⁺) = lim of its clopen neighbourhoods splits over a neighbourhood.
- Quasicompactness is necessary: the non-quasicompact open X ∖ ({s₀} × Spa(K, O_K)) of S × Spa(K, O_K) does not descend.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-faithfulness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-fullness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-essential-surjectivity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 27: “Let Xét,qcqs ⊂ Xét denote the full subcategory of qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X (and similarly for Xi ).” — The statement of part (ii).
- ECD, Section 7, proof of Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “Recall that Yét,qcqs = 2- limi (Yi )ét,qcqs by Proposition 6.4 (ii).” — A use of part (ii) in ECD.

#### `separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage` — Separatedness of a qcqs étale map is recognised at a finite stage of a cofiltered limit

*lemma.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). In the situation of P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces let f_i: Y_i → X_i be qcqs étale. If the base change f: Y → X is separated (ECD Definition 5.10: Δ_f is a closed immersion; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map), then f_j: Y_j → X_j is separated for some a: j → i.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; f_i qcqs étale.

**Proof outline.**

1. For an étale map g: Z → T of perfectoid spaces, Δ_g: Z → Z ×_T Z is an open immersion (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open (5); ECD Proposition 5.9, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map), with quasicompact image when Z is quasicompact; g is separated iff |Δ_g| is a closed immersion (ECD Proposition 5.11 (i)⇔(ii), PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness), i.e. iff the quasicompact open Δ_g(|Z|) is also closed.
2. S_j := |Y_j ×_{X_j} Y_j| is spectral and lim_j S_j = |Y ×_X Y| (P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes applied to the qcqs Y_i ×_{X_i} Y_i); the preimage of U_i := Δ_{f_i}(|Y_i|) is Δ_f(|Y|), which is open and closed. By P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (d), the preimage U_j of U_i in S_j is open and closed for some j; U_j = Δ_{f_j}(|Y_j|) since diagonals commute with base change. So f_j is separated.

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent: prerequisite of: Quasicompact separated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (iii))
- PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects: prerequisite of: Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii))

**Acceptance.**

- Let X_n := {|T| ≤ |ϖ|^n} ⊆ X_0 = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), with limit Spa(K, K⁺) (the origin); Y_1 := two copies of X_1 glued along V_1 = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|^2} is qcqs étale over X_1 and not separated, while its base change to X_2 (two copies of X_2 glued along X_2) is X_2, which is separated: the stage must be enlarged.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-of-qcqs-base-changes`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/valuative-criterion-separatedness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map`.

**Sources.**

- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (iii), p. 28: “The map fj : Yj → Xj is separated if and only if the quasicompact open immersion ∆fj : Yj → Yj ×Xj Yj is also a closed immersion.” — Step 1.
- ECD, Section 5, Proposition 5.11 (ii), p. 25: “(ii) The map |∆f | : |Y | → |Y ×X Y | is a closed immersion.” — The topological criterion for separatedness.
- ECD, Section 6, proof of Proposition 6.4 (iii), p. 28: “we see that if ∆f is an open and closed immersion, then ∆fj is an open and closed immersion for large enough j.” — Step 2.

#### `quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent` — Quasicompact separated étale objects over a cofiltered limit form the 2-colimit (ECD Proposition 6.4 (iii))

*theorem.* Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X = lim_i X_i be a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Then the base change functors (X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep induce an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep, where X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs is the full subcategory of quasicompact separated étale perfectoid spaces over X (a separated étale space over an affinoid is quasiseparated).

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting.

**Proof outline.**

1. Base change preserves separatedness (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/separated-perfectoid-map), so (X_i)_ét,qc,sep are full subcategories stable under base change and the 2-colimit is the full subcategory of 2-colim (X_i)_ét,qcqs on separated objects (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories, API fullSubcategory); full faithfulness follows from P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent.
2. Essential surjectivity: a quasicompact separated étale Y → X is the base change of a qcqs étale Y_i → X_i (P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent), and Y_j → X_j is separated for some j (P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- ECD proof of Proposition 9.7: separated étale spaces with descent data over an affinoid pro-étale limit come from a finite stage

#### `finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects` — Finite-stage descent along cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4 (i)–(iii)) (kept identifier)

*theorem.* **Planet:** *Finite-stage descent*. Library: `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/FiniteStageDescent`, namespace `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`.

**Statement.** For a perfectoid space Z, Z_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over Z (ECD Definition 6.2, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), Z_fét, Z_ét,qcqs and Z_ét,qc,sep its full subcategories of finite étale, of quasicompact quasiseparated (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/quasicompact-and-quasiseparated-maps), and of quasicompact separated étale spaces, and base change along X_j → X_i or X → X_i is the fibre product of perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), which preserves these classes (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open). Let X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces with limit X = Spa(R, R⁺) (P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces). The base change functor Φ: 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qcqs → X_ét,qcqs is an equivalence of categories (ECD 6.4(ii)), and it restricts to equivalences 2-colim_i (X_i)_fét → X_fét (ECD 6.4(i)) and 2-colim_i (X_i)_ét,qc,sep → X_ét,qc,sep (ECD 6.4(iii)) on the full subcategories X_fét ⊆ X_ét,qc,sep ⊆ X_ét,qcqs (a finite étale space over an affinoid perfectoid space is affinoid perfectoid, hence quasicompact and separated). In explicit form: (full faithfulness) colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_j, Y_j') → Hom_X(Y, Y') is bijective for Y_i, Y_i' ∈ (X_i)_ét,qcqs; (essential surjectivity) every qcqs, resp. quasicompact separated, resp. finite étale, étale Y → X is the base change of a qcqs, resp. quasicompact separated, resp. finite étale, Y_i → X_i; (recognition) a morphism of (X_i)_ét,qcqs whose base change to X is surjective, resp. an isomorphism, is so over some X_j (P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection), and a qcqs étale Y_i whose base change is separated is separated over some X_j (P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage). Part (iv), affinoid étale objects, is AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-6-4-iv and is not claimed here; the cardinal bound of ECD 6.4 is P5/limit-cardinal-bounds.

**Hypotheses.**

- The standing setting; no noetherian or characteristic hypothesis.
- The henselian approximation used for (i) is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (Elkik, Gabber–Ramero).

**Proof outline.**

1. (i): P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation.
2. (ii): P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent.
3. (iii): P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent.
4. Compatibility: finite étale spaces over affinoid perfectoid spaces are affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), affinoid perfectoid spaces are quasicompact and separated, the inclusions commute with base change, and restriction of an equivalence to full subcategories that it matches is an equivalence (P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories, API fullSubcategory).

**Uses** (what the API is derived from).

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/strictly-totally-disconnected: a splitting of an étale cover over a connected component extends to a neighbourhood
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover: an étale cover of the limit comes from a finite stage and becomes split at the next
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves: a surjection of the pro-étale site is an étale surjection at a finite level
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks: spreading out qc separated étale objects and descent data to a finite level
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons: the three 2-colimit equivalences for diamonds are deduced by v-descent
- AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/etale-descent-to-finite-stage-6-4: ECD 6.4 assembled: (o)-(iii) from here, (iv) from A3

**Acceptance.**

- A finite étale cover of a limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces is the pullback of one at a finite stage, unique up to unique isomorphism at a further stage; an étale surjection over the limit is an étale surjection at a finite stage.
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons: for diagrams of diamonds the same three equivalences are deduced from this theorem by v-descent.
- Profinite sets: finite étale, qcqs étale and qc separated étale spaces over S × Spa(K, O_K) are locally on S constant.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-etale-finite-stage-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-separated-etale-finite-stage-descent`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-isomorphism-detection`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/separatedness-recognition-at-finite-stage`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/filtered-two-colimit-of-categories`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`.

- ECD, Section 6, Proposition 6.4 (ii), p. 27: “Then the base change functors (Xi )ét,qcqs → Xét,qcqs induce an equivalence of categories” — The central statement (ii).

### Acceptance tests of the layer

- Profinite sets: for a perfectoid field K and S = lim_n {0,1}^n, lim_n ({0,1}^n × Spa(K, O_K)) =
  Spa(C^0(S, K), C^0(S, O_K)) with underlying space S × |Spa(K, O_K)|; the uncompleted colimit LC(S, O_K) is not
  complete; finite étale, qcqs étale and qc separated étale objects over the limit are locally constant along S; the
  open complement of one fibre is étale, quasiseparated and not quasicompact, and does not descend.
- Residue fields (ECD Example 5.2): the limit of the rational neighbourhoods of a point is Spa(K(x), K(x)⁺), the
  pro-rational subspace of PerfectoidSpaces:P4/intersection-of-rational-subsets.
- Non-injectivity: the system of shrinking perfectoid discs T ↦ ϖT has limit the origin, and T dies in R⁺.
- ω₁: the limit over an ω₁-cofiltered category needs no completion; C^0({0,1}^{ℵ₁}, C_p) is the ω₁-cofiltered limit
  of the C^0({0,1}^J, C_p), J countable, and is not the limit of an ℕ-indexed tower of countably generated pieces.
- Separatedness: two copies of {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} glued along {|T| ≤ |ϖ|²} are not separated, and become separated after
  base change to the next stage of the system of discs shrinking to the origin.
- Finite presentation is not enough: C^0(S, K)/(f) with f(s) = Σ_k s_k ϖ^k is finitely presented, not flat, and not a
  base change from any finite stage; only finite étale algebras descend.
- Non-perfectoid towers: Spa(Q_p(p^{1/p^n})) is not a diagram in Perfd; its limit statement is a tilde-limit
  (PerfectoidSpaces:P7).

## P6. Affinoid approximation and pro-étale presentations


This layer supplies the set-theoretic size control and the pro-étale calculus of perfectoid spaces on
which the totally disconnected spaces, the pro-étale and v-sites and the theory of diamonds are built
(DiamondsAndVStacks D1–D5). It follows Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds* (arXiv v4, 2026; "ECD"),
§4 (Lemma 4.1 to Proposition 4.4), Proposition 6.4(iv) and §7 up to Lemma 7.11, with the Berkeley
Lectures §8.2 and Scholze's *p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties* §4. Everything is stated
for perfectoid Tate rings in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, in any characteristic and with no
perfectoid base field.

### Scope

The layer contains:

- κ-small perfectoid spaces (ECD Definition 4.2), their uniform variant, the cover criterion (ECD
  Proposition 4.4, corrected), stability under open subspaces, disjoint unions, fibre products and
  tilting, κ-smallness of cofiltered limits (the set-theoretic clause of ECD 6.4), the size of the
  affinoid étale site, and κ-bounded perfectoid sub-pairs (the κ-form of ECD 6.5 used in ECD 8.2);
- ECD Proposition 6.4(iv), imported from AdicEtaleGeometry A3 and assembled with the finite-stage
  descent of P5, together with the descent of surjectivity and the relative form that the §7 proofs use;
- affinoid pro-étale and pro-étale morphisms as actual cofiltered limits of affinoid étale maps (ECD
  Definition 7.8), the product X × S with a profinite set, the geometric-point example, Zariski closed
  immersions in their rational-intersection form and diagonals (ECD Remark 7.9), the pro-category
  equivalence with its κ-bounded form (ECD Proposition 7.10), and composition, base change,
  cancellation, sections and limits (ECD Lemma 7.11);
- a comparison with the affinoid perfectoid objects of Scholze's 2013 pro-étale site.

The layer does not contain: totally disconnected, w-local, strictly totally disconnected and
w-strictly local perfectoid spaces, the w-localization and the universally open strictly totally
disconnected cover (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1); the pro-étale and v-sites and their cohomology
(DiamondsAndVStacks:D2); the abstract cutoff-cardinal lemma and the counting lemma for completions
(DiamondsAndVStacks:D0); the essential surjectivity in ECD 6.4(iv) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A3); parts
(o)–(iii) of ECD 6.4 and cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P5); Zariski
closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions, injections and immersions (PerfectoidSpaces:P4). No proof
in this layer uses v-descent, a diamond atlas or the comparison of analytic adic spaces with diamonds.

### Conventions

- A cutoff cardinal is a cardinal κ as in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (ECD Lemma 4.1). All of
  §4 needs only that κ is an uncountable strong limit (ℵ₀ < κ and 2^λ < κ for λ < κ); Mathlib's
  `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts ℵ₀, so ℵ₀ < κ is always a separate hypothesis.
- The cutoff cardinals built in ECD's proof of Lemma 4.1 are suprema of sequences indexed by ordinals of
  uncountable cofinality, hence singular (for instance of cofinality ω₁). ECD Proposition 4.4's converse
  and its "stable under finite products" need a uniform bound for such κ; the layer states the correct
  forms, introduces the uniformly κ-small spaces for which they hold, and records the counterexamples.
  Affinoid and quasicompact spaces are unaffected.
- Cardinalities are those of underlying sets; |X| is the set of points of the underlying topological
  space of X.
- X_ét^aff is the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces étale over X (ECD Definition 6.2), X_proét^aff
  the category of affinoid pro-étale maps to an affinoid X, and X_proét the category of perfectoid spaces
  pro-étale over X, all with X-morphisms. Limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces are those of
  PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (the plus ring of lim Y_i is the
  ϖ-adic completion of colim O⁺(Y_i)).
- Pro(C) is the pro-category of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces, the opposite of
  Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Ind` of Cᵒᵖ, with small cofiltered index categories; Pro_κ(C) is its full
  subcategory of pro-objects isomorphic to one indexed by a category with fewer than κ morphisms.
- Pro-étale presentations in the sense of ECD have étale transition maps with no surjectivity or
  finiteness condition. They differ from the presentations of Scholze 2013 (transition maps eventually
  finite étale surjective) used by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1, and from Mathlib's pro-étale site of a scheme
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt`, by weakly étale maps).
- Geometric statements live in `TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`, ring-level bounds in `TauCeti.Perfectoid`
  (written without the `TauCeti.` prefix below).

### Dependencies

Inside this roadmap: P1 (perfectoid Tate rings, tilts), P2 (perfectoid spaces, affinoid perfectoid
spaces, rational localisation, fibre products, sheafiness, tilting of spaces), P3 (étale and finite étale
morphisms, almost purity, surjectivity on fibre products of points), P4 (injections, immersions,
Zariski closed and strongly Zariski closed immersions, diagonals), P5 (cofiltered limits of affinoid
perfectoid spaces, finite-stage descent (o)–(iii), the ring-level limit cardinal bound). Other roadmaps:
AdicEtaleGeometry:A3 (ECD 6.4(iv)), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1 (Scholze 2013 pro-étale site, for the
comparison), DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 (cutoff cardinals, the completion counting lemma, spectral spaces,
Pro-categories), AdicSpacesPartII:R0 (completed tensor products, in the fibre-product size bound), the
Tau Ceti anchor Layer 1 (the valuation spectrum as valuative relations, already in the pinned tree) and,
through P2, anchor Layers 2–5. AdicSpacesPartII:R5 enters only through A3.

Consumers: DiamondsAndVStacks D1 (w-localization, strictly totally disconnected covers, Lemma 7.19,
Corollary 7.22), D2 (Perfd_κ, the pro-étale and v-sites, cutoff independence, ν*), D3 (quasi-pro-étale
maps, torsors), D4 (pro-étale equivalence relations, diagonals), D5 (limits of diamonds);
AdicEtaleGeometry:A4; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H2 and H4.

### Planets

κ-small perfectoid space; Affinoid pro-étale morphism; Pro-étale morphism; Product with a profinite set;
Pro-category equivalence; Stability of pro-étale morphisms.

### P6.1 Set-theoretic bounds (ECD §4)

κ-smallness is a two-clause condition on points and on the rings of all open affinoid subspaces. For affinoid and quasicompact spaces it reduces to a bound on finitely many rings; in general it is not uniform, and the uniform variant is what makes the cover criterion and the closure under fibre products hold for singular cutoff cardinals. The ring-level counting (dense subrings, rational localisations, completed tensor products, the adic spectrum) is stated against Tau Ceti's Tate rings and `ValuationSpectrum.spa`.

#### `kappa-small-perfectoid-space` — κ-small perfectoid spaces

*definition*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-space`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/Size/KappaSmall`. **Planet:** *κ-small perfectoid space*.

**Statement.** Fix a cardinal κ with ℵ₀ < κ that is a strong limit (2^λ < κ for every cardinal λ < κ); every cutoff cardinal of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal (ECD Lemma 4.1) is one. A perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space: an adic space locally isomorphic to Spa(R, R⁺) for a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, with no perfectoid base field) is κ-small if (i) its underlying set |X| has cardinality #|X| < κ, and (ii) for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X (so A = O_X(U)) the ring A has cardinality #A < κ. The full subcategory of κ-small perfectoid spaces is written Perfd_κ, and for a κ-small X the category of κ-small perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X is X_proét,κ (ECD Definition 8.1). Conventions: cardinalities are those of underlying sets; the plus rings carry no condition (A⁺ ⊆ A); clause (ii) quantifies over all open affinoid subspaces, and there are at most 2^{#|X|} < κ of them, so no separate count of charts is imposed; the predicate is invariant under isomorphism and monotone in κ. The bound in (ii) is not uniform over the charts: the stronger notion with a single bound λ < κ is PerfectoidSpaces:P6/uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space, and for quasicompact X the two agree.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- κ is an uncountable strong limit cardinal; ECD notes that this is all §4 needs. Mathlib's `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` counts ℵ₀ as a strong limit, so ℵ₀ < κ is a separate hypothesis.
- The cofinality clauses (ii) and (iii) of the cutoff lemma are not part of the definition; they are used only in the limit statements (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits) and in D1's countable iteration.
- Clause (ii) is not implied by clause (i) (a one-point space with a large field), and clause (i) is not implied by clause (ii) (a disjoint union of κ points): both are needed.

**Proof or construction.**

1. Define `IsKappaSmall κ X` as the conjunction of #|X| < κ and #O_X(U) < κ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X, using the open affinoid subspaces of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space.
2. Record invariance under isomorphisms of perfectoid spaces (an isomorphism induces a bijection of points and of open affinoid subspaces with isomorphic rings) and monotonicity in κ.
3. Record the affinoid characterisation #A < κ and the cover criterion, which are the theorems PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion.
4. Essential smallness of Perfd_κ: a κ-small X is determined up to isomorphism by the topological space |X| (a set of cardinality < κ) and the restriction of (O_X, O_X⁺) with its valuations to the basis of open affinoid subspaces, whose rings have cardinality < κ; transporting all of these along injections into κ shows that the isomorphism classes of κ-small perfectoid spaces form a set, so Perfd_κ is essentially small (mathlib `CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`).

**API.**

| name | role | statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall` | structure | IsKappaSmall κ X: #∣X∣ < κ and #O_X(U) < κ for every open affinoid perfectoid subspace U ⊆ X. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.card_lt` | projection | If X is κ-small then #∣X∣ < κ. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.card_sections_lt` | projection | If X is κ-small and U ⊆ X is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace, then #O_X(U) < κ. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.of_iso` | compatibility | If X ≅ Y as perfectoid spaces and X is κ-small, then Y is κ-small. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.mono` | relation | If κ ≤ κ' (both uncountable strong limits) and X is κ-small, then X is κ'-small. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.isKappaSmall_affinoid_iff` | characterisation | For X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid perfectoid: IsKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.of_cover` | constructor | If X has a cover by open affinoid subspaces Spa(A_j, A_j⁺) with #A_j < κ and #∣X∣ < κ, then X is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.isOpen` | functoriality | An open subspace of a κ-small perfectoid space is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-closure). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.tilt_iff` | compatibility | X is κ-small iff its tilt X♭ is κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-tilting). |
| `PerfectoidSpace.KappaSmall` | structure | Perfd_κ: the full subcategory of perfectoid spaces on the κ-small objects. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.KappaSmall.essentiallySmall` | instance | Perfd_κ is essentially small. |
| `PerfectoidSpace.IsKappaSmall.empty` | example | The empty perfectoid space is κ-small. |

**Unit tests.**

- `isKappaSmall_spa_Cp` (computation): For every cardinal κ with ℵ₀ < κ and κ a strong limit, Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is κ-small: it has one point and #C_p = 2^ℵ₀ < κ.
- `isKappaSmall_empty` (degenerate): The empty perfectoid space is κ-small for every κ.
- `isKappaSmall_affinoid_iff` (characterisation): For an affinoid perfectoid space X = Spa(A, A⁺), IsKappaSmall κ X ↔ #A < κ.
- `not_isKappaSmall_bigField` (non-example): Let K be the completion, for the Gauss norm, of the perfection of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < κ); K is a perfectoid field with #K ≥ κ. Then Spa(K, K°) has one point but is not κ-small: clause (i) does not imply clause (ii).
- `not_isKappaSmall_sigma` (non-example): The disjoint union of κ copies of Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) is not κ-small, although each of its open affinoid subspaces (a finite union of copies) has a ring of cardinality 2^ℵ₀: clause (ii) does not imply clause (i).
- `isKappaSmall_not_uniform` (non-example): If cf κ = ω₁ (as for the cutoff cardinals κ(µ) with cf µ = ω₁ built in the proof of ECD Lemma 4.1) and K_α (α < ω₁) are perfectoid fields with #K_α < κ cofinal in κ, then ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°) is κ-small, but no λ < κ bounds the cardinalities of the rings of all its open affinoid subspaces.

**Acceptance.**

- For every uncountable strong limit κ, Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) and the perfectoid disc Spa(C_p⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, O_{C_p}⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) are κ-small: their rings have cardinality 2^ℵ₀ < κ.
- The empty perfectoid space is κ-small.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1(i)–(iii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site, D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site): the big pro-étale site and the v-site are topologies on Perfd_κ, and X_proét,κ is the site of κ-small pro-étale X-spaces
- ECD Proposition 8.2 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence): pullback c*_{κ,κ'} from X_proét,κ to X_proét,κ' for a κ-small X; the proof writes κ'-small affinoids as limits of κ-small ones
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the strictly totally disconnected cover X̃ of a κ-small affinoid X can be taken κ-small
- ECD Corollary 7.22 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps): κ-small affinoid pro-étale spaces over a strictly totally disconnected X correspond to spectral data of cardinality < κ
- ECD Proposition 6.4, set-theoretic clause (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits): a small cofiltered limit of uniformly κ'-small affinoid perfectoid spaces is κ-small
- ECD Proposition 7.10 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations): κ-small affinoid pro-étale X-spaces correspond to Pro_κ(X_ét^aff)
- ECD Lemma 11.22, Proposition 11.23, Lemma 12.17 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5): κ-smallness of cofiltered limits of diamonds and of v-sheaves admitting a surjection from a κ-small perfectoid space

**Prerequisites.** `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `mathlib:Cardinal.IsStrongLimit`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk`, `mathlib:Cardinal.mk_set`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §4, Definition 4.2, p. 20: “Definition 4.2. A perfectoid space X is κ-small if the cardinality of |X| is less than κ, and for all open affinoid subspaces U = Spa(A, A+ ) ⊂ X, the cardinality of A is less than κ.” — The definition, verbatim.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §4, after Definition 4.2, p. 20: “For the results of this section, it is actually enough to assume that κ is an uncountable strong limit cardinal.” — The standing hypothesis on κ adopted by the node.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §8, Definition 8.1, p. 39: “Let Perfd be the category of perfectoid spaces and Perfdκ ⊂ Perfd the subcategory of κ-small perfectoid spaces.” — The consumer: the sites of DiamondsAndVStacks:D2 live on Perfd_κ.

#### `uniformly-kappa-small-perfectoid-space` — Uniformly κ-small perfectoid spaces
