3. Almost surjectivity on plus rings then follows from PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings (ECD notes that BS22 Theorem 7.4 also gives it).
4. Alternative routes recorded for the owner of ECD 5.8: Kedlaya AWS Theorem 2.9.12 (Bhatt) proves surjectivity of a perfectoid ring onto the uniform completion of A/I through André's flatness lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/andre-flatness-lemma); in characteristic p the statement is Scholze's elementary Lemma II.2.5.

*Acceptance.* I = (T − 1) in ℂ_p⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩: S_I = C⁰(ℤ_p, ℂ_p) is a quotient of R (Fresnel–de Mathan, Kedlaya AWS Example 2.4.10); the ideal (T − 1) is closed but not radical.

*Dependencies.* `PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/universal-perfectoid-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/zariski-closed-immersion-is-universal`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/surjective-perfectoid-map-almost-surjective-on-plus-rings`.

*Sources.* Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, Theorem 5.8 with proof, p. 25; Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, after Definition 5.7, p. 24; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Theorem 2.9.12; Kedlaya-AWSNotes-2017, Lecture 2, Example 2.4.10.

#### `diagonals-are-pro-etale` — Diagonals and graphs of morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/diagonals-are-pro-etale`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/ZariskiClosed`.

**Statement.** Let f : Y → X be any morphism of perfectoid spaces. (a) The diagonal Δ_f : Y → Y ×_X Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) is pro-étale; if X = Spa(R, R⁺) and Y = Spa(S, S⁺) are affinoid, Δ_f is a Zariski closed immersion, cut out by the kernel of the multiplication map S ⊗̂_R S → S, and affinoid pro-étale. (b) For morphisms Y → X and Y' → X and an X-morphism g : Y → Y', the graph Γ_g : Y → Y ×_X Y' is pro-étale, affinoid pro-étale when X, Y, Y' are affinoid.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- f arbitrary; no separatedness or finiteness hypothesis.

**Proof or construction.**

1. (a), affinoid case: S ⊗̂_R S → S is surjective, so Δ_f is strongly Zariski closed (ECD Proposition 5.9, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map, PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion), hence Zariski closed with ideal the kernel (PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed), hence affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale).
2. (a), general case: for y ∈ Y choose an affinoid W ⊆ X containing f(y) and an affinoid V ⊆ f⁻¹(W) containing y; V ×_W V is an open affinoid subspace of Y ×_X Y (P2) with Δ_f⁻¹(V ×_W V) = V and Δ_f|_V = Δ_{V/W}, which is affinoid pro-étale; so Δ_f is pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map).
3. (b): Γ_g is the base change of Δ_{Y'/X} along g ×_X id : Y ×_X Y' → Y' ×_X Y', so it is pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits (ii)); in the affinoid case use PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change.

**Acceptance.**

- Δ : Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K, O_K) ×_{Spa(k, O_k)} Spa(K, O_K) for a finite Galois extension K/k of perfectoid fields is the inclusion of one of the [K:k] points, an open and closed immersion.
- ECD Proposition 11.4: the diagonal of any map of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale, which makes the equivalence relation of a fibre product of diamonds pro-étale (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds).

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 11.4 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds): fibre products of diamonds
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation: the graph factorisation of an X-morphism

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/zariski-closed-immersions-are-pro-etale`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/diagonal-of-perfectoid-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-immersion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P4/strongly-zariski-closed-is-zariski-closed`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Remark 7.9, p. 32: “In particular, if f : Y → X is any morphism of perfectoid spaces, then ∆f : Y → Y ×X Y is pro-étale.” — Part (a).
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §5, proof of Proposition 5.9, p. 25: “But then ∆f is strongly Zariski closed, as S ⊗ b R S → S is surjective.” — The affinoid diagonal is strongly Zariski closed.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §11, proof of Proposition 11.4, p. 55: “But the diagonal of any representable map is pro-étale by Remark 7.9.” — The consumer in DiamondsAndVStacks:D4.

### P6.4 The pro-category equivalence (ECD 7.10)

The heart of the equivalence is that maps from a cofiltered limit to an affinoid étale space factor through a finite stage (ECD 6.4(ii)). The canonical index category of all affinoid étale X-spaces under Y gives a quasi-inverse and, by counting, the κ-bounded form.

#### `maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage` — Maps from a cofiltered limit of affinoid perfectoid spaces to a qcqs étale space factor through a finite stage

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/ProCategory`.

**Statement.** Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, (Y_i)_{i∈I} a cofiltered system of affinoid perfectoid spaces over X (compatible structure maps; no étaleness assumed) with limit Y = lim_i Y_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces), and T → X an étale morphism from a quasicompact quasiseparated perfectoid space (for instance T ∈ X_ét^aff). Then the canonical map colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, T) → Hom_X(Y, T) is bijective: every X-morphism Y → T factors through some Y_i, and two X-morphisms Y_i → T that agree on Y agree on Y_j for some j → i.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- T quasicompact quasiseparated and étale over X; the Y_i need not be étale over X.

**Proof or construction.**

1. Hom_X(Y, T) = Hom_Y(Y, Y ×_X T), sections of the base change, which is qcqs étale over Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. For a fixed i, Y ×_X T = (Y_i ×_X T) ×_{Y_i} Y and Y = Y_i ×_{Y_i} Y are base changes of objects of (Y_i)_ét,qcqs; full faithfulness in ECD Proposition 6.4(ii) for the system (Y_j)_{j→i} (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects) gives Hom_Y(Y, Y ×_X T) = colim_j Hom_{Y_j}(Y_j, Y_j ×_X T).
3. Hom_{Y_j}(Y_j, Y_j ×_X T) = Hom_X(Y_j, T), compatibly in j.
4. (Alternative route, Berkeley Lemma 8.2.4: T is locally a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps; for rational embeddings use the constructible-topology argument on |Y| = lim |Y_i|, for finite étale maps ECD 6.4(i).)

**Acceptance.**

- T = U a rational subset of X: a map Y → X factoring through U factors through U at a finite stage.
- T = Spa(B, B⁺) finite étale over X = Spa(A, A⁺): Hom_A(B, colim-completion) = colim_i Hom_A(B, S_i).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence: full faithfulness of the realisation of Pro(X_ét^aff)
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation: initiality of a presentation in the canonical index category
- ECD Proposition 8.5 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves): ν^+F(Y) = colim F(Y_i)

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “Without loss of generality J is a singleton, so Z → X is étale.” — The reduction to an étale target, after which the statement is this lemma.
- ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, proof of Lemma 8.2.4, p. 58: “An étale morphism is locally a composition of rational embeddings and finite étale morphisms.” — The alternative route through rational embeddings and finite étale maps.

#### `canonical-pro-etale-presentation` — The canonical presentation: Y is affinoid pro-étale over X iff Y is the limit of all affinoid étale X-spaces under it

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/ProCategory`.

**Statement.** Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space and g : Y → X a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space. Let E_Y be the category of pairs (T, t) with T ∈ X_ét^aff and t : Y → T an X-morphism, with morphisms (T, t) → (T', t') the X-morphisms u : T → T' with u ∘ t = t' — the category of elements of Hom_X(Y, −) on X_ét^aff. Then: (a) E_Y is essentially small and cofiltered; (b) there is a canonical X-morphism c_Y : Y → lim_{E_Y} T (limit over a small skeleton, in perfectoid spaces); (c) g is affinoid pro-étale iff c_Y is an isomorphism; (d) for any pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i, the functor I → E_Y, i ↦ (Y_i, pr_i), is initial.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Y and X affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof or construction.**

1. (a): X_ét^aff is essentially small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound) and has finite limits: X is final; T_1 ×_{T_0} T_2 is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and étale over X (T_1 → T_0 is étale as a map of étale X-spaces; base change and composition, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); the equalizer of u, v : T_1 ⇉ T_2 is T_1 ×_{T_2 ×_X T_2} T_2 along (u, v) and the diagonal, étale over T_1 because the diagonal is a map of étale X-spaces. Hom_X(Y, −) preserves finite limits, so its category of elements is cofiltered (mathlib `IsCofiltered.of_hasFiniteLimits` applied to E_Y, which inherits the finite limits).
2. (b): the (T, t) form a cone over the forgetful functor E_Y → perfectoid spaces over X.
3. (d): by mathlib `Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`: every (T, t) receives a morphism from some (Y_i, pr_i) since t factors through some Y_i, and two such factorizations agree after some j → i — both by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage.
4. (c): if g is affinoid pro-étale, (d) and mathlib `Functor.Initial.limitIso` identify lim_{E_Y} T with lim_I Y_i = Y, compatibly with c_Y; conversely, if c_Y is an isomorphism, a small skeleton of E_Y is a pro-étale presentation.

**Acceptance.**

- For Y ∈ X_ét^aff, (Y, id) is initial in E_Y and c_Y is the identity.
- ECD Lemma 7.13 is the topological model: the category of factorizations X^wl → T → X through finite disjoint unions of rational subsets is cofiltered with limit X^wl.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence: the quasi-inverse of the realisation functor
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits: recognising a cofiltered limit of affinoid pro-étale spaces as affinoid pro-étale
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations: a presentation indexed by fewer than κ objects

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Elements`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.of_hasFiniteLimits`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11(iv), p. 34: “For this, it is enough to check that it has a final object and fibre products, which is clear.” — Finite limits in X_ét^aff, which make E_Y cofiltered.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.13, p. 34: “let C be the category of factorizations X wl → T → X, where T is a finite disjoint union of elements of B. Then C is cofiltered” — The same canonical index category in ECD's topological model.

#### `pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence` — Affinoid pro-étale spaces over X are the pro-objects of the affinoid étale site (ECD Proposition 7.10)

*theorem*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/ProCategory`. **Planet:** *Pro-category equivalence*.

**Statement.** Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space, X_ét^aff the category of étale maps Y → X from affinoid perfectoid spaces (essentially small and finitely complete, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound, PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation) and X_proét^aff the category of affinoid pro-étale maps Y → X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map). Let Pro(X_ét^aff) be the pro-category (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces; the opposite of Mathlib's Ind of the opposite category), with objects formal limits "lim" Y_i over small cofiltered categories and Hom("lim" Y_i, "lim" Z_j) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j). Then the realisation functor ρ_X : Pro(X_ét^aff) → X_proét^aff, "lim" Y_i ↦ lim Y_i (limit in perfectoid spaces), is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse Y ↦ "lim"_{(T,t)∈E_Y} T. Equivalently, for affinoid pro-étale Y = lim Y_i and Z = lim Z_j over X, Hom_X(Y, Z) = lim_j colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; Pro is taken with small cofiltered index categories after replacing X_ét^aff by a small skeleton.

**Proof or construction.**

1. ρ_X on morphisms: a compatible family of classes in colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j) induces maps lim Y_i → Z_j and hence lim Y_i → lim Z_j; functoriality is formal.
2. Essential surjectivity: every affinoid pro-étale Y has a pro-étale presentation, by definition.
3. Full faithfulness: Hom_X(Y, lim_j Z_j) = lim_j Hom_X(Y, Z_j) by the universal property of the limit, and Hom_X(lim_i Y_i, Z_j) = colim_i Hom_X(Y_i, Z_j) by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage.
4. Quasi-inverse: PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation (c).

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(C, O_C), C algebraically closed: X_ét^aff ≃ FinSet, and the theorem becomes Pro(FinSet) ≃ Profinite ≃ X_proét^aff, S ↦ X × S (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-over-geometric-point).
- ECD Proposition 8.5: ν*F is the sheafification of Y = lim Y_i ↦ colim F(Y_i), well defined because of the Hom formula (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves).

**Uses.**

- ECD Proof of Lemma 7.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition, P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits): composition through Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C) and limits through limits in Pro(C)
- ECD Proposition 8.5 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves): ν*F is the sheafification of ν^+F(lim Y_i) = colim F(Y_i)
- ECD Proposition 11.23 and §14 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5): 'as in the proof of Proposition 7.10' full faithfulness arguments

**Prerequisites.** `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Ind`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “f : Y → X from affinoid perfectoid spaces Y , and Xproét the category of affinoid pro-étale maps f : Y → X. Then the functor” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “By definition, the functor is essentially surjective, so we need to see that it is fully faithful.” — The structure of the proof.
- ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Lemma 8.2.4, p. 57: “be a diagram of affinoid pro-étale morphisms of affinoid perfectoid spaces” — The Hom formula in Berkeley's version.

#### `kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations` — κ-small affinoid pro-étale spaces are the pro-objects with fewer than κ indices (ECD Proposition 7.10, κ-part)

*theorem*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/ProCategory`.

**Statement.** Let κ be an uncountable strong limit cardinal and X a κ-small affinoid perfectoid space. (a) An affinoid pro-étale Y → X is κ-small iff it admits a pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i with #Mor(I) < κ; all Y_i ∈ X_ét^aff are then κ-small (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound). (b) Let Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) be the full subcategory of Pro(X_ét^aff) of pro-objects isomorphic to one indexed by a cofiltered category with fewer than κ morphisms. The realisation ρ_X of PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence restricts to an equivalence Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) ≃ X_proét,κ^aff with the full subcategory of κ-small affinoid pro-étale X-spaces. (c) Every affinoid pro-étale Y → X is the limit, along a directed poset, of κ-small affinoid pro-étale Y_J → X: for a presentation indexed by I, J runs over the full cofiltered subcategories of I with fewer than κ morphisms and Y_J := lim_{i∈J} Y_i (the pro-étale form of the first step of ECD's proof of Proposition 8.2; for arbitrary affinoid Y see PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-perfectoid-subpairs).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- κ uncountable strong limit; X κ-small affinoid. ECD states (b) without proof.

**Proof or construction.**

1. (a) ⇒: by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation Y = lim over a small skeleton of E_Y. Objects of X_ét^aff have fewer than κ isomorphism classes and rings of cardinality ≤ μ(X) < κ; #Hom_X(Y, T) ≤ #O(Y)^{#O(T)} < κ as κ is a strong limit and #O(Y) < κ; so the skeleton has fewer than κ objects and morphisms (sums of fewer than κ cardinals uniformly bounded below κ).
2. (a) ⇐: #colim_i O⁺(Y_i) ≤ #Mor(I)·μ(X) < κ, so #O(Y) < κ (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits (a)), and Y is κ-small by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion (d).
3. (b): from (a), since both sides are full subcategories and ρ_X is an equivalence.
4. (c): every subset of I of cardinality ≤ λ (λ infinite) lies in a full cofiltered subcategory with at most λ morphisms (add cones for finite subdiagrams, countably many rounds); these J form a directed poset with union I, so lim_J Y_J = lim_I Y_i = Y; each Y_J is κ-small by (a).

**Acceptance.**

- X = Spa(C, O_C): X × S is κ-small iff S is the limit of fewer than κ finite sets, and then #C⁰(S, C) < κ.
- ECD Proposition 8.2: a κ'-small affinoid pro-étale Y → X is a cofiltered limit of κ-small affinoid pro-étale Y_J → X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence).

**Uses.**

- ECD Proposition 8.2 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/cutoff-independence): κ-cofiltered approximations of κ'-small affinoid pro-étale spaces
- ECD Corollary 7.22 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/topological-classification-of-pro-etale-maps): the κ-small versions of the classification

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cover-criterion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-small-cofiltered-limits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/complete-tate-ring-cardinality`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “If X is κ-small and one restricts to κ-small objets in Xproét” — Part (b) (ECD prints 'objets').
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, after Proposition 7.10, p. 33: “Here, Proκ denotes the category of pro-systems whose index category is bounded by κ.” — The meaning of Pro_κ.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §8, proof of Proposition 8.2, p. 39: “If Y → X is affinoid pro-étale, one can assume all Yj → X to be affinoid pro-étale.” — Part (c).

### P6.5 Stability and limits (ECD 7.11)

Everything is proved first for affinoid pro-étale maps and then localised. Composition uses ECD 6.4(iv) and the closure of X_proét^aff under cofiltered limits, the geometric form of Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C); cancellation factors a morphism through its graph, a section of an affinoid pro-étale projection.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-base-change` — Base change of affinoid pro-étale maps (ECD Lemma 7.11(ii), affinoid case)

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** Let f : Y → X be affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i, and g : X' → X a morphism from an affinoid perfectoid space. Then Y' := X' ×_X Y is affinoid perfectoid and f' : Y' → X' is affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation Y' = lim_i X' ×_X Y_i; moreover |Y'| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y| is surjective.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X, X', Y affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof or construction.**

1. X' ×_X Y_i is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces) and étale over X' (base change, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open), so it lies in X'_ét^aff; the transition maps are X'-morphisms.
2. Fibre products commute with cofiltered limits in perfectoid spaces (both are limits and exist here: P2, P5), so lim_i (X' ×_X Y_i) = X' ×_X lim_i Y_i = Y'.
3. Surjectivity on points: each |X' ×_X Y_i| → |X'| ×_{|X|} |Y_i| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change); over a point (x', y) the fibres form a cofiltered system of nonempty spectral spaces, with nonempty limit (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

**Acceptance.**

- Base change of X × S → X along X' → X is X' × S → X' (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set).
- Base change of a Zariski closed immersion is the Zariski closed immersion cut out by the extended ideal.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site): pullbacks of pro-étale covers

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.11(ii), p. 33: “Let f : Y → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale), and let g : X ′ → X be a map from a perfectoid space (resp. affinoid perfectoid space).” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “Part (ii) follows directly from the definition.” — The proof.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits` — Cofiltered limits of affinoid pro-étale X-spaces are affinoid pro-étale (the geometric form of Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C))

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** Let X be an affinoid perfectoid space and (Y_k)_{k∈K} a small cofiltered diagram in X_proét^aff (affinoid pro-étale X-spaces and X-morphisms). Then its limit Y = lim_k Y_k in perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces) is affinoid pro-étale over X and is the limit of the diagram in X_proét^aff. Under the equivalence ρ_X of PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence, Y corresponds to the limit in Pro(X_ét^aff) of the corresponding pro-objects: ρ_X preserves cofiltered limits.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X affinoid perfectoid; K small cofiltered.

**Proof or construction.**

1. By PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation it suffices that c_Y : Y → lim_{E_Y} T is an isomorphism. Fix a pseudouniformiser ϖ of O(X). By P5, O⁺(lim_{E_Y} T)/ϖ = colim_{E_Y} O⁺(T)/ϖ and O⁺(Y)/ϖ = colim_k O⁺(Y_k)/ϖ = colim_k colim_{E_{Y_k}} O⁺(T)/ϖ.
2. The comparison colim_{E_Y} O⁺(T)/ϖ → O⁺(Y)/ϖ is surjective, since every object (T, Y_k → T) of E_{Y_k} gives an object of E_Y; and injective: if a ∈ O⁺(T)/ϖ dies in O⁺(Y)/ϖ, factor t : Y → T through some Y_k and then through some object T' of E_{Y_k} (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage, twice); a dies in O⁺(T'')/ϖ for some T'' further along E_{Y_{k'}}, which gives a morphism (T'', ·) → (T, t) of E_Y killing a.
3. Both O⁺-rings are ϖ-adically complete and ϖ-torsion free, so c_Y is an isomorphism on O⁺ and O, hence of affinoid perfectoid spaces over X (P5).
4. Pro side: the natural functor Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C) and the cofiltered limits of Pro(C) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces) correspond to this limit under ρ_X.

**Acceptance.**

- A pro-étale presentation Y = lim Y_i is the special case of a diagram of affinoid étale X-spaces.
- The countable iterate X̃ = lim_n X_n of ECD Lemma 7.18, each X_{n+1} → X_n affinoid pro-étale, is affinoid pro-étale over X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover).

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition: the composite is a cofiltered limit of affinoid pro-étale X-spaces
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits: cofiltered limits in X_proét^aff
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): the countable iteration

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/maps-to-etale-factor-through-finite-stage`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “For part (i), we use Proposition 7.10, Proposition 6.4 (iv) and the natural functor Pro(Pro(C)) → Pro(C), which exists for any category C.” — The categorical input this node makes geometric.
- ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Proposition 8.2.5(3), p. 59: “(Note: the category of affinoid perfectoid spaces has all connected limits. In particular fiber products of perfectoid spaces exist.)” — Existence of the limits involved.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-composition` — Composites of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale (ECD Lemma 7.11(i), affinoid case)

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** If g : Z → Y and f : Y → X are affinoid pro-étale, then f ∘ g : Z → X is affinoid pro-étale. Explicitly, for pro-étale presentations Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i over X and Z = lim_{j∈J} Z_j over Y, each Z_j is Y-isomorphic to W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y for some i(j) ∈ I and W_j ∈ (Y_{i(j)})_ét^aff, and Z is the limit of the cofiltered diagram of the affinoid étale X-spaces W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y_i, i → i(j).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X, Y, Z affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof or construction.**

1. For each j, apply ECD 6.4(iv) to the cofiltered system (Y_i) with limit Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly (a)): Z_j ≅ W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y with W_j ∈ (Y_{i(j)})_ét^aff.
2. Then Z_j = lim_{i→i(j)} W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y_i (fibre products commute with limits), and each W_j ×_{Y_{i(j)}} Y_i is affinoid perfectoid and étale over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly (d)); so Z_j ∈ X_proét^aff.
3. The transition maps Z_j → Z_{j'} are Y-, hence X-morphisms, so Z = lim_j Z_j is a cofiltered limit in X_proét^aff and is affinoid pro-étale over X by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits.

**Acceptance.**

- Rational subset of a rational subset; finite étale over rational: composites of affinoid étale maps.
- X × S × S' = (X × S) × S' → X × S → X is X × (S × S') → X.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site): composites of pro-étale covers
- ECD Lemma 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1/universally-open-std-cover): X̃ → X_n → X

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-finite-stage-assembly`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.11(i), p. 33: “Let g : Z → Y and f : Y → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale) morphisms. Then f ◦ g : Z → X is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “It is enough to prove the assertions in the affinoid pro-étale case.” — The reduction used by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-sections` — Sections of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-sections`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** Let f : Y → X be affinoid pro-étale with pro-étale presentation Y = lim_{i∈I} Y_i, and s : X → Y a section of f. Then s is affinoid pro-étale, with pro-étale presentation X ≅ lim_i (X ×_{Y_i} Y) → Y, where X → Y_i is s_i := pr_i ∘ s and Y → Y_i is pr_i.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X, Y affinoid perfectoid; s a section, f ∘ s = id_X.

**Proof or construction.**

1. s_i : X → Y_i is an X-morphism between étale X-spaces, hence étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open); its base change X ×_{Y_i} Y → Y along pr_i is étale, and affinoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces), so it lies in Y_ét^aff.
2. lim_i (X ×_{Y_i} Y) = X ×_{lim_i Y_i} Y = X ×_Y Y = X, the fibre product along s and id_Y, since limits commute with fibre products; the resulting map to Y is s.

**Acceptance.**

- The zero section Spa(K) → Spa(K) × S of a point x ∈ S is the inclusion Spa(K) × {x}.
- The identity section is presented by the constant system.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation: graphs are sections of affinoid pro-étale projections

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphisms-composition-base-change-open`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “thus, it is enough to show that sections of affinoid pro-étale maps are affinoid pro-étale.” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “section, then s is given by a compatible system of sections si : X → Yi , and X = limi (X ×Yi Y ) → Y” — The presentation.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation` — Morphisms between affinoid pro-étale X-spaces are affinoid pro-étale (ECD Lemma 7.11(iii), affinoid case)

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** Let Y → X and Y' → X be affinoid pro-étale. Then every X-morphism g : Y → Y' is affinoid pro-étale. Consequently, for Y' ∈ X_proét^aff, an affinoid perfectoid space Z → Y' is affinoid pro-étale over Y' iff Z → X is affinoid pro-étale, so (Y')_proét^aff ≃ X_proét^aff/Y' (slice category).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X, Y, Y' affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof or construction.**

1. Factor g = pr_2 ∘ Γ_g with Γ_g : Y → Y ×_X Y' the graph, a section of pr_1 : Y ×_X Y' → Y.
2. pr_1 is the base change of Y' → X along Y → X and pr_2 the base change of Y → X along Y' → X, both affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change); Γ_g is a section of pr_1, hence affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-sections); compose (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
3. Slice: ⇒ by composition, ⇐ by the first part applied to Z → Y' over X.

**Acceptance.**

- Every morphism X × S → X × S' over X (a continuous map S → S' when |X| is connected) is affinoid pro-étale.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1(ii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site): all morphisms of X_proét are pro-étale, and slices
- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits: fibre products in X_proét^aff

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-sections`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.11(iii), p. 33: “Let f : Y → X and f ′ : Y ′ → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale). Then any map g : Y → Y ′ over X is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “For part (iii), we can factor g as the composite of a section of the affinoid pro-étale map Y ×X Y ′ → Y (given by the graph), and the affinoid pro-étale map Y ×X Y ′ → Y ′” — The proof.

#### `affinoid-pro-etale-limits` — X_proét^aff has all small limits, computed in perfectoid spaces (ECD Lemma 7.11(iv))

*theorem*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** For an affinoid perfectoid space X, the category X_proét^aff has all small limits, and they are computed in perfectoid spaces over X: the final object is id_X; fibre products Y ×_Z Y' of objects of X_proét^aff are the fibre products of perfectoid spaces; cofiltered limits are the limits of P5; every small limit is a cofiltered limit of finite limits of affinoid perfectoid spaces, and the inclusion X_proét^aff → (perfectoid spaces over X) preserves all small limits. Under ρ_X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence) this is the statement that Pro(C) has all small limits for C = X_ét^aff finitely complete.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- X affinoid perfectoid.

**Proof or construction.**

1. Final object: id_X.
2. Fibre products: Y ×_Z Y' is affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces); Y → Z is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation), so its base change Y ×_Z Y' → Y' is (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change), and so is the composite with Y' → X (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
3. Cofiltered limits: PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits.
4. All small limits: a limit over J is the cofiltered limit, over the finite subdiagrams of J, of their finite limits, and finite limits come from the final object, fibre products and equalizers (equalizers are fibre products with the diagonal).
5. Pro side: C has finite limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation (a)), so Cᵒᵖ has finite colimits, Ind(Cᵒᵖ) has all small colimits (mathlib `CategoryTheory.Ind`), and Pro(C) = Ind(Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ has all small limits (mathlib `hasLimits_of_hasColimits_op`, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces).

**Acceptance.**

- Infinite fibre products over X of copies of X × {0, 1} are X × {0, 1}^ℕ, the product with the Cantor set.
- Equalizer of two X-maps X × S ⇉ X × S' (|X| connected) is X × E for the closed subset E ⊆ S where the corresponding maps agree.

**Uses.**

- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site: X_proét^aff is a site with all finite limits
- ECD Proposition 8.5 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves): the equivalent topoi of X_proét and X_proét^aff

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cofiltered-limits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/canonical-pro-etale-presentation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Ind`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.hasLimits_of_hasColimits_op`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimits`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.11(iv), p. 33: “For any affinoid perfectoid space X, the category Xproét has all small limits.” — The statement.
- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11(iv), p. 34: “For this, it is enough to check that it has a final object and fibre products, which is clear.” — The finite limits in X_ét^aff.

#### `pro-etale-local-shrinking` — Étale maps are pro-étale, and affinoid pro-étale maps restrict to affinoid opens

*lemma*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`.

**Statement.** (a) Every étale morphism of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale, and every étale morphism between affinoid perfectoid spaces is affinoid pro-étale. (b) If f : Y → X is affinoid pro-étale, U ⊆ X is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace and V ⊆ f⁻¹(U) is an open affinoid perfectoid subspace, then f|_V : V → U is affinoid pro-étale. (c) Consequently f : Y → X is pro-étale iff every y ∈ Y has rational neighbourhoods V ∋ y and U ∋ f(y), inside any given neighbourhoods, with f(V) ⊆ U and f|_V affinoid pro-étale; pro-étaleness is local on the source, local on the target for open covers, and stable under restriction to open subspaces of the source and over open subspaces of the target.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- No hypotheses beyond those stated.

**Proof or construction.**

1. (a): by ECD Definition 6.2(ii), near y an étale map is V ↪ W → U with V open in W and W finite étale over an open U ⊆ X; shrink U to a rational subset U' ∋ f(y), replace W by W ×_U U', which is affinoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids), and V by a rational subset of W ×_U U' containing y; the result is affinoid étale over U', hence affinoid pro-étale.
2. (b): f⁻¹(U) = U ×_X Y → U is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change); V ↪ f⁻¹(U) is an open immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces, hence affinoid étale; compose (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
3. (c): combine (b) with PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map and the fact that rational subsets form a basis of each affinoid perfectoid space.

**Acceptance.**

- A rational subset of a rational subset is affinoid pro-étale over X.
- X × S_c ⊆ X × S for a compact open S_c of a locally profinite S.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits: reduction of 7.11(i)–(iii) to the affinoid case
- DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site: étale covers are pro-étale covers; analytic covers are coverings

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, proof of Lemma 7.11, p. 33: “It is enough to prove the assertions in the affinoid pro-étale case.” — The reduction this lemma makes precise.
- ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Definition 8.2.1, p. 57: “A morphism f : X → Y of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale if it is locally (on the source and target) affinoid pro-étale.” — Locality on source and target.

#### `pro-etale-stability-and-limits` — Stability of pro-étale morphisms: composition, base change, cancellation and limits (ECD Lemma 7.11)

*theorem*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-stability-and-limits`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Stability`. **Planet:** *Stability of pro-étale morphisms*.

**Statement.** (i) Composites of pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are pro-étale. (ii) If f : Y → X is pro-étale and g : X' → X is any morphism of perfectoid spaces, then f' : X' ×_X Y → X' is pro-étale. (iii) If Y → X and Y' → X are pro-étale, every X-morphism Y → Y' is pro-étale. (iv) For affinoid X, X_proét^aff has all small limits (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits). The affinoid versions of (i)–(iii) are PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition, P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change and P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation. Consequences: X_proét (perfectoid spaces pro-étale over X, with all X-morphisms) contains X_ét, is closed under fibre products, which are computed in perfectoid spaces, and for Y ∈ X_proét, Y_proét ≃ X_proét/Y. These are the stability assertions the big and small pro-étale sites of DiamondsAndVStacks:D2 rest on; pro-étaleness is not claimed to be local on the target for the pro-étale topology.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- Arbitrary perfectoid spaces in (i)–(iii); X affinoid in (iv).

**Proof or construction.**

1. (ii): for y' ∈ X' ×_X Y over x' ∈ X' and y ∈ Y, choose affinoid V ∋ y and U ⊇ f(V) with V → U affinoid pro-étale and an affinoid U' ⊆ g⁻¹(U) containing x'; U' ×_U V is an open subspace of X' ×_X Y containing y', and U' ×_U V → U' is affinoid pro-étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change).
2. (i): for z ∈ Z choose V_Y ∋ g(z), U ⊆ X with V_Y → U affinoid pro-étale, and V_Z ∋ z, W ⊆ Y with V_Z → W affinoid pro-étale; shrink to a rational W' ⊆ W ∩ V_Y containing g(z) and V_Z' ⊆ V_Z ∩ g⁻¹(W') (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking); then V_Z' → W' → V_Y → U is a composite of affinoid pro-étale maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition).
3. (iii): for y ∈ Y choose a rational U ⊆ X containing the image of y over which both Y and Y' are affinoid pro-étale near y and g(y), shrink to rational V ∋ y and V' ∋ g(y) with g(V) ⊆ V' affinoid pro-étale over U (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking), and apply PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation to V → V' over U.
4. (iv): PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits.
5. Consequences: fibre products Y ×_Z Y' in X_proét are pro-étale over Y' by (iii) and (ii) and over X by (i); étale maps are pro-étale by PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking (a); the slice statement is (i) and (iii).

**Acceptance.**

- X × S × S' → X is pro-étale, as a composite.
- The w-localization X^wl → X and the cover X̃ → X of ECD 7.12 and 7.18 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1) are pro-étale, and so are their base changes.

**Uses.**

- ECD Definition 8.1 and the pretopology axioms (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/big-pro-etale-site): pro-étale covers are stable under composition and base change
- ECD Definition 8.1(ii) (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site): X_proét is a site with fibre products
- ECD Definition 10.1 and Proposition 10.3 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-quasi-pro-etale-morphisms-of-stacks): quasi-pro-étale maps compose and base change because pro-étale maps do
- ECD Propositions 11.3–11.4 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/quotient-presentations-of-diamonds): pro-étale equivalence relations and their base changes

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-local-shrinking`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-composition`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-cancellation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-limits`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-EtaleCohomologyDiamonds, §7, Lemma 7.11(i), p. 33: “Let g : Z → Y and f : Y → X be pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale) morphisms. Then f ◦ g : Z → X is pro-étale (resp. affinoid pro-étale).” — Part (i); parts (ii)–(iv) are cited with the affinoid nodes.
- ScholzeWeinstein-Berkeley-2020, Lecture 8, Proposition 8.2.5, p. 58: “Proposition 8.2.5 ([Sch17, Lemma 7.11]). 1. Compositions of pro-étale maps are pro-étale.” — Berkeley's version of the same lemma.

### P6.6 Comparison with Scholze 2013

Affinoid perfectoid objects of the pro-étale site of a locally noetherian adic space over a perfectoid field give perfectoid spaces, and pro-étale maps to them built from rational and finite étale pieces give affinoid pro-étale maps in the sense of this layer.

#### `scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison` — Scholze 2013's affinoid perfectoid objects of X_proét give affinoid pro-étale perfectoid spaces in the sense of ECD Definition 7.8

*comparison*, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/scholze-2013-affinoid-perfectoid-comparison`; library `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/ProEtale/Scholze2013Comparison`.

**Statement.** Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0, X a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(K, K⁺), and X_proét Scholze's pro-étale site (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, on the category pro-X_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism). Let U = lim U_i ∈ X_proét be affinoid perfectoid (Scholze 2013, Definition 4.3: a pro-étale presentation by affinoid U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) whose completed colimit (R, R⁺) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K⁺)-algebra) and Û := Spa(R, R⁺). (a) If V_i → U_i is étale and a composite of rational subsets and finite étale maps, then V := V_i ×_{U_i} U is affinoid perfectoid and V̂ = V_i ×_{U_i} Û (fibre product of adic spaces over K) is an object of Û_ét^aff, étale in the sense of ECD Definition 6.2 (Scholze 2013, Lemma 4.5(i)). (b) If V = lim_k V^{(k)} → U is a cofiltered limit in X_proét of objects V^{(k)} → U as in (a), then V is affinoid perfectoid and V̂ = lim_k V̂^{(k)} (limit in perfectoid spaces, P5) is affinoid pro-étale over Û with pro-étale presentation (V̂^{(k)})_k (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map); V ↦ V̂ is functorial, being induced on pro-objects by the functor of (a) followed by the realisation of PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence. (c) Boundary: Scholze 2013's presentations require eventually finite étale surjective transition maps over a locally noetherian base, ECD's do not; the erratum restricts only the covering families of X_proét, not its objects, so (a)–(b) are unaffected; no converse is asserted (an affinoid pro-étale Û-space need not come from X_proét).

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- K perfectoid of characteristic 0 (Scholze 2013's setting); X locally noetherian.
- The perfectoid spaces are over K; the comparison is with the base-field-free notion of P6 restricted to spaces over Spa(K, K⁺).

**Proof or construction.**

1. (a): Scholze 2013, Lemma 4.5(i): rational subsets pull back to rational subsets of Û, whose rings are perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids); finite étale maps pull back to finite étale maps with perfectoid source by almost purity (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem), and the fibre product is computed by Sch12 Proposition 7.10 (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change). V̂ → Û is a composite of rational embeddings and finite étale maps, hence étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces).
2. (b): as in the proof of Scholze 2013, Lemma 4.6, the completed colimit over i and k of the rings of the V^{(k)} ×_U U_i is the completed colimit of the rings of the V̂^{(k)}, and a completed colimit of perfectoid affinoid algebras is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces); hence V̂ = lim_k V̂^{(k)} with V̂^{(k)} ∈ Û_ét^aff.
3. Functoriality: morphisms in pro-X_ét are given by the double-limit formula (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism), and the realisation respects it (PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze 2013, Example 4.4: the torus tower T̃ⁿ = lim Spa(K⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩) is affinoid perfectoid, and for a finite étale cover of the torus pulled back to T̃ⁿ the associated perfectoid space is affinoid étale over the perfectoid torus.
- ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/H4 transfer étale cohomology of classical spaces to perfectoid limits through such objects.

**Uses.**

- ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2, H4: affinoid perfectoid pro-étale covers of classical spaces viewed as perfectoid spaces pro-étale over Û, to transfer cohomology to perfectoid limits

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-pro-etale-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-pro-category-equivalence`

**Sources.**

- Scholze-PadicHodgeRigid-2013, §4, Definition 4.3(i), p. 22: “We say that U is affinoid perfectoid if U has a pro-étale presentation U = lim Ui → X” — The objects compared.
- Scholze-PadicHodgeRigid-2013, §4, Lemma 4.5(i), p. 23: “(K, K + )-algebra. In particular, V is affinoid perfectoid.” — Part (a).
- Scholze-PadicHodgeRigid-2013, §4, proof of Lemma 4.6, p. 25: “But the completion of a direct limit of perfectoid affinoid (K, K + )-algebras is again perfectoid affinoid.” — Part (b).
- Scholze-PadicHodgeRigid-Erratum, Erratum, item (1), p. 1: “the class of covers gets restricted.” — Part (c): the erratum changes the covers, not the objects.

### Mistakes found in the sources

- **PerfectoidSpaces/E40** (error, affects a stated result), §4, Proposition 4.4 and its proof, pp. 20–21 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). The 'if' direction needs a uniform bound: if X has a cover by fewer than κ open affinoids Spa(A_j, A_j⁺) with sup_j #A_j < κ (automatic for finite covers, for covers indexed by fewer than cf κ sets, and for every cover when κ is regular), then X is κ-small; without the uniform bound only 'every open affinoid ring has cardinality < κ' follows. Likewise fibre products X ×_Z Y are κ-small when X and Y are uniformly κ-small (κ'-small for one κ' < κ), in particular when they are quasicompact, but not in general. Reason: The cutoff cardinals κ(µ) produced in the proof of Lemma 4.1 are suprema of µ-sequences, hence singular; take κ = κ(ω₁), of cofinality ω₁. With perfectoid fields K_α (α < ω₁), #K_α < κ cofinal in κ (completed perfections of F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))(x_β : β < λ_α) for the Gauss norm), the disjoint union of the perfectoid discs over the K_α is covered by ω₁ < κ affinoids with rings of cardinality < κ but has at least κ points (the classical points of each disc), so it is not κ-small. Similarly X = ⊔_{α<ω₁} Spa(K_α, K_α°), with the K_α ⊇ L transcendental over a perfectoid field L, is κ-small (ℵ₁ points, every open affinoid a finite union of components), but X ×_{Spa L} X is not: Spa(K_α ⊗̂_L K_α) has at least λ_α points, distinguished by |x_β ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ x_β|.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E41** (misprint, affects nothing), §6, Definition 6.2(ii), p. 26 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). … such that y ∈ V, f(V) ⊂ U … Reason: The condition y ∈ Y is vacuous; the definition is local at y, as Berkeley Definition 7.5.1(2) ('there exists an open U ∋ x') states.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E42** (gap, affects the proof), §7, Proposition 7.10, second sentence, p. 33 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). Correct as stated ('objets' should read 'objects'); the printed proof covers only the first sentence. A proof: X_ét^aff has fewer than κ isomorphism classes with rings of cardinality ≤ (#O(X)+ℵ₀)^ℵ₀, so a κ-small affinoid pro-étale Y is the limit over the canonical index category of maps Y → T, which has fewer than κ objects and morphisms; conversely a presentation with fewer than κ indices has a completed colimit ring of cardinality < κ. Reason: The proof in the source addresses full faithfulness of Pro(X_ét^aff) → X_proét^aff only; the κ-bounded statement needs the size bound on X_ét^aff and a bounded presentation, supplied in PerfectoidSpaces:P6/affinoid-etale-size-bound and PerfectoidSpaces:P6/kappa-bounded-pro-etale-presentations.
- **PerfectoidSpaces/E43** (gap, affects nothing), §8, proof of Proposition 8.2, p. 39 (arXiv:1709.07343v4). The κ-small closed perfectoid subrings of O(Y) containing the image of O(X) form a directed, ω₁-directed system in which every subfamily of at most λ members of cardinality at most λ (λ < κ) has an upper bound; it is not κ-directed when κ is singular. The argument of Proposition 8.2 uses only filtered colimits of Čech complexes, so this directedness suffices. Reason: For singular κ (every cutoff cardinal κ(µ) of Lemma 4.1's proof), a family of cf κ subrings with cardinalities cofinal in κ has no upper bound of cardinality < κ.

### Acceptance for the layer

- For every cutoff cardinal κ, affinoid perfectoid spaces with rings of cardinality < κ are κ-small, their fibre products are, and so are cofiltered limits of fewer than κ of them with a uniform bound; the counterexamples for singular κ show why the uniform bound is part of the statements.
- For an affinoid perfectoid X: X_ét^aff is essentially small and finitely complete, Pro(X_ét^aff) ≃ X_proét^aff, and for κ-small X this restricts to Pro_κ(X_ét^aff) ≃ X_proét,κ^aff.
- Over a geometric point Spa(C, O_C), X_proét^aff ≃ Profinite by S ↦ X × S.
- Zariski closed immersions, diagonals and graphs are (affinoid) pro-étale; pro-étale maps are stable under composition, base change and cancellation; X_proét^aff has all small limits, computed in perfectoid spaces.
- The statements DiamondsAndVStacks requested (ECD 7.8–7.11 and 4.2–4.4 with the finite-products clause) are the nodes of P6.3–P6.5 and P6.1, the latter in the corrected uniform form.

<a id="p7"></a>

## P7. Tilde-limits and Frobenius-controlled towers


**Coverage: partial** (every target of the narrowed layer is realised; the remaining items are the unpublished Huber
arguments behind Scholze 2012 §7 and one conditional statement of Scholze's survey, both recorded as gaps).

This layer turns towers of analytic adic spaces into perfectoid spaces. Its objects are *perfectoid tilde-limits*
X ~ lim X_i: a perfectoid space X with compatible maps to a cofiltered system (X_i) such that |X| → lim |X_i| is a
homeomorphism and finite-level sections are dense in the sections of X over an affinoid cover. The general Huber
carrier of this notion (topology and affinoid density as two separate conditions) and the classical continuity of
étale cohomology belong to `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity`, which this
layer imports; what the layer owns is the perfectoid theory built on it:

- uniqueness in the perfectoid representable class (a perfectoid tilde-limit represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on
  perfectoid spaces) and the comparison with inverse limits of represented functors and of diamonds;
- the basis of *good* affinoid perfectoids (preimages of finite-level quasicompact opens with dense finite-level
  sections), their description as uniform completions of finite-level coordinate rings, and descent of rational
  subsets and finite étale algebras to a finite level;
- restriction to compatible open and rational subsets, cofinal change of index with the cofinality witness for
  compact open subgroup towers, finite étale and étale base change, and locality and gluing;
- *Frobenius-controlled integral towers* A_0⁺ → A_1⁺ → ⋯ with a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ and eventual
  Frobenius lifting modulo ϖ^p, their completion/inversion formula, the uniformity bound, and the *perfectoid Frobenius
  criterion*: the generic fibres have a perfectoid tilde-limit even though no finite level is perfectoid; the tilt of
  that limit and the characteristic-p perfection as a special case;
- the separate, easier theorem for towers of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps;
- the specialised comparison of étale topoi of Scholze 2012 7.14–7.19 (Proposition 7.16, Theorem 7.17, Corollaries
  7.18–7.19), for index spaces that are quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces over **no
  perfectoid base field**.

Scholze–Weinstein's preperfectoid spaces and their strong completions X̂ ~ X are included as the first instance of the
represented-functor comparison: X̂ represents Hom(−, X) on perfectoid spaces.

**Not in this layer.** The general (non-perfectoid) tilde-limit and Huber's continuity theorem: H0. Cofiltered limits of
affinoid perfectoid spaces and ECD 6.4(o)–(iii) finite-stage descent over perfectoid towers: P5, which this layer cites.
Finite group quotients of towers and Zariski-closed loci in towers (Hansen–Johansson §5, ECD 5.8): P8, which consumes this
layer. The construction of Shimura towers, their cofinal level systems and the verification of the Frobenius estimates
on the anticanonical tower: `PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0`, `S1`, which apply the criterion and the cofinality witness.

### Conventions

- p is a fixed prime. Perfectoid Tate rings are those of ECD Definition 3.1 (`PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`):
  complete, uniform, with a pseudouniformiser ϖ, ϖ^p | p in R°, Frobenius R°/ϖ ≅ R°/ϖ^p; characteristic 0 or p; no
  perfectoid base field anywhere in this layer. Perfectoid spaces are those of `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`
  (full subcategory of the anchor's analytic adic spaces).
- Index categories I are small and cofiltered (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`); systems i ↦ X_i have transition
  maps f_a: X_j → X_i for a: j → i, required to be quasicompact and quasiseparated; the X_i themselves need not be qcqs,
  except in the Scholze 2012 comparison, where they are qcqs locally noetherian.
- Underlying spaces: |X|; limits of topological spaces are Mathlib's `TopCat` limits. A tilde-limit is **not** a limit in
  adic spaces: X ~ X_0 may hold with X ≇ X_0.
- Two variants: ~ (sections dense on an affinoid cover; Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1, Huber Definition 2.4.2) and
  ~′ (residue fields dense; Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14). ~ implies ~′ for qcqs locally noetherian X_i.
- Frobenius towers are indexed by ℕ; the eventual Frobenius lifting condition is stated modulo ϖ^p for a compatible
  pseudouniformiser ϖ with p ∈ ϖ^pA_0⁺ (in Scholze's torsion paper ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}, so ϖ^p = p^{1−ε}).
- Plus rings: for a ring of definition A⁺ ∋ ϖ, A = A⁺[1/ϖ] and A⁺⁺ is the integral closure of A⁺ in A.
- Level families: compact open subgroups of a locally profinite group G ordered by inclusion; a *cofinality witness* is
  a choice, for every open subgroup U, of a member of the family contained in U.

### Objects

#### `perfectoid-tilde-limit` — Perfectoid tilde-limits X ~ lim X_i of analytic adic spaces

*definition* · planet: **Perfectoid tilde-limit** · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Basic` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Fix a prime p. Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ X_i a functor from I to analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5: every point analytic) whose transition morphisms f_a: X_j → X_i (a: j → i) are quasicompact and quasiseparated, X a perfectoid space in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space (ECD Definition 3.19: locally Spa(R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1, of characteristic 0 or p, no base field), and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i)_i a compatible family (f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i). The pair (X, φ) is a perfectoid tilde-limit of (X_i), written X ~ lim_i X_i, if it is a tilde-limit for Huber's carrier ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity in the generality of Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1, i.e. (a) the continuous map |X| → lim_i |X_i| into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`) is a homeomorphism, and (b) every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X such that the union, over i ∈ I and over open subsets V ⊆ X_i with φ_i(U) ⊆ V, of the images of the restriction maps O_{X_i}(V) → A is dense in A. Conventions pinned: (i) the index category is cofiltered and only the transition maps, not the X_i, are required to be quasicompact and quasiseparated; (ii) no perfectoid base field is fixed: the X_i may be of characteristic 0 or p, and X may lie over a different base than the X_i (Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: the X_i over Q_p, X perfectoid; Scholze's universal cover of an affinoid over Q_p with limit over C_p); (iii) the two conditions (a) and (b) are independent and both are required (tests below); (iv) a tilde-limit is not a categorical limit in adic spaces: X ~ X_0 may hold with X ≇ X_0 (Scholze–Weinstein after Proposition 2.4.4). Equivalent forms of (b), used throughout the stage: (b′) there is an open cover of X by affinoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) for which colim_{(i, V)} O_{X_i}(V) → A has dense image, V running over open affinoids of X_i through which U → X_i factors (Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1); (b″) the same with U affinoid perfectoid and V a quasicompact open at one level (the good affinoid perfectoids of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid; Scholze's survey Definition 2.20). The equivalences (b) ⇔ (b′) ⇔ (b″) given (a) are PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis.

**Hypotheses.**

- I small and cofiltered; transition maps of (X_i) quasicompact and quasiseparated; each X_i an analytic adic space (sheafy, anchor Layer 5).
- X a perfectoid space (sheafy by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy) and φ a compatible family of morphisms of adic spaces.
- Only the density clause is formulated with sections; the weaker residue-field variant of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition: the predicate is the conjunction of (a) and (b); (a) uses the limit of underlying topological spaces, (b) the sheaf O_X and the presheaves O_{X_i} on open subsets.
2. The predicate is H0's Huber tilde-limit for the underlying adic spaces, read with Scholze–Weinstein's hypotheses on the system (transition maps qcqs rather than all X_i qcqs); the compatibility test below records the agreement when all spaces are qcqs.
3. The equivalent forms (b′), (b″) are proved in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis; the relation with the residue-field variant is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit.

**Uses.**

- Scholze–Weinstein, Moduli of p-divisible groups, §2.4 and Theorem 6.3.4: the Lubin–Tate/Rapoport–Zink tower at infinite level is a perfectoid tilde-limit of the finite-level spaces.
- Scholze, torsion paper, Theorem III.1.2 and Corollary III.2.19: existence and uniqueness of perfectoid Shimura varieties X ~ lim X_{K_p}, and of the anticanonical tower.
- Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson, Theorem 2.8 and §4.1: X_∞ ~ lim X_{K(p^n)} over Spa(Q_p, Z_p); pro-étale G-coverings X_∞ ~ lim X_j.
- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, Theorem 5.11: the Hilbert modular anticanonical towers have perfectoid tilde-limits.
- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: the universal pro-finite-étale cover of an affinoid over Q_p is a perfectoid tilde-limit.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers, P8/good-tower, P8/finite-level-affinoid-basis, P9/profinite-galois-tower: the tower theorems of the next stages are stated for perfectoid tilde-limits.
- PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0, S1 and PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: infinite-level Shimura varieties and the K(π,1) argument are tilde-limits.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit` (structure): The predicate X ~ lim X_i on a perfectoid space X, a cofiltered system (X_i) of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps and a compatible cone φ: the two fields `homeomorph` and `dense` below.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.homeomorph` (projection): The homeomorphism |X| ≃ lim_i |X_i| induced by φ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.dense` (projection): Every x ∈ X has an affinoid open neighbourhood U with ⋃_{i, V ⊇ φ_i(U)} im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U)) dense in O_X(U).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.toHuber` (compatibility): For X and all X_i qcqs, IsTildeLimit is H0's Huber tilde-limit predicate on the underlying adic spaces, and conversely.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.iff_goodCover` (characterisation): X ~ lim X_i if and only if (a) holds and X is covered by good affinoid perfectoids (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.lift` (universal-property): For a perfectoid space Y, compatible maps ψ_i: Y → X_i factor uniquely as φ_i ∘ g (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.uniqueIso` (universal-property): Two perfectoid tilde-limits of the same system are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with the cones.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.ofIso` (functoriality): Transport of the predicate along an isomorphism X ≅ X' commuting with the cones.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.restrict` (functoriality): Restriction to the preimage of an open subset at a finite level (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.reindex` (functoriality): Invariance under an initial change of index category (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.const` (example): The constant system on a perfectoid space with the identity cone is a tilde-limit.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (other): If all X_i are qcqs, |X| is a spectral space and each φ_i is a spectral map (Scholze 2012 Remark 7.15; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces).

**Unit tests.**

- `isTildeLimit_test_perfectoidDisc` (computation): For a perfectoid Tate ring R with pseudouniformiser ϖ admitting compatible p-power roots, the compatible maps Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) → Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) exhibit a perfectoid tilde-limit, and the same holds for the torus R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ over the tower R⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩.
- `isTildeLimit_test_const` (degenerate): For a perfectoid space X and the constant system X_i = X (I = the one-object category) with φ = id, X ~ lim X_i; more generally any isomorphism X ≅ X_0 of adic spaces with X perfectoid exhibits X ~ X_0.
- `isTildeLimit_test_not_categorical` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K, Spa(K, O_K) ~ Spa(K[ε]/(ε²), O_K + Kε) along the quotient map K[ε]/(ε²) → K (the image is all of K, the underlying spaces are points), although the two adic spaces are not isomorphic: a tilde-limit is not an isomorphism onto a limit.
- `isTildeLimit_test_density_needed` (non-example): The point Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) with its map to the constant system Spa(Q_p, Z_p) satisfies (a) (both spaces are one point) but not (b) (Q_p is not dense in C_p); so (a) alone does not define tilde-limits.
- `isTildeLimit_test_topology_needed` (non-example): For a perfectoid Tate ring R and X = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), mapping X into the first summand of X_n := D_n ⊔ D_n (D_n = Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩)) satisfies (b) but not (a) (|X| → lim |X_n| misses the second summand); so (b) alone does not define tilde-limits.
- `isTildeLimit_test_huber_compat` (compatibility): If X and all X_i are quasicompact and quasiseparated, X ~ lim X_i in this sense if and only if (X, φ) is a tilde-limit in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity (Huber's Definition 2.4.2) for the underlying adic spaces.

**Acceptance.**

- Compatible-root disc: for a perfectoid Tate ring R whose pseudouniformiser ϖ has a compatible system of p-power roots, Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim_n Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) along T^{1/p^n} ↦ T^{1/p^n} (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers).
- Siegel tower: the perfectoid Shimura variety X*_{Γ(p^∞)} ~ lim_{K_p} X*_{K_p} of Scholze's torsion paper Theorem III.1.2(i) is a perfectoid tilde-limit in this sense (the paper uses ~ of Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1).

**Prerequisites.** `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`, `mathlib:TopCat.limitCone`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, pp. 19-20.

  > Let Xi be a filtered inverse system of adic spaces with quasicompact and quasiseparated transition maps, let X be an adic space, and let fi : X → Xi be a compatible family of morphisms. We write X ∼ lim Xi if the map of underlying topological spaces |X| → lim |Xi | is a homeomorphism

  The two clauses of the definition, with the hypothesis on the transition maps pinned here.

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, Definition 2.4.1, p. 19.

  > and if there is an open cover of X by affinoid Spa(A, A+ ) ⊂ X, such that the map ... has dense image, where the direct limit runs over all open affinoid

  The density clause in the form (b′).

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, after Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20.

  > Of course, this shows that one may have X ∼ X0 , while X 6= X0 .

  A tilde-limit is not a categorical limit (convention (iv)).

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, Remark 2.21, p. 11.

  > In [31, Definition 2.4.1], this notion is introduced for general adic spaces (in the sense of [31, Definition 2.1.5]). The elementary properties of the following proposition also hold in that generality.

  The survey's perfectoid-affinoid form (b″) and its generality.

#### `residue-field-tilde-limit` — Residue-field tilde-limits X ~′ lim X_i over locally noetherian adic spaces (Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14)

*definition* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/ResidueField` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let I be a small cofiltered category, (X_i) an I-indexed system of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space: covered by Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring), X a perfectoid space and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i) a compatible family. Then X ~′ lim X_i (Scholze's notation X ~ lim X_i of Definition 7.14, written ~′ in Scholze–Weinstein after Theorem 2.4.7) means: (a) |X| → lim_i |X_i| is a homeomorphism, and (c) for every x ∈ X with images x_i = φ_i(x), the map of completed residue fields colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^ has dense image, where k(y)^ is the completion of the residue field of O_{Y,y} for the valuation of y (equivalently, colim_i k(x_i) → k(x) has dense image for the valuation topologies). Conventions: no perfectoid base field is fixed (Scholze 2012 works over a perfectoid field K; the definition and the results of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison use only that X is perfectoid and the X_i are qcqs locally noetherian); by Remark 7.15, (a) forces |X| to be spectral, in particular X quasicompact and quasiseparated.

**Hypotheses.**

- Every X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; transition maps are then automatically qcqs.
- The density condition is pointwise on residue fields; the sectionwise condition of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit implies it (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition by the two conditions (a), (c).
2. Remark 7.15: the X_i are spectral with spectral transition maps (qcqs adic spaces and qcqs morphisms), so lim |X_i| is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces; Stacks Lemma 5.24.5), and (a) transports this to |X|.

**Uses.**

- Scholze 2012, Proposition 7.16 - Corollary 7.19: the étale-topos comparison is stated under this hypothesis.
- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: the universal cover is a residue-field tilde-limit and Corollary 7.18 computes its cohomology.
- PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion: H^j(X_∞, F_p) = colim H^j(X_i, F_p) for the universal cover.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit` (structure): The predicate X ~′ lim X_i: fields `homeomorph` and `residueField_dense`.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.homeomorph` (projection): |X| ≃ lim |X_i|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.residueField_dense` (projection): For every x, colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^ has dense image.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.spectralSpace` (other): |X| is spectral and X is qcqs (Remark 7.15).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_isTildeLimit` (compatibility): Every tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian X_i is a residue-field tilde-limit.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.of_bijective` (characterisation): Bijectivity of |X| → lim |X_i| together with (c) already gives (a) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.etaleBaseChange` (functoriality): For Y → X_i étale, Y ×_{X_i} X ~′ lim_{j} Y ×_{X_i} X_j (Proposition 7.16).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsResidueFieldTildeLimit.reindex` (functoriality): Invariance under an initial change of index category.

**Unit tests.**

- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_disc` (computation): For a perfectoid field K, Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~′ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, K°⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩): the underlying spaces agree by the tilde-limit of the disc tower, and at every point the colimit of the residue fields is dense.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_point` (degenerate): For a perfectoid field K, the constant system Spa(K, K°) (noetherian, as K is a field) with the identity satisfies Spa(K, K°) ~′ lim Spa(K, K°).
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_not_dense` (non-example): Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}) → Spa(Q_p, Z_p) (constant system) satisfies (a) but not (c): Q_p is not dense in C_p.
- `isResidueFieldTildeLimit_test_of_tildeLimit` (compatibility): If X ~ lim X_i in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit and all X_i are qcqs locally noetherian, then X ~′ lim X_i.

**Acceptance.**

- The universal pro-finite-étale cover X_∞ = Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) of a connected affinoid noetherian X = Spa(A, A⁺) over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), with X_∞ ~′ lim X_i for the finite étale X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) → X (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, proof of Theorem 4.9).
- The Frobenius tower (P^n)^{ad} ~′ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad} over a perfectoid field of characteristic p (Scholze 2012 Theorem 8.5), for which Corollary 7.19 applies.

**Prerequisites.** `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `mathlib:SpectralSpace`, `mathlib:IsSpectralMap`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, Definition 7.14, pp. 43-44.

  > Let X be a perfectoid space. Further, let Xi , i ∈ I, be a filtered inverse system of noetherian adic spaces over K, and let ϕi : X → Xi , i ∈ I, be a map to the inverse system.

  The data of the definition (over K in the source).

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, Definition 7.14, p. 44.

  > Then we write X ∼ lim Xi if the mapping of underlying topological spaces |X| → lim |Xi | is a homeomorphism, and for any x ∈ X with images xi ∈ Xi , the map of residue fields

  Conditions (a) and (c).

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, Remark 7.15, p. 44.

  > We recall that by assumption all Xi are qcqs. If X ∼ lim Xi , then |X| is an inverse limit of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps, hence spectral, and in particular qcqs again.

  The spectrality clause.

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, after Theorem 2.4.7, p. 21.

  > We remark that the notion ∼ introduced here is stronger than the notion ∼′ introduced in [Sch12], which only talks about the residue fields instead of the sections of the structure sheaf in an open neighborhood.

  The notation ~′ and its relation with ~.
