#### `good-affinoid-perfectoid` — Good affinoid perfectoid subsets of a tilde-limit

*definition* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Good` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be as in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, X a perfectoid space with a compatible cone φ. A good affinoid perfectoid of (X, φ) is a triple (W, i_0, V) where W = Spa(R, R⁺) ⊆ X is an affinoid perfectoid open subset (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space), i_0 ∈ I and V ⊆ X_{i_0} is a quasicompact open subset such that (i) W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V), and (ii) writing V_a := f_a^{-1}(V) ⊆ X_j for a: j → i_0 (the slice category I/i_0, cofiltered), the ring map colim_{a ∈ (I/i_0)^op} O_{X_j}(V_a) → R has dense image. When moreover the V_a are affinoid, V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺), the pair (R, R⁺) is determined by the system (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-uniform-completion). This is the form of Scholze's survey (the paragraph before Proposition 2.22: dense image and homeomorphism with the limit of the finite-level affinoids), of Scholze's torsion paper Theorem III.1.2(iii) and Definition III.3.5(i) (V the preimage of an affinoid V_m at finite level, lim H⁰(V_m, O) → H⁰(V, O) with dense image), and of Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8 (standard affinoids pulled back from level K(p^N)). Under X ~ lim X_i the homeomorphism |W| ≅ lim_a |V_a| is automatic, since W is the preimage of V.

**Hypotheses.**

- W affinoid perfectoid and exactly the preimage of the quasicompact open V ⊆ X_{i_0}; the colimit is over the cofiltered slice I/i_0.
- The density is for the topology of R; no topology is placed on the colimit.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition (a structure carrying W, i_0, V and the two properties).
2. The homeomorphism |W| ≅ lim |V_a| under X ~ lim X_i: preimages commute with limits of topological spaces, and V is open.

**Uses.**

- Scholze's survey, Propositions 2.22 and 2.26: good affinoids cover a tilde-limit and are stable under rational subsets.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/finite-level-affinoid-basis and P8/good-tower: affinoid perfectoids that are preimages of affinoids at finite levels, with closures.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers: density of lim O(V_i) in R for V pulled back from finite level.
- Scholze, torsion paper, Theorem III.1.2(iii) and Definition III.3.5: the affinoid perfectoid subsets of the Siegel tower.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness and P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison: all local arguments are made on good affinoids.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid` (structure): The data (W, i_0, V) with W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V) and dense image of colim_a O(V_a) in O(W).
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.level` (projection): The level i_0 and the finite-level quasicompact open V ⊆ X_{i_0}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.preimage_eq` (characterisation): W = φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V).
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.denseRange` (characterisation): colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a) → O_X(W) has dense range.
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.homeomorph` (compatibility): Under X ~ lim X_i, |W| ≃ lim_a |V_a|.
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.rationalSubset` (functoriality): A rational subset of W is good at a possibly larger level (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis).
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.raise` (functoriality): (W, i_0, V) is good at every level j → i_0 with the preimage V_a.
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.isUniformCompletion` (equivalence): If all V_a are affinoid, O_X(W) is the uniform completion of colim_a O(V_a) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-uniform-completion).
- `PerfectoidSpace.GoodAffinoid.finiteEtaleEquiv` (equivalence): If all V_a are affinoid, FÉt(O_X(W)) ≃ 2-colim_a FÉt(O(V_a)).

**Unit tests.**

- `goodAffinoid_test_disc` (computation): In the perfectoid disc tower over a perfectoid Tate ring R, W = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is good at level 0 with V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}: its coordinate ring is the rational localisation R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩⟨T/ϖ⟩, and the image of colim_n R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩⟨T/ϖ⟩ contains the image of R[T^{1/p^∞}, T/ϖ], which is dense.
- `goodAffinoid_test_empty` (degenerate): The empty subset, with V = ∅ at any level, is a good affinoid perfectoid (R = 0).
- `goodAffinoid_test_not_dense` (non-example): For Spa(C_p) → constant Spa(Q_p), W = Spa(C_p) is the preimage of V = Spa(Q_p) but Q_p is not dense in C_p, so W is not good.
- `goodAffinoid_test_ecd_limit` (compatibility): If all X_i = Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) are affinoid perfectoid, the limit Spa(R, R⁺) of ECD Proposition 6.5 (R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim R_i⁺) is good at every level with V = X_{i_0}.

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid Tate ring R with compatible p-power roots of ϖ, the whole perfectoid disc Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) is good at level 0 with V = X_0, and so is its rational subset {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} with V = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} ⊆ X_0.
- Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: V_i = π_HT^{-1}(V_i) (i = 1, 2) are good at level K(p^N) with V = S_i.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, after Remark 2.21, p. 11.

  > Let us say that a perfectoid affinoid open subset Spa(R, R+ ) ⊂ X is good if

  The notion of good affinoid perfectoid.

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, Definition 2.20 and the definition of good, p. 11.

  > has dense image, where the direct limit runs over all

  The density clause of the notion.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.1, Theorem III.1.2 (i)-(iii), p. 28.

  > There is a unique (up to unique isomorphism) perfectoid space

  Theorem III.1.2, whose part (iii) gives the basis of affinoid perfectoid preimages with dense finite-level sections.

- Przemyslaw Chojecki, David Hansen, Christian Johansson, *Overconvergent modular forms and perfectoid Shimura curves*, §2, Theorem 2.8, p. 11.

  > there exists an N and affinoid opens S1 , S2 ⊆ XK(pN ) such that Vi is the preimage of Si

  Good affinoids pulled back from a finite level.

#### `frobenius-controlled-integral-tower` — Frobenius-controlled integral towers

*definition* · planet: **Frobenius-controlled integral tower** · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Basic` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Fix a prime p. A Frobenius-controlled integral tower (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) consists of: (1) a sequence of rings A_0⁺ → A_1⁺ → A_2⁺ → ⋯ with transition maps t_m: A_m⁺ → A_{m+1}⁺; (2) an element ϖ ∈ A_0⁺ (its images again written ϖ), the compatible pseudouniformiser, such that every A_m⁺ is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete (Mathlib `IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {ϖ}) A_m⁺`) and p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺; then every A_m⁺/ϖ^p is an F_p-algebra and absolute Frobenius induces a ring homomorphism Φ_m: A_m⁺/ϖ → A_m⁺/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p (well defined because (x + ϖy)^p ≡ x^p mod pϖA_m⁺ + ϖ^pA_m⁺ = ϖ^pA_m⁺); (3) the eventual Frobenius lifting condition modulo ϖ^p: an index m_0 and, for every m ≥ m_0, a ring isomorphism w_m: A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p such that (i) t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1} as maps A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p (t_m reduced modulo ϖ^p), and (ii) the w_m are compatible with the transition maps: w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m as maps A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ → A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p (t reduced modulo ϖ on the left and modulo ϖ^p on the right). The generic fibres are the complete Tate rings A_m := A_m⁺[1/ϖ] with ring of definition A_m⁺ (ϖ-adic topology) and the Huber pairs (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) with A_m⁺⁺ the integral closure of A_m⁺ in A_m; X_m := Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺). The finite levels A_m are not assumed perfectoid (in the sources they are strongly noetherian). Source form: if all A_m⁺ are flat algebras over an integral perfectoid ring O with ϖ ∈ O (O = Z_p^cycl or O_K for a perfectoid field K) and t_m modulo ϖ^p is identified, O-linearly, with the relative Frobenius of A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p over O/ϖ^p, then w_m is the composite of the canonical isomorphism A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ, Φ_O} O/ϖ^p ≅ (A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ^p)^{(p)} ≅ A_m⁺/ϖ^p with A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ≅ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ ⊗_{O/ϖ,Φ_O} O/ϖ^p (Φ_O: O/ϖ ≅ O/ϖ^p is bijective because O is perfectoid); in Scholze's torsion paper ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p} and ϖ^p = p^{1−ε}.

**Hypotheses.**

- ϖ ∈ A_0⁺ with p ∈ ϖ^p A_0⁺ (the condition ϖ^p | p of ECD Definition 3.1, placed on the integral model); A_m⁺ ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete.
- The w_m are data (isomorphisms), compatible with the transition maps, and exist only from m_0 on: this is the eventual Frobenius lifting condition modulo the p-th power of the pseudouniformiser.
- Characteristic p is allowed (p = 0 ∈ A_m⁺, e.g. relative Frobenius towers over a perfect base).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition. Well-definedness of Φ_m uses only p ∈ ϖ^pA_m⁺ and the binomial theorem.
2. The constructor from relative Frobenius over an integral perfectoid base O uses that Frobenius O/ϖ → O/ϖ^p is bijective (BMS Lemma 3.10 for O; PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison) and base change of the Frobenius twist along it.

**Uses.**

- Scholze, torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞) tower of Siegel spaces is perfectoid because its integral transition maps are relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε}.
- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, Lemma 5.12 and Theorem 5.11: the Hilbert-modular anticanonical tower, with the transition maps reducing to relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ}.
- PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S1: the anticanonical tower's integral transition maps approximate Frobenius with the required estimates; S1 verifies this definition and applies PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers.
- Scholze, torsion paper, Definition III.2.18: the perfection of a characteristic-p formal scheme along relative Frobenius is the characteristic-p instance.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion and P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound: completion, inversion and the uniformity bound are computed from these data.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower` (structure): The data (A_m⁺, t_m, ϖ, m_0, w_m) with ϖ-torsion-freeness, ϖ-adic completeness, p ∈ ϖ^pA_0⁺ and the lifting conditions (i), (ii).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.frobMod` (data): Φ_m: A_m⁺/ϖ →+* A_m⁺/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p, well defined since p ∈ ϖ^pA_m⁺ (built from Mathlib `frobenius` on the F_p-algebra A_m⁺/ϖ^p).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.transition_comp_lift` (characterisation): t_m ∘ w_m = Φ_{m+1} for m ≥ m_0.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.lift_comp_transition` (characterisation): w_{m+1} ∘ t_{m+1} = t_m ∘ w_m for m ≥ m_0.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.ofRelativeFrobenius` (constructor): From flat ϖ-adically complete algebras over an integral perfectoid O ∋ ϖ whose transition maps reduce modulo ϖ^p to relative Frobenius over O/ϖ^p.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.shift` (functoriality): Dropping the first k terms (and lowering m_0) gives a Frobenius-controlled tower with the same completion.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.Hom` (functoriality): Morphisms of towers: compatible ring maps A_m⁺ → B_m⁺ sending ϖ to ϖ and intertwining the w_m; identity and composition.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.genericFibre` (data): The Huber pairs (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) = (A_m⁺[1/ϖ], integral closure of A_m⁺) and X_m = Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.frobenius_colimit_bijective` (characterisation): Φ: colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.constPerfectoid` (example): The constant tower of a ϖ-torsion-free ϖ-complete integral perfectoid ring, with w = Φ.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.perfection` (example): The relative Frobenius tower of a flat t-adic algebra over a perfect base of characteristic p (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit).

**Unit tests.**

- `frobeniusTower_test_disc` (computation): For a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) and ϖ ∈ R⁺ with compatible p-power roots and ϖ^p | p in R⁺, A_m⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ with inclusions t_m and w_m: (R⁺/ϖ)[T^{1/p^{m+1}}] → (R⁺/ϖ^p)[T^{1/p^m}], r T^{a/p^{m+1}} ↦ Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}, is Frobenius-controlled with m_0 = 0; likewise the torus R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩.
- `frobeniusTower_test_constPerfectoid` (degenerate): For an integral perfectoid ring S that is ϖ-torsion-free and ϖ-adically complete with ϖ^p | p, the constant tower A_m⁺ = S, t_m = id, with w_m = Φ: S/ϖ ≅ S/ϖ^p (bijective by BMS Lemma 3.10) is Frobenius-controlled.
- `frobeniusTower_test_constDisc_not` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K with pseudouniformiser ϖ, the constant tower A_m⁺ = K°⟨T⟩ with identity transition maps is not Frobenius-controlled for any m_0: t_m ∘ w_m = Φ would make T a p-th power modulo ϖ^p in K°⟨T⟩, which it is not.
- `frobeniusTower_test_powerMap` (compatibility): The tower A_m⁺ = K°⟨T⟩ with transition maps T ↦ T^p is isomorphic, as a direct system, to the compatible-root disc tower K°⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ (via T ↦ T^{1/p^m} at level m), hence Frobenius-controlled; the definition is invariant under isomorphism of direct systems.
- `frobeniusTower_test_relativeFrobenius` (characterisation): For a flat ϖ-adic algebra B over an integral perfectoid O ∋ ϖ, the tower whose m-th term is B with O-structure twisted by Φ_O^{-m} and transition maps the relative Frobenius is Frobenius-controlled, and its w_m are the canonical base-change isomorphisms.

**Acceptance.**

- The Siegel anticanonical tower X(p^{-m}ε) of Scholze's torsion paper (ε < 1/2): over an affine Spf R_{m_0} ⊂ X(p^{-m_0}ε) the preimages Spf R_m form a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p} (Corollary III.2.19).
- The compatible-root disc R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ over a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) whose ϖ has compatible p-power roots, with w_m(r T^{a/p^{m+1}}) = Φ(r) T^{a/p^m}.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Ideal.span`, `mathlib:frobenius`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/pseudouniformizer-with-compatible-roots`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 42.

  > On the tower ... of the X(p−mǫ), the transition maps agree with the relative Frobenius map modulo p1−ǫ.

  The eventual Frobenius lifting condition in the source: transition maps equal to relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε} = ϖ^p with ϖ = p^{(1−ε)/p}.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42-43.

  > Moreover, using that the transition maps Rm/p1−ǫ → Rm+1/p1−ǫ agree with the relative Frobenius map, we ﬁnd that (absolute) Frobenius induces an isomorphism

  The colimit Frobenius isomorphism R_∞/ϖ ≅ R_∞/ϖ^p deduced from the lifting condition.

- Christopher Birkbeck, Ben Heuer, Chris Williams, *Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms via perfectoid modular varieties*, §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1748.

  > is a flat formal scheme for which the relative Frobenius mod p1−δ is an isomorphism. It follows that the generic fibre X ∗ (p−∞ ϵ) is perfectoid and moreover, by [30, Proposition 2.4.2], on the generic fibres we have

  The Hilbert-modular instance: relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ} an isomorphism on the limit, whence perfectoid generic fibre and the tilde-limit.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43.

  > where the inverse limit is taken in the category of formal schemes over Zcycl

  The tower is a tower of flat formal schemes over the integral perfectoid base Z_p^cycl.

#### `frobenius-tower-completion` — Completion and inversion of a Frobenius-controlled tower

*construction* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Completion` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** For a Frobenius-controlled integral tower (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower) define: A_∞⁺ := the ϖ-adic completion of the direct limit colim_m A_m⁺ (Mathlib `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {ϖ})` of `Ring.DirectLimit`); A_∞ := A_∞⁺[1/ϖ], topologised so that A_∞⁺ is an open ring of definition with the ϖ-adic topology (a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ); A_∞⁺⁺ := the integral closure of A_∞⁺ in A_∞ (a ring of integral elements). Completion/inversion formula: (i) A_∞⁺/ϖ^k A_∞⁺ = colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^k A_m⁺ for every k ≥ 1; (ii) A_∞⁺ is ϖ-torsion-free, so A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞; (iii) (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is the completed direct limit of the Huber pairs (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) in the sense of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 (compatible rings of definition A_m⁺ with ideals of definition ϖA_m⁺, so ϖA_{m'}⁺ = (ϖA_m⁺)A_{m'}⁺); (iv) the construction depends only on the tail of the tower (shift invariance) and is functorial for morphisms of towers. No uniform completion is taken: by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound the ϖ-adic topology on A_∞⁺ is already the spectral topology of A_∞.

**Hypotheses.**

- A Frobenius-controlled integral tower; ϖ-torsion-freeness of the A_m⁺ is what makes the direct limit and its completion ϖ-torsion-free.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): for the finitely generated ideal (ϖ), the ϖ-adic completion M^ of a module satisfies M^/ϖ^k = M/ϖ^k (Mathlib `AdicCompletion`; Stacks 05GG as cited there), and quotients commute with direct limits.
2. (ii): a direct limit of ϖ-torsion-free rings is ϖ-torsion-free, and ϖ-torsion-freeness passes to the ϖ-adic completion by (i) (multiplication by ϖ on the inverse system of the M/ϖ^k).
3. (iii): the conditions of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 hold with A_{m,0} = A_m⁺ and I_m = ϖA_m⁺; the plus rings: the integral closure of colim A_m⁺⁺ in colim A_m is the integral closure of colim A_m⁺, and completion followed by integral closure gives A_∞⁺⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit).
4. (iv): a cofinal subsequence has the same direct limit; morphisms of towers induce maps of direct limits and of completions.

**Uses.**

- Scholze, torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19 and Definition III.3.5: R_∞⁺ is the p-adic completion of lim R_m⁺ and R_∞ = R_∞⁺[p^{-1}] on affinoid perfectoid subsets.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers: the perfectoid ring of the criterion is this completion.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-tilt: the tilt is computed from A_∞⁺/ϖ^p = colim A_m⁺/ϖ^p.
- PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S1: the completed direct-limit rings of the anticanonical tower.

**API.**

- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completedPlus` (data): A_∞⁺ = ϖ-adic completion of colim_m A_m⁺.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completedPlus_quotient` (simp): A_∞⁺/ϖ^k ≅ colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^k for all k ≥ 1.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completedPlus_torsionFree` (other): A_∞⁺ is ϖ-torsion-free.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completed` (data): A_∞ = A_∞⁺[1/ϖ] with A_∞⁺ an open ring of definition (ϖ-adic).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completed_isTateRing` (instance): A_∞ is a complete Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsTateRing`, `Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completedPair` (data): The Huber pair (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺), A_∞⁺⁺ the integral closure of A_∞⁺ (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.toCompleted` (projection): The compatible maps A_m⁺ → A_∞⁺ and (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) → (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺).
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completedPlus_lift` (universal-property): Compatible maps A_m⁺ → B into a ϖ-adically complete ring extend uniquely to A_∞⁺ → B; uniqueness from density of colim A_m⁺.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completed_shift` (functoriality): The completion of a shifted tower is canonically the same.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.completed_map` (functoriality): A morphism of towers induces a continuous map of completions; identity and composition.
- `Perfectoid.FrobeniusTower.isCompletedDirectLimit` (compatibility): (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is the completed direct limit of (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit.

**Unit tests.**

- `frobeniusTower_completion_test_disc` (computation): For the compatible-root disc tower over (R, R⁺), the completion is R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ (the ϖ-adic completion of R⁺[T^{1/p^∞}]) and A_∞ = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- `frobeniusTower_completion_test_const` (degenerate): For the constant tower of an integral perfectoid S (ϖ-torsion-free, ϖ-complete), the completion is S and A_∞ = S[1/ϖ].
- `frobeniusTower_completion_test_needsCompletion` (non-example): For the disc tower, the element Σ_{n≥1} ϖ^n T^{1/p^n} lies in A_∞⁺ but in no A_m⁺: the direct limit itself is not complete, so the formula needs the completion.
- `frobeniusTower_completion_test_quotient` (characterisation): A_∞⁺/ϖ^p ≅ colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p as rings, compatibly with the maps from the A_m⁺.
- `frobeniusTower_completion_test_ecd` (compatibility): If every A_m⁺ is the ring of integral elements of a perfectoid Tate ring, the completion agrees with the ring R⁺ of ECD Proposition 6.5 for the limit of the Spa(A_m, A_m⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- Compatible-root disc: for the tower R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩, A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_∞ = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- Siegel tower: R_∞ = the p-adic completion of colim_m R_m (Scholze's torsion paper, proof of Corollary III.2.19).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`, `mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:integralClosure`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43.

  > we get a corresponding open aﬃne subset Spf R∞ ⊂ XΓ0(p∞)(ǫ)a, where R∞ is the p-adic comple- tion of lim

  The completion formula in the source.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42.

  > where Rperf+ is the t-adic completion of lim

  The same formula for the perfection tower, with R^{perf} = R^{perf+}[t^{-1}].

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §6, Proposition 6.5, p. 29.

  > Let Xi = Spa(Ri , Ri+ ), i ∈ I, be a cofiltered diagram of affinoid perfectoid spaces. Then the inverse X = limi Xi in the category of perfectoid spaces exists, is affinoid perfectoid

  The analogous completion/inversion formula for towers of perfectoid rings, which the construction extends to non-perfectoid finite levels.

#### `preperfectoid-space` — Preperfectoid adic spaces

*definition* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Preperfectoid` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X be an analytic adic space in the generality of Scholze–Weinstein §2.1 (an analytic Yoneda-adic space, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation; the sheafy adic spaces of anchor Layer 5 form a full subcategory). For an open affinoid U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X with a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A⁺, the strong completion (Â, Â⁺) of (A, A⁺) is the completion of (A, A⁺) for the topology on A that gives A⁺ the ϖ-adic topology (Â⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of A⁺, Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ]; independent of ϖ). X is preperfectoid if X has a cover by open affinoids U_α = Spa(A_α, A_α⁺) whose strong completions (Â_α, Â_α⁺) are perfectoid Tate pairs (ECD Definition 3.1). Over a perfectoid field K this is Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.3.4 (they complete for the p-adic topology on A⁺); Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.3.9 defines X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) to be preperfectoid when every base change to a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 is, and Proposition 2.3.10 compares the two when X lies over a perfectoid K. The natural topology of A and the ϖ-adic topology of A⁺ can differ, and then A itself need not be perfectoid: the nonreduced point Spa(K[X]/X², O_K + KX) is preperfectoid with strong completion (K, O_K).

**Hypotheses.**

- X analytic; the strong completion is taken for the ϖ-adic topology on the plus ring, not the natural topology of A.
- Stability: locally closed subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid (Scholze–Weinstein Propositions 2.3.7 and 2.3.11).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition. Independence of ϖ: two pseudouniformisers of A lying in A⁺ each divide a power of the other in A⁺ (both are topologically nilpotent units with inverses bounded by powers of the other), so they define the same adic topology on A⁺.
2. Stability under locally closed subspaces: open subspaces by definition; for closed subspaces Scholze–Weinstein's proof of Proposition 2.3.7 writes Y = Spa(A/I, B⁺) as the intersection of rational neighbourhoods U_i = {|f_1|, …, |f_k| ≤ |ϖ|^n} and shows the strong completion of O_Y is the completed colimit of the perfectoid O_X(U_i), hence perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower).

**Uses.**

- Scholze–Weinstein, §§2.3-2.4 and §6: the infinite-level moduli spaces of p-divisible groups are first constructed as preperfectoid spaces; their strong completions are the perfectoid tilde-limits.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/strong-completion: the strong completion X̂ represents the restriction of Hom(−, X) to perfectoid spaces.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/represented-functor-comparison: comparison of X, X̂ and the diamond X^◇.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletionPair` (data): For a Huber pair (A, A⁺) with pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A⁺: (Â, Â⁺) with Â⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of A⁺ and Â = Â⁺[1/ϖ].
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletionPair_indep` (characterisation): The strong completion does not depend on the choice of ϖ.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid` (structure): X is covered by open affinoids with perfectoid strong completion.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid.of_isPerfectoid` (instance): Perfectoid spaces are preperfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid.openSubspace` (functoriality): Open subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid.
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid.closedSubspace` (functoriality): Closed (hence locally closed) subspaces of preperfectoid spaces are preperfectoid (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.3.7).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid.baseChange` (compatibility): For X over a perfectoid field K, preperfectoid over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) (all base changes to perfectoid fields) implies preperfectoid over K (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.3.10).
- `PerfectoidSpace.IsPreperfectoid.strongCompletion` (projection): The strong completion X̂ (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/strong-completion).

**Unit tests.**

- `isPreperfectoid_test_nonreducedPoint` (computation): For a perfectoid field K, Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) is preperfectoid: the X-component is infinitely ϖ-divisible in O_K + KX, so the ϖ-adic completion of the plus ring is O_K and the strong completion is (K, O_K).
- `isPreperfectoid_test_perfectoid` (degenerate): Every perfectoid space is preperfectoid, with every affinoid perfectoid its own strong completion.
- `isPreperfectoid_test_disc_not` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K, the closed unit disc D = Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) is not preperfectoid: every open affinoid of D is Spa(A, A⁺) with A a reduced one-dimensional K-affinoid algebra and A⁺ bounded, so the strong completion is (A, A⁺) itself, and A is not perfectoid (for A = K⟨T⟩, T is not a p-th power modulo ϖ^p in K°⟨T⟩).
- `isPreperfectoid_test_overField` (compatibility): For X over a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0, X is preperfectoid in this sense iff it is preperfectoid over Spa(K, O_K) in the sense of Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.3.4: K° ⊂ A⁺ contains a pseudouniformiser ϖ with ϖ^p | p and p | ϖ^N, so the ϖ-adic and p-adic topologies on A⁺ agree.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.3.13: the generic fibre of Spf Z_p⟦X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟧ over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is preperfectoid.
- Every perfectoid space is preperfectoid (its affinoid perfectoids are their own strong completions).

**Prerequisites.** `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.3, Definition 2.3.4, pp. 17-18.

  > Then X is preperfectoid if there is a cover of X by open affinoid Ui = Spa(Ai , A+ i ) ⊂ X such that (Âi , Â+ i ) is a perfectoid

  The definition.

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.3, Definition 2.3.4, p. 18.

  > affinoid (K, OK )-algebra, where we take the completion with respect to the topology on Ai giving A+i the p-adic topology.

  The strong completion uses the p-adic (ϖ-adic) topology on the plus ring.

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.3, Remark 2.3.5, p. 18.

  > As an example, the nonreduced rigid-analytic point X = Spa(K[X]/X 2 , OK + KX) is preperfectoid.

  The non-reduced example used as a test.

#### `strong-completion` — The strong completion X̂ of a preperfectoid space and X̂ ~ X

*construction* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Preperfectoid` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X be a preperfectoid analytic adic space (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/preperfectoid-space). There is a perfectoid space X̂ with a morphism X̂ → X (of Yoneda-adic spaces) such that: (i) |X̂| → |X| is a homeomorphism; (ii) for every open affinoid U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X whose strong completion (Â, Â⁺) is perfectoid, the corresponding open subspace of X̂ is Spa(Â, Â⁺); (iii) X̂ is universal for morphisms from perfectoid spaces to X: every morphism Y → X with Y perfectoid factors uniquely through X̂; (iv) when X is an adic space in the sense of anchor Layer 5 (sheafy affinoid coordinate rings), X̂ ~ X, i.e. (X̂, X̂ → X) is a perfectoid tilde-limit of the one-object system X in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.4, stated there for adic spaces in their §2.1 generality). X̂ is unique up to unique isomorphism by (iii).

**Hypotheses.**

- X preperfectoid; the construction is over no base field (Scholze–Weinstein state it over Spa(K, O_K)).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Affinoid case: for U = Spa(A, A⁺) with (Â, Â⁺) perfectoid, Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism: continuous valuations of (A, A⁺) bounded by 1 on A⁺ are continuous for the ϖ-adic topology on A⁺ (their restriction to A⁺ satisfies |ϖ^n| → 0), and extend uniquely to the completion; rational subsets correspond (anchor Layer 2).
2. Gluing: for a rational subset U′ ⊆ U, the strong completion of O_X(U′) is the rational localisation of (Â, Â⁺), perfectoid by PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids; so the Spa(Â, Â⁺) glue along the open cover to a perfectoid space (anchor Layer 5 gluing).
3. (iii): a map from an affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(B, B⁺) to U corresponds to a continuous (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺); since B⁺ is ϖ-adically complete and the map A⁺ → B⁺ is continuous for the ϖ-adic topologies, it extends uniquely to (Â, Â⁺); glue over covers.
4. (iv): (a) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit is (i); (b) holds on each Spa(Â, Â⁺) since A is dense in Â.

**Uses.**

- Scholze–Weinstein, §2.4 and §6: the moduli space at infinite level is the strong completion of a preperfectoid space and a tilde-limit of the finite levels.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P7/represented-functor-comparison: Hom(−, X̂) = Hom(−, X) on perfectoid spaces.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion` (data): The perfectoid space X̂ of a preperfectoid X, with its map to X.
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.homeomorph` (characterisation): |X̂| → |X| is a homeomorphism.
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.affinoid` (characterisation): Over U = Spa(A, A⁺) with perfectoid strong completion, the open subspace of X̂ is Spa(Â, Â⁺).
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.lift` (universal-property): Every morphism from a perfectoid space to X factors uniquely through X̂.
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.isTildeLimit` (compatibility): X̂ ~ X (a perfectoid tilde-limit of the one-object system).
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.map` (functoriality): A morphism of preperfectoid spaces induces one of strong completions; identity and composition.
- `PerfectoidSpace.strongCompletion.of_perfectoid` (example): For X perfectoid the canonical map X̂ → X is an isomorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `strongCompletion_test_nonreducedPoint` (computation): The strong completion of Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) over a perfectoid field K is Spa(K, O_K).
- `strongCompletion_test_perfectoid` (degenerate): For X perfectoid, the canonical X̂ → X is an isomorphism.
- `strongCompletion_test_not_iso` (non-example): The map Spa(K, O_K) → Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) is a homeomorphism with dense image on functions but not an isomorphism of adic spaces: X̂ ~ X does not mean X̂ ≅ X.
- `strongCompletion_test_universal` (characterisation): For every perfectoid Y, Hom(Y, X̂) → Hom(Y, X) is bijective; for the non-reduced point this says every map from a perfectoid space kills X.

**Acceptance.**

- For a perfectoid field K: the strong completion of Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) is Spa(K, O_K), and Spa(K, O_K) ~ Spa(K[X]/(X²), O_K + KX) although the two spaces differ.
- For X perfectoid, X̂ = X.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/preperfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/generalized-adic-presentation`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.3, Proposition 2.3.6, p. 18.

  > Then there exists a perfectoid space X̂ over Spa(K, OK ) with the same underlying topological space, and such that for any open subset U = Spa(A, A+ ) ⊂ X for which (Â, Â+ ) is perfectoid, the corresponding open subset of X̂ is given by Û = Spa(Â, Â+ ).

  Properties (i) and (ii).

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.3, Proposition 2.3.6, p. 18.

  > The space X̂ is universal for morphisms from perfectoid spaces over Spa(K, OK ) to X.

  Property (iii).

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.4, p. 20.

  > Let X be a preperfectoid space over Spa(K, OK ), where K is a perfectoid field. Let X̂ be the strong completion of X. Then X̂ ∼ X.

  Property (iv).

#### `level-cofinality-witness` — Cofinality witnesses for families of compact open subgroups

*definition* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Cofinality` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let G be a Hausdorff topological group in which the compact open subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of 1 (a locally profinite group: a profinite group, or G(Q_p) for a linear algebraic group G over Q_p). Write CO(G) for the set of compact open subgroups, a cofiltered category under inclusion (K′ → K when K′ ⊆ K; K ∩ K′ is compact open). A level family is a cofiltered category J with a functor j ↦ K_j to CO(G). A cofinality witness for (K_j) is a function U ↦ j(U) from the open subgroups U of G (equivalently from open neighbourhoods of 1) to J with K_{j(U)} ⊆ U. By Mathlib's criterion `CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` (morphisms in CO(G) are unique, so the second condition is automatic), a witness makes j ↦ K_j an initial functor J → CO(G); hence, for every tower (X_K)_{K ∈ CO(G)} of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps (a Shimura tower at p) and every perfectoid X with compatible maps, X ~ lim_{K ∈ CO(G)} X_K iff X ~ lim_{j ∈ J} X_{K_j} (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change). A level family without a witness only computes the tilde-limit of the subtower it indexes: no infinite-level statement for the full tower follows from it.

**Hypotheses.**

- G locally profinite (Hausdorff, compact open subgroups a neighbourhood basis of 1).
- The witness is data; its existence for decreasing sequences inside a compact open subgroup is characterised in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/compact-open-subgroup-cofinality.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Definition. Initiality: for K ∈ CO(G) take j = j(K); any two maps K_j → K agree (thin category), so Mathlib's criterion applies.

**Uses.**

- PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0: prove cofinality of the chosen principal/congruence systems before forming the inverse limit.
- Scholze, torsion paper, Theorem III.1.2: the tower over all K_p ⊂ GSp_{2g}(Q_p) and the subtower of the Γ(p^m) have the same perfectoid tilde-limit.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P8/good-tower (API `reindex`): restricting to a cofinal subsystem gives a good tower with the same limit.
- PerfectoidSpaces:P9/profinite-galois-tower (test `tower_not_cofinal`): a non-cofinal family of levels gives no torsor under the full group.

**API.**

- `PerfectoidSpace.LevelFamily` (structure): A cofiltered J with a functor to the compact open subgroups of a locally profinite group G.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness` (structure): A choice j(U) with K_{j(U)} ⊆ U for every open subgroup U of G.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.initial` (equivalence): A witnessed family J → CO(G) is a Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.isTildeLimit_iff` (compatibility): For a tower (X_K) and perfectoid X: X ~ lim_{CO(G)} X_K ⟺ X ~ lim_J X_{K_j}.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.ofDecreasing` (constructor): A decreasing sequence of open subgroups of a compact open K_0 with trivial intersection has a witness (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/compact-open-subgroup-cofinality).
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.principalCongruence` (example): The principal congruence subgroups of a closed subgroup H ⊆ GL_N(Z_p) are witnessed in H.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.conj` (functoriality): If (K_j) is witnessed, so is (gK_jg^{-1}) for g ∈ G.
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.mono` (functoriality): If K′_j ⊆ K_j compatibly and (K_j) is witnessed, so is (K′_j).
- `PerfectoidSpace.CofinalityWitness.openNormal` (example): In a profinite group the open normal subgroups are witnessed (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`).

**Unit tests.**

- `cofinalityWitness_test_principalCongruence` (computation): In G = GL_N(Q_p) the family K(p^n) = 1 + p^n M_N(Z_p) (n ≥ 1) has the witness U ↦ the least n with K(p^n) ⊆ U, which exists by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/compact-open-subgroup-cofinality since ⋂_n K(p^n) = {1}.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_discrete` (degenerate): For G finite with the discrete topology, the one-element family K = {1} has the witness U ↦ ∗; the tilde-limit of a tower (X_K) over CO(G) is then its value X_{1}.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_gamma0_not` (non-example): In GL_2(Q_p) the decreasing family Γ_0(p^n) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL_2(Z_p) : c ≡ 0 mod p^n} has no witness: every Γ_0(p^n) contains the upper-triangular unipotent (1 1; 0 1), which lies outside the open subgroup K(p). Its tilde-limit (the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞) level) is not the full infinite level.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_const_not` (non-example): The constant family K_j = K with K ≠ {1} (G infinite profinite) has no witness; the limit of the subtower is X_K itself.
- `cofinalityWitness_test_initial` (compatibility): A witness makes j ↦ K_j a Mathlib `Functor.Initial` J → CO(G), so `Functor.Initial.limitIso` identifies lim_J |X_{K_j}| with lim_{CO(G)} |X_K|.

**Acceptance.**

- The principal congruence subgroups K(p^n) = ker(GSp_{2g}(Z_p) → GSp_{2g}(Z/p^n)) have a witness in GSp_{2g}(Q_p), so the Siegel tower of Scholze's torsion paper Theorem III.1.2 may be indexed by n (Theorem III.1.2(iii)).
- The family Γ_0(p^n) ⊂ GL_2(Z_p) has no witness: its limit computes the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞)-level of Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(1), not the full infinite level.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:OpenSubgroup`, `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp`, `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Erratum to 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties'*, item (1), p. 1.

  > Recall that if I is any coﬁltered category, then one can ﬁnd an ordinal λ and a coﬁnal map {µ<λ }→ I. If I is countable, one can choose λ =ω.

  Reindexing a cofiltered system along a cofinal map, the operation a witness licenses.

- Przemyslaw Chojecki, David Hansen, Christian Johansson, *Overconvergent modular forms and perfectoid Shimura curves*, §2, Theorem 2.8, p. 11.

  > There exist a perfectoid space X∞ over Spa(Qp , Zp ) such that

  The infinite-level Shimura curve as a tilde-limit indexed by the principal congruence levels K(p^n).

- Christopher Birkbeck, Ben Heuer, Chris Williams, *Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms via perfectoid modular varieties*, §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1748.

  > To deduce parts (2) and (3), we use that the forgetful morphism

  The towers of Γ_0-, Γ_1- and Γ-levels treated separately: different level families give different tilde-limits.

### General theory of perfectoid tilde-limits

#### `tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit` — Completed direct limits of Huber pairs give tilde-limits (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2)

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/CompletedColimit` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} be a filtered direct system of complete Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with continuous transition maps, and assume there are rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i mapped into one another and finitely generated ideals of definition I_i ⊆ A_{i,0} with I_j = I_i A_{j,0} for j ≥ i. Let A := colim_i A_i with the topology making A_0 := colim_i A_{i,0} an open subring with the I-adic topology, I := colim_i I_i; let A⁺ := the integral closure in A of the image of colim_i A_i⁺, and (Â, Â⁺) the completion. Then (i) (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (A, A⁺) are continuous; (ii) a valuation on A is a continuous valuation with |A⁺| ≤ 1 iff its restrictions to all A_i are, so the restriction map Spa(Â, Â⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a bijection, and it is a homeomorphism; (iii) every rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺); (iv) colim_i A_i → Â has dense image. Consequently, if the X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are adic spaces (A_i sheafy) and Â is perfectoid, then Spa(Â, Â⁺) ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit). In the Tate case with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i_0,0}, the hypotheses hold with I_i = ϖA_{i,0}.

**Hypotheses.**

- Filtered system of complete Huber pairs with compatible rings of definition and ideals of definition satisfying I_j = I_i A_{j,0}.
- Perfectoidness of Â is a hypothesis of the final clause; it is supplied by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers, by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower, or by the application.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i) A_0 is open with f.g. ideal of definition I (images of generators of I_{i_0}); each A_i⁺ contains the topologically nilpotent A_{i,0}-ideal I_i (anchor Layer 0: open integrally closed subrings contain the topologically nilpotent elements, Tau Ceti `Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`), so A⁺ ⊇ I is open; power-boundedness of the image of A_i⁺ follows from continuity.
2. (ii) A valuation v on A restricts to valuations v_i; v is continuous iff v(I^n) → 0 in the sense of continuity for the I-adic ring of definition, which is detected on the generators of I_{i_0}, hence on any single A_i; |A⁺| ≤ 1 iff |A_i⁺| ≤ 1 for all i (integral closure does not change the condition: Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure`). Completion does not change Spa (anchor Layer 2).
3. (iii) and the topology: a rational subset R(T/s) of Spa(A, A⁺) with T, s ⊂ A involves finitely many elements, which come from some A_i, and its preimage statement is Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`; rational subsets form bases on both sides, so the continuous bijection is open.
4. (iv) A is dense in its completion.
5. In the Tate case (compatible pseudouniformiser), (i)-(iii) are PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs; this node adds the general Huber-ring form of Scholze–Weinstein and the tilde-limit conclusion.
6. Final clause: (a) of the tilde-limit is (ii), (b) is (iv) applied to the single affinoid Spa(Â, Â⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- The compatible-root disc: (R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) with A_{n,0} = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩, I_n = ϖA_{n,0}; the completion is R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.
- Scholze–Weinstein §3: T(G)^{ad} ~ lim G[p^n]^{ad} from this proposition (proof of Proposition 3.3.2 there).

#### `good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis` — Good affinoid perfectoids cover a tilde-limit and are stable under rational subsets (Scholze's survey Proposition 2.22)

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Good` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i) be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps and X a perfectoid space with a compatible cone such that |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism. (i) If X ~ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), then X is covered by good affinoid perfectoids (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid) with V affinoid at their level. (ii) If (W, i_0, V) is good and U ⊆ W is a rational subset, then U is good at some level j → i_0 with a quasicompact open V′ ⊆ V_a; if V is affinoid, V′ can be taken a rational subset of V_a. (iii) Hence the good affinoid perfectoids form a basis of the topology of X. (iv) Conversely, if X is covered by good affinoid perfectoids, then X ~ lim X_i. Consequently the conditions (b), (b′), (b″) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit are equivalent given (a).

**Hypotheses.**

- |X| → lim |X_i| a homeomorphism throughout.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i) Given x, choose an affinoid U ∋ x as in (b); choose a rational neighbourhood U′ = U(f/g) ⊆ U of x that is affinoid perfectoid (rational subsets of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids) and maps into an affinoid open of some X_i; by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem` the parameters f, g can be replaced by nearby elements of the dense image of the finite-level sections without changing U′.
2. |U′| is quasicompact open in |X| ≅ lim |X_i|; restricting to the preimages of an affinoid open of X_i (spectral, with spectral transition maps since the transition maps are qcqs), Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 gives a quasicompact open V at a finite level with U′ = φ^{-1}(V) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces); shrinking by (ii) makes V affinoid.
3. Density on U′: O_X(U′) is the completion of O_X(U)[1/g] with ring of definition generated by O_X(U)_0[f/g] (anchor Layer 3 structure presheaf); since f, g come from a finite level, the images of the O_{X_j}(V_a) contain a dense subring (survey: 'the density statement is preserved').
4. (ii) same argument inside W; (iii) rational subsets of the members of a cover form a basis; (iv) the good affinoids give (b″), which implies (b).

**Acceptance.**

- In the compatible-root disc tower every rational subset of the perfectoid disc is the preimage of a rational subset at a finite level and is good.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-basis`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, Proposition 2.22, p. 11.

#### `rational-subsets-from-finite-level` — Quasicompact opens and rational subsets of a tilde-limit come from finite level

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/FiniteLevel` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit. (i) Every quasicompact open U ⊆ X is φ_i^{-1}(U_i) for some i and a quasicompact open U_i ⊆ X_i; if U_i, U′_i ⊆ X_i are quasicompact open with φ_i^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ φ_i^{-1}(U′_i), then f_a^{-1}(U_i) ⊆ f_a^{-1}(U′_i) for some a: j → i, and likewise for equalities, finite unions and finite intersections; (ii) a finite cover of a quasicompact open U ⊆ X by quasicompact opens is the preimage of a finite cover at some finite level; (iii) if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and U = W ∩ {|f_k| ≤ |g| ≠ 0} is a rational subset of W, there are j → i_0 and f′_k, g′ ∈ O(V_a) with U = φ_j^{-1}(U_a(f′/g′)) for the rational subset U_a(f′/g′) of V_a when V_a is affinoid; in general U = φ_j^{-1} of the quasicompact open {|f′_k| ≤ |g′| ≠ 0} ⊆ V_a.

**Hypotheses.**

- X ~ lim X_i; in (iii) the finite-level V_a affinoid for the rational form.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i), (ii): reduce to the spectral case over an affinoid open at a finite level and apply Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 (parts (1)-(4)) to lim |V_a| ≅ φ^{-1}(V).
2. (iii): perturb f_k, g inside the neighbourhood of Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem` to elements of the dense image of colim O(V_a) (the ideal generated by the f_k is open since W is Tate and the f_k generate the unit ideal); the preimage of a rational subset is rational (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`).

**Acceptance.**

- Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson, proof of Theorem 2.17: the rational subset X_{∞,w} of V_1 is the preimage of an affinoid S ⊆ X_{K(p^N)} 'since rational subsets come from finite level'.

#### `good-affinoid-uniform-completion` — A good affinoid perfectoid is the uniform completion of the finite-level coordinate rings; finite étale algebras descend

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Good` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit and (W, i_0, V) a good affinoid perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid), W = Spa(R, R⁺), such that every V_a (a: j → i_0) is affinoid, V_a = Spa(A_a, A_a⁺) (for instance when the transition maps are affinoid). Let (C, C⁺) be the completed direct limit of the (A_a, A_a⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit, Tate case with a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A_{i_0} that is also one of R). Then: (i) the canonical map (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) identifies (R, R⁺) with the uniformization of (C, C⁺) (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization), R⁺ being the integral closure of the closure of the image of C⁺; in particular R is determined by the system (V_a); (ii) base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_a FÉt(A_a) → FÉt(R), and similarly for every rational localisation of W pulled back from a finite level.

**Hypotheses.**

- All V_a affinoid; ϖ a common pseudouniformiser.
- R perfectoid, hence uniform (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Spectral seminorms: for c ∈ colim A_a, sup over rank-one points of Spa(R, R⁺) of |c| equals the sup over rank-one points of Spa(C, C⁺), because Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ lim |V_a| ≅ Spa(C, C⁺) compatibly with evaluation (tilde-limit condition (a) and PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (ii)).
2. R is uniform, so its topology is defined by its spectral norm; the image of colim A_a is dense (goodness); hence C → R extends to an isometric isomorphism from the separated completion of C for the spectral seminorm, i.e. C^u ≅ R (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13). Plus rings: both are the elements of absolute value ≤ 1 on the common spectrum (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`).
3. (ii): FÉt(colim A_a) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(A_a) since finite étale algebras and their morphisms are finitely presented; FÉt(colim A_a) ≃ FÉt(C) because colim A_{a,0} is henselian along ϖ as a filtered colimit of ϖ-adically complete rings (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions) and Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8 (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation); FÉt(C) ≃ FÉt(C^u) = FÉt(R) by Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(a).

**Acceptance.**

- For the compatible-root disc tower, C = R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ already uniform, and every finite étale R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebra is defined over some R⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩.
- ECD Lemma 15.3/Proposition 15.4: for the universal finite étale tower A → A_i of a Tate Z_p-algebra, the uniform completion of colim A_i is perfectoid and is the ring of the tilde-limit.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`

**Sources.**

- Kiran S. Kedlaya, Ruochuan Liu, *Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations*, §2.8, Definition 2.8.13, p. 63.

#### `tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness` — A perfectoid tilde-limit represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on perfectoid spaces and is unique (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.5)

*theorem* · planet: **Uniqueness of perfectoid tilde-limits** · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Uniqueness` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with quasicompact quasiseparated transition maps and X ~ lim X_i a perfectoid tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit). Then for every perfectoid space Y (of any characteristic, over no fixed base field), and more generally every analytic adic space Y covered by affinoids Spa(B, B⁺) with B uniform, the map Hom(Y, X) → lim_i Hom(Y, X_i), g ↦ (φ_i ∘ g)_i, is bijective. Consequently: (i) X represents the functor Y ↦ lim_i Hom(Y, X_i) on perfectoid spaces; (ii) if (X′, φ′) is another perfectoid tilde-limit of the same system, there is a unique isomorphism X ≅ X′ compatible with the cones; (iii) a morphism of systems (X_i) → (X′_i) (over a common index category) induces a unique morphism between perfectoid tilde-limits commuting with the cones; (iv) over a base S (all X_i over S compatibly), the same holds for S-morphisms.

**Hypotheses.**

- Only uniformity of the coordinate rings of Y is used, not perfectoidness; no perfectoid base field (Scholze–Weinstein state it for perfectoid affinoid (K, O_K)-algebras).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Both sides are sheaves on Y for the analytic topology (adic spaces are sheaves; lim of sheaves), so one may assume Y = Spa(B, B⁺) affinoid with B uniform, and, using the continuous map |Y| → lim |X_i| ≅ |X| and the basis of good affinoids (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis), that the compatible maps ψ_i factor through V_a for a good (W, i_0, V), W = Spa(R, R⁺).
2. Injectivity: two maps g, g′: Y → W with φ_i g = φ_i g′ agree on |Y| (|W| ≅ lim |V_a|) and their ring maps R → B agree on the dense image of colim_a O(V_a), hence everywhere by continuity.
3. Valuation comparison: for y ∈ Y let x ∈ W be the point with φ_j(x) = ψ_j(y) for all j (bijectivity of |W| → lim |V_a|). For c ∈ colim_a O(V_a), |ψ^*c(y)| ≤ |ψ^*c′(y)| iff |c(x)| ≤ |c′(x)| (both valuations restrict to the same point of each V_a).
4. Factorisation: if c maps to 0 in R then |c(x)| = 0 for all x, so ψ^*c vanishes at every point of Spa(B, B⁺); B uniform implies ψ^*c = 0 (its spectral seminorm is a norm). So colim O(V_a) → B factors through the image C′ ⊆ R.
5. Continuity: choose a pseudouniformiser ϖ′ of R in C′ (units near a pseudouniformiser are pseudouniformisers). If c ∈ C′ ∩ ϖ′^n R⁺ then |c(x)| ≤ |ϖ′(x)|^n on W, hence |ψ^*c| ≤ |ψ^*ϖ′|^n on Spa(B, B⁺), so ψ^*c ∈ (ψ^*ϖ′)^n B⁺ (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`); ψ^*ϖ′ is a topologically nilpotent unit of B (it is nonvanishing and of absolute value < 1 at every point; anchor Layers 1-2). Hence C′ → B is uniformly continuous and extends to R → B, R⁺ → B⁺ (C′ ∩ R⁺ is dense in R⁺ because R⁺ is open).
6. The resulting map of Huber pairs gives g: Y → W with φ_j g = ψ_j (maps into an affinoid adic space are maps of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 5). Glue over covers; (ii)-(iv) are formal consequences of representability.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper Corollary III.2.19 and Theorem III.1.2(i): uniqueness of the perfectoid anticanonical tower and of X*_{Γ(p^∞)} up to unique isomorphism.
- Two perfectoid tilde-limits of the compatible-root disc tower (for instance R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and its presentation through T ↦ T^p transition maps) are uniquely isomorphic.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_of_forall_vle_one`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.5, p. 20.

  > assume that there is a perfectoid space X over Spa(K, OK ) such that X ∼ lim Xi . Then for any perfectoid affinoid (K, OK )-algebra

  The hypothesis of the statement.

*comparison* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Diamond` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces over Spa(Z_p, Z_p) with qcqs transition maps. (i) If X ~ lim X_i is a perfectoid tilde-limit, then h_X ≅ lim_i h_{X_i} as presheaves on the category of perfectoid spaces (h_Y = Hom(−, Y)), and the induced map of v-sheaves X^◇ → lim_i X_i^◇ on Perf (diamonds of DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor; the limit is a diamond by DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons) is an isomorphism, compatible with |X^◇| = |X| ≅ lim |X_i| = lim |X_i^◇|. (ii) If the X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) are affinoid with completed direct limit (A, A⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit) and uniformization (A^u, A^{u+}), then lim_i Spd(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spd(A^u, A^{u+}) and |lim_i X_i^◇| ≅ |Spa(A^u, A^{u+})|; if moreover A^u is perfectoid, then X := Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ~ lim X_i and X^◇ ≅ lim X_i^◇. (iii) If lim_i X_i^◇ ≅ X^◇ for a perfectoid space X with compatible maps to the X_i (the hypothesis of Hansen–Johansson Lemma 5.11 and Definition 5.12), then |X| → lim_i |X_i| is a homeomorphism and (when the X_i are qcqs, or locally over a qcqs open at a finite level) every quasicompact open and every rational subset of X is the preimage of one at a finite level; the density condition (b) of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit is then equivalent, on an affinoid W = φ^{-1}(Spa(A_a, A_a⁺)), to perfectoidness of the uniformization of colim A_a (then W = Spa of it by (ii) and full faithfulness of untilts).

**Hypotheses.**

- X_i analytic over Spa(Z_p, Z_p) so that X_i^◇ is defined (ECD Definition 15.5).
- Representability of lim X_i^◇ alone gives the topological clause and finite-level descriptions; the density clause is stated separately in (iii).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): the presheaf statement is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness. For S ∈ Perf, a point of lim X_i^◇(S) is a compatible family of untilts (S^♯_i, ι_i) with maps S^♯_i → X_i; marked untilts have no automorphisms and are compatible with the transition maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair), so it is one untilt S^♯ with compatible maps S^♯ → X_i, i.e. by representability a map S^♯ → X. Topological compatibility: |Y^◇| = |Y| for analytic Y (DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor) and |lim Y_i| ≅ lim |Y_i| for locally spatial diamonds with qcqs transition maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons).
2. (ii): compatible maps of pairs (A_i, A_i⁺) → (O(S^♯), O⁺(S^♯)) are a map from colim, which extends uniquely to the completion (O(S^♯) is complete) and then to the uniformization (O(S^♯) is uniform; uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of uniform rings, Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization). If A^u is perfectoid, Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ~ lim X_i by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (Spa is unchanged by uniformization) and Spd(A^u, A^{u+}) = Spa(A^u, A^{u+})^◇ (ECD Lemma 15.2).
3. (iii): topology as in (i); finite-level descriptions by Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 as in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/rational-subsets-from-finite-level; for the density clause, W^◇ ≅ lim Spd(A_a, A_a⁺) ≅ Spd((colim A_a)^u) by (ii), and a perfectoid pair is determined by its diamond with untilt (tilting slice equivalence, PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence), so W ≅ Spa of the uniformization exactly when the latter is perfectoid, in which case colim A_a is dense in O(W).

**Acceptance.**

- ECD Proposition 15.4: for the universal finite étale G_i-torsor tower A → A_i of a Tate Z_p-algebra, Spd(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) = lim Spd(A_i, A_i⁺), and Spa(Â_∞, Â_∞⁺) ~ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) by (ii).
- Hansen–Johansson Lemma 5.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/finite-level-affinoid-basis): for locally noetherian X_i with finite transition maps and lim X_i^◇ perfectoid, rational subsets of the limit are pulled back from finite levels, by (iii).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/rational-subsets-from-finite-level`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/limits-and-finite-stage-comparisons`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, Proposition 2.23, p. 12.

  > on perfectoid spaces over K. In particular, it is unique up to unique isomorphism.

  Representability of the inverse limit of represented functors.

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §15, Proposition 15.4, p. 90.

  > Let A be a Tate Zp -algebra with an open and integrally closed subring A+ ⊂ A, and choose a cofiltered inverse system of finite groups Gi with surjective transition maps

  The diamond of a completed tower as an inverse limit of diamonds.

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §15, Lemma 15.3, p. 90.

  > If A is a Tate Zp -algebra, then the uniform completion A d∞ of A∞ is perfectoid.

  Uniform completion in (ii).

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §15, after Definition 15.5, p. 91.

  > We note that this definition (and the next lemma) work in the generality of adic spaces as defined in [SW13, Section 2.1].

  The diamond functor on analytic adic spaces in the generality used here.

#### `tilde-limit-rational-restriction` — Restriction of a tilde-limit to compatible open and rational subsets

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Restriction` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I, U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0} an open subset (in particular a rational subset of an affinoid open), U_a := f_a^{-1}(U_{i_0}) ⊆ X_j for a: j → i_0, and U := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(U_{i_0}), an open perfectoid subspace of X (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces). Then U ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} U_a (the slice category I/i_0, which is initial in I by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change). Moreover, if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and U_{i_0} = V(f/g) is a rational subset of V, then W ∩ U = Spa(R⟨f/g⟩, R⟨f/g⟩⁺) is the rational localisation of (R, R⁺) = (O(W), O⁺(W)) at the pulled-back parameters (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids), it is good at level i_0 with the rational subset V(f/g), and colim_a O_{X_j}(V_a(f/g)) → R⟨f/g⟩ has dense image.

**Hypotheses.**

- U_{i_0} open at one finite level; the transition maps restricted to the U_a stay qcqs.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Topology: preimages of an open subset commute with limits of topological spaces, so the homeomorphism |X| ≅ lim |X_i| restricts to |U| ≅ lim_a |U_a|.
2. Density: U is covered by the rational subsets of good affinoids W of X that lie in U and are pulled back from finite levels (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis); these are good for the system (U_a), which gives (b″) and hence (b).
3. The rational form: the structure presheaf on rational subsets (anchor Layer 3) and PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids identify O(W ∩ U); the finite-level sections O(V_a)[f/g] have dense image.

**Acceptance.**

- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11: from X*(p^{-∞}ε) ~ lim X*(p^{-n}ε) one restricts to the open modular locus to get the perfectoid tilde-limit X(p^{-∞}ε) ~ lim X(p^{-n}ε).
- In the compatible-root disc tower, the preimage of {|T| ≥ 1} (the torus) is ~ lim of the tori {|T^{1/p^n}| ≥ 1}.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-cofinal-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`

**Sources.**

- Christopher Birkbeck, Ben Heuer, Chris Williams, *Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms via perfectoid modular varieties*, §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1748.

  > By [30, Proposition 2.4.3], we can now restrict to the open modular curve to deduce that there is a perfectoid tilde-limit

  Restriction of a perfectoid tilde-limit to an open subset pulled back from finite level.

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces: a survey*, §2, proof of Proposition 2.22, p. 11.

  > Moreover, the density statement is preserved (by the definition of the structure presheaf on rational subsets), so U ′ is good.

  Density on rational subsets.

#### `tilde-limit-cofinal-change` — Tilde-limits are invariant under initial changes of index category

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Reindex` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let u: J → I be an initial functor between small cofiltered categories (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`; for directed sets, a coinitial subset). For a system (X_i)_{i∈I} of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, a perfectoid space X and a compatible cone (φ_i), X ~ lim_{i∈I} X_i iff X ~ lim_{j∈J} X_{u(j)} for the restricted cone (φ_{u(j)}). In particular: (a) for every i_0 ∈ I the forgetful functor I/i_0 → I is initial, so a tilde-limit depends only on the tail of the system; (b) for I = ℕ (as an inverse system) any infinite subsequence may be used; (c) for level families of compact open subgroups with a cofinality witness (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness), the full tower and the witnessed subtower have the same perfectoid tilde-limits.

**Hypotheses.**

- u initial; both categories small and cofiltered.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Topology: for u initial, the canonical map lim_I |X_i| → lim_J |X_{u(j)}| is an isomorphism in TopCat (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`), compatible with the maps from |X|.
2. Density: for each i there is j with a morphism u(j) → i (initiality), and the images of O_{X_i}(V) in O_X(U) are contained in the images of O_{X_{u(j)}}(f^{-1}V); conversely J-terms are I-terms, so the unions in condition (b) agree.
3. (a) uses Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered` for the slice; (c) is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Theorem III.1.2: X*_{Γ(p^∞)} ~ lim_{K_p} X*_{K_p} and the statements at levels Γ(p^m) for m large refer to the same tilde-limit.
- Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8 indexes the Shimura-curve tower by K(p^n); the full tower of compact open subgroups gives the same X_∞.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_of_exists_of_isCofiltered`, `mathlib:TopCat.limitCone`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Erratum to 'p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties'*, item (1), p. 1.

  > Recall that if I is any coﬁltered category, then one can ﬁnd an ordinal λ and a coﬁnal map {µ<λ }→ I. If I is countable, one can choose λ =ω.

  Reindexing a cofiltered system along a cofinal functor.

- Przemyslaw Chojecki, David Hansen, Christian Johansson, *Overconvergent modular forms and perfectoid Shimura curves*, §2, Theorem 2.8 and the remarks after it, p. 11.

  > A few remarks are in order. For the definition of ∼ we refer to [SW, Definition 2.4.1].

  The Shimura-curve tilde-limit indexed by the cofinal principal congruence levels.

#### `compact-open-subgroup-cofinality` — A decreasing family of open subgroups of a profinite group is cofinal iff its intersection is trivial

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Cofinality` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let K be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group; Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp`) and (K_n)_{n≥0} a decreasing sequence of closed subgroups (more generally a family of closed subgroups directed downwards). Then every open neighbourhood of 1 in K (equivalently every open subgroup) contains some K_n if and only if ⋂_n K_n = {1}. Consequences: (i) for a closed subgroup H ⊆ GL_N(Z_p), the principal congruence subgroups H ∩ (1 + p^n M_N(Z_p)), n ≥ 1, are cofinal among the open subgroups of H and give a cofinality witness (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness) in any locally profinite G containing H as a compact open subgroup; (ii) Γ_0(p^n) and Γ_1(p^n) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL_2(Z_p): c ≡ 0, d ≡ 1 mod p^n} are not cofinal in GL_2(Z_p), since both contain the unipotent upper triangular subgroup; (iii) a family (K′_n) with K′_n ⊆ K_n and (K_n) cofinal is cofinal.

**Hypotheses.**

- K profinite (compactness is essential: in a non-compact group a decreasing family of open subgroups with trivial intersection need not be cofinal).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. ⇐: for U open with 1 ∈ U, the sets K_n \ U are closed in the compact space K, directed downwards, with empty intersection (⋂ K_n = {1} ⊆ U); by the finite intersection property one of them is empty, i.e. K_n ⊆ U.
2. ⇒: open subgroups of a profinite group intersect to {1}: every open neighbourhood of 1 contains an open normal subgroup (Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`) and K is Hausdorff; equivalently apply Mathlib `ProfiniteGrp.closedSubgroup_eq_sInf_open` to the trivial subgroup.
3. (i): ⋂_n (1 + p^n M_N(Z_p)) = {1}; (ii): the matrix (1 1; 0 1) lies in every Γ_0(p^n) and Γ_1(p^n) but not in 1 + pM_2(Z_p); (iii) immediate.

**Acceptance.**

- The Siegel levels Γ(p^m) ⊂ GSp_{2g}(Z_p) of Scholze's torsion paper form a cofinal family; the anticanonical levels Γ_0(p^m) do not, and their tilde-limit is the Γ_0(p^∞)-level of Corollary III.2.19.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp`, `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.exist_openNormalSubgroup_sub_open_nhds_of_one`, `mathlib:ProfiniteGrp.closedSubgroup_eq_sInf_open`, `mathlib:OpenSubgroup`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/level-cofinality-witness`

**Sources.**

- Przemyslaw Chojecki, David Hansen, Christian Johansson, *Overconvergent modular forms and perfectoid Shimura curves*, §2, proof of Lemma 2.24, p. 20.

  > Recall that, by the definitions, we may find a system of open normal subgroups Gj of G such that G ∼= lim G/Gj

  A cofinal system of open normal subgroups of a profinite group, presenting G as the limit of its finite quotients.

- Christopher Birkbeck, Ben Heuer, Chris Williams, *Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms via perfectoid modular varieties*, §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1748.

  > To deduce parts (2) and (3), we use that the forgetful morphism

  The Γ_0-, Γ_1- and Γ-level towers are distinct towers, obtained from one another by finite étale steps, not by cofinal reindexing.

#### `tilde-limit-gluing` — Locality and gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits

*theorem* · planet: **Gluing of perfectoid tilde-limits** · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/Gluing` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of analytic adic spaces with qcqs transition maps, i_0 ∈ I, and (V^α)_{α} an open cover of X_{i_0}, with preimages V^α_a := f_a^{-1}(V^α) ⊆ X_j (a: j → i_0). (i) Locality: a perfectoid space X with a compatible cone satisfies X ~ lim X_i iff for every α the open subspace U^α := φ_{i_0}^{-1}(V^α) satisfies U^α ~ lim_a V^α_a. (ii) Gluing: if for every α the system (V^α_a)_a has a perfectoid tilde-limit U^α, then there is a perfectoid space X with a compatible cone and X ~ lim X_i; X is glued from the U^α along the open subspaces U^{αβ} ⊆ U^α that are the restrictions of U^α to V^α ∩ V^β (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), identified by the unique isomorphisms of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness (which also give the cocycle condition). (iii) Torsion-paper form: suppose that for all large m the X_m are the generic fibres of a tower and that |lim_m X_m| is covered by subsets W that are preimages of affinoid opens V_m = Spa(R_m, R_m⁺) ⊆ X_m for all sufficiently large m (compatible with the transition maps) such that, with R_∞⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_m R_m⁺ and R_∞ = R_∞⁺[1/ϖ], (R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺) is perfectoid (R_∞⁺⁺ the integral closure of R_∞⁺); then there is a unique perfectoid space X_∞ with |X_∞| = lim |X_m| and X_∞ ~ lim X_m, whose restriction to each W is Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺).

**Hypotheses.**

- Transition maps qcqs; the cover is by opens of one finite level.
- In (iii), 'for all large m' allows the affinoid description to start at a level depending on W.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): lim |V^α_a| is the preimage of V^α in lim |X_j|, an open subset, and these cover; a continuous bijection that restricts to homeomorphisms over an open cover is a homeomorphism; condition (b) is local by definition.
2. (ii): the U^α restricted to V^α ∩ V^β are tilde-limits of the same system (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), hence uniquely isomorphic compatibly with cones (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness); uniqueness gives the cocycle condition on triple overlaps; glue adic spaces along opens (anchor Layer 5) — perfectoidness is local (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space); the cones glue by uniqueness, and (i) gives X ~ lim X_i.
3. (iii): for each W, Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m V_m by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (Tate case, rings of definition R_m⁺); apply (ii) to the cover of the finite level by the V_m (and their finite unions, using that the W are open in |lim X_m|).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, §III.3: |X*_{Γ(p^∞)}| has a natural structure of perfectoid space obtained by gluing the Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺) over affinoid perfectoid subsets (Definition III.3.5), and X*_{Γ(p^∞)} ~ lim X*_{K_p}.
- Chojecki–Hansen–Johansson Theorem 2.8: X_∞ is glued from the two affinoid perfectoids V_1, V_2 pulled back from level K(p^N).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/open-subspaces-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.3, Definition III.3.5 (ii), p. 56.

  > Γ(p∞)| is perfectoid if it can be covered by aﬃnoid perfectoid subsets.

  Perfectoid subsets of the topological limit are those covered by affinoid perfectoid subsets.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.3, after Definition III.3.5, p. 57.

  > by gluing the spaces

  The perfectoid structure is obtained by gluing the affinoid pieces Spa(R_∞, R_∞⁺).

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43.

  > cf. [56, Deﬁnition 2.4.1, Proposition 2.4.2]; for uniqueness, cf. [56, Proposition 2.4.5].

  Existence on affinoids by the completed direct limit and uniqueness by representability, which is what makes gluing possible.
