#### `tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change` — Finite étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/BaseChange` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I and g: Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0} a finite étale morphism of analytic adic spaces (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism). Put Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j for a: j → i_0 (finite étale over X_j; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change) and Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X. Then Y exists in adic spaces, is a perfectoid space, Y → X is finite étale (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-perfectoid-is-perfectoid), and Y ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} Y_a. Affinoid formula: if (W, i_0, V) is good with V = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid and g^{-1}(V) = Spa(B, B⁺) with B ∈ FÉt(A) and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), then the preimage of W in Y is Spa(B ⊗_A R, (B ⊗_A R)⁺) with (B ⊗_A R)⁺ the integral closure of R⁺, and colim_a (B ⊗_A O(V_a)) → B ⊗_A R has dense image; it is good at level i_0 with V′ = g^{-1}(V).

**Hypotheses.**

- g finite étale at one finite level; X perfectoid.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Existence and perfectoidness: the fibre product along a map from a perfectoid space exists and is perfectoid and finite étale over X (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii)-(iv) and Proposition 7.10, in PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change; ECD Theorem 6.1(i) for B ⊗_A R).
2. Density: B is finite projective over A, so B ⊗_A − commutes with direct limits and carries a dense-image map colim_a O(V_a) → R to a dense-image map (locally B is a direct summand of A^n).
3. Topology: over a good W with all V_a affinoid, |Spa(B ⊗_A R)| = |Spa((B ⊗_A C)^u)| = |Spa(B ⊗_A C)| = lim_a |Spa(B ⊗_A O(V_a))| by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-uniform-completion (R = C^u), Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.8.16(b) and Definition 2.8.13 (uniformization commutes with finite étale base change and does not change Spa) and PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit applied to the finite étale pairs; in general cover by such W (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis) and use that the question is local over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (i)).
4. Hence (a) and (b″) hold for Y.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, §III.2.4: D_m → X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a finite étale pulls back to the perfectoid space D_{mΓ_0(p^∞)} over the anticanonical tower.
- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11(2): pulling back the finite étale X_{Γ_1*(p^n)} → X_{Γ_0*(p^n)} gives a tower of finite étale perfectoid spaces over X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a.
- Kummer test: over a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0 and p ≠ 2, the perfectoid torus X = Spa(K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩); pulling back the finite étale S ↦ S² = T cover gives Y = Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^n}⟩).

#### `tilde-limit-base-change` — Étale base change of perfectoid tilde-limits (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3, étale case)

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/BaseChange` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit, i_0 ∈ I and g: Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0} an étale morphism of analytic adic spaces in the sense of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism (locally an open immersion into a space finite étale over an open subset). Put Y_a := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j and Y := Y_{i_0} ×_{X_{i_0}} X. Then Y exists, is a perfectoid space étale over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces), and Y ~ lim_{a ∈ I/i_0} Y_a. This is the case of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3 (base change along an arbitrary Y_{i_0} → X_{i_0}, proved there by reference to Huber's Remark 2.4.3) in which the base change of a perfectoid space is again perfectoid, and the sectionwise version of Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16.

**Hypotheses.**

- g étale; for non-étale g the fibre product Y need not be perfectoid and is not considered here (Zariski-closed base changes are PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Existence and étaleness: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii), Proposition 7.10).
2. Locality: by the local description of étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, equivalent form: rational subset of a finite étale cover of a rational subset of an affinoid open), Y_{i_0} is covered by opens Z ⊆ Y_{i_0} of the form Z ⊆ Z′ → V ⊆ X_{i_0} with V open, Z′ → V finite étale and Z ⊆ Z′ open.
3. For each such piece: restrict to V (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction), base change along Z′ → V (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change), restrict to Z (rational restriction again); so the preimage of Z in Y is ~ lim of the preimages of Z in the Y_a.
4. Glue: the preimages of the Z cover Y, so Y ~ lim Y_a by the locality clause of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing.

**Acceptance.**

- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11: 'perfectoid tilde-limits commute with fibre products', used for the finite étale torsors between the Γ_0-, Γ_1- and Γ-level towers.
- An open immersion U_{i_0} ⊆ X_{i_0} recovers PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.3, p. 20.

  > In the situation of Definition 2.4.1, let Yi → Xi be any map of adic spaces, and let Yj = Yi ×Xi Xj → Xj for j ≥ i be the pullback, as well as Y = Yi ×Xi X → X. Then Y ∼ limj≥i Yj .

  The statement for arbitrary maps; this node proves the étale case.

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, Proposition 7.16, p. 44.

  > Let the situation be as in Definition 7.14, and let Y → Xi be an étale morphism of noetherian adic spaces. Then Y ×Xi X ∼ limj≥i Y ×Xi Xj .

### Frobenius-controlled towers and perfectoid towers

#### `frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound` — Frobenius on the completed tower is bijective modulo ϖ, and the uniformity bound ϖA_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺

*lemma* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Uniformity` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with completion (A_∞⁺, A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion). Then: (i) Φ: A_∞⁺/ϖ → A_∞⁺/ϖ^p, x ↦ x^p, is a bijection (in fact colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ → colim_m A_m⁺/ϖ^p is, and these are the quotients of A_∞⁺); (ii) A_∞⁺ is a ϖ-torsion-free, ϖ-adically complete ring with p ∈ ϖ^pA_∞⁺ and bijective Frobenius modulo ϖ, hence an integral perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Definition 3.5 (Lemma 3.10(ii)); (iii) uniformity bound: A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞° and ϖ·A_∞° ⊆ A_∞⁺; more precisely, after replacing ϖ by a unit multiple admitting a compatible system of p-power roots (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.9), the cokernel of A_∞⁺ → A_∞° is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, i.e. A_∞⁺ → A_∞° is an almost isomorphism for the ideal (ϖ^{1/p^∞}) (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup); consequently A_∞° is bounded, A_∞ is uniform, and the ϖ-adic topology on A_∞⁺ is the topology of the spectral norm of A_∞; (iv) A_∞⁺⁺ satisfies A_∞⁺ ⊆ A_∞⁺⁺ ⊆ A_∞° ⊆ ϖ^{-1}A_∞⁺.

**Hypotheses.**

- A Frobenius-controlled integral tower; only the terms m ≥ m_0 matter.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i) Surjectivity: for y ∈ A_m⁺/ϖ^p with m ≥ m_0 put x = w_m^{-1}(y) ∈ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ; then t_m(y) = t_m(w_m(x)) = Φ_{m+1}(x), so y becomes a p-th power in the colimit. Injectivity: if x ∈ A_{m+1}⁺/ϖ has Φ_{m+1}(x) = t_m(w_m(x)) = 0 in A_k⁺/ϖ^p for some k > m, then by the compatibility w_k(t(x)) = t(w_m(x)) = 0 in A_k⁺/ϖ^p (x transported to A_{k+1}⁺/ϖ), and w_k is injective, so x vanishes in A_{k+1}⁺/ϖ. The quotients of A_∞⁺ are those of the colimit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (i)).
2. (ii) Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.10(ii) applied with π = ϖ, a non-zero-divisor by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (ii); the definition of integral perfectoid rings is PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings.
3. (iii) Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.21 (R_0 = A_∞⁺, π = ϖ): R_0[1/π] with the π-adic topology on R_0 is a complete Tate ring, perfectoid in Fontaine's sense, with πR° ⊆ R_0 and R_0 ⊆ R° with cokernel killed by all fractional powers of π; imported through PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison. Directly: A_∞⁺ is p-root closed in A_∞ by injectivity in (i) (x ∈ A_∞, x^p ∈ A_∞⁺ ⇒ x ∈ A_∞⁺, by induction on the ϖ-adic valuation of a denominator), and for x ∈ A_∞° with x^{p^n} ∈ ϖ^{-c}A_∞⁺ for all n, (ϖ^{c/p^n}x)^{p^n} ∈ A_∞⁺ gives ϖ^{c/p^n}x ∈ A_∞⁺ for all n, hence ϖx ∈ A_∞⁺.
4. (iv) A_∞° is integrally closed in A_∞ and contains A_∞⁺, so it contains A_∞⁺⁺.

**Acceptance.**

- For the compatible-root disc tower, A_∞⁺ = R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and A_∞° = R°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩; the bound ϖR°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊆ R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ holds because ϖR° ⊆ R°° ⊆ R⁺.
- Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: absolute Frobenius induces R_∞/p^{(1−ε)/p} ≅ R_∞/p^{1−ε}, so R_∞ is a perfectoid Z_p^cycl,a-algebra.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-almost-setup`, `PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings`, `mathlib:frobenius`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion`, `mathlib:Ring.DirectLimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, pp. 42-43.

  > Moreover, using that the transition maps Rm/p1−ǫ → Rm+1/p1−ǫ agree with the relative Frobenius map, we ﬁnd that (absolute) Frobenius induces an isomorphism

  The colimit Frobenius isomorphism R_∞/ϖ ≅ R_∞/ϖ^p deduced from the lifting condition.

- Bhargav Bhatt, Matthew Morrow, Peter Scholze, *Integral p-adic Hodge theory*, §3.2, Lemma 3.10 (ii), p. 22.

  > (ii) Conversely, if ϕ : S/πS → S/π p S is an isomorphism and π is a non-zero-divisor, then Ker θ is a principal ideal (and hence S is perfectoid).

  Step (ii).

- Bhargav Bhatt, Matthew Morrow, Peter Scholze, *Integral p-adic Hodge theory*, §3.2, Lemma 3.21, p. 27.

  > Let R0 be a perfectoid ring which is π-adically complete for some non-zero-divisor π such that π p divides p. Then R = R0 [ π1 ], endowed with the π-adic topology on R0 , is a complete Tate ring which is perfectoid in Fontaine’s sense.

  The uniformity bound.

#### `perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers` — The perfectoid Frobenius criterion: Frobenius-controlled towers have perfectoid tilde-limits

*theorem* · planet: **Perfectoid Frobenius criterion for towers** · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Criterion` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower) with generic fibres (A_m, A_m⁺⁺) and completion (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion). Then: (i) A_∞ is a perfectoid Tate ring in the sense of ECD Definition 3.1 (complete, uniform, with the pseudouniformiser ϖ satisfying ϖ^p | p in A_∞° and Φ: A_∞°/ϖ ≅ A_∞°/ϖ^p), of characteristic 0 or p according to A_0⁺, and (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) is a perfectoid Tate pair; (ii) the restriction map identifies |Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺)| with lim_m |Spa(A_m, A_m⁺⁺)|, and, when the A_m are sheafy (for instance strongly noetherian, as for affinoids of rigid spaces), X_∞ := Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) ~ lim_m X_m in the sense of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, X_∞ is unique up to unique isomorphism, and it represents lim_m Hom(−, X_m) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) global form: let (𝔛_m) be a tower of flat ϖ-adic formal schemes (over a ϖ-adically complete base) with generic fibres X_m analytic adic spaces, and suppose 𝔛_{m_0} has an affine open cover by Spf A_{m_0}⁺ whose preimages Spf A_m⁺ (m ≥ m_0) form Frobenius-controlled towers compatibly with restriction; then the generic fibres have a perfectoid tilde-limit X_∞ ~ lim X_m, glued from the Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing), which is the generic fibre of the formal scheme lim 𝔛_m (limit in formal schemes, affine-locally Spf A_∞⁺). This theorem concerns towers whose finite levels are not perfectoid; the case of perfectoid finite levels is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/limit-of-perfectoid-tower.

**Hypotheses.**

- Frobenius-controlled integral tower (the eventual Frobenius lifting modulo ϖ^p is the only input beyond flatness and completeness).
- For (ii)-(iii), the generic fibres are adic spaces (sheafy coordinate rings) so that the tilde-limit is defined.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound gives that A_∞⁺ is integral perfectoid, A_∞ uniform with A_∞° almost equal to A_∞⁺, and A_∞ perfectoid in Fontaine's sense (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.21), which is ECD Definition 3.1 (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras). A_∞⁺⁺ is open (contains A_∞⁺), integrally closed and contained in A_∞°.
2. (ii): the tower of pairs satisfies the hypotheses of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{m,0} = A_m⁺ and I_m = ϖA_m⁺, whose completed direct limit is (A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺) (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (iii)); perfectoid Tate pairs are sheafy (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy), so X_∞ is a perfectoid space and the final clause of that lemma gives X_∞ ~ lim X_m; uniqueness and representability are PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness.
3. (iii): on each affine piece apply (ii); the pieces are compatible with restriction (rational localisation commutes with the construction on both sides, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction) and glue by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii)-(iii). The formal-scheme limit is affine-locally Spf of the ϖ-adic completion of colim A_m⁺, whose generic fibre is Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: for 0 ≤ ε < 1/2 there are unique perfectoid spaces X_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_m X_{Γ_0(p^m)}(ε)_a (and similarly X*, A) over Q_p^cycl, the transition maps of the integral models X(p^{-m}ε) agreeing with relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−ε}.
- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(1): X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)}(ε)_a ~ lim_n X_{Γ_0*(p^n)}(ε)_a for Hilbert modular varieties, via Lemma 5.12 (relative Frobenius modulo p^{1−δ}).
- Compatible-root disc and torus: the towers R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ and R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩ over a perfectoid Tate pair give Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩) and Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩) (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Example 4.4 for the torus over a perfectoid field).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 42.

  > On the tower ... of the X(p−mǫ), the transition maps agree with the relative Frobenius map modulo p1−ǫ.

  The tilde-limit and its uniqueness from the completed limit.

#### `frobenius-tower-tilt` — The tilt of the limit of a Frobenius-controlled tower

*lemma* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Tilt` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let (A_•⁺, ϖ, m_0, w) be a Frobenius-controlled integral tower and (S_•⁺, t, m_0, w′) a Frobenius-controlled integral tower of characteristic p (p = 0 in S_0⁺), together with ring isomorphisms α_m: A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ S_m⁺/t^p for m ≥ m_0 compatible with the transition maps (and with the w, w′). Then the perfectoid Tate ring S_∞ = S_∞⁺[1/t] of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers is perfect, and S_∞ is the tilt of A_∞: there is a unique isomorphism A_∞♭ ≅ S_∞ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring) carrying ϖ♭ to a unit multiple of t and inducing the colimit of the α_m modulo ϖ and t, namely A_∞⁺/ϖ = colim A_m⁺/ϖ ≅ colim S_m⁺/t = S_∞⁺/t; under it, Spa(S_∞, S_∞⁺⁺) is the tilt of Spa(A_∞, A_∞⁺⁺), and in the global form of the criterion the tilt of X_∞ is the limit of the characteristic-p tower.

**Hypotheses.**

- The comparison α is given only modulo ϖ^p and t^p (it need not lift).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. A_∞⁺/ϖ^p = colim A_m⁺/ϖ^p ≅ colim S_m⁺/t^p = S_∞⁺/t^p (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion (i)).
2. S_∞⁺ is perfect: Φ: S_∞⁺/t → S_∞⁺/t^p is bijective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound) and S_∞⁺ is t-adically complete and t-torsion-free, so Frobenius is bijective on S_∞⁺ (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect).
3. Tilt: A_∞♭⁺ ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} A_∞⁺/ϖ up to almost zero (ECD Lemma 3.10, PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings); via α this is lim_Φ S_∞⁺/t = S_∞⁺ (perfect and t-complete), compatibly with the rings of integral elements; invert ϖ♭ ↔ t (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Corollary III.2.19: the tilt of X*_{Γ_0(p^∞)}(ε)_a is the open subset of the perfection X′*perf where |Ha| ≥ |t|^ε, using X′*(p^{-m}ε)/t^{1−ε} = X*(p^{-m}ε)/p^{1−ε} (Theorem III.2.15(i)).
- For the compatible-root disc over R, the characteristic-p tower R♭⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ with α_m induced by R⁺/ϖ^p ≅ R♭⁺/(ϖ♭)^p gives the tilt R♭⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ of R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-integral-subrings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, proof of Corollary III.2.19, p. 43.

  > From [53, Theorem 5.2], it follows that R∞[p−1] and S∞[t−1] are tilts, as desired.

  The tilt identification from the congruence of the two towers.

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, before Definition III.2.18, p. 42.

  > In characteristic p, one can pass to perfections.

  The characteristic-p side is a perfection.

#### `perfection-tilde-limit` — The perfection of a characteristic-p adic space as a tilde-limit along relative Frobenius

*lemma* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FrobeniusTower/Perfection` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let k be a perfect complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic p with pseudouniformiser t (more generally a perfect complete Tate ring of characteristic p with t ∈ k° admitting all p-power roots), (S, S⁺) a complete Tate pair over (k, k°) with S⁺ flat over k° and t-adically complete, and Φ: S → S^{(p)} ≅ S the relative Frobenius over k (an isomorphism of the base, k being perfect). (i) The tower S⁺ →Φ S⁺ →Φ ⋯ (level m carrying the k°-structure twisted by Φ_k^{-m}) is a Frobenius-controlled integral tower with ϖ = t and w_m the canonical base-change isomorphisms (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower, constructor from relative Frobenius); (ii) its completion is S^{perf⁺} := the t-adic completion of colim_Φ S⁺ with S^{perf} = S^{perf⁺}[1/t], a perfect, hence perfectoid, Tate ring; (iii) if S is sheafy, Y^{perf} := Spa(S^{perf}, S^{perf⁺⁺}) ~ lim_Φ Y for Y = Spa(S, S⁺), the maps |Y^{perf}| → |Y| are homeomorphisms, and Y^{perf} is the unique perfectoid space over k with this property; (iv) for an analytic adic space Y over k covered by such affinoids, the Y^{perf} glue to a perfectoid space Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing). The corresponding statement for flat t-adic formal schemes 𝔜: lim_Φ 𝔜 is representable by the perfect flat formal scheme 𝔜^{perf}, locally Spf(R^{perf}), compatibly with generic fibres.

**Hypotheses.**

- Base perfect of characteristic p so that relative Frobenius is k-linear and the Frobenius twist is isomorphic to the original algebra; S⁺ flat over k°.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): relative Frobenius over a perfect base satisfies the source form of the definition: the twist S⁺/t ⊗_{k°/t, Φ} k°/t^p is S⁺/t^p after identifying k°/t ≅ k°/t^p by Frobenius.
2. (ii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion; perfectness of the completion and PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect (ECD Proposition 3.5: in characteristic p, perfectoid = perfect complete Tate).
3. (iii) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers (ii); Frobenius induces homeomorphisms on adic spectra (a valuation is determined by its values on p-th powers), so all transition maps and the projections are homeomorphisms.
4. (iv) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing, since the construction commutes with rational localisation.

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze's torsion paper, Definition III.2.18: X′*perf over F_p((t^{1/(p−1)p^∞})) is the tilde-limit of the Siegel space X′* along relative Frobenius.
- For Y = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩), Y^{perf} = Spa(k⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, k°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩), and the étale topoi of Y^{perf} and Y agree (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-completion`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties*, §III.2.3, Definition III.2.18 (ii), p. 42.

#### `limit-of-perfectoid-tower` — Towers of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps have perfectoid tilde-limits

*theorem* · planet: **Limits of perfectoid towers** · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/PerfectoidTower` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of perfectoid spaces whose transition maps are affinoid (for every a: j → i and every affinoid open V ⊆ X_i, f_a^{-1}(V) is affinoid; hence qcqs). Then: (i) the limit X := lim_i X_i exists in the category of perfectoid spaces; (ii) X ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), and X represents lim_i Hom(−, X_i) on perfectoid spaces; (iii) for i_0 ∈ I and an affinoid perfectoid open V = Spa(R_{i_0}, R_{i_0}⁺) ⊆ X_{i_0} with preimages V_a = Spa(R_a, R_a⁺), the preimage of V in X is Spa(R, R⁺) with R⁺ the ϖ-adic completion of colim_a R_a⁺ and R = R⁺[1/ϖ] (ϖ a compatible pseudouniformiser), and R is perfectoid; (iv) |X| ≅ lim_i |X_i|; (v) if I is ω_1-cofiltered, colim R_a → R and colim R_a⁺ → R⁺ are bijective. This is the easy limit theorem, in which every finite level is already perfectoid; it is distinct from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers, whose finite levels are not perfectoid.

**Hypotheses.**

- Every X_i perfectoid; affinoid transition maps (as for finite étale or pro-étale towers of affinoids).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Affinoid case: PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4(o), 6.5) gives the limit Spa(R, R⁺), the formula and the homeomorphism; the perfectoidness of (R, R⁺) is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid (each R_a⁺ integral perfectoid by Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Lemma 3.20; bijective Frobenius modulo ϖ and ϖ-torsion-freeness pass to the colimit and its completion; Lemmas 3.10(ii) and 3.21), the same argument as PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound with w_m replaced by the inverse Frobenius at each level.
2. Tilde-limit on affinoids: PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit with A_{a,0} = R_a⁺.
3. Global case: cover X_{i_0} by affinoid perfectoids V; affinoid transition maps make every V_a affinoid perfectoid; glue the affinoid limits by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing (ii) (uniqueness on overlaps from PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness), which also gives (ii) and (iv).
4. (v) as in ECD Proposition 6.5 (a Cauchy sequence lives at a finite stage).

**Acceptance.**

- Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams, proof of Theorem 5.11(2): the finite étale tower X_{Γ_0*(p^∞)∩Γ_1*(p^n)}(ε)_a of perfectoid spaces has the perfectoid tilde-limit X_{Γ_1*(p^∞)}(ε)_a.
- A pro-étale G-tower of perfectoid spaces X_j → X with X_∞ = lim X_j (PerfectoidSpaces:P9/profinite-galois-tower in the perfectoid case).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/frobenius-tower-uniformity-bound`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`

**Sources.**

- Christopher Birkbeck, Ben Heuer, Chris Williams, *Overconvergent Hilbert modular forms via perfectoid modular varieties*, §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.11, p. 1749.

  > Since perfectoid tilde-limits of inverse systems of perfectoid spaces with affinoid transition maps exist, we obtain a perfectoid tilde-limit

  The statement in the source's words.

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §6, Proposition 6.5, p. 29.

  > Then the inverse X = limi Xi in the category of perfectoid spaces exists, is affinoid perfectoid

  The affinoid case.

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §6, proof of Proposition 6.5, p. 29.

  > The first part follows from uniformity of perfectoid spaces, which means that whenever Y maps compatibly to all Xi , the map limi Ri+ → O+ (Y ) extends uniquely to the ϖ-adic completion

  The universal property on affinoids.

#### `regular-finite-flat-residue-tower` — Finite flat regular towers with algebraically closed residue field (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.1)

*theorem* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/RegularTower` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring with residue field k. There is a filtered direct system of finite flat R-algebras R_i such that each (R_i, mR_i) is a regular local ring and (lim→ R_i, m·lim→ R_i) is a regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field. If k is separably closed of characteristic p > 0, the R_i may be chosen of p-power rank over R. The colimit is Noetherian; it is not claimed to be complete.

**Hypotheses.**

- R complete regular local, of any characteristic. The proof uses the three Cohen presentations: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (equal characteristic); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ with W a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p (p ∈ m∖m²); R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (p ∈ m²).
- The Cohen structure theorem and regular local rings are not in the pinned libraries (gap).
- The p-power clause needs k separably closed: then k̄/k is purely inseparable, and its finite subextensions have p-power degree.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Equal characteristic: R ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ (Matsumura 29.7). Let k_i range over the finite subextensions of k̄/k and put R_i := k_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, free of rank [k_i : k] over R. The m-adic completion of lim→ R_i is k̄⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧, so lim→ R_i is Noetherian (Stacks 033E, 05UU, 00MK), hence a regular local ring.
2. Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m∖m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧. There is an integral extension W′/W of discrete valuation rings with uniformizer p and residue field k̄ (Matsumura, proof of 29.1). With W_i ranging over the finite discrete valuation ring subextensions of W′/W, put R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧; as before, the colimit has completion Ŵ′⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and is regular local.
3. Mixed characteristic with p ∈ m²: R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² (Matsumura 29.3 and the proof of 29.8(ii)). Each R_i := W_i⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) is a finite flat R-algebra and a regular local ring. By the previous case lim→ W_i⟦x⟧ is regular local with regular system of parameters (p, x_1, …, x_n), so lim→ R_i is regular local with regular system of parameters (x_1, …, x_n).
4. p-power ranks: in all three cases rank_R R_i = [k_i : k] (= [W_i : W]); if k is separably closed of characteristic p, this is a power of p.

**Acceptance.**

- Non-example: the colimit is not complete. For R = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧ the colimit is lim→ 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧, whose completion 𝔽̄_p⟦x⟧ is strictly larger.
- The p-power clause needs k separably closed: for k = 𝔽_p the stages 𝔽_{p^n}⟦x⟧ have rank n.
- Ramified case: R = ℤ_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = ℤ_p[√p] has p ∈ m², R_i = W(𝔽_{p^i})[√p] with i ranging over the positive integers ordered by divisibility, and the colimit is regular with parameter x = √p.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`, `mathlib:Module.Flat`

**Sources.**

- Kęstutis Česnavičius, *Purity for the Brauer group*, §5, Lemma 5.1, p. 11.

  > Lemma 5.1. For a complete, regular, local ring (R, m), there is a filtered direct system of finite, flat R-algebras R_i such that each (R_i, mR_i) is a regular local ring and (lim R_i, m(lim R_i)) is a regular local ring with an algebraically closed residue field; if the residue field k of R is separably closed of characteristic p > 0, then the R_i may be chosen to be of p-power rank over R.

  The statement, read on the arXiv v4 PDF.

- Kęstutis Česnavičius, *Purity for the Brauer group*, §5, proof of Lemma 5.1, pp. 11–12.

  > In the remaining case when R is of mixed characteristic and p ∈ m², by [Mat89, 29.3 and the proof of 29.8 (ii)], there is a W as above such that R ≅ W⟦x_1, . . . , x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, . . . , x_n)².

  The ramified case of the construction.


#### `regular-finite-flat-perfectoid-tower` — Finite flat regular towers with perfectoid completion (Česnavičius 2019, Lemma 5.2)

*theorem* · `TauCeti/RingTheory/Perfectoid/RegularTower` (`TauCeti.Perfectoid`)

**Statement.** Let (R, m) be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field k, and W := W(k). There is a tower {R_m}_{m≥0} of finite flat R-algebras R_m of p-power rank over R, each a regular local ring, such that the p-adic completion R̂_∞ of R_∞ := lim→_m R_m is perfectoid (integral perfectoid in the sense of BMS1 Definition 3.5, so R̂_∞[1/p] is a perfectoid Tate ring). Explicitly: if p ∈ m∖m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ and R_m := W[p^{1/p^m}]⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧; if p ∈ m², then R ≅ W⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧/(p − f) with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_n)² and R_m := W⟦x_1^{1/p^m}, …, x_n^{1/p^m}⟧/(p − f). The finite stages are not perfectoid, and R_∞ is not complete.

**Hypotheses.**

- k perfect, so W ≅ W(k) in the Cohen presentations of P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower; mixed characteristic (0, p).
- The criterion used is Česnavičius's Lemma 4.7: for a p-torsion-free ring S with (ϖ^p) = (p) for some ϖ ∈ S, if S is integrally closed in S[1/p] then x ↦ x^p : S/ϖ → S/p is injective, and if moreover every element of S/p is a p-th power then the p-adic completion of S is perfectoid. PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19 route 7 plans that lemma at PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra, which is not upstream of P7, so step 1 proves the instance needed here.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Criterion. If x ∈ S and x^p = ϖ^p s with s ∈ S, then x/ϖ ∈ S[1/ϖ] = S[1/p] satisfies (x/ϖ)^p = s, so x/ϖ ∈ S by integral closedness, that is x ∈ ϖS. Since Ŝ/ϖ ≅ S/ϖ and Ŝ/p ≅ S/p, Frobenius Ŝ/ϖ → Ŝ/p is bijective, and Ŝ is integral perfectoid; P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid gives the Tate ring.
2. Each R_m is regular local and finite free of p-power rank over R: in the first case it is a power series ring over the discrete valuation ring W[p^{1/p^m}] (rank p^{m(n+1)}), and in the second it is the quotient of the regular ring W⟦x^{1/p^m}⟧ by p − f, which is not in the square of its maximal ideal (rank p^{mn}). Being regular, each R_m is a normal domain, so R_∞ is a normal domain, integrally closed in R_∞[1/p], and p-torsion free.
3. p ∈ m∖m²: take ϖ := p^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, since k is perfect and p and the x_i have compatible p-power roots in R_∞. Apply step 1.
4. p ∈ m²: by step 1 it suffices to find u ∈ R_∞^× with up a p-th power in R_∞, and then ϖ := (up)^{1/p}. Every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power and p ∈ m_∞², so p = Σ_i (s_i^p + p t_i)(s′_i^p + p t′_i) with s_i, s′_i ∈ m_∞ and t_i, t′_i ∈ R_∞. Hence p = s^p + pt with s, t ∈ m_∞, and u := 1 − t is a unit of the local ring R_∞ (Česnavičius follows Shimomoto's argument, [Shi16, 4.9]).

**Acceptance.**

- R = ℤ_p (n = 0): R_m = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}], and R̂_∞ is the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}], a perfectoid ring.
- Non-example: no finite stage is perfectoid, since Frobenius is not surjective on R_m/p; for R = ℤ_p, p^{1/p^m} is not a p-th power modulo p in ℤ_p[p^{1/p^m}].
- The residue field must be perfect: k is a quotient of R_∞/p, so if every element of R_∞/p is a p-th power, every element of k is one.
- The completion is p-adic. R_∞ is not complete, and its m_∞-adic topology is not the one used.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/regular-finite-flat-residue-tower`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-ring-from-integral-perfectoid`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison`, `mathlib:WittVector`, `mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosedIn`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`

**Sources.**

- Kęstutis Česnavičius, *Purity for the Brauer group*, §5, Lemma 5.2, p. 12.

  > Lemma 5.2. For a mixed characteristic (0, p), complete, regular, local ring (R, m) with a perfect residue field k, there is a tower {R_m}_{m∈Z≥0} of finite, flat R-algebras R_m of p-power rank over R such that each R_m is a regular, local ring and the p-adic completion R̂_∞ of R_∞ := lim R_m is perfectoid.

  The statement, read on the arXiv v4 PDF.

- Kęstutis Česnavičius, *Purity for the Brauer group*, §5, proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 12.

  > Due to Lemma 4.7, to show that the p-adic completion of the local ring (R_∞, m_∞) is perfectoid, we only need to argue that for some u ∈ R_∞^× the element up is a p-th power in R_∞.

  The reduction of the ramified case to a unit multiple of p.

- Kęstutis Česnavičius, *Purity for the Brauer group*, §4, Lemma 4.7, p. 8.

  > For a prime p and a p-torsion free ring R such that (ϖ^p) = (p) for some ϖ ∈ R, if R is integrally closed in R[1/p], then the map R/ϖ → R/p, x ↦ x^p, is injective; if, in addition, every element of R/p is a p-th power, then the p-adic completion R̂ of R is perfectoid.

  The criterion of step 1.

### The étale-topos comparison of Scholze 2012 §7

#### `tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit` — A perfectoid tilde-limit over qcqs locally noetherian spaces is a residue-field tilde-limit

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/ResidueField` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~ lim X_i be a perfectoid tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit) with every X_i quasicompact, quasiseparated and locally noetherian. Then X ~′ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit): for every x ∈ X with images x_i, colim_i k(x_i)^ → k(x)^ has dense image.

**Hypotheses.**

- X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic, so that ~′ is defined.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Condition (a) is common to both notions.
2. Fix x ∈ X and a good affinoid perfectoid W ∋ x (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis). The rational neighbourhoods of x in W are good (same node) and cofinal among neighbourhoods of x; the residue field k(x) is the colimit of the O_X(U) over them modulo the support of x, and O_X(U) → k(x)^ is continuous.
3. For each good U with level V_a, the image of colim_a O(V_a) is dense in O_X(U), hence its image in k(x)^ is dense in the image of O_X(U); the image of O(V_a) → k(x)^ factors through k(x_j) (x_j ∈ V_a). Taking the union over U, colim_j k(x_j) has dense image in k(x), hence colim_j k(x_j)^ in k(x)^.

**Acceptance.**

- For the compatible-root disc tower over a perfectoid field, the Gauss point x has k(x_n)^ = completion of K(T^{1/p^n}) for the Gauss norm, whose union is dense in k(x)^.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Moduli of p-divisible groups*, §2.4, after Theorem 2.4.7, p. 21.

  > We remark that the notion ∼ introduced here is stronger than the notion ∼′ introduced in [Sch12], which only talks about the residue fields instead of the sections of the structure sheaf in an open neighborhood.

  The implication ~ ⇒ ~′.

#### `residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change` — Étale base change of residue-field tilde-limits, and bijectivity suffices (Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16)

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/ResidueField` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit), i_0 ∈ I and g: Y → X_{i_0} an étale morphism of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces. Put Y_a := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X_j (a: j → i_0) and Y_X := Y ×_{X_{i_0}} X, a perfectoid space étale over X. Then (i) Y_X ~′ lim_a Y_a; (ii) (the remark in the proof) in Definition 7.14, if |X| → lim |X_i| is bijective and the residue-field condition (c) holds, then |X| → lim |X_i| is already a homeomorphism, i.e. X ~′ lim X_i.

**Hypotheses.**

- X_i and Y qcqs locally noetherian analytic; g étale (Huber's étale = A1's local description, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Existence of Y_X, perfectoid and étale over X: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.3(iii), Proposition 7.10).
2. Bijectivity of |Y_X| → lim_a |Y_a|, fibrewise over x ∈ X with images x_j: points over x are the extensions of the valuation of x to the finite étale k(x)^-algebra obtained from the fibre (étale maps are locally quasi-finite with finite étale fibres over completed residue fields); by (c) and henselian approximation (Berkeley Theorem 7.4.8, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^), and the valuation ring k(x)⁺ and its extensions are determined on the dense subfield colim k(x_j); so the fibres correspond.
3. Residue-field density for points of Y_X: residue fields of Y_X are finite separable over those of X and are the base changes of those of the Y_a, so density is preserved.
4. Homeomorphism (ii): Scholze refers to Huber's Remark 2.4.3 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). A route through public inputs: over an affinoid perfectoid W ⊆ X the map W → lim |X_i| is spectral (W qc, X_i qs); spectral bijections are homeomorphisms for the constructible topologies (Stacks Lemma 5.23.3 and 5.24.5), and generalising maps of spectral spaces that are surjective are quotient maps (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient); generalisations of an analytic point are its vertical generalisations, i.e. valuation rings between k(x)⁺ and k(x)°, which by (c) correspond to those of colim k(x_j).

**Acceptance.**

- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for U → X étale, U ×_X X_∞ ~′ lim U ×_X X_i for the universal cover tower.
- For an open immersion Y ⊆ X_{i_0}, Y_X is the open subspace φ_{i_0}^{-1}(Y) (compare PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-rational-restriction).

#### `tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent` — Qcqs étale spaces over a residue-field tilde-limit descend to a finite level

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/EtaleDescent` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let X ~′ lim X_i be a residue-field tilde-limit with all X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) base change induces an equivalence of categories 2-colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} → X_{ét,qcqs} between qcqs étale adic spaces over the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space), and likewise 2-colim_i (X_i)_{fét} → X_{fét}; (ii) a finite family of morphisms (Z^k_i → Y_i)_k in (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} is jointly surjective after base change to X if and only if it is so after base change to some X_j. This is the perfectoid-limit analogue of ECD Proposition 6.4(i)-(ii) (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects), with the X_i locally noetherian instead of affinoid perfectoid.

**Hypotheses.**

- X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid; ~′ (hence also ~).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. Finite étale over neighbourhoods of a point: for x ∈ X, 2-colim_{U ∋ x} FÉt(U) ≃ FÉt(k(x)^) (Berkeley Lemma 7.4.6, via k(x)^⁺ = the ϖ-adic completion of colim_{U ∋ x} O⁺(U) and Theorem 7.4.8; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit), and the same at x_j ∈ X_j; by (c), FÉt(k(x)^) ≃ 2-colim_j FÉt(k(x_j)^) (the colimit of the k(x_j)^ is dense in k(x)^ and topologically henselian; finite étale algebras are finitely presented). Hence a finite étale cover of a neighbourhood of x is, near x, pulled back from a neighbourhood of some x_j, uniquely up to shrinking.
2. Faithfulness and fullness: as in ECD Proposition 6.4(ii) — graphs of maps between étale spaces are quasicompact open immersions (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal); two quasicompact opens of Z_i = Y_i ×_{X_i} Y′_i with the same preimage in Z_X agree in some Z_j, because |Z_X| → lim |Z_j| is surjective (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change) and quasicompact opens of a limit of spectral spaces descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6; PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces); morphisms whose base change is an isomorphism become isomorphisms at a finite stage (surjectivity of f and of Δ_f descend).
3. Essential surjectivity: a qcqs étale Y → X is covered by finitely many pieces that are rational subsets of finite étale covers of rational subsets of X (local structure, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces); quasicompact opens descend (Stacks Lemma 5.24.6 through |X| ≅ lim |X_i|), finite étale covers descend by the first step and quasi-compactness, and the pieces glue at a finite stage by full faithfulness (X qcqs).
4. (ii): images of étale maps are open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map); joint surjectivity is an equality of quasicompact opens, which descends by Stacks Lemma 5.24.6(3) and the surjectivity of |Y_X| → lim |Y_j|.

**Acceptance.**

- For the compatible-root disc tower over a perfectoid field K, every finite étale cover of the perfectoid disc is pulled back from some K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ (the disc's finite étale site is the 2-colimit).
- For the universal pro-finite-étale tower of a connected affinoid X over Q_p, the limit X_∞ has no nonsplit finite étale covers (Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, proof of Theorem 4.9, citing Lemma 7.5(i) of Scholze 2012).

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-residue-fields`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, proof of Theorem 7.17, p. 44.

  > The latter kind of morphisms can be descended to a finite level because of Lemma 7.5.

  Finite étale maps descend by henselian approximation (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 28.

  > By approximation of quasicompact open subsets, we can find a quasicompact open immersion Vj ⊂ Yj ×Xj Yj′ whose pullback agrees with the image of Γf .

  The graph argument for fullness.

- Peter Scholze, *Étale cohomology of diamonds*, §6, proof of Proposition 6.4, p. 28.

  > Finally, for essential surjectivity, take any qcqs étale f : Y → X. It is enough to cover Y be quasicompact open subsets which descend to Xi for large i

  The essential-surjectivity argument.

- Peter Scholze, Jared Weinstein, *Berkeley Lectures on p-adic Geometry*, Lecture 7, after Theorem 7.4.8, p. 54.

  > As a corollary, let Ai be a filtered directed system of complete Tate rings

  Finite étale algebras over completed colimits of complete Tate rings.

#### `tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison` — Tilde-limits X ~ lim X_i of noetherian adic spaces and the comparison of etale topoi

*comparison* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/EtaleTopos` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of quasicompact quasiseparated locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space; no perfectoid base field is assumed, and the X_i may lie over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) while X lies over a perfectoid field), X a perfectoid space and X ~′ lim X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit; this holds whenever X ~ lim X_i, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit). Then: (i) |X| is a spectral space and X is qcqs (Scholze 2012 Remark 7.15); (ii) (Theorem 7.17) the étale topos X_ét^~ of the perfectoid space X (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space) is the projective limit of the fibred topos (X_{i,ét}^~)_i of the étale topoi of the X_i (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site, equal to Huber's): X_ét^~ is equivalent to the topos of sheaves on the colimit site colim_i (X_i)_{ét,qcqs} (objects qcqs étale over some X_i, morphisms the filtered colimits of Hom sets, coverings the families that are coverings at some finite level), compatibly with the pullback morphisms X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~; (iii) (Corollary 7.18) for i_0 ∈ I and a sheaf of abelian groups F_{i_0} on X_{i_0,ét}, with pullbacks F_j to X_{j,ét} (j → i_0) and F to X_ét, the natural map colim_j H^n(X_{j,ét}, F_j) → H^n(X_ét, F) is bijective for all n ≥ 0 (for sheaves of sets, n = 0; for sheaves of groups, n ≤ 1). When X is itself locally noetherian (and not assumed perfectoid), the corresponding statements are Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6, supplied by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity; this node is their perfectoid extension. Corollary 7.19 is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers.

**Hypotheses.**

- All X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic; X perfectoid (its étale site is that of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.11 / ECD Definition 6.2); no base field (Scholze 2012 states the result over a perfectoid field K; Scholze's rigid paper applies it to X_i over Q_p).
- Proofs follow Huber [Hub96] Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.6 with Scholze's modification; the step through Huber's unpublished text is recorded as a gap, and the steps below use public inputs.

**Proof, in steps.**

1. (i): Remark 7.15 via DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces.
2. (ii): PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent identifies X_{ét,qcqs} with the colimit site, including coverings; since X is qcqs, the qcqs étale perfectoid spaces over X form a generating subcategory of X_ét stable under fibre products, so X_ét^~ is the topos of the colimit site; a filtered colimit of coherent sites with finite-limit- and covering-preserving pullbacks has as topos the projective limit of the fibred topos (SGA 4 VI.8.2.3; request to DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).
3. Scholze's modification of Huber's proof: instead of Huber's Corollary 1.7.3, étale maps factor locally as an open immersion followed by a finite étale map (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison on the X_i; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces on X), and finite étale maps descend to a finite level by henselian approximation (Scholze 2012 Lemma 7.5; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).
4. (iii): cohomology on a projective limit of coherent topoi of sheaves pulled back from a stage is the colimit of the cohomologies (SGA 4 VI.8.7.7, as in Huber's Corollary 2.4.6); on the colimit site this is DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites applied to the filtered colimit of the pulled-back sheaves, the cohomology of each stage being computed on its qcqs étale site.

**Acceptance.**

- Spa K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim_n Spa K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ and Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ~ lim Spa K⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩ (compatible-root disc and torus).
- Theorem 1.12/8.5's (P^n)^{ad} ~ lim_φ (P^n)^{ad} (Frobenius tower) is the source's application; in this case Cor. 7.19 does not apply but Thm 7.17 does.
- Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Theorem 4.9: for the universal cover X_∞ ~ lim X_i of a connected affinoid noetherian X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) (X_i finite étale over X, over Q_p; X_∞ over C_p), H^j(X_{∞,ét}, L) = colim_i H^j(X_{i,ét}, L) for all j ≥ 0 (the use made by PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion). The tower satisfies X_∞ ~ lim X_i also in the sectionwise sense, by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-qcqs-etale-finite-stage-descent`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit-etale-base-change`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-morphism-of-perfectoid-spaces`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphisms-local-description-and-comparison`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.limit`, `mathlib:TopCat.Presheaf`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces`

**Sources.**

#### `etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers` — Towers with homeomorphic, purely inseparable transition maps do not change the étale topos (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.19)

*lemma* · `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfectoid/TildeLimit/EtaleTopos` (`TauCeti.PerfectoidSpace`)

**Statement.** In the situation of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (X ~′ lim X_i, X_i qcqs locally noetherian analytic, X perfectoid), assume that every transition map X_j → X_i induces a homeomorphism |X_j| → |X_i| and purely inseparable extensions of completed residue fields. Then for every i the pullback X_ét^~ → X_{i,ét}^~ is an equivalence of topoi; in particular H^n(X_ét, F) = H^n(X_{i,ét}, F_i) for every abelian sheaf F_i on X_{i,ét} with pullback F.

**Hypotheses.**

- Transition maps homeomorphisms on underlying spaces with purely inseparable residue-field extensions (a universal-homeomorphism condition, typically relative Frobenius in characteristic p).

**Proof, in steps.**

1. For such a transition map, pullback X_{i,ét}^~ → X_{j,ét}^~ is an equivalence: Scholze refers to the remark after Huber's Proposition 2.3.7 (Huber 1996, not public; gap). This is the adic analogue of the topological invariance of the étale site (SGA 4 VIII.1.1).
2. The projective limit of a system of equivalences of topoi is equivalent to each member (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (ii)).

**Acceptance.**

- Perfection: for Y an analytic adic space of characteristic p locally noetherian over a perfect field, Y^{perf} ~ lim_Φ Y along relative Frobenius (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit), and Y^{perf}_ét ≃ Y_ét.
- Non-example: the Frobenius tower T ↦ T^p of P^n in characteristic 0 (Scholze 2012 Theorem 8.5) has non-inseparable residue extensions; there only the limit statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison applies.

**Prerequisites.** `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit`

**Sources.**

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, Corollary 7.19, p. 44.

  > Assume that in the situation of Definition 7.14 all transition maps Xj → Xi induce purely inseparable extensions on completed residue fields

  The hypothesis.

- Peter Scholze, *Perfectoid spaces*, §7, proof of Corollary 7.19, p. 44.

  > Use the remark after Proposition 2.3.7 of [20].

  The proof, by reference to Huber.

### Stage acceptance tests

- **Compatible-root discs and tori.** For a perfectoid Tate pair (R, R⁺) whose pseudouniformiser ϖ has compatible p-power
  roots, the towers R⁺⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩ and R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩ are Frobenius-controlled (test `frobeniusTower_test_disc`), their
  completions are R⁺⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ and R⁺⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩, and Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{1/p^m}⟩),
  Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(R⟨T^{±1/p^m}⟩) (`perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`); every rational subset of the
  perfectoid disc is pulled back from a finite level (`rational-subsets-from-finite-level`); over a perfectoid field the
  étale cohomology of the perfectoid disc is the colimit of that of the finite levels (`tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison`).
- **A finite étale tower.** (a) Over a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and p ≠ 2, pulling back the Kummer cover S² = T
  of the torus to the perfectoid torus gives Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^∞}⟩) ~ lim Spa(K⟨S^{±1/p^n}⟩) (`tilde-limit-finite-etale-base-change`);
  (b) the Γ_1-level tower over the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞)-level of Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Theorem 5.11(2), a tower of
  perfectoid spaces with finite étale transition maps (`limit-of-perfectoid-tower`); (c) the universal pro-finite-étale
  tower of an affinoid over Q_p (ECD Lemma 15.3, Scholze's rigid paper Theorem 4.9), whose limit is the uniform completion
  of the colimit (`good-affinoid-uniform-completion`, `represented-functor-comparison`) and whose étale cohomology is the
  colimit of the finite levels (`tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison`).
- **A non-cofinal descending level family.** Γ_0(p^n) ⊂ GL_2(Z_p) decreases with intersection the upper-triangular Borel;
  it has no cofinality witness (`cofinalityWitness_test_gamma0_not`, `compact-open-subgroup-cofinality`), so its tilde-limit
  (the anticanonical Γ_0(p^∞)-level, `perfectoid-frobenius-criterion-for-towers`) says nothing about the full infinite
  level; by contrast the principal congruence subgroups K(p^n) are witnessed and compute it (`tilde-limit-cofinal-change`).
- **Non-examples of the definition.** Spa(C_p) over the constant system Spa(Q_p) (topology but no density), a disjoint
  double of the disc tower (density but no homeomorphism), and Spa(K) ~ Spa(K[ε]/ε²) (a tilde-limit that is not an
  isomorphism).

- **tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets** — For a Huber pair (A, A⁺) with completion (Â, Â⁺): Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets (Huber, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48); and for a complete Tate pair, an element is a unit if it vanishes at no point of Spa(A, A⁺) and is topologically nilpotent if |f(x)| < 1 at every point (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(2) and Corollary 7.33 type statements; the pinned `isUnit_of_forall_not_vle_zero` assumes open maximal ideals and is vacuous for Tate rings). (needed by `tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`, `strong-completion`).
- **tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf** — The structure presheaf on rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) for a complete Tate pair: O(U(T/s)) is the completion of A[1/s] with ring of definition generated by A_0[T/s], with the universal property of rational localisation, compatibly with the pinned `completionLocalization`; used to transfer density of finite-level sections to rational subsets. (needed by `good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis`, `tilde-limit-rational-restriction`, `tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit`).
- **tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-1-valuation-spectra-and-continuous-valuations** — Continuous valuations and their restriction along continuous ring maps, with rank-one (maximal) points computing spectral seminorms of Tate rings; continuity of a valuation on a Huber ring detected on generators of an ideal of definition. (needed by `tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`, `good-affinoid-uniform-completion`, `tilde-limit-perfectoid-uniqueness`).
- **tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras** — Complete Tate rings with a ring of definition carrying the ϖ-adic topology built from a ϖ-adically complete ϖ-torsion-free ring A⁺ (A = A⁺[1/ϖ]), their completion, and open integrally closed subrings containing all topologically nilpotent elements. (needed by `frobenius-controlled-integral-tower`, `frobenius-tower-completion`, `tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit`).

### Gaps

- **Huber's §2.4 arguments behind Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16, Theorem 7.17 and Corollary 7.19 (Huber 1996 is not public).** Scholze 2012 proves Proposition 7.16 by 'the same proof as for Remark 2.4.3 of [20]', Theorem 7.17 by 'the same proof as for Proposition 2.4.4 of [20]' with the local open-immersion/finite-étale factorisation, Corollary 7.18 as Huber's Corollary 2.4.6, and Corollary 7.19 by 'the remark after Proposition 2.3.7 of [20]'. None of these Huber passages was read. The nodes give a proof route through public inputs: pointwise finite étale descent from Berkeley Lemma 7.4.6 and Theorem 7.4.8, the graph argument of ECD Proposition 6.4, Stacks Lemmas 5.23.3, 5.24.5-5.24.6, and SGA 4 VI.8. Two steps remain tied to Huber's text: the claim that bijectivity of |X| → lim |X_i| with dense residue fields already gives a homeomorphism (the route through DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/generalizing-surjection-is-quotient is sketched in the node and not checked against Huber's argument), and the invariance of the étale site of a locally noetherian analytic adic space under homeomorphic morphisms with purely inseparable residue-field extensions used in Corollary 7.19. Next action: read Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces (Aspects of Math. E30, 1996) §2.3-2.4, or locate the invariance statement in a public source (e.g. Huber's Proposition 2.3.7 as cited in subsequent public work).
- **Perfectoidness of the limit of a tilde-limit of affinoids from representability of the diamond limit.** Scholze's survey Proposition 2.26 (every X ~ lim Spa(R_i, R_i⁺) is affinoid perfectoid with lim R_i dense) is proved there only assuming Conjecture 2.24 (perfectoidness of (A, A⁺) with p-adic topology on A⁺ from a rational cover by perfectoid rational localisations). The node PerfectoidSpaces:P7/represented-functor-comparison therefore states density as a separate clause and identifies it with perfectoidness of the uniformisation of the finite-level colimit; whether representability of lim X_i^◇ by a perfectoid space forces this density was not settled in the sources read. Consumers that need density (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers) assume the tilde-limit explicitly.

- **The Cohen structure theorem and regular local rings are absent from the pinned libraries.** Česnavičius's Lemmas 5.1–5.2 rest on the Cohen structure theorem for complete regular local rings (Matsumura 29.3, 29.7, and the proofs of 29.1 and 29.8(ii)) and on regular local rings with their regular systems of parameters. A search of the pinned declaration index finds neither (Mathlib has regular sequences, not regular local rings), and no atlas stage plans the Cohen structure theorem. Matsumura was not read here; the citations are Česnavičius's. Next action: find an owner in a commutative-algebra roadmap, or record the three presentations as imports (RT-AREA-padic-1/7).

### Mistakes recorded in the sources

- `PerfectoidSpaces/E44` (gap, affects the proof): p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, §4, proof of Theorem 4.9, p. 26, in arXiv:1205.3463v2. Printed: “Moreover, X∞ ∼ lim Xi in the sense of [18, Definition 7.14], where Xi = Spa(Ai , A+ i )→ X is finite étale. Then by [18, Corollary 7.18], we have” Correction: Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 and Corollary 7.18 are stated for noetherian adic spaces X_i over a perfectoid field K, whereas here the X_i are affinoid noetherian adic spaces over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) and X_∞ lies over C_p. The proof of Theorem 7.17/Corollary 7.18 does not use the base field beyond the perfectoidness of X; the statement needed is Corollary 7.18 for qcqs locally noetherian analytic X_i with no base field, as in PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison.
- `PerfectoidSpaces/E45` (misprint, affects nothing): Moduli of p-divisible groups, §2.3, proof of Proposition 2.3.11, p. 19, in arXiv:1211.6357v2. Printed: “Proposition 2.3.11. Let X be a preperfectoid adic space over Spa(Qp , Zp ), and let Y ⊂ X be a locally closed subspace. Then Y is preperfectoid. Proof. This follows directly from Proposition 2.3.11.” Correction: The proof should cite Proposition 2.3.7 (locally closed subspaces of preperfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field), applied to the base changes Y_K ⊂ X_K for every perfectoid field K of characteristic 0.
- `PerfectoidSpaces/E46` (misprint, affects nothing): Moduli of p-divisible groups, §2.3, Definition 2.3.4, pp. 17-18, in arXiv:1211.6357v2. Printed: “affinoid (K, OK )-algebra, where we take the completion with respect to the topology on Ai giving A+i the p-adic topology.” Correction: For a perfectoid field K of characteristic p (allowed by Definition 2.3.1) the p-adic topology is discrete; the completion is meant for the ϖ-adic topology on A_i⁺, ϖ a pseudouniformiser of K. In characteristic 0 the two agree.

### Coverage

Narrowed by RS-05 to perfectoid tilde-limits (uniqueness and represented-functor comparison), Frobenius-controlled integral towers with completion/inversion and the uniformity bound, rational restriction, cofinality, étale base change and gluing; the general Huber tilde-limit carrier and classical continuity are imported from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity. Every target of the narrowed stage is realised by a node; the Scholze 2012 §7 comparison is the kept node, generalised to locally noetherian index spaces over no perfectoid base field.

- Remaining: Huber 1996 §2.3-2.4 (Remark 2.4.3, Proposition 2.4.4, Corollary 2.4.6, the remark after Proposition 2.3.7), on which Scholze 2012 Proposition 7.16 - Corollary 7.19 rest 'by the same proof', is not public and was not read; the nodes carry a public-source route and the gap records the two steps still tied to Huber's text.
- Remaining: Whether representability of lim X_i^◇ by a perfectoid space forces the density clause of a tilde-limit (Scholze's survey Proposition 2.26 is conditional on Conjecture 2.24) is recorded as a gap on PerfectoidSpaces:P7/represented-functor-comparison.
- Remaining: Open requests: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0 (tilde-limit carrier in Scholze–Weinstein generality), DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 (SGA 4 VI.8 limits of coherent topoi and continuity of cohomology), anchor Layers 0, 1, 2, 3, 5. Cross-stage inputs are the planned nodes of P1, P2, P3 and P5 cited by id (among them P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces, P5/completed-colimit-is-perfectoid, P3/finite-etale-completed-direct-limit, P3/residue-field-finite-etale-colimit).
